# Codex conversation

## User

This repo is aimed being our data engineering repo `CCFinance` which aims to filter and enrich public copies of CCNews (a project of CommonCrawl organization) for use in studies like `~/Git/PricingPerspective` (and similar such cited studes like Linton and Ge, Box etc), aimed at offering an open-source, public dataset for research into natural language in finance. The aim is for this to be a large dataset, much larger that ~/Git/PricingPerspectives both in terms of articles per companies and the number of companies with >K (~42) article in at least T (5-10) consecutive years, which also coming from a set of 'trusted', major financial news outlets. 

Similar to ~/Git/PricingPerspective, we have a huggngface dataset (which should just be considered a staging dataset), an we have  a huggingface bucket called CCFinance meant for use for intermediate or experiment results to ensure experimental reproducibility. Currently the staging HF dataset is at `~/Git/fine-news-financial-publishers`, which has a 'mess' of hacky explortory results, data, notes and code. Which we want to start evaluating (for the feasiblity and scientific rigour/qualty for researchers to use in their studies) and cleaning up. 

So, with that background in mind. Can you start by templating using our marcusinthesky.github.io/exordio copier template, a python and latex toolchain for this repo, and setup dvc for us to start building our our reproducicle analysis in a part 2. 

Start with just the copier and dvc, ensuring we have a app called pipeline, which exposes a simpler typer cli, with submodule for data processing stages and bulletproof tach, ruff, pyrefly quality gates.

## Assistant

I’ll inspect the repo and Exordio template, then set up the Python/LaTeX toolchain, `pipeline` CLI, DVC, and quality gates.

    description: Start a project with only the tools you need.
    ---
    
    # Exordio
    
    ![Exordio: an open spellbook beneath a rising spark](docs/assets/exordio-wordmark.svg)
    
    **A spell for good beginnings.**
    
    Choose your languages and, if useful, Markdown planning or reference records.
    Exordio supplies a reproducible Nix environment, checks and documentation.
    Each choice is independent: a TypeScript project needs no planning system.
    
    ## Start with one useful thing
    
    Use Linux x86-64 or ARM64 with Git, Nix and
    [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) installed.
    Initial setup downloads pinned dependencies.
    
    This example creates only a TypeScript workspace:
    
    ```bash
    env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME uvx --from copier==9.16.0 copier copy --vcs-ref v0.1.0 --defaults -d 'languages=["typescript"]' gh:marcusinthesky/exordio my-project
    cd my-project
    git init -b main
    bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh
    devenv shell
    just setup
    just typescript::run Ada
    just check
    ```
    
    Omit `--defaults` to choose interactively. Both workflow and language selections
    default to empty. The example pins the `v0.1.0` release.
    
    ## Choose what belongs in your project
    
    | Choice | What you get |
    | --- | --- |
    | Planning | Nested Markdown tasks, immediate-child views and a roadmap |
    | References | Citation records, backlinks and an index |
    | Python | A typed library and application in one uv workspace |
    | TypeScript | A Bun library and CLI workspace |
    | Lean4 | Mathlib proofs, LeanArchitect and a LeanBlueprint graph/PDF |
    | LaTeX | A Tectonic article; references can generate its bibliography |
    | AgentSync | Shared instructions projected into Codex and/or Claude configuration |
    | SecretSpec | Secret access only for an explicitly invoked command |
    
    Read the [feature guide](docs/features.md), or follow the
    [planning walkthrough](docs/index.md) to see source metadata become a useful view.
    Nix supports every selection; no cloud infrastructure is created.
    
    ## Let your agent help
    
    Paste this into an agent with access to your local repositories:
    
    ```text
    Create a project using Exordio:
    https://github.com/marcusinthesky/exordio
    
    Read its README and feature guide first. Choose only the workflows, languages
    and integrations needed for my goal. Use Copier 9.16.0 and release v0.1.0.
    Generate into a new directory, initialize Git and enter its pinned environment.
    Run explicit setup and deliver one useful working result.
    Read adjacent READMEs, preserve authored content, and run applicable sync/checks.
    Report what works and my next useful step. Do not commit or push unless asked.
    ```
    
    ## Find your next step
    
    - [Everyday work](docs/daily-use.md)

    - [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md)
    - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)
    - [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md)
    
    Copier owns project structure; optional Insitu views derive from authored files.
    Your records stay ordinary Markdown in Git.

    ---
    description: Choose independent workflows, languages and integrations.
    ---
    
    # Choose only what you need
    
    There are no starter profiles. Workflow and language selections default to empty.
    You can select TypeScript alone, references without planning, or Lean without
    a manuscript.
    
    ## Markdown workflows
    
    | Selection | Adds |
    | --- | --- |
    | `planning` | Plans, nested tasks, a roadmap and local child views |
    | `reference` | Citation records, an index and declared backlinks |
    
    Either selection installs Insitu and the document validators. With neither
    selected, the project has no workflow environment or context tree.
    
    Reference records live in `.context/reference/KEY/README.md`. Flat CSL fields
    describe the source; the directory supplies its citation key. References plus
    LaTeX derive the manuscript bibliography automatically during `just sync`.
    Without reference records, LaTeX owns its ordinary `refs.bib` directly.
    
    ## Languages
    
    | Selection | First useful result |
    | --- | --- |
    | `python` | Typed library imported by an application in a locked uv workspace |
    | `typescript` | Bun library imported by a runnable CLI workspace |
    | `lean` | Mathlib proofs with LeanArchitect annotations and a LeanBlueprint graph/PDF |
    | `latex` | A Tectonic article with cached local builds |
    
    Each language has a local README and namespaced commands. Python and TypeScript
    retain their library/application package boundaries. Lean includes its blueprint
    tooling even when manuscript LaTeX is absent.
    
    ## Integrations
    
    AgentSync optionally projects shared instructions into Codex and/or Claude
    configuration. Nix builds its pinned Rust CLI; no npm installation is needed.
    Its Python preflight stops on authored destinations; migrate those files
    deliberately. Without it, the README and agent prompt remain useful; projects may author their own instructions.
    
    SecretSpec optionally resolves declared credentials for `just secret-run COMMAND`.
    Shell entry and ordinary checks never load secrets. Configure a provider when a
    real project needs one; never put secret values in Copier answers.
    
    Nix supplies the reproducible environment for every project. There is no empty
    Terraform/Kubernetes scaffold or automatic deployment.

    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    set positional-arguments
    
    [% for language in languages %]
    mod [[ language ]] 'src/[[ language ]]/justfile'
    [% endfor %]
    [% if agents %]
    mod agents '.agents/justfile'
    [% endif %]
    [% if workflows %]
    workflow := "env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py"
    [% endif %]
    
    # Discover this project's commands.
    default:
        @just --list
    
    # Prepare locked dependencies and Git hooks (uses the network).
    setup:
    [% if workflows %]
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py prepare
    [% endif %]
    [% for language in languages %]
        just [[ language ]]::setup
    [% endfor %]
    [% if agents %]
        just agents::apply
    [% endif %]
        prek install
    
    # Check source, views and selected languages without repairing files.
    check:
        bash infra/nix/check.sh
    [% if workflows %]
        {{ workflow }} check
    [% endif %]
    [% for language in languages %]
        just [[ language ]]::check
    [% endfor %]
    
    [% if agents %]
        just agents::check
    [% endif %]
    
    # Run the selected language tests.
    test:
    [% for language in languages %]
        just [[ language ]]::test
    [% else %]
        @echo 'No languages selected.'
    [% endfor %]
    
    # Explicitly format sources.
    fmt:
        nixfmt devenv.nix infra/nix/devenv.nix[% if workflows %] infra/nix/pkgs/schematter.nix[% endif %][% if 'lean' in languages %] infra/nix/pkgs/lean-toolchain.nix[% endif %][% if agents %] infra/nix/pkgs/agentsync.nix[% endif %]
        rumdl fmt .
    [% for language in languages %]
        just [[ language ]]::fmt
    [% endfor %]
    [% if workflows %]
    
    # Refresh generated indexes, child views and bibliography.
    sync:
        {{ workflow }} sync
    [% endif %]
    [% if 'planning' in workflows %]
    
    # Create a plan without overwriting existing content.
    plan-new slug title:
        {{ workflow }} plan-new "$1" --title "$2"
    
    # Create a task inside an existing plan or task.
    task-new parent slug title:
        {{ workflow }} task-new "$1" "$2" --title "$3"
    [% endif %]
    [% if 'reference' in workflows %]
    
    # Create a citation record with its directory as citation key.
    reference-new key title:
        {{ workflow }} reference-new "$1" --title "$2"
    [% endif %]
    
    # Check external links online.
    links:
        git ls-files -z '*.md' | xargs -0 -r lychee --config lychee.toml --no-progress
    [% if secrets %]
    
    # Resolve credentials only for this explicit subprocess.
    secret-run +command:
        secretspec run -- "$@"
    [% endif %]

    ignore_type_checking_imports = false
    forbid_circular_dependencies = true

    setup:

    lint:

    # Local impacted-test selection, with a bounded number of workers.
    test-changed:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest -q -n 2 --testmon
    
    # The test and CI gates never use affected-test selection.

    tach:

    check: lint typecheck tach test build
    
    fmt:
        ruff check --fix .
        ruff format .
    ---
    description: Why Python libraries and applications share one uv workspace and lock.
    ---
    
    # Python workspace
    
    Libraries and executable consumers have separate package boundaries. A single
    uv workspace resolves cross-package imports locally and locks test, build
    and runtime dependencies together. This keeps the example runnable and lets the
    project grow without publishing internal packages.
    
    | Tool | Responsibility |
    | --- | --- |
    | uv | Dependency resolution, installation and packaging |
    | Ruff | Lint and formatting |
    | Pyrefly | Static type checking |
    | pytest | Behavior and entry-point tests |
    
    The pinned Nix environment supplies native Ruff and Pyrefly executables. This
    avoids Python wheels whose ELF interpreter assumes a conventional Linux layout,
    so the checker commands also work on NixOS without a machine-level loader service.
    
    Python commands scrub inherited `PYTHONPATH` and `PYTHONHOME` so an unrelated Nix
    or user environment cannot inject incompatible Python packages. Setup is the
    network boundary; checks use frozen, offline dependencies and never update locks.
    [project]
    name = "example-app"
    version = "0.1.0"
    requires-python = ">=3.13,<3.14"
    dependencies = ["example-core"]
    
    [project.scripts]
    example-app = "example_app:main"
    
    [tool.uv.sources]
    example-core = {workspace = true}
    
    [build-system]
    requires = ["hatchling==1.27.0"]
    build-backend = "hatchling.build"
    
    [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
    packages = ["src/example_app"]
    default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit]
    default_stages: [pre-commit]

    name: CI
    on:
      pull_request:
        types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, ready_for_review, converted_to_draft]
      push:
        branches: [main]
      workflow_dispatch:
    permissions:
      contents: read
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    jobs:
      check:
        # Draft PRs emit a skipped run; compute-heavy checks only run when ready.
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.draft == false }}
        env:
          TECTONIC_CACHE_DIR: /tmp/exordio-tectonic-cache
        strategy:
          matrix:
            runner: [ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-24.04-arm]
        runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262
            with:
              persist-credentials: false
          - name: Free hosted runner disk space
            run: |
              df -h /
              sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /usr/local/share/powershell /opt/ghc
              df -h /
          # cache-nix-action requires a store writable by the runner user.
          - uses: nixbuild/nix-quick-install-action@9f63be77f412a248c9d9a65a4c82cf066cdf8f0c # v35
            with:
              nix_version: 2.34.7
          - uses: nix-community/cache-nix-action@135667ec418502fa5a3598af6fb9eb733888ce6a
            if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
            with:
              primary-key: nix-single-user-v1-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('devenv.lock', 'devenv.nix', 'infra/nix/**') }}
              restore-prefixes-first-match: nix-single-user-v1-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
          - uses: actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830
            if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
            with:
              path: |
                ~/.cache/uv
                ${{ env.TECTONIC_CACHE_DIR }}
                ~/.cache/mathlib
                ~/.bun/install/cache
              key: tools-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('**/uv.lock', '**/*.py.lock', '**/bun.lock', '**/lake-manifest.json') }}
          - name: Install matching devenv
            run: bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh
          - name: Prepare dependencies
            run: devenv shell -- just setup
          - name: Validate
            run: devenv shell -- just check
    name: GitHub Actions security
    
    on:
      pull_request:
        types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, ready_for_review, converted_to_draft]
      push:
        branches: [main]
      workflow_dispatch:
    
    permissions:
      contents: read
    
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    
    jobs:
      zizmor:
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.draft == false }}
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
            with:
              persist-credentials: false
          - name: Audit workflow security with upstream zizmor
            uses: zizmorcore/zizmor-action@53290badfa369cb0bf7ad16342cb62c2fa47ac7b # v0.8.0
            with:
              advanced-security: false
    ---
    description: A small LaTeX manuscript built with a versioned Tectonic asset bundle.
    ---
    
    # LaTeX
    
    `main.tex` is the manuscript. Tectonic produces `build/main.pdf`; its output and
    intermediate files are ignored. Edit the source, and use:
    
    ```bash
    just latex::setup
    just latex::build
    just latex::check
    ```
    
    Setup is an explicit network step that primes the Tectonic cache using the
    versioned `tlextras-2022.0r0` bundle. Ordinary builds use only cached assets. After
    adding an uncached TeX package, run setup again. Formatting uses tex-fmt and lint
    uses ChkTeX. The build gate rejects unresolved citations and references.
    
    `refs.bib` is authored content. The sample article demonstrates a real citation;
    add your own records and cite them with `\citep{key}`.
    
    See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for source and artifact ownership.
    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    
    # The versioned bundle is shared by setup and cached builds.
    bundle := "https://data1.fullyjustified.net/tlextras-2022.0r0.tar"
    
    default:
        @just --list
    
    # Explicit network step: fetch TeX resources needed by the current manuscript.
    setup:
        mkdir -p build
        bash ../../infra/nix/retry-tex-setup.sh tectonic --untrusted --bundle "{{ bundle }}" --keep-logs --outdir build main.tex
    
    build:
        mkdir -p build
        tectonic --untrusted --only-cached --bundle "{{ bundle }}" --keep-logs --outdir build main.tex
        if rg -n 'Citation.+undefined|Reference.+undefined|There were undefined|multiply-defined|Multiply defined' build/main.log; then echo 'Unresolved citations, references or duplicate labels' >&2; exit 1; fi
    
    lint:
        tex-fmt --check main.tex
        chktex -q -n 1 -n 8 -n 46 main.tex
    
    check: lint build
    
    test: build
    
    fmt:
        tex-fmt main.tex
    cat: AGENTS.md: No such file or directory

        import sys
        
        from typer.testing import CliRunner
        
        from pipeline.cli import app
        
        
        def test_version() -> None:
            result = CliRunner().invoke(app, ["version"])
            assert result.exit_code == 0
            assert result.stdout.strip() == "0.1.0"
        
        
        def test_stages() -> None:
            result = CliRunner().invoke(app, ["stages", "list"])
            assert result.exit_code == 0
            assert "No data processing stages registered" in result.stdout
        
        
        def test_unknown_stage_fails() -> None:
            assert CliRunner().invoke(app, ["stages", "missing"]).exit_code != 0

    ---
    description: Python workspace and repository scripts.
    ---
    
    # Python
    
    The example application imports the shared `example_core` library. Both use a
    `src` layout and share this directory's `uv.lock`; the library ships `py.typed`.
    The sample package identifiers are stable so the complete lock is reusable.
    Rename them together with their imports and regenerate the lock when adopting
    your own domain vocabulary.
    
    Run from the repository root:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::run Ada
    just python::check
    ```
    
    `setup` installs locked dependencies. Ordinary checks use the local environment
    and cache. Add libraries under `packages/` and executable applications under
    `apps/`, then explicitly run `uv lock` here and commit the updated manifest and
    lock. `just python::build` writes wheels and source archives to ignored `dist/`.
    
    The pinned Nix environment supplies native Ruff and Pyrefly executables. Ruff
    checks style, Pyrefly checks types, and the uv environment supplies pytest to
    exercise the library and real application entry point. See
    [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for ownership.
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # Check existing tracked and untracked source without treating deletions as files.
    set -euo pipefail
    files=()
    while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
      if [[ -f "$file" || -L "$file" ]]; then files+=("$file"); fi
    done < <(git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard -z)
    if (( ${#files[@]} )); then prek run --files "${files[@]}"; fi

        CCFinance is a data engineering project for filtering and enriching public
        Common Crawl News (CC-News) copies for research into language in finance.
        The intended public research dataset will emphasize trusted major financial
        publishers and broad company coverage across consecutive years. Dataset quality,
        feasibility, licensing, provenance and coverage remain research questions; this
        scaffold makes no claims about achieved coverage.
        
        ## Start
        
        Exordio supplies the Python and LaTeX toolchains, a pinned Nix environment and CI.
        Copier answers record Exordio `v0.1.1-alpha` (the documented `v0.1.0` tag was not
        available in the local source). No exploratory staging data has been imported.
        
        ```bash

        devenv shell
        just setup
        just python::run --help
        just python::run stages list
        just check
        ```
        
        For Python alone, with Python 3.13, uv and just installed:
        
        ```bash
        just python::setup
        just python::check
        ```
        
        `pipeline` is a Typer application. `pipeline.stages` is the reserved namespace for
        part 2's data processing stages. `python -m pipeline` exposes the same commands.
        The committed uv lock covers runtime, DVC, build and quality tools. CI runs Ruff,
        strict Pyrefly, explicit Tach boundaries, all tests and package builds, as well
        as the template's infrastructure and LaTeX gates.
        
        ## Data and reproducibility
        
        DVC is initialized at the repository root with analytics disabled. Use:
        
        ```bash
        just dvc status
        just dvc dag
        ```
        
        [`dvc.yaml`](dvc.yaml) deliberately has no stages yet. Part 2 should add real
        stages with explicit commands, code/data dependencies, parameters and outputs,
        then commit `dvc.lock` after execution. Never substitute placeholder results for
        measured coverage or enrichment. Large inputs, intermediates and outputs belong
        under `data/`, which Git ignores; DVC metadata belongs in Git.
        
        The existing Hugging Face dataset is staging material. The CCFinance Hugging Face
        bucket is intended for intermediate and experiment artifacts. A DVC remote is
        not configured yet: its supported transport and exact bucket identifier need to
        be established during part 2. This setup neither uploads data nor assumes a
        Hugging Face bucket is an S3 endpoint. Store credentials outside Git, using
        `.dvc/config.local` for local DVC configuration.
        
        See [Python commands](src/python/README.md), [LaTeX commands](src/latex/README.md)

        ''')
        Path('src/python/README.md').write_text('''# Python workspace

        ```bash
        just python::setup
        just python::run --help
        just python::run version
        just python::run stages list
        just python::check
        ```
        
        Setup installs the committed lock. Checks run offline with frozen dependencies.
        Ruff checks formatting, annotations, docstrings and common correctness/security
        issues; strict Pyrefly checks all app code and tests. Tach requires explicit
        module declarations and rejects circular dependencies. The CLI may depend on
        stages; stages must not import the CLI. Declare new stage modules and their
        allowed dependencies in `tach.toml` when adding them.
        
        Keep CLI argument parsing in `pipeline.cli`; implement research stages under
        `pipeline.stages`, with explicit inputs and outputs. Add corresponding DVC
        stages at the repository root in part 2. No dataset access occurs on import.
        
        `just python::test` runs all tests. `test-changed` is a local optimization only.
        `build` builds a wheel and source archive. `fmt` explicitly repairs formatting.
        Ruff and Pyrefly run from the same uv lock locally and in CI.
        ''')
        Path('src/python/ARCHITECTURE.md').write_text('''# Python architecture
        
        One uv workspace and lock own runtime, development and build dependencies.
        `apps/pipeline/src/pipeline` owns the executable application:
        
        - `cli` parses arguments and dispatches commands.
        - `stages` owns data processing commands and future stage implementations.
        - `__main__` exposes the same application through `python -m pipeline`.
        
        Tach enforces the declared dependency direction from the application entry point
        to CLI to stages, including type-checking imports, with cycles forbidden.
        Ruff and strict Pyrefly check source and tests. Tests exercise CLI dispatch and
        installed module execution; packaging is checked independently by a wheel build.
        
        All Python recipes scrub inherited Python paths and virtual environments.
        Setup is the network boundary; validation uses frozen offline dependencies.
        ''')

    AgentSync, when selected, checks all destinations before projecting shared sources.
    Authored files and unexpected links stop apply. SecretSpec, when selected, resolves

    infrastructure; no cloud resources are created.
    
    Keep Copier answers in Git. Tagged updates preserve selections or add features;
    review conflicts before committing. Removing a feature or adopting an existing
    repository requires manual migration: Copier can delete previously owned paths.

        from pathlib import Path
        p=Path('ARCHITECTURE.md');p.write_text('''# Architecture
        
        CCFinance separates code and research artifacts. Git stores source, configuration,
        locks, provenance definitions and documentation. DVC will track large data and
        experiment outputs once the actual stages are defined in part 2.
        
        - `src/python/apps/pipeline` owns the CLI and data stage implementations.
        - `src/python/uv.lock` locks runtime, quality, testing, packaging and DVC tools.
        - `src/latex` owns the manuscript source and bibliography.
        - `data` holds ignored data payloads and versioned DVC pointer files.
        - `infra/nix` and `devenv.lock` own the reproducible system environment.
        
        Tach enforces module boundaries; Ruff and strict Pyrefly check Python source.
        CI executes those checks, tests and builds through the same just recipes as local
        work. Setup may download dependencies; ordinary checks use cached dependencies
        and do not repair authored content. LaTeX uses a versioned Tectonic asset bundle.
        
        The Hugging Face dataset is staging, and the bucket is intended for intermediate
        and experiment artifacts. Neither is accessed by scaffold commands. Pipeline
        stages, provenance, study parameters, coverage criteria and remote transport are
        part 2 work, rather than implied by this scaffold.
        
        Copier answers record the source and tag for future template updates. Review
        update conflicts and preserve project-specific code and configuration. The
        upstream template is [Exordio](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/exordio).
        ''')

    # CCFinance
    
    CCFinance is a data engineering project for filtering and enriching public
    Common Crawl News (CC-News) copies for research into language in finance.
    
    
    ## Start
    
    Exordio supplies the Python and LaTeX toolchains, a pinned Nix environment and CI.
    Copier answers record Exordio `v0.1.1-alpha` (the documented `v0.1.0` tag was not
    available in the local source).
    
    ```bash
    bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh
    devenv shell
    just setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run stages list
    just check
    ```
    
    For Python alone, with Python 3.13, uv and just installed:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::check
    ```
    
    ## Data and reproducibility
    
    DVC is initialized at the repository root with analytics disabled. Use:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc status
    just dvc dag
    ```
    
    See [Python commands](src/python/README.md), [LaTeX commands](src/latex/README.md)
    and [infrastructure](infra/README.md). The scaffold's Apache-2.0 license covers
    code; it does not grant rights to upstream article content.

    ## Introduction
    
    Read all adjacent and parent `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` files — they offer progressive disclosure of the project's structure and purpose and document key concepts, conventions and dependencies that must be followed. Per-area `AGENTS.md` (e.g. `src/latex/AGENTS.md`) carry binding house rules and are **not** auto-loaded; read the nearest one when working in a subtree.
    
    Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` files for the "why" behind architectural and tool decisions — comparison tables, trade-offs, and alternatives considered. These are the canonical source of truth for design decisions.
    
    ## Environment
    
    The devenv `dev` profile is the default and is auto-activated by `direnv`, so `just`, `uv`, `lake`, `secretspec`, and `prek` are already on `PATH` — **run them directly; do not prefix with a shell command.** If a fresh worktree has not activated, use `devenv shell -- <cmd>`. The legacy `nix develop ./infra/nix -c <cmd>` also remains available. Both shells set capped BLAS/OpenMP threads (`OMP_NUM_THREADS` etc. default to 4, overridable), `JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu`, and scrubbed `PYTHONPATH`. After `just setup`, `devenv --profile watch up` runs the opt-in Insitu sync watcher. There is **no** root `flake.nix`.
    
    Python dependencies are **not** installed globally — `ruff`, `pytest`, and imports like `duckdb`/`pandas` resolve only inside a `uv` project. Run Python through the `just` recipes, or ad-hoc via `uv run --project <app> …` (e.g. `uv run --project src/python/apps/pipeline pytest -q`). Do not call bare `python3`, `pip`, `ruff`, or `pytest`.
    
    Use targeted tests and the existing Testmon recipes during iteration. For final validation, use the prescribed package/workspace recipes and their complete, no-Testmon fast-suite path where required. Keep projects in separate pytest processes. Report which suites ran and which were not run; a selective Testmon pass is not evidence that the complete suite passed.
    
    Python consumers resolve credentials lazily through the pinned SecretSpec SDK: dry runs and cache hits need no GCP access. Explicit process-environment keys override SDK resolution for tests. For other commands, use `secretspec run --profile mineru --reason "Purpose" -- <command>` (or profile `openrouter`). GCSM uses per-host ADC; shell activation never fetches secrets. See `infra/nix/docs/secretspec/README.md`.
    
    ## Commands
    
    Run `just --list` to discover available commands at different levels of abstraction across the codebase. The root justfile aggregates per-area modules; invoke a module recipe with `::` — e.g. `just lean::build`, `just python::lint`, `just python::typecheck`. Some recipes (such as a package's tests) live only in that package's own justfile, so if a recipe is missing at the root, check `just --list` inside the relevant `src/…` directory. For what CLI tools exist, read the **generated** table in `infra/nix/README.md` (§ Tools provided) — it is emitted from the dev-shell definition by `just nix::tools`, so it cannot drift. Each tool's one-line purpose and the binary it puts on `PATH` are there; `infra/nix/shells/groups/*.nix` says why each is present, and `<tool> --help` covers the rest.
    
    Choose the cheapest evidence source that can answer the claim, inspect its output, then escalate only when it has no candidate, is ambiguous or conflicting, or cannot represent the required evidence:
    
    1. Known path, phrase, or regex → direct read or `rg`.
    2. Known code symbol → `ast-grep run --lang <lang> --pattern '<pattern>' <path>` for a structural match, or `rg` for the literal name. The language servers this shell pins (`texlab`, `marksman`, `nixd`, `pyrefly`, `harper-ls`, …) are stdio-only and cannot be driven from a shell — use them through an editor runtime that exposes one, not from a command.
    3. Unknown code behavior or reference concept → `semble_rs search --outline <query> <path>` (see the `code-search` skill for the escalation ladder) / `just references search`, then compact or raw hydration only if needed.
    4. Transitive, aggregate, historical, or cross-plane repository fact → DuckDB harness.
    5. Broad exploration of a long unfamiliar PDF, or a layout/equation/table/chart/annotation/scan/render claim → bounded low-resolution pixels first; exact wording → source text or `pdftotext`.
    
    Hydrate only a small candidate set, reassess, and stop when evidence is sufficient;
    do not run semantic, graph, and visual retrieval merely because they are available.
    For manuscript changes, inspect affected pages of the final release PDF by default;
    run a whole-document visual pass only when the task asks for one. Treat compiler,
    type-checker, and proof-tool results as authoritative over LSP diagnostics.
    
    ## Research-code changes
    
    Prefer the smallest coherent implementation of the requested scientific behavior. Before adding a numerical or statistical routine, search for an existing repository implementation and an established library implementation. Prefer reuse or a thin domain adapter over another algorithm or framework.
    
    Keep JAX where the retained computation needs accelerator execution, transformations, or differentiation. Do not reimplement ordinary host-side econometrics merely for backend uniformity. Preserve supported numerical APIs; an unused DVC materialization does not make its underlying library API dead.
    
    Distinguish behavior-preserving refactoring from changes to the estimand, sample, inference, solver, or numerical contract. Report scientific corrections separately; do not hide them through new defaults, renamed outputs, or relaxed tests.
    
    Retire code using evidence from retained consumers and their dependencies. Vulture findings, whitelist entries, absent Semflow membership, and test-only usage are review signals, not sufficient deletion proofs.
    
    Tests should protect scientific behavior, public contracts, and meaningful operational safeguards. Do not add arbitrary counts, file-layout requirements, or source-text assertions merely to preserve an implementation.
    
    For changes to experiment scope, statistical implementations, numerical backends, or DVC dataflow, load the `research-pipeline-change` skill. Follow the relevant Python and pipeline `ARCHITECTURE.md` sections; do not duplicate their registries or conventions.
    
    ## Code Quality
    
    This repository imposes strict quality gates and automated code-generation using `prek` `.pre-commit-config.yaml` hooks, which must be installed and configured correctly, and passed before any code can be committed.
    
    ## Project management
    
    As you work, keep the plan layer current: reflect progress in the owning `.context/plan/{plan}/README.md` or its `tasks/tNN-*/README.md` frontmatter and `- [ ]`/`- [X]` checkboxes — never in the generated `:::` tables — and update `/ROADMAP.md` when scope shifts. See `.context/plan/AGENTS.md` for the workflow.
    
    ## Safety
    
    Never perform `git commit`, `git push`, or other sensitive 'write' operations - these are reserved for human contributors. You can only perform 'read' git or gh cli commands. `git mv` and `git write-tree`, for instance, are fine as they are non-destructive and non-permanent, still allowing for human review before commit.
    
    ## Style
    
    Respond tersely with clear Markdown and only useful sections. Put review commands, decisions, and other user actions at the end.
    
    - Explain what changed, why, how it was verified, and material limitations. Distinguish checks that passed from checks not run.
    - State errors as cause → fix, with `file:line` where useful.
    - Give time estimates in concrete units, such as “15 minutes” or “an afternoon.”
    - Keep recommendations ranked and limited to five; split longer lists into immediate and later work.
    - Omit announcing preambles, post-task recaps, closers, and unrelated sidebars.

    ---
    
    # Context
    
    `.context/` is the project's knowledge context store: a "vault" of durable knowledge
    that sits alongside the code and is versioned with it. Four subfolders, each read
    first via its own `README.md` (and `AGENTS.md`/`ARCHITECTURE.md` where present):
    
    - **`chat/`** — AI-session and deep-research artifacts, one per `{date}_{slug}/README.md`.
      Hot (cited from an active plan/`ROADMAP.md`) vs cold (archive candidate) is tracked
      via generated backlinks. See [`chat/README.md`](chat/README.md).
    - **`plan/`** — the typed plan/task knowledge graph, derived from `/ROADMAP.md`: durable
      plans, each with a physically-nested task tree. See [`plan/README.md`](plan/README.md),
      [`plan/ARCHITECTURE.md`](plan/ARCHITECTURE.md), [`plan/AGENTS.md`](plan/AGENTS.md).
    - **`reference/`** — the bibliography corpus: one `{cite_key}/` per paper, with
      CSL-frontmatter `README.md`, `raw/paper.pdf`, and MinerU `paper.md` conversion.
      See [`reference/README.md`](reference/README.md).
    - **`correspondence/`** — meeting notes and other external-communication records,
      `{date}_{slug}/README.md`.
    
    ## Directory Tree
    
    <!-- insitu:begin gittree
    id = "gittree"
    path = ".context"
    depth = 1
    -->
    
    ```text
    .
    ├── archive
    ├── chat
    ├── correspondence
    ├── plan # The plan layer — durable per-concern plans with physically-nested task trees, derived from ROADMAP.md and kept honest by prek hooks. Documentation for the layer; the live index lives in ROADMAP.md. Middle of the Roadmap → Plan → Task → TODO hierarchy.
    └── reference # Reference packages with CSL frontmatter, source artifacts, and source-grounded lab notes.
    ```
    
    <!-- insitu:end -->
    
    ## Shared conventions
    
    **Canonical metadata model.** Minimal authored frontmatter lives in each entry's
    `README.md` (`description` is required; subfolders add fields). Paths and Git supply
    derived identity and history. Discovery uses the canonical READMEs, inline generated
    rollups, exact/semantic search, and the DuckDB harness; `.context/**/index.md`
    projections are deliberately absent.
    
    **Execution boundary.** Keep executable source under its owning `src/` project
    (for example, Python under `src/python` and Lean under `src/lean`). Context holds specifications, records and results.
    Delete retired code; Git history preserves it. The native `context-no-source-code`
    hook rejects executable source anywhere under this store, including archives.
    
    **Validation.** prek schema gates check complete documents against the static
    profiles under `infra/schemas/documents/` (including CSL for `reference/`);
    Rumdl's `MD051`/`MD057` hooks check
    prose links against the maintained Markdown corpus.
    
    **Evidence storage.** Keep authored decisions, task metadata and readable execution
    summaries in ordinary Git. Selected immutable numerical reports, qualification
    records and diagnostic logs use explicit Git LFS rules while retaining their
    paths and original bytes; hydrate them with `git lfs pull` before reading or
    parsing payloads. Existing DVC-owned research artifacts retain their dataflow and
    aliases. Successful operational logs may be removed when the execution summary
    fully records their checks; preserve unique numerical results, failures and
    diagnostics. Task completion alone does not make evidence disposable.
    
    **Generation.** All tables and trees inside native `insitu:begin`/`insitu:end`
    regions are generated by the Python Insitu engine (`gittree`,
    `backlinks`, …) — never hand-edit inside a region. Regenerate with
    `just insitu::sync`; this also runs as the `insitu-projections` prek hook.
    
    **Layered data flow.** Knowledge flows one way through four layers, and no layer
    re-derives what another owns. (1) Authored Layer-1 `README.md` frontmatter is the
    only source of truth. (2) Static Schematter profiles under
    `infra/schemas/documents/` plus `prek` hooks constrain it. (3) Native Insitu
    regions provide only bounded inline rollups.
    (4) The DuckDB harness (`src/python/apps/harnessme`, dbt) is a *derived*
    query plane that ingests these artifacts; it never re-derives them nor becomes a
    second source of truth. `.agents/skills` wrap the owning `just` recipes and never
    bypass those boundaries.
    
    ## Obsidian compatibility
    
    `.context/` is already vault-shaped: YAML frontmatter is Obsidian's native
    **Properties** format (no transform needed), and cross-references between
    entries — a chat session citing a reference, a plan task citing prior
    correspondence — should use `[[wikilinks]]` (relative to the linked file's
    folder name, Obsidian's default resolution) alongside or instead of a prose
    Markdown link, so the same edge renders in Obsidian's graph/backlink views and
    in plain Markdown readers.
    
    A gitignored `notes -> .context` symlink at the repo root (plus a gitignored
    `.context/.obsidian/` for vault config) lets you open this store directly as
    an Obsidian vault — graph view, backlinks, Dataview, citation plugins — with
    zero risk to the git-tracked tree: delete the symlink and nothing changes.
    This is a **probe**, not a commitment: `.context` stays the canonical name
    unless the ecosystem access proves durably useful, and any rename would run
    through the DuckDB harness's pre-move impact-closure query first (prek path
    regexes, both intake skills, and plan tooling all key on the current name).
    
    ## Cross-corpus lookups
    
    ```bash
    # Search across all reference markdown
    grep -r "energy distance" .context/reference/
    
    # Check reference download status
    jq '.[] | select(.status == "downloaded") | .key' .context/manifest.json
    
    # Freshness (git > frontmatter timestamps)
    git log -1 --format=%cI -- .context/plan/<name>/README.md
    git log --oneline -- .context/reference/<key>/
    
    # Validate canonical reference metadata and strict CSL projection
    just references::structure
    just references::graph-check
    ```

    # Plan Context
    
    A **typed knowledge graph over the repo**: durable plans, each with a physically-nested
    task tree, all derived from `/ROADMAP.md` and validated by hooks. Frontmatter is the
    single source of truth; every generated table in the tree is derived from it — edit the
    plan, never the table. This file is documentation for the layer, not an index of it: the
    live index is the children block in [`/ROADMAP.md`](../../ROADMAP.md).
    
    New here? Read this file (structure + style), then [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md)
    (why it's built this way) and [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) (the agent workflow).
    
    ## The layers
    
    | Level | ID form | Where | Function | Granularity | Owner | Quality gate |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | 0 | — | `/ROADMAP.md` (one) | **Roadmap view** — typed, generated rollup of durable plans; no authored priorities or policy prose | years | generated | roadmap schema + body profile |
    | — | — | `.context/plan/README.md` (this file) and [`.archive/README.md`](.archive/README.md) | **Documentation + index view** — this file documents the layer; `.archive/README.md` indexes retired plans. Explicitly **not** plan nodes | — | author / generated | — |
    | 1 | bare name (`paper1`, `paper3`, `paper5`, `paper6`, `proofs`, `infra-tooling`) | `{plan}/README.md` | **Plan, durable root** — a functional domain or workstream that accretes and retires tasks | months | author | never reaches a terminal status |
    | 1 | `{YYYY-MM-DD}_{slug}` | `{plan}/README.md` | **Plan, dated issue** — one genuinely one-off repair or recovery | months | author | closes, then archives under `.archive/` |
    | 2 | `tNN` | `{plan}/tasks/tNN-slug/README.md` | **Task** — one concern, spec-driven (goal → acceptance) | weeks | orchestrator | `just check` passes without hacks |
    | 3 | `tNN.M` | `{plan}/tasks/tNN-slug/tasks/tNN.M-slug/README.md` | **Sub-task** — one bounded change | days | implementer | `prek run <hook_id> --files …` |
    | 4 | `tNN.M.K` | one further `tasks/` segment under the level-3 node | **Sub-sub-task** — the deepest node that gets a directory | hours | implementer | `prek run <hook_id> --files …` |
    | 5 | — | `TODO.md` next to code (e.g. `src/lean/TODO.md`) | **TODO** — live scratch checklist while working | live | whoever is working | — |
    
    Level and role are derived from the path: level = (number of `tasks/` segments) + 1.
    Frontmatter repeats the derived role as a required assertion (`type: plan` or
    `type: task`), and the applicable path-scoped hook fails a mismatch; `type` never
    selects the schema.
    `.context/plan/README.md` and `.archive/README.md` are documentation/index views rather
    than plan nodes and are excluded explicitly.
    
    A leading `YYYY-MM-DD_` on a level-1 name means the plan is finite: it closes and moves
    under `.archive/`. A bare name never does.
    
    Nothing below level 4 gets a directory — it is an acceptance checkbox on the level-4
    node, or a `TODO.md` beside the code. The one exception is closed and stays where it is:
    `paper1/tasks/t34-final-feedback-structural-revision/tasks/t34.6-deferred-extension-coordination/tasks/t34.6.3-effect-translation-calibration-integration/tasks/`
    holds `t34.6.3.1-…` and `t34.6.3.2-…`, which predate this rule. They are grandfathered,
    not precedent; nothing new joins them, and the task-ID regex stays permissive only so
    they do not hard-fail.
    
    A plan is decomposed into tasks. Lifecycle lives in frontmatter `status`, never in path
    segments or roadmap prose.
    
    ## Where "what are we working on" is answered
    
    **Only by the generated children block in [`/ROADMAP.md`](../../ROADMAP.md)**, and by the
    one in each plan and task README below it — all derived from `status`, `depends_on` and
    `target`. Never by prose — not here, not in `/ROADMAP.md`, not in a plan's Goal or
    Context section.
    
    This rule exists because it was broken: focus claims written into prose during one
    paper's push ("X is the current build priority") outlived the push and then misled every
    later reader, human and agent, into working the wrong paper. A sentence asserting what is
    current is stale the moment the next task lands, and nothing regenerates it.
    
    - Live = `status` in `draft` / `ready` / `in-progress` / `blocked`.
    - `backlog` = real, still wanted, deliberately sequenced behind the nearest milestone.
    - Terminal = verified `done`, intentionally discontinued `closed`, or replaced
      `superseded`; only `done` claims completion.
    - Dates live in `target`, in exactly one place per plan.
    
    If prose and a generated block disagree, the block wins and the prose is a bug — delete
    it rather than syncing it.
    
    The indexes themselves live in exactly two places, and neither is this file.
    [`/ROADMAP.md`](../../ROADMAP.md) carries the single live index — one row per open plan,
    regenerated from plan frontmatter — and every plan and task README below it carries a
    children block indexing its own open immediate children, one level deep. Retired plans
    are indexed once, in [`.archive/README.md`](.archive/README.md). This file is the layer's
    documentation and holds no generated table at all.
    
    ## Naming
    
    - **Durable roots** — bare `paper1`, `paper3`, `paper5`, `paper6`, `proofs`,
      `infra-tooling`: permanent
      per-concern homes that accrete and retire tasks. These are the norm.
    - **Dated issues** — `{YYYY-MM-DD}_{slug}` for genuinely one-off work (a repair, a
      recovery). Archived when done; never re-split.
    
    IDs (durable name or dated slug) are **immutable** once created — to rename, supersede.
    
    ## Task tree
    
    Tasks nest **physically** — a sub-task lives in its parent's `tasks/` dir. The parent
    is the containing directory; there is no `parent:` field. Every node that has children —
    plan or task — carries one generated children block indexing its **immediate** children
    only; deeper nodes are reached by descending, not by reading a recursive dump. Terminal
    children are counted in the block's footer rather than listed.
    
    ```text
    paper2/
      README.md                       # spec + children block (t03, …)
      tasks/
        t03-promote-h1-stage/
          README.md                   # frontmatter + Goal + acceptance + children block (t03.1, …)
          tasks/
            t03.1-add-dvc-stage/README.md
    ```
    
    - **IDs** are plan-scoped, two-digit, local-max+1 (`t03`; sub-tasks `t03.1`). Never
      hand-number — scaffold with the helper, which allocates the next free ID:
    
      ```bash
      just plan::task-new \
        .context/plan/paper2 promote-h1-stage -d "Promote H1 pilot into DVC" -s ready
      ```
    
    - IDs are the idempotent git handle: branch `paper2/t03-…`, commit `feat(paper2/t03): …`.
    
    ## Attachments
    
    A node's directory may carry attachment directories beside its `README.md`. The
    vocabulary is **closed at five names**:
    
    | Directory | Holds |
    | --- | --- |
    | `artifacts/` | outputs the node produced |
    | `evidence/` | proof that an acceptance criterion holds; immutable after the fact |
    | `figures/` | rendered images and diagrams |
    | `manifests/` | machine-readable inventories consumed by tooling |
    | `pilot/` | throwaway exploration kept for provenance — explicitly **not** evidence |
    
    1. **Attachments are content, never nodes.** No frontmatter, no `status`, never in a
       children block or the graph.
    2. **The five names are closed.** Wanting a sixth directory means the thing is really a
       node — scaffold it with `just plan::task-new`.
    3. **No loose non-`README` `.md` at a node root.** It belongs in one of the five.
    4. **Every attachment must be reachable from its owning README**, via `links:` or a
       prose link.
    
    Rule 4 buys one-directional enforcement, for free: `plan-graph` already fails an
    unresolvable `links:` path, and `docs links` already fails a dead prose link in any
    `.context/**/README.md`. So once the link exists, moving or deleting the attachment
    turns the tree red. Nothing detects a newly added *unlinked* file — and that is the
    intended consequence, not a hole to patch: an unlinked attachment is an orphan by
    definition, and orphans get deleted, not preserved.
    
    Gate reality, verified: a non-`README` `.md` under `.context/plan/` is held to rumdl
    style (with `MD013`/`MD041` disabled), `MD051`/`MD057` link checks, lychee, and the
    hygiene hooks — but **no** frontmatter schema, **no** `plan-graph`, and **no**
    `docs links`. Attachments are style-checked prose, not validated structure.
    
    Two deliberate exclusions, so they do not get "fixed": [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) and
    [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md) at the plan root are layer documentation, not
    attachments; and the loose `.md` files under `.archive/` stay exactly where they are —
    relocating historical evidence rewrites provenance for no benefit.
    
    ## Frontmatter
    
    Plans and tasks validate against their static document profiles under
    `infra/schemas/documents/`. Those profiles carry the same 8-value `status`
    contract; these definitions are binding for humans, validators, and
    structured-decoding loops.
    
    | Status | Use when | Class |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `draft` | Scope, requirements, or acceptance criteria are still forming; execution should not start. | Open, live |
    | `backlog` | Work is accepted and wanted but deliberately deferred beyond the current milestone; no unmet external dependency. Retain open acceptance and record the deferral reason. | Open, deferred |
    | `ready` | Specification and acceptance are complete, dependencies and authority are satisfied, and substantive execution has not begun. | Open, live |
    | `in-progress` | Substantive execution has begun and an acceptance criterion or non-terminal child remains. | Open, live |
    | `blocked` | A specific named dependency, external condition, or required authority prevents progress. Use `backlog` for priority deferral. | Open, live |
    | `done` | The deliverable and closure evidence are verified, every criterion still in final scope is complete, retired criteria are struck through with a disposition, and every immediate child is terminal. | Terminal, completed |
    | `closed` | Arbitration intentionally ends the work without claiming completion because it is no longer valuable, relevant, necessary, or worth pursuing. Record the reason and reopening condition; strike through retired criteria. | Terminal, discontinued |
    | `superseded` | A named successor, absorbing node, or binding decision replaced the work; retarget links. This is not evidence of completion. | Terminal, replaced |
    
    Status describes the node's present execution state, not its importance or archive
    location. Record backlog and blocked reasons in task scope or requirements. Terminal
    disposition lives in structured `resolution`; `closed` additionally records `reason` and
    `reopen_when`, while `superseded` records `reason` and `successor`. Reopening is a
    transition, not a ninth status: change the node to the appropriate open state, remove the
    terminal resolution, and restore only the criteria that have become active again.
    
    | Field         | Plan | Task | Notes                                                               |
    | ------------- | ---- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    | `type`        | req  | req  | path-checked assertion: `plan` or `task`; never a routing input       |
    | `description` | req  | req  | bounded discovery sentence; feeds generated rollups                  |
    | `status`      | req  | req  | lifecycle; the only place state lives                                |
    | `target`      | opt  | opt  | `YYYY-MM-DD`                                                         |
    | `depends_on`  | opt  | opt  | plan IDs or task IDs accepted by the graph gate                      |
    | `links`       | opt  | opt  | repository-relative evidence and implementation paths                |
    | `resolution`  | —    | terminal | dated disposition; extra fields required for `closed`/`superseded` |
    
    Not in frontmatter (git owns it): creation date (dir name), modification date, author.
    
    ## Body structure + style guide
    
    Human-readable and **skimmable** is the goal. Every README follows the same section
    order so agents parse uniformly and readers know where to look:
    
    1. **Goal** — one or two short paragraphs describing what done means.
    2. **Requirements** — optional numbered, testable statements.
    3. **Acceptance** — bounded `- [ ]` / `- [X]` criteria; this is where progress lives.
    4. **Out of scope** — optional explicit non-goals.
    5. **Children** — optional generated immediate-child rollup; never authored by hand.
    
    Leaf tasks may collapse to a short spec + acceptance boxes.
    
    **Checklists** — use **only** these markers (capital `X` for done):
    
    | Marker | Meaning |
    |---|---|
    | `- [ ] …` | open / not done |
    | `- [X] …` | done |
    | 2-space indent under an open `- [ ]` | sub-item of a still-open parent |
    
    Never `- [x]`, `- [~]`, `- [-]`, or emoji. For partial work: keep the **parent** open,
    mark completed **children** `[X]`. `ROADMAP.md` and durable plan roots are generated
    views only; executable gates belong in the owning task.
    
    ### Writing rules
    
    - **DRY** — state each fact once, in the node that owns it; elsewhere **link**
      (`[t03](tasks/t03-promote-h1-stage/README.md)`), don't restate. The generated children
      blocks are never copied by hand.
    - **Breadth vs depth** — a plan is broad and shallow (what + why + acceptance); a task is
      narrow and deep (exactly one change). Push detail *down* to the task, not into the plan.
    - **Succinct** — prefer a table or a checkbox to a paragraph; cut ceremony. If a sentence
      isn't a fact, a spec, or a link, it's probably noise.
    - **No status in prose** — never write what is currently being worked on, what the
      priority is, how far along something is, or a deadline restated from a `target`. Those
      are `status`/`target` frontmatter, rendered into the generated blocks. Prose that
      asserts a moment ("the current focus is…", "now blocked on…", "70% done") is stale on
      the next commit and nothing regenerates it. Write what is *true of the work* — the
      goal, the constraint, the verified fact with a `file:line` — and let the children
      blocks say when.
    - **Links & cross-references** — prose links are **doc-relative** (`../paper3/README.md`),
      never bare file/theorem names, so `grep` and the link-checker can traverse the graph.
      `links:` / `depends_on` carry the machine-readable edges.
    - **Headers** — the fixed section order above; keep headings short, no dated
      parentheticals (git has the date).
    
    ## Archive policy
    
    | Do | Don't |
    |---|---|
    | `git mv` under `.archive/` only after `done`/`closed`/`superseded` | Relocate for `ready` ↔ `in-progress` churn |
    | Keep the ID unchanged under `.archive/` | Rename a slug to "finish" without absorbing its claims |
    | On supersede, add `> Superseded {date} → [target](…).` banner | Leave hot links pointing at an emptied path |
    | Point `depends_on` at the **durable root** that absorbed the work | Depend on a superseded predecessor (or on yourself) |
    
    ## Validation
    
    The frontmatter is the source of truth; views and edges are derived and checked, never
    hand-maintained. Everything runs under `just check` (= `prek run --all-files`):
    
    | Hook | Guarantees |
    |---|---|
    | `schema-durable-plan-document` / `schema-dated-plan-document` | Closed plan frontmatter and body shape through native Schematter profiles |
    | `schema-task-document` / `schema-legacy-task-document` | Closed task frontmatter and body shape through native Schematter profiles |
    | `plan-graph` | Every edge resolves, terminal nodes have coherent children/active criteria, closed nodes carry dispositions, and completion prose agrees with child state |
    | `insitu-projections` | Every children region regenerated from frontmatter, one per node that has children — and only there: the writer adds a missing region and deletes one on a node whose children are gone |
    
    ```bash
    prek run --all-files       # all repository hooks
    just plan::graph           # sweep plan/task edges and lifecycle consistency
    just plan::board --write   # refresh every children block; takes no file arguments
    ```
    
    `just plan::board` walks the tree itself — `/ROADMAP.md`, `.archive/README.md`, and every
    node with a `tasks/` directory — so there is nothing to pass it and nothing to keep in
    sync by hand. The generated blocks are machine-written: **never edit one by hand**; edit
    frontmatter and let the hook regenerate.
    ## Working the plan layer
    
    Read [`README.md`](README.md) (structure + style) and [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md)
    (the why) first. This file is the operational checklist for agents editing plans/tasks.
    
    ## Process flow
    
    1. **Find the home.** Papers → `paper1`, `paper3`, `paper5`, or `paper6`;
       cross-cutting Lean → `proofs`, shared
       substrate/tooling → `infra-tooling`. One-off work → a new dated `{YYYY-MM-DD}_{slug}`
       plan. One concept per node — split, don't grow.
    2. **Add a task, don't hand-number.** Scaffold via the helper so IDs never collide:
    
       ```bash
       just plan::task-new \
         .context/plan/paper6 promote-h1-stage -d "Promote H1 pilot into the DVC graph" -s ready
       ```
    
       Point it at a plan dir for a top-level `tNN`, or at a task dir for a nested `tNN.M`.
    3. **Do the work**, updating the task README's acceptance checkboxes as you go.
    4. **Propagate state in the same turn.** Keep `status`, acceptance checkboxes, and the
       immediate parent's status consistent whenever work starts, blocks, defers, completes,
       closes, reopens, or is superseded. State changes are part of the work, not later cleanup.
    5. **Resolve honestly.** Use `done` only for verified completion. Use `closed` when
       arbitration intentionally discontinues work without completion; add structured
       `resolution.date`, `resolution.reason`, and `resolution.reopen_when`, then strike
       through each retired unchecked criterion. A superseded task instead names
       `resolution.successor`. Reopen by restoring the criterion, removing `resolution`, and
       selecting the appropriate open status.
    6. **Refresh views** — run once, at the end (see hard rules):
       `just plan::board --write`, then `just plan::graph`.
    
    ## Hard rules
    
    - **Never edit an `insitu:begin`/`insitu:end` region body by hand.** The children
      region on every node with children and other repository projections are generated.
      Edit frontmatter or the region's TOML header; let Insitu write the body.
    - **`prek run --all-files` skips untracked files.** Validate new, uncommitted plan/task
      files by running the schema/graph scripts directly on them, not via `just check`.
    - **Never run `just plan::board --write` or `just insitu::sync` from a subagent, or in parallel.** It takes no file
      arguments and walks the tree itself, rewriting every shared node with children
      (`/ROADMAP.md`, `.archive/README.md`, every plan README, every parent task) —
      concurrent runs race. The orchestrator runs it once, serially, after edits settle.
    - **Never `git commit` / `git push` / `git rm`.** Stage and edit only; humans commit.
      `git mv` is fine (non-destructive, reviewable).
    - **Python only via `uv run`** — never bare `python`/`pip`/`ruff`/`pytest`. Secrets via
      `secretspec run --profile mineru --reason "Purpose" -- …` (or profile `openrouter`).
    - **IDs and slugs are immutable** once created. To rename, supersede (new node +
      `status: superseded` on the old). Archiving changes only the parent folder.
    - **Attachments go in one of five directories, and must be linked.** `artifacts/`
      (outputs), `evidence/` (proof a criterion holds), `figures/` (rendered images),
      `manifests/` (machine-readable inventories), `pilot/` (throwaway exploration, not
      evidence). Never leave a non-`README` `.md` loose at a node root, and link every
      attachment from its owning README via `links:` or prose — an unlinked attachment is an
      orphan and gets deleted. The vocabulary is closed: wanting a sixth directory means the
      thing is a node, so scaffold it with `just plan::task-new`. See
      [`README.md`](README.md) § Attachments.
    - **Keep parents terse.** A parent owns purpose, binding decisions, constraints, and
      acceptance only. Put implementation detail and evidence in child nodes, then link;
      never duplicate child narratives. A node's generated children block is its status
      summary; the program-level one lives in [`/ROADMAP.md`](../../ROADMAP.md).
    - **Strikethrough is a disposition, not completion.** Use it only for an acceptance
      criterion removed by explicit arbitration, always with a reason. Do not turn an
      unfinished but still-wanted criterion into a struck item; use `backlog` or `blocked`.
      Write it as `- [ ] Retired: ~~criterion~~ — reason`: the lead-in is required
      because the task schema matches an item's first text node, so an item opening
      with `~~` presents as an empty checkbox and fails validation.
    - **Do not add freshness stamps by hand.** The graph gate validates semantic consistency
      across the whole tree, and the board gate deterministically regenerates every children
      block — adding one to a node that has just gained children, removing one from a node
      that has none.
    
    ## Branch / commit handles
    
    Task IDs are the idempotent handle for git:
    
    ```bash
    git checkout -b paper2/t03-promote-h1-stage
    git commit -m "feat(paper2/t03): wire H1 pilot into DVC graph"   # human runs this
    ```
    
    ## Parallel-edit safety (orchestrators)
    
    Fan out only over **disjoint plan folders** — agents writing different plans never
    conflict. Use plain `mv` (not `git mv`) inside agents to avoid index-lock races, and
    keep the single `plan/board`/`just check` pass for yourself at the end.

    description: "Reference packages with CSL frontmatter, source artifacts, and source-grounded lab notes."

    # Reference Papers
    
    Papers cited (or soon-to-be cited) in the project. Each subdirectory holds:
    
    - `README.md` — closed CSL-compatible YAML frontmatter plus repository
      `description`, `tags`, `cites`, and typed `relations`; the cite key/CSL `id` is
      derived from the directory and never authored
    - `raw/paper.pdf` — source PDF (when available)
    - `paper.md` — MinerU (or earlier) markdown conversion with LaTeX math
    - optional `chapters/` — per-chapter split for long textbooks
    
    Annotations in the tree come from each entry's `description` frontmatter field
    (kept short: *Author (year), purpose*).

    description: Locked planning and reference commands, independent of the Python application workspace.
    ---
    
    # Document workflows
    
    The root justfile exposes plan/task/reference creation, `sync` and `check`.
    These commands run this PEP 723 script with its pinned dependencies and sidecar
    `script.py.lock`; selecting workflows does not select the Python application example.
    
    `just setup` explicitly prepares the script environment and its native Insitu
    executable. Preparation changes only the installed executable in uv's disposable
    script environment, preserving shared package caches. Run setup again after
    clearing caches or changing dependencies. Ordinary commands use frozen, offline
    dependencies and never prepare native executables implicitly.
    
    Creation refuses existing destinations. Schematter validates document contracts;
    Insitu owns generated regions. `check` reports invalid records and stale views
    without repairing them. With references and LaTeX, `sync` derives the bibliography
    through Pandoc. Keep canonical metadata in the authored records.
    version = 1

    [% if 'planning' in workflows %]
    include = [".context/**/*.md", "ROADMAP.md"]
    [% else %]
    include = [".context/**/*.md"]
    [% endif %]
    respect_gitignore = true
    
    [paths]
    models = "insitu/models"
    templates = "insitu/templates"
    state = ".insitu/index.db"
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # Prepare ignored installed GNU/Linux executables without modifying uv caches.
    set -euo pipefail
    : "${PROJECT_RUNTIME_LINKER:?Enter the pinned devenv shell first}"
    : "${PROJECT_RUNTIME_LIBRARIES:?Enter the pinned devenv shell first}"
    for executable in "$@"; do
      [[ -f "$executable" ]] || continue
      interpreter=$(patchelf --print-interpreter "$executable" 2>/dev/null) || continue
      # Static executables and musl binaries do not use the GNU loader.
      [[ "$interpreter" == *ld-linux* ]] || continue
      rpath=$(patchelf --print-rpath "$executable")
      if [[ "$interpreter" == "$PROJECT_RUNTIME_LINKER" && "$rpath" == "$PROJECT_RUNTIME_LIBRARIES"* ]]; then
        continue
      fi
      temporary=$(mktemp "${executable}.XXXXXX")
      trap 'rm -f "$temporary"' EXIT
      cp --dereference --preserve=mode "$executable" "$temporary"
      chmod u+w "$temporary"
      patchelf --set-interpreter "$PROJECT_RUNTIME_LINKER" \
        --set-rpath "$PROJECT_RUNTIME_LIBRARIES${rpath:+:$rpath}" "$temporary"
      mv -f "$temporary" "$executable"
      trap - EXIT
      printf 'Prepared native runtime: %s\n' "$executable"
    done
    # schematter validates Markdown document shape; it is not in nixpkgs, so this
    # pins its release binaries rather than compiling it into every shell.
    # Bumping: change `version` and refresh each hash with
    # `nix store prefetch-file <release asset URL>`.
    {
      lib,
      stdenv,
      fetchurl,
      autoPatchelfHook,
    }:
    let
      version = "0.2.0";
      targets = {
        x86_64-linux = {
          target = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu";
          hash = "sha256-jgxWrmfWcL/7zJ7HwbFZ7hCKhtLaLeQgcVxs94u6Jdc=";
        };
        aarch64-linux = {
          target = "aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu";
          hash = "sha256-+7HwVHsgGz77l/AHscLxYnOzPagow/oDOArROuxHkng=";
        };
      };
      platform =
        targets.${stdenv.hostPlatform.system}
          or (throw "schematter: no release binary for ${stdenv.hostPlatform.system}");
    in
    stdenv.mkDerivation {
      pname = "schematter";
      inherit version;
      src = fetchurl {
        url = "https://github.com/iwe-org/schematter/releases/download/schematter-v${version}/schematter-v${version}-${platform.target}.tar.gz";
        inherit (platform) hash;
      };
      sourceRoot = ".";
      # The Linux binaries link glibc and libgcc_s from the build host.
      nativeBuildInputs = [ autoPatchelfHook ];
      buildInputs = [ stdenv.cc.cc.lib ];
      installPhase = ''
        install -Dm755 schematter "$out/bin/schematter"
      '';
      meta = {
        description = "Validator for Markdown document schemas";
        homepage = "https://github.com/iwe-org/schematter";
        license = lib.licenses.asl20;
        mainProgram = "schematter";
        platforms = builtins.attrNames targets;
      };
    }
    [% if 'lean' in languages and workflows %]
    {
      pkgs,

      lib,
      ...
    }:
    [% else %]
    { pkgs[% if 'lean' in languages %], inputs[% endif %][% if workflows %], lib[% endif %], ... }:
    [% endif %]
    {
