    # /// script
    # requires-python = ">=3.13,<3.14"
    # dependencies = ["insitu-cli==0.2.0rc2", "pyyaml==6.0.3"]
    # ///
    """Create project-owned plans and references; Insitu owns their derived views."""
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import argparse
    import json
    import os
    import re
    import subprocess
    import sys
    from dataclasses import dataclass
    from pathlib import Path
    from typing import Any
    from urllib.parse import unquote, urlsplit
    
    import yaml
    
    ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
    TERMINAL = ("done", "closed")
    SLUG = re.compile(r"[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\Z")
    CHILDREN_BLOCK = (
        '<!-- insitu:begin sql\nid = "planning-children"\nmodel = "children"\n'
        'template = "children.md.j2"\n-->\n<!-- insitu:end -->'
    )
    BACKLINKS_BLOCK = (
        '<!-- insitu:begin sql\nid = "reference-backlinks"\nmodel = "backlinks"\n'
        'template = "backlinks.md.j2"\n-->\n<!-- insitu:end -->'
    )
    
    
    class UniqueLoader(yaml.SafeLoader):
        """Reject repeated keys rather than silently changing canonical state."""
    
    
    def unique_mapping(
        loader: UniqueLoader, node: Any, deep: bool = False
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        result: dict[str, Any] = {}
        for key_node, value_node in node.value:
            key = loader.construct_object(key_node, deep=deep)
            if not isinstance(key, str) or key in result:
                raise ValueError(f"duplicate or non-string frontmatter key: {key!r}")
            result[key] = loader.construct_object(value_node, deep=deep)
        return result
    
    
    UniqueLoader.add_constructor(
        yaml.resolver.BaseResolver.DEFAULT_MAPPING_TAG, unique_mapping
    )
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class Record:
        path: Path
        data: dict[str, Any]
        body: str
        kind: str
    
    
    def config(root: Path = ROOT) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return yaml.load((root / ".copier-answers.yml").read_text(), Loader=UniqueLoader)
    
    
    def read_document(path: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str]:
        match = re.fullmatch(r"---\n(.*?)\n---(?:\n|\Z)(.*)", path.read_text(), re.DOTALL)
        if not match:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: expected YAML frontmatter")
        data = yaml.load(match[1], Loader=UniqueLoader)
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: frontmatter must be an object")
        return data, match[2]
    
    
    def path_kind(path: Path, root: Path) -> str | None:
        parts = path.relative_to(root).parts
        if len(parts) < 4 or parts[0] != ".context" or parts[-1] != "README.md":
            return None
        if parts[1] == "reference":
            return "reference" if len(parts) == 4 else None
        if parts[1] != "plan":
            return None
        if len(parts[3:-1]) % 2 or any(part != "tasks" for part in parts[3:-1:2]):
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: tasks must nest inside a parent's tasks/ directory")
        if any(not SLUG.fullmatch(part) for part in parts[2:-1:2]):
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: invalid plan/task slug")
        return "plan" if len(parts) == 4 else "task"
    
    
    def read_records(root: Path = ROOT) -> list[Record]:
        records = []
        for path in sorted((root / ".context").rglob("README.md")):
            kind = path_kind(path, root)
            if kind is not None:
                if path.is_symlink() or path.resolve() != path.absolute():
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"{path}: records must use regular files and directories"
                    )
                data, body = read_document(path)
                records.append(Record(path, data, body, kind))
        return records
    
    
    def verified_acceptance(body: str) -> bool:
        """Require checked, substantive criteria in the real Acceptance section."""
        fence: tuple[str, int] | None = None
        in_comment = False
        in_acceptance = False
        criteria: list[bool] = []
        for line in body.splitlines():
            marker = re.match(r"^[ \t]*(`{3,}|~{3,})(.*)$", line)
            if fence is not None:
                if (
                    marker
                    and marker[1][0] == fence[0]
                    and len(marker[1]) >= fence[1]
                    and not marker[2].strip()
                ):
                    fence = None
                continue
            if marker and not in_comment:
                fence = marker[1][0], len(marker[1])
                continue
            # Comments inside examples remain examples; only prose comments are hidden.
            while in_comment or "<!--" in line:
                start = 0 if in_comment else line.index("<!--")
                end = line.find("-->", start if in_comment else start + 4)
                if end < 0:
                    line = line[:start]
                    in_comment = True
                    break
                line = line[:start] + line[end + 3 :]
                in_comment = False
            heading = re.match(r"^ {0,3}(#{1,6})(?:[ \t]+(.*?)|[ \t]*)$", line)
            if heading:
                title = re.sub(r"[ \t]+#+[ \t]*$", "", heading[2] or "").strip()
                if len(heading[1]) <= 2:
                    if in_acceptance:
                        break
                    in_acceptance = len(heading[1]) == 2 and title == "Acceptance"
                continue
            if in_acceptance:
                criterion = re.match(
                    r"^\s*(?:[-+*]|\d{1,9}[.)])[ \t]+\[([ xX])\](?:[ \t]+(.*))?$", line
                )
                if criterion:
                    content = (criterion[2] or "").strip()
                    if content and not re.fullmatch(r"~~(?:(?!~~).)+~~", content):
                        criteria.append(criterion[1].lower() == "x")
        return bool(criteria) and all(criteria)
    
    
    def link_error(link: str, root: Path) -> str | None:
        """Keep declared edges identical to the paths queried by the SQL models."""
        guidance = (
            "use a plain repository-relative file path; put URLs and sections in body links"
        )
        try:
            parsed = urlsplit(link)
        except ValueError:
            return f"invalid link {link!r}; {guidance}"
        if parsed.scheme or parsed.netloc or not parsed.path:
            return f"invalid link {link!r}; {guidance}"
        try:
            target = (root / unquote(parsed.path).replace("\\", "/")).resolve()
            relative = target.relative_to(root.resolve()).as_posix()
        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError):
            return f"missing or escaping link {link!r}; {guidance}"
        if target.is_dir() and (target / "README.md").is_file():
            suggestion = "README.md" if relative == "." else relative + "/README.md"
            return f"link {link!r} names a directory; use {suggestion!r} instead"
        if not target.is_file():
            return f"missing or escaping link {link!r}; {guidance}"
        if link != parsed.path or link != relative:
            return f"noncanonical link {link!r}; use {relative!r} instead"
        return None
    
    
    def validate_records(root: Path, records: list[Record] | None = None) -> list[str]:
        """Check relationships after schema validation establishes field shapes."""
        records = read_records(root) if records is None else records
        errors = []
        by_path = {record.path: record for record in records}
        for record in records:
            label, data = record.path.relative_to(root), record.data
            errors.extend(
                f"{label}: {error}"
                for link in data.get("links", [])
                if (error := link_error(link, root))
            )
            if "id" in data or "csl" in data or "depends_on" in data:
                errors.append(
                    f"{label}: identity comes from paths; remove id, csl and depends_on"
                )
            if record.kind == "reference":
                continue
            if data.get("type") != record.kind:
                errors.append(f"{label}: type must assert path role {record.kind!r}")
            status = data.get("status")
            if (
                record.kind == "task"
                and record.path.parent.parent.parent / "README.md" not in by_path
            ):
                errors.append(f"{label}: containing plan/task is missing")
            children = [
                item
                for item in records
                if item.path.parent.parent == record.path.parent / "tasks"
            ]
            if status in TERMINAL and any(
                child.data.get("status") not in TERMINAL for child in children
            ):
                errors.append(f"{label}: terminal parent has open children")
            if status == "done" and not verified_acceptance(record.body):
                errors.append(
                    f"{label}: done requires nonempty active checked acceptance criteria"
                )
            if (
                status == "closed"
                and not data.get("resolution", {}).get("reason", "").strip()
            ):
                errors.append(f"{label}: closed requires resolution.reason")
            markers = re.findall(
                r'<!-- insitu:begin sql\s+id = "planning-children".*?<!-- insitu:end -->',
                record.body,
                re.DOTALL,
            )
            if len(markers) != 1:
                errors.append(f"{label}: restore exactly one planning-children region")
        return errors
    
    
    def run(root: Path, *command: str, **kwargs: Any) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        return subprocess.run(command, cwd=root, check=True, text=True, **kwargs)
    
    
    def schema_check(root: Path, records: list[Record]) -> None:
        schemas = root / "infra" / "schemas" / "documents"
        entries = [
            root / "README.md",
            root / ".context" / "README.md",
            *sorted((root / ".context").glob("*/README.md")),
        ]
        entries.extend(
            root / name
            for name in ("ROADMAP.md", "AGENTS.md", ".agents/AGENTS.md")
            if (root / name).is_file()
        )
        for schema, paths in (
            ("budget", entries),
            ("workitem", [item.path for item in records if item.kind != "reference"]),
            ("reference", [item.path for item in records if item.kind == "reference"]),
        ):
            if paths:
                run(
                    root,
                    "schematter",
                    "validate",
                    "--schema",
                    str(schemas / f"{schema}.document-schema.yaml"),
                    *map(str, paths),
                )
    
    
    def serialize(data: dict[str, Any], body: str) -> str:
        metadata = yaml.safe_dump(data, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True, width=88)
        return f"---\n{metadata}---\n\n{body.rstrip()}\n"
    
    
    def create_record(
        kind: str, slug: str, title: str, root: Path = ROOT, parent: str | None = None
    ) -> Path:
        workflow = "reference" if kind == "reference" else "planning"
        if workflow not in config(root)["workflows"]:
            raise ValueError(f"{workflow} is not selected")
        if not SLUG.fullmatch(slug):
            raise ValueError(
                "slug must use lowercase words, digits and single hyphens, "
                "starting with a letter"
            )
        if not title.strip() or "\n" in title or "\r" in title or len(title.strip()) > 160:
            raise ValueError("title must occupy one line with between 1 and 160 characters")
        title = title.strip()
        directory = (
            root / ".context" / ("reference" if kind == "reference" else "plan") / slug
        )
        if kind == "task":
            container = (root / (parent or "")).resolve()
            if container.name == "README.md":
                container = container.parent
            if not container.is_relative_to(root.resolve() / ".context" / "plan"):
                raise ValueError(
                    "parent must be an existing plan or task within .context/plan"
                )
            role = path_kind(container / "README.md", root)
            data, _ = read_document(container / "README.md")
            if (
                role not in {"plan", "task"}
                or data.get("type") != role
                or data.get("status") not in ("backlog", "in-progress", "blocked")
            ):
                raise ValueError("parent must be an open plan or task")
            directory = container / "tasks" / slug
        if not directory.resolve().is_relative_to(root.resolve()):
            raise ValueError("record destination escapes the repository")
        data = {
            "type": "document" if kind == "reference" else kind,
            "title": title,
            "description": title,
            "links": [],
        }
        body = f"# {title}\n\n"
        if kind != "reference":
            data["status"] = "backlog"
            body += f"## Goal\n\n{title}\n\n## Acceptance\n\n"
            body += (
                "- [ ] Define and verify the intended outcome.\n\n"
                + CHILDREN_BLOCK
                + "\n\n"
            )
        else:
            body += "Summarize the source and why it matters here.\n\n"
        body += "## Backlinks\n\n" + BACKLINKS_BLOCK
        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
        destination = directory / "README.md"
        with destination.open("x") as stream:
            stream.write(serialize(data, body))
        return destination
    
    
    def bibliography(root: Path, records: list[Record], *, check: bool) -> None:
        settings = config(root)
        if "reference" not in settings["workflows"] or "latex" not in settings["languages"]:
            return
        references = [
            record.data | {"id": record.path.parent.name}
            for record in records
            if record.kind == "reference"
        ]
        for item in references:
            item.pop("description", None)
            item.pop("links", None)
        expected = ""
        if references:
            expected = run(
                root,
                "pandoc",
                "--from",
                "csljson",
                "--to",
                "bibtex",
                input=json.dumps(references, ensure_ascii=False),
                capture_output=True,
            ).stdout
        destination = root / "src" / "latex" / "refs.bib"
        if destination.is_symlink() or destination.parent.resolve() != destination.parent:
            raise ValueError(
                "bibliography destination must use regular files and directories"
            )
        actual = destination.read_text() if destination.exists() else ""
        if actual != expected:
            if check:
                raise ValueError("src/latex/refs.bib is stale; run just sync")
            destination.write_text(expected)
    
    
    def insitu(root: Path, command: str) -> None:
        executable = Path(sys.executable).with_name("insitu")
        if not executable.is_file():
            raise ValueError("insitu is missing; run just setup")
        run(
            root,
            str(executable),
            command,
            env={**os.environ, "INSITU_PYTHON": sys.executable},
        )
    
    
    def main() -> int:
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
        for name in ("plan-new", "task-new", "reference-new"):
            command = commands.add_parser(name)
            if name == "task-new":
                command.add_argument("parent")
            command.add_argument("slug")
            command.add_argument("--title", required=True)
        for name in ("prepare", "sync", "check"):
            commands.add_parser(name)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        try:
            if args.command == "prepare":
                run(
                    ROOT,
                    "bash",
                    str(ROOT / "infra/nix/prepare-runtime.sh"),
                    str(Path(sys.executable).with_name("insitu")),
                )
            elif args.command.endswith("-new"):
                kind = args.command.removesuffix("-new")
                parent = getattr(args, "parent", None)
                print(create_record(kind, args.slug, args.title, parent=parent))
            else:
                records = read_records()
                schema_check(ROOT, records)
                errors = validate_records(ROOT, records)
                if errors:
                    raise ValueError("\n".join(errors))
                bibliography(ROOT, records, check=args.command == "check")
                insitu(ROOT, args.command)
        except (
            ValueError,
            OSError,
            yaml.YAMLError,
            subprocess.CalledProcessError,
        ) as error:
            print(f"workflow: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        return 0
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        raise SystemExit(main())

    title: Planning
    description: Project-owned plans and nested tasks with honest completion and local views.
    ---
    
    # Planning
    
    Create a plan, then its first task:
    
    ```bash
    just plan-new project "Project plan"
    just task-new .context/plan/project first-step "Make the first useful change"
    just sync
    ```
    
    The [root roadmap](../../ROADMAP.md) lists plans. Each plan or task shows only
    its immediate open children and counts terminal children. A deeper task lives
    in its parent's `tasks/SLUG/README.md`; its path supplies identity and parentage.
    Changing status never moves a file or breaks its links.
    
    Edit `status` in frontmatter: `backlog`, `in-progress`, `blocked`, `done` or
    `closed`. `done` requires at least one nonempty active acceptance criterion,
    all checked. Fenced examples and struck-through criteria do not count.
    `closed` stops work without claiming completion and requires `resolution.reason`.
    Terminal parents cannot retain open children. Reopen a parent before adding work.
    
    Every work item keeps one generated children region, including leaves. Edit
    outside the markers; `just sync` refreshes views, while `just check` reports
    invalid records or drift without repairing them. Put longer supporting detail
    in linked files rather than growing the 1,500-token entry point.

    ```bash
    just sync
    ```
    
    Each `KEY/README.md` owns flat CSL (Citation Style Language) metadata such as
    `type`, `title`, `author`, `issued`, `DOI` and `URL`, plus a local `description`
    and optional `links`. Its directory name is the citation key; never author an
    `id` or nested `csl` object. Edit the new record's metadata and body to explain

    key with `\citep{shannon1948}` in the manuscript. Edit records rather than the

    # CHANGELOG
    
    ## [PR #94](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/pricing-perspective/pull/94): JCOR estimation, architecture and JAX
    
    ### Added
    
    - Added empirical/FWL components and fit-owned linear/IV/GMM, GLM and panel
      estimation, inference and refit resampling; spatial likelihood/IV/GMM,
      diagnostics, impacts and balanced static panels with exogenous time-varying W.
    - Qualified standalone artifacts and matched statsmodels, linearmodels and spreg
      comparisons with opt-in reference dependencies.
    
    ### Changed
    
    - Organized public families with initializer docs, Tach boundaries, protocols and
      shape checks; separated GEL fitting/inference.
    - Added immutable JAX geometry, weighted unequal-support transport and checked
      solvers; migrated Hotelling numerics/shocks with float64 and Threefry ownership.
    - Integrated incoming designs, revised Paper 6 prose and replayed
      retained DVC/publications; consolidated Lean certification and Paper 6 inputs.
    
    ### Fixed
    
    - Corrected RBF derivatives, QR, GMV scaling and scientific prose; retained
      support-sensitive SLSQP and sampling schedules.
    - Recorded BF16 significance/equivalence changes versus archived FP32 separately
      from the JAX migration, preserving thresholds.
    
    ## [PR #95](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/pricing-perspective/pull/95): Paper 6 information recovery and MathEconLib integration
    
    ### Added
    
    - Added a resumable Paper 6 recovery study: 16 fixed news histories, 128 article
      redraws per history, common/changing reporting and 1x/4x/16x coverage, with
      saved provenance and audited checkpoints.
    - Added conditional operating-to-financial exposure bridges and explicit
      boundaries on covariance-envelope and spatial equivalence.
    - Integrated pinned MathEconLib game, probability and reporting-order adapters,
      including tied scores and reported observables, with compiled-statement,
      axiom and dependency audits in CI.
    
    ### Changed
    
    - Reworked Paper 6 around competitive adjustment, same-path valuation and
      reported information. Reconciled frozen directional estimates and retained
      their historical, conditional interpretation and identification limits.
    - Refreshed audited arXiv, Management Science and WFBS releases, recovery
      exhibits and other manuscripts' verification artifacts. Paper 3's authored
      chapters are unchanged.
    - Upgraded Lean/mathlib to 4.35.0 and consolidated recovery execution and
      publication under pipeline ownership, with Hotelling owning operating,
      valuation and reporting primitives.
    
    ### Removed
    
    - Retired superseded Paper 6 simulation/publication branches, commands, DVC
      stages and exhibits.
    - Retired historical context executables and unused replay/writer code while
      retaining scientific records, source identities and integrity audits.
    
    ### Fixed
    
    - Preserved subnormal covariance targets at JCOR's zero-weight shrinkage
      endpoint, with float32/float64 regressions and unchanged kernel derivatives.
    - Repaired DVC source hashing and merged task IDs; moved oversized evidence to
      DVC and verified empty-cache retrieval.
    
    ## [PR #76](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/pricing-perspective/pull/76): Public portfolio synchronization
    
    ### Changed
    
    - Synced the TypeScript workspace from public PricingPerspective revision
      `33b64a0`, including the hydrographic visual identity, new research notes and
      narration assets, mathematical typesetting, and updated site metadata.
    - Removed the constellation component, story, and social cards retired upstream.
    
    ## [PR #66](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/pricing-perspective/pull/66): JFDS revision and spatial-risk validation
    
    ### Added
    
    - Added outcome-free annual ChronoBERT parquets with pinned inference,
      deterministic selection, raw masked pooling and completion provenance;
      verified 2017–2024 on the unchanged 100-firm, 128-article sample.
    - Added Paper 1's JFDS target, response letter and audited bundles.
    - Added sector/industry matching, firm effects, within-industry and Hoberg--Phillips
      ETNIC comparisons; archived common-sample extract/crosswalk provenance/checksums.
    - Added a Lean residual-variance bridge from total-return distance to systematic
      transport excess; retained covariance theorems and extended claim bindings.
    - Added Paper 5 economic-value/spatial Ledoit--Wolf and Paper 3 portfolio evidence
      under formation/evaluation contracts.
    
    ### Changed
    
    - Replaced EttaX arms with annual ChronoBERT; recomputed paired contrasts and
      2017 pre-period sensitivity, retaining base results and bootstrap schedules.

    ---
    description: "Canonical static document schemas consumed directly by Schematter and prek without a repository-local compiler."
    ---
    
    # Static document schemas
    
    `documents/` contains the canonical Schematter profiles for repository Markdown.
    They are authored and reviewed as data, then consumed directly by the nested and
    root prek hooks.
    
    ```bash
    schematter validate \
      --schema infra/schemas/documents/readme.document-schema.yaml \
      README.md
    just references::structure
    ```
    
    There is no compile step. Change the affected static profile and run its consuming
    hook. Runtime JSON contracts remain beside the Python code that owns them.

    # Document schemas
    
    `just check` selects a schema by each record's path. Plans and tasks share one
    work-item contract; their `type` must assert the physical role. References use
    flat CSL metadata, with their citation key derived from their directory name.
    
    Entry points and records have a 1,500-token budget. Keep supporting detail in
    linked files beside the owning record. Schematter checks document shape; the
    workflow helper checks containment, links and honest completion.

            if (result.returncode == 0) != success:
                raise AssertionError(result.stdout + result.stderr)
            return result

            just("task-new", ".context/plan/workflow-probe", "first-step", "Validate task creation")

    version = 1
    
    [sources]

    [paths]

    ---
    description: Locked planning and reference commands, independent of the Python application workspace.
    ---
    
    # Document workflows
    
    The root justfile exposes plan/task/reference creation, `sync` and `check`.
    These commands run this PEP 723 script with its pinned dependencies and sidecar
    `script.py.lock`; selecting workflows does not select the Python application example.
    
    `just setup` explicitly prepares the script environment and its native Insitu
    executable. Preparation changes only the installed executable in uv's disposable
    script environment, preserving shared package caches. Run setup again after
    clearing caches or changing dependencies. Ordinary commands use frozen, offline
    dependencies and never prepare native executables implicitly.
    
    Creation refuses existing destinations. Schematter validates document contracts;
    Insitu owns generated regions. `check` reports invalid records and stale views
    without repairing them. Local reference records stay in the ignored `.context/reference/` directory.
    Their backlinks do not appear in versioned plans. The manuscript bibliography
    is authored independently so checkout validation needs no local references.
    ---
    description: Small SQL queries and templates for views beside their source records.
    ---
    
    # Derived views
    
    `just sync` refreshes these views; `just check` rejects stale output. The ignored
    SQLite index is disposable. Frontmatter and authored bodies remain canonical;
    Insitu owns only the regions between its markers.
    
    The reference index lists immediate records. Each plan exposes immediate tasks;
    the root roadmap lists plans. Terminal work is counted rather than copied into
    every parent. Reading deeper means following one child link, keeping context small.
    
    Backlinks derive from explicit canonical repository-relative file paths in `links`.
    Use a full file path without `./`, traversal, URL encoding, queries or fragments.
    Body links retain ordinary URL and section syntax.
    
    SQL and templates describe project policy; Insitu supplies the independent query
    and materialization engine. Work items always contain one children region, so
    synchronization never inserts or removes record structure.
    ---
    title: Project context
    description: Plans, nested tasks and local literature records.
    ---
    
    # Project context
    
    [Planning](plan/README.md) holds versioned plans and nested tasks. The root
    [roadmap](../ROADMAP.md) lists their immediate children. Schematter validates
    document contracts; Insitu generates child views and backlinks.
    
    `.context/reference/` holds local bibliographic records and source material.
    The entire directory is ignored by Git. Create a record with
    `just reference-new KEY TITLE`; its README owns flat CSL metadata and source
    notes. Local reference records are validated when present but are not required
    for a fresh checkout. The manuscript's `src/latex/refs.bib` remains authored
    and versioned independently.
    
    Edit record frontmatter and prose outside generated regions. Run `just sync`
    to refresh views and `just context-check` to validate them without repairs.
    Reference backlinks stay local; versioned plans must remain understandable
    without the local literature folder. Cite public sources directly in plan prose.
    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    set positional-arguments
    
    mod python 'src/python/justfile'
    mod latex 'src/latex/justfile'
    workflow := "env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py"
    
    # Discover this project's commands.
    default:
        @just --list
    
    # Prepare locked dependencies and Git hooks (uses the network).
    setup:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py prepare
        just python::setup
        just latex::setup
        prek install
    
    # Check source, views and selected languages without repairing files.
    check:
        bash infra/nix/check.sh
        {{ workflow }} check
        just python::check
        just latex::check
        just data-check
        just changelog-check
    
    
    # Run the selected language tests.
    test:
        just python::test
        just latex::test
    
    # Explicitly format sources.
    fmt:
        nixfmt devenv.nix infra/nix/devenv.nix infra/nix/pkgs/schematter.nix
        rumdl fmt .
        just python::fmt
        just latex::fmt
    
    # Check external links online.
    links:
        git ls-files -z '*.md' | xargs -0 -r lychee --config lychee.toml --no-progress
    
    # Run root-level DVC using the locked Python environment.
    dvc *args:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen dvc "$@"
    
    # Validate DVC metadata without fetching data.
    data-check:
        just dvc status
        just dvc dag
    
    # Refresh generated planning and reference views.
    sync:
        {{ workflow }} sync
    
    # Validate document schemas, links and generated views.
    context-check:
        {{ workflow }} check
    
    # Create a plan without overwriting existing content.
    plan-new slug title:
        {{ workflow }} plan-new "$1" --title "$2"
    
    # Create a task inside an existing plan or task.
    task-new parent slug title:
        {{ workflow }} task-new "$1" "$2" --title "$3"
    
    # Create a local reference record with its directory as citation key.
    reference-new key title:
        {{ workflow }} reference-new "$1" --title "$2"
    
    # Validate the repository changelog structure and change categories.
    changelog-check:
        schematter validate --schema infra/schemas/documents/changelog.document-schema.yaml CHANGELOG.md

    # Fine News Financial Publishers
    
    Tools for cleaning and enriching the monthly financial news Parquet shards in
    this repository. `data/00_raw/domains.csv` records the acquisition allowlist.
    The raw article source is upstream Fine News; publisher- and
    language-filtered shards live in `data/01_intermediate/YYYY-MM/eng_Latn/`.
    Cleaned records belong in `data/02_primary/`, with derived attributes in
    `data/03_feature/`. Generated primary/feature files and `outputs/` are ignored;
    the intermediate shards stay tracked with Git LFS. See [data stages](data/README.md).
    
    ## Development
    
    Use Linux x86-64 or ARM64 with Nix and Git LFS installed:
    
    ```bash
    bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh
    devenv shell
    just setup
    just check
    ```
    
    The environment pins Python 3.13, uv, Git LFS, Ruff and Pyrefly. Setup installs the
    locked Python workspace and repository-local pre-commit hooks. `hf` is available
    through `cd src/python && uv run --frozen hf --help`.
    
    ## Restore data from the Hugging Face cache
    
    After an `hf download marcusinthesky/fine-news-financial-publishers --type dataset`,
    reuse its cache without another download:
    
    ```bash
    just data-restore --dry-run
    just data-restore
    ```
    
    The helper checks every indexed LFS object's cached size, copies each blob into
    `.git/lfs/objects` with `cp --reflink=auto`, verifies SHA256, and runs the offline
    `git lfs checkout`. Reflinks share disk blocks when supported and keep the cache
    independent from working files; other filesystems fall back to copying. Checkout
    preserves locally modified data. The helper honors `HF_HOME` and `HF_HUB_CACHE`,
    or accepts `--cache-dir /path/to/datasets--owner--repo` (the directory containing
    `blobs/`). `--dry-run` checks availability and sizes without hashing or writing.
    No cache files are moved, changed or deleted. Incomplete blobs fail explicitly.
    It follows the Git index, so staged shard renames are restored at their new paths.
    
    If the cache is missing files, fetch those through `hf download` first, or use
    `git lfs pull` to download the missing LFS objects from the configured remote.
    
    ## Build intermediate data
    
    The concise [acquisition pipeline](data/00_raw/README.md) reads the pinned Fine
    News revision through DuckDB's `hf://` support, filters by the 115-domain CSV and
    English capture paths, and writes the original monthly shard layout.
    
    ```bash
    just python::run intermediate build --month 2016-08 --dry-run
    just python::run intermediate build --month 2016-08 --output .tmp/intermediate-trial
    ```
    
    Omit `--month` for all English capture months. This requires network access.
    The default output is `data/01_intermediate`; existing shard paths are refused.
    Use a fresh directory for a rebuild.
    
    ## Clean and enrich
    
    Run from the repository root inside `devenv shell`:
    
    ```bash
    just python::run intermediate inspect
    just python::run primary build data/01_intermediate/2016-08/eng_Latn/part-000000.parquet --output data/02_primary/2016-08.parquet
    just python::run feature build data/02_primary/2016-08.parquet --output data/03_feature/2016-08.parquet
    ```
    
    The Typer root attaches separate `intermediate`, `primary` and `feature` command
    modules. Each stage supports `inspect` and `build`.
    The former top-level `inspect` and `clean` commands are replaced by these stage
    commands. Pass `.` to `intermediate inspect` to discover the intermediate shards
    from the repository root. Repository-root scans exclude generated stages. Polars uses lazy scans and a
    streaming Parquet sink. Cleaning preserves original text, IDs and metadata,
    adds whitespace-normalized `clean_text`, and drops null or blank articles.
    Enrichment adds character and word counts, the lowercased publisher hostname
    (with an initial `www.` removed), publication date and source file path.
    Invalid dates become null. Output creation refuses to overwrite existing files.
    These cleaning stages do not deduplicate or resolve entities. The separate
    [company tagging pipeline](src/python/apps/fine_news_cli/docs/company-tagging.md)
    extracts candidate companies and evidence; its completed 14.81M-row run and
    the Nasdaq coverage comparison are documented alongside the command.
    
    All Python workflows live in the `fine-news` Typer application; see
    [Python](src/python/README.md).
    Explore the historical candidate comparison in the
    [marimo notebooks](src/python/notebooks/candidate_datasets/README.md).
    Run `just fmt` to format and `just check` to lint, typecheck, test and build.
    
    ## Template updates
    
    This project adopts [Exordio](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/template) from the
    local `~/Git/template` checkout, pinned in `.copier-answers.yml`. Commit local
    work before using Copier 9.16.0 to update; review conflicts in the renamed
    Python packages and project documentation. The existing LFS attributes are
    project-owned and must be preserved when merging template updates.
    
    The configured `origin` is the Hugging Face dataset repository. The included
    GitHub Actions workflow is ready for a GitHub remote; publishing is separate.
    # Architecture
    
    The raw source is upstream Fine News, pinned by `_filter_config.json`.
    `data/00_raw/domains.csv` is the acquisition allowlist. The intermediate builder
    uses a short parameterized DuckDB SQL query over `hf://` files, selecting English
    paths and retaining only text, IDs and metadata. It preserves the original
    Colab hostname predicate, without the Drive/quota/resume runtime machinery. Monthly
    publisher- and language-filtered shards live under
    `data/01_intermediate/YYYY-MM/eng_Latn/`, tracked with Git LFS. Hugging Face's
    README configuration selects only these shards for the default dataset split.
    
    `data/02_primary` holds cleaned articles; `data/03_feature` holds enriched
    records. Each directory retains a tracked `.gitkeep`, with generated contents
    ignored. Model-input and later stages are deferred until their contracts exist.
    See [data stages](data/README.md) for current transformations and boundaries.
    
    The `fine-news` Typer application owns the data workflows and transformations
    under `src/python/apps/fine_news_cli`. Its root registers `intermediate`,
    `primary`, `feature`, `eval` and `company` command groups. Intermediate building
    queries the upstream files, while inspection reads the
    filtered shards; primary building cleans text; feature building derives the existing
    publisher/date/count attributes. Scans preserve `source_path` lineage across
    stages and repository-root scans select only intermediate inputs.
    
    Tests cover the stage workflow, whitespace, missing values, enrichment, LFS
    pointer detection, source lineage and overwrite protection. Lazy scans and
    streaming writes support both single-shard trials and the full intermediate set.
    
    The standalone `scripts/restore-lfs-cache.py` uses Python's standard library,
    Git LFS and GNU cp. It seeds verified objects from existing Hugging Face cache
    blobs without network requests. It reads LFS paths from the index so staged
    renames are respected during checkout. Independent reflinks protect the cache from
    working file edits; checksum verification precedes checkout.
    
    Devenv pins system tools in `devenv.lock`; `src/python/uv.lock` pins Python
    runtime, build and test dependencies. Setup prepares dependencies and local Git
    hooks. Formatting is explicit; checks do not repair tracked source files.
    
    The project was rendered from `~/Git/template` with Copier 9.16.0, selecting only
    Python. `.copier-answers.yml` records the source revision. The package names,
    project documentation and original LFS attributes are project customizations;
    review these when merging a template update.
    # Data stages
    
    The raw source is `ksolovev/fine-news` at the revision recorded in
    [`_filter_config.json`](../_filter_config.json). [00_raw](00_raw/README.md) records the domain allowlist used to query that
    source. The full upstream raw corpus is not duplicated locally.
    
    | Stage | Contents | Git policy |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `00_raw/` | Domain CSV used by the acquisition query; raw articles remain upstream | Tracked text inputs |
    | `01_intermediate/YYYY-MM/eng_Latn/` | Publisher and English-language filtered shards, preserving upstream text, IDs and metadata | Tracked with Git LFS |
    | `02_primary/` | Cleaned article records, retaining original fields and source lineage | Generated files ignored; `.gitkeep` tracked |
    | `03_feature/` | Primary records enriched with derived attributes | Generated files ignored; `.gitkeep` tracked |
    
    Numbering begins at `00_raw`. Model input, models and reporting stages can be
    introduced when they have a concrete consumer and data contract.
    
    ## Current transformations
    
    `fine-news intermediate build` runs a short DuckDB `hf://` query on the pinned
    upstream revision, selects English capture paths and filters by
    [the domain CSV](00_raw/domains.csv). It retains `text`, `id` and `metadata` and
    preserves monthly shard paths. See [acquisition inputs](00_raw/README.md) for
    reproduction and the differences from the original Colab runtime.
    
    `fine-news primary build` normalizes whitespace into `clean_text` and removes
    blank articles. It does not deduplicate, assign new IDs or resolve company
    memberships. These remain future primary-stage work.
    
    `fine-news feature build` adds publisher hostname, publication date, character
    count and word count. It retains the primary record and original `source_path`.
    Publication dates that cannot be parsed become null. No embedding or model
    features are computed yet. Both builders refuse to overwrite existing outputs.
    
    ## Commands
    
    Run from the repository root inside `devenv shell`:
    
    ```bash
    just python::run intermediate build --month 2016-08 --dry-run
    just python::run intermediate inspect
    just python::run primary build
    just python::run feature build
    ```
    
    The default builders process their entire preceding stage. For a small trial:
    
    ```bash
    just python::run primary build data/01_intermediate/2016-08/eng_Latn/part-000000.parquet --output data/02_primary/2016-08.parquet
    just python::run feature build data/02_primary/2016-08.parquet --output data/03_feature/2016-08.parquet
    ```
    
    After setup, commands use frozen dependencies. Inspection and primary/feature
    builds operate offline; remote intermediate acquisition requires network access. Use `--help` on
    any stage to see its commands. Derived files stay local until their versioning
    and publication policies are explicitly defined.
    # Raw acquisition inputs
    
    [domains.csv](domains.csv) is the exact 115-hostname allowlist used by the
    original Colab publisher filter. It contains domains rather than individual
    article URLs. Matching includes each listed host and its subdomains, preserving
    specific hosts such as `fortune.cnn.com` without admitting all of `cnn.com`.
    
    The article source remains upstream `ksolovev/fine-news`, pinned to commit
    `7a841090e69f3c58a9e04b0c39213d879af68e8a` in
    [`_filter_config.json`](../../_filter_config.json). Raw article/media files are
    queried remotely and are not duplicated in this directory. The CSV is the
    builder's filter input; the root JSON records the historical dataset filter.
    
    Run from the repository root inside `devenv shell`:
    
    ```bash
    just python::run intermediate build --month 2016-08 --dry-run
    just python::run intermediate build --month 2016-08 --output .tmp/intermediate-trial
    ```
    
    Omit `--month` to select all English capture months. Without `--output`, the
    builder targets `data/01_intermediate`; it refuses any existing destination
    shard before scanning articles. Use a fresh output directory for a rebuild.
    `--source` accepts an explicit `hf://` or local glob with the same
    `YYYY-MM/eng_Latn/*.parquet` layout; `--domains` selects another domain CSV.
    
    The builder runs the [filter SQL](../../src/python/apps/fine_news_cli/src/fine_news_cli/intermediate/filter.sql.j2)
    once per source shard and retains its month/language/filename layout. It
    prefers nonblank `metadata.url_hostname`, falling back to the URL hostname,
    then normalizes case, whitespace and trailing dots. It projects only `text`,
    `id` and `metadata`, excluding separate media columns. Text, IDs and metadata
    values are retained; row ordering and encoded Parquet bytes need not match.
    
    This is the Colab filtering operation without Google Drive mounting, runtime
    package installation, quota monitoring or resume machinery. DuckDB uses two
    threads, a 2 GiB memory limit, a 4 GiB spill limit and Zstandard level 9, as in
    the original. Completed shards are published atomically; failed temporary files
    are removed. A later failure can leave earlier completed shards in place.
    
    The dependency environment can be prepared with `just setup`. Remote builds and
    remote dry runs need network access; a dry run only lists paths. DuckDB installs
    and loads its `httpfs` extension on first remote use. Local source globs work
    offline and are used by the regression tests.
    # Universe Metadata
    
    The company research inputs are [nasdaq_100.csv](nasdaq_100.csv) and
    [gawronsky_huang_2026.csv](gawronsky_huang_2026.csv). See the
    [company reference notes](company_references.README.md) for their constituent
    windows, SEC and Wikipedia descriptions, aliases, access dates and provenance.
    
    ## Free Foundations top 1,000
    
    [Issuer descriptions](free_foundations_us_top_1000.csv), the
    [security-year membership panel](free_foundations_us_top_1000_membership.csv),
    and [provenance](free_foundations_us_top_1000.provenance.json) are a preliminary
    research snapshot. The panel has 1,000 December-ranked securities per effective
    year from 2002 through 2025. The source archive has no December 2000 observation;
    2026 is outside its study window. Issuers are grouped by PERMCO and CIK, with
    unresolved identities kept separate. Candidate links are not verified identity
    evidence. SEC and Wikipedia descriptions are not complete or all reviewed.
    
    The issuer CSV contains multiline source text and JSON-encoded lists. Read CIKs
    as strings to preserve leading zeros. SEC descriptions are source text, not
    generated summaries. Wikipedia text is attributed to the contributors at its
    linked permanent revision and is available under
    [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Latest-access
    descriptions, names and aliases are not point-in-time historical features.
    
    To validate the snapshot and attempt conservative recovery, with the pinned
    Free Foundations archive available at `~/Git/free-foundations/research/crsp-study`:
    
    ```sh
    src/python/.venv/bin/python src/python/scripts/recover_universe.py
    EDGAR_IDENTITY='Your Name your.email@example.com' \
      src/python/.venv/bin/python src/python/scripts/recover_universe.py --network
    ```
    
    Use `--archive` to select another copy of the same archive; its four prepared
    inputs must match the recorded hashes. The script uses the workspace's Polars
    installation. Requests are disabled unless `--network` is supplied, SEC requests
    also require `EDGAR_IDENTITY`, and a failed host is skipped for the rest of that
    run. Successful network responses and a review queue are saved under the ignored
    `.tmp/universe-recovery/` directory; reruns reuse cached successes. Output CSVs
    must match the provenance hashes before updates are made.
    Use `--source sec` or `--source wikipedia` to retry one source independently;
    `--workers` controls concurrency while all requests share the rate limit.
    
    The recovery pass only promotes a candidate when the pinned crosswalk already
    has matching, dated, verified SEC evidence. It extracts unambiguous 10-K Item 1
    boundaries as **unreviewed**, and accepts a Wikipedia match only when its
    Wikidata item supplies the same CIK. It does not yet discover new historical
    identities, extract other SEC forms, or resolve ambiguous boundaries and pages;
    those cases remain in the queue for later research. The latest run's status
    counts and access failures are in `.tmp/universe-recovery/last_run.json`.
    # Full-corpus company candidates
    
    The production CPU runner tags every source row with candidate companies from
    the annual US top-1000 panel and the fixed Gawronsky–Huang roster. It extracts
    mentions and publisher evidence; it does not claim substantive relevance,
    primary-company truth or calibrated probabilities.
    
    Install the [CPU extra](company-cpu.md) before running from the repository root
    inside the development environment:
    
    ```sh
    src/python/.venv/bin/python -m fine_news_cli company tag-corpus
    ```
    
    Defaults are six processes, one native thread per process, 128 input rows per
    batch, and compressed Parquet output chunks of 8,192 rows. The default run first
    processes a 100,000-row pilot distributed proportionally across source files,
    then continues to the full corpus. Both stages enforce an 8 GiB combined process
    memory ceiling. Pilot ranges are deterministic contiguous ranges for bounded
    Parquet reads, not a random sample suitable for prevalence inference. Reported
    throughput includes source reads, matching and durable output; preflight source
    hashing and final reports are separate.
    
    The initial successful 100,000-row pilot covered all 168 local files and took
    13.0 seconds (about 7,700 rows/second), with 3.3 GiB peak combined resident memory.
    The reader uses a 512 MiB DuckDB budget per process; the aggregate ceiling also
    accounts for Python objects and output buffers. All 322 CLI tests passed before
    the production run. The optimized matcher produced identical evidence on all
    2,000 checked raw rows,
    and its cased projection matched the frozen policy on all 1,135 clean supported
    evaluation rows.
    
    ## Completed production run
    
    The 2026-11-04 run completed all **14,807,287 source rows in 168 files** with
    exit code zero. Processing took **1,643 seconds (27 minutes 23 seconds)**,
    averaging **9,012 articles/second**, including source reads, matching and durable
    writes. Preflight hashing and final report generation are outside that timing.
    Peak combined process-tree resident memory was **7,533,608,960 bytes (7.02 GiB)**,
    below the 8 GiB guard. Six CPU workers ran on the Ryzen 5 9600X; the GPU was not
    used. No per-core utilization trace was collected, so these measurements do not
    establish exact CPU saturation.
    
    | Universe | Source rows with candidates | Rows with cased name evidence | Rows with publisher evidence |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | Annual US top-1000 | 12,159,551 | 8,365,194 | 512,169 |
    | Fixed GH roster | 3,764,426 | 1,569,478 | 139,298 |
    
    Evidence categories overlap. Candidates include ambiguous and lowercase aliases;
    these counts are not estimates of substantive coverage, precision or recall.
    The independent [2,000-row prevalence audit](company-prevalence.md) addresses
    substantive coverage with a different procedure and remains provisional.
    
    The committed [findings snapshot](company-tagging-findings.json) retains run
    metrics, contract and artifact fingerprints, the GH minimum, and the Nasdaq
    comparison below. Generated predictions remain in the local output directory.
    
    Use `--phase preflight`, `--phase pilot` or `--phase run` for individual stages.
    Use `--resume` to verify and continue a run. `--limit` restricts the processing
    frame in source-file order for development. Configuration, registry, code,
    dependencies and source fingerprints must match the frozen manifest on resume.
    
    ## Evidence and identities
    
    One Rust Aho–Corasick DFA searches the union of registry names and aliases.
    Extended legal suffixes follow the existing tested policy, with separate alias
    ownership and overlap selection for each universe. Publication year controls
    top-1000 eligibility; the GH roster is fixed across years. Current registry
    names and fixed GH ticker spellings are not certified historical identities.
    
    Rows retain all candidate companies. Single-token lowercase matches, shared
    aliases, ambiguous symbols and incomplete catalogs have explicit flags.
    `cased_name_match_count` distinguishes evidence that survives the tested case
    policy; lowercase evidence remains available rather than becoming a negative.
    Neither a complete catalog nor a no-candidate result proves irrelevance.
    
    Publisher exchange annotations, cashtags and conservative standalone ticker
    tags are extracted separately. Explicit annotations are masked in the name
    matching view. Ordinary prose and complete company names remain intact; the
    evaluation sanitizer that could remove parts of company names is not applied.
    No bare ticker search is added to prose unless that spelling already appears
    as a catalog name or alias. Publisher evidence is unverified and must not be
    used as independent evaluation truth for predictions derived from that evidence.
    
    Top-1000 issuer IDs are `top1000:PERMCO`; GH IDs are `gh:CIK` with padded CIKs.
    Their identities remain separate, including when a company belongs to both.
    The output retains catalog CIK link status without inferring a crosswalk.
    Tickers are labels from the relevant catalog, not additional issuer identities.
    
    ## Output and recovery
    
    The destination defaults to `data/02_primary/company_tags/dfa-v1/`:
    
    - `manifest.json` freezes source SHA-256 fingerprints and the run contract.
    - `shards/NNNNN/part-NNNNN.parquet` stores every source row with native nested
      candidate/evidence structs. Each source directory has a `completed.json`.
    - `pilot/` contains separate pilot predictions and timing.
    - `progress.jsonl` records progress, resource observations and failures.
    - `summary.json` reconciles rows and counts by year, universe and evidence.
    - `company-year-counts.csv` counts candidate and publisher-supported source rows.
    - `gh-company-year-2018-2022.csv` includes zero-count cells for all GH companies;
      `gh-floor-2018-2022.json` identifies the minimum candidate count and ties.
    
    Read production predictions with `shards/*/part-*.parquet`; a recursive glob over
    the entire run directory would also include the separate pilot predictions.
    For the launched background run, `background-job.json` and `worker-process.json`
    identify the processes, `runner.log` captures errors, and `background-exit.json`
    records the eventual exit code. A final `summary.json` with `status=complete`
    confirms successful processing and report generation.
    
    `row_key` hashes the relative source path and zero-based physical row number.
    Original article IDs remain nullable and are not assumed unique. Duplicate or
    syndicated source rows are retained. Article text is not copied into outputs.
    Each candidate has full occurrence counts and at most four representative spans
    per field; offsets describe the NFKC/casefold matching view, not raw text.
    
    Workers commit a source directory atomically after row-count reconciliation and
    durable writes. Incomplete `.partial` source directories are rebuilt on resume.
    Completed chunks are checksum-verified and reused; corruption or changed inputs
    causes an error. Source failures prevent successful completion. An output lock
    prevents concurrent writers. A failed row is never silently dropped.
    
    Company-year counts describe source rows with candidate evidence, not unique
    stories or adjudicated substantive company coverage. In particular, the GH
    candidate floor is not a validated academic coverage floor.
    
    ## GH annual floor and Nasdaq comparison
    
    Across the fixed 100-company GH roster and the five publication years 2018–2022,
    the minimum among all 500 company-year cells is **CDNS in 2018: 16 candidate
    source rows**. Fifteen have cased company-name evidence and two have publisher
    ticker evidence; one row has both. None of the 500 candidate cells is zero.
    These source rows have not been deduplicated or adjudicated for substantive
    company coverage.
    
    The local `pricing-perspective` Nasdaq archive is a separately acquired,
    ticker-directed source. Its `main` revision
    `c8a4bd69cf26c87163d5db3c0a2de7b0d8b14cef` documents collection through
    `api.nasdaq.com/api/news/topic/articlebysymbol` in December 2022–January 2023.
    The immutable raw archive contains 397,041 rows; the current normalized local
    artifact contains 214,480 records across 100 symbols. Its global article-ID
    deduplication keeps one scrape-symbol assignment, potentially losing other
    article–symbol memberships. Nasdaq assignments and our extracted candidates
    therefore measure different things.
    
    | Publication year | Nasdaq normalized CDNS records | Fine News CDNS candidates | Fine News Nasdaq-hosted rows, all companies |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | 2018 | 123 | 16 | 0 |
    | 2019 | 97 | 126 | 74,258 |
    | 2020 | 69 | 275 | 212,834 |
    | 2021 | 57 | 134 | 174,027 |
    | 2022 | 381 | 314 | 241,988 |
    
    There are also 123 distinct CDNS article IDs in the raw Nasdaq archive for 2018,
    so deduplication does not explain that year's 123-versus-16 difference. The
    historical `annual_raw_article_floor: 47` admission rule precedes normalization;
    it is not a guaranteed deduplicated annual floor. The realized normalized
    archive's minimum is SNPS in 2018 with 34 records. Its documented minimum of
    449 per ticker concerns the entire recovered history, rather than one year.
    
    The Fine News host counts use publication year from `metadata.publish_date`,
    and the normalized URL hostname with URL fallback. They include `nasdaq.com`
    and its subdomains across all 168 source files. None of the 123 Nasdaq CDNS
    URLs from 2018 matches a Fine News source URL after stripping the Nasdaq
    scheme/hostname and query/fragment components. This establishes a source URL
    coverage gap; it does not rule out copies hosted by original publishers.
    Title matching alone is insufficient: repeated earnings and market-summary
    headlines also occur in different years. The snapshot retains this diagnostic
    with its dates rather than treating repeated titles as duplicate stories.
    
    ## Confirmed recall gaps and next experiment
    
    The frozen GH catalog supplies `Cadence Design Systems` and the branded
    `cādence`, plus the legal name. Suffix expansion adds `CADENCE DESIGN SYSTEMS`;
    neither normalization nor that expansion produces plain `Cadence` or
    `Cadence Design`. Bare `CDNS` in prose is also outside the current ticker policy.
    
    A case-sensitive whole-word search for `Cadence` or `CDNS` in 2018 titles and
    bodies finds 75 source rows, of which 15 already have CDNS candidates. The
    remaining 60 are not all false negatives: they include Cadence Bank, Aerospace,
    Minerals, personal names, ordinary prose and an unrelated CDNS acronym.
    Three inspected untagged examples do identify the semiconductor/EDA company:
    
    | Source and date | Article | Missing spelling |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Korea Herald, 2018-02-28 | [Samsung's non-memory chips at MWC](http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20180228000675) | Cadence |
    | Business Day, 2018-08-17 | [SA is on wrong side of global shift towards new industries](https://www.businesslive.co.za/bd/opinion/2018-08-17-sa-is-on-wrong-side-of-global-shift-towards-new-industries/) | Cadence Design |
    | Forbes, 2018-11-01 | [Simulation Becomes Increasingly Important For Self-Driving Cars](https://www.forbes.com/sites/davidsilver/2018/11/01/simulation-becomes-increasingly-important-for-self-driving-cars/) | Cadence |
    
    These are confirmed missed name mentions from local extracted text, not new
    human gold labels for substantive relevance. Their source IDs and excerpts are
    retained in the snapshot. Consequently, 16 undercounts available mentions and
    cannot establish the academic coverage floor. Both acquisition coverage and
    matching recall require attention.
    
    The next experiment should combine the Nasdaq archive with Fine News while
    preserving provenance and all article–company memberships through deduplication.
    Test provenance-backed aliases and contextual handling of ambiguous names on
    independent data before changing the production dictionary. Then recompute the
    company-year table and review its low-count cells. The completed run and its
    catalog remain frozen; this comparison does not merge sources or revise tags.
    # Company matching evaluation pilot
    
    This pilot produces article-level company matching data, using publisher ticker
    markup as partial reference evidence. It does not produce exact NER span labels.
    The sample and article text are local generated data under ignored
    `.tmp/company-eval-v2/`; they are not automatically licensed for redistribution.
    
    From the repository root, in `devenv shell` after workspace setup:
    
    ```sh
    src/python/.venv/bin/python -m fine_news_cli eval build \
      --background-publishers src/python/apps/fine_news_cli/docs/company-eval-publishers.json
    src/python/.venv/bin/python -m fine_news_cli eval status
    ```
    
    `build` refuses to overwrite a nonempty output directory; `--output`, `--input`,
    `--membership` and `--seed` are configurable. Background articles are drawn
    from all available capture months in 2016–2025, restricted to publishers named
    in the policy, with nonempty retained tags and no detected ticker annotation
    in tags, title or body. It selects up to 200 per publication year, then fills
    any shortfall from other eligible years to reach 2,000. The signal stratum
    draws up to 100 articles per year from one seed-selected capture month per year.
    The background is selected first and the signal sample is disjoint. The
    manifest records file hashes, DuckDB version, membership hash, publisher policy,
    counts, pool limits and seed. Each candidate pool is capped at 4,000 per year.
    Build fails if it cannot find 2,000 qualifying background articles.
    
    The policy is based on the strongest *observed* agreement in a preliminary
    screen, not a guarantee that a publisher always annotates every company. It
    records its evidence and limitations. An article without a detected annotation
    is a candidate negative, not a confirmed negative. The filter conservatively
    rejects known exchange-qualified symbols and uppercase ticker-shaped tag tokens;
    it can reject unrelated acronyms and miss unrecognized ticker formats. A human
    review is needed to establish the actual in-scope companies.
    
    Documents must have at least 200 body characters after trimming and a parseable
    publication date in the capture year. Exact duplicate bodies or normalized URLs
    are removed. The corpus is already filtered to selected publishers, so scores
    and prevalence are not representative of unfiltered news. Press releases are
    not separately excluded. Publication dates are source metadata, not crawl-date
    substitutions. Full article text may include publisher navigation or other
    extraction artifacts.
    
    The membership CSV is a security-year panel. A publisher exchange-qualified
    symbol found in title, body or tags is recorded even if it is not in the panel.
    The automated resolver produces `unique_year_ticker_candidate` only when its
    symbol maps to one PERMCO in the publication year. This is evidence for review,
    not a verified exchange, issuer, CIK or company mention: the panel does not
    itself contain exchange identifiers, CIK links may be candidate-only, and
    symbols can be reused. Ambiguous and out-of-universe signals are retained.
    The data itself does not establish whether a publisher tag was created by a
    person or automation, or whether its list is exhaustive.
    
    The output contains:
    
    - `articles.jsonl`: original body, title, tags, URL, publisher, date, source path,
      source ID, stable article ID, publication year and sampling stratum.
    - `signals.jsonl`: source string, exchange, symbol, tag index or character
      offsets in title/body, candidate PERMCO, issuer keys and link status.
    - `review.jsonl`: a pending queue for 250 independently sampled background
      articles and all sampled signal articles, ordered deterministically within
      each group. No entry is considered a human-reviewed label until explicitly
      completed.
    - `manifest.json`: frozen inputs, output hashes and aggregate counts. The review
      hash is the initial blank queue and will differ once review has begun.
    
    ## Review protocol
    
    Join an article and its signals to a queue row using `article_id`. Review the
    **whole title and body** for all companies in that publication year's top-1,000
    security panel, not just the extracted tickers. Consult the signals and the
    membership CSV as aids; resolve ambiguous tickers and share classes from dated
    source evidence. `text_company_permcos` is the complete list of distinct
    in-scope PERMCO strings explicitly mentioned in title or body. Put additional
    in-scope companies supported only by publisher metadata in
    `metadata_company_permcos`; use `[]` when there are none. Record evidence and
    ambiguities in `notes`. Do not equate a metadata tag with a text mention.
    
    Set `reviewer` to the reviewer's identifier. Set `review_status` to `reviewed`
    only when both lists are complete and `unresolved` is empty. Use `uncertain`
    for ambiguous cases and keep their unresolved details in that list. Keep
    `pending` entries unscored. Review the 250 background rows and keep reviewing
    signal rows until at least 250 articles have confirmed positive matches. The
    `status` command reports progress. More than one company can occur in an
    article; GOOG and GOOGL may resolve to the same PERMCO and should appear once.
    
    Example completed queue record (IDs and evidence are illustrative):
    
    ```json
    {"article_id":"...","stratum":"publisher_signal","review_status":"reviewed","reviewer":"reviewer-id","text_company_permcos":["8048"],"metadata_company_permcos":[],"unresolved":[],"notes":"Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) in the first paragraph"}
    ```
    
    ## Scoring
    
    A tool adapter should produce UTF-8 JSONL with one line per predicted article:
    
    ```json
    {"article_id":"...","company_permcos":["8048"]}
    ```
    
    Use an empty list for an article with no predictions. Predictions must cover
    all reviewed articles; unknown or duplicate article IDs are rejected. Supply
    only title and body to a text-only tool. For a metadata-aware tool, document its
    inputs and run separately:
    
    ```sh
    src/python/.venv/bin/python -m fine_news_cli eval score \
      --predictions /path/to/predictions.jsonl --mode text
    src/python/.venv/bin/python -m fine_news_cli eval score \
      --predictions /path/to/predictions.jsonl --mode metadata
    ```
    
    Scores are micro-aggregated issuer precision, recall and F1 over completed,
    fully reviewed articles, separately by sampling stratum. The metadata-aware
    reference is the union of text and metadata labels; the text reference excludes
    metadata-only labels. The report also provides alignment with unreviewed
    publisher signals for predicted articles, deduplicated by article and PERMCO.
    Those signals are partial and may be wrong: alignment is **not** precision,
    recall or a substitute for human review. No reviewed labels means there is no
    measured precision or recall. Retain reviewer and source evidence when comparing
    tools, and document any overlap between tool development and this sample.

    # Random-source company coverage estimate
    
    This experiment estimates the fraction of source rows that substantively cover
    at least one company in the article-year universe. It accepts multiple central
    companies, including product, operational and legal stories without stock-market
    discussion. It does not require a unique primary company or attempt exhaustive
    company extraction. Passing examples, analyst employers, author holdings,
    advertisements and fund-sponsor attribution alone do not qualify.
    
    ## Completed result
    
    All 2,000 sampled rows have outcomes. Eight failed requests were retried once in
    a separate ledger; all retries completed. The effective outcomes are 310 positive
    (15.5%), 1,333 negative (66.65%) and 357 unknown (17.85%). Unknowns comprise 320
    historical catalog gaps and 37 unsupported years, rather than outstanding requests.
    
    The weighted AI-assisted audit estimates **18.06–20.56%** substantive eligible
    company coverage. The range spans seven unresolved review labels. The approximate
    95% interval for source sampling and review subsampling is **14.12–24.50%**;
    systematic AI-review error and corpus-coverage error are additional uncertainties.
    This corresponds to **2.67–3.04 million** of the observed 14.81M local source rows,
    or **3.61–4.11 million per 20M** if the larger source has the same mix.

    | Tev1 final choice | 10.73% |

    ## Audit and interpretation
    
    An independent random base audit contains 200 articles selected without viewing
    model outcomes. Three AI reviewers read full prepared texts, with Tev1, DFA and
    publisher annotations hidden, and checked annual membership. Fifty articles,
    prioritizing uncertain cases, received a second blinded review. One binary
    disagreement was reconciled from the full text; this targeted cross-review is
    not a representative inter-rater agreement estimate.
    
    The audit then adds randomly selected unreviewed articles within final Tev1
    positive, negative and unknown strata, targeting at least 100, 100 and 50 reviews
    respectively. The 82 additions bring this random audit to 282 rows: 100 positive,
    132 negative and 50 unknown outcomes. Existing base reviews are retained.
    
    A further 57 targeted reviews complete a census of all 82 potential new-link
    cases, giving **339 unique reviewed articles**. The enhanced estimate separates
    the model-positive population into 228 overlap cases (75 randomly reviewed) and
    82 potential new-link cases (all reviewed). Negative and unknown samples retain
    their original design. Conditional on these cell counts, the non-census reviews
    remain uniform within each cell. The original three-stratum estimate is also
    retained, without mixing targeted additions into its random positive sample.
    
    Estimates weight each cell by its share of the full 2,000-row draw, rather than
    averaging an oversampled positive review set. Unresolved review labels span bounds.
    Approximate intervals include source-sampling and review-subsampling variation,
    but exclude systematic reviewer errors and source-coverage errors.
    
    Review is **AI-assisted, not human gold**. It supplies a provisional planning
    estimate. Article-level valid-link yield means that at least one returned PERMCO
    is accepted. It is distinct from complete company-set precision, recall or F1.
    The DFA candidate rate is also distinct from substantive company coverage.

    ## Local Kev with SGLang Docker
    
    `company local-extract` uses the native `/v1/systemone` pointer-head API of
    `jaredpalmer/kev-0.8b`, with the model's fitted temperature and no text generation.
    It asks one Choice question per group of 32 year-eligible issuers, retaining each
    group's highest-probability company even when its null option won. A final Choice
    over these company finalists includes no-match and unclear options. Probabilities
    from separate groups are never compared. This covers every eligible issuer
    without a NER shortlist and avoids losing all finalists to first-stage nulls.
    The grouping seed matches the earlier grouped pilot; this local prompt contract
    is versioned separately.
    
    The [upstream Kev recipe](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Kev/kev)
    explicitly disables radix caching, chunked prefill and CUDA graphs. Each question
    prefills the article separately. SGLang batches these prefills, but this run does
    not demonstrate prefix-cache reuse. The running server's resolved settings are
    recorded in the runtime provenance. No unsupported cache override is applied.
    
    The pilot pins SGLang 0.5.23 and the Kev adapter, pointer head, tokenizer and Qwen
    base revision. Model hashes are retained in `.tmp/kev-runtime/`. Its Docker
    launch script binds port 30000 only to localhost, mounts the adapter read-only,
    uses a separate model cache, and attaches the local RTX 5060 Ti through NVIDIA
    CDI. The base model is cached before launch; the container runs with
    `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.

    ```sh
    hf download Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base \

      --cache-dir .tmp/kev-runtime/hf-cache
    bash .tmp/kev-runtime/launch.sh
    
    # Use the frozen article-ID-only selection for the existing comparison.
    just python::run company local-extract \
      --runtime-provenance .tmp/kev-runtime/runtime.json \
      --article-ids .tmp/kev-runtime/comparison-article-ids.jsonl \
      --output .tmp/company-decisions-kev-v1
    ```

    The runner verifies sanitized inputs and membership, sends only task/title/text,

    are truncated. The local command does not resolve OpenRouter credentials or
    consume the paid pilot's ledger.
