    made 12 predictions without an observed signal, and left 132 pairs unpredicted.
    These are partial-reference overlap counts, not independently verified errors.
    
    The run took 423.8 seconds including local orchestration, with 405.4 seconds
    inside HTTP inference calls and 12,080,196 counted input tokens across 7,072
    question prefills. There were 442 localhost HTTP requests and zero paid API
    charges. The measured run used BF16 on the RTX 5060 Ti, with 16 maximum running
    requests and a 16,384-token prefill batch limit. Four separate synthetic controls
    (weather, public library, outside-universe workshop, equally central companies)
    all returned no company; the weather and library controls chose unclear rather
    than no-match. These controls do not validate performance on real background
    articles.
    
    Kev's F1 advantage over Span-02 was 0.020. An exploratory paired article
    bootstrap (10,000 resamples) gave a 95% interval of -0.017 to +0.058 for that
    difference, so this sample does not establish superiority. The bootstrap does
    not account for publisher clusters, near duplicates, incomplete reference labels
    or exploratory model selection. Results and provenance are in
    `.tmp/company-method-comparison-kev-v1/`, with predictions in
    `.tmp/company-decisions-kev-v1/`. The GPU container was stopped after the run.
    
    ## Reproducible local optimization trials
    
    `company benchmark` now manages pinned SGLang or vLLM Docker servers, queues
    articles concurrently, and measures the complete extraction policy. It records
    actual HTTP requests and question prefills separately: putting several questions
    in one HTTP request does not turn them into one model forward pass. Every first
    stage covers the full article-year issuer universe. No NER shortlist is used.
    
    The model contracts are pinned in `company/profiles.py`. Available paths are:
    
    | Profile | Engine/API | Maximum options | Prefix reuse |
    | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
    | Kev 0.8B | SGLang native `/v1/systemone` | 255 | Disabled by native pointer path |
    | OneJev 1.6 0.8B | SGLang `/v1/score`; vLLM one-token completions | 255 | Supported |
    | Tev1 0.8B experimental | SGLang `/v1/score`; vLLM one-token completions | 24 | Supported |
    | D3-edge, D3-lite | vLLM native `/v1/systemone` classifier | 255 | Disabled: bidirectional attention |
    
    The SGLang D3 checkpoint-loading canary produced missing-parameter warnings and
    an unusable answer. That path is refused; only vLLM's native D3 classifier is
    enabled. Kev 0.5B and Liquid d1-omni-600M do not have a verified native path in
    these pinned images and are not substituted with a different checkpoint or a
    custom integration. The native D3 head stays in its trained FP32 representation.
    See [vLLM's D3 contract](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/models/structured_decisions_models/#decision-30)
    and [SGLang's Kev recipe](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Kev/kev).
    
    Download the immutable checkpoint revisions before running. For example:
    
    ```sh
    hf download OmniJev/OneJev1.6-0.8B \
      --revision c89933c277629b707895bff752c61d2b0664c85e \
      --local-dir .tmp/models/onejev-0.8b
    hf download vllm-sr/d3-edge \
      --revision bee5e872f75b9c5d1405767bf244a6948b95c0af \
      --local-dir .tmp/models/d3-edge
    hf download vllm-sr/d3-lite \
      --revision 6c01fba14e74f63b70e1ef442b0b6d1b934339d5 \
      --local-dir .tmp/models/d3-lite
    hf download togethercomputer/Tev1-0.8B-experimental \
      --revision 6bb2dff14b38fea90ddb14d870166ccaf77374e9 \
      --local-dir .tmp/models/tev-0.8b
    ```
    
    The example configurations pin both images by digest. Pull them explicitly if
    they are not cached. Allow sufficient disk space for extraction and checkpoint
    weights; the two installed engine images report approximately 56 GB and 33 GB.
    Containers mount checkpoints read-only, reuse a persistent compilation cache,
    bind only localhost, and run offline. An exclusive GPU lock prevents overlapping
    benchmark processes. Cleanup removes the owned container even if saving its log
    fails.
    
    ```sh
    just python::run company benchmark \
      --config src/python/apps/fine_news_cli/examples/company-benchmark.json \
      --output .tmp/company-model-benchmark
    just python::run company benchmark \
      --config src/python/apps/fine_news_cli/examples/company-cache-benchmark.json \
      --output .tmp/company-cache-benchmark
    ```
    
    Each suite consists of `base` RunConfig fields and named `trials` with
    `overrides`. Keep inputs, selection and reference identical between trials.
    Tune `article_concurrency`, `max_sequences`, `token_budget`,
    `chunked_prefill_size`, `attention_backend`, `precision` and `group_size` explicitly.
    OneJev supports BF16 and an online FP8 canary in the pinned SGLang image. NVFP4
    requires a supported quantized checkpoint; the runner does not manufacture one
    from BF16 weights. Engine support and F1 must be rechecked after precision changes.
    
    The default `exhaustive` policy asks about every group, keeps one company from
    each, and recursively reduces finalists to a final choice. Group sizes can
    shrink when a complete prompt would exceed context. An article that cannot fit
    even with one issuer stops the run; text is never truncated. Intermediate
    `outside_group` and final `no_primary_match` have distinct meanings.
    
    `layout=catalog_first` places the complete trusted issuer catalog before article
    text to permit reuse across different articles from the same year.
    `compact_options=true` refers back to catalog identifiers instead of repeating
    names in the question. The optional `catalog` policy first routes among catalog
    pages, then decides among companies in the selected pages. Every issuer appears
    in the routing state. Uncertain or null routes fall back to exhaustive scoring.
    This policy can still miss the correct company through a confident routing
    error; it must pass the same frozen reference test before promotion.
    
    `prime_prefix=true` performs an additional prefix-only score call before
    parallel SGLang questions, allowing the shared article prefix to enter the
    cache before fan-out. This extra call is included in work and timing counters.
    Cache effectiveness is measured from before/after Prometheus counters, rather
    than inferred from the presence of a launch flag. Per-question distributions
    are normalized within each question only; normalized confidence above uniform
    chance is a routing heuristic, not a calibrated correctness probability.
    
    Outputs include source snapshots, model and input hashes, resolved server
    settings, GPU samples, engine cache counters, traces, SQLite checkpoints and
    bounded Parquet shards. Reuse is limited to exact sanitized text and year under
    the same run contract, with separate article lineage. `local-extract --config`
    resumes a matching contract; benchmark timing requires a fresh directory.
    
    Quality passes only when **every** frozen reference article completed and its
    observed-signal F1 exceeds 0.68. Incomplete screening runs report no passing F1.
    Reports include exploratory article bootstrap intervals and, for suites with
    multiple complete policies, five-fold policy selection with identical input
    hashes kept together. Reusing this previously inspected publisher-reference
    sample does not create an independent primary-company gold evaluation.
    
    For timing independently of annotation presence:
    
    ```sh
    just python::run company prepare-throughput \
      --input data/01_intermediate --limit 30000 \
      --output .tmp/company-throughput-corpus
    ```
    
    The SQL resource samples source rows by a seeded hash without a ticker or NER
    filter, retains duplicates, and passes them through the existing leakage audit.
    Use its `prepared` directory in a RunConfig and set `article_ids` to null. The
    sample's year, length, duplicate and quarantine counts are recorded. Missing
    historical issuer names stop extraction with details in `universe.json`.
    Quarantined articles are never counted as completed labeling.
    
    30 million articles in one day requires 347.2 articles/s before overhead; the
    sample runtime gate uses 400/s for headroom. Two to three days requires
    173.6 to 115.7 articles/s. A sample projection is always labeled unverified.
    After a candidate passes quality, coverage and throughput screening, use at
    least 10,000 fresh eligible documents, three fresh-output repetitions and a
    one-hour stream of distinct documents to test sustained throughput. Replaying
    the 221-article comparison would inflate cache reuse and is not a corpus test.
    
    The independent 2026-11-04 sample at `.tmp/company-throughput-corpus-v1`
    contained 30,000 source articles: 9,910 passed the strict leakage boundary and
    20,090 were quarantined. It exposed 229 missing historical year/issuer names
    before the 2016–2025 pilot window. Its body-length median/p90/p99 were
    2,826/6,240/21,463 characters, with a maximum of 89,539. These are source-sample
    lengths, not tokenizer counts. The full-corpus timing gate remains unmet;
    excluding old years or quarantined articles would change the task's coverage.
    
    ### Measured results on the frozen comparison
    
    The following trials each completed all 221 articles and use the same 304
    observed publisher article/issuer pairs. F1 is partial-reference overlap, not
    adjudicated primary-company accuracy. All paths used groups of up to 253
    companies, a final runoff, 16 concurrent articles and 64 server sequences,
    except Tev, whose trained option limit requires groups of 22 companies.
    These compare complete policies, not model architecture in isolation.
    
    | Model / engine | Precision | F1 | Articles/s | Pilot projection for 30M (days) |
    | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | Tev1 experimental / SGLang | BF16 | 0.729 | 0.85 | 410 |
    | Kev / SGLang | BF16 | 0.708 | 1.05 | 331 |
    | OneJev / SGLang | BF16 | 0.700 | 1.05 | 332 |
    | OneJev / SGLang, primed | FP8 | 0.696 | 1.42 | 244 |
    | D3-edge / vLLM | BF16 | 0.577 | 1.78 | 195 |
    | D3-lite / vLLM | BF16 | 0.593 | 1.04 | 334 |
    
    The BF16 Kev/OneJev observations are earlier exploratory trials in
    `.tmp/company-optimization-v2-quality-clean`. The native D3 and FP8 trials in
    `.tmp/company-optimization-v4-quality` also retain frozen source ZIPs. The
    fastest passing configuration is FP8 OneJev: P/R = 0.949/0.549, with an
    exploratory F1 bootstrap interval of 0.644–0.746. Its point estimate passes
    0.68; this interval does not establish F1 above 0.68 with 95% confidence.
    
    Tev's full run is in `.tmp/company-optimization-v5-tev-quality`, with
    P/R = 0.924/0.602 and exploratory F1 interval 0.681–0.776. Its F1 advantage
    over the earlier Kev policy was 0.022; a paired article bootstrap gave
    [-0.009, 0.052], so this comparison does not establish superiority. Its smaller
    trained option limit required 10,943 question prefills, versus approximately
    1,100 for the 253-company BF16 policies. The combined six-method report and
    source-summary hashes are in `.tmp/company-optimization-report-v1`.
    
    D3-edge processed 48,294 input tokens/s at mean GPU utilization of 95.1%, while
    FP8 OneJev averaged 96.2% GPU utilization. These results are consistent with
    prefill throughput in the tens of thousands of tokens/s. D3-edge used 27,172
    input tokens per article; FP8 OneJev counted 30,328 including priming, with
    16.1% of prompt tokens cached. The company choices and repeated reads make
    article throughput much lower than a short, one-question synthetic benchmark.
    
    On a separate 40-article screen, placing the complete catalog first and using
    compact options achieved 81.9% aggregate prompt-token reuse, but only 0.56
    articles/s and exploratory F1 0.129. A high cache-hit rate alone does not
    establish either quality or throughput. The catalog policy was not promoted.
    Those outputs are in `.tmp/company-optimization-v4-catalog-tev`. The earlier
    catalog router fell back on 35 of 40 articles and was also slower.
    
    The independent clean-input profile in `.tmp/company-optimization-v4-input-profile`
    contained 9,910 distinct sanitized year/text pairs, averaging 580 title/body
    tokens (p50/p90/p99 = 504/1,036/1,716). It excludes quarantined source rows,
    instructions, options and serialization overhead. Even hypothetical single
    prefill at 50,000 new tokens/s would take about four days for 30 million such
    articles. This conditional sample is not a full-corpus runtime estimate.
    
    The 10,000-document repeated throughput test and hour-long soak were not run:
    the independent-input coverage preflight failed and all measured policies
    missed the runtime screening target by a large margin. No one-day or
    two-to-three-day completion claim is supported. All owned containers are
    removed after trials; no paid API requests are involved.
    
    ### Evaluating a learned fast stage
    
    A fast classifier followed by selective decision-model inference is a separate
    production candidate. A useful first stage must resolve confident matches as
    well as irrelevant documents, since merely rejecting some background articles
    does not remove enough GPU work at the measured decision-model rate. It should
    read the full sanitized article and preserve the unique-primary-company,
    no-match and unclear outcomes. No such gate is enabled by these experiments.
    
    Benchmark TF–IDF with a linear model as an inexpensive learned baseline, and a
    fine-tuned encoder such as ModernBERT for full-text decisions. Treat spaCy,
    GLiNER and linking as mention/identity components; primary-company salience
    requires its own task labels and validation. Independently maintained aliases
    can aid discovery. Publisher ticker annotations used as reference must stay
    stripped before every learned or matching stage. A no-alias-hit result does not
    by itself establish a negative label.
    
    The [ModernBERT paper](https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.127/)
    supports testing efficient encoders for classification. The
    [entity-salience study](https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-naacl.28.pdf)
    reports RoBERTa cross-encoder F1 of 0.811 on abstract-aligned NYT labels, but
    0.606 and 0.630 on human-annotated SEL and EntSUM. These different tasks and
    datasets do not establish expected primary-company F1 on this corpus. The
    [credit-news funnel](https://aclanthology.org/2022.naacl-industry.40.pdf)
    discarded 70% using a classifier trained on over 30 million Reuters-coded
    documents; its credit-relevance definition is different from ours.
    
    If a fraction `f` reaches a decision stage sustaining `r` articles/s, that
    stage alone needs `30,000,000 * f / r` seconds. At the observed FP8 rate,
    two days permits at most 0.82% fallback and three days at most 1.23%, ignoring
    the first stage, I/O and retries. Retaining 30% would require about 73 days of
    decision-model work. CPU/GPU overlap can hide some first-stage time, while
    stages sharing the one GPU compete for its capacity.
    
    Before claiming an improvement, split training/calibration/test documents by
    time and duplicate group, audit rejected/no-hit articles, and measure the
    entire cascade on the same primary-company reference. A sufficiently fast
    first stage, a measured fallback fraction, and preserved end-to-end recall
    are all necessary; a paper's F1 or a model's raw confidence is insufficient.

    # Candidate datasets
    
    These notebooks revisit the saved exploration dated 2026-10-29. Each reads a
    small, local evidence snapshot and discusses the acquisition decision it can
    support. Historical article-level extraction has not been rerun.
    
    | Candidate | Sample input rows | Qualifying articles | Frozen-universe articles | Cohort / input | Companies |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | [Fine News](fine_news/README.md) | 523,950 | 4,453 | 495 | 0.0945% | 92 |
    | [Infini News](infini_news/README.md) | 317,283 | 1,430 | 127 | 0.0400% | 60 |
    | [DCLM](dclm/README.md) | 98,889 | 86 | 22 | 0.0222% | 23 |
    | [RefinedWeb](refinedweb/README.md) | 174,919 | 99 | 13 | 0.0074% | 10 |
    | [FineWeb-HQ](fineweb_hq/README.md) | 367,000 | 154 | 19 | 0.0052% | 16 |
    
    ## Shared definitions
    
    Qualifying articles require a URL, explicit ticker notation, a publication date
    and a nonempty body, using the same 93-publisher / 115-domain registry. The
    cohort is pricing-perspective's frozen 100-company research universe, not current
    Nasdaq-100 membership. URLs are deduplicated within each source; articles may
    mention several companies and are counted once. Cross-source overlap is unknown.
    
    Press releases remain included in the baseline. The notebook switch excludes
    labelled releases; investment analysis remains in the nonrelease category.
    Publication time, author and title are optional. Crawl dates are never used as
    publication-date fallbacks. Classification and extraction remain heuristic.
    
    ## Interpretation
    
    Fine News and Infini News merit the next pilots, based on observed yield and
    metadata availability. Their samples have different time coverage and selection
    mechanisms, so the table cannot establish a population ranking or an annual
    all-company floor. Yields are unweighted, with all raw sample rows as denominator;
    publication-year yields are contributions to total yield, not annual retention.
    
    Fine News's separate December pilot uses a publisher-prefiltered denominator:
    1,832 cohort articles / 72,813 rows. It is discussed separately in that notebook.
    The later 14,807,287-row local collection and reported metadata-only matches are
    also distinct from date/body-qualified pilot counts. Acquisition completeness
    against the upstream inventory remains unverified.
    
    Historical population extrapolations are omitted. The earlier 599,979 Fine News
    scenario mixed English yield with a multilingual population; the corrected
    207,082 remains biased by the August 2020 capture stratum. Neither is a forecast.
    
    ## Reproduction and evidence
    
    Follow the [notebook commands](../README.md). Every candidate keeps a standalone
    `notebook.py`, sidecar uv lock, findings README and `evidence/` directory. Evidence
    contains selected aggregate rows, original method notes, source references and
    SHA256 provenance. No runtime dependency on `.tmp/` or the other repository exists.
    
    Exact historical input identity is not established for several remote sources;
    DCLM's original shard directory is uncertain. The current December Fine News
    file has the recorded pilot row count but a different SHA256. A new extraction
    must be labelled as a new run until source equivalence is demonstrated.
    
    The archive's aggregate validator passes. Migration validation reconciles source,
    year and publisher totals and checks retained evidence hashes. Notebook execution
    reproduces displays from aggregates; it does not validate the original parser's
    precision or recall. FineWeb-HQ discusses the separate cosine experiment's
    limitations; the unrun MLP draft and bulk extraction scripts are not migrated.
    24:publication-year and ticker-year coverage on the local collection before making
    25:an acquisition claim. Preserve article–company memberships when deduplicating.

    def _progress(output: Path, event: str, **values):
        record = {"time": time.time(), "event": event, **values}
        with (output / "progress.jsonl").open("a", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            stream.write(json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True) + "\n")

    def _sync_directory(path: Path):
        fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY)
        try:
            os.fsync(fd)
        finally:
            os.close(fd)
    
    
    @contextmanager
    def _run_lock(output: Path):
        output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with (output / ".run.lock").open("a") as stream:
            try:
                fcntl.flock(stream, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
            except BlockingIOError:
                raise ValueError("another process owns this tagging output") from None
            try:
                yield
            finally:
                fcntl.flock(stream, fcntl.LOCK_UN)

    # DFA alias and evidence refinement
    
    A subsequent [blinded text adjudication](company-dfa-adjudication.md) reviews all
    60 disagreements and accepts multiple central ticker associations. It finds
    semantic benefits from Tev1 that the publisher-overlap proxy does not capture;
    the original F1 tables below remain unchanged.
    
    The experiment preserves the original dictionary implementation and adds opt-in
    policies, shared evidence features, and grouped training experiments. It uses
    complete sanitized text and article-year membership. No additional neural
    inference or publisher ticker metadata enters the matching features.
    
    ## Reproduce
    
    From the repository root, after installing the CPU extra:
    
    ```sh
    src/python/.venv/bin/python -m fine_news_cli eval cpu-refine \
      --config src/python/apps/fine_news_cli/examples/company-cpu-benchmark.json \
      --output .tmp/company-dfa-refinement-v2
    ```
    
    Use `--phase quality` or `--phase timing` separately. Quality requires a fresh
    output directory. The timing phase reads the fitted bundles and checks their
    checksums before loading trusted local joblib files. It tests one/six workers,
    batches of 128, and three repetitions on the same 8,267 supported clean articles
    as the earlier benchmark. Startup is separate from prediction and durable writes.
    
    ## Diagnostic evidence
    
    On the frozen 221-article reference, the original DFA retrieves 270 of 304
    publisher-observed issuer pairs. Of Tev1's 198 company selections, 171 already
    appear among DFA candidates. Twenty-four selected-company disagreements can be
    addressed by ranking existing candidates; another 27 involve a missing candidate.
    Tev1 abstains on 23 articles for which the original DFA selects a company.
    
    Generic single-word aliases account for substantial extra matches: `price`
    appears on 105 articles lacking that publisher annotation, `new` on 35 and
    `people` on 30. Missing publisher annotations do not prove those companies are
    absent. Historical display names and PERMCO mappings can also be misleading, so
    teacher output is not automatically converted into new aliases or identities.
    
    ## Methods and safeguards
    
    Typography normalization canonicalizes Unicode apostrophes, dashes and
    whitespace. An additional punctuation experiment removes apostrophes and treats
    hyphens as spaces symmetrically in text and aliases. Legal suffix expansion
    removes generic suffixes; the extended variant also strips Company/Co. Derived
    roots must have at least four alphanumeric characters, be non-generic and have
    one owner within the year. Capitalization filtering rejects lower-case evidence
    for single-token aliases. This can miss legitimately lowercase company names;
    it is an accuracy experiment rather than a universal proper-name rule.
    
    Evidence models share one logistic regression across all issuers. Features are
    counts, title/lead placement, case, alias length, legal-name matches, owner
    ambiguity and relative frequency. They contain no issuer/alias identifiers,
    publisher metadata, article IDs or Tev confidence. Numeric scaling, regression
    weights and mention/primary thresholds are fit within grouped folds. Inner
    three-fold predictions select thresholds; outer five-fold predictions supply
    quality scores. Duplicate groups remain together. A second training source uses
    only existing Tev1 decisions; articles without teacher coverage never enter its
    fitting or threshold selection. Tev1 is an imperfect teacher.
    
    All alias policies are generic and label-independent, but choosing among policies
    uses this previously inspected sample. Results are exploratory, not an untouched

The main recommendation is to **retain a broad corpus and derive K/T study cohorts downstream**. The exploratory repo shows why: candidate mentions do not establish substantive coverage, duplicated source rows inflate counts, and acquisition gaps can resemble matching failures.

The comments therefore specify historical company identities, independent evaluation including no-hit articles, explicit unknown outcomes, and company-year panels that distinguish zero coverage from missing data.

For DVC, the proposed boundaries follow independently reusable artifacts, with shard/month partitioning for local work and global stages for deduplication and coverage. Dependencies determine execution order. [DVC pipeline guidance](https://doc.dvc.org/user-guide/pipelines/defining-pipelines)

    [project]
    name = "ccfinance-pipeline"
    version = "0.1.0"
    description = "Reproducible CCFinance data engineering stages"
    requires-python = ">=3.13,<3.14"
    dependencies = ["typer>=0.16,<1"]
    
    [project.scripts]
    pipeline = "pipeline.cli:app"
    
    [build-system]
    requires = ["hatchling==1.27.0"]
    build-backend = "hatchling.build"
    
    [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
    packages = ["src/pipeline"]
    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    set positional-arguments
    
    default:
        @just --list
    
    # Install exactly the committed workspace and build dependencies.
    setup:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv sync --locked --all-packages
    
    run *args:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline pipeline "$@"
    
    lint:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff check .
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff format --check .
    
    typecheck:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pyrefly check
    
    # Local impacted-test selection, with a bounded number of workers.
    test-changed:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest -q -n 2 --testmon
    
    # The test and CI gates never use affected-test selection.
    test:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest -q -n 2 --no-testmon
    
    # Enforce module dependencies, reject unused declarations and forbid cycles.
    tach:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen tach check
    
    build:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv build --python .venv/bin/python --offline --no-build-isolation --all-packages
    
    check: lint typecheck tach test build
    
    fmt:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff check --fix .
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff format .
    # Data workspace
    
    Large raw, intermediate and processed data belong here. Git ignores payloads;
    track reproducible inputs/outputs with DVC in part 2. Keep `.dvc` pointer files
    and documentation in Git. No data has been copied from the exploratory repo.
    # Architecture
    
    CCFinance separates code and research artifacts. Git stores source, configuration,
    locks, provenance definitions and documentation. DVC will track large data and
    experiment outputs once the actual stages are defined in part 2.
    
    - `src/python/apps/pipeline` owns the CLI and data stage implementations.
    - `src/python/uv.lock` locks runtime, quality, testing, packaging and DVC tools.
    - `src/latex` owns the manuscript source and bibliography.
    - `data` holds ignored data payloads and versioned DVC pointer files.
    - `infra/nix` and `devenv.lock` own the reproducible system environment.
    
    Tach enforces module boundaries; Ruff and strict Pyrefly check Python source.
    CI executes those checks, tests and builds through the same just recipes as local
    work. Setup may download dependencies; ordinary checks use cached dependencies
    and do not repair authored content. LaTeX uses a versioned Tectonic asset bundle.
    
    The Hugging Face dataset is staging, and the bucket is intended for intermediate
    and experiment artifacts. Neither is accessed by scaffold commands. Pipeline
    stages, provenance, study parameters, coverage criteria and remote transport are
    part 2 work, rather than implied by this scaffold.
    
    Copier answers record the source and tag for future template updates. Review
    update conflicts and preserve project-specific code and configuration. The
    upstream template is [Exordio](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/exordio).

    # CCFinance
    
    CCFinance is a data engineering project for filtering and enriching public
    Common Crawl News (CC-News) copies for research into language in finance.
    
    ## Start
    
    Exordio supplies the Python and LaTeX toolchains, a pinned Nix environment and CI.
    Copier answers record Exordio `v0.1.1-alpha` (the documented `v0.1.0` tag was not
    available in the local source).
    
    ```bash
    bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh
    devenv shell
    just setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run stages list
    just check
    ```
    
    For Python alone, with Python 3.13, uv and just installed:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::check
    ```
    
    ## Data and reproducibility
    
    DVC is initialized at the repository root with analytics disabled. Use:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc status
    just dvc dag
    ```
    
    See [Python commands](src/python/README.md), [LaTeX commands](src/latex/README.md)
    and [infrastructure](infra/README.md). The scaffold's Apache-2.0 license covers
    code; it does not grant rights to upstream article content.
    # Architecture
    
    CCFinance separates code and research artifacts. Git stores source, configuration,
    locks, provenance definitions and documentation. DVC will track large data and
    experiment outputs once the actual stages are defined in part 2.
    
    - `src/python/apps/pipeline` owns the CLI and data stage implementations.
    - `src/python/uv.lock` locks runtime, quality, testing, packaging and DVC tools.
    - `src/latex` owns the manuscript source and bibliography.
    - `data` holds ignored data payloads and versioned DVC pointer files.
    - `infra/nix` and `devenv.lock` own the reproducible system environment.
    
    Tach enforces module boundaries; Ruff and strict Pyrefly check Python source.
    CI executes those checks, tests and builds through the same just recipes as local
    work. Setup may download dependencies; ordinary checks use cached dependencies
    and do not repair authored content. LaTeX uses a versioned Tectonic asset bundle.
    
    The Hugging Face dataset is staging, and the bucket is intended for intermediate
    and experiment artifacts. Neither is accessed by scaffold commands. Pipeline
    stages, provenance, study parameters, coverage criteria and remote transport are
    part 2 work, rather than implied by this scaffold.
    
    Copier answers record the source and tag for future template updates. Review
    update conflicts and preserve project-specific code and configuration. The
    upstream template is [Exordio](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/exordio).
    # Python workspace
    
    `apps/pipeline` is an installable Typer application in a Python 3.13 uv workspace.
    Run from the repository root:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run version
    just python::run stages list
    just python::run stages raw --help
    just python::check
    ```
    
    Data processing is organized into three layers, matching `dvc.yaml`:
    
    | Module and CLI group | Purpose | Data location |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `pipeline.stages.raw` / `stages raw` | Preserve source snapshots and provenance | `data/raw/` |
    | `pipeline.stages.processed` / `stages processed` | Build reusable cleaned and enriched tables | `data/processed/` |
    | `pipeline.stages.research` / `stages research` | Curate coverage panels, cohorts and release datasets | `data/research/` |
    
    Each group provides a namespace for future processing sub-stages. No data
    transformations are implemented yet. Add stage commands under their owning layer,
    with explicit inputs and outputs, and declare their dependencies in `dvc.yaml`.
    DVC connects layers through artifacts; Python modules need not import earlier
    layers to read their outputs. Importing a module performs no dataset access.
    
    Setup installs the committed lock. Checks run offline with frozen dependencies.
    Ruff checks formatting, annotations, docstrings and common correctness/security
    issues; strict Pyrefly checks all app code and tests. Tach enforces module
    boundaries, rejects unused dependency declarations and forbids cycles. The CLI
    imports the stage router, which registers the three independent layer modules.
    
    `just python::test` runs all tests. `test-changed` is a local optimization only.
    `build` builds a wheel and source archive. `fmt` explicitly repairs formatting.
    Ruff and Pyrefly run from the same uv lock locally and in CI.
    # Python architecture
    
    One uv workspace and lock own runtime, development and build dependencies.
    `apps/pipeline/src/pipeline` owns the executable application:
    
    - `cli` parses arguments and dispatches commands.
    - `stages` registers the data layer command groups.
    - `stages.raw` owns source acquisition and provenance.
    - `stages.processed` owns cleaning, deduplication and enrichment.
    - `stages.research` owns coverage panels, study cohorts and release datasets.
    - `__main__` exposes the same application through `python -m pipeline`.
    
    Tach enforces the declared dependency direction from the application entry point
    to CLI to the stage router and its independent layer modules, including
    type-checking imports, with cycles forbidden. Artifact dependencies in DVC
    connect the layers; no cross-layer Python imports are currently needed.
    Ruff and strict Pyrefly check source and tests. Tests exercise CLI dispatch and
    installed module execution; packaging is checked independently by a wheel build.
    
    All Python recipes scrub inherited Python paths and virtual environments.
    Setup is the network boundary; validation uses frozen offline dependencies.
    [project]
    name = "ccfinance-workspace"
    version = "0.1.0"
    requires-python = ">=3.13,<3.14"
    
    [tool.uv]
    package = false
    
    [tool.uv.workspace]
    members = ["apps/*"]
    
    [dependency-groups]
    dev = [
      "hatchling==1.27.0",
      "pytest==9.1.1",
      "pytest-xdist>=3.8,<5",
      "pytest-testmon>=2.3,<3",
      "tach==0.35.3",
      "ruff==0.14.5",
      "pyrefly==0.64.1",
      "dvc>=3.63,<4",
    ]
    
    [tool.ruff]
    target-version = "py313"
    
    [tool.ruff.lint]
    select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "C4", "SIM", "RUF", "ANN", "D", "S"]
    
    [tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
    "**/tests/**" = ["S101", "D"]
    
    [tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
    convention = "google"
    
    [tool.pyrefly]
    preset = "strict"
    project-includes = ["apps"]
    python-version = "3.13"
    
    [tool.pytest.ini_options]
    testpaths = ["apps"]
    addopts = ["--import-mode=importlib", "--strict-config", "--strict-markers"]
    source_roots = ["apps/pipeline/src"]
    exact = true
    ignore_type_checking_imports = false
    forbid_circular_dependencies = true
    
    [[modules]]
    path = "pipeline"
    depends_on = ["pipeline.cli"]
    
    [[modules]]
    path = "pipeline.cli"
    depends_on = ["pipeline.stages"]
    
    [[modules]]
    path = "pipeline.stages"
    depends_on = ["pipeline.stages.raw", "pipeline.stages.processed", "pipeline.stages.research"]
    
    [[modules]]
    path = "pipeline.stages.raw"
    depends_on = []
    
    [[modules]]
    path = "pipeline.stages.processed"
    depends_on = []
    
    [[modules]]
    path = "pipeline.stages.research"
    depends_on = []
    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    set positional-arguments
    
    default:
        @just --list
    
    # Install exactly the committed workspace and build dependencies.
    setup:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv sync --locked --all-packages
    
    run *args:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline pipeline "$@"
    
    lint:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff check .
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff format --check .
    
    typecheck:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pyrefly check
    
    # Local impacted-test selection, with a bounded number of workers.
    test-changed:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest -q -n 2 --testmon
    
    # The test and CI gates never use affected-test selection.
    test:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest -q -n 2 --no-testmon
    
    # Enforce module dependencies, reject unused declarations and forbid cycles.
    tach:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen tach check
    
    build:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv build --python .venv/bin/python --offline --no-build-isolation --all-packages
    
    check: lint typecheck tach test build
    
    fmt:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff check --fix .
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff format .
    default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit]
    default_stages: [pre-commit]
    repos:
      - repo: builtin
        hooks:
          - id: check-yaml
          - id: check-toml
          - id: check-json
          - id: check-merge-conflict
            args: [--assume-in-merge]
          - id: detect-private-key
          - id: check-case-conflict
      - repo: local
        hooks:
          - id: workflow-lint
            name: GitHub Actions workflow syntax
            entry: bash -c 'actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml'
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            always_run: true
          - id: shellcheck
            name: ShellCheck scripts
            entry: shellcheck

          - id: markdown
            name: Markdown formatting and local links

            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            types: [markdown]
          - id: nix-format
            name: Nix formatting
            entry: nixfmt --check

          - id: nix-lint
            name: Nix anti-patterns
            entry: statix check infra/nix
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            types: [nix]
          - id: text-check
            name: Whitespace and final newlines
            entry: bash infra/nix/check-text.sh

          - id: python-quality
            name: Python lint, strict types and architecture

            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            files: ^src/python/
          - id: dvc-metadata
            name: DVC metadata
            entry: just data-check
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false

    # pytest-layout-enforcer
    
    `pytest-layout-enforcer` keeps test files structurally aligned with the Python
    modules they exercise. It is both a pytest plugin and a standalone command, so
    the same invariant can run during test collection, in CI, in pre-commit, or
    immediately after an automated refactor.
    
    Given:
    
    ```text
    src/my_package/
    ├── core.py
    └── services/
        └── billing.py
    ```
    
    these test paths are valid:
    
    ```text
    tests/
    ├── test_core.py
    ├── test_core_parsing.py
    └── services/
        ├── test_billing.py
        └── test_billing_refunds.py
    ```
    
    ## Installation
    
    ```console
    uv add --dev 'pytest-layout-enforcer @ git+https://github.com/marcusinthesky/pytest-layout-enforcer.git@4a1911f444e30328e7e01a0c885f24486807021b'
    ```
    
    This fork's reviewed fixes are available at the pinned Git revision above.
    JCOR installs it through its locked development environment; no PyPI release is
    needed. The Git installation is independent of the retained publishing workflow.
    
    The package uses `uv_build` and can be built locally with:
    
    ```console
    uv build
    ```
    
    ## Configuration
    
    Add at least one source-to-test mapping to the host project's
    `pyproject.toml`:
    
    ```toml
    [tool.pytest-layout-enforcer]
    enabled = true
    feature-pattern = "[a-z][a-z0-9_]*"
    feature-separator = "_"
    require-tests = false
    include-init = false
    include-packages = false
    
    exclude-sources = ["**/_version.py", "**/migrations/**"]
    exclude-tests = ["**/test_integration_*.py"]
    
    [[tool.pytest-layout-enforcer.layouts]]
    source = "src/my_package"
    tests = "tests"
    ```
    
    For tests stored inside the package, only the test root changes:
    
    ```toml
    [[tool.pytest-layout-enforcer.layouts]]
    source = "src/my_package"
    tests = "src/my_package/tests"
    ```
    
    Paths are relative to `pyproject.toml`. Add more layout tables for monorepos.
    Test roots must be disjoint; shared or nested roots are configuration errors.
    Missing source or test directories are violations, even with `require-tests = false`.
    An existing empty test directory is allowed unless source coverage is required.
    
    Set `include-packages = true` to let `services/billing/__init__.py` own
    `tests/services/test_billing.py` and feature variants such as
    `test_billing_refunds.py`. This is independent of `include-init`, which enables
    literal `test___init__.py` matching. The source-root initializer has no package
    alias. Package aliases are opt-in, and either alias tests the same initializer.
    
    Exclusions containing `/` match relative paths: `*`, `?`, and character classes
    match within a component; a complete `**` component matches zero or more
    directories. Thus `**/migrations/**` includes root-level migrations. Patterns
    without `/`, such as `_version.py`, match basenames at any depth.
    The tool ignores `__init__.py` by default and only examines files named
    `test_*.py` in test roots. `conftest.py` and test helper modules are therefore
    left alone.
    
    `require-tests = false` checks that every discovered test maps to a source
    module without requiring every source module to have tests. Set it to `true`
    to require at least one matching test file per source module.
    
    ## Usage
    
    The plugin runs automatically before pytest collection when configuration is
    present:
    
    ```console
    uv run pytest
    ```
    
    Run the same check without running tests:
    
    ```console
    uv run pytest-layout-enforcer check
    uv run pytest-layout-enforcer check --format json
    ```
    
    The command exits with status 0 on success, 1 for layout violations, and 2 for
    configuration errors.
    
    ## Publishing
    
    CI runs the test suite on Python 3.11 through 3.14 for every pull request and
    push to `main`. Version tags such as `v0.1.0` build, smoke-test, attest, and
    publish the wheel and source distribution to PyPI using Trusted Publishing.
    
    Before the first release:
    
    1. Create a GitHub environment named `pypi` in the repository settings.
    2. In the PyPI project's Publishing settings, add a GitHub Trusted Publisher
       for this repository, workflow `release.yml`, and environment `pypi`.
    3. Make sure the version in `pyproject.toml` matches the release tag.
    
    Then publish a release with:
    
    ```console
    git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "v0.1.0"
    git push origin main --follow-tags
    ```
    
    No PyPI API token or GitHub repository secret is required.
    
    ## Naming and ambiguity
    
    A module such as `data_loader.py` permits `test_data_loader.py` and feature
    files such as `test_data_loader_cache.py`. If a feature filename could refer
    to multiple modules—for example when both `data.py` and `data_loader.py`
    exist in the same directory—the tool reports an `ambiguous-test` violation instead of guessing.
    
    Directory-local matches take precedence over unrelated global names, with
    exact names preferred over feature interpretations within that directory.
    Global matches are used only to diagnose misplaced or ambiguous tests.
    
    For projects that prefer unambiguous names, configure a double underscore:
    
    ```toml
    [tool.pytest-layout-enforcer]
    feature-separator = "__"
    ```
    
    That produces names such as `test_data_loader__cache.py`.
    [build-system]
    requires = ["uv_build>=0.12.19,<0.13"]
    build-backend = "uv_build"
    
    [project]
    name = "pytest-layout-enforcer"
    version = "0.1.0"
    description = "Keep Python test layouts in sync with package layouts."
    readme = "README.md"
    requires-python = ">=3.11"
    license = "MIT"
    authors = [{ name = "Connor Charles" }]
    classifiers = [
        "Framework :: Pytest",
        "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
        "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
    ]
    dependencies = ["pytest>=8"]
    
    [project.scripts]
    pytest-layout-enforcer = "pytest_layout_enforcer.cli:main"
    
    [project.entry-points.pytest11]
    layout-enforcer = "pytest_layout_enforcer.plugin"
    
    [dependency-groups]
    dev = ["pytest>=8", "pytest-xdist>=3.6"]
    
    [tool.pytest.ini_options]
    addopts = "-ra"
    testpaths = ["tests"]
    
    [tool.pytest-layout-enforcer]
    
    [[tool.pytest-layout-enforcer.layouts]]
    source = "src/pytest_layout_enforcer"
    tests = "tests"

    ---
    description: "Semantic Python fingerprints and review-first DVC dependency patches that suppress non-executable pipeline churn without taking ownership of the stage graph."
    ---
    
    # semflow
    
    `semflow` resolves a DVC stage's installed Typer command, computes the conservative
    first-party symbol closure reachable from its callback, and replaces the stage's raw
    Python `deps:` entries with one deterministic entrypoint JSON fingerprint. DVC
    continues to own commands, data dependencies, parameters, outputs, matrices,
    `foreach`, caching, and frozen stages.
    
    ## Quickstart
    
    Use Python 3.13 and install `semflow` in the same uv environment as the Typer
    application named by your DVC commands:
    
    ```bash
    uv add git+ssh://git@github.com/marcusinthesky/semflow.git
    uv run semflow check
    uv run semflow patch
    uv run semflow patch --apply
    uv run semflow check
    ```
    
    Start with the [runnable example](examples/quickstart/dvc.yaml) and its
    [getting started guide](docs/getting-started.md). The first `check` exits 1 when
    fingerprints are stale; `patch` prints a diff without writing, and `--apply`
    accepts it. For pip environments, install with
    `python -m pip install 'git+ssh://git@github.com/marcusinthesky/semflow.git'`.
    GitHub access to the private repository is required. Pin a Git commit or tag
    for repeatable installation. The
    [Python API reference](docs/reference.md) covers programmatic use.
    
    Version 0.1 deliberately has three verbs:
    
    ```bash
    semflow check          # read-only; exit 1 when YAML or hashes are stale
    semflow patch          # print the exact unified diff; write nothing
    semflow patch --apply  # materialize the reviewed diff; atomic per file, YAML last
    semflow refresh --apply # materialize JSON changes only; refuse stale DVC YAML
    ```
    
    The same commands are available from the pipeline application as
    `pipeline semflow …`.
    
    `refresh` is the pure control-plane operation used by the optional DVC
    `semflow_refresh` stage. It recomputes the fingerprints but never adds, removes,
    or rewrites a dependency alias in `dvc.yaml`. Run `patch --apply` first when
    instrumentation itself is stale.
    
    ## Configuration
    
    `semflow.toml` is discovered from the current directory upward. A
    `[tool.semflow]` table in `pyproject.toml` is also supported.
    
    ```toml
    project-root = "."
    pipeline-file = "dvc.yaml"
    hash-dir = ".semflow/hashes"
    source-roots = [
      "src",
    ]
    
    # Optional when a console script is not installed in the active environment.
    [applications]
    example = "example.cli:app"
    
    [hashing]
    ignore-docstrings = true
    ignore-annotations = true
    ignore-type-checking-blocks = true
    
    [tracking]
    auto-typer = true
    control-stages = ["semflow_refresh"]
    ```
    
    With `auto-typer = true`, installed Typer callbacks referenced by DVC commands are
    tracked automatically. The stage's Python dependencies collapse to a path such as
    `.semflow/hashes/entrypoints/simulation/audit-kappa-identity.json`. Its `members`
    array records only the reachable functions, classes, globals, and import bindings,
    plus an explained whole-module fallback if a first-party reference cannot be
    resolved safely.
    
    Manual tracking uses an identity-preserving decorator, so Typer receives the same
    function object and signature:
    
    ```python
    from semflow import track
    
    
    @app.command("audit")
    @track(include=("example.audit:EXTRA_POLICY",))
    def audit() -> None: ...
    ```
    
    Set `auto-typer = false` to instrument only callbacks carrying `@track`. Explicit
    `include` entries use `module:symbol` syntax and seed the same transitive static
    closure. Paths outside `source-roots` remain ordinary DVC dependencies. Stages whose
    commands are outside the discovered applications retain file/directory fingerprint
    behavior for their declared Python deps.
    
    ## Safety contract
    
    - `patch` is preview-only unless `--apply` is explicit. Apply aborts if any planned
      file changed after the plan was built; fingerprint files are replaced atomically
      before the authored YAML is replaced last.
    - YAML editing is source-dependency-local: command folding, matrices, stage order,
      and unrelated comments remain byte-for-byte unchanged. A comment directly attached
      to a removed Python dependency is removed with that dependency rather than left
      misleadingly in place.
    - Generated JSON records the entrypoint, callback, normalization policy, aggregate
      digest, reachable member digests, and any conservative fallbacks; it contains no
      timestamps or host-specific values.
    - `check` must gate commits once the DVC patch is activated. Without that gate, a
      semantic source edit could leave a stale JSON proxy and suppress invalidation.
    - Configured `control-stages` are excluded from instrumentation discovery so a
      DVC refresh stage cannot instrument itself.
    - Annotation removal is opt-in and limited to undecorated function signatures and
      function-local annotations. Typer callbacks and decorated functions always retain
      annotations; class/module annotations remain semantic because dataclasses, Pydantic,
      and `NamedTuple` can consume them as runtime schema.
    
    The closure is static and first-party: direct names, imports, attributes, globals,
    decorators, defaults, and transitively reached symbols are followed. Runtime tracing
    is deliberately not authoritative, and string-driven dynamic imports are outside the
    initial contract. An unresolved static first-party edge hashes the owning module as a
    conservative fallback and records the reason in JSON.
    
    ## Development
    
    ```bash
    direnv allow
    just check
    just test
    just lint
    just watch
    ```
    
    The pinned devenv shell manages Python 3.13, uv, development dependencies, and
    the prek hooks. `just check` runs the same quality gates as CI; `just watch`
    reruns tests whenever package sources or tests change. Run `just docs-check`
    to validate the documentation site.
    
    See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the boundary decisions.
    project-root = "."
    pipeline-file = "dvc.yaml"
    hash-dir = ".semflow/hashes"
    source-roots = ["src"]
    
    [applications]
    example = "example.cli:app"
    
    [tracking]
    auto-typer = true
    stages:
      greet:
        cmd: example greet
        deps:
          - src/example/stage.py
          - data/name.txt
        outs:
          - data/greeting.txt
    [project]
    name = "semflow"
    version = "0.1.1"
    description = "Semantic Python fingerprints and review-first DVC dependency patches."
    readme = "README.md"
    requires-python = "~=3.13.0"
    dependencies = [
      "pyyaml>=6.0",
      "typer>=0.12.0",
    ]
    
    [project.scripts]

    [dependency-groups]

    [project.scripts]
    # Getting started
    
    `semflow` requires Python 3.13. Install it in the same environment as your
    Typer application so it can discover the application's console script:
    
    ```bash
    uv add git+ssh://git@github.com/marcusinthesky/semflow.git
    ```
    
    For a complete example, copy the files from the
    [quickstart project](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/semflow/tree/main/examples/quickstart)
    into a new directory. It contains an installable `example` command, one DVC
    stage, input data, and `semflow.toml`. Run `uv add` above in that directory; uv
    will install both the local application and `semflow` into one environment.
    
    `dvc.yaml` initially names a raw Python dependency:
    
    ```yaml
    stages:
      greet:
        cmd: example greet
        deps:
          - src/example/stage.py
          - data/name.txt
        outs:
          - data/greeting.txt
    ```
    
    Run the review sequence:
    
    ```bash
    uv run semflow check          # exit 1: the fingerprint is missing
    uv run semflow patch          # preview the proposed YAML and JSON changes
    uv run semflow patch --apply  # accept the reviewed changes
    uv run semflow check          # exit 0: the fingerprint is current
    ```
    
    The patch replaces the Python dependency with a generated entrypoint JSON
    fingerprint. The input data dependency remains in DVC. Commit the updated
    `dvc.yaml` and `.semflow/hashes` files, and make `semflow check` part of your
    project's CI before relying on fingerprints for DVC invalidation.
    
    After a semantic source edit, `uv run semflow refresh --apply` updates only the
    fingerprint JSON. If DVC instrumentation itself changes, preview and apply a
    full `patch` again. For pip environments, use
    `python -m pip install 'git+ssh://git@github.com/marcusinthesky/semflow.git'`
    in the application's environment. GitHub access to the private repository is
    required; pin a Git commit or tag for reproducibility.

    """Command-line interface for semantic fingerprint checks and patches."""
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    from pathlib import Path
    from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Annotated
    
    import typer
    
    from semflow.api import check as check_project
    from semflow.api import patch as patch_project
    from semflow.api import refresh as refresh_project
    from semflow.config import ConfigError
    from semflow.dvc import DvcPatchError
    
    if TYPE_CHECKING:
        from semflow.model import PatchPlan
    
    app = typer.Typer(
        help="Semantic Python fingerprints for DVC dependencies.",
        no_args_is_help=True,
    )
    
    ConfigOption = Annotated[
        Path | None,
        typer.Option(
            "--config",
            help="semflow.toml or pyproject.toml containing [tool.semflow].",
            dir_okay=False,
            readable=True,
            resolve_path=True,
        ),
    ]
    
    
    @app.command("check")
    def check_command(config: ConfigOption = None) -> None:
        """Fail when DVC instrumentation or semantic hash JSON is stale."""
        try:
            plan = check_project(config)
        except (ConfigError, DvcPatchError) as error:
            typer.echo(f"semflow: {error}", err=True)
            raise typer.Exit(code=2) from error
        if plan.clean:
            typer.echo("semflow: fingerprints are current.")
            return
        typer.echo(_summary(plan), err=True)
        typer.echo("Run `semflow patch` to review the required changes.", err=True)
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)
    
    
    @app.command("patch")
    def patch_command(
        config: ConfigOption = None,
        *,
        apply: Annotated[
            bool,
            typer.Option(
                "--apply",
                help="Write the reviewed DVC YAML and fingerprint changes.",
            ),
        ] = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Preview a unified diff, or atomically apply it with --apply."""
        try:
            plan = patch_project(config, apply=apply)
        except (ConfigError, DvcPatchError) as error:
            typer.echo(f"semflow: {error}", err=True)
            raise typer.Exit(code=2) from error
        if plan.clean:
            typer.echo("semflow: no patch required.")
            return
        if apply:
            typer.echo(f"semflow: applied {len(plan.changes)} file change(s).")
            return
        typer.echo(plan.diff(), nl=False)
    
    
    @app.command("refresh")
    def refresh_command(
        config: ConfigOption = None,
        *,
        apply: Annotated[
            bool,
            typer.Option(
                "--apply",
                help="Write only the reviewed fingerprint JSON changes.",
            ),
        ] = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Preview or apply fingerprint JSON changes without rewriting DVC YAML."""
        try:
            plan = refresh_project(config, apply=apply)
        except (ConfigError, DvcPatchError) as error:
            typer.echo(f"semflow: {error}", err=True)
            raise typer.Exit(code=2) from error
        if plan.clean:
            typer.echo("semflow: fingerprints are current.")
            return
        if apply:
            typer.echo(f"semflow: refreshed {len(plan.changes)} fingerprint file(s).")
            return
        typer.echo(plan.diff(), nl=False)
    
    
    def _summary(plan: PatchPlan) -> str:
        changes = plan.changes
        counts = {
            operation: sum(change.operation == operation for change in changes)
            for operation in ("create", "update", "delete")
        }
        rendered = ", ".join(
            f"{count} {operation}" for operation, count in counts.items() if count
        )
        return f"semflow: patch required ({rendered})."
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        app()

    """Command-line interface for pytest-layout-enforcer."""
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import argparse
    import json
    from pathlib import Path
    import sys
    from collections.abc import Sequence
    
    from .checker import CheckResult, check_layout
    from .config import Config, ConfigError, find_pyproject
    
    
    def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
            prog="pytest-layout-enforcer",
            description="Enforce mirrored source and test layouts.",
        )
        subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
        check = subparsers.add_parser("check", help="check the configured layouts")
        check.add_argument(
            "--root",
            type=Path,
            default=Path.cwd(),
            help="project directory or pyproject.toml (default: current directory)",
        )
        check.add_argument(
            "--format",
            choices=("text", "json"),
            default="text",
            help="output format (default: text)",
        )
        return parser
    
    
    def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
        args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
        try:
            pyproject = (
                args.root.resolve()
                if args.root.name == "pyproject.toml"
                else find_pyproject(args.root)
            )
            config = Config.from_pyproject(pyproject)
            if config is None:
                raise ConfigError(
                    f"{pyproject} has no [tool.pytest-layout-enforcer] configuration"
                )
        except ConfigError as error:
            if args.format == "json":
                print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "error": str(error)}, indent=2))
            else:
                print(f"configuration error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
    
        if not config.enabled:
            if args.format == "json":
                print(
                    json.dumps({"ok": True, "enabled": False, "violations": []}, indent=2)
                )
            else:
                print("pytest-layout-enforcer is disabled")
            return 0
    
        result = check_layout(config)
        if args.format == "json":
            print(json.dumps(result.as_dict(), indent=2))
        else:
            _print_text(result)
        return 0 if result.ok else 1
    
    
    def _print_text(result: CheckResult) -> None:
        if result.ok:
            print(
                f"layout check passed ({result.source_count} source modules, "
                f"{result.test_count} test files)"
            )
            return
    
        for violation in result.violations:
            data = violation.as_dict(result.root)
            print(f"{data['path']}: {violation.code}: {violation.message}")
            for expected in data["expected"]:
                print(f"  expected: {expected}")
        count = len(result.violations)
        print(f"layout check failed with {count} violation{'s' if count != 1 else ''}")
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        raise SystemExit(main())

    class DvcPatchError(ValueError):
        """Raised when a DVC dependency cannot be instrumented unambiguously."""
    
    
    def build_patch(config: Config) -> PatchPlan:
        """Compute the exact DVC YAML and fingerprint changes without writing them."""
        pipeline_text = config.pipeline_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        try:
            authored_stages = stage_nodes(pipeline_text)
            variables = _pipeline_variables(pipeline_text)
        except (YamlPatchError, yaml.YAMLError) as error:
            raise DvcPatchError(str(error)) from error
    
        try:
            index = ModuleIndex(
                project_root=config.project_root,
                source_roots=config.source_roots,
            )
        except ModuleIndexError as error:
            raise DvcPatchError(str(error)) from error
        applications = available_applications(config.applications)
        replacements: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = []
        desired_files: dict[Path, str] = {}
        expected_fingerprints: set[Path] = set()
        entrypoint_cache: dict[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]], EntrypointFingerprint] = {}
        found_python = False
    
        for stage in authored_stages:
            if stage.name in config.control_stages:
                continue
            raw_dependencies = _raw_python_dependencies(config, stage)
            entrypoint_dependencies = tuple(
                dependency
                for dependency in stage.dependencies
                if _is_entrypoint_dependency(config, dependency.value)
            )
            if not raw_dependencies and not entrypoint_dependencies:
                continue
            found_python = True
            _plan_stage(
                config,
                stage,
                raw_dependencies=raw_dependencies,
                fingerprint_dependencies=entrypoint_dependencies,
                variables=variables,
                applications=applications,
                pipeline_text=pipeline_text,
                index=index,
                cache=entrypoint_cache,
                desired_files=desired_files,
                expected_fingerprints=expected_fingerprints,
                replacements=replacements,
            )
    
        if not found_python:
            msg = f"No Python dependencies found in {config.pipeline_file}."
            raise DvcPatchError(msg)
    
        try:
            desired_pipeline = replace_spans(pipeline_text, replacements)
        except YamlPatchError as error:
            raise DvcPatchError(str(error)) from error
        changes = _desired_changes(desired_files)
        changes.extend(_orphan_changes(config, expected_fingerprints))
        if desired_pipeline != pipeline_text:
            changes.append(
                FileChange(
                    path=config.pipeline_file,
                    before=pipeline_text,
                    after=desired_pipeline,
                )
            )
        changes.sort(key=lambda change: change.path.relative_to(config.project_root))
        return PatchPlan(
            root=config.project_root,
            pipeline_file=config.pipeline_file,
            changes=tuple(changes),
        )
    
    
    def build_refresh(config: Config) -> PatchPlan:
        """Compute a JSON-only refresh after DVC instrumentation is current."""
    """Stable programmatic API for checking, previewing, and applying semflow state."""
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
    
    from semflow.config import Config, load_config
    from semflow.dvc import apply_patch, apply_refresh, build_patch, build_refresh
    
    if TYPE_CHECKING:
        from pathlib import Path
    
        from semflow.model import PatchPlan
    
    
    def check(config: Config | Path | None = None) -> PatchPlan:
        """Return the changes required to make semantic fingerprints current."""
        return build_patch(_resolve_config(config))
    
    
    def patch(
        config: Config | Path | None = None,
        *,
        apply: bool = False,
    ) -> PatchPlan:
        """Build a patch and optionally apply it to the configured repository."""
        plan = check(config)
        if apply and not plan.clean:
            apply_patch(plan)
        return plan
    
    
    def refresh(
        config: Config | Path | None = None,
        *,
        apply: bool = False,
    ) -> PatchPlan:
        """Build or apply a JSON-only fingerprint refresh plan."""
        plan = build_refresh(_resolve_config(config))
        if apply and not plan.clean:
            apply_refresh(plan)
        return plan
    
    
    def _resolve_config(config: Config | Path | None) -> Config:
        if isinstance(config, Config):
            return config
        return load_config(config)

Set up **Semflow** and **pytest-layout-enforcer** with pinned Git revisions, local commands, pre-commit hooks and CI checks.

Tach enforces import boundaries and selects impacted tests; it does not enforce test-file placement, so the layout plugin fills that gap. The plugin checks existing test paths without requiring every source module to have a test. [Tach command documentation](https://docs.gauge.sh/usage/commands/)

Semflow is configured in [semflow.toml](/home/marcussky/Git/CCFinance/semflow.toml). Once a Python DVC stage exists, use `just semflow-patch` to review its fingerprints and `just semflow-apply` to create them. Its check currently skips fingerprint comparison because the DVC stage map is empty; the pinned Semflow version requires a Python dependency once stages are present.

    mod latex 'src/latex/justfile'
    workflow := "env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py"
    
    # Discover this project's commands.
    default:
        @just --list
    
    # Prepare locked dependencies and Git hooks (uses the network).
    setup:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py prepare
        just python::setup
        just latex::setup
        prek install
    
    # Check source, views and selected languages without repairing files.
    check:
        bash infra/nix/check.sh
        {{ workflow }} check
        just python::check
        just latex::check
        just data-check
        just semflow-check
        just changelog-check
    
    
    # Run the selected language tests.
    test:
        just python::test
        just latex::test
    
    # Explicitly format sources.
    fmt:
        nixfmt devenv.nix infra/nix/devenv.nix infra/nix/pkgs/schematter.nix
        rumdl fmt .
        just python::fmt
        just latex::fmt
    
    # Check external links online.
    links:
        git ls-files -z '*.md' | xargs -0 -r lychee --config lychee.toml --no-progress
    
    # Run root-level DVC using the locked Python environment.
    dvc *args:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen dvc "$@"
    
    # Validate DVC metadata without fetching data.
    data-check:
        just dvc status
        just dvc dag
    
    # Refresh generated planning and reference views.
    sync:
        {{ workflow }} sync
    
    # Validate document schemas, links and generated views.
    context-check:
        {{ workflow }} check
    
    # Create a plan without overwriting existing content.
    plan-new slug title:
        {{ workflow }} plan-new "$1" --title "$2"
    
    # Create a task inside an existing plan or task.
    task-new parent slug title:
        {{ workflow }} task-new "$1" "$2" --title "$3"
    
    # Create a local reference record with its directory as citation key.
    reference-new key title:
        {{ workflow }} reference-new "$1" --title "$2"
    
    # Validate the repository changelog structure and change categories.
    changelog-check:
        schematter validate --schema infra/schemas/documents/changelog.document-schema.yaml CHANGELOG.md
    
    # Check semantic fingerprints once DVC has executable stages.
    semflow-check:
        if env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen python -c 'import pathlib, sys, yaml; from semflow.config import load_config; load_config(); doc = yaml.safe_load(pathlib.Path("dvc.yaml").read_text()); sys.exit(0 if isinstance(doc, dict) and doc.get("stages") == {} else 1)'; then echo 'Semflow: no DVC stages to instrument.'; else env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow check; fi
    
    # Preview the semantic dependency changes before applying them.
    semflow-patch:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow patch
    
    # Apply reviewed DVC and semantic fingerprint changes.
    semflow-apply:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow patch --apply
    
    # Refresh existing semantic fingerprints without editing the DVC graph.
    semflow-refresh:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow refresh --apply

    ---
    description: Choose independent workflows, languages and integrations.
    ---
    
    # Choose only what you need
    
    There are no starter profiles. Workflow and language selections default to empty.
    You can select TypeScript alone, references without planning, or Lean without
    a manuscript.
    
    ## Markdown workflows
    
    | Selection | Adds |
    | --- | --- |
    | `planning` | Plans, nested tasks, a roadmap and local child views |
    | `reference` | Citation records, an index and declared backlinks |
    
    Either selection installs Insitu and the document validators. With neither
    selected, the project has no workflow environment or context tree.
    
    Reference records live in `.context/reference/KEY/README.md`. Flat CSL fields
    describe the source; the directory supplies its citation key. References plus
    LaTeX derive the manuscript bibliography automatically during `just sync`.
    Without reference records, LaTeX owns its ordinary `refs.bib` directly.
    
    ## Languages
    
    | Selection | First useful result |
    | --- | --- |
    | `python` | Typed library imported by an application in a locked uv workspace |
    | `typescript` | Bun library imported by a runnable CLI workspace |
    | `lean` | Mathlib proofs with LeanArchitect annotations and a LeanBlueprint graph/PDF |
    | `latex` | A Tectonic article with cached local builds |
    
    Each language has a local README and namespaced commands. Python and TypeScript
    retain their library/application package boundaries. Lean includes its blueprint
    tooling even when manuscript LaTeX is absent.
    
    ## Integrations
    
    AgentSync optionally projects shared instructions into Codex and/or Claude
    configuration. Nix builds its pinned Rust CLI; no npm installation is needed.
    Its Python preflight stops on authored destinations; migrate those files
    deliberately. Without it, the README and agent prompt remain useful; projects may author their own instructions.
    
    SecretSpec optionally resolves declared credentials for `just secret-run COMMAND`.
    Shell entry and ordinary checks never load secrets. Configure a provider when a
    real project needs one; never put secret values in Copier answers.
    
    Nix supplies the reproducible environment for every project. There is no empty
    Terraform/Kubernetes scaffold or automatic deployment.
    ---
    description: Update structure while preserving authored records.
    ---
    
    # Keep the project current
    
    Commit local work and keep `.copier-answers.yml` under version control:
    
    ```bash
    env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME uvx --from copier==9.16.0 copier update
    ```
    
    Review changes and conflicts, then run `just setup`, `just sync` when available,
    and `just check`. Copier selects the latest stable tag from the source saved in
    `.copier-answers.yml`. Projects created from Exordio releases use
    `gh:marcusinthesky/exordio`. To target a particular release, add
    `--vcs-ref v0.1.0`, substituting the desired tag.
    
    ## Add a feature
    
    Use Copier's questionnaire and retain existing selections. Saved empty lists
    remain authoritative. Plans, tasks and references created by commands belong to
    your project and never occur in template output.
    
    ## Preserve agent instructions
    
    When enabling AgentSync, existing authored destinations or unexpected links
    stop apply before any destination is changed. Merge intended instructions into
    the canonical `.agents/` sources, preserve them in Git, then deliberately remove
    old destinations and stop tracking generated links. Follow the generated
    AgentSync README before applying again.
    
    ## Migrate deliberately
    
    Removing capabilities or adopting into an existing repository is a manual
    migration. Copier can remove previously owned paths, including customized code.
    Use a branch, preserve retained content and inspect a trial update.
    
    Projects from the earlier profile/stack prototype need regeneration or a manual
    migration; there is no legacy converter. A project created from another source
    repository keeps that source in its Copier answers; it does not switch to
    Exordio automatically.

    name: CI
    on:
      pull_request:
        types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, ready_for_review, converted_to_draft]
      push:
        branches: [main]
      workflow_dispatch:
    permissions:
      contents: read
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    jobs:
      check:
        # Draft PRs emit a skipped run; compute-heavy checks only run when ready.
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.draft == false }}
        env:
          TECTONIC_CACHE_DIR: /tmp/exordio-tectonic-cache
        strategy:
          matrix:
            runner: [ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-24.04-arm]
        runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262
            with:
              persist-credentials: false
          - name: Free hosted runner disk space
            run: |
              df -h /
              sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /usr/local/share/powershell /opt/ghc
              df -h /
          # cache-nix-action requires a store writable by the runner user.
          - uses: nixbuild/nix-quick-install-action@9f63be77f412a248c9d9a65a4c82cf066cdf8f0c # v35
            with:
              nix_version: 2.34.7
          - uses: nix-community/cache-nix-action@135667ec418502fa5a3598af6fb9eb733888ce6a
            if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
            with:
              primary-key: nix-single-user-v1-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('devenv.lock', 'devenv.nix', 'infra/nix/**') }}
              restore-prefixes-first-match: nix-single-user-v1-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
          - uses: actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830
            if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
            with:
