    description: Optional native Codex and Claude configuration managed by AgentSync.
    ---
    
    # Agent configuration
    
    Canonical instructions and skills live here. Nix builds the pinned AgentSync release with Cargo. Run
    `just agents::apply` to create native links.
    `just agents::check` verifies their state. Setup performs no model calls.
    
    Codex reads root AGENTS.md and its native TOML configuration; Claude reads
    CLAUDE.md, skills and native settings. Shared instructions point to local
    README and architecture documents rather than copying their content.
    
    ## Preserve existing instructions
    
    Before applying links, a preflight checks every selected destination. Existing
    files, skills directories, unexpected links and symlinked parent directories stop
    the operation before any native target changes. Already-correct managed links are
    safe to apply again. No backup or automatic merge replaces your existing rules.
    
    When adding agents to an existing project:
    
    1. Read each reported target and its canonical source in `.agents/`. Merge the
       instructions, settings or skills you want to keep into that source, then review
       the changes. For example, merge root `AGENTS.md` into `.agents/AGENTS.md`.
    2. After preserving its contents, remove the old target. If Git tracks it, use
       `git rm PATH` so the generated native link will be ignored. Keep the canonical
       `.agents/` source under version control.
    3. Run `just agents::apply`, then `just agents::check`. Review the Git diff before
       committing; native files should now link to your canonical sources.
    
    The preflight reads `agentsync.toml`, so its targets remain the single source of
    truth. It is a standard-library Python script under src/python/scripts/agent_preflight/,
    run with its committed PEP 723 lock. Bun is needed only for TypeScript.
    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    
    # Inspect every destination before the native CLI changes any links.
    apply:
        cd .. && env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --script src/python/scripts/agent_preflight/script.py
        cd .. && agentsync apply
    
    check:
        cd .. && agentsync status
        cd .. && agentsync apply --dry-run
        cd .. && agentsync doctor
    source_dir = "."
    default_agents = [[ agents | tojson ]]
    
    [gitignore]
    enabled = false
    
    [% if 'codex' in agents %]
    [agents.codex]
    enabled = true
    [agents.codex.targets.instructions]
    source = "AGENTS.md"
    destination = "AGENTS.md"
    type = "symlink"
    [agents.codex.targets.settings]
    source = "codex.toml"
    destination = ".codex/config.toml"
    type = "symlink"
    [agents.codex.targets.skills]
    source = "skills"
    destination = ".codex/skills"

    # Agent preflight
    
    `just agents::apply` runs this zero-dependency Python script before native
    AgentSync. It reads `.agents/agentsync.toml`, preserves authored destinations,
    rejects unexpected links and symlinked parents, and accepts correct managed
    links on repeated runs. Canonical source paths must stay inside the repository
    without symlink aliases. No configuration is written by this check.
    
    PEP 723 metadata and `script.py.lock` keep this utility independent of the
    optional Python application workspace. Its interpreter comes from Devenv.

    description: Create and maintain repository plans, references and task views with local commands.
    ---
    
    # Repository workflow
    
    Read the root README and the relevant local README before changing records.
    Use `just --list` to discover the installed workflow and language commands. Create
    records through their commands, edit canonical metadata, then run `just sync`
    when available and `just check`. Keep task parents terse and store detailed
    evidence in linked records. Verification establishes only what the actual
    command output supports; record incomplete or inconclusive checks honestly.

      lib,
      rustPlatform,
      fetchFromGitHub,
      cmake,
      pkg-config,
      zlib,
      git,
    }:
    rustPlatform.buildRustPackage {
      pname = "agentsync";
      version = "1.45.2";
    
      src = fetchFromGitHub {
        owner = "dallay";
        repo = "agentsync";
        rev = "80333b6269bec5702d23f9ccca41335ddbe9bce1";
        hash = "sha256-pthsvCW3W1bUoXtng2sWcry2w5HpTKFiqiA3ndd86aM=";
      };
      cargoHash = "sha256-juIEEmDKjG5yTARQ5Zd2HBbRuYJB5ugFjjHk3GVTzDg=";
    
      nativeBuildInputs = [
        cmake
        pkg-config
      ];
      buildInputs = [ zlib ];
      nativeCheckInputs = [ git ];
      cargoTestFlags = [ "--lib" ];
    
      meta = {
        description = "Synchronize coding-agent instructions and configuration";
        homepage = "https://github.com/dallay/agentsync";
        license = lib.licenses.mit;
        mainProgram = "agentsync";
        platforms = [
          "x86_64-linux"
          "aarch64-linux"
        ];
      };
    }
    # /// script
    # requires-python = ">=3.13,<3.14"
    # dependencies = []
    # ///
    """Refuse agent configuration collisions before AgentSync creates any links."""
    
    import os
    import stat
    import sys
    import tomllib
    from pathlib import Path
    
    ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
    CONFIGURATION = ROOT / ".agents"
    
    
    def absolute(base: Path, value: str) -> Path:
        """Normalize traversal without following links that must be inspected first."""
        return Path(os.path.abspath(base / value))
    
    
    def inspect(path: Path) -> os.stat_result | None:
        try:
            return path.lstat()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return None
    
    
    def parent_collision(path: Path) -> str | None:
        for parent in path.parents:
            if parent == ROOT:
                break
            state = inspect(parent)
            if state and stat.S_ISLNK(state.st_mode):
                return f"{parent.relative_to(ROOT)} is a symlink"
            if state and not stat.S_ISDIR(state.st_mode):
                return f"{parent.relative_to(ROOT)} is not a directory"
        return None
    
    
    def main() -> int:
        with (CONFIGURATION / "agentsync.toml").open("rb") as stream:
            configuration = tomllib.load(stream)
        source_directory = absolute(CONFIGURATION, configuration.get("source_dir", "."))
        selected = configuration.get("default_agents")
        if not isinstance(selected, list) or not selected:
            raise ValueError("default_agents must explicitly select the configured agents")
        collisions = []
        destinations = {}
        for agent in selected:
            settings = configuration.get("agents", {}).get(agent, {})
            if settings.get("enabled") is False:
                continue
            if not settings.get("targets"):
                raise ValueError(f"{agent} must explicitly configure its native targets")
            for target in settings["targets"].values():
                source = absolute(source_directory, target["source"])
                destination = absolute(ROOT, target["destination"])
                label = os.path.relpath(destination, ROOT)
                if (
                    any(
                        path == ROOT or not path.is_relative_to(ROOT)
                        for path in (source, destination)
                    )
                    or target.get("type") != "symlink"
                ):
                    collisions.append(
                        f"{label}: targets must use repository-owned sources "
                        "and native symlinks"
                    )

    ---
    description: Check AgentSync's complete target set before creating any native links.
    ---
    
    # Agent preflight
    
    `just agents::apply` runs this zero-dependency Python script before native
    AgentSync. It reads `.agents/agentsync.toml`, preserves authored destinations,
    rejects unexpected links and symlinked parents, and accepts correct managed
    links on repeated runs. Canonical source paths must stay inside the repository
    without symlink aliases. No configuration is written by this check.
    
    PEP 723 metadata and `script.py.lock` keep this utility independent of the
    optional Python application workspace. Its interpreter comes from Devenv.
    # /// script
    # requires-python = ">=3.13,<3.14"
    # dependencies = []
    # ///
    """Refuse agent configuration collisions before AgentSync creates any links."""
    
    import os
    import stat
    import sys
    import tomllib
    from pathlib import Path
    
    ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
    CONFIGURATION = ROOT / ".agents"
    
    
    def absolute(base: Path, value: str) -> Path:
        """Normalize traversal without following links that must be inspected first."""
        return Path(os.path.abspath(base / value))
    
    
    def inspect(path: Path) -> os.stat_result | None:
        """Inspect a path without following symlinks."""
        try:
            return path.lstat()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return None
    
    
    def parent_collision(path: Path) -> str | None:
        """Report unsafe destination parents."""
        for parent in path.parents:
            if parent == ROOT:
                break
            state = inspect(parent)
            if state and stat.S_ISLNK(state.st_mode):
                return f"{parent.relative_to(ROOT)} is a symlink"
            if state and not stat.S_ISDIR(state.st_mode):
                return f"{parent.relative_to(ROOT)} is not a directory"
        return None
    
    
    def main() -> int:
        """Validate all selected AgentSync targets."""
        with (CONFIGURATION / "agentsync.toml").open("rb") as stream:
            configuration = tomllib.load(stream)
        source_directory = absolute(CONFIGURATION, configuration.get("source_dir", "."))
        selected = configuration.get("default_agents")
        if not isinstance(selected, list) or not selected:
            raise ValueError("default_agents must explicitly select the configured agents")
        collisions = []
        destinations = {}
        for agent in selected:
            settings = configuration.get("agents", {}).get(agent, {})
            if settings.get("enabled") is False:
                continue
            if not settings.get("targets"):
                raise ValueError(f"{agent} must explicitly configure its native targets")
            for target in settings["targets"].values():
                source = absolute(source_directory, target["source"])
                destination = absolute(ROOT, target["destination"])
                label = os.path.relpath(destination, ROOT)
                if (
                    any(
                        path == ROOT or not path.is_relative_to(ROOT)
                        for path in (source, destination)
                    )
                    or target.get("type") != "symlink"
                ):
                    collisions.append(
                        f"{label}: targets must use repository-owned sources "
                        "and native symlinks"
                    )
                    continue
                if destination in destinations:
                    if destinations[destination] != source:
                        collisions.append(
                            f"{label}: more than one canonical source claims this target"
                        )
                    continue
                destinations[destination] = source
                problem = parent_collision(source) or parent_collision(destination)
                if problem:
                    collisions.append(f"{label}: {problem}")
                    continue
                source_state = inspect(source)
                if source_state is None:
                    collisions.append(
                        f"{label}: source {source.relative_to(ROOT)} is missing"
                    )
                    continue
                if stat.S_ISLNK(source_state.st_mode):
                    collisions.append(
                        f"{label}: source {source.relative_to(ROOT)} is a symlink"
                    )
                    continue
                state = inspect(destination)
                if state is None:
                    continue
                if (
                    stat.S_ISLNK(state.st_mode)
                    and absolute(destination.parent, os.readlink(destination)) == source
                ):
                    continue
                collisions.append(
                    f"{label}: preserve its contents in {source.relative_to(ROOT)} first"
                )
        if not collisions:
            return 0
        print("Agent setup stopped before changing any native targets:", file=sys.stderr)
        for collision in collisions:
            print(f"- {collision}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(
            "Merge existing instructions, settings or skills into their .agents sources, "
            "then remove the old targets only after preserving their contents. "
            "Stop tracking native targets in Git before applying managed links. "
            "See .agents/README.md.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 1
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        try:
            raise SystemExit(main())
        except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as error:
            print(f"Agent preflight: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
            raise SystemExit(1) from None
    ---
    description: Optional native Codex and Claude configuration managed by AgentSync.
    ---
    
    # Agent configuration
    
    Canonical instructions and skills live here. Nix builds the pinned AgentSync release with Cargo. Run
    `just agents::apply` to create native links.
    `just agents::check` verifies their state. Setup performs no model calls.
    
    Codex reads root AGENTS.md and its native TOML configuration; Claude reads
    CLAUDE.md, skills and native settings. Shared instructions point to local
    README and architecture documents rather than copying their content.
    
    ## Preserve existing instructions
    
    Before applying links, a preflight checks every selected destination. Existing
    files, skills directories, unexpected links and symlinked parent directories stop
    the operation before any native target changes. Already-correct managed links are
    safe to apply again. No backup or automatic merge replaces your existing rules.
    
    When adding agents to an existing project:
    
    1. Read each reported target and its canonical source in `.agents/`. Merge the
       instructions, settings or skills you want to keep into that source, then review
       the changes. For example, merge root `AGENTS.md` into `.agents/AGENTS.md`.
    2. After preserving its contents, remove the old target. If Git tracks it, use
       `git rm PATH` so the generated native link will be ignored. Keep the canonical
       `.agents/` source under version control.
    3. Run `just agents::apply`, then `just agents::check`. Review the Git diff before
       committing; native files should now link to your canonical sources.
    
    The preflight reads `agentsync.toml`, so its targets remain the single source of
    truth. It is a standard-library Python script under src/python/scripts/agent_preflight/,
    run with its committed PEP 723 lock. Bun is needed only for TypeScript.
    source_dir = "."
    default_agents = ["codex"]
    
    [gitignore]
    enabled = false
    
    [agents.codex]
    enabled = true
    [agents.codex.targets.instructions]
    source = "AGENTS.md"
    destination = "AGENTS.md"
    type = "symlink"
    [agents.codex.targets.settings]
    source = "codex.toml"
    destination = ".codex/config.toml"
    type = "symlink"
    [agents.codex.targets.skills]
    source = "skills"
    destination = ".codex/skills"
    type = "symlink"
    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    
    # Inspect every destination before the native CLI changes any links.
    apply:
        cd .. && env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --script src/python/scripts/agent_preflight/script.py
        cd .. && agentsync apply
    
    check:
        cd .. && agentsync status
        cd .. && agentsync apply --dry-run
        cd .. && agentsync doctor
    # Agent contract
    
    - Read the nearest README.md for commands and ARCHITECTURE.md for design decisions.
    - Use the pinned devenv environment and repository just commands.
    - Run Python commands through the appropriate locked uv project.
    - Authored records own state. Use explicit creation and synchronization commands; never edit generated Insitu regions by hand.
    - Task parents expose immediate children. Put supporting evidence in separate records and preserve stable paths.
    - Checks validate without repair; use just fmt and just sync for explicit changes.
    - Run just check before handoff and report any checks that could not run.
    - Resolve secrets only for commands that need them. Never place credentials in tracked files.

    ---
    description: Recover from setup and validation failures.
    ---
    
    # Troubleshooting
    
    ## The shell does not start
    
    Check that Nix is installed and its daemon is available. Run
    `bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh` to install the CLI version matching the lock,
    then enter `devenv shell`. Linux x86-64 and ARM64 are supported.
    
    ## A dependency or native executable is missing
    
    Run `just setup` inside the pinned shell. Setup prepares frozen environments
    and native runtime paths without rewriting locks. It needs network access.
    Checks use installed dependencies and do not fetch missing inputs.
    
    For Lean, use `just lean::setup` after a fresh checkout. Blueprint rendering needs
    the Graphviz/compiler dependencies supplied by Lean's own environment.
    Read the Lean README before changing Lean, Mathlib or Architect versions.
    
    ## A view or bibliography is stale
    
    Edit the source record, then run `just sync` and `just check`. Do not repair a
    generated table manually. With references and LaTeX, source citation metadata
    belongs in reference records rather than the exported bibliography.
    
    ## A task cannot finish
    
    `done` needs at least one nonempty active acceptance criterion, all checked.
    Use `closed` with a reason for discontinued work. Finish or close children before
    making their parent terminal. Neither state propagates automatically.
    
    ## A declared link fails
    
    Use the exact repository-relative filename suggested by the error. Directories,
    URLs and section fragments belong in normal body links rather than `links`.
    
    ## AgentSync refuses to apply
    
    Preserve the authored destination, merge its intended content into canonical
    `.agents/` sources, and follow their README before removing old native files.
    Preflight checks all destinations before apply. It does not hide collisions
    in ignored backups.
    
    ## A preview destination already exists
    
    Choose a new directory for `just render`. This deliberate guard prevents
    overwriting a previous preview. The command renders local uncommitted changes.
    
    ## An update conflicts
    
    Resolve conflicts before setup/synchronization and check the diff.
    Removing a feature and migrating the old profile-based preview require manual
    review; see [updates](updates.md).

## Assistant

AgentSync does not require it to run, but I recommend keeping it while `just setup` applies agent configuration automatically.

I tested the pinned AgentSync in temporary directories. With an existing `AGENTS.md` or `.codex/config.toml`, it moved the file to a `.bak` and replaced it with a link. It also replaced an unrelated skills symlink. The preflight instead checks all destinations first and stops without changing any of them.

The tradeoff is a small amount of repository code to maintain. Once this repo’s configuration is established, the practical risk is lower, but the guard still protects fresh checkouts and anyone with existing local Codex settings. It applies when using `just agents::apply`; calling `agentsync apply` directly bypasses it.

## User

COuld we not just use the agensync cli and just (without any python)?

## Assistant

Yes. AgentSync can manage the links directly; I’ll simplify the recipes to use its CLI and document how it handles existing destinations.

    ---
    description: Update structure while preserving authored records.
    ---
    
    # Keep the project current
    
    Commit local work and keep `.copier-answers.yml` under version control:
    
    ```bash
    env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME uvx --from copier==9.16.0 copier update
    ```
    
    Review changes and conflicts, then run `just setup`, `just sync` when available,
    and `just check`. Copier selects the latest stable tag from the source saved in
    `.copier-answers.yml`. Projects created from Exordio releases use
    `gh:marcusinthesky/exordio`. To target a particular release, add
    `--vcs-ref v0.1.0`, substituting the desired tag.
    
    ## Add a feature
    
    Use Copier's questionnaire and retain existing selections. Saved empty lists
    remain authoritative. Plans, tasks and references created by commands belong to
    your project and never occur in template output.
    
    ## Preserve agent instructions
    
    When enabling AgentSync, existing authored destinations or unexpected links
    stop apply before any destination is changed. Merge intended instructions into
    the canonical `.agents/` sources, preserve them in Git, then deliberately remove
    old destinations and stop tracking generated links. Follow the generated
    AgentSync README before applying again.
    
    ## Migrate deliberately
    
    Removing capabilities or adopting into an existing repository is a manual
    migration. Copier can remove previously owned paths, including customized code.
    Use a branch, preserve retained content and inspect a trial update.
    
    Projects from the earlier profile/stack prototype need regeneration or a manual
    migration; there is no legacy converter. A project created from another source
    repository keeps that source in its Copier answers; it does not switch to
    Exordio automatically.

    - Read the nearest README.md for commands and ARCHITECTURE.md for design decisions.
    - Use the pinned devenv environment and repository just commands.
    - Run Python commands through the appropriate locked uv project.
    - Authored records own state. Use explicit creation and synchronization commands; never edit generated Insitu regions by hand.

    ---
    description: Optional native Codex and Claude configuration managed by AgentSync.
    ---
    
    # Agent configuration
    
    Canonical instructions and skills live here. Nix builds the pinned AgentSync release with Cargo. Run
    `just agents::apply` to create native links.
    `just agents::check` verifies their state. Setup performs no model calls.
    
    Codex reads root AGENTS.md and its native TOML configuration; Claude reads
    CLAUDE.md, skills and native settings. Shared instructions point to local
    README and architecture documents rather than copying their content.
    
    ## Preserve existing instructions
    
    Before applying links, a preflight checks every selected destination. Existing
    files, skills directories, unexpected links and symlinked parent directories stop
    the operation before any native target changes. Already-correct managed links are
    safe to apply again. No backup or automatic merge replaces your existing rules.
    
    When adding agents to an existing project:
    
    1. Read each reported target and its canonical source in `.agents/`. Merge the
       instructions, settings or skills you want to keep into that source, then review
       the changes. For example, merge root `AGENTS.md` into `.agents/AGENTS.md`.
    2. After preserving its contents, remove the old target. If Git tracks it, use
       `git rm PATH` so the generated native link will be ignored. Keep the canonical
       `.agents/` source under version control.
    3. Run `just agents::apply`, then `just agents::check`. Review the Git diff before
       committing; native files should now link to your canonical sources.
    
    The preflight reads `agentsync.toml`, so its targets remain the single source of
    truth. It is a standard-library Python script under src/python/scripts/agent_preflight/,
    run with its committed PEP 723 lock. Bun is needed only for TypeScript.
    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    
    # Inspect every destination before the native CLI changes any links.
    apply:
        cd .. && env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --script src/python/scripts/agent_preflight/script.py
        cd .. && agentsync apply
    
    check:
        cd .. && agentsync status
        cd .. && agentsync apply --dry-run
        cd .. && agentsync doctor
    source_dir = "."
    default_agents = ["codex"]
    
    [gitignore]
    enabled = false
    
    [agents.codex]
    enabled = true
    [agents.codex.targets.instructions]
    source = "AGENTS.md"
    destination = "AGENTS.md"
    type = "symlink"
    [agents.codex.targets.settings]
    source = "codex.toml"
    destination = ".codex/config.toml"
    type = "symlink"
    [agents.codex.targets.skills]
    source = "skills"
    destination = ".codex/skills"
    type = "symlink"
    # CCFinance
    
    CCFinance is a data engineering project for filtering and enriching public
    Common Crawl News (CC-News) copies for research into language in finance.
    
    ## Start
    
    Exordio supplies the Python and LaTeX toolchains, a pinned Nix environment and CI.
    Copier answers record Exordio `v0.1.1-alpha` (the documented `v0.1.0` tag was not
    available in the local source).
    
    ```bash
    bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh
    devenv shell
    just setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run stages list
    just check
    ```
    
    Shared agent instructions and Codex configuration are maintained in
    [`.agents/`](.agents/README.md). `just setup` applies them; use
    `just agents::check` to verify the generated links.
    
    For Python alone, with Python 3.13, uv and just installed:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::check
    ```
    
    ## Data and reproducibility
    
    DVC is initialized at the repository root with analytics disabled. Use:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc status
    just dvc dag
    ```
    
    Semflow tracks the executable Python dependencies of DVC stages. When adding a
    stage, run `just semflow-patch` to review its proposed fingerprints, then
    `just semflow-apply` to materialize them. Commit the generated
    `.semflow/hashes/` files with the DVC definition. After semantic source changes,
    run `just semflow-refresh`; `just semflow-check` detects stale fingerprints.
    There are no executable stages to instrument yet. The check skips fingerprint
    comparison only while the stage mapping is empty; any future stage must pass
    Semflow's check. Keep data, configuration and environment dependencies explicit
    in DVC: Semflow's static analysis cannot discover string-driven dynamic imports.
    
    See [Python commands](src/python/README.md), [LaTeX commands](src/latex/README.md)
    and [infrastructure](infra/README.md). The scaffold's Apache-2.0 license covers
    code; it does not grant rights to upstream article content.

    description: Check AgentSync's complete target set before creating any native links.

    # Agent preflight
    
    `just agents::apply` runs this zero-dependency Python script before native
    AgentSync. It reads `.agents/agentsync.toml`, preserves authored destinations,
    rejects unexpected links and symlinked parents, and accepts correct managed
    links on repeated runs. Canonical source paths must stay inside the repository
    without symlink aliases. No configuration is written by this check.
    
    PEP 723 metadata and `script.py.lock` keep this utility independent of the
    optional Python application workspace. Its interpreter comes from Devenv.

## Assistant

Yes. I removed the Python preflight and switched the recipes to the AgentSync CLI:

- `just agents::preview` shows proposed changes.
- `just agents::apply` applies them.
- `just agents::check` checks the configuration.

AgentSync may back up existing files to ignored `.bak` files and replace existing symlinks, so the preview is useful before applying. Full `just check` passes.

    # Agent contract
    
    - Read the nearest README.md for commands and ARCHITECTURE.md for design decisions.
    - Use the pinned devenv environment and repository just commands.
    - Run Python commands through the appropriate locked uv project.
    - Authored records own state. Use explicit creation and synchronization commands; never edit generated Insitu regions by hand.
    - Task parents expose immediate children. Put supporting evidence in separate records and preserve stable paths.
    - Checks validate without repair; use just fmt and just sync for explicit changes.
    - Run just check before handoff and report any checks that could not run.
    - Resolve secrets only for commands that need them. Never place credentials in tracked files.
    # CCFinance
    
    CCFinance is a data engineering project for filtering and enriching public
    Common Crawl News (CC-News) copies for research into language in finance.
    
    ## Start
    
    Exordio supplies the Python and LaTeX toolchains, a pinned Nix environment and CI.
    Copier answers record Exordio `v0.1.1-alpha` (the documented `v0.1.0` tag was not
    available in the local source).
    
    ```bash
    bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh
    devenv shell
    just setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run stages list
    just check
    ```
    
    Shared agent instructions and Codex configuration are maintained in
    [`.agents/`](.agents/README.md). `just setup` applies them; use
    `just agents::preview` to preview link changes and `just agents::check` to
    verify the generated links.
    
    For Python alone, with Python 3.13, uv and just installed:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::check
    ```
    
    ## Data and reproducibility
    
    DVC is initialized at the repository root with analytics disabled. Use:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc status
    just dvc dag
    ```
    
    Semflow tracks the executable Python dependencies of DVC stages. When adding a
    stage, run `just semflow-patch` to review its proposed fingerprints, then
    `just semflow-apply` to materialize them. Commit the generated
    `.semflow/hashes/` files with the DVC definition. After semantic source changes,
    run `just semflow-refresh`; `just semflow-check` detects stale fingerprints.
    There are no executable stages to instrument yet. The check skips fingerprint
    comparison only while the stage mapping is empty; any future stage must pass
    Semflow's check. Keep data, configuration and environment dependencies explicit
    in DVC: Semflow's static analysis cannot discover string-driven dynamic imports.
    
    See [Python commands](src/python/README.md), [LaTeX commands](src/latex/README.md)
    and [infrastructure](infra/README.md). The scaffold's Apache-2.0 license covers
    code; it does not grant rights to upstream article content.
    # Architecture
    
    CCFinance separates code and research artifacts. Git stores source, configuration,
    locks, provenance definitions and documentation. DVC will track large data and
    experiment outputs once the actual stages are defined in part 2.
    
    - `src/python/apps/pipeline` owns the CLI and data stage implementations.
    - `src/python/uv.lock` locks runtime, quality, testing, packaging and DVC tools.
    - `src/latex` owns the manuscript source and bibliography.
    - `data` holds ignored data payloads and versioned DVC pointer files.
    - `infra/nix` and `devenv.lock` own the reproducible system environment.
    
    Tach enforces module boundaries; Ruff and strict Pyrefly check Python source.
    pytest-layout-enforcer checks test file placement during collection and CI.
    Semflow fingerprints the Python code used by DVC stages, allowing DVC to
    invalidate tracked results when executable behavior changes.
    CI executes those checks, tests and builds through the same just recipes as local
    work. Setup may download dependencies; ordinary checks use cached dependencies
    and do not repair authored content. LaTeX uses a versioned Tectonic asset bundle.
    
    The Hugging Face dataset is staging, and the bucket is intended for intermediate
    and experiment artifacts. Neither is accessed by scaffold commands. Pipeline
    stages, provenance, study parameters, coverage criteria and remote transport are
    part 2 work, rather than implied by this scaffold.
    
    Copier answers record the source and tag for future template updates. Review
    update conflicts and preserve project-specific code and configuration. The
    upstream template is [Exordio](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/exordio).
    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    set positional-arguments
    
    mod python 'src/python/justfile'
    mod latex 'src/latex/justfile'
    mod agents '.agents/justfile'
    workflow := "env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py"
    
    # Discover this project's commands.
    default:
        @just --list
    
    # Prepare locked dependencies and Git hooks (uses the network).
    setup:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py prepare
        just python::setup
        just latex::setup
        just agents::apply
        prek install
    
    # Check source, views and selected languages without repairing files.
    check:
        bash infra/nix/check.sh
        {{ workflow }} check
        just python::check
        just latex::check
        just data-check
        just semflow-check
        just changelog-check
        just agents::check
    
    
    # Run the selected language tests.
    test:
        just python::test
        just latex::test
    
    # Explicitly format sources.
    fmt:
        nixfmt devenv.nix infra/nix/devenv.nix infra/nix/pkgs/schematter.nix infra/nix/pkgs/agentsync.nix
        rumdl fmt .
        just python::fmt
        just latex::fmt
    
    # Check external links online.
    links:
        git ls-files -z '*.md' | xargs -0 -r lychee --config lychee.toml --no-progress
    
    # Run root-level DVC using the locked Python environment.
    dvc *args:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen dvc "$@"
    
    # Validate DVC metadata without fetching data.
    data-check:
        just dvc status
        just dvc dag
    
    # Refresh generated planning and reference views.
    sync:
        {{ workflow }} sync
    
    # Validate document schemas, links and generated views.
    context-check:
        {{ workflow }} check
    
    # Create a plan without overwriting existing content.
    plan-new slug title:
        {{ workflow }} plan-new "$1" --title "$2"
    
    # Create a task inside an existing plan or task.
    task-new parent slug title:
        {{ workflow }} task-new "$1" "$2" --title "$3"
    
    # Create a local reference record with its directory as citation key.
    reference-new key title:
        {{ workflow }} reference-new "$1" --title "$2"
    
    # Validate the repository changelog structure and change categories.
    changelog-check:
        schematter validate --schema infra/schemas/documents/changelog.document-schema.yaml CHANGELOG.md
    
    # Check semantic fingerprints once DVC has executable stages.
    semflow-check:
        if env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen python -c 'import pathlib, sys, yaml; from semflow.config import load_config; load_config(); doc = yaml.safe_load(pathlib.Path("dvc.yaml").read_text()); sys.exit(0 if isinstance(doc, dict) and doc.get("stages") == {} else 1)'; then echo 'Semflow: no DVC stages to instrument.'; else env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow check; fi
    
    # Preview the semantic dependency changes before applying them.
    semflow-patch:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow patch
    
    # Apply reviewed DVC and semantic fingerprint changes.
    semflow-apply:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow patch --apply
    
    # Refresh existing semantic fingerprints without editing the DVC graph.
    semflow-refresh:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow refresh --apply
    default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit]
    default_stages: [pre-commit]
    repos:
      - repo: builtin
        hooks:
          - id: check-yaml
          - id: check-toml
          - id: check-json
          - id: check-merge-conflict
            args: [--assume-in-merge]
          - id: detect-private-key
          - id: check-case-conflict
      - repo: local
        hooks:
          - id: workflow-lint
            name: GitHub Actions workflow syntax
            entry: bash -c 'actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml'
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            always_run: true
          - id: shellcheck
            name: ShellCheck scripts
            entry: shellcheck
            language: system
            types: [shell]
            files: \.sh$
          - id: markdown
            name: Markdown formatting and local links
            entry: rumdl check .
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            types: [markdown]
          - id: nix-format
            name: Nix formatting
            entry: nixfmt --check
            language: system
            types: [nix]
          - id: nix-lint
            name: Nix anti-patterns
            entry: statix check infra/nix
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            types: [nix]
          - id: text-check
            name: Whitespace and final newlines
            entry: bash infra/nix/check-text.sh
            language: system
            types: [text]
    
          - id: python-quality
            name: Python lint, strict types and architecture
            entry: bash -c 'just python::lint python::typecheck python::tach python::layout'
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            files: ^src/python/
          - id: dvc-metadata
            name: DVC metadata
            entry: just data-check
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            files: ^(dvc\.(yaml|lock)|\.dvc/|.*\.dvc$)
    
          - id: context-documents
            name: Context schemas and generated views
            entry: just context-check
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            always_run: true
    
          - id: schema-changelog-document
            name: Changelog structure and categories
            entry: just changelog-check
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            files: ^(CHANGELOG\.md|infra/schemas/documents/changelog\.document-schema\.yaml)$
    
          - id: semflow-check
            name: Semflow fingerprints
            entry: just semflow-check
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            always_run: true

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # Check existing tracked and untracked source without treating deletions as files.
    set -euo pipefail
    files=()
    while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
      if [[ -f "$file" || -L "$file" ]]; then files+=("$file"); fi
    done < <(git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard -z)
    if (( ${#files[@]} )); then prek run --files "${files[@]}"; fi

            types_or: [toml]
            # Lock files are content-identified as TOML by prek but are generated —
            # reformatting one churns thousands of lines and fights the next lock
            # operation. The formatter owns hand-authored TOML only (pyproject,
            # agent configuration, and .rumdl.toml).
            exclude: (^|/)[^/]*\.lock$
    
          # One `--justfile` invocation per file, mirroring just-lsp-analyze below.
          # A bare `just --fmt` resolves ONE justfile — the root one — so with
          # `pass_filenames: false` this hook fired on every one of the 27 module
          # justfiles its `files:` pattern names and checked none of them. Measured:
          # a clean root beside a wildly misformatted module exits 0 with no output;
          # the same module via `--justfile` exits 1. Modules had zero format
          # coverage while the gate reported green.
          - id: just-fmt
            name: just fmt (format justfiles)
            language: system
            entry: >-
              bash -c 'rc=0; for f; do just --justfile "$f" --fmt --check --unstable || rc=1; done; exit $rc' --
            files: ^justfile$|^.*\/justfile$
            pass_filenames: true
    
          - id: just-lsp-analyze
            name: just-lsp analyze (lint module justfiles)
            language: system
            entry: bash -c 'for f in "$@"; do just-lsp analyze "$f"; done' --
            files: ^.+/justfile$
            pass_filenames: true
    
          # PEP 723 script locks. The upstream astral-sh/uv-pre-commit `uv-lock`
          # hook (used by the src/python workspace) is project-only —
          # `files: ^(uv\.lock|pyproject\.toml|uv\.toml)$`, `pass_filenames: false` —
          # so it never sees a `# /// script` header and gives the inline-metadata
          # scripts zero coverage. Those span src/latex, src/lean, src/python, and
          # .context/, so the check is root-owned. `uv lock --check --script` exits
          # 2 on a missing `<script>.py.lock` and 1 on a stale one, but its stale
    ---
    description: just — the polyglot command runner for the monorepo
    ---
    
    # just
    
    [just](https://github.com/casey/just) is the monorepo's command runner.
    
    ## Key commands
    
    ```bash
    just --list      # list all available commands
    just setup       # install workspace deps
    just lint        # lint all code
    just fmt         # auto-format all code
    just typecheck   # static type checking
    just check       # run all prek hooks
    just build       # rebuild DVC pipeline
    just hooks       # install git hooks
    ```
    
    ## Module structure
    
    The root justfile imports sub-modules via `mod`:
    
    ```just
    mod nix 'infra/nix/justfile'
    mod python 'src/python/justfile'
    ```
    
    Sub-module recipes are available as `nix::fmt`, `python::lint`, etc.
    Aggregate recipes like `just fmt` chain layer-specific targets.
    
    See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for why just over alternatives.

     set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
     set positional-arguments
    
     mod python 'src/python/justfile'
     mod latex 'src/latex/justfile'
     mod agents '.agents/justfile'
     workflow := "env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py"
    
     # Discover this project's commands.
     default:
         @just --list
    
     # Prepare locked dependencies and Git hooks (uses the network).
     setup:
         env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py prepare
         just python::setup
         just latex::setup
         just agents::apply
         prek install
    
     # Check source, views and selected languages without repairing files.
     check:
         bash infra/nix/check.sh
         {{ workflow }} check
         just python::check
         just latex::check
         just data-check
         just semflow-check
         just changelog-check
         just agents::check
    
    -
     # Run the selected language tests.
     test:
         just python::test
         just latex::test
    
     # Explicitly format sources.
     fmt:
         nixfmt devenv.nix infra/nix/devenv.nix infra/nix/pkgs/schematter.nix infra/nix/pkgs/agentsync.nix
         rumdl fmt .
         just python::fmt
         just latex::fmt
    
     # Check external links online.
     links:
         git ls-files -z '*.md' | xargs -0 -r lychee --config lychee.toml --no-progress
    
     # Run root-level DVC using the locked Python environment.
     dvc *args:
         env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen dvc "$@"
    
     # Validate DVC metadata without fetching data.
     data-check:
         just dvc status
         just dvc dag
    
     # Refresh generated planning and reference views.
     sync:
         {{ workflow }} sync
    
     # Validate document schemas, links and generated views.
     context-check:
         {{ workflow }} check
    
     # Create a plan without overwriting existing content.
     plan-new slug title:
         {{ workflow }} plan-new "$1" --title "$2"
    
     # Create a task inside an existing plan or task.
     task-new parent slug title:
         {{ workflow }} task-new "$1" "$2" --title "$3"
    
     # Create a local reference record with its directory as citation key.
     reference-new key title:
         {{ workflow }} reference-new "$1" --title "$2"
    
     # Validate the repository changelog structure and change categories.
     changelog-check:
         schematter validate --schema infra/schemas/documents/changelog.document-schema.yaml CHANGELOG.md
    
     # Check semantic fingerprints once DVC has executable stages.
     semflow-check:
         if env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen python -c 'import pathlib, sys, yaml; from semflow.config import load_config; load_config(); doc = yaml.safe_load(pathlib.Path("dvc.yaml").read_text()); sys.exit(0 if isinstance(doc, dict) and doc.get("stages") == {} else 1)'; then echo 'Semflow: no DVC stages to instrument.'; else env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow check; fi
    
     # Preview the semantic dependency changes before applying them.
     semflow-patch:
         env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow patch
    
     # Apply reviewed DVC and semantic fingerprint changes.
     semflow-apply:
         env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow patch --apply
    
     # Refresh existing semantic fingerprints without editing the DVC graph.
     semflow-refresh:
         env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow refresh --apply

    # Agent contract
    
    - Read the nearest README.md for commands and ARCHITECTURE.md for design decisions.
    - Use the pinned devenv environment and repository just commands.
    - Run Python commands through the appropriate locked uv project.
    - Authored records own state. Use explicit creation and synchronization commands; never edit generated Insitu regions by hand.
    - Task parents expose immediate children. Put supporting evidence in separate records and preserve stable paths.
    - Checks validate without repair; use just fmt and just sync for explicit changes.
    - Run just check before handoff and report any checks that could not run.
    - Resolve secrets only for commands that need them. Never place credentials in tracked files.
    # CCFinance
    
    CCFinance is a data engineering project for filtering and enriching public
    Common Crawl News (CC-News) copies for research into language in finance.
    
    ## Start
    
    Exordio supplies the Python and LaTeX toolchains, a pinned Nix environment and CI.
    Copier answers record Exordio `v0.1.1-alpha` (the documented `v0.1.0` tag was not
    available in the local source).
    
    ```bash
    bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh
    devenv shell
    just setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run stages list
    just check
    ```
    
    Shared agent instructions and Codex configuration are maintained in
    [`.agents/`](.agents/README.md). `just setup` applies them; use
    `just agents::preview` to preview link changes and `just agents::check` to
    verify the generated links.
    
    `just check` validates Justfile syntax and formatting alongside the other
    quality gates. Run `just fmt` to format Justfiles and other source files.
    
    For Python alone, with Python 3.13, uv and just installed:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::check
    ```
    
    ## Data and reproducibility
    
    DVC is initialized at the repository root with analytics disabled. Use:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc status
    just dvc dag
    ```
    
    Semflow tracks the executable Python dependencies of DVC stages. When adding a
    stage, run `just semflow-patch` to review its proposed fingerprints, then
    `just semflow-apply` to materialize them. Commit the generated
    `.semflow/hashes/` files with the DVC definition. After semantic source changes,
    run `just semflow-refresh`; `just semflow-check` detects stale fingerprints.
    There are no executable stages to instrument yet. The check skips fingerprint
    comparison only while the stage mapping is empty; any future stage must pass
    Semflow's check. Keep data, configuration and environment dependencies explicit
    in DVC: Semflow's static analysis cannot discover string-driven dynamic imports.
    
    See [Python commands](src/python/README.md), [LaTeX commands](src/latex/README.md)
    and [infrastructure](infra/README.md). The scaffold's Apache-2.0 license covers
    code; it does not grant rights to upstream article content.
    ---
    description: Static Schematter contracts for plans, references and the repository changelog.
    ---
    
    # Document schemas
    
    `just context-check` selects schemas by record path. Plans and tasks share the
    work-item contract; `type` asserts their physical role. References use flat CSL
    metadata and derive citation keys from directory names. Local references are
    validated when present.
    
    Entry points and records have a 1,500-token budget. Schematter checks document
    shape; the workflow helper checks containment, declared links and completion.
    
    `just changelog-check` validates the root `CHANGELOG.md` using the
    Pricing Perspective changelog contract, with `Unreleased` allowed for changes
    awaiting a pull request. Published entries use `PR #NUMBER: Title` headings.
    Categories are `Added`, `Changed`, `Deprecated`, `Removed`, `Fixed` and `Security`,
    each containing a bullet list. Frontmatter permits only `type` and `description`.
    Both checks run in CI and through pre-commit hooks.

    default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit]
    default_stages: [pre-commit]
    repos:

        hooks:
          - id: check-yaml

      - repo: local
        hooks:
          - id: workflow-lint

            language: system

          - id: shellcheck

          - id: nix-format

          - id: just-format
            name: Justfile formatting and syntax
            entry: >-

            language: system
            files: (^|/)([Jj]ustfile|[^/]+\.just)$
          - id: just-lint
            name: Justfile analysis
            entry: >-
              bash -c 'rc=0; for f; do just-lsp analyze "$f" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"' --
            language: system
            files: (^|/)([Jj]ustfile|[^/]+\.just)$
          - id: text-check
            name: Whitespace and final newlines
            entry: bash infra/nix/check-text.sh
            language: system
            types: [text]
    
          - id: python-quality
            name: Python lint, strict types and architecture
            entry: bash -c 'just python::lint python::typecheck python::tach python::layout'
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            files: ^src/python/
          - id: dvc-metadata
            name: DVC metadata
            entry: just data-check
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            files: ^(dvc\.(yaml|lock)|\.dvc/|.*\.dvc$)
    
          - id: context-documents
            name: Context schemas and generated views
            entry: just context-check
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            always_run: true
    
          - id: schema-changelog-document
            name: Changelog structure and categories
            entry: just changelog-check
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            files: ^(CHANGELOG\.md|infra/schemas/documents/changelog\.document-schema\.yaml)$
    
          - id: semflow-check
            name: Semflow fingerprints
            entry: just semflow-check
            language: system
            pass_filenames: false
            always_run: true
    ---
    name: repository-workflow
    description: Create and maintain repository plans, references and task views with local commands.
    ---
    
    # Repository workflow
    
    Read the root README and the relevant local README before changing records.
    Use `just --list` to discover the installed workflow and language commands. Create
    records through their commands, edit canonical metadata, then run `just sync`
    when available and `just check`. Keep task parents terse and store detailed
    evidence in linked records. Verification establishes only what the actual
    command output supports; record incomplete or inconclusive checks honestly.

    # Repository workflow
    
    Read the root README and the relevant local README before changing records.
    Use `just --list` to discover the installed workflow and language commands. Create
    records through their commands, edit canonical metadata, then run `just sync`
    when available and `just check`. Keep task parents terse and store detailed
    evidence in linked records. Verification establishes only what the actual
    command output supports; record incomplete or inconclusive checks honestly.

    ---
    
    # Document schemas
    
    `just context-check` selects schemas by record path. Plans and tasks share the
    work-item contract; `type` asserts their physical role. References use flat CSL
    metadata and derive citation keys from directory names. Local references are
    validated when present.
    
    Entry points and records have a 1,500-token budget. Schematter checks document
    shape; the workflow helper checks containment, declared links and completion.
    
    `just changelog-check` validates the root `CHANGELOG.md` using the
    Pricing Perspective changelog contract, with `Unreleased` allowed for changes
    awaiting a pull request. Published entries use `PR #NUMBER: Title` headings.
    Categories are `Added`, `Changed`, `Deprecated`, `Removed`, `Fixed` and `Security`,
    each containing a bullet list. Frontmatter permits only `type` and `description`.
    Both checks run in CI and through pre-commit hooks.

    ---
    name: skill-creator
    description: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources.
    metadata:
      short-description: Create or update a skill
    ---
    
    # Skill Creator
    
    Create skills that give Codex useful, non-obvious guidance without constraining unrelated work.
    
    ## Core Principles
    
    **Assume Codex is already capable.** Include only information that changes its decisions or improves its work. Remove generic advice, repeated instructions, speculative edge cases, and examples that do not materially clarify the task.
    
    **Preserve user intent and scope.** A skill should support the requested task, not replace the user's chosen product, expand the assignment, modify unrelated configuration, or imply permission for additional external actions. Do not turn a particular example, past failure, or personal preference into a universal requirement.
    
    Approval to complete a task does not expand its scope or execution permissions. For retrying or externally mutating workflows, define a stopping condition proportional to the risk.
    
    **Match specificity to the risk.** Give the model room to choose an appropriate approach when multiple approaches are reasonable. Use detailed steps, deterministic scripts, or absolute language only when correctness, safety, permissions, or a genuinely fragile workflow requires them.
    
    For open-ended work, describe the outcome and relevant decision criteria. For workflows with a preferred shape, offer useful examples or configurable scripts. Reserve fixed sequences and narrow parameters for operations where deviation would cause a concrete problem. Preserve non-obvious operational invariants, distinguish actual requirements from optional recommendations or local conventions, and avoid restating policies already enforced elsewhere.
    
    **Keep discovery cheap and precise.** Skill names and descriptions are available before a skill is loaded. Describe the actual capability and when it applies, adding exclusions only when they prevent likely misrouting. Avoid exhaustive capability lists and catchalls that attract unrelated requests.
    
    Keep skills self-contained; refer to another skill or tool only when the requested workflow genuinely requires it and it is available in the target environment. Specialized review, hardening, or audit workflows should apply when requested or genuinely needed, not merely because ordinary work touches the same subject.
    
    **Disclose detail progressively.** Keep shared purpose, essential constraints, and useful routing in `SKILL.md`. Put substantial mode-specific guidance, schemas, examples, or procedures in supporting references and read only the references relevant to the current task. A simple self-contained skill does not need a router or extra files.
    
    ## Anatomy of a Skill
    
    Every skill is a folder containing a required `SKILL.md` file and any optional resources its actual workflow needs:
    
    ```text
    skill-name/
    |-- SKILL.md                 Required skill instructions
    |   |-- YAML frontmatter     Required name and description
    |   `-- Markdown body        Instructions loaded when the skill is used
    |-- agents/                  Optional UI metadata and invocation policy
    |   `-- openai.yaml
    |-- scripts/                 Optional executable helpers
    |-- references/              Optional documentation loaded as needed
    `-- assets/                  Optional files used in generated output
    ```
    
    Choose the structure that fits the actual task. Some skills are short and self-contained; others route among operating modes or delegate complex mechanics to scripts. Avoid creating directories, placeholders, examples, or ancillary documentation without a clear use.
    
    ### SKILL.md
    
    The YAML frontmatter identifies the skill and determines when it should be considered. Include the required `name` and `description`, and preserve supported optional fields such as existing `metadata` when appropriate.
    
    The Markdown body is loaded only when the skill is used. Put the purpose, essential workflow, real constraints, and useful links there. Keep detailed procedures and examples in supporting references when they are relevant only to particular modes.
    
    Skill information is disclosed in three stages:
    
    1. **Name and description:** Available during skill selection, so keep them concise and discriminating.
    2. **SKILL.md body:** Loaded when the skill applies, so keep its instructions relevant to that task.
    3. **Supporting resources:** Read or execute only when the current task actually needs them.
    
    The entrypoint should be as short as the task permits while retaining important constraints. A large upper bound is not a target: move conditional detail into references when doing so improves clarity or context use, rather than waiting for the file to become unwieldy.
    
    ### Scripts
    
    Use `scripts/` for executable code when the same logic would otherwise be rewritten repeatedly or deterministic execution materially improves reliability.
    
    - **Example:** `scripts/rotate_pdf.py` for a PDF operation that would otherwise require recreating the same code.
    - **Useful for:** Repeated transformations, reliable API operations, data processing, and other concrete automation.
    - **Validation:** Run new or changed scripts to verify their behavior. Scripts can usually be executed without loading their full implementation into context, although an agent may need to inspect them when patching or adapting them.
    
    ### References
    
    Use `references/` for documentation that is needed only in particular contexts.
    
    - **Examples:** `references/schema.md` for database tables, `references/policies.md` for domain rules, `references/api_docs.md` for an API, or separate writing guides for different deliverables.
    - **Useful for:** Schemas, API documentation, company policies, format-specific procedures, detailed workflows, and substantial examples.
    - **Routing:** Link each reference from `SKILL.md` or another relevant resource and explain when it should be read. Keep information in one place instead of duplicating it across the entrypoint and references.
    
    Keep references focused on maintained, task-specific information that changes the agent's decisions. Avoid copied manuals, exhaustive catalogs, and generic tutorials already available from authoritative sources. Before removing existing resources, inspect their callers and purpose.
    
    For large references, include useful search terms or a short contents section when that makes the needed material easier to find.
    
    ### Assets
    
    Use `assets/` for files that belong in generated output rather than in the model's instructions.
    
    - **Examples:** `assets/logo.png`, `assets/slides.pptx`, `assets/font.ttf`, or `assets/frontend-template/`.
    - **Useful for:** Templates, images, fonts, icons, boilerplate projects, and other files copied or adapted into the result.
    - **Context:** Do not load assets as instructions unless the task requires inspecting them.
    
    ### UI Metadata and Invocation Policy
    
    `agents/openai.yaml` can provide UI-facing metadata such as `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt`, along with invocation policy. When creating or updating those settings, read [references/openai_yaml.md](references/openai_yaml.md) and keep the values consistent with the skill.
    
    Automatic skill selection is allowed by default. Change that default only when the user explicitly requests an explicit-only skill:
    
    ```yaml
    policy:
      allow_implicit_invocation: false
    ```
    
    This keeps the skill available when explicitly invoked as `$skill-name` without adding it to the model context automatically. Preserve unrelated existing UI, policy, and dependency fields when updating `agents/openai.yaml`.
    
    The initializer creates this file automatically. For new or interface-only metadata, generate it with:
    
    ```bash
    scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py <path/to/skill-folder> --interface key=value
    ```
    
    The generator replaces the entire file. If an existing file contains `policy` or `dependencies`, update only the intended fields in place instead of regenerating it.
    
    Include optional interface fields only when the user provides or requests them.
    
    ### What Not to Include
    
    Include files that directly support the skill's work. Avoid adding a `README.md`, installation guide, changelog, duplicated quick reference, or other auxiliary documentation unless a specific task or packaging requirement calls for it.
    
    ## Progressive Disclosure in Practice
    
    For a skill with multiple substantial modes, keep the shared guidance and mode-selection criteria in `SKILL.md`. Link each supporting reference where its use becomes relevant. Do not load every reference by default, duplicate reference content in the entrypoint, or add a routing layer when there is nothing meaningful to route.
    
    For example, a deployment skill can keep provider selection in `SKILL.md` and separate provider details:
    
    ```text
    cloud-deploy/
    |-- SKILL.md
    `-- references/
        |-- aws.md
        |-- gcp.md
        `-- azure.md
    ```
    
    When the user chooses AWS, read `references/aws.md`; do not also load the GCP and Azure guides. The same pattern can separate business domains, deliverable types, or other genuinely distinct operating modes.
    
    A short skill can instead route to details only when an advanced operation needs them:
    
    ```markdown
    ## Documents
    
    Handle ordinary edits directly.
    
    - For tracked changes, read [references/redlining.md](references/redlining.md).
    - For document internals, read [references/ooxml.md](references/ooxml.md).
    ```
    
    These examples illustrate options, not a required structure. Choose the organization that makes the skill easier to use without loading irrelevant material.
    
    ## Create or Update a Skill
    
    Adapt the work to the request. Creating a complex new skill may involve understanding realistic use cases, choosing supporting resources, initializing files, writing instructions, and validating the result. A narrow update to an existing skill may require only a focused edit and validation.
    
    Ask clarifying questions only when the missing information matters and cannot be reasonably inferred. Respect a user-specified location; otherwise create discoverable skills in `$CODEX_HOME/skills`, or `~/.codex/skills` when `CODEX_HOME` is unset.
    
    Keep automatic skill selection enabled unless the user explicitly requests an explicit-only skill. When the intended invocation mode is genuinely unclear and matters to the requested workflow, ask whether the user wants normal automatic discovery or explicit-only invocation; otherwise preserve the default. Do not infer explicit-only invocation from sensitive operations or required approvals: keep the skill discoverable and require authorization immediately before the actual mutation. Preserve an existing skill's invocation policy unless the user asks to change it.
    
    For a new or substantially revised skill, consider the actual requests it should handle and which reusable resources would improve those tasks:
    
    - A repeated PDF transformation may justify a `scripts/rotate_pdf.py` helper.
    - An application-building workflow may benefit from an `assets/frontend-template/` starter.
    - A data-analysis skill may need a `references/schema.md` guide to avoid rediscovering table relationships.
    
    Create those resources only when their concrete benefit justifies them. If the user has already explained the task clearly, proceed without requesting additional examples.
    
    ### Naming
    
    - Use lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.
    - Keep names under 64 characters and prefer short action-oriented names.
    - Namespace by tool or domain when doing so improves discovery.
    - Name the skill folder after the skill.
    
    ### Initialize a New Skill
    
    For a new skill, use the bundled initializer when it helps create the required files consistently:
    
    ```bash
    scripts/init_skill.py <skill-name> --path <output-directory> [--resources scripts,references,assets] [--examples]
    ```
    
    For example:
    
    ```bash
    scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills"
    scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills" --resources references
    ```
    
    Request only the resource directories the skill needs. Use `--examples` only when concrete placeholders would help, and replace or remove them before finishing. Do not initialize an existing skill again.
    
    The initializer creates the skill directory, a concise `SKILL.md` starter, and `agents/openai.yaml`. It creates resource directories and example files only when requested. Pass generated UI values as `--interface key=value` when needed.
    
    ### Write the Instructions
    
    The frontmatter `description` should briefly explain what the skill does and when it applies. Include a meaningful boundary when similar requests should not activate the skill.
    
    For example:
    
    ```yaml
    description: Create or edit Word documents when formatting, tracked changes, or comments require document-specific handling.
    ```
    
    Put detailed workflows, tool choices, examples, and operating modes in the body or relevant references rather than listing them all in the description. Preserve supported optional frontmatter, such as existing `metadata`, when appropriate.
    
    Write only the instructions needed for another Codex instance to perform the task well. State the desired outcome, non-obvious context, real constraints, and relevant references or tools. Preserve the user's explicit choices and existing authorization boundaries. Avoid prescribing a fixed structure, process, or number of steps when the task does not require one.
    
    ### Validate and Iterate
    
    Validate the completed skill with:
    
    ```bash
    scripts/quick_validate.py <path/to/skill-folder>
    ```
    
    The validator checks frontmatter, naming, and unfinished scaffold placeholders; it does not prove that the skill makes good decisions. Also check that descriptions remain discriminating, instructions preserve user intent, references are discoverable, and any added scripts actually work.
    
    When testing is warranted, verify observable behavior or meaningful invariants. Avoid tests that merely match generated wording, headings, or regex patterns.
    
    Improve the skill based on real usage or demonstrated failures. Prefer a narrow correction to accumulating universal rules for every observed example.
    
    ## Independent Forward-Testing
    
    Use an independent subagent pass when a skill is sufficiently complex or risky that realistic behavioral validation would add meaningful confidence, and when delegation is available and authorized. Ordinary creation or small edits do not automatically require subagents.
    
    Give the evaluating agent a realistic user request, the skill, and the minimum raw artifacts needed to perform the task. Do not provide the intended answer, suspected bug, proposed fix, or prior conclusions unless the evaluation genuinely requires them.
    
    For example:
    
    ```text
    Use $skill-name at /path/to/skill-name to complete this realistic request.
    ```
    
    Keep the evaluation scoped to permitted resources and side effects. Use an isolated temporary workspace for generated artifacts so they do not enter the working tree or contaminate later evaluations. Ask for approval when the proposed evaluation would require additional authorization, affect a live production system, or impose substantial time or cost. Review the actual outcome and artifacts, then make only changes supported by the observed behavior.

        # One title with a required workflow underneath it. Other subsections may explain

        # This heading convention is a repository rule, not an Agent Skills requirement.
        sections:
          - header:
              pattern: '^.+$'
            description: A concise title identifying the skill.
            minContains: 1
            maxContains: 1
            sections:
              - header:
                  pattern: '^(Instructions|Steps|Workflow|Usage|How to Run)$'
                description: >-
                  Provide actionable instructions, including prerequisites and checks
                  when relevant. Prefer specific guidance based on real experience.
                minContains: 1
                maxContains: 1
                blocks:
                  - type: [paragraph, bullet-list, ordered-list, code]
                    minContains: 1
            additionalSections: true
        additionalSections: false
        
        frontmatter:
          $schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema
          type: object
          required: [name, description]
          additionalProperties: false
          properties:
            name:
              description: >-
                Skill identifier, matching its parent directory. Use lowercase letters,
                digits and single hyphens; choose a short, distinctive name.
              type: string
              minLength: 1
              maxLength: 64
              pattern: '^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$'
            description:
              description: >-
                Describe what the skill does and when to use it, using concrete user
                intents and relevant keywords. State exclusions when they prevent
                confusion. Test triggering on varied positive and near-miss prompts.
              type: string
              minLength: 1
              maxLength: 1024
              pattern: '\\S'
            license:
              description: A short license identifier or path to a bundled license.
              type: string
              minLength: 1
              maxLength: 128
              pattern: '\\S'
            compatibility:
              description: >-
                Include only when needed; state required tools, versions, environment
                or network access. The Agent Skills specification caps this at 500.
              type: string
              minLength: 1
              maxLength: 500
              pattern: '\\S'
            metadata:
              description: >-
                Optional uniquely named string metadata. Quote YAML values such as
                versions to preserve their string type.
              type: object
              maxProperties: 32
              propertyNames:
                minLength: 1
                maxLength: 64
                pattern: '\\S'
              additionalProperties:
                type: string
                maxLength: 500
            allowed-tools:
              description: >-
                Experimental, client-dependent space-separated list of pre-approved
                tools. Tool availability does not itself grant external-action approval.
              type: string
              minLength: 1
              maxLength: 500
              pattern: '\\S'
        EOF

        from pathlib import Path
        import shutil
        import subprocess
        import tempfile
        
        root = Path.cwd()
        schema = root / 'infra/schemas/documents/skill.document-schema.yaml'
        base = '''---
        name: example-skill
        description: Use when evaluating a skill schema and validating its constraints.
        ---
        
        # Example skill
        
        ## Workflow
        
        Run the checks.
        '''
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='ccfinance-schema-') as temp:
            file = Path(temp) / 'SKILL.md'
            def validate(content):
                file.write_text(content)
                return subprocess.run(['schematter', 'validate', '--schema', str(schema), str(file)], capture_output=True, text=True)
            assert validate(base).returncode == 0
            failures = {
                'invalid name': base.replace('example-skill', 'Example--Skill'),
                'missing description': base.replace('description: Use when evaluating a skill schema and validating its constraints.\n', ''),
                'blank description': base.replace('Use when evaluating a skill schema and validating its constraints.', '   '),
                'long description': base.replace('Use when evaluating a skill schema and validating its constraints.', 'a' * 1025),
                'invalid metadata': base.replace('---\n\n# Example', 'metadata:\n  version: 1\n---\n\n# Example'),
                'extra frontmatter': base.replace('---\n\n# Example', 'unknown: value\n---\n\n# Example'),
                'missing workflow': base.replace('## Workflow', '## Notes'),
                'empty workflow': base.replace('Run the checks.\n', ''),
                'lowercase heading': base.replace('## Workflow', '## workflow'),
                'deep heading': base + '\n### Detail\n\n#### Too deep\n\nText.\n',
                'oversized body': base + '\n' + ('word ' * 6000) + '\n',
            }
            for label, content in failures.items():
                result = validate(content)
                assert result.returncode != 0, f'{label} unexpectedly passed'
            print(f'Schema accepts a valid skill and rejects {len(failures)} invalid variants.')
        
        probe = root / '.skill-gate-test' / 'example-skill'
        assert not probe.exists()
        try:
            probe.mkdir(parents=True)
            file = probe / 'SKILL.md'
            file.write_text(base)
            def check():
                return subprocess.run(['just', 'skills-check'], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True)
            result = check()
            assert result.returncode == 0, result.stdout + result.stderr
            file.write_text(base.replace('name: example-skill', 'name: different-skill'))
            result = check()
            assert result.returncode != 0 and 'must match parent directory' in result.stderr
            file.write_text(base + '\n' * 501)
            result = check()
            assert result.returncode != 0 and 'exceeds 500 lines' in result.stderr
            print('Repository gate detects mismatched directory names and excessive lines.')
        finally:
            shutil.rmtree(probe.parent, ignore_errors=True)
        PY
