    # Full-corpus company candidates
    
    The production CPU runner tags every source row with candidate companies from
    the annual US top-1000 panel and the fixed Gawronsky–Huang roster. It extracts
    mentions and publisher evidence; it does not claim substantive relevance,
    primary-company truth or calibrated probabilities.
    
    Install the [CPU extra](company-cpu.md) before running from the repository root
    inside the development environment:
    
    ```sh
    src/python/.venv/bin/python -m fine_news_cli company tag-corpus
    ```
    
    Defaults are six processes, one native thread per process, 128 input rows per
    batch, and compressed Parquet output chunks of 8,192 rows. The default run first
    processes a 100,000-row pilot distributed proportionally across source files,
    then continues to the full corpus. Both stages enforce an 8 GiB combined process
    memory ceiling. Pilot ranges are deterministic contiguous ranges for bounded
    Parquet reads, not a random sample suitable for prevalence inference. Reported
    throughput includes source reads, matching and durable output; preflight source
    hashing and final reports are separate.
    
    The initial successful 100,000-row pilot covered all 168 local files and took
    13.0 seconds (about 7,700 rows/second), with 3.3 GiB peak combined resident memory.
    The reader uses a 512 MiB DuckDB budget per process; the aggregate ceiling also
    accounts for Python objects and output buffers. All 322 CLI tests passed before
    the production run. The optimized matcher produced identical evidence on all
    2,000 checked raw rows,
    and its cased projection matched the frozen policy on all 1,135 clean supported
    evaluation rows.
    
    ## Completed production run
    
    The 2026-11-04 run completed all **14,807,287 source rows in 168 files** with
    exit code zero. Processing took **1,643 seconds (27 minutes 23 seconds)**,
    averaging **9,012 articles/second**, including source reads, matching and durable
    writes. Preflight hashing and final report generation are outside that timing.
    Peak combined process-tree resident memory was **7,533,608,960 bytes (7.02 GiB)**,
    below the 8 GiB guard. Six CPU workers ran on the Ryzen 5 9600X; the GPU was not
    used. No per-core utilization trace was collected, so these measurements do not
    establish exact CPU saturation.
    
    | Universe | Source rows with candidates | Rows with cased name evidence | Rows with publisher evidence |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | Annual US top-1000 | 12,159,551 | 8,365,194 | 512,169 |
    | Fixed GH roster | 3,764,426 | 1,569,478 | 139,298 |
    
    Evidence categories overlap. Candidates include ambiguous and lowercase aliases;
    these counts are not estimates of substantive coverage, precision or recall.
    The independent [2,000-row prevalence audit](company-prevalence.md) addresses
    substantive coverage with a different procedure and remains provisional.
    
    The committed [findings snapshot](company-tagging-findings.json) retains run
    metrics, contract and artifact fingerprints, the GH minimum, and the Nasdaq
    comparison below. Generated predictions remain in the local output directory.
    
    Use `--phase preflight`, `--phase pilot` or `--phase run` for individual stages.
    Use `--resume` to verify and continue a run. `--limit` restricts the processing
    frame in source-file order for development. Configuration, registry, code,
    dependencies and source fingerprints must match the frozen manifest on resume.
    
    ## Evidence and identities
    
    One Rust Aho–Corasick DFA searches the union of registry names and aliases.
    Extended legal suffixes follow the existing tested policy, with separate alias
    ownership and overlap selection for each universe. Publication year controls
    top-1000 eligibility; the GH roster is fixed across years. Current registry
    names and fixed GH ticker spellings are not certified historical identities.
    
    Rows retain all candidate companies. Single-token lowercase matches, shared
    aliases, ambiguous symbols and incomplete catalogs have explicit flags.
    `cased_name_match_count` distinguishes evidence that survives the tested case
    policy; lowercase evidence remains available rather than becoming a negative.
    Neither a complete catalog nor a no-candidate result proves irrelevance.
    
    Publisher exchange annotations, cashtags and conservative standalone ticker
    tags are extracted separately. Explicit annotations are masked in the name
    matching view. Ordinary prose and complete company names remain intact; the
    evaluation sanitizer that could remove parts of company names is not applied.
    No bare ticker search is added to prose unless that spelling already appears
    as a catalog name or alias. Publisher evidence is unverified and must not be
    used as independent evaluation truth for predictions derived from that evidence.
    
    Top-1000 issuer IDs are `top1000:PERMCO`; GH IDs are `gh:CIK` with padded CIKs.
    Their identities remain separate, including when a company belongs to both.
    The output retains catalog CIK link status without inferring a crosswalk.
    Tickers are labels from the relevant catalog, not additional issuer identities.
    
    ## Output and recovery
    
    The destination defaults to `data/02_primary/company_tags/dfa-v1/`:
    
    - `manifest.json` freezes source SHA-256 fingerprints and the run contract.
    - `shards/NNNNN/part-NNNNN.parquet` stores every source row with native nested
      candidate/evidence structs. Each source directory has a `completed.json`.
    - `pilot/` contains separate pilot predictions and timing.
    - `progress.jsonl` records progress, resource observations and failures.
    - `summary.json` reconciles rows and counts by year, universe and evidence.
    - `company-year-counts.csv` counts candidate and publisher-supported source rows.
    - `gh-company-year-2018-2022.csv` includes zero-count cells for all GH companies;
      `gh-floor-2018-2022.json` identifies the minimum candidate count and ties.
    
    Read production predictions with `shards/*/part-*.parquet`; a recursive glob over
    the entire run directory would also include the separate pilot predictions.
    For the launched background run, `background-job.json` and `worker-process.json`
    identify the processes, `runner.log` captures errors, and `background-exit.json`
    records the eventual exit code. A final `summary.json` with `status=complete`
    confirms successful processing and report generation.
    
    `row_key` hashes the relative source path and zero-based physical row number.
    Original article IDs remain nullable and are not assumed unique. Duplicate or
    syndicated source rows are retained. Article text is not copied into outputs.
    Each candidate has full occurrence counts and at most four representative spans
    per field; offsets describe the NFKC/casefold matching view, not raw text.
    
    Workers commit a source directory atomically after row-count reconciliation and
    durable writes. Incomplete `.partial` source directories are rebuilt on resume.
    Completed chunks are checksum-verified and reused; corruption or changed inputs
    causes an error. Source failures prevent successful completion. An output lock
    prevents concurrent writers. A failed row is never silently dropped.
    
    Company-year counts describe source rows with candidate evidence, not unique
    stories or adjudicated substantive company coverage. In particular, the GH
    candidate floor is not a validated academic coverage floor.
    
    ## GH annual floor and Nasdaq comparison
    
    Across the fixed 100-company GH roster and the five publication years 2018–2022,
    the minimum among all 500 company-year cells is **CDNS in 2018: 16 candidate
    source rows**. Fifteen have cased company-name evidence and two have publisher
    ticker evidence; one row has both. None of the 500 candidate cells is zero.
    These source rows have not been deduplicated or adjudicated for substantive
    company coverage.
    
    The local `pricing-perspective` Nasdaq archive is a separately acquired,
    ticker-directed source. Its `main` revision
    `c8a4bd69cf26c87163d5db3c0a2de7b0d8b14cef` documents collection through
    `api.nasdaq.com/api/news/topic/articlebysymbol` in December 2022–January 2023.
    The immutable raw archive contains 397,041 rows; the current normalized local
    artifact contains 214,480 records across 100 symbols. Its global article-ID
    deduplication keeps one scrape-symbol assignment, potentially losing other
    article–symbol memberships. Nasdaq assignments and our extracted candidates
    therefore measure different things.
    
    | Publication year | Nasdaq normalized CDNS records | Fine News CDNS candidates | Fine News Nasdaq-hosted rows, all companies |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | 2018 | 123 | 16 | 0 |
    | 2019 | 97 | 126 | 74,258 |
    | 2020 | 69 | 275 | 212,834 |
    | 2021 | 57 | 134 | 174,027 |
    | 2022 | 381 | 314 | 241,988 |
    
    There are also 123 distinct CDNS article IDs in the raw Nasdaq archive for 2018,
    so deduplication does not explain that year's 123-versus-16 difference. The
    historical `annual_raw_article_floor: 47` admission rule precedes normalization;
    it is not a guaranteed deduplicated annual floor. The realized normalized
    archive's minimum is SNPS in 2018 with 34 records. Its documented minimum of
    449 per ticker concerns the entire recovered history, rather than one year.
    
    The Fine News host counts use publication year from `metadata.publish_date`,
    and the normalized URL hostname with URL fallback. They include `nasdaq.com`
    and its subdomains across all 168 source files. None of the 123 Nasdaq CDNS
    URLs from 2018 matches a Fine News source URL after stripping the Nasdaq
    scheme/hostname and query/fragment components. This establishes a source URL
    coverage gap; it does not rule out copies hosted by original publishers.
    Title matching alone is insufficient: repeated earnings and market-summary
    headlines also occur in different years. The snapshot retains this diagnostic
    with its dates rather than treating repeated titles as duplicate stories.
    
    ## Confirmed recall gaps and next experiment
    
    The frozen GH catalog supplies `Cadence Design Systems` and the branded
    `cādence`, plus the legal name. Suffix expansion adds `CADENCE DESIGN SYSTEMS`;
    neither normalization nor that expansion produces plain `Cadence` or
    `Cadence Design`. Bare `CDNS` in prose is also outside the current ticker policy.
    
    A case-sensitive whole-word search for `Cadence` or `CDNS` in 2018 titles and
    bodies finds 75 source rows, of which 15 already have CDNS candidates. The
    remaining 60 are not all false negatives: they include Cadence Bank, Aerospace,
    Minerals, personal names, ordinary prose and an unrelated CDNS acronym.
    Three inspected untagged examples do identify the semiconductor/EDA company:
    
    | Source and date | Article | Missing spelling |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Korea Herald, 2018-02-28 | [Samsung's non-memory chips at MWC](http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20180228000675) | Cadence |
    | Business Day, 2018-08-17 | [SA is on wrong side of global shift towards new industries](https://www.businesslive.co.za/bd/opinion/2018-08-17-sa-is-on-wrong-side-of-global-shift-towards-new-industries/) | Cadence Design |
    | Forbes, 2018-11-01 | [Simulation Becomes Increasingly Important For Self-Driving Cars](https://www.forbes.com/sites/davidsilver/2018/11/01/simulation-becomes-increasingly-important-for-self-driving-cars/) | Cadence |
    
    These are confirmed missed name mentions from local extracted text, not new
    human gold labels for substantive relevance. Their source IDs and excerpts are
    retained in the snapshot. Consequently, 16 undercounts available mentions and
    cannot establish the academic coverage floor. Both acquisition coverage and
    matching recall require attention.
    
    The next experiment should combine the Nasdaq archive with Fine News while
    preserving provenance and all article–company memberships through deduplication.
    Test provenance-backed aliases and contextual handling of ambiguous names on
    independent data before changing the production dictionary. Then recompute the
    company-year table and review its low-count cells. The completed run and its
    catalog remain frozen; this comparison does not merge sources or revise tags.

    # Raw acquisition inputs
    
    [domains.csv](domains.csv) is the exact 115-hostname allowlist used by the
    original Colab publisher filter. It contains domains rather than individual
    article URLs. Matching includes each listed host and its subdomains, preserving
    specific hosts such as `fortune.cnn.com` without admitting all of `cnn.com`.
    
    The article source remains upstream `ksolovev/fine-news`, pinned to commit
    `7a841090e69f3c58a9e04b0c39213d879af68e8a` in
    [`_filter_config.json`](../../_filter_config.json). Raw article/media files are
    queried remotely and are not duplicated in this directory. The CSV is the
    builder's filter input; the root JSON records the historical dataset filter.
    
    Run from the repository root inside `devenv shell`:
    
    ```bash
    just python::run intermediate build --month 2016-08 --dry-run
    just python::run intermediate build --month 2016-08 --output .tmp/intermediate-trial
    ```
    
    Omit `--month` to select all English capture months. Without `--output`, the
    builder targets `data/01_intermediate`; it refuses any existing destination
    shard before scanning articles. Use a fresh output directory for a rebuild.
    `--source` accepts an explicit `hf://` or local glob with the same
    `YYYY-MM/eng_Latn/*.parquet` layout; `--domains` selects another domain CSV.
    
    The builder runs the [filter SQL](../../src/python/apps/fine_news_cli/src/fine_news_cli/intermediate/filter.sql.j2)
    once per source shard and retains its month/language/filename layout. It
    prefers nonblank `metadata.url_hostname`, falling back to the URL hostname,
    then normalizes case, whitespace and trailing dots. It projects only `text`,
    `id` and `metadata`, excluding separate media columns. Text, IDs and metadata
    values are retained; row ordering and encoded Parquet bytes need not match.
    
    This is the Colab filtering operation without Google Drive mounting, runtime
    package installation, quota monitoring or resume machinery. DuckDB uses two
    threads, a 2 GiB memory limit, a 4 GiB spill limit and Zstandard level 9, as in
    the original. Completed shards are published atomically; failed temporary files
    are removed. A later failure can leave earlier completed shards in place.
    
    The dependency environment can be prepared with `just setup`. Remote builds and
    remote dry runs need network access; a dry run only lists paths. DuckDB installs
    and loads its `httpfs` extension on first remote use. Local source globs work
    offline and are used by the regression tests.
    # Universe Metadata
    
    The company research inputs are [nasdaq_100.csv](nasdaq_100.csv) and
    [gawronsky_huang_2026.csv](gawronsky_huang_2026.csv). See the
    [company reference notes](company_references.README.md) for their constituent
    windows, SEC and Wikipedia descriptions, aliases, access dates and provenance.
    
    ## Free Foundations top 1,000
    
    [Issuer descriptions](free_foundations_us_top_1000.csv), the
    [security-year membership panel](free_foundations_us_top_1000_membership.csv),
    and [provenance](free_foundations_us_top_1000.provenance.json) are a preliminary
    research snapshot. The panel has 1,000 December-ranked securities per effective
    year from 2002 through 2025. The source archive has no December 2000 observation;
    2026 is outside its study window. Issuers are grouped by PERMCO and CIK, with
    unresolved identities kept separate. Candidate links are not verified identity
    evidence. SEC and Wikipedia descriptions are not complete or all reviewed.
    
    The issuer CSV contains multiline source text and JSON-encoded lists. Read CIKs
    as strings to preserve leading zeros. SEC descriptions are source text, not
    generated summaries. Wikipedia text is attributed to the contributors at its
    linked permanent revision and is available under
    [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Latest-access
    descriptions, names and aliases are not point-in-time historical features.
    
    To validate the snapshot and attempt conservative recovery, with the pinned
    Free Foundations archive available at `~/Git/free-foundations/research/crsp-study`:
    
    ```sh
    src/python/.venv/bin/python src/python/scripts/recover_universe.py
    EDGAR_IDENTITY='Your Name your.email@example.com' \
      src/python/.venv/bin/python src/python/scripts/recover_universe.py --network
    ```
    
    Use `--archive` to select another copy of the same archive; its four prepared
    inputs must match the recorded hashes. The script uses the workspace's Polars
    installation. Requests are disabled unless `--network` is supplied, SEC requests
    also require `EDGAR_IDENTITY`, and a failed host is skipped for the rest of that
    run. Successful network responses and a review queue are saved under the ignored
    `.tmp/universe-recovery/` directory; reruns reuse cached successes. Output CSVs
    must match the provenance hashes before updates are made.
    Use `--source sec` or `--source wikipedia` to retry one source independently;
    `--workers` controls concurrency while all requests share the rate limit.
    
    The recovery pass only promotes a candidate when the pinned crosswalk already
    has matching, dated, verified SEC evidence. It extracts unambiguous 10-K Item 1
    boundaries as **unreviewed**, and accepts a Wikipedia match only when its
    Wikidata item supplies the same CIK. It does not yet discover new historical
    identities, extract other SEC forms, or resolve ambiguous boundaries and pages;
    those cases remain in the queue for later research. The latest run's status
    counts and access failures are in `.tmp/universe-recovery/last_run.json`.

## Activity

    $ cat src/python/apps/fine_news_cli/docs/company-prevalence.md
    # Random-source company coverage estimate
    
    This experiment estimates the fraction of source rows that substantively cover
    at least one company in the article-year universe. It accepts multiple central
    companies, including product, operational and legal stories without stock-market
    discussion. It does not require a unique primary company or attempt exhaustive
    company extraction. Passing examples, analyst employers, author holdings,
    advertisements and fund-sponsor attribution alone do not qualify.
    
    ## Completed result
    
    All 2,000 sampled rows have outcomes. Eight failed requests were retried once in
    a separate ledger; all retries completed. The effective outcomes are 310 positive
    (15.5%), 1,333 negative (66.65%) and 357 unknown (17.85%). Unknowns comprise 320
    historical catalog gaps and 37 unsupported years, rather than outstanding requests.
    
    The weighted AI-assisted audit estimates **18.06–20.56%** substantive eligible
    company coverage. The range spans seven unresolved review labels. The approximate
    95% interval for source sampling and review subsampling is **14.12–24.50%**;
    systematic AI-review error and corpus-coverage error are additional uncertainties.
    This corresponds to **2.67–3.04 million** of the observed 14.81M local source rows,
    or **3.61–4.11 million per 20M** if the larger source has the same mix.
    
    | Output | Estimated source articles with at least one correct returned company |
    | --- | ---: |
    | DFA candidates | 16.75% |
    | Tev1 final choice | 10.73% |
    | Either method | 17.45% |
    
    These are valid-link yields, not company-set precision, recall or F1. DFA emits
    candidates on 1,127/2,000 rows (56.35%), including many incidental matches. Its
    larger valid-link yield does not make all those candidate links acceptable.
    
    Every one of the 82 Tev1-positive cases whose selected company is absent from
    DFA's candidates was reviewed. Tev1's proposed company is accepted in 17 cases;
    DFA already has a different accepted company in three of those. Tev1 therefore
    adds **14/2,000 articles (0.70 percentage points)** with a valid association.
    Six of these have no DFA candidate at all: **6/2,000 (0.30 percentage points)**.
    The remaining eight have DFA candidates, all incidental or otherwise incorrect.
    
    Preparation accounts for part of that apparent advantage. A separate DFA-only
    sensitivity check preserves distinctive symbols inside complete registry-derived
    multiword company names, while still removing standalone symbols and explicit
    annotations. It changes 31 article views and recovers two of the 14 incremental
    links (CF Industries and Sirius XM). The residual is 12/2,000 (0.60 points).
    Original model inputs/results remain frozen. This diagnostic is not a new gold
    sanitizer certification; full company-name spans should be protected before a
    production labeling run.
    
    Other incremental cases suggest registry/normalization improvements to test on
    independent data: Wal-Mart/Walmart, Papa John's/Papa Johns, Uber/Uber Technologies,
    Wells Fargo's `/MN` legal-name suffix, and subsidiary names such as Janssen and
    OneMain Financial. The experiment supports high-recall dictionary retrieval plus
    better name preservation, identity data and semantic filtering. It does not
    establish a fast CPU routing policy that captures Tev1's marginal benefits.
    
    ## Source sample and preparation
    
    The frozen draw contains 2,000 uniformly hash-selected Parquet rows from all
    14,807,287 rows in the 168 local English intermediate files. Selection happens
    before annotation, dictionary, date, ID or length filtering. A physical source
    row is the sampling unit: syndicated copies count separately. The seed, exact
    query paths, DuckDB version, SQL hash, source file sizes/mtime and output hashes
    are saved in `sample.json`. The source Parquet files are not fully checksummed.
    The local source population is smaller than the user's 20M+ target, so larger
    corpus projections require the same publisher, language and date mix.
    
    The separate `company-prevalence-text-1` profile strips explicit exchange/ticker
    annotations, cashtags, metadata markup and distinctive bare symbols. Publisher
    tags and expected labels never enter the decision state. Ambiguous prose and
    company names remain, with an audit warning: 890 inputs are clean and 1,110 are
    usable with ambiguity. All 2,000 rows remain in the denominator. This is unlabeled
    prevalence inference; the profile does not certify leakage-free gold evaluation
    inputs or replace the existing frozen evaluation sanitizer.
    
    ## Frozen model protocol
    
    Tev1 runs locally through Docker/SGLang on the RTX 5060 Ti in BF16, using its
    pinned checkpoint and image, FlashInfer and radix caching. The checkpoint
    revision and runtime arguments are in `runtime.json`; the actual sample-client
    configuration is `inference-config.json`. The container startup manifest retains
    older benchmark input-path defaults, which the client configuration overrides.
    
    Every named issuer in the article-year catalog is scored, without a DFA candidate
    restriction. Groups contain at most 22 companies plus none/unclear. Each group
    nominates its highest-scoring company; intermediate reductions lead to a final
    company-or-none choice. Any substantive co-central company is accepted. Full
    title/body text is preserved; context failures are recorded rather than truncated.
    Group probabilities are conditional and uncalibrated.
    
    The `substantial-company-presence-4` protocol was fixed before the independent
    sample inference. Earlier canaries used the previously reviewed 60 disagreements
    to reveal logical-OR false positives and excessive model abstention; those cases
    are not independent validation of the new protocol. No sample audit labels were
    used to tune its prompts or thresholds.
    
    A negative requires a complete catalog and successful inference. Missing
    historical company names, unsupported years and request failures remain unknown.
    There are 37 sampled rows outside the available annual membership panel. Some
    older display names and aliases also disagree with historical tickers; catalog
    completeness alone does not establish semantic identity correctness.
    
    Transient group-request failures are retried separately after the main pass.
    The original predictions remain frozen. Complete retries can supply a separate
    effective result, with provenance linking each replacement to its original.
    
    The client first saved 567 rows before exiting with code 137 during severe host
    memory pressure. A four-article concurrency resume reached 939 saved rows;
    growing native tokenizer memory then prompted bounded 128-article subprocesses
    with `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2`. Each chunk releases its memory and resumes only missing
    IDs. Execution segments and chunk logs record these operational changes. The
    model, article inputs and question protocol remain fixed; this mixed execution
    is not a controlled throughput benchmark.
    
    ## Audit and interpretation
    
    An independent random base audit contains 200 articles selected without viewing
    model outcomes. Three AI reviewers read full prepared texts, with Tev1, DFA and
    publisher annotations hidden, and checked annual membership. Fifty articles,
    prioritizing uncertain cases, received a second blinded review. One binary
    disagreement was reconciled from the full text; this targeted cross-review is
    not a representative inter-rater agreement estimate.
    
    The audit then adds randomly selected unreviewed articles within final Tev1
    positive, negative and unknown strata, targeting at least 100, 100 and 50 reviews
    respectively. The 82 additions bring this random audit to 282 rows: 100 positive,
    132 negative and 50 unknown outcomes. Existing base reviews are retained.
    
    A further 57 targeted reviews complete a census of all 82 potential new-link
    cases, giving **339 unique reviewed articles**. The enhanced estimate separates
    the model-positive population into 228 overlap cases (75 randomly reviewed) and
    82 potential new-link cases (all reviewed). Negative and unknown samples retain
    their original design. Conditional on these cell counts, the non-census reviews
    remain uniform within each cell. The original three-stratum estimate is also
    retained, without mixing targeted additions into its random positive sample.
    
    Estimates weight each cell by its share of the full 2,000-row draw, rather than
    averaging an oversampled positive review set. Unresolved review labels span bounds.
    Approximate intervals include source-sampling and review-subsampling variation,
    but exclude systematic reviewer errors and source-coverage errors.
    
    Review is **AI-assisted, not human gold**. It supplies a provisional planning
    estimate. Article-level valid-link yield means that at least one returned PERMCO
    is accepted. It is distinct from complete company-set precision, recall or F1.
    The DFA candidate rate is also distinct from substantive company coverage.
    
    ## Reproduction and artifacts
    
    Run from the repository root, using the installed CLI environment:
    
    ```sh
    fine-news eval prevalence \
      --output .tmp/company-prevalence-tev-v1 \
      --source data/01_intermediate --phase sample
    
    # Start the pinned local Docker runtime before inference.
    fine-news eval prevalence \
      --output .tmp/company-prevalence-tev-v1 --phase infer \
      --runtime-config .tmp/company-prevalence-tev-v1/inference-config.json \
      --concurrency 4
    
    fine-news eval prevalence-audit \
      --output .tmp/company-prevalence-tev-v1 \
      --reviews .tmp/company-prevalence-tev-v1/audit/all-reviews.jsonl \
      --predictions .tmp/company-prevalence-tev-v1/effective-predictions.jsonl \
      --reviewer-type ai_assisted --census-additions
    ```
    
    `prevalence_sample.sql.j2` is packaged with the eval module. Resume validates
    frozen sample/config/protocol hashes and article IDs/input hashes. The source
    archive and dependency hash sidecar retain the inference implementation. The
    primary resume contract checks the orchestrator, preparer and presence module;
    additional serving dependencies are recorded separately rather than all enforced
    by that resume check.
    
    Artifacts under `.tmp/company-prevalence-tev-v1/` include the raw sampled rows,
    prepared inputs and sanitization sidecars, annual universe, group distributions,
    final decisions, DFA candidates, blinded dossiers, review judgments, cross-review
    reconciliation and weighted summaries. Original and post-retry results remain
    separate. The GPU runtime is removed after inference and retries finish.
    
    The main result is `audit-census-summary.json`; `audit-effective-summary.json`
    retains the original 282-row random audit. `audit/all-reviews.csv` contains the
    339 judgments, and `audit/routing-census.json` lists every potential addition.
    `name-sensitivity-summary.json` records the separate preparation diagnostic.
    The final Docker log and cleanup confirmation are retained. The original runtime
    helper session was unavailable at teardown, so no complete GPU-monitor trace
    was recovered; the owned container was removed explicitly after preserving logs.

## Assistant

After reviewing the staging project, I would make **reliable company-linked article coverage** the central requirement for CCFinance. The corpus is already large enough to justify investigation; the unresolved questions are whether it contains enough *distinct, substantively relevant articles per company and year*, whether those articles can be linked accurately, and how much coverage is missing.

I would also revise two points from my earlier answer:

- **The 500-firm and 200-firm targets were speculative.** They are useful scenarios to measure, but I would not make them release promises until the staging data has been evaluated.
- **CC-News beginning in 2016 does not mean every article has a publication date in 2016 or later.** Later crawls can capture older articles. The staging run reports some earlier publication dates, although their validity and coverage need checking. What CC-News cannot establish by itself is that an article was observable to a researcher or the market before it was crawled.

## What the staging results tell us

The [company-tagging report](/home/marcussky/Git/fine-news-financial-publishers/src/python/apps/fine_news_cli/docs/company-tagging.md) documents a complete run over **14,807,287 source rows in 168 files**. That is a promising starting population, but these are neither deduplicated stories nor validated company-relevant articles.

The strongest warning is the 2018 Cadence example:

| Measure | Count |
|---|---:|
| Fine News candidate rows for Cadence | 16 |
| Pricing Perspective’s normalized Nasdaq records | 123 |

These counts have different definitions. The staging analysis nevertheless identifies both a source-URL coverage gap and confirmed missed Cadence name mentions. The 16 cannot be treated as a reliable firm-year coverage estimate, and the 123 cannot establish that every Nasdaq article meets a stricter substantive-relevance definition.

The separate [prevalence audit](/home/marcussky/Git/fine-news-financial-publishers/src/python/apps/fine_news_cli/docs/company-prevalence.md) estimates that **18.06–20.56% of source rows** substantively cover at least one eligible company. It is a useful planning estimate, but it is AI-assisted, includes uncertainty about historical catalogs, counts source rows rather than distinct stories, and does not measure complete company-link precision or recall.

Those findings change the priority: **we need to establish coverage and quality before promising a particular corpus size.**

## Recommended dataset requirements

### 1. Research coverage and sampling

CCFinance should let researchers construct and report firm-level samples for any supported period and company universe.

- Publish counts of **distinct usable articles per company per publication year**, including zero-count company-years for a declared universe.
- Report how many companies satisfy a configurable minimum of \(K\) articles in **every year of a consecutive \(T\)-year window**.
- Provide a standard comparison for **\(K = 47\), \(T = 5\)** alongside alternative thresholds and ten-year windows.
- Report both the raw-candidate counts and stricter counts after deduplication, text-quality filtering and company relevance assessment.
- Break coverage down by year, firm, publisher, sector and, where available, firm size. Document partial years and known acquisition gaps.

The benchmark is Pricing Perspective’s **100 firms with a raw admission floor of 47 articles in each year from 2018–2022**. Its staging comparison also notes that the realized normalized minimum was **34 records** in a firm-year, because the admission rule preceded normalization. CCFinance should aim to exceed that study in *both* the number of qualifying firms and usable articles, but only declare numerical release targets after the audit.

### 2. Article records and source provenance

Each released article should have:

- A stable article identifier; source URL; publisher; headline; extracted body; language; and publication date or timestamp where supported.
- Separate **publication, update and capture times**, including their precision and uncertainty. Never invent intraday precision from a date.
- Source dataset revision and enough lineage to trace the article to its original capture **when available**; explicitly flag missing WARC-level provenance.
- Text-quality indicators, including missing, truncated or extraction-failed bodies.
- A duplicate/story-group identifier, with the underlying records retained or traceable.

Researchers need both the article text and enough context to decide whether it is suitable for their method. Full-body access is particularly important for [Pricing Perspective](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.23447v3) and [Box-style textual similarity](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378426618300773).

### 3. Company identification and relevance

The dataset must represent a **many-to-many relationship between articles and companies**. One article can be associated with several firms, and duplicate handling must preserve all supported article–company associations.

For each association, expose:

- A stable issuer identifier and sourced, time-aware external identifiers where available.
- The company name or evidence that supports the match, its method and version, and any ambiguity.
- Whether the company is merely mentioned or is substantively relevant to the article.
- An explicit unknown or unresolved state when the evidence is insufficient.

Tickers should be treated as dated labels, not permanent identities. The existing staging documentation explicitly says that current registry names, fixed ticker spellings and some crosswalks are **not certified historical identities**.

This requirement also serves [Ge, Li and Linton’s co-mention-network approach](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304407622001488). For that use, finding only one correct company per article is insufficient: the system must evaluate how many of the article’s relevant companies it finds.

### 4. Source selection and content type

The dataset should use a **versioned set of major, credible financial-news sources**, with documented inclusion criteria and coverage by source and year.

The current acquisition list contains **115 hostnames**, but a hostname list is not yet a reviewed list of independent news outlets: it includes aggregators and press-release distributors alongside publishers. CCFinance should distinguish, where possible:

- Original publisher from the hosting or syndicating site.
- Editorial reporting from press releases and other content.
- Different copies of the same story from genuinely distinct reporting.

Researchers should be able to select a publisher set and content types appropriate to their study.

### 5. Scientific quality and evaluation

Before a release claims research readiness, it should include a **human-adjudicated evaluation sample** with published sampling and annotation methods. AI assistance can reduce review effort, but should not be the sole ground truth.

Evaluate at least:

- Company-link **precision and recall**, including missed firms and ambiguous names.
- Substantive relevance separately from name-mention detection.
- Duplicate detection and extraction quality.
- Publication-date accuracy and timestamp precision.
- Performance across publishers, years and company coverage levels, with uncertainty intervals where feasible.

A representative random sample is needed to estimate overall performance. Targeted samples of rare firms, ambiguous names and low-coverage years are also needed to find failure modes; their results should not be pooled into prevalence estimates without accounting for the sampling design.

I would **set numerical precision and recall acceptance thresholds after the initial human audit**, with separate thresholds for the intended applications. For example, a high-precision firm-specific corpus and a high-recall co-mention network may require different operating points.

### 6. Reproducible, accessible releases

A researcher should be able to cite a fixed release and reconstruct its sample from published inputs and configuration. Each release should include:

- Versioned data and schemas, publisher list, company universe, filtering rules, model versions and checksums.
- A data dictionary, coverage tables, quality report and documented limitations.
- Downloadable, partitioned research data and examples for constructing a firm-year panel and a co-mention network.
- A clear article-text access and redistribution policy, with provenance or reconstruction options where full-text redistribution is unavailable.

The Hugging Face staging dataset remains an **input to this process**, not evidence that the final corpus meets these requirements. Experiment outputs and manifests can be preserved in the CCFinance bucket to make comparisons reproducible.

### 7. Later enrichment requirements

To support more of the research currently using RavenPack or Reuters analytics, add separately versioned and evaluated layers for:

- **Article topics:** controlled, multi-label categories.
- **Company-specific events:** event type and company role where supported.
- **Company-specific sentiment:** the target entity, method and model version.
- **Novelty and syndication:** clearly defined comparison windows and methods.

These are valuable goals, but I would not make them prerequisites for a first **text-and-company-link** research release. They need their own evaluation before being described as substitutes for vendor annotations.

The next analysis should produce a defensible **coverage table and error budget**, starting with the 2018–2022 Pricing Perspective roster and then expanding to the historical top-1,000 universe. That will tell us whether the first release can meet the 47-article benchmark, which source and matching gaps matter most, and what realistic five- and ten-year targets should be.

    # CCFinance
    
    CCFinance is a data engineering project for filtering and enriching public
    Common Crawl News (CC-News) copies for research into language in finance.
    
    ## Start
    
    Exordio supplies the Python and LaTeX toolchains, a pinned Nix environment and CI.
    Copier answers record Exordio `v0.1.1-alpha` (the documented `v0.1.0` tag was not
    available in the local source).
    
    ```bash
    bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh
    devenv shell
    just setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run stages list
    just check
    ```
    
    Shared agent instructions and Codex configuration are maintained in
    [`.agents/`](.agents/README.md). `just setup` applies them; use
    `just agents::preview` to preview link changes and `just agents::check` to
    verify the generated links.
    
    `just check` validates Justfile syntax and formatting alongside the other
    quality gates. Run `just fmt` to format Justfiles and other source files.
    
    For Python alone, with Python 3.13, uv and just installed:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::check
    ```
    
    ## Data and reproducibility
    
    DVC is initialized at the repository root with analytics disabled. Use:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc status
    just dvc dag
    ```
    
    Semflow tracks the executable Python dependencies of DVC stages. When adding a
    stage, run `just semflow-patch` to review its proposed fingerprints, then
    `just semflow-apply` to materialize them. Commit the generated
    `.semflow/hashes/` files with the DVC definition. After semantic source changes,
    run `just semflow-refresh`; `just semflow-check` detects stale fingerprints.
    There are no executable stages to instrument yet. The check skips fingerprint
    comparison only while the stage mapping is empty; any future stage must pass
    Semflow's check. Keep data, configuration and environment dependencies explicit
    in DVC: Semflow's static analysis cannot discover string-driven dynamic imports.
    
    See [Python commands](src/python/README.md), [LaTeX commands](src/latex/README.md)
    and [infrastructure](infra/README.md). The scaffold's Apache-2.0 license covers
    code; it does not grant rights to upstream article content.
    ---
    title: Project context
    description: Plans, nested tasks and local literature records.
    ---
    
    # Project context
    
    [Planning](plan/README.md) holds versioned plans and nested tasks. The root
    [roadmap](../ROADMAP.md) lists their immediate children. Schematter validates
    document contracts; Insitu generates child views and backlinks.
    
    `.context/reference/` holds local bibliographic records and source material.
    The entire directory is ignored by Git. Create a record with
    `just reference-new KEY TITLE`; its README owns flat CSL metadata and source
    notes. Local reference records are validated when present but are not required
    for a fresh checkout. The manuscript's `src/latex/refs.bib` remains authored
    and versioned independently.
    
    Edit record frontmatter and prose outside generated regions. Run `just sync`
    to refresh views and `just context-check` to validate them without repairs.
    Reference backlinks stay local; versioned plans must remain understandable
    without the local literature folder. Cite public sources directly in plan prose.
    ---
    title: Planning
    description: Project-owned plans and nested tasks with honest completion and local views.
    ---
    
    # Planning
    
    Create a plan, then its first task:
    
    ```bash
    just plan-new project "Project plan"
    just task-new .context/plan/project first-step "Make the first useful change"
    just sync
    ```
    
    The [root roadmap](../../ROADMAP.md) lists plans. Each plan or task shows only
    its immediate open children and counts terminal children. A deeper task lives
    in its parent's `tasks/SLUG/README.md`; its path supplies identity and parentage.
    Changing status never moves a file or breaks its links.
    
    Edit `status` in frontmatter: `backlog`, `in-progress`, `blocked`, `done` or
    `closed`. `done` requires at least one nonempty active acceptance criterion,
    all checked. Fenced examples and struck-through criteria do not count.
    `closed` stops work without claiming completion and requires `resolution.reason`.
    Terminal parents cannot retain open children. Reopen a parent before adding work.
    
    Every work item keeps one generated children region, including leaves. Edit
    outside the markers; `just sync` refreshes views, while `just check` reports
    invalid records or drift without repairing them. Put longer supporting detail
    in linked files rather than growing the 1,500-token entry point.
    # Architecture
    
    CCFinance separates code and research artifacts. Git stores source, configuration,
    locks, provenance definitions and documentation. DVC will track large data and
    experiment outputs once the actual stages are defined in part 2.
    
    - `src/python/apps/pipeline` owns the CLI and data stage implementations.
    - `src/python/uv.lock` locks runtime, quality, testing, packaging and DVC tools.
    - `src/latex` owns the manuscript source and bibliography.
    - `data` holds ignored data payloads and versioned DVC pointer files.
    - `infra/nix` and `devenv.lock` own the reproducible system environment.
    
    Tach enforces module boundaries; Ruff and strict Pyrefly check Python source.
    pytest-layout-enforcer checks test file placement during collection and CI.
    Semflow fingerprints the Python code used by DVC stages, allowing DVC to
    invalidate tracked results when executable behavior changes.
    CI executes those checks, tests and builds through the same just recipes as local
    work. Setup may download dependencies; ordinary checks use cached dependencies
    and do not repair authored content. LaTeX uses a versioned Tectonic asset bundle.
    
    The Hugging Face dataset is staging, and the bucket is intended for intermediate
    and experiment artifacts. Neither is accessed by scaffold commands. Pipeline
    stages, provenance, study parameters, coverage criteria and remote transport are
    part 2 work, rather than implied by this scaffold.
    
    Copier answers record the source and tag for future template updates. Review
    update conflicts and preserve project-specific code and configuration. The
    upstream template is [Exordio](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/exordio).

    +Specify a public, reproducible financial news dataset for firm-level text,
    +co-mention networks and market research.
    +
    +## Requirements
     
    +- **Coverage:** Report distinct usable articles per company-year, including zero
    +  counts for a declared universe, and firms meeting selectable annual thresholds
    +  over consecutive years. Compare with 47 raw articles per year over 2018–2022
    +  for the 100-firm Pricing Perspective frame; report raw and usable counts separately.
    +- **Articles:** Provide stable IDs, source and publisher, URL, title, article text,
    +  language, publication and capture times with precision, quality flags, and
    +  traceable capture provenance where available.
    +- **Companies:** Preserve all article–company links, dated issuer identifiers,
    +  supporting evidence, ambiguity and substantive relevance. Distinguish mentions
    +  from company-focused coverage and retain unresolved identities.
    +- **Sources:** Maintain versioned publisher selection criteria and distinguish
    +  original reporting, syndicated material and press releases where possible.
    +  Deduplicate stories without discarding source records or company links.
    +- **Research validity:** Evaluate extraction, deduplication, dates, company links
    +  and relevance against human-adjudicated samples. Report precision, recall,
    +  uncertainty and coverage gaps across years, publishers and firms.
    +- **Reproducibility:** Publish a versioned schema, data dictionary, lineage,
    +  checksums, methods, coverage reports and examples for firm-year panels and
    +  co-mention networks. Document article-text access and redistribution conditions.
    +- **Extensions:** Treat company-specific sentiment and events, article topics and
    +  novelty as separately versioned, evaluated enrichments.
    +
    +Numerical coverage and quality targets remain provisional until the staging audit.
    +Publication dates before CC-News began do not establish when text was observable.
    +See the [Pricing Perspective comparison](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.23447v3#Sx1)
    +for the baseline and its limitations.
    +
     ## Acceptance
     
    -- [ ] Define and verify the intended outcome.

    # Raw acquisition inputs
    
    [domains.csv](domains.csv) is the exact 115-hostname allowlist used by the
    original Colab publisher filter. It contains domains rather than individual
    article URLs. Matching includes each listed host and its subdomains, preserving
    specific hosts such as `fortune.cnn.com` without admitting all of `cnn.com`.
    
    The article source remains upstream `ksolovev/fine-news`, pinned to commit
    `7a841090e69f3c58a9e04b0c39213d879af68e8a` in
    [`_filter_config.json`](../../_filter_config.json). Raw article/media files are
    queried remotely and are not duplicated in this directory. The CSV is the
    builder's filter input; the root JSON records the historical dataset filter.
    
    Run from the repository root inside `devenv shell`:
    
    ```bash
    just python::run intermediate build --month 2016-08 --dry-run
    just python::run intermediate build --month 2016-08 --output .tmp/intermediate-trial
    ```
    
    Omit `--month` to select all English capture months. Without `--output`, the
    builder targets `data/01_intermediate`; it refuses any existing destination
    shard before scanning articles. Use a fresh output directory for a rebuild.
    `--source` accepts an explicit `hf://` or local glob with the same
    `YYYY-MM/eng_Latn/*.parquet` layout; `--domains` selects another domain CSV.
    
    The builder runs the [filter SQL](../../src/python/apps/fine_news_cli/src/fine_news_cli/intermediate/filter.sql.j2)
    once per source shard and retains its month/language/filename layout. It
    prefers nonblank `metadata.url_hostname`, falling back to the URL hostname,
    then normalizes case, whitespace and trailing dots. It projects only `text`,
    `id` and `metadata`, excluding separate media columns. Text, IDs and metadata
    values are retained; row ordering and encoded Parquet bytes need not match.
    
    This is the Colab filtering operation without Google Drive mounting, runtime
    package installation, quota monitoring or resume machinery. DuckDB uses two
    threads, a 2 GiB memory limit, a 4 GiB spill limit and Zstandard level 9, as in
    the original. Completed shards are published atomically; failed temporary files
    are removed. A later failure can leave earlier completed shards in place.
    
    The dependency environment can be prepared with `just setup`. Remote builds and
    remote dry runs need network access; a dry run only lists paths. DuckDB installs
    and loads its `httpfs` extension on first remote use. Local source globs work
    offline and are used by the regression tests.
    -- Match a listed hostname or its subdomains, using the Colab fallback rules.
    -- Language selection happens in the source path: YYYY-MM/eng_Latn/*.parquet.
    COPY (
        SELECT text, id, metadata
        FROM read_parquet($source)
        WHERE regexp_matches(
            lower(rtrim(trim(coalesce(
                nullif(trim(metadata.url_hostname), ''),
                regexp_extract(metadata.url, '(?i)^https?://([^/:?#]+)', 1)
            )), '.')),
            $domains
        )
    ) TO $target (
        FORMAT PARQUET, COMPRESSION ZSTD, COMPRESSION_LEVEL 9,
        ROW_GROUP_SIZE 16384
    );

Use when: handling authentication; managing local cache; managing Hugging Face Buckets; running or scheduling jobs on Hugging Face infrastructure; managing Hugging Face repos; discussions and pull requests; browsing models, datasets and spaces; reading, searching, or browsing academic papers; managing collections; querying datasets; configuring spaces; setting up webhooks; or deploying and managing HF Inference Endpoints.     # Pipeline layers: raw -> processed -> research.
    # Each layer will contain independently reproducible DVC sub-stages.
    
    ## Raw: source snapshots
    # Ingest versioned article and company-reference snapshots with source manifests.
    # Preserve source content, metadata and provenance for replay and reconciliation.
    # Proposed location: data/raw/.
    
    ## Processed: reusable tables
    # Clean, standardize and deduplicate articles; resolve dated company identities
    # and enrich article-company relationships. Retain evidence and quality flags.
    # Produce reusable article, company and relationship tables.
    # Proposed location: data/processed/.
    
    ## Research: study datasets
    # Build company-year coverage panels, study cohorts and publication-ready datasets
    # from processed tables. Apply explicit publisher, relevance and K/T coverage policies.
    # Include dataset documentation, provenance and measured quality in each release.
    # Proposed location: data/research/.
    
    ## Validation and evaluation
    # Validate contracts and reconcile counts at every layer. Keep method experiments,
    # independent evaluation labels and quality reports as versioned supporting
    # artifacts; they inform promotion between layers rather than forming a data tier.
    
    # Declare commands, dependencies, parameters and outputs as sub-stages are added.
    stages: {}
    [core]
        analytics = false
    # Python workspace
    
    `apps/pipeline` is an installable Typer application in a Python 3.13 uv workspace.
    Run from the repository root:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run version
    just python::run stages list
    just python::run stages raw --help
    just python::layout
    just python::check
    ```
    
    Data processing is organized into three layers, matching `dvc.yaml`:
    
    | Module and CLI group | Purpose | Data location |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `pipeline.stages.raw` / `stages raw` | Preserve source snapshots and provenance | `data/raw/` |
    | `pipeline.stages.processed` / `stages processed` | Build reusable cleaned and enriched tables | `data/processed/` |
    | `pipeline.stages.research` / `stages research` | Curate coverage panels, cohorts and release datasets | `data/research/` |
    
    Each group provides a namespace for future processing sub-stages. No data
    transformations are implemented yet. Add stage commands under their owning layer,
    with explicit inputs and outputs, and declare their dependencies in `dvc.yaml`.
    DVC connects layers through artifacts; Python modules need not import earlier
    layers to read their outputs. Importing a module performs no dataset access.
    
    Setup installs the committed lock. Checks run offline with frozen dependencies.
    Ruff checks formatting, annotations, docstrings and common correctness/security
    issues; strict Pyrefly checks all app code and tests. Tach enforces module
    boundaries, rejects unused dependency declarations and forbids cycles. The CLI
    imports the stage router, which registers the three independent layer modules.
    
    `pytest-layout-enforcer` checks test paths against their owning source modules
    both during pytest collection and with `just python::layout`. Test paths mirror
    `apps/pipeline/src/pipeline` under `apps/pipeline/tests`: for example,
    `cli.py` maps to `test_cli.py`, and `stages/raw/loader.py` maps to
    `stages/raw/test_loader.py`. Feature variants use `__`, as in
    `test_loader__empty.py`; `include-packages` also allows tests for package
    initializers. This checks existing test placement, not test coverage. Tach checks
    imports and does not enforce this layout.
    
    `just python::test` runs all tests. `test-changed` is a local optimization only.
    `build` builds a wheel and source archive. `fmt` explicitly repairs formatting.
    Ruff and Pyrefly run from the same uv lock locally and in CI.

    $ cat src/python/apps/fine_news_cli/src/fine_news_cli/intermediate/extract.py && cat src/python/apps/fine_news_cli/src/fine_news_cli/intermediate/__init__.py && cat data/README.md
    """Build English publisher shards with the original Colab filter query."""
    
    import csv
    import os
    import re
    from collections.abc import Iterator
    from pathlib import Path
    from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
    
    import duckdb
    
    from fine_news_cli._sql import render_query
    
    QUERY = render_query("fine_news_cli.intermediate", "filter.sql.j2")
    ENGLISH_SHARD = re.compile(
        r"(?:^|/)(\d{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2]))/(eng_Latn)/([^/]+\.parquet)$"
    )
    
    
    def domain_pattern(csv_path: Path) -> str:
        """Read exact hostname allowlist; dots are literal and boundaries explicit."""
        with csv_path.open(newline="") as stream:
            rows = csv.DictReader(stream)
            if rows.fieldnames != ["domain"]:
                raise ValueError("Domain CSV must have one column named domain")
            domains = sorted({row["domain"].strip().lower().rstrip(".") for row in rows})
        if not domains or any(
            not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9-]+(?:\.[a-z0-9-]+)+", d) for d in domains
        ):
            raise ValueError("Domain CSV must contain hostnames, not URLs or blank values")
        return r"(^|\.)(" + "|".join(map(re.escape, domains)) + r")$"
    
    
    def build_intermediate(
        source: str, domains_csv: Path, output: Path, *, dry_run: bool = False
    ) -> Iterator[tuple[str, Path]]:
        """Filter a local or hf:// glob into monthly shards, without overwriting.
    
        Only eng_Latn paths are eligible. Dry runs list files without reading Parquet.
        Outputs retain text/id/metadata exactly; no article qualification is applied.
        """
        pattern = domain_pattern(domains_csv)
        with duckdb.connect(config={"threads": 2, "memory_limit": "2GiB"}) as con:
            if source.startswith("hf://"):
                con.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs")
            con.execute(
                "SET preserve_insertion_order=false; SET max_temp_directory_size='4GiB'"
            )
            con.execute("SET enable_external_file_cache=false")
            files = con.execute(
                "SELECT file FROM glob(?) ORDER BY file", [source]
            ).fetchall()
            plan = [
                (str(file), output.joinpath(*match.groups()))
                for (file,) in files
                if (match := ENGLISH_SHARD.search(str(file)))
            ]
            if not plan:
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    f"No YYYY-MM/eng_Latn Parquet shards match {source}"
                )
            if len({target for _, target in plan}) != len(plan):
                raise ValueError(
                    "Source glob maps multiple inputs to the same output shard"
                )
            if not dry_run:
                for _, target in plan:
                    if target.exists():
                        raise FileExistsError(
                            f"Output exists: {target}; use a fresh output directory"
                        )
            for file, target in plan:
                if not dry_run:
                    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    with TemporaryDirectory(dir=target.parent) as staging:
                        temporary = Path(staging) / "shard.parquet"
                        con.execute(
                            QUERY,
                            {"source": file, "domains": pattern, "target": str(temporary)},
                        )
                        # Publish only a complete file; link refuses a concurrent overwrite.
                        os.link(temporary, target)
                yield file, target
    """Commands for the publisher- and language-filtered intermediate shards."""
    
    import json
    import re
    from pathlib import Path
    from typing import Annotated
    
    import typer
    
    from fine_news_cli._shared import inspect_source
    from fine_news_cli.intermediate.extract import build_intermediate
    
    app = typer.Typer(
        help="Build and inspect 01_intermediate shards.", no_args_is_help=True
    )
    
    
    @app.command()
    def inspect(
        source: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Argument(help="Parquet shard, stage directory or repo root.")
        ] = Path("data/01_intermediate"),
    ) -> None:
        """Report row count and schema as JSON."""
        inspect_source(source)
    
    
    @app.command()
    def build(
        month: Annotated[
            str, typer.Option(help="Capture month YYYY-MM, or * for all.")
        ] = "*",
        source: Annotated[
            str | None, typer.Option(help="Override with a local or hf:// glob.")
        ] = None,
        domains: Annotated[Path, typer.Option(help="CSV with one domain column.")] = Path(
            "data/00_raw/domains.csv"
        ),
        output: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="Destination root; existing shards are refused.")
        ] = Path("data/01_intermediate"),
        dry_run: Annotated[
            bool, typer.Option(help="List planned files without scanning articles.")
        ] = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Query Fine News on Hugging Face and retain English publisher articles."""
        if not re.fullmatch(r"\*|\d{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2])", month):
            raise ValueError("Month must be YYYY-MM or *")
        if source is not None and month != "*":
            raise ValueError("Use either --month or --source")
        if source is None:
            config = json.loads(Path("_filter_config.json").read_text())
            source = (
                f"hf://datasets/{config['repo']}@{config['commit']}"
                f"/data/{month}/eng_Latn/*.parquet"
            )
        for file, target in build_intermediate(source, domains, output, dry_run=dry_run):
            typer.echo(f"{'Plan' if dry_run else 'Wrote'}: {file} -> {target}")
    # Data stages
    
    The raw source is `ksolovev/fine-news` at the revision recorded in
    [`_filter_config.json`](../_filter_config.json). [00_raw](00_raw/README.md) records the domain allowlist used to query that
    source. The full upstream raw corpus is not duplicated locally.
    
    | Stage | Contents | Git policy |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `00_raw/` | Domain CSV used by the acquisition query; raw articles remain upstream | Tracked text inputs |
    | `01_intermediate/YYYY-MM/eng_Latn/` | Publisher and English-language filtered shards, preserving upstream text, IDs and metadata | Tracked with Git LFS |
    | `02_primary/` | Cleaned article records, retaining original fields and source lineage | Generated files ignored; `.gitkeep` tracked |
    | `03_feature/` | Primary records enriched with derived attributes | Generated files ignored; `.gitkeep` tracked |
    
    Numbering begins at `00_raw`. Model input, models and reporting stages can be
    introduced when they have a concrete consumer and data contract.
    
    ## Current transformations
    
    `fine-news intermediate build` runs a short DuckDB `hf://` query on the pinned
    upstream revision, selects English capture paths and filters by
    [the domain CSV](00_raw/domains.csv). It retains `text`, `id` and `metadata` and
    preserves monthly shard paths. See [acquisition inputs](00_raw/README.md) for
    reproduction and the differences from the original Colab runtime.
    
    `fine-news primary build` normalizes whitespace into `clean_text` and removes
    blank articles. It does not deduplicate, assign new IDs or resolve company
    memberships. These remain future primary-stage work.
    
    `fine-news feature build` adds publisher hostname, publication date, character
    count and word count. It retains the primary record and original `source_path`.
    Publication dates that cannot be parsed become null. No embedding or model
    features are computed yet. Both builders refuse to overwrite existing outputs.
    
    ## Commands
    
    Run from the repository root inside `devenv shell`:
    
    ```bash
    just python::run intermediate build --month 2016-08 --dry-run
    just python::run intermediate inspect
    just python::run primary build
    just python::run feature build
    ```
    
    The default builders process their entire preceding stage. For a small trial:
    
    ```bash
    just python::run primary build data/01_intermediate/2016-08/eng_Latn/part-000000.parquet --output data/02_primary/2016-08.parquet
    just python::run feature build data/02_primary/2016-08.parquet --output data/03_feature/2016-08.parquet
    ```
    
    After setup, commands use frozen dependencies. Inspection and primary/feature
    builds operate offline; remote intermediate acquisition requires network access. Use `--help` on
    any stage to see its commands. Derived files stay local until their versioning
    and publication policies are explicitly defined.

## Assistant

The staging acquisition is a single English-and-publisher filter over a pinned Fine News revision. One important detail is that the checked-in builder describes the historical transformation; we have not yet established that rerunning it produces byte-identical staging shards.

## Plan

# Document the historical Fine News acquisition

## Summary

Add one frozen `raw` stage describing how the existing staging dataset was selected from [Fine News](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ksolovev/fine-news):

1. Read English-language Parquet shards from the pinned upstream revision.
2. Keep rows whose publisher hostname matches the historical allowlist.
3. Write the original `text`, `id` and `metadata` columns into monthly Parquet shards.

This describes the **staging dataset**, not the final research-ready CCFinance dataset. Cleaning, company tagging and evaluation are later stages.

## Assets and stage

- Add a versioned configuration containing upstream repository `ksolovev/fine-news`, revision `7a841090e69f3c58a9e04b0c39213d879af68e8a`, language `eng_Latn` and the output location.
- Copy the staging project’s historical **115-domain CSV** as the filter input. Preserve its contents; reviewing which publishers are trusted is separate work.
- Add a small `pipeline.stages.raw` implementation and Typer command using DuckDB. Match the staging filter: prefer `metadata.url_hostname`, fall back to the hostname in `metadata.url`, normalize it, and accept an allowlisted hostname or its subdomains. Preserve the month/language/shard layout and selected fields.
- Add a `dvc.yaml` stage with explicit configuration, domain-list, code and environment dependencies; declare the filtered shard directory as its output and set `frozen: true`. Integrate the new stage with Semflow and the existing quality gates.
- Document the input revision, transformation, output contract and limitations. Capture months are crawl months, not necessarily publication months. The upstream dataset has its own filtering and deduplication history; its article-text terms require separate assessment. [Fine News dataset card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ksolovev/fine-news)

## Verification

- Use a small local Parquet fixture to check exact-domain and subdomain matches, URL fallback, excluded domains and preservation of the selected fields and shard layout.
- Check that DVC recognizes the stage and that ordinary `dvc repro` skips it, then run `just check`.
- Do not run the full acquisition, download the corpus or publish data during this work.

## Assumptions and limits

The stage is a reproducible **recipe**, not proof that the existing staging shards can be rebuilt byte-for-byte. No DVC lock entry or cached output should be presented as a completed acquisition until outputs are actually built or verified and tracked.

DVC freezing prevents execution during `dvc repro`, including forced reproduction; explicitly unfreezing the stage or invoking its command directly can still run it. [DVC freeze documentation](https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/freeze)


## User

Implement the plan.

## Assistant

I’ll add the frozen acquisition recipe using the historical revision and domain list, then verify it against a small local Parquet fixture and the repository’s quality gates.
