    ---
    name: python-testing
    description: Use when writing, changing, reviewing or organizing Python tests, pytest fixtures or Hypothesis strategies in CCFinance.
    ---
    
    # Python testing
    
    ## Workflow
    
    1. Inspect the code contract, nearby tests, `conftest.py`, shared fixtures and
       strategies, the package's test README, and pytest configuration. Reuse an
       existing test or generator when it covers the behavior; extend it only for a
       distinct, meaningful risk. Do not add tests for trivial or reversible changes
       just to increase counts, or tests that restate implementation details.
    2. Prefer Hypothesis for input variation when a general property is meaningful.
       Prefer a small explicit example for a single known boundary, regression or
       command smoke check. Decide the expected outcome independently of the code
       under test. Use tiny representative data, bounded generators and the smallest
       appropriate test boundary. Assert public behavior, including error contracts.
    3. Place a test beside its source owner under the mirrored `tests/` layout. Reuse
       existing factories and strategies first. Keep a helper local until several
       tests need it; put cross-module strategies in `tests/_strategies.py` and
       shared pytest fixtures in the nearest common `conftest.py`. Place a fixture
       at broader scope only when its state is safe to share. Measure costly setup
       before broadening scope; avoid creating generic fixture frameworks.
    4. Arrange inputs and prerequisites, act on the behavior, and assert observable
       results (AAA). Cleanup belongs in a fixture finalizer or context manager.
       Label each phase with an `# Arrange`, `# Act` or `# Assert` comment, as in
       the example below. Favor DAMP: clear names and visible expected values can
       justify a little repetition.
    5. Give each new or modified test exactly one scope marker from the table below;
       add `slow` or `external` only when applicable. Mark a class or module only
       when every inherited test has the same scope. Never stack or override scope
       markers, including inherited marks. Before using markers, register the six
       names in the owning pytest configuration; unknown names fail under
       `--strict-markers`. This skill defines the policy; it does not mean the
       current unmarked suite already enforces it. Migrate existing tests deliberately
       if adding a collection-time enforcement hook.
    6. During development, run the smallest relevant test or selection and check
       its output. Before handoff run the repository's required full checks, including
       the complete non-Testmon suite. Run any affected slow or external tests when
       their prerequisites and authorization are available; report what was not run
       and why. A targeted pass is not evidence that the full suite passed.
    
    ## Markers
    
    Use only these six custom markers. Built-in pytest mechanisms such as
    `parametrize`, `skipif` and `xfail` remain available for their intended purposes.
    Scope describes the boundary the assertions exercise, not the number of files,
    the use of Hypothesis, or the choice of a reference oracle.
    
    | Marker | Rule |
    | --- | --- |
    | `unit` | Exactly one scope: an isolated operation or small self-contained behavior. |
    | `component` | Exactly one scope: one coherent subsystem or component through its public behavior. |
    | `integration` | Exactly one scope: interactions across components or a real dependency boundary. |
    | `e2e` | Exactly one scope: a complete user-visible workflow through the public CLI or API. A CLI help check alone is not end-to-end. |
    | `slow` | Optional execution label: the complete test, including setup, teardown and generated examples, consistently exceeds two seconds on the normal local environment. Confirm with repeated pytest duration reports; a single noisy measurement is not enough. |
    | `external` | Optional execution label: the test accesses a live network service or external account. Use even if it is usually fast; require explicit opt-in and appropriate credentials. A local temporary file, subprocess or fake alone does not qualify. |
    
    `slow` and `external` are independent and may accompany any one scope. Do not
    invent custom markers for regression, reference, property, smoke, tools or
    implementation techniques; communicate those in descriptive test names and
    assertions. Run fast local iteration with `-m "not slow and not external"`
    after the markers are registered. Full checks must not silently omit slow tests;
    external tests need a separate explicit lane and must not mutate live services
    without authorization.
    
    ## Hypothesis examples and fixtures
    
    Hypothesis strategies generate values; pytest fixtures manage resources. If
    Hypothesis is absent, add it to the locked workspace development dependencies
    when introducing the first test that uses it. Search
    for reusable strategies or an appropriate first-party Hypothesis extra before
    adding one. Compose built-in strategies, use `@composite` for dependent values,
    and generate valid inputs directly rather than filtering most examples. Keep
    sizes bounded and counterexamples understandable. Preserve an important known
    failure using `@example` or an explicit regression; do not duplicate a property
    with a long list of examples that establish the same behavior.
    
    A function-scoped pytest fixture runs once per test function, not once per
    `@given` example. For per-example mutable resources, create and clean them inside
    the test, for example with `TemporaryDirectory()`. Reuse immutable shared data
    only when safe. Do not suppress health checks or disable deadlines globally to
    make a test pass; investigate the cause and document a narrowly justified
    exception. Choose explicit settings or a shared profile only when warranted by
    measured cost. Preserve failing examples and replay information as appropriate.
    
    This self-contained example illustrates a small property, AAA and the scope
    marker; it uses the standard-library URL parser rather than a CCFinance stage:
    
    ```python
    from string import ascii_lowercase, digits
    from urllib.parse import urlsplit
    
    import pytest
    from hypothesis import example, given, strategies as st
    
    
    @pytest.mark.unit
    @example(host="news")
    @given(host=st.text(alphabet=ascii_lowercase + digits, min_size=1, max_size=20))
    def test_url_hostname_normalizes_ascii_case(host: str) -> None:
        # Arrange: build a URL with an uppercase hostname.
        url = f"https://{host.upper()}.example/article"
    
        # Act: extract the hostname.
        hostname = urlsplit(url).hostname
    
        # Assert: the hostname is lowercase.
        assert hostname == f"{host}.example"
    ```
    
    Use a real local Parquet or filesystem boundary for a small integration test
    when that interaction matters; use a stub or fake for costly or nondeterministic
    remote services. A fake cannot establish that the real service works. Keep
    randomized tests independent of execution order; for numerical or sampling
    claims define tolerances and uncertainty rather than requiring arbitrary
    bit-for-bit agreement across environments.
    
    Consult the Hypothesis [tutorial](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorial/),
    [how-to guides](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how-to/),
    [strategies and API reference](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/)
    and [extras](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/extras.html) when
    choosing or debugging a strategy.
    ---
    name: architecture-layout
    description: Use when evaluating or designing where CCFinance code, data stages, tests, documents or infrastructure belong, including module boundaries and repository restructures.
    ---
    
    # Architecture layout
    
    ## Workflow
    
    1. Establish the requested scope and outcome: evaluate the current layout,
       design a layout, or implement an authorized change. Read nearby README and
       ARCHITECTURE files. Identify existing owners and consumers before proposing
       a new abstraction; reuse an existing module or library when it satisfies the
       contract. File size alone is not a reason to split or create a package.
    2. Examine the relevant boundaries using evidence:
       - **Ownership and cohesion:** Can a contributor find the owner, and do things
         that change together live together? Keep each unit's responsibility clear.
       - **Dependencies and encapsulation:** Trace relevant imports and public
         interfaces. Keep intended dependency direction clear and cycles forbidden;
         avoid reaching into another module's internals without a reason.
       - **Coupling:** Identify changes that force unrelated owners to change.
         Share a contract only when consumers actually need the same behavior; a
         little local duplication may be preferable to coupling distinct contracts.
       - **Discoverability:** Make CLI commands, transformations, schemas, tests,
         fixtures and documents easy to find from their owning area.
    3. Choose the smallest useful boundary: a function, module, package or separate
       workspace project. A package or project should reflect an actual dependency,
       distribution, build or ownership need. Organize by layer, capability or a
       combination according to the work; do not impose a universal directory tree.
    4. For pipeline work, preserve the established `raw`, `processed` and `research`
       stage ownership. Organize capabilities within those layers as they arise.
       Distinguish Python imports from DVC artifact dependencies: the latter connect
       producers and consumers without requiring cross-layer Python imports. Apply
       Tach rules to durable module boundaries and DVC to artifact dependencies.
    5. For a move or split, trace the affected consumers before changing paths:
       imports and public APIs, CLI registration, package configuration, tests and
       fixtures, Tach, DVC and Semflow dependencies, and documentation links as
       applicable. Preserve behavior and scientific contracts unless the user asks
       for a change; report any intended behavior change separately. Do not treat
       missing static references as proof that dynamic or external consumers do not
       exist.
    6. Use the repository's existing gates rather than adding tests that merely
       assert a directory tree or private call sequence. For tests and fixtures,
       follow [Python testing](../python-testing/SKILL.md). Run focused checks while
       working and `just check` before handoff; report checks that could not run.
    
    ## Results
    
    For an evaluation, report concrete findings with locations, effects and ranked
    recommendations. For a design, show the proposed ownership and dependency
    boundaries, explain meaningful tradeoffs and how they are enforced. For an
    implementation, summarize what moved, whether behavior changed and the evidence
    from verification. Keep the review proportional to the requested change.
    
    For example, if both article cleaning and company linking need the same
    publication-date parser, first inspect its existing owner and date semantics.
    Share it only if both consumers require the same contract; keep separate rules
    when their treatment of missing or ambiguous dates differs.

    - Use the pinned devenv environment and repository just commands.
    - Run Python commands through the appropriate locked uv project.
    - Authored records own state. Use explicit creation and synchronization commands; never edit generated Insitu regions by hand.
    - Task parents expose immediate children. Put supporting evidence in separate records and preserve stable paths.
    - Checks validate without repair; use just fmt and just sync for explicit changes.
    - Run just check before handoff and report any checks that could not run.
    - Resolve secrets only for commands that need them. Never place credentials in tracked files.

    """Data layers and their processing commands."""
    
    import typer
    
    from pipeline.stages import processed, raw, research
    
    app = typer.Typer(no_args_is_help=True, help="Data processing layers.")
    app.add_typer(raw.app, name="raw", help=raw.__doc__)
    app.add_typer(processed.app, name="processed", help=processed.__doc__)
    app.add_typer(research.app, name="research", help=research.__doc__)
    
    
    @app.command(name="list")
    def list_stages() -> None:
        """List pipeline layers and their purpose."""
        for group in app.registered_groups:
            typer.echo(f"{group.name}: {group.help}")
    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    set positional-arguments
    
    default:
        @just --list
    
    # Install exactly the committed workspace and build dependencies.
    setup:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv sync --locked --all-packages
    
    run *args:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline pipeline "$@"
    
    lint:

        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff format --check .

    # Local impacted-test selection, with a bounded number of workers.
    test-changed:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest -q -n 2 --testmon
    
    # The test and CI gates never use affected-test selection.
    test:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest -q -n 2 --no-testmon
    
    # Check that test paths correspond to source modules.

    # Enforce module dependencies, reject unused declarations and forbid cycles.
    tach:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen tach check
    
    build:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv build --python .venv/bin/python --offline --no-build-isolation --all-packages
    
    check: lint typecheck tach layout test build

    """Reproduce the historical Fine News publisher filter."""
    
    import csv
    import json
    import os
    import re
    from pathlib import Path
    from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
    from typing import Annotated
    
    import duckdb
    import typer
    
    SHARD = re.compile(r"(?:^|/)(\d{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2]))/(eng_Latn)/([^/]+\.parquet)$")
    QUERY = """
        COPY (
            SELECT text, id, metadata FROM read_parquet($source)
            WHERE regexp_matches(
                lower(rtrim(trim(coalesce(
                    nullif(trim(metadata.url_hostname), ''),
                    regexp_extract(metadata.url, '(?i)^https?://([^/:?#]+)', 1)
                )), '.')), $domains
            )
        ) TO $target (FORMAT PARQUET, COMPRESSION ZSTD, COMPRESSION_LEVEL 9,
                     ROW_GROUP_SIZE 16384)
    """
    
    
    def domain_pattern(path: Path) -> str:
        """Build a boundary-aware pattern from the historical hostname list."""
        with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            reader = csv.DictReader(stream)
            if reader.fieldnames != ["domain"]:
                raise ValueError("Domain CSV must have one column named domain")
            domains = sorted({row["domain"].strip().lower().rstrip(".") for row in reader})
        if not domains or any(
            not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9-]+(?:\.[a-z0-9-]+)+", domain) for domain in domains
        ):
            raise ValueError("Domain CSV must contain hostnames")
        return r"(^|\.)(" + "|".join(map(re.escape, domains)) + r")$"
    
    
    def filter_shards(source: str, domains: Path, output: Path, *, dry_run: bool = False) -> None:
        """Filter English shards without overwriting an existing output."""
        pattern = domain_pattern(domains)
        with duckdb.connect(config={"threads": 2, "memory_limit": "2GiB"}) as con:
            if source.startswith("hf://"):
                con.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs")
            con.execute("SET preserve_insertion_order=false; SET max_temp_directory_size='4GiB'")
            con.execute("SET enable_external_file_cache=false")
            files = con.execute("SELECT file FROM glob(?) ORDER BY file", [source]).fetchall()
            plan = [
                (str(file), output.joinpath(*match.groups()))
                for (file,) in files
                if (match := SHARD.search(str(file)))
            ]
            if not plan:
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"No English Parquet shards match {source}")
            if len({target for _, target in plan}) != len(plan):
                raise ValueError("Multiple source files map to the same output")
            if not dry_run:
                for _, target in plan:
                    if target.exists():
                        raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {target}")
            for file, target in plan:
                if not dry_run:
                    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    with TemporaryDirectory(dir=target.parent) as staging:
                        temporary = Path(staging) / "shard.parquet"
                        con.execute(QUERY, {"source": file, "domains": pattern, "target": str(temporary)})
                        os.link(temporary, target)
                typer.echo(f"{'Plan' if dry_run else 'Wrote'}: {file} -> {target}")
    
    
    def filter_fine_news(
        config: Annotated[Path, typer.Option(help="Historical acquisition configuration.")] = Path(
            "config/fine-news/acquisition.json"
        ),
        source: Annotated[str | None, typer.Option(help="Override with a local or hf:// glob.")] = None,
        output: Annotated[Path | None, typer.Option(help="Override the output directory.")] = None,
        dry_run: Annotated[bool, typer.Option(help="List input and output shards without filtering.")] = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Select English publisher shards from a pinned Fine News revision."""
        settings = json.loads(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if settings["language"] != "eng_Latn":
            raise ValueError("Only the historical eng_Latn selection is supported")
        if source is None:
            source = (
                f"hf://datasets/{settings['repository']}@{settings['revision']}"
                f"/data/*/{settings['language']}/*.parquet"
            )
        filter_shards(source, Path(settings["domains"]), output or Path(settings["output"]), dry_run=dry_run)

    """Exercise the historical acquisition against local Parquet files."""
    
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import duckdb
    import pytest
    from pipeline.stages.raw.fine_news import filter_shards
    
    
    @pytest.mark.integration
    def test_filter_preserves_english_publisher_rows(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        # Arrange: create a tiny source shard and a historical-style domain list.
        source = tmp_path / "input/2020-01/eng_Latn/part-000000.parquet"
        source.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        domains = tmp_path / "domains.csv"
        domains.write_text("domain\nexample.com\n", encoding="utf-8")
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            con.execute(
                """COPY (SELECT * FROM (VALUES
                    ('1', 'one', {'url_hostname': 'EXAMPLE.COM.', 'url': 'https://wrong.test/a'}),
                    ('2', 'two', {'url_hostname': 'news.example.com', 'url': 'https://wrong.test/b'}),
                    ('3', 'three', {'url_hostname': '', 'url': 'https://example.com/c'}),
                    ('4', 'four', {'url_hostname': 'notexample.com', 'url': 'https://example.com/d'})
                ) AS rows(id, text, metadata)) TO ? (FORMAT PARQUET)""",
                [str(source)],
            )
    
        # Act: filter the source through the public acquisition operation.
        output = tmp_path / "output"
        filter_shards(str(source), domains, output)
    
        # Assert: only eligible rows and their original fields are preserved.
        target = output / "2020-01/eng_Latn/part-000000.parquet"
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            result = con.execute(
                "SELECT id, text, metadata.url_hostname, metadata.url FROM read_parquet(?) ORDER BY id",
                [str(target)],
            ).fetchall()
        assert result == [
            ("1", "one", "EXAMPLE.COM.", "https://wrong.test/a"),
            ("2", "two", "news.example.com", "https://wrong.test/b"),
            ("3", "three", "", "https://example.com/c"),
        ]

    """Reproduce the historical Fine News publisher filter."""
    
    import csv
    import json
    import os
    import re
    from pathlib import Path
    from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
    from typing import Annotated
    
    import duckdb
    import typer
    
    SHARD = re.compile(r"(?:^|/)(\d{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2]))/(eng_Latn)/([^/]+\.parquet)$")
    QUERY = """
        COPY (
            SELECT text, id, metadata FROM read_parquet($source)
            WHERE regexp_matches(
                lower(rtrim(trim(coalesce(
                    nullif(trim(metadata.url_hostname), ''),
                    regexp_extract(metadata.url, '(?i)^https?://([^/:?#]+)', 1)
                )), '.')), $domains
            )
        ) TO $target (FORMAT PARQUET, COMPRESSION ZSTD, COMPRESSION_LEVEL 9,
                     ROW_GROUP_SIZE 16384)
    """
    
    
    def domain_pattern(path: Path) -> str:
        """Build a boundary-aware pattern from the historical hostname list."""
        with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            reader = csv.DictReader(stream)
            if reader.fieldnames != ["domain"]:
                raise ValueError("Domain CSV must have one column named domain")
            domains = sorted({row["domain"].strip().lower().rstrip(".") for row in reader})
        if not domains or any(
            not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9-]+(?:\.[a-z0-9-]+)+", domain) for domain in domains
        ):
            raise ValueError("Domain CSV must contain hostnames")
        return r"(^|\.)(" + "|".join(map(re.escape, domains)) + r")$"
    
    
    def filter_shards(
        source: str, domains: Path, output: Path, *, dry_run: bool = False
    ) -> None:
        """Filter English shards without overwriting an existing output."""
        pattern = domain_pattern(domains)
        with duckdb.connect(config={"threads": 2, "memory_limit": "2GiB"}) as con:
            if source.startswith("hf://"):
                con.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs")
            con.execute(
                "SET preserve_insertion_order=false; SET max_temp_directory_size='4GiB'"
            )
            con.execute("SET enable_external_file_cache=false")
            files = con.execute(
                "SELECT file FROM glob(?) ORDER BY file", [source]
            ).fetchall()
            plan = [
                (str(file), output.joinpath(*match.groups()))
                for (file,) in files
                if (match := SHARD.search(str(file)))
            ]
            if not plan:
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"No English Parquet shards match {source}")
            if len({target for _, target in plan}) != len(plan):
                raise ValueError("Multiple source files map to the same output")
            if not dry_run:
                for _, target in plan:
                    if target.exists():
                        raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {target}")
            for file, target in plan:
                if not dry_run:
                    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    with TemporaryDirectory(dir=target.parent) as staging:
                        temporary = Path(staging) / "shard.parquet"
                        con.execute(
                            QUERY,
                            {"source": file, "domains": pattern, "target": str(temporary)},
                        )
                        os.link(temporary, target)
                typer.echo(f"{'Plan' if dry_run else 'Wrote'}: {file} -> {target}")
    
    
    def filter_fine_news(
        config: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="Historical acquisition configuration.")
        ] = Path("config/fine-news/acquisition.json"),
        source: Annotated[
            str | None, typer.Option(help="Override with a local or hf:// glob.")
        ] = None,
        output: Annotated[
            Path | None, typer.Option(help="Override the output directory.")
        ] = None,
        dry_run: Annotated[
            bool, typer.Option(help="List input and output shards without filtering.")
        ] = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Select English publisher shards from a pinned Fine News revision."""
        settings = json.loads(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if settings["language"] != "eng_Latn":
            raise ValueError("Only the historical eng_Latn selection is supported")
        if source is None:
            source = (
                f"hf://datasets/{settings['repository']}@{settings['revision']}"
                f"/data/*/{settings['language']}/*.parquet"
            )
        filter_shards(
            source,
            Path(settings["domains"]),
            output or Path(settings["output"]),
            dry_run=dry_run,
        )

    $ sed -n '38,65p' README.md && sed -n '20,45p' src/python/README.md && tail -20 dvc.yaml && cat ARCHITECTURE.md
    DVC is initialized at the repository root with analytics disabled. Use:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc status
    just dvc dag
    ```
    
    Semflow tracks the executable Python dependencies of DVC stages. When adding a
    stage, run `just semflow-patch` to review its proposed fingerprints, then
    `just semflow-apply` to materialize them. Commit the generated
    `.semflow/hashes/` files with the DVC definition. After semantic source changes,
    run `just semflow-refresh`; `just semflow-check` detects stale fingerprints.
    There are no executable stages to instrument yet. The check skips fingerprint
    comparison only while the stage mapping is empty; any future stage must pass
    Semflow's check. Keep data, configuration and environment dependencies explicit
    in DVC: Semflow's static analysis cannot discover string-driven dynamic imports.
    
    See [Python commands](src/python/README.md), [LaTeX commands](src/latex/README.md)
    and [infrastructure](infra/README.md). The scaffold's Apache-2.0 license covers
    code; it does not grant rights to upstream article content.
    | `pipeline.stages.raw` / `stages raw` | Preserve source snapshots and provenance | `data/raw/` |
    | `pipeline.stages.processed` / `stages processed` | Build reusable cleaned and enriched tables | `data/processed/` |
    | `pipeline.stages.research` / `stages research` | Curate coverage panels, cohorts and release datasets | `data/research/` |
    
    Each group provides a namespace for future processing sub-stages. No data
    transformations are implemented yet. Add stage commands under their owning layer,
    with explicit inputs and outputs, and declare their dependencies in `dvc.yaml`.
    DVC connects layers through artifacts; Python modules need not import earlier
    layers to read their outputs. Importing a module performs no dataset access.
    
    Setup installs the committed lock. Checks run offline with frozen dependencies.
    Ruff checks formatting, annotations, docstrings and common correctness/security
    issues; strict Pyrefly checks all app code and tests. Tach enforces module
    boundaries, rejects unused dependency declarations and forbids cycles. The CLI
    imports the stage router, which registers the three independent layer modules.
    
    `pytest-layout-enforcer` checks test paths against their owning source modules
    both during pytest collection and with `just python::layout`. Test paths mirror
    `apps/pipeline/src/pipeline` under `apps/pipeline/tests`: for example,
    `cli.py` maps to `test_cli.py`, and `stages/raw/loader.py` maps to
    `stages/raw/test_loader.py`. Feature variants use `__`, as in
    `test_loader__empty.py`; `include-packages` also allows tests for package
    initializers. This checks existing test placement, not test coverage. Tach checks
    imports and does not enforce this layout.
    
    `just python::test` runs all tests. `test-changed` is a local optimization only.
    
    ## Validation and evaluation
    # Validate contracts and reconcile counts at every layer. Keep method experiments,
    # independent evaluation labels and quality reports as versioned supporting
    # artifacts; they inform promotion between layers rather than forming a data tier.
    
    stages:
      filter_fine_news:
        desc: Reproduce the historical English financial-publisher selection from Fine News.
        cmd: >-
          env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python
          --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline pipeline stages raw filter-fine-news
        frozen: true
        deps:
          - config/fine-news/acquisition.json
          - config/fine-news/domains.csv
          - src/python/uv.lock
          - src/python/apps/pipeline/src/pipeline/stages/raw/fine_news.py
        outs:
          - data/raw/fine-news
    # Architecture
    
    CCFinance separates code and research artifacts. Git stores source, configuration,
    locks, provenance definitions and documentation. DVC will track large data and
    experiment outputs once the actual stages are defined in part 2.
    
    - `src/python/apps/pipeline` owns the CLI and data stage implementations.
    - `src/python/uv.lock` locks runtime, quality, testing, packaging and DVC tools.
    - `src/latex` owns the manuscript source and bibliography.
    - `data` holds ignored data payloads and versioned DVC pointer files.
    - `infra/nix` and `devenv.lock` own the reproducible system environment.
    
    Tach enforces module boundaries; Ruff and strict Pyrefly check Python source.
    pytest-layout-enforcer checks test file placement during collection and CI.
    Semflow fingerprints the Python code used by DVC stages, allowing DVC to
    invalidate tracked results when executable behavior changes.
    CI executes those checks, tests and builds through the same just recipes as local
    work. Setup may download dependencies; ordinary checks use cached dependencies
    and do not repair authored content. LaTeX uses a versioned Tectonic asset bundle.
    
    The Hugging Face dataset is staging, and the bucket is intended for intermediate
    and experiment artifacts. Neither is accessed by scaffold commands. Pipeline
    stages, provenance, study parameters, coverage criteria and remote transport are
    part 2 work, rather than implied by this scaffold.
    
    Copier answers record the source and tag for future template updates. Review
    update conflicts and preserve project-specific code and configuration. The
    upstream template is [Exordio](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/exordio).
    ✓ • 0ms

    # Fine News acquisition
    
    `filter_fine_news` documents the historical staging selection from
    [Fine News](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ksolovev/fine-news) at the revision
    in [acquisition.json](acquisition.json). It selects `eng_Latn` capture-month
    shards and the exact 115-hostname [allowlist](domains.csv), including subdomains.
    The hostname comes from `metadata.url_hostname`, falling back to `metadata.url`
    when blank. The output preserves `text`, `id` and `metadata` under
    `data/raw/fine-news/YYYY-MM/eng_Latn/`.
    
    This is the historical source filter, not a reviewed publisher list or a
    research-ready article corpus. Fine News applies its own filters and
    deduplication; capture month is not necessarily publication month. The upstream
    dataset card describes content rights and usage restrictions. No full output has
    been built, verified or cached here, and no DVC lock entry is claimed.
    
    The stage is frozen: `dvc repro` will not execute it, even with `--force`.
    Since the declared output is absent, targeting it currently reports missing data.
    After obtaining or rebuilding and verifying the output, track its actual state
    before relying on it downstream. Unfreezing or invoking the command directly can
    run the acquisition and requires network access and substantial resources.
    DuckDB may download its `httpfs` extension on first remote access.
    
    For a local trial, use `just python::run stages raw filter-fine-news --help`;
    `--source` and `--output` can select a local shard and fresh destination.
    The script refuses to overwrite existing shards. Output order and Parquet bytes
    are not guaranteed to match the existing staging dataset.

    ---
    name: architecture-layout
    description: Use when evaluating or designing where CCFinance code, data stages, tests, documents or infrastructure belong, including module boundaries and repository restructures.
    ---
    
    # Architecture layout
    
    ## Workflow
    
    1. Establish the requested scope and outcome: evaluate the current layout,
       design a layout, or implement an authorized change. Read nearby README and
       ARCHITECTURE files. Identify existing owners and consumers before proposing
       a new abstraction; reuse an existing module or library when it satisfies the
       contract. File size alone is not a reason to split or create a package.
    2. Examine the relevant boundaries using evidence:
       - **Ownership and cohesion:** Can a contributor find the owner, and do things
         that change together live together? Keep each unit's responsibility clear.
       - **Dependencies and encapsulation:** Trace relevant imports and public
         interfaces. Keep intended dependency direction clear and cycles forbidden;
         avoid reaching into another module's internals without a reason.
       - **Coupling:** Identify changes that force unrelated owners to change.
         Share a contract only when consumers actually need the same behavior; a
         little local duplication may be preferable to coupling distinct contracts.
       - **Discoverability:** Make CLI commands, transformations, schemas, tests,
         fixtures and documents easy to find from their owning area.
    3. Choose the smallest useful boundary: a function, module, package or separate
       workspace project. A package or project should reflect an actual dependency,
       distribution, build or ownership need. Organize by layer, capability or a
       combination according to the work; do not impose a universal directory tree.
    4. For pipeline work, preserve the established `raw`, `processed` and `research`
       stage ownership. Organize capabilities within those layers as they arise.
       Distinguish Python imports from DVC artifact dependencies: the latter connect
       producers and consumers without requiring cross-layer Python imports. Apply
       Tach rules to durable module boundaries and DVC to artifact dependencies.
    5. For a move or split, trace the affected consumers before changing paths:
       imports and public APIs, CLI registration, package configuration, tests and
       fixtures, Tach, DVC and Semflow dependencies, and documentation links as
       applicable. Preserve behavior and scientific contracts unless the user asks
       for a change; report any intended behavior change separately. Do not treat
       missing static references as proof that dynamic or external consumers do not
       exist.
    6. Use the repository's existing gates rather than adding tests that merely
       assert a directory tree or private call sequence. For tests and fixtures,
       follow [Python testing](../python-testing/SKILL.md). Run focused checks while
       working and `just check` before handoff; report checks that could not run.
    
    ## Results
    
    For an evaluation, report concrete findings with locations, effects and ranked
    recommendations. For a design, show the proposed ownership and dependency
    boundaries, explain meaningful tradeoffs and how they are enforced. For an
    implementation, summarize what moved, whether behavior changed and the evidence
    from verification. Keep the review proportional to the requested change.
    
    For example, if both article cleaning and company linking need the same
    publication-date parser, first inspect its existing owner and date semantics.
    Share it only if both consumers require the same contract; keep separate rules
    when their treatment of missing or ambiguous dates differs.

    # Python testing
    
    ## Workflow
    
    1. Inspect the code contract, nearby tests, `conftest.py`, shared fixtures and
       strategies, the package's test README, and pytest configuration. Reuse an
       existing test or generator when it covers the behavior; extend it only for a
       distinct, meaningful risk. Do not add tests for trivial or reversible changes

    # Agent contract
    
    - Read the nearest README.md for commands and ARCHITECTURE.md for design decisions.
    - Use the pinned devenv environment and repository just commands.
    - Run Python commands through the appropriate locked uv project.
    - Authored records own state. Use explicit creation and synchronization commands; never edit generated Insitu regions by hand.
    - Task parents expose immediate children. Put supporting evidence in separate records and preserve stable paths.
    - Checks validate without repair; use just fmt and just sync for explicit changes.
    - Run just check before handoff and report any checks that could not run.
    - Resolve secrets only for commands that need them. Never place credentials in tracked files.
    """Reproduce the historical Fine News publisher filter."""
    
    import csv
    import json
    import os
    import re
    from pathlib import Path
    from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
    from typing import Annotated
    
    import duckdb
    import typer
    
    SHARD = re.compile(r"(?:^|/)(\d{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2]))/(eng_Latn)/([^/]+\.parquet)$")
    QUERY = """
        COPY (
            SELECT text, id, metadata FROM read_parquet($source)
            WHERE regexp_matches(
                lower(rtrim(trim(coalesce(
                    nullif(trim(metadata.url_hostname), ''),
                    regexp_extract(metadata.url, '(?i)^https?://([^/:?#]+)', 1)
                )), '.')), $domains
            )
        ) TO $target (FORMAT PARQUET, COMPRESSION ZSTD, COMPRESSION_LEVEL 9,
                     ROW_GROUP_SIZE 16384)
    """
    
    
    def domain_pattern(path: Path) -> str:
        """Build a boundary-aware pattern from the historical hostname list."""
        with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            reader = csv.DictReader(stream)
            if reader.fieldnames != ["domain"]:
                raise ValueError("Domain CSV must have one column named domain")
            domains = sorted({row["domain"].strip().lower().rstrip(".") for row in reader})
        if not domains or any(
            not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9-]+(?:\.[a-z0-9-]+)+", domain) for domain in domains
        ):
            raise ValueError("Domain CSV must contain hostnames")
        return r"(^|\.)(" + "|".join(map(re.escape, domains)) + r")$"
    
    
    def filter_shards(
        source: str, domains: Path, output: Path, *, dry_run: bool = False
    ) -> None:
        """Filter English shards without overwriting an existing output."""
        pattern = domain_pattern(domains)
        with duckdb.connect(config={"threads": 2, "memory_limit": "2GiB"}) as con:
            if source.startswith("hf://"):
                con.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs")
            con.execute(
                "SET preserve_insertion_order=false; SET max_temp_directory_size='4GiB'"
            )
            con.execute("SET enable_external_file_cache=false")
            files = con.execute(
                "SELECT file FROM glob(?) ORDER BY file", [source]
            ).fetchall()
            plan = [
                (str(file), output.joinpath(*match.groups()))
                for (file,) in files
                if (match := SHARD.search(str(file)))
            ]
            if not plan:
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"No English Parquet shards match {source}")
            if len({target for _, target in plan}) != len(plan):
                raise ValueError("Multiple source files map to the same output")
            if not dry_run:
                for _, target in plan:
                    if target.exists():
                        raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {target}")
            for file, target in plan:
                if not dry_run:
                    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    with TemporaryDirectory(dir=target.parent) as staging:
                        temporary = Path(staging) / "shard.parquet"
                        con.execute(
                            QUERY,
                            {"source": file, "domains": pattern, "target": str(temporary)},
                        )
                        os.link(temporary, target)
                typer.echo(f"{'Plan' if dry_run else 'Wrote'}: {file} -> {target}")
    
    
    def filter_fine_news(
        config: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="Historical acquisition configuration.")
        ] = Path("config/fine-news/acquisition.json"),
        source: Annotated[
            str | None, typer.Option(help="Override with a local or hf:// glob.")
        ] = None,
        output: Annotated[
            Path | None, typer.Option(help="Override the output directory.")
        ] = None,
        dry_run: Annotated[
            bool, typer.Option(help="List input and output shards without filtering.")
        ] = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Select English publisher shards from a pinned Fine News revision."""
        settings = json.loads(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if settings["language"] != "eng_Latn":
            raise ValueError("Only the historical eng_Latn selection is supported")
        if source is None:
            source = (
                f"hf://datasets/{settings['repository']}@{settings['revision']}"
                f"/data/*/{settings['language']}/*.parquet"
            )
        filter_shards(
            source,
            Path(settings["domains"]),
            output or Path(settings["output"]),
            dry_run=dry_run,
        )
    # Fine News acquisition
    
    `filter_fine_news` documents the historical staging selection from
    [Fine News](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ksolovev/fine-news) at the revision
    in [acquisition.json](acquisition.json). It selects `eng_Latn` capture-month
    shards and the exact 115-hostname [allowlist](domains.csv), including subdomains.
    The hostname comes from `metadata.url_hostname`, falling back to `metadata.url`
    when blank. The output preserves `text`, `id` and `metadata` under
    `data/raw/fine-news/YYYY-MM/eng_Latn/`.
    
    This is the historical source filter, not a reviewed publisher list or a
    research-ready article corpus. Fine News applies its own filters and
    deduplication; capture month is not necessarily publication month. The upstream
    dataset card describes content rights and usage restrictions. No full output has
    been built, verified or cached here, and no DVC lock entry is claimed.
    
    The stage is frozen: `dvc repro` will not execute it, even with `--force`.
    Since the declared output is absent, targeting it currently reports missing data.
    After obtaining or rebuilding and verifying the output, track its actual state
    before relying on it downstream. Unfreezing or invoking the command directly can
    run the acquisition and requires network access and substantial resources.
    DuckDB may download its `httpfs` extension on first remote access.
    
    For a local trial, use `just python::run stages raw filter-fine-news --help`;
    `--source` and `--output` can select a local shard and fresh destination.
    The script refuses to overwrite existing shards. Output order and Parquet bytes
    are not guaranteed to match the existing staging dataset.
    # Pipeline layers: raw -> processed -> research.
    # Each layer will contain independently reproducible DVC sub-stages.
    
    ## Raw: source snapshots
    # Ingest versioned article and company-reference snapshots with source manifests.
    # Preserve source content, metadata and provenance for replay and reconciliation.
    # Proposed location: data/raw/.
    
    ## Processed: reusable tables
    # Clean, standardize and deduplicate articles; resolve dated company identities
    # and enrich article-company relationships. Retain evidence and quality flags.
    # Produce reusable article, company and relationship tables.
    # Proposed location: data/processed/.
    
    ## Research: study datasets
    # Build company-year coverage panels, study cohorts and publication-ready datasets
    # from processed tables. Apply explicit publisher, relevance and K/T coverage policies.
    # Include dataset documentation, provenance and measured quality in each release.
    # Proposed location: data/research/.
    
    ## Validation and evaluation
    # Validate contracts and reconcile counts at every layer. Keep method experiments,
    # independent evaluation labels and quality reports as versioned supporting
    # artifacts; they inform promotion between layers rather than forming a data tier.
    
    stages:
      filter_fine_news:
        desc: Reproduce the historical English financial-publisher selection from Fine News.
        cmd: >-
          env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python
          --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline pipeline stages raw filter-fine-news
        frozen: true
        deps:
          - config/fine-news/acquisition.json
          - config/fine-news/domains.csv
          - src/python/uv.lock
          - devenv.lock
          - infra/nix/devenv.nix
          - .semflow/hashes/entrypoints/pipeline/stages/raw/filter-fine-news.json
        outs:
          - data/raw/fine-news

    """Exercise the historical acquisition against local Parquet files."""
    
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import duckdb
    import pytest
    from pipeline.stages.raw.fine_news import filter_shards
    
    
    @pytest.mark.integration
    def test_filter_preserves_english_publisher_rows(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        # Arrange: create a tiny source shard and a historical-style domain list.
        source = tmp_path / "input/2020-01/eng_Latn/part-000000.parquet"
        source.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        domains = tmp_path / "domains.csv"
        domains.write_text("domain\nexample.com\n", encoding="utf-8")
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            con.execute(
                """COPY (SELECT * FROM (VALUES
                    ('1', 'one', {'url_hostname': 'EXAMPLE.COM.', 'url': 'https://wrong.test/a'}),
                    ('2', 'two', {'url_hostname': 'news.example.com', 'url': 'https://wrong.test/b'}),
                    ('3', 'three', {'url_hostname': '', 'url': 'https://example.com/c'}),
                    ('4', 'four', {'url_hostname': 'notexample.com', 'url': 'https://example.com/d'})
                ) AS rows(id, text, metadata)) TO ? (FORMAT PARQUET)""",
                [str(source)],
            )
    
        # Act: filter the source through the public acquisition operation.
        output = tmp_path / "output"
        filter_shards(str(source), domains, output)
    
        # Assert: only eligible rows and their original fields are preserved.
        target = output / "2020-01/eng_Latn/part-000000.parquet"
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            result = con.execute(
                "SELECT id, text, metadata.url_hostname, metadata.url "
                "FROM read_parquet(?) ORDER BY id",
                [str(target)],
            ).fetchall()
        assert result == [
            ("1", "one", "EXAMPLE.COM.", "https://wrong.test/a"),
            ("2", "two", "news.example.com", "https://wrong.test/b"),
            ("3", "three", "", "https://example.com/c"),
        ]
    {
      "repository": "ksolovev/fine-news",
      "revision": "7a841090e69f3c58a9e04b0c39213d879af68e8a",
      "language": "eng_Latn",
      "domains": "config/fine-news/domains.csv",
      "output": "data/raw/fine-news"
    }

    """Reproduce the historical Fine News publisher filter."""
    
    import json
    import os
    import re
    from pathlib import Path
    from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
    from typing import Annotated
    
    import duckdb
    import typer
    
    SHARD = re.compile(r"(?:^|/)(\d{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2]))/(eng_Latn)/([^/]+\.parquet)$")
    QUERY = """
        COPY (
            WITH articles AS (
                SELECT text, id, metadata, lower(rtrim(trim(coalesce(
                    nullif(trim(metadata.url_hostname), ''),
                    regexp_extract(metadata.url, '(?i)^https?://([^/:?#]+)', 1)
                )), '.')) AS hostname
                FROM read_parquet($source)
            )
            SELECT text, id, metadata FROM articles
            WHERE EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM read_csv($domains, header=true) AS d
                WHERE hostname = lower(rtrim(trim(d.domain), '.'))
                   OR ends_with(hostname, '.' || lower(rtrim(trim(d.domain), '.')))
            )
        ) TO $target (FORMAT PARQUET, COMPRESSION ZSTD, COMPRESSION_LEVEL 9,
                     ROW_GROUP_SIZE 16384)
    """
    
    
    def filter_shards(
        source: str, domains: Path, output: Path, *, dry_run: bool = False
    ) -> None:
        """Filter English shards without overwriting an existing output."""
        with duckdb.connect(config={"threads": 2, "memory_limit": "2GiB"}) as con:
            if source.startswith("hf://"):
                con.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs")
            con.execute(
                "SET preserve_insertion_order=false; SET max_temp_directory_size='4GiB'"
            )
            con.execute("SET enable_external_file_cache=false")
            files = con.execute(
                "SELECT file FROM glob(?) ORDER BY file", [source]
            ).fetchall()
            plan = [
                (str(file), output.joinpath(*match.groups()))
                for (file,) in files
                if (match := SHARD.search(str(file)))
            ]
            if not plan:
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"No English Parquet shards match {source}")
            if len({target for _, target in plan}) != len(plan):
                raise ValueError("Multiple source files map to the same output")
            if not dry_run:
                for _, target in plan:
                    if target.exists():
                        raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {target}")
            for file, target in plan:
                if not dry_run:
                    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    with TemporaryDirectory(dir=target.parent) as staging:
                        temporary = Path(staging) / "shard.parquet"
                        con.execute(
                            QUERY,
                            {
                                "source": file,
                                "domains": str(domains),
                                "target": str(temporary),
                            },
                        )
                        os.link(temporary, target)
                typer.echo(f"{'Plan' if dry_run else 'Wrote'}: {file} -> {target}")
    
    
    def filter_fine_news(
        config: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="Historical acquisition configuration.")
        ] = Path("data/inputs/fine-news/acquisition.json"),
        source: Annotated[
            str | None, typer.Option(help="Override with a local or hf:// glob.")
        ] = None,
        output: Annotated[
            Path | None, typer.Option(help="Override the output directory.")
        ] = None,
        dry_run: Annotated[
            bool, typer.Option(help="List input and output shards without filtering.")
        ] = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Select English publisher shards from a pinned Fine News revision."""
        settings = json.loads(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if settings["language"] != "eng_Latn":
            raise ValueError("Only the historical eng_Latn selection is supported")
        if source is None:
            source = (
                f"hf://datasets/{settings['repository']}@{settings['revision']}"
                f"/data/*/{settings['language']}/*.parquet"
            )
        filter_shards(
            source,
            Path(settings["domains"]),
            output or Path(settings["output"]),
            dry_run=dry_run,
        )
    # Fine News acquisition
    
    `filter_fine_news` documents the historical staging selection from
    [Fine News](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ksolovev/fine-news) at the revision
    in [acquisition.json](acquisition.json). It selects `eng_Latn` capture-month
    shards and the exact 115-hostname [allowlist](domains.csv), including subdomains.
    The hostname comes from `metadata.url_hostname`, falling back to `metadata.url`
    when blank. The output preserves `text`, `id` and `metadata` under
    `data/raw/fine-news/YYYY-MM/eng_Latn/`.
    
    This is the historical source filter, not a reviewed publisher list or a
    research-ready article corpus. Fine News applies its own filters and
    deduplication; capture month is not necessarily publication month. The upstream
    dataset card describes content rights and usage restrictions. No full output has
    been built, verified or cached here, and no DVC lock entry is claimed.
    
    The stage is frozen: `dvc repro` will not execute it, even with `--force`.
    Since the declared output is absent, targeting it currently reports missing data.
    After obtaining or rebuilding and verifying the output, track its actual state
    before relying on it downstream. Unfreezing or invoking the command directly can
    run the acquisition and requires network access and substantial resources.
    DuckDB may download its `httpfs` extension on first remote access.
    
    For a local trial, use `just python::run stages raw filter-fine-news --help`;
    `--source` and `--output` can select a local shard and fresh destination.
    The script refuses to overwrite existing shards. Output order and Parquet bytes
    are not guaranteed to match the existing staging dataset.

## Assistant

Yes. DuckDB can read the pinned `hf://` glob directly and run the publisher filter in a single `COPY` query. The Python code could simply load the configuration and execute that query; it does not need to list and process every shard itself. DuckDB documents both [Hugging Face globs](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/core_extensions/httpfs/hugging_face) and [`COPY` to Parquet](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/sql/statements/copy).

The trade-off is the **output layout**. The current loop preserves each input shard’s month, language and filename. A single `COPY` to one Parquet file would preserve the selected records, but not those individual shard paths. DuckDB can also write partitioned output, although its generated paths and filenames would differ from the historical staging layout. [DuckDB partitioned writes](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/data/partitioning/partitioned_writes)

For this frozen documentation stage, I’d favor **one query and one output dataset**, with the input revision and capture metadata retained. We should describe it as reproducing the *selection*, not the exact historical files. The full output would still need to be verified before claiming equivalence.

    """Reproduce the historical Fine News publisher filter."""
    
    import json
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
    from typing import Annotated
    
    import duckdb
    import typer
    
    QUERY = """
        COPY (
            WITH articles AS (
                SELECT text, id, metadata, lower(rtrim(trim(coalesce(
                    nullif(trim(metadata.url_hostname), ''),
                    regexp_extract(metadata.url, '(?i)^https?://([^/:?#]+)', 1)
                )), '.')) AS hostname
                FROM read_parquet($source)
            )
            SELECT text, id, metadata FROM articles
            WHERE EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM read_csv($domains, header=true) AS d
                WHERE hostname = lower(rtrim(trim(d.domain), '.'))
                   OR ends_with(hostname, '.' || lower(rtrim(trim(d.domain), '.')))
            )
        ) TO $target (FORMAT PARQUET, COMPRESSION ZSTD, COMPRESSION_LEVEL 9,
                     ROW_GROUP_SIZE 16384)
    """
    
    
    def filter_shards(
        source: str, domains: Path, output: Path, *, dry_run: bool = False
    ) -> None:
        """Filter a Parquet glob without overwriting the output."""
        target = output / "articles.parquet"
        if dry_run:
            typer.echo(f"Plan: {source} -> {target}")
            return
        if target.exists():
            raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {target}")
        output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with duckdb.connect(config={"threads": 2, "memory_limit": "2GiB"}) as con:
            if source.startswith("hf://"):
                con.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs")
            con.execute(
                "SET preserve_insertion_order=false; SET max_temp_directory_size='4GiB'"
            )
            con.execute("SET enable_external_file_cache=false")
            with TemporaryDirectory(dir=output) as staging:
                temporary = Path(staging) / "articles.parquet"
                con.execute(
                    QUERY,
                    {"source": source, "domains": str(domains), "target": str(temporary)},
                )
                os.link(temporary, target)
        typer.echo(f"Wrote: {source} -> {target}")
    
    
    def filter_fine_news(
        config: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="Historical acquisition configuration.")
        ] = Path("data/inputs/fine-news/acquisition.json"),
        source: Annotated[
            str | None, typer.Option(help="Override with a local or hf:// glob.")
        ] = None,
        output: Annotated[
            Path | None, typer.Option(help="Override the output directory.")
        ] = None,
        dry_run: Annotated[
            bool, typer.Option(help="Show the source glob and output without filtering.")
        ] = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Select English publisher shards from a pinned Fine News revision."""
        settings = json.loads(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if settings["language"] != "eng_Latn":
            raise ValueError("Only the historical eng_Latn selection is supported")
        if source is None:
            source = (
                f"hf://datasets/{settings['repository']}@{settings['revision']}"
                f"/data/*/{settings['language']}/*.parquet"
            )
        filter_shards(
            source,
            Path(settings["domains"]),
            output or Path(settings["output"]),
            dry_run=dry_run,
        )
    {
      "repository": "ksolovev/fine-news",
      "revision": "7a841090e69f3c58a9e04b0c39213d879af68e8a",
      "language": "eng_Latn",
      "domains": "data/inputs/fine-news/domains.csv",
      "output": "data/raw/fine-news"
    }
    # Fine News acquisition
    
    `filter_fine_news` documents the historical staging selection from
    [Fine News](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ksolovev/fine-news) at the revision
    in [acquisition.json](acquisition.json). It selects `eng_Latn` capture-month
    shards and the exact 115-hostname [allowlist](domains.csv), including subdomains.
    The hostname comes from `metadata.url_hostname`, falling back to `metadata.url`
    when blank. One query reads the input glob and writes `text`, `id` and `metadata`
    to `data/raw/fine-news/articles.parquet`.
    
    This is the historical source filter, not a reviewed publisher list or a
    research-ready article corpus. Fine News applies its own filters and
    deduplication; capture month is not necessarily publication month. The upstream
    dataset card describes content rights and usage restrictions. No full output has
    been built, verified or cached here, and no DVC lock entry is claimed.
    
    The stage is frozen: `dvc repro` will not execute it, even with `--force`.
    Since the declared output is absent, targeting it currently reports missing data.
    After obtaining or rebuilding and verifying the output, track its actual state
    before relying on it downstream. Unfreezing or invoking the command directly can
    run the acquisition and requires network access and substantial resources.
    DuckDB may download its `httpfs` extension on first remote access.
    
    For a local trial, use `just python::run stages raw filter-fine-news --help`;
    `--source` and `--output` can select a local glob and fresh destination. `--dry-run`
    prints those paths without checking or reading the source. The script refuses to
    overwrite an existing output. Output layout, order and Parquet bytes differ from
    the staging shards; selected rows have not been compared with that dataset.
    # Pipeline layers: raw -> processed -> research.
    # Each layer will contain independently reproducible DVC sub-stages.
    
    ## Raw: source snapshots
    # Ingest versioned article and company-reference snapshots with source manifests.
    # Preserve source content, metadata and provenance for replay and reconciliation.
    # Proposed location: data/raw/.
    
    ## Processed: reusable tables
    # Clean, standardize and deduplicate articles; resolve dated company identities
    # and enrich article-company relationships. Retain evidence and quality flags.
    # Produce reusable article, company and relationship tables.
    # Proposed location: data/processed/.
    
    ## Research: study datasets
    # Build company-year coverage panels, study cohorts and publication-ready datasets
    # from processed tables. Apply explicit publisher, relevance and K/T coverage policies.
    # Include dataset documentation, provenance and measured quality in each release.
    # Proposed location: data/research/.
    
    ## Validation and evaluation
    # Validate contracts and reconcile counts at every layer. Keep method experiments,
    # independent evaluation labels and quality reports as versioned supporting
    # artifacts; they inform promotion between layers rather than forming a data tier.
    
    stages:
      filter_fine_news:
        desc: Reproduce the historical English financial-publisher selection from Fine News.
        cmd: >-
          env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python
          --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline pipeline stages raw filter-fine-news
        frozen: true
        deps:
          - data/inputs/fine-news/acquisition.json
          - data/inputs/fine-news/domains.csv
          - src/python/uv.lock
          - devenv.lock
          - infra/nix/devenv.nix
          - .semflow/hashes/entrypoints/pipeline/stages/raw/filter-fine-news.json
        outs:
          - data/raw/fine-news

## Assistant

The largest remaining simplification is to make `fine_news.py` a **thin adapter around the query**. It currently combines configuration loading, CLI options, execution settings, output safety and progress reporting.

I’d simplify it in this order:

1. **Use a single function for the CLI and execution.** `filter_shards` currently has only one production caller; the test can exercise the CLI command.
2. **Store the complete pinned source glob in the configuration.** That removes the language check and URL assembly while keeping the exact source visible and versioned.
3. **Remove `--dry-run`.** It only prints paths and does not validate the source. The configuration already shows what will run.
4. **Reconsider the DuckDB settings.** The thread, memory, spill and cache settings came from the historical environment. Unless we need them to reproduce a documented constraint, DuckDB defaults would make the recipe simpler. Changing them could affect performance and output bytes, which we have already agreed are not a fidelity requirement.

I’d retain the parameterized SQL, `httpfs` loading, and the temporary output plus no-overwrite check. Those protect the intended filter and prevent a failed or concurrent run from leaving a misleading output.

The resulting shape would be roughly:

```python
def filter_fine_news(config: Path = DEFAULT_CONFIG) -> None:
    settings = json.loads(config.read_text())
    target = Path(settings["output"])

    with duckdb.connect() as connection:
        connection.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs")
        # Execute QUERY with the configured source and domains,
        # then publish the completed temporary file.
```

For local tests, the command can accept a different **configuration file** pointing to local Parquet and a temporary destination; separate `--source` and `--output` overrides would no longer be necessary. The SQL itself is already doing the substantive work, so moving it to another file would improve separation but would not meaningfully reduce the total code.

## Assistant

Yes—**Pydantic would be useful for validating the acquisition configuration**, especially as the pipeline grows. For this stage, though, I’d start with a Pydantic `BaseModel` rather than `BaseSettings`.

The distinction is relevant to reproducibility: the acquisition JSON is a declared DVC dependency, while Pydantic Settings normally also reads environment variables and other sources. An environment override could change the selected source or output without changing the file DVC tracks. Pydantic Settings lets us customize those sources, but that adds machinery we don’t need yet. [Pydantic Settings: value priority](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/pydantic_settings/#field-value-priority)

A small model would give us typed paths, clear validation errors and rejection of unexpected fields:

```python
from pathlib import Path

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class FineNewsConfig(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    source: str
    domains: Path
    output: Path


settings = FineNewsConfig.model_validate_json(
    config_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
)
```

The versioned JSON could then hold the complete pinned `hf://` glob. That removes the current manual dictionary access, language check and URL assembly. It adds a Pydantic dependency and a model, so it may not reduce the line count immediately, but it gives the configuration an explicit contract.

I’d introduce **Pydantic Settings** when we have genuine runtime settings—such as resource limits, credentials or service endpoints—and keep those separate from the versioned inputs that determine a research dataset. Any override that changes dataset contents should be recorded in the run configuration and made visible to DVC.

    def test_filter_preserves_english_publisher_rows(tmp_path: Path) -> None:

        with duckdb.connect() as con:

                """COPY (SELECT * FROM (VALUES

    """Reproduce the historical Fine News publisher filter."""
    
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
    from typing import Annotated
    
    import duckdb
    import typer
    from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
    
    QUERY = """
        COPY (
            WITH articles AS (
                SELECT text, id, metadata, lower(rtrim(trim(coalesce(
                    nullif(trim(metadata.url_hostname), ''),
                    regexp_extract(metadata.url, '(?i)^https?://([^/:?#]+)', 1)
                )), '.')) AS hostname
                FROM read_parquet($source)
            )
            SELECT text, id, metadata FROM articles
            WHERE EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM read_csv($domains, header=true) AS d
                WHERE hostname = lower(rtrim(trim(d.domain), '.'))
                   OR ends_with(hostname, '.' || lower(rtrim(trim(d.domain), '.')))
            )
        ) TO $target (FORMAT PARQUET, COMPRESSION ZSTD, COMPRESSION_LEVEL 9,
                     ROW_GROUP_SIZE 16384)
    """
    
    
    class FineNewsConfig(BaseModel):
        """Versioned inputs and output for the Fine News selection."""
    
        model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    
        source: str
        domains: Path
        output: Path
    
    
    def filter_fine_news(
        config: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="Historical acquisition configuration.")
        ] = Path("data/inputs/fine-news/acquisition.json"),
    ) -> None:
        """Select English publisher shards from a pinned Fine News revision."""
        settings = FineNewsConfig.model_validate_json(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        target = settings.output / "articles.parquet"
        if target.exists():
            raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {target}")
        settings.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            if settings.source.startswith("hf://"):
                con.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs")
            with TemporaryDirectory(dir=settings.output) as staging:
                temporary = Path(staging) / "articles.parquet"
                con.execute(
                    QUERY,
                    {
                        "source": settings.source,
                        "domains": str(settings.domains),
                        "target": str(temporary),
                    },
                )
                os.link(temporary, target)
        typer.echo(f"Wrote: {settings.source} -> {target}")

    # Candidate datasets
    
    These notebooks revisit the saved exploration dated 2026-10-29. Each reads a
    small, local evidence snapshot and discusses the acquisition decision it can
    support. Historical article-level extraction has not been rerun.
    
    | Candidate | Sample input rows | Qualifying articles | Frozen-universe articles | Cohort / input | Companies |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | [Fine News](fine_news/README.md) | 523,950 | 4,453 | 495 | 0.0945% | 92 |
    | [Infini News](infini_news/README.md) | 317,283 | 1,430 | 127 | 0.0400% | 60 |
    | [DCLM](dclm/README.md) | 98,889 | 86 | 22 | 0.0222% | 23 |
    | [RefinedWeb](refinedweb/README.md) | 174,919 | 99 | 13 | 0.0074% | 10 |
    | [FineWeb-HQ](fineweb_hq/README.md) | 367,000 | 154 | 19 | 0.0052% | 16 |
    
    ## Shared definitions
    
    Qualifying articles require a URL, explicit ticker notation, a publication date
    and a nonempty body, using the same 93-publisher / 115-domain registry. The
    cohort is pricing-perspective's frozen 100-company research universe, not current
    Nasdaq-100 membership. URLs are deduplicated within each source; articles may
    mention several companies and are counted once. Cross-source overlap is unknown.
    
    Press releases remain included in the baseline. The notebook switch excludes
    labelled releases; investment analysis remains in the nonrelease category.
    Publication time, author and title are optional. Crawl dates are never used as
    publication-date fallbacks. Classification and extraction remain heuristic.
    
    ## Interpretation
    
    Fine News and Infini News merit the next pilots, based on observed yield and
    metadata availability. Their samples have different time coverage and selection
    mechanisms, so the table cannot establish a population ranking or an annual
    all-company floor. Yields are unweighted, with all raw sample rows as denominator;
    publication-year yields are contributions to total yield, not annual retention.
    
    Fine News's separate December pilot uses a publisher-prefiltered denominator:
    1,832 cohort articles / 72,813 rows. It is discussed separately in that notebook.
    The later 14,807,287-row local collection and reported metadata-only matches are
    also distinct from date/body-qualified pilot counts. Acquisition completeness
    against the upstream inventory remains unverified.
    
    Historical population extrapolations are omitted. The earlier 599,979 Fine News
    scenario mixed English yield with a multilingual population; the corrected
    207,082 remains biased by the August 2020 capture stratum. Neither is a forecast.
    
    ## Reproduction and evidence
    
    Follow the [notebook commands](../README.md). Every candidate keeps a standalone
    `notebook.py`, sidecar uv lock, findings README and `evidence/` directory. Evidence
    contains selected aggregate rows, original method notes, source references and
    SHA256 provenance. No runtime dependency on `.tmp/` or the other repository exists.
    
    Exact historical input identity is not established for several remote sources;
    DCLM's original shard directory is uncertain. The current December Fine News
    file has the recorded pilot row count but a different SHA256. A new extraction
    must be labelled as a new run until source equivalence is demonstrated.
    
    The archive's aggregate validator passes. Migration validation reconciles source,
    year and publisher totals and checks retained evidence hashes. Notebook execution
    reproduces displays from aggregates; it does not validate the original parser's
    precision or recall. FineWeb-HQ discusses the separate cosine experiment's
    limitations; the unrun MLP draft and bulk extraction scripts are not migrated.
    # DCLM
    
    Can a broad web corpus supply usable financial articles despite sparse metadata?
    
    The historical sample contains **98,889 input rows**, yielding
    **86 qualifying articles** and **22
    frozen-universe articles** (0.0222% of input rows), covering
    23 companies. Excluding labelled releases leaves
    22 cohort articles. These are descriptive,
    unweighted sample counts, not population estimates.
    
    ## Findings and next step
    
    The input is **one compressed JSONL shard**, not Parquet. `WARC-Date` is
    crawl time. Publication dates must come from retained headers/datelines or URLs:
    84 of the 86 qualifying articles use URL dates and two use text headers.
    
    The 22 frozen-universe matches cover 23 companies because one article can mention
    multiple companies. Their seven observed publication years lie between 2007 and
    2016; they do not directly establish coverage of the 2018–2022 study window.
    
    Keep DCLM as a candidate requiring stronger provenance and date validation.
    The original global/local shard directory was not recorded; the manifest names
    a candidate path whose exact historical bytes remain unverified.
    
    All 86 qualifying articles are labelled nonrelease, including 73 analysis pieces.
    That describes this sample and heuristic classifier; it does not demonstrate
    that releases are absent from DCLM. Verify the source checksum and audit inferred
    publication dates before expanding the sample or projecting acquisition volume.

    # Infini News
    
    Does a multi-file news corpus offer useful company coverage with structured metadata?
    
    The historical sample contains **317,283 input rows**, yielding
    **1,430 qualifying articles** and **127
    frozen-universe articles** (0.0400% of input rows), covering
    60 companies. Excluding labelled releases leaves
    114 cohort articles. These are descriptive,
    unweighted sample counts, not population estimates.
    
    ## Findings and next step
    
    This is a **ten-file sample** with dedicated publication date, title, author,
    tags and text fields. All 1,430 qualifying articles obtained their dates from
    metadata. The 127 frozen-universe matches cover 60 companies.
    
    Having ten files does not establish representative sampling: inclusion
    probabilities and population-stratum definitions were not supplied. Interpret
    file and year breakdowns as descriptions of these observed records.
    
    Infini News merits a second pilot alongside Fine News. Its structured fields
    reduce dependence on text heuristics, while its observed cohort yield is lower.
    The samples differ in temporal composition, so this is not a population ranking.
    
    The extraction already corrected a case-insensitive exchange pattern that read
    `NYSE: You` as a symbol. Preserve that counterexample when consolidating parsers.
    Next audit publication-year coverage, US identifier precision and cross-source
    URL/content overlap before claiming incremental company coverage.

    # RefinedWeb
    
    How much usable financial news survives conservative extraction from general web text?
    
    The historical sample contains **174,919 input rows**, yielding
    **99 qualifying articles** and **13
    frozen-universe articles** (0.0074% of input rows), covering
    10 companies. Excluding labelled releases leaves
    11 cohort articles. These are descriptive,
    unweighted sample counts, not population estimates.
    
    ## Findings and next step
    
    This is **one general-web Parquet shard** with content, URLs and crawl
    metadata, but no structured publication dates or security identifiers. Dates
    come from URLs (74 articles), release datelines (17), release headers (7) and a
    text header (1). URL dates are evidence, not independently verified metadata.
    
    Only 13 frozen-universe articles match, covering ten companies. Of all 99
    qualifying articles, 34 are labelled press releases. The toggle below exposes
    how release inclusion changes the observed result.
    
    RefinedWeb is a useful baseline for extraction difficulty. Its observed
    cohort yield is small, but one shard cannot establish population-wide absence
    or make a definitive case against the corpus.
    
    Prioritize date-source precision, body completeness and ticker precision over
    more elaborate ranking. Navigation, truncation and comments can survive in
    retained text. Restore and verify the original shard before treating a new
    remote extraction as an exact reproduction of these historical counts.
