    # FineWeb-HQ
    
    Do cleaned web text and stored embeddings make this an efficient financial-news source?
    
    The historical sample contains **367,000 input rows**, yielding
    **154 qualifying articles** and **19
    frozen-universe articles** (0.0052% of input rows), covering
    16 companies. Excluding labelled releases leaves
    18 cohort articles. These are descriptive,
    unweighted sample counts, not population estimates.
    
    ## Findings and next step
    
    This is **one Parquet shard from the August 2017 crawl**. The `date` field
    is capture time, not publication time. Of 154 qualifying articles, 115 use URL
    dates, 38 use release datelines and one uses a text header. Embeddings were
    excluded from article extraction.
    
    The 19 frozen-universe articles cover 16 companies. Metadata sparsity and the
    chosen time slice constrain interpretation of that low observed yield.
    
    Treat the retained outlet-discovery experiment as a diagnostic, not evidence
    for accepting new financial publishers. Sports and general news lead its cosine
    ranking; in a convenience sample of 64 vectors, median pairwise cosine was
    0.9981 and two dimensions held 98.35% of mean unit-vector energy.
    
    The seed registry labels publisher membership, not each article's financial
    topic. Topic-labelled evaluation and embedding diagnostics are needed before
    ranking new sources. The MLP remains an unrun draft. Neither approach establishes
    additional date/ticker-qualified yield or publisher trustworthiness.

    METHOD: RefinedWeb financial-news extraction handoff
    Updated: 2026-10-29
    Project directory: /home/marcussky/Downloads/sample_data/tiiuae_falcon-refinedweb
    Dataset: tiiuae/falcon-refinedweb, one local shard
    Source file: train-00028-of-05534-09ffe38fe3bb6c59.parquet
    
    User objective and final requirements
    Extract publisher-specific financial article candidates using DuckDB SQL. Produce
    query/{publisher}.sql and filtered/{publisher}.jsonl, report per-publisher and
    aggregate qualifying counts, and compute yield against every row in the shard.
    Include major global publishers, geographic/regional and sector publications,
    and historical/legacy domains. Publication date is required; publication time is
    optional (a user correction superseded the original datetime requirement).
    
    Fields
    url; author (optional string/null); ticker_identifiers (required nonempty List[str]);
    publication_date (required YYYY/MM/DD); publication_time (optional HH:MM:SS/null);
    title (optional string/null); article_body (required nonempty string).
    Provenance fields: publication_date_source, publication_date_precision, content_type.
    
    Dataset findings
    174919 rows. Original columns: content, url, timestamp, dump, segment,
    image_urls. No structured security identifiers or publication dates. timestamp is
    crawl time and is never used as a publication-date fallback. Financial identifiers
    must be recovered from explicit notation in text/URLs; date signals are retained
    publication headers, wire-release datelines, or explicit dates in article URLs.
    Source text can include truncation, navigation, reader comments and press releases.
    Dates inferred from URLs are not independently verified publisher metadata.
    
    Current results
    93 source groups with one SQL/JSONL pair each.
    1516 raw domain-matching pages; 99 qualifying URL records.
    65 non-release articles/analyses, including 31 labeled analysis.
    34 press releases; 7 retained publication times.
    Total yield: 0.0565976252% of the entire shard.
    Non-release yield: 0.0371600569%.
    Regional: 29 groups, 310 raw pages, 0 passing records.
    Sector: 34 groups, 143 raw pages, 0 passing records.
    Legacy: 6 groups, 68 raw pages, 1 passing record.
    Empty exports are intentional; they indicate no match under these extraction rules.
    Counts are per URL, not content-deduplicated across syndicated publishers. This
    single shard does not establish a representative yield for all RefinedWeb.
    
    Press-release status: labeled, NOT excluded
    All records from PR Newswire, Business Wire and GlobeNewswire are labeled
    press_release. Most queries also recognize case-insensitive GLOBE NEWSWIRE,
    BUSINESS WIRE and PRNewswire markers in content. The original seven queries use a
    narrower combination of URL and text signals. This is heuristic and can miss
    stripped attributions or flag incidental wire-service mentions.
    The user asked how exclusion works; they have NOT requested filtering releases
    out of the exports yet. To exclude them, add the following to each final WHERE:
      AND content_type <> 'press_release'
    Or read only the JSONL exports:
      SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('filtered/*.jsonl', format='newline_delimited')
      WHERE content_type <> 'press_release';
    Do not match filtered/counts.json as an article export.
    
    Reproduce from the project directory
      bash query/run_all.sh
    Single publisher:
      duckdb -bail < query/reuters.sql
    Validate exports and refresh reports:
      python query/validate_and_report.py
    The Python module duckdb is not installed; scripts use the available DuckDB CLI.
    
    Files to read first
    query/publishers.json: authoritative publisher-to-domain registry.
    query/publisher_categories.json: exclusive category assignment for additive totals.
    query/publisher_inventory.txt: readable source and artifact inventory.
    query/extraction_notes.txt: methods, extraction limitations and complete counts.
    filtered/counts.json: per-publisher funnel counts and aggregate/category yield.
    file_integrity.json: SHA-256 hashes confirming dataset/exports survived the move.

    Fine News versus the current 100-equity Nasdaq study
    ==================================================
    Result: Fine News has a promising observed per-document yield, but this shard
    cannot establish a higher all-ticker floor or additional qualifying years.
    
    Volume arithmetic (conditional, unweighted projection)
    ------------------------------------------------------
    Fine News: 635,068,343 * 495/523,950 = 599,979 projected cohort documents.
    DCLM: 3,017,780,768 * 22/98,889 = 671,371 projected cohort documents.
    Fine News is 21.04% of DCLM's document count and 89.37% of its projected cohort
    volume. That makes it attractive as the next pilot under the existing yield
    assumption. These remain mechanical extrapolations, not established population
    counts, minimum-per-ticker estimates, or incremental documents versus Nasdaq.
    
    Measured size of the current study, same exact 100-symbol roster
    --------------------------------------------------------------
    Layer                                   Articles/rows    Smallest ticker
    Normalized full archive                     214,480                  449
    Full archive, body >=200 chars               199,223                  445
    2018--2022, body >=200 chars                  124,917                  328
    Realized deterministic source subsamples      43,720                  328
    Canonical Qwen3-8B embedding panel             12,800                  128
    
    The deterministic source sample reaches its configured cap of 445 for 89 of
    100 tickers. The canonical embedding panel is deliberately capped at 128 per
    firm. Thus the 12,800 embeddings are a research design choice, not the size
    of the available archive. See study_artifacts.csv.
    
    The ~599,979 Fine News extrapolation would be 2.80x the full 214,480-row
    normalized archive, or 4.80x the 124,917 eligible study-window records, IF its
    sampling assumptions held and its time range aligned. The time-range condition
    is not established, so neither ratio proves improved usable annual coverage.
    
    The important sample limitation
    -------------------------------
    All 523,950 input records come from the August 2020 capture-month stratum.
    509,106 (97.17%) have an August 2020 publication-month value. All 495 cohort
    matches were published between 2020-04-30 and 2020-08-31; all meet the 200-char
    body rule. They cover 92 of the 100 equities, with 629 distinct article/ticker
    associations. Eight have no matched sample article:
    ASML, CHKP, CTSH, HAS, JBHT, KLAC, PAYX, STX.
    
    Fine News's sample-only minimum over the 100 tickers is zero, its median is
    four matched article/ticker associations, and its maximum is 47 (GOOG). Those
    are sample observations, NOT full-corpus forecasts. Zero sample observations
    do not prove the companies are absent from the full corpus. One positive sample
    record would be multiplied by ~1212 in the mechanical population scenario;
    that multiplication cannot repair the absence of evidence for a ticker-year.
    
    The DCLM cohort sample has only 22 documents, 32 associations and 23 covered
    companies; its seven observed publication years lie between 2007 and 2016.
    It likewise provides no direct evidence about the 2018--2022 annual panel.
    The two source shards' different time strata also limit the cross-source
    ranking inferred from their observed yields.
    
    Annual floor and an existing-data improvement
    ---------------------------------------------
    params.yaml declares annual_raw_article_floor: 47, for each firm in each year
    2018--2022. The repo documents this as a pre-global-ID-deduplication admission
    rule. The balanced 128-row embedding panel is a separate pooled sample cap.
    
    Year    Current normalized minimum   Tickers >=47    Raw-membership minimum
    2018                           33          98/100                        48
    2019                           36          98/100                        47
    2020                           39          96/100                        48
    2021                           57         100/100                        59
    2022                           80         100/100                        81
    
    The normalized archive's 2018--2022 global ticker-year minimum is 33, with 95
    firms meeting >=47 in all five years. All 100 meet >=47 simultaneously in two
    years. Five firms fall below 47 in at least one normalized year:
    SNPS, ASML, KLAC, ZS, IDXX.
    
    The existing immutable raw archive supports a >=47 floor across all 100 firms
    in all five years if deduplication preserves (article ID, scrape symbol)
    memberships rather than discarding all but one assigned symbol per article ID.
    This sensitivity follows the repository's preflight method, recomputed for
    the current 100-firm roster rather than using its older 53-firm report.
    It provides 145,199 eligible article/ticker associations on 136,019 distinct
    articles in 2018--2022. This does not require downloading a new corpus. It is
    an analysis of an alternative normalization, not a change to the study.
    
    At annual floors 64, 100 and 128, respectively, the number of years in which
    ALL 100 firms qualify is 1, 0 and 0 in both current and membership-preserving
    Nasdaq counts. Fine News's inspected shard demonstrates no all-100 year at
    47; the full Fine News corpus's achievable annual floor remains unknown.
    
    Counting and projection limits
    ------------------------------
    * Fine News/DCLM use the same 93-publisher registry as previous reports.
      Nasdaq baseline counts use all publishers in the current governed study.
    * Current normalized Nasdaq records have one assigned symbol each. The
      membership-preserving sensitivity and new-source records can match multiple
      symbols. Per-ticker totals are article/ticker associations; document totals
      count distinct IDs (Nasdaq) or URLs (new sources).
    * New-source ticker matches use the previously defined explicit-identifier
      rules; Nasdaq symbols are API query memberships. Their tagging recall differs.
    * Press releases remain included in the headline Fine News count (8 of 495).
      The nonrelease total projection is 590,282. Nasdaq is not newly classified
      into press-release/editorial categories by this analysis.
    * sampling_weight is not applied, matching the previous headline projections.
      Inclusion probabilities are not established. No population confidence
      interval, unseen-company forecast, or annual extrapolation is justified here.
    * Article overlap with the existing Nasdaq archive is not yet deduplicated;
      599,979 is not an estimate of net-new unique articles.
    * Year-grid zeros outside a source's observed years mean no observations in
      this sample. source_year_observed=false explicitly flags them; they must
      not be read as demonstrated population absences.
    
    Decision supported by these data
    -------------------------------
    Fine News is the stronger next pilot for acquisition efficiency and observed
    cohort breadth. Before a full-corpus commitment, obtain publication-year and
    capture-month stratified evidence across 2018--2022 and desired additional
    years, preserve article/ticker memberships, and evaluate the all-100 yearly
    minimum at 47/64/100/128. The current one-month shard cannot answer whether
    Fine News produces a higher floor or a longer balanced panel.

```
You can combine Hugging Face (hf://) remote querying, Hive partition pruning, and row sampling in DuckDB to inspect or extract subsets of massive remote datasets without downloading the entire repository. [1] (https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/data/partitioning/hive_partitioning), [2] (https://duckdb.org/docs/1.5/sql/query_syntax/samples), [3] (https://duckdb.org/2026/09/25/hugging-face)

1. Partition Filtering on Hugging Face

DuckDB automatically detects Hive-style directory structures (key=value) when scanning remote Parquet files over hf://. Putting a WHERE clause on those partition keys prunes irrelevant remote files before reading them. [1] (https://motherduck.com/glossary/partition-pruning/), [2] (https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/datasets-duckdb), [3] (https://duckdb.org/docs/1.4/data/partitioning/hive_partitioning), [4] (https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/data/partitioning/hive_partitioning)
sql
-- Only downloads metadata/data for the matching partition directory
SELECT *
FROM read_parquet('hf://datasets/username/dataset_name/*/*/*.parquet', hive_partitioning = true)
WHERE year = 2025 AND split = 'train';
Use code with caution.
• Auto-converted Parquet: If a dataset was uploaded as CSV or JSONL, append @~parquet to the repo name (e.g., hf://datasets/user/repo@~parquet/**/*.parquet) to query Hugging Face's auto-generated Parquet branch for faster pushdown. [1] (https://duckdb.org/2026/09/25/hugging-face), [2] (https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/datasets-duckdb)
• Explicit path globbing: If the repository uses custom folders instead of key=value names (such as data/en/train-00000.parquet), filter directly in the hf:// glob path (e.g., hf://datasets/user/repo/data/en/*.parquet) to avoid listing unnecessary directories. [1] (https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/jobs-large-datasets), [2] (https://duckdb.org/2026/09/25/hugging-face)

2. Sampling Filtered Partitions

Once partition filters narrow down the remote files, apply USING SAMPLE (or TABLESAMPLE) to pull a random subset without scanning every row in those partitions. [1] (https://duckdb.org/docs/1.5/sql/query_syntax/samples)
sql
-- Filter to a specific partition, then take a fast random sample
SELECT *
FROM read_parquet('hf://datasets/username/dataset_name/**/*.parquet', hive_partitioning = true)
WHERE language = 'en'
USING SAMPLE 1000 ROWS (reservoir);
Use code with caution.
Choose the sampling method based on your speed and accuracy needs: [1] (https://duckdb.org/docs/1.5/sql/query_syntax/samples)
• System sampling (USING SAMPLE 5% (system)): Samples at the row-group/vector block level. It is the fastest method over HTTP because DuckDB skips entire chunks of remote Parquet files. [1] (https://duckdb.org/docs/1.5/sql/query_syntax/samples)
• Bernoulli sampling (USING SAMPLE 5% (bernoulli)): Evaluates each row independently after reading. It gives a more uniform random distribution than system sampling, though exact row counts will vary slightly. [1] (https://duckdb.org/docs/1.5/sql/query_syntax/samples)
• Reservoir sampling (USING SAMPLE 500 ROWS (reservoir, 42)): Returns an exact number of rows and supports a random seed (42) for reproducibility, though it requires materializing the sample in memory. [1] (https://duckdb.org/docs/1.5/sql/query_syntax/samples)

3. Saving the Sampled Subset

To avoid re-querying Hugging Face over the network during downstream work, wrap the filtered sample in a CREATE TABLE or COPY statement: [1] (https://duckdb.org/2026/09/25/hugging-face), [2] (https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/jobs-large-datasets)
sql
COPY (
    SELECT text, label
    FROM read_parquet('hf://datasets/username/dataset_name/**/*.parquet', hive_partitioning = true)
    WHERE split = 'train'
    USING SAMPLE 10 PERCENT (system)
) TO 'local_sample.parquet' (FORMAT parquet);
Use code with caution.
If you are working with a specific dataset or running into slow remote scans, let me know:
• The Hugging Face dataset path or folder layout you are querying
• Whether you need exact reproducible row counts or maximum network speed
I can help you write the exact query or optimize the EXPLAIN plan for it.
```

    # CCFinance
    
    CCFinance is a data engineering project for filtering and enriching public
    Common Crawl News (CC-News) copies for research into language in finance.
    
    ## Start
    
    Exordio supplies the Python and LaTeX toolchains, a pinned Nix environment and CI.
    Copier answers record Exordio `v0.1.1-alpha` (the documented `v0.1.0` tag was not
    available in the local source).
    
    ```bash
    bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh
    devenv shell
    just setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run stages list
    just check
    ```
    
    Shared agent instructions and Codex configuration are maintained in
    [`.agents/`](.agents/README.md). `just setup` applies them; use
    `just agents::preview` to preview link changes and `just agents::check` to
    verify the generated links.
    
    `just check` validates Justfile syntax and formatting alongside the other
    quality gates. Run `just fmt` to format Justfiles and other source files.
    
    For Python alone, with Python 3.13, uv and just installed:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::check
    ```
    
    ## Data and reproducibility
    
    DVC is initialized at the repository root with analytics disabled. Use:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc status
    just dvc dag
    ```
    
    Semflow tracks the executable Python dependencies of DVC stages. When adding a
    stage, run `just semflow-patch` to review its proposed fingerprints, then
    `just semflow-apply` to materialize them. Commit the generated
    `.semflow/hashes/` files with the DVC definition. After semantic source changes,
    run `just semflow-refresh`; `just semflow-check` detects stale fingerprints.
    The frozen [Fine News acquisition stage](data/inputs/fine-news/README.md) documents
    the staging dataset's historical selection. Keep data, configuration and
    environment dependencies explicit
    in DVC: Semflow's static analysis cannot discover string-driven dynamic imports.
    
    See [Python commands](src/python/README.md), [LaTeX commands](src/latex/README.md)
    and [infrastructure](infra/README.md). The scaffold's Apache-2.0 license covers
    code; it does not grant rights to upstream article content.
    # Architecture
    
    CCFinance separates code and research artifacts. Git stores source, configuration,
    locks, provenance definitions and documentation. DVC defines data dependencies
    and will track large data and experiment outputs once they are materialized.
    
    - `src/python/apps/pipeline` owns the CLI and data stage implementations.
    - `src/python/uv.lock` locks runtime, quality, testing, packaging and DVC tools.
    - `src/latex` owns the manuscript source and bibliography.
    - `data` holds ignored data payloads and versioned DVC pointer files.
    - `infra/nix` and `devenv.lock` own the reproducible system environment.
    
    Tach enforces module boundaries; Ruff and strict Pyrefly check Python source.
    pytest-layout-enforcer checks test file placement during collection and CI.
    Semflow fingerprints the Python code used by DVC stages, allowing DVC to
    invalidate tracked results when executable behavior changes.
    CI executes those checks, tests and builds through the same just recipes as local
    work. Setup may download dependencies; ordinary checks use cached dependencies
    and do not repair authored content. LaTeX uses a versioned Tectonic asset bundle.
    
    The Hugging Face dataset is staging, and the bucket is intended for intermediate
    and experiment artifacts. The frozen raw acquisition stage documents the
    historical selection without fetching its output. Coverage criteria, later stages
    and remote transport remain future work.
    
    Copier answers record the source and tag for future template updates. Review
    update conflicts and preserve project-specific code and configuration. The
    upstream template is [Exordio](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/exordio).

Make sure to use this skill whenever the user mentions 'hf', 'huggingface', 'Hugging Face', 'huggingface-cli', or 'hugging face cli', or wants to do anything related to the Hugging Face ecosystem and to AI and ML in general.     - `hf repos duplicate FROM_ID` — Duplicate a repo on the Hub (model, dataset, or Space). `[--type [model|dataset|space] --private --public --protected --exist-ok --flavor [cpu-basic|cpu-upgrade|zero-a10g|t4-small|t4-medium|l4x1|l4x4|l40sx1|l40sx4|l40sx8|a10g-small|a10g-large|a10g-largex2|a10g-largex4|a100-large|a100x4|a100x8] --storage [small|medium|large] --sleep-time INTEGER --secrets TEXT --secrets-file TEXT --env TEXT --env-file TEXT --volume TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf repos list` — List all repos (models, datasets, spaces, buckets) with storage info. `[--namespace TEXT --type [model|dataset|space|bucket] --search TEXT --limit INTEGER --explore --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf repos move FROM_ID TO_ID` — Move a repository from a namespace to another namespace. `[--type [model|dataset|space] --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf repos settings REPO_ID` — Update the settings of a repository. `[--gated [auto|manual|false] --private --public --protected --type [model|dataset|space] --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf repos tag create REPO_ID TAG` — Create a tag for a repo. `[--message TEXT --revision TEXT --type [model|dataset|space] --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf repos tag delete REPO_ID TAG` — Delete a tag for a repo. `[--yes --type [model|dataset|space] --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf repos tag list REPO_ID` — List tags for a repo. `[--type [model|dataset|space] --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    
    ### `hf sandbox` — Run and manage experimental sandboxes on Hugging Face Jobs.
    
    - `hf sandbox cp SRC DST` — Copy a file between the local machine and a sandbox (docker-style). `[--namespace TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox create` — Create a sandbox: a dedicated VM by default, or a cheap shared one with `--pool`. `[--pool TEXT --flavor [cpu-basic|cpu-upgrade|cpu-performance|cpu-xl|t4-small|t4-medium|l4x1|l4x4|l40sx1|l40sx4|l40sx8|a10g-small|a10g-large|a10g-largex2|a10g-largex4|a100-large|a100x4|a100x8|h200|h200x2|h200x4|h200x8|rtx-pro-6000|rtx-pro-6000x2|rtx-pro-6000x4|rtx-pro-6000x8] --idle-timeout TEXT --env TEXT --secrets TEXT --env-file TEXT --secrets-file TEXT --volume TEXT --namespace TEXT --forward-hf-token --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox exec SANDBOX_ID COMMAND` — Run a command in a sandbox, streaming output. Exits with the command's exit code. `[--workdir TEXT --env TEXT --env-file TEXT --timeout FLOAT --namespace TEXT]`
    - `hf sandbox kill` — Terminate a sandbox, a whole shared host, or everything (--all). `[--all --yes --namespace TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox pool create` — Warm a pool: boot one host VM now, tagged so it can be found later by its pool id. `[--flavor [cpu-basic|cpu-upgrade|cpu-performance|cpu-xl|t4-small|t4-medium|l4x1|l4x4|l40sx1|l40sx4|l40sx8|a10g-small|a10g-large|a10g-largex2|a10g-largex4|a100-large|a100x4|a100x8|h200|h200x2|h200x4|h200x8|rtx-pro-6000|rtx-pro-6000x2|rtx-pro-6000x4|rtx-pro-6000x8] --per-host INTEGER RANGE --max-hosts INTEGER RANGE --idle-timeout TEXT --namespace TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox pool delete POOL_ID` — Terminate every host VM of a pool (and therefore all its sandboxes). `[--yes --namespace TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox pool ls` — List running sandbox pools (grouped from their host VMs). `[--namespace TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox process kill SANDBOX_ID PID` — Stop a background process running in a sandbox. `[--namespace TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox process ls SANDBOX_ID` — List the background processes running in a sandbox (started with `hf sandbox spawn`). `[--namespace TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox spawn SANDBOX_ID COMMAND` — Start a long-running command in the background and return its pid (don't wait). `[--workdir TEXT --env TEXT --env-file TEXT --namespace TEXT]`
    
    ### `hf skills` — Manage skills for AI assistants.
    
    - `hf skills add` — Install a Hugging Face skill for an AI assistant. `[--claude --global --dest PATH --force --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf skills list` — List available skills from the Hugging Face marketplace. `[--format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`

    ### `hf spaces` — Interact with spaces on the Hub.

    - `hf spaces hot-reload SPACE_ID` — Hot-reload any Python file of a Space without a full rebuild + restart. `[--local-file PATH --skip-checks --skip-summary --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf spaces info SPACE_ID` — Get info about a space on the Hub. `[--revision TEXT --expand TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf spaces list` — List spaces on the Hub, or files in a space repo. `[--search TEXT --author TEXT --filter TEXT --sort [created_at|last_modified|likes|trending_score] --limit INTEGER --expand TEXT --human-readable --tree --recursive --revision TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf spaces logs SPACE_ID` — Fetch the run or build logs of a Space. `[--build --follow --tail INTEGER --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`

    - `hf spaces secrets add SPACE_ID` — Add or update secrets for a Space. `[--secrets TEXT --secrets-file TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`

    ### `hf webhooks` — Manage webhooks on the Hub.
    
    - `hf webhooks create --watch TEXT` — Create a new webhook. `[--url TEXT --job-id TEXT --domain [repo|discussions] --secret TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf webhooks delete WEBHOOK_ID` — Delete a webhook permanently. `[--yes --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`

    ## Common options
    
    - `--format` — Output format: `--format json` (or `--json`) or `--format table` (default).
    - `-q / --quiet` — Quiet output (one ID per line).
    - `--revision` — Git revision id which can be a branch name, a tag, or a commit hash.
    - `--token` — Use a User Access Token. Prefer setting `HF_TOKEN` env var instead of passing `--token`.
    - `--type` — The type of repository (model, dataset, or space).
    
    ## Mounting repos as local filesystems
    
    To mount Hub repositories or buckets as local filesystems — no download, no copy, no waiting — use `hf-mount`. Files are fetched on demand. GitHub: https://github.com/huggingface/hf-mount
    
    Install: `brew install hf-mount`, or download a binary from https://github.com/huggingface/hf-mount/releases
    
    Some command examples:
    - `hf-mount start repo openai-community/gpt2 /tmp/gpt2` — mount a repo (read-only)
    - `hf-mount start --hf-token $HF_TOKEN bucket myuser/my-bucket /tmp/data` — mount a bucket (read-write)
    - `hf-mount status` / `hf-mount stop /tmp/data` — list or unmount
    
    ## Tips
    
    - Use `hf <command> --help` for full options, descriptions, usage, and real-world examples
    - Authenticate with `HF_TOKEN` env var (recommended) or with `--token`
    - Update the CLI with `hf update` (uses the correct command for the detected install method)set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]

    default:

    # Install exactly the committed workspace and build dependencies.
    setup:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv sync --locked --all-packages
    
    run *args:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline pipeline "$@"
    
    lint:

    typecheck:

    # Local impacted-test selection, with a bounded number of workers.
    test-changed:

    # The test and CI gates never use affected-test selection.
    test:

    # Check that test paths correspond to source modules.
    layout:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest-layout-enforcer check
    
    # Enforce module dependencies, reject unused declarations and forbid cycles.
    tach:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen tach check
    
    build:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv build --python .venv/bin/python --offline --no-build-isolation --all-packages
    
    check: lint typecheck tach layout test build
    
    fmt:

        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff format .
    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    set positional-arguments
    
    mod python 'src/python/justfile'

    mod agents '.agents/justfile'
    workflow := "env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py"
    
    # Discover this project's commands.
    default:
        @just --list
    
    # Prepare locked dependencies and Git hooks (uses the network).
    setup:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py prepare
        just python::setup
        just latex::setup
        just agents::apply
        prek install
    
    # Check source, views and selected languages without repairing files.
    check:

        just changelog-check
        just skills-check
        just agents::check
    
    # Run the selected language tests.
    test:
        just python::test
        just latex::test

    fmt:

        nixfmt devenv.nix infra/nix/devenv.nix infra/nix/pkgs/schematter.nix infra/nix/pkgs/agentsync.nix
        rumdl fmt .
        just python::fmt
        just latex::fmt
    
    # Check external links online.
    links:

    # Refresh generated planning and reference views.

    # Validate document schemas, links and generated views.

    # Create a plan without overwriting existing content.

    # Create a task inside an existing plan or task.

    # Preview the semantic dependency changes before applying them.
    semflow-patch:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow patch
    
    # Apply reviewed DVC and semantic fingerprint changes.
    semflow-apply:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow patch --apply
    
    # Refresh existing semantic fingerprints without editing the DVC graph.
    semflow-refresh:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow refresh --apply
    
    # Validate repository-owned skill documents and their directory names.
    skills-check:

    # Pipeline layers: raw -> processed -> research.
    # Each layer will contain independently reproducible DVC sub-stages.
    
    ## Raw: source snapshots
    # Ingest versioned article and company-reference snapshots with source manifests.
    # Preserve source content, metadata and provenance for replay and reconciliation.
    # Proposed location: data/raw/.
    
    ## Processed: reusable tables
    # Clean, standardize and deduplicate articles; resolve dated company identities
    # and enrich article-company relationships. Retain evidence and quality flags.
    # Produce reusable article, company and relationship tables.
    # Proposed location: data/processed/.
    
    ## Research: study datasets
    # Build company-year coverage panels, study cohorts and publication-ready datasets
    # from processed tables. Apply explicit publisher, relevance and K/T coverage policies.
    # Include dataset documentation, provenance and measured quality in each release.
    # Proposed location: data/research/.
    
    ## Validation and evaluation
    # Validate contracts and reconcile counts at every layer. Keep method experiments,
    # independent evaluation labels and quality reports as versioned supporting
    # artifacts; they inform promotion between layers rather than forming a data tier.
    
    stages:
      filter_fine_news:
        desc: Reproduce the historical English financial-publisher selection from Fine News.
        cmd: >-
          env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python
          --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline pipeline stages raw filter-fine-news
        frozen: true
        deps:
          - data/inputs/fine-news/acquisition.json
          - data/inputs/fine-news/domains.csv
          - src/python/uv.lock
          - devenv.lock
          - infra/nix/devenv.nix
          - .semflow/hashes/entrypoints/pipeline/stages/raw/filter-fine-news.json
        outs:
          - data/raw/fine-news
    """Reproduce the historical Fine News publisher filter."""
    
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
    from typing import Annotated
    
    import duckdb
    import typer
    from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
    
    QUERY = """
        COPY (
            WITH articles AS (
                SELECT text, id, metadata, lower(rtrim(trim(coalesce(
                    nullif(trim(metadata.url_hostname), ''),
                    regexp_extract(metadata.url, '(?i)^https?://([^/:?#]+)', 1)
                )), '.')) AS hostname
                FROM read_parquet($source)
            )
            SELECT text, id, metadata FROM articles
            WHERE EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM read_csv($domains, header=true) AS d
                WHERE hostname = lower(rtrim(trim(d.domain), '.'))
                   OR ends_with(hostname, '.' || lower(rtrim(trim(d.domain), '.')))
            )
        ) TO $target (FORMAT PARQUET, COMPRESSION ZSTD, COMPRESSION_LEVEL 9,
                     ROW_GROUP_SIZE 16384)
    """
    
    
    class FineNewsConfig(BaseModel):
        """Versioned inputs and output for the Fine News selection."""
    
        model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    
        source: str
        domains: Path
        output: Path
    
    
    def filter_fine_news(
        config: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="Historical acquisition configuration.")
        ] = Path("data/inputs/fine-news/acquisition.json"),
    ) -> None:
        """Select English publisher shards from a pinned Fine News revision."""
        settings = FineNewsConfig.model_validate_json(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        target = settings.output / "articles.parquet"
        if target.exists():
            raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {target}")
        settings.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            if settings.source.startswith("hf://"):
                con.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs")
            with TemporaryDirectory(dir=settings.output) as staging:
                temporary = Path(staging) / "articles.parquet"
                con.execute(
                    QUERY,
                    {
                        "source": settings.source,
                        "domains": str(settings.domains),
                        "target": str(temporary),
                    },
                )
                os.link(temporary, target)
        typer.echo(f"Wrote: {settings.source} -> {target}")
    {
      "source": "hf://datasets/ksolovev/fine-news@7a841090e69f3c58a9e04b0c39213d879af68e8a/data/*/eng_Latn/*.parquet",
      "domains": "data/inputs/fine-news/domains.csv",
      "output": "data/raw/fine-news"
    }
    # Fine News acquisition
    
    `filter_fine_news` documents the historical staging selection from
    [Fine News](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ksolovev/fine-news) at the revision
    in [acquisition.json](acquisition.json). It selects `eng_Latn` capture-month
    shards and the exact 115-hostname [allowlist](domains.csv), including subdomains.
    The hostname comes from `metadata.url_hostname`, falling back to `metadata.url`
    when blank. One query reads the input glob and writes `text`, `id` and `metadata`
    to `data/raw/fine-news/articles.parquet`.
    
    This is the historical source filter, not a reviewed publisher list or a
    research-ready article corpus. Fine News applies its own filters and
    deduplication; capture month is not necessarily publication month. The upstream
    dataset card describes content rights and usage restrictions. No full output has
    been built, verified or cached here, and no DVC lock entry is claimed.
    
    The stage is frozen: `dvc repro` will not execute it, even with `--force`.
    Since the declared output is absent, targeting it currently reports missing data.
    After obtaining or rebuilding and verifying the output, track its actual state
    before relying on it downstream. Unfreezing or invoking the command directly can
    run the acquisition and requires network access and substantial resources.
    DuckDB may download its `httpfs` extension on first remote access.
    
    For a local trial, provide `--config` with a local source glob, domain CSV and
    fresh output directory. The script refuses to overwrite an existing output.
    Output layout, order and Parquet bytes differ from
    the staging shards; selected rows have not been compared with that dataset.

    ignore-type-checking-blocks = true

    control-stages = ["semflow_refresh"]

    """Exercise the historical acquisition against local Parquet files."""
    
    import json
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import duckdb
    import pytest
    from pipeline.cli import app
    from typer.testing import CliRunner
    
    
    @pytest.mark.integration
    def test_filter_preserves_english_publisher_rows(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        # Arrange: create two source shards and a historical-style domain list.
        source = tmp_path / "input/2020-01/eng_Latn/part-000000.parquet"
        source.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        domains = tmp_path / "domains.csv"
        domains.write_text("domain\nexample.com\n", encoding="utf-8")
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            con.execute(
                """COPY (SELECT * FROM (VALUES
                    ('1', 'one', {'url_hostname': 'EXAMPLE.COM.', 'url': 'https://wrong.test/a'}),
                    ('2', 'two', {'url_hostname': 'news.example.com', 'url': 'https://wrong.test/b'}),
                    ('3', 'three', {'url_hostname': '', 'url': 'https://example.com/c'}),
                    ('4', 'four', {'url_hostname': 'notexample.com', 'url': 'https://example.com/d'})
                ) AS rows(id, text, metadata)) TO ? (FORMAT PARQUET)""",
                [str(source)],
            )
            second = source.parent / "part-000001.parquet"
            con.execute(
                "COPY (SELECT * FROM read_parquet($source) WHERE id = '2') "
                "TO $target (FORMAT PARQUET)",
                {"source": str(source), "target": str(second)},
            )
    
        output = tmp_path / "output"
        config = tmp_path / "config.json"
        config.write_text(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    "source": str(source.parent / "*.parquet"),
                    "domains": str(domains),
                    "output": str(output),
                }
            ),
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
    
        # Act: filter the source through the public CLI.
        result = CliRunner().invoke(
            app, ["stages", "raw", "filter-fine-news", "--config", str(config)]
        )
    
        # Assert: only eligible rows and their original fields are preserved.
        assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
        target = output / "articles.parquet"
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            result = con.execute(
                "SELECT id, text, metadata.url_hostname, metadata.url "
                "FROM read_parquet(?) ORDER BY id",
                [str(target)],
            ).fetchall()
        assert result == [
            ("1", "one", "EXAMPLE.COM.", "https://wrong.test/a"),
            ("2", "two", "news.example.com", "https://wrong.test/b"),
            ("2", "two", "news.example.com", "https://wrong.test/b"),
            ("3", "three", "", "https://example.com/c"),
        ]

    ### `hf sandbox` — Run and manage experimental sandboxes on Hugging Face Jobs.
    
    - `hf sandbox cp SRC DST` — Copy a file between the local machine and a sandbox (docker-style). `[--namespace TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox create` — Create a sandbox: a dedicated VM by default, or a cheap shared one with `--pool`. `[--pool TEXT --flavor [cpu-basic|cpu-upgrade|cpu-performance|cpu-xl|t4-small|t4-medium|l4x1|l4x4|l40sx1|l40sx4|l40sx8|a10g-small|a10g-large|a10g-largex2|a10g-largex4|a100-large|a100x4|a100x8|h200|h200x2|h200x4|h200x8|rtx-pro-6000|rtx-pro-6000x2|rtx-pro-6000x4|rtx-pro-6000x8] --idle-timeout TEXT --env TEXT --secrets TEXT --env-file TEXT --secrets-file TEXT --volume TEXT --namespace TEXT --forward-hf-token --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox exec SANDBOX_ID COMMAND` — Run a command in a sandbox, streaming output. Exits with the command's exit code. `[--workdir TEXT --env TEXT --env-file TEXT --timeout FLOAT --namespace TEXT]`
    - `hf sandbox kill` — Terminate a sandbox, a whole shared host, or everything (--all). `[--all --yes --namespace TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox pool create` — Warm a pool: boot one host VM now, tagged so it can be found later by its pool id. `[--flavor [cpu-basic|cpu-upgrade|cpu-performance|cpu-xl|t4-small|t4-medium|l4x1|l4x4|l40sx1|l40sx4|l40sx8|a10g-small|a10g-large|a10g-largex2|a10g-largex4|a100-large|a100x4|a100x8|h200|h200x2|h200x4|h200x8|rtx-pro-6000|rtx-pro-6000x2|rtx-pro-6000x4|rtx-pro-6000x8] --per-host INTEGER RANGE --max-hosts INTEGER RANGE --idle-timeout TEXT --namespace TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox pool delete POOL_ID` — Terminate every host VM of a pool (and therefore all its sandboxes). `[--yes --namespace TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox pool ls` — List running sandbox pools (grouped from their host VMs). `[--namespace TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox process kill SANDBOX_ID PID` — Stop a background process running in a sandbox. `[--namespace TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox process ls SANDBOX_ID` — List the background processes running in a sandbox (started with `hf sandbox spawn`). `[--namespace TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf sandbox spawn SANDBOX_ID COMMAND` — Start a long-running command in the background and return its pid (don't wait). `[--workdir TEXT --env TEXT --env-file TEXT --namespace TEXT]`

    ### `hf webhooks` — Manage webhooks on the Hub.
    
    - `hf webhooks create --watch TEXT` — Create a new webhook. `[--url TEXT --job-id TEXT --domain [repo|discussions] --secret TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`

    - `hf webhooks disable WEBHOOK_ID` — Disable an active webhook. `[--format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`

    - `hf webhooks info WEBHOOK_ID` — Show full details for a single webhook. `[--format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf webhooks list` — List all webhooks for the current user. `[--format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf webhooks update WEBHOOK_ID` — Update an existing webhook. Only provided options are changed. `[--url TEXT --watch TEXT --domain [repo|discussions] --secret TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    
    ## Common options
    
    - `--format` — Output format: `--format json` (or `--json`) or `--format table` (default).
    - `-q / --quiet` — Quiet output (one ID per line).
    - `--revision` — Git revision id which can be a branch name, a tag, or a commit hash.
    - `--token` — Use a User Access Token. Prefer setting `HF_TOKEN` env var instead of passing `--token`.
    - `--type` — The type of repository (model, dataset, or space).
    
    ## Mounting repos as local filesystems
    
    To mount Hub repositories or buckets as local filesystems — no download, no copy, no waiting — use `hf-mount`. Files are fetched on demand. GitHub: https://github.com/huggingface/hf-mount
    
    Install: `brew install hf-mount`, or download a binary from https://github.com/huggingface/hf-mount/releases

    # Define dataset requirements
    
    ## Goal
    
    Specify a public, reproducible financial news dataset for firm-level text,
    co-mention networks and market research.
    
    ## Requirements
    
    - **Coverage:** Report distinct usable articles per company-year, including zero
      counts for a declared universe, and firms meeting selectable annual thresholds
      over consecutive years. Compare with 47 raw articles per year over 2018–2022
      for the 100-firm Pricing Perspective frame; report raw and usable counts separately.
    - **Articles:** Provide stable IDs, source and publisher, URL, title, article text,
      language, publication and capture times with precision, quality flags, and
      traceable capture provenance where available.
    - **Companies:** Preserve all article–company links, dated issuer identifiers,
      supporting evidence, ambiguity and substantive relevance. Distinguish mentions
      from company-focused coverage and retain unresolved identities.
    - **Sources:** Maintain versioned publisher selection criteria and distinguish
      original reporting, syndicated material and press releases where possible.
      Deduplicate stories without discarding source records or company links.
    - **Research validity:** Evaluate extraction, deduplication, dates, company links
      and relevance against human-adjudicated samples. Report precision, recall,
      uncertainty and coverage gaps across years, publishers and firms.
    - **Reproducibility:** Publish a versioned schema, data dictionary, lineage,
      checksums, methods, coverage reports and examples for firm-year panels and
      co-mention networks. Document article-text access and redistribution conditions.
    - **Extensions:** Treat company-specific sentiment and events, article topics and
      novelty as separately versioned, evaluated enrichments.
    
    Numerical coverage and quality targets remain provisional until the staging audit.
    Publication dates before CC-News began do not establish when text was observable.
    See the [Pricing Perspective comparison](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.23447v3#Sx1)
    for the baseline and its limitations.
    
    ## Acceptance
    
    - [ ] Review these requirements against staging evidence and intended studies.
    - [ ] Set evidence-based coverage and quality targets for a first release.

    # Define dataset requirements
    
    ## Goal
    
    Specify a public, reproducible financial news dataset for firm-level text,
    co-mention networks and market research.
    
    ## Requirements
    
    - **Coverage:** Report distinct usable articles per company-year, including zero
      counts for a declared universe, and firms meeting selectable annual thresholds
      over consecutive years. Compare with 47 raw articles per year over 2018–2022
      for the 100-firm Pricing Perspective frame; report raw and usable counts separately.
    - **Articles:** Provide stable IDs, source and publisher, URL, title, article text,
      language, publication and capture times with precision, quality flags, and
      traceable capture provenance where available.
    - **Companies:** Preserve all article–company links, dated issuer identifiers,
      supporting evidence, ambiguity and substantive relevance. Distinguish mentions
      from company-focused coverage and retain unresolved identities.
    - **Sources:** Maintain versioned publisher selection criteria and distinguish
      original reporting, syndicated material and press releases where possible.
      Deduplicate stories without discarding source records or company links.
    - **Research validity:** Evaluate extraction, deduplication, dates, company links
      and relevance against human-adjudicated samples. Report precision, recall,
      uncertainty and coverage gaps across years, publishers and firms.
    - **Reproducibility:** Publish a versioned schema, data dictionary, lineage,
      checksums, methods, coverage reports and examples for firm-year panels and
      co-mention networks. Document article-text access and redistribution conditions.
    - **Extensions:** Treat company-specific sentiment and events, article topics and
      novelty as separately versioned, evaluated enrichments.
    
    Numerical coverage and quality targets remain provisional until the staging audit.
    Publication dates before CC-News began do not establish when text was observable.
    See the [Pricing Perspective comparison](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.23447v3#Sx1)
    for the baseline and its limitations.
    
    ## Acceptance
    
    - [ ] Review these requirements against staging evidence and intended studies.
    - [ ] Set evidence-based coverage and quality targets for a first release.

    ---
    title: Planning
    description: Project-owned plans and nested tasks with honest completion and local views.
    ---
    
    # Planning
    
    Create a plan, then its first task:
    
    ```bash
    just plan-new project "Project plan"
    just task-new .context/plan/project first-step "Make the first useful change"
    just sync
    ```
    
    The [root roadmap](../../ROADMAP.md) lists plans. Each plan or task shows only
    its immediate open children and counts terminal children. A deeper task lives
    in its parent's `tasks/SLUG/README.md`; its path supplies identity and parentage.
    Changing status never moves a file or breaks its links.
    
    Edit `status` in frontmatter: `backlog`, `in-progress`, `blocked`, `done` or
    `closed`. `done` requires at least one nonempty active acceptance criterion,
    all checked. Fenced examples and struck-through criteria do not count.
    `closed` stops work without claiming completion and requires `resolution.reason`.
    Terminal parents cannot retain open children. Reopen a parent before adding work.
    
    Every work item keeps one generated children region, including leaves. Edit
    outside the markers; `just sync` refreshes views, while `just check` reports
    invalid records or drift without repairing them. Put longer supporting detail
    in linked files rather than growing the 1,500-token entry point.

## Assistant

Your choices set the scope: publisher-only yield across English source snapshots, starting with a capped pilot.

The DuckDB docs change one part of the proposed approach: `SYSTEM` samples execution vectors and does not promise proportional savings in remote Parquet reads. Selecting exact files gives us a dependable boundary. Hugging Face’s converted Parquet can also cover only a dataset prefix, so it cannot automatically stand in for the full source.

I recommend sampling four files per source at random and scanning them completely. That gives us a small pilot with measurable between-file variation, though its confidence intervals may be wide.

    ### `hf repos` — Manage repos on the Hub.
    
    - `hf repos branch create REPO_ID BRANCH` — Create a new branch for a repo on the Hub. `[--revision TEXT --type [model|dataset|space] --exist-ok --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf repos branch delete REPO_ID BRANCH` — Delete a branch from a repo on the Hub. `[--type [model|dataset|space] --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf repos cp SRC` — Copy files between local paths, repositories, and buckets. `[--format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
    - `hf repos create REPO_ID` — Create a new repo on the Hub. `[--type [model|dataset|space] --sdk TEXT --template TEXT --private --public --protected --exist-ok --resource-group-id TEXT --region [us|eu] --flavor [cpu-basic|cpu-upgrade|zero-a10g|t4-small|t4-medium|l4x1|l4x4|l40sx1|l40sx4|l40sx8|a10g-small|a10g-large|a10g-largex2|a10g-largex4|a100-large|a100x4|a100x8] --storage [small|medium|large] --sleep-time INTEGER --secrets TEXT --secrets-file TEXT --env TEXT --env-file TEXT --volume TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`

## Assistant

The byte-counting check found a useful option in our pinned DuckDB version. On a local HTTP-served Parquet file:

- Full scan and `SYSTEM 5%` each transferred about **27.4 MB**.
- Selecting one row group through a `file_row_number` range transferred **1.18 MB**.
- Reading the row-group metadata transferred about **67 KB**.

So we can sample a few small groups across Parquet files without downloading those files in full. Savings will depend on the actual group sizes, which the preparation step can report. DCLM’s compressed JSONL remains the whole-file exception.

## Plan

# Build a bandwidth-conscious source comparison

## Summary

Compare **Fine News, Infini News, RefinedWeb and FineWeb-HQ**, using the existing publisher filter and **four randomly selected Parquet row groups per source**. Defer DCLM until bandwidth or a complete columnar copy is available.

Implementation will prepare manifests and transfer-size estimates, without acquiring article payloads. The experiment measures publisher-matched English **source records**; research qualification, deduplication and company-year coverage remain later analyses.

The physical sampling method is verified on pinned DuckDB 1.5.6: explicit row-number ranges skipped remote Parquet reads in a local HTTP experiment. `SYSTEM` sampling transferred the full projected input in that experiment. Savings on the real sources will depend on their row-group sizes.

## Configuration and pipeline

Keep [params.yaml](/home/marcussky/Git/CCFinance/params.yaml) to one commented `comparison` section:

- Shared `seed: 42`, `draws: 4` and the existing domain CSV path.
- A `datasets` mapping containing the four active sources and their pinned `hf://` Parquet globs.
- A comment explaining why DCLM is deferred.
- Derive output locations from dataset keys; keep SQL and schema adapters in Python.

Use the existing Fine News revision. Resolve current revisions for the other sources to immutable commits before recording their configuration.

Extend [dvc.yaml](/home/marcussky/Git/CCFinance/dvc.yaml) with three steps:

1. **`prepare_comparison`**, using `foreach` over the dataset mapping: enumerate eligible files, select groups and persist metadata.
2. **`sample_comparison`**, using the same `foreach`: read the selected groups, apply the publisher filter and retain matching records.
3. **`compare_sources`**: combine counts, sizes and population estimates into a comparison table and DVC metrics.

Track only each iteration’s relevant parameter keys. Keep manifests, articles and reports as separate DVC outputs, with explicit allowlist, lockfile and Semflow dependencies. Preserve the frozen historical acquisition stage.

Expose corresponding Typer commands under `raw` for preparation/acquisition and `research` for comparison. Run only preparation during implementation.

## Sampling, reuse and reporting

**Prepare a reproducible probability sample.**

- Enumerate the complete eligible file inventory using Hub metadata, recording the revision, paths, object identities and listed sizes.
- Make four independent draws **with replacement**. For each draw, choose a file uniformly, then choose one of its row groups uniformly. Only selected files require footer reads.
- Persist every draw’s file, group, row bounds and probability. Repeated draws remain in the statistical calculation; acquire their payload only once.
- Use native English partitions or labels: Fine News’s English directories, Infini News’s inline English label, and the English release scope of RefinedWeb and FineWeb-HQ. Record these definitions explicitly.
- Never substitute cheaper files or groups after selection. An unaffordable selection is deferred.

This avoids fetching every file’s footer while retaining known sampling probabilities. Row-group boundaries and compressed column sizes come from DuckDB’s [Parquet metadata functions](https://duckdb.org/docs/1.5/data/parquet/metadata).

**Reuse the acquisition implementation.**

Refactor [fine_news.py](/home/marcussky/Git/CCFinance/src/python/apps/pipeline/src/pipeline/stages/raw/fine_news.py) just enough to share its hostname normalization, exact/subdomain matching and atomic Parquet writing.

Add small, explicit source projections and optional bound row-number ranges. Preserve the historical command’s behavior. Keep schema differences in those projections, rather than building a general plugin framework.

Retain article text, useful native metadata and source-file/row provenance. Exclude media and embeddings. Apply row bounds at the Parquet reader, before publisher filtering. Do not use `USING SAMPLE`, prefixes or `LIMIT` as the acquisition design.

**Separate observations from estimates.**

For each source, report:

- Listed population files and stored bytes, with multilingual scope identified where applicable.
- Selected files/groups, sampled rows, English rows and publisher matches.
- Observed retention, retained output bytes and elapsed acquisition time.
- Projected compressed column-chunk bytes, clearly distinguished from measured network traffic. Leave network bytes unavailable unless reliably measured.

For a draw selecting a group from file \(i\), let \(M\) be the eligible file count and \(G_i\) its group count. Its draw probability is:

\[
q=\frac{1}{M G_i}.
\]

Estimate publisher-matched and English population totals using the **Hansen–Hurwitz mean of weighted draw counts**:

\[
\widehat Y=\operatorname{mean}(y/q),\qquad
\widehat N=\operatorname{mean}(n_{\mathrm{English}}/q),\qquad
\widehat p=\widehat Y/\widehat N.
\]

Use variance across weighted draws and linearized variance for the yield ratio. This accounts for unequal file/group sizes; pooling the sampled rows without weights would generally be incorrect. See the [Hansen–Hurwitz formulas in Appendix A](https://www.scb.se/contentassets/ca21efb41fee47d293bbee5bf7be7fb3/variances-in-repeated-weighting-with-an-application-to-the-dutch-labour-force-survey.pdf#page=17).

Label uncertainty estimates **exploratory**: four draws provide little information about rare or unevenly distributed matches. Approximate 95% intervals use three degrees of freedom; zero matches or degenerate variance produce an “insufficient evidence” result, not a zero-width interval. Fix the sample before observing outcomes.

These estimates describe extractable source records in each snapshot. They do not establish unique articles, incremental coverage across overlapping sources or final research eligibility. Assess precision from the pilot before planning a larger, potentially stratified study.

## Validation and handoff

- Preserve the existing historical-filter integration test.
- Add focused tests for unequal sampling weights, repeated draws and unavailable uncertainty; use Hypothesis for suitable small-frame properties.
- Exercise source projections and count reconciliation against tiny local Parquet fixtures.
- Retain one local HTTP integration check proving row-bound selection reduces transferred bytes relative to a full projected scan.
- Check DVC expansion, per-source parameter dependencies, Semflow and the existing quality gates.

Preparation must finish with a reviewable table of selected groups, row counts, footer costs and projected column bytes. Verify HTTP range support; never silently fall back to downloading complete files.

Record the sampling design, limitations and acceptance criteria in a terse task and linked methods note under the existing dataset-research plan. Article acquisition remains a subsequent explicit run.

    # Architecture layout
    
    ## Workflow
    
    1. Establish the requested scope and outcome: evaluate the current layout,
       design a layout, or implement an authorized change. Read nearby README and
       ARCHITECTURE files. Identify existing owners and consumers before proposing
       a new abstraction; reuse an existing module or library when it satisfies the
       contract. File size alone is not a reason to split or create a package.
    2. Examine the relevant boundaries using evidence:
       - **Ownership and cohesion:** Can a contributor find the owner, and do things
         that change together live together? Keep each unit's responsibility clear.
       - **Dependencies and encapsulation:** Trace relevant imports and public
         interfaces. Keep intended dependency direction clear and cycles forbidden;
         avoid reaching into another module's internals without a reason.
       - **Coupling:** Identify changes that force unrelated owners to change.
         Share a contract only when consumers actually need the same behavior; a
         little local duplication may be preferable to coupling distinct contracts.
       - **Discoverability:** Make CLI commands, transformations, schemas, tests,
         fixtures and documents easy to find from their owning area.
    3. Choose the smallest useful boundary: a function, module, package or separate
       workspace project. A package or project should reflect an actual dependency,
       distribution, build or ownership need. Organize by layer, capability or a
       combination according to the work; do not impose a universal directory tree.
    4. For pipeline work, preserve the established `raw`, `processed` and `research`
       stage ownership. Organize capabilities within those layers as they arise.
       Distinguish Python imports from DVC artifact dependencies: the latter connect
       producers and consumers without requiring cross-layer Python imports. Apply
       Tach rules to durable module boundaries and DVC to artifact dependencies.
    5. For a move or split, trace the affected consumers before changing paths:
       imports and public APIs, CLI registration, package configuration, tests and
       fixtures, Tach, DVC and Semflow dependencies, and documentation links as
       applicable. Preserve behavior and scientific contracts unless the user asks
       for a change; report any intended behavior change separately. Do not treat
       missing static references as proof that dynamic or external consumers do not
       exist.
    6. Use the repository's existing gates rather than adding tests that merely
       assert a directory tree or private call sequence. For tests and fixtures,
       follow [Python testing](../python-testing/SKILL.md). Run focused checks while
       working and `just check` before handoff; report checks that could not run.
    
    ## Results
    
    For an evaluation, report concrete findings with locations, effects and ranked
    recommendations. For a design, show the proposed ownership and dependency
    boundaries, explain meaningful tradeoffs and how they are enforced. For an
    implementation, summarize what moved, whether behavior changed and the evidence

    For example, if both article cleaning and company linking need the same

    # Python testing
    
    ## Workflow
    
    1. Inspect the code contract, nearby tests, `conftest.py`, shared fixtures and
       strategies, the package's test README, and pytest configuration. Reuse an
       existing test or generator when it covers the behavior; extend it only for a
       distinct, meaningful risk. Do not add tests for trivial or reversible changes
       just to increase counts, or tests that restate implementation details.
    2. Prefer Hypothesis for input variation when a general property is meaningful.
       Prefer a small explicit example for a single known boundary, regression or
       command smoke check. Decide the expected outcome independently of the code
       under test. Use tiny representative data, bounded generators and the smallest
       appropriate test boundary. Assert public behavior, including error contracts.
    3. Place a test beside its source owner under the mirrored `tests/` layout. Reuse
       existing factories and strategies first. Keep a helper local until several
       tests need it; put cross-module strategies in `tests/_strategies.py` and
       shared pytest fixtures in the nearest common `conftest.py`. Place a fixture
       at broader scope only when its state is safe to share. Measure costly setup
       before broadening scope; avoid creating generic fixture frameworks.
    4. Arrange inputs and prerequisites, act on the behavior, and assert observable
       results (AAA). Cleanup belongs in a fixture finalizer or context manager.
       Label each phase with an `# Arrange`, `# Act` or `# Assert` comment, as in
       the example below. Favor DAMP: clear names and visible expected values can
       justify a little repetition.
    5. Give each new or modified test exactly one scope marker from the table below;
       add `slow` or `external` only when applicable. Mark a class or module only
       when every inherited test has the same scope. Never stack or override scope
       markers, including inherited marks. Before using markers, register the six
       names in the owning pytest configuration; unknown names fail under
       `--strict-markers`. This skill defines the policy; it does not mean the
       current unmarked suite already enforces it. Migrate existing tests deliberately
       if adding a collection-time enforcement hook.
    6. During development, run the smallest relevant test or selection and check
       its output. Before handoff run the repository's required full checks, including
       the complete non-Testmon suite. Run any affected slow or external tests when
       their prerequisites and authorization are available; report what was not run
       and why. A targeted pass is not evidence that the full suite passed.
    
    ## Markers
    
    Use only these six custom markers. Built-in pytest mechanisms such as
    `parametrize`, `skipif` and `xfail` remain available for their intended purposes.
    Scope describes the boundary the assertions exercise, not the number of files,
    the use of Hypothesis, or the choice of a reference oracle.
    
    | Marker | Rule |
    | --- | --- |
    | `unit` | Exactly one scope: an isolated operation or small self-contained behavior. |
    | `component` | Exactly one scope: one coherent subsystem or component through its public behavior. |
    | `integration` | Exactly one scope: interactions across components or a real dependency boundary. |
    | `e2e` | Exactly one scope: a complete user-visible workflow through the public CLI or API. A CLI help check alone is not end-to-end. |
    | `slow` | Optional execution label: the complete test, including setup, teardown and generated examples, consistently exceeds two seconds on the normal local environment. Confirm with repeated pytest duration reports; a single noisy measurement is not enough. |
    | `external` | Optional execution label: the test accesses a live network service or external account. Use even if it is usually fast; require explicit opt-in and appropriate credentials. A local temporary file, subprocess or fake alone does not qualify. |
    
    `slow` and `external` are independent and may accompany any one scope. Do not
    invent custom markers for regression, reference, property, smoke, tools or
    implementation techniques; communicate those in descriptive test names and
    assertions. Run fast local iteration with `-m "not slow and not external"`
    after the markers are registered. Full checks must not silently omit slow tests;
    external tests need a separate explicit lane and must not mutate live services
    without authorization.
    
    ## Hypothesis examples and fixtures
    
    Hypothesis strategies generate values; pytest fixtures manage resources. If
    Hypothesis is absent, add it to the locked workspace development dependencies
    when introducing the first test that uses it. Search
    for reusable strategies or an appropriate first-party Hypothesis extra before
    adding one. Compose built-in strategies, use `@composite` for dependent values,
    and generate valid inputs directly rather than filtering most examples. Keep
    sizes bounded and counterexamples understandable. Preserve an important known
    failure using `@example` or an explicit regression; do not duplicate a property
    with a long list of examples that establish the same behavior.
    
    A function-scoped pytest fixture runs once per test function, not once per
    `@given` example. For per-example mutable resources, create and clean them inside
    the test, for example with `TemporaryDirectory()`. Reuse immutable shared data
    only when safe. Do not suppress health checks or disable deadlines globally to
    make a test pass; investigate the cause and document a narrowly justified
    exception. Choose explicit settings or a shared profile only when warranted by
    measured cost. Preserve failing examples and replay information as appropriate.
    
    This self-contained example illustrates a small property, AAA and the scope
    marker; it uses the standard-library URL parser rather than a CCFinance stage:
    
    ```python
    from string import ascii_lowercase, digits
    from urllib.parse import urlsplit
    
    import pytest
    from hypothesis import example, given, strategies as st
    
    
    @pytest.mark.unit
    @example(host="news")
    @given(host=st.text(alphabet=ascii_lowercase + digits, min_size=1, max_size=20))
    def test_url_hostname_normalizes_ascii_case(host: str) -> None:
        # Arrange: build a URL with an uppercase hostname.
        url = f"https://{host.upper()}.example/article"
    
        # Act: extract the hostname.
        hostname = urlsplit(url).hostname
    
        # Assert: the hostname is lowercase.
        assert hostname == f"{host}.example"
    ```
    
    Use a real local Parquet or filesystem boundary for a small integration test
    when that interaction matters; use a stub or fake for costly or nondeterministic
    remote services. A fake cannot establish that the real service works. Keep
    randomized tests independent of execution order; for numerical or sampling
    claims define tolerances and uncertainty rather than requiring arbitrary
    bit-for-bit agreement across environments.
    
    Consult the Hypothesis [tutorial](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorial/),
    [how-to guides](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how-to/),
    [strategies and API reference](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/)
    and [extras](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/extras.html) when
    choosing or debugging a strategy.

            )
            SELECT text, id, metadata FROM articles
            WHERE EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM read_csv($domains, header=true) AS d
                WHERE hostname = lower(rtrim(trim(d.domain), '.'))
                   OR ends_with(hostname, '.' || lower(rtrim(trim(d.domain), '.')))
            )
        ) TO $target (FORMAT PARQUET, COMPRESSION ZSTD, COMPRESSION_LEVEL 9,
                     ROW_GROUP_SIZE 16384)
    """
    
    
    class FineNewsConfig(BaseModel):
        """Versioned inputs and output for the Fine News selection."""
    
        model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    
        source: str
        domains: Path
        output: Path
    
    
    def filter_fine_news(
        config: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="Historical acquisition configuration.")
        ] = Path("data/inputs/fine-news/acquisition.json"),
    ) -> None:
        """Select English publisher shards from a pinned Fine News revision."""
        settings = FineNewsConfig.model_validate_json(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        target = settings.output / "articles.parquet"
        if target.exists():
            raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {target}")
        settings.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            if settings.source.startswith("hf://"):
                con.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs")
            with TemporaryDirectory(dir=settings.output) as staging:
                temporary = Path(staging) / "articles.parquet"
                con.execute(
                    QUERY,
                    {
                        "source": settings.source,
                        "domains": str(settings.domains),
                        "target": str(temporary),
                    },
                )
                os.link(temporary, target)
        typer.echo(f"Wrote: {settings.source} -> {target}")
    """Preserve versioned source snapshots and provenance."""
    
    import typer
    
    from pipeline.stages.raw.fine_news import filter_fine_news
    
    app = typer.Typer(no_args_is_help=True, help=__doc__)
    
    
    @app.callback()
    def main() -> None:
        """Preserve versioned source snapshots and provenance."""
    
    
    app.command("filter-fine-news")(filter_fine_news)

    app = typer.Typer(no_args_is_help=True, help=__doc__)
    
    
    @app.callback()
    def main() -> None:

    [project]
    name = "ccfinance-pipeline"
    version = "0.1.0"
    description = "Reproducible CCFinance data engineering stages"
    requires-python = ">=3.13,<3.14"
    dependencies = ["duckdb==1.5.6", "pydantic>=2,<3", "typer>=0.16,<1"]
    
    [project.scripts]
    pipeline = "pipeline.cli:app"
    
    [build-system]
    requires = ["hatchling==1.27.0"]
    build-backend = "hatchling.build"
    
    [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
    packages = ["src/pipeline"]
    # Pipeline layers: raw -> processed -> research.
    # Each layer will contain independently reproducible DVC sub-stages.
    
    ## Raw: source snapshots
    # Ingest versioned article and company-reference snapshots with source manifests.
    # Preserve source content, metadata and provenance for replay and reconciliation.
    # Proposed location: data/raw/.
    
    ## Processed: reusable tables
    # Clean, standardize and deduplicate articles; resolve dated company identities
    # and enrich article-company relationships. Retain evidence and quality flags.
    # Produce reusable article, company and relationship tables.
    # Proposed location: data/processed/.
    
    ## Research: study datasets
    # Build company-year coverage panels, study cohorts and publication-ready datasets
    # from processed tables. Apply explicit publisher, relevance and K/T coverage policies.
    # Include dataset documentation, provenance and measured quality in each release.
    # Proposed location: data/research/.
    
    ## Validation and evaluation
    # Validate contracts and reconcile counts at every layer. Keep method experiments,
    # independent evaluation labels and quality reports as versioned supporting
    # artifacts; they inform promotion between layers rather than forming a data tier.
    
    stages:
      filter_fine_news:
        desc: Reproduce the historical English financial-publisher selection from Fine News.
        cmd: >-
          env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python
          --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline pipeline stages raw filter-fine-news
        frozen: true
        deps:
          - data/inputs/fine-news/acquisition.json
          - data/inputs/fine-news/domains.csv
          - src/python/uv.lock
          - devenv.lock
          - infra/nix/devenv.nix
          - .semflow/hashes/entrypoints/pipeline/stages/raw/filter-fine-news.json
        outs:
          - data/raw/fine-news
