    # Python workspace
    
    `apps/pipeline` is an installable Typer application in a Python 3.13 uv workspace.
    Run from the repository root:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run version
    just python::run stages list
    just python::run stages raw --help
    just python::layout
    just python::check
    ```
    
    Data processing is organized into three layers, matching `dvc.yaml`:
    
    | Module and CLI group | Purpose | Data location |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `pipeline.stages.raw` / `stages raw` | Preserve source snapshots and provenance | `data/raw/` |
    | `pipeline.stages.processed` / `stages processed` | Build reusable cleaned and enriched tables | `data/processed/` |
    | `pipeline.stages.research` / `stages research` | Curate coverage panels, cohorts and release datasets | `data/research/` |
    
    The raw layer includes the frozen historical Fine News publisher filter described
    in [its acquisition configuration](../../data/inputs/fine-news/README.md). Add other
    stage commands under their owning layer,
    with explicit inputs and outputs, and declare their dependencies in `dvc.yaml`.
    DVC connects layers through artifacts; Python modules need not import earlier
    layers to read their outputs. Importing a module performs no dataset access.
    
    Setup installs the committed lock. Checks run offline with frozen dependencies.
    Ruff checks formatting, annotations, docstrings and common correctness/security
    issues; strict Pyrefly checks all app code and tests. Tach enforces module
    boundaries, rejects unused dependency declarations and forbids cycles. The CLI
    imports the stage router, which registers the three independent layer modules.
    
    `pytest-layout-enforcer` checks test paths against their owning source modules
    both during pytest collection and with `just python::layout`. Test paths mirror
    `apps/pipeline/src/pipeline` under `apps/pipeline/tests`: for example,
    `cli.py` maps to `test_cli.py`, and `stages/raw/loader.py` maps to
    `stages/raw/test_loader.py`. Feature variants use `__`, as in
    `test_loader__empty.py`; `include-packages` also allows tests for package
    initializers. This checks existing test placement, not test coverage. Tach checks
    imports and does not enforce this layout.
    
    `just python::test` runs all tests. `test-changed` is a local optimization only.
    `build` builds a wheel and source archive. `fmt` explicitly repairs formatting.
    Ruff and Pyrefly run from the same uv lock locally and in CI.
    # Data workspace
    
    Data follows the same layers as `dvc.yaml` and `pipeline.stages`:
    
    - `raw/`: versioned source snapshots and provenance.
    - `processed/`: reusable cleaned, deduplicated and enriched tables.
    - `research/`: coverage panels, study cohorts and release datasets.
    - `inputs/`: small, Git-tracked inputs to pipeline stages.
    
    Stage commands create their output directories when implemented. Git ignores
    large data payloads; track reproducible data with DVC. Keep small input files,
    `.dvc` pointer files and documentation in Git.

    title: Planning
    description: Project-owned plans and nested tasks with honest completion and local views.
    ---
    
    # Planning
    
    Create a plan, then its first task:
    
    ```bash
    just plan-new project "Project plan"
    just task-new .context/plan/project first-step "Make the first useful change"
    just sync
    ```
    
    The [root roadmap](../../ROADMAP.md) lists plans. Each plan or task shows only
    its immediate open children and counts terminal children. A deeper task lives
    in its parent's `tasks/SLUG/README.md`; its path supplies identity and parentage.
    Changing status never moves a file or breaks its links.
    
    Edit `status` in frontmatter: `backlog`, `in-progress`, `blocked`, `done` or
    `closed`. `done` requires at least one nonempty active acceptance criterion,
    all checked. Fenced examples and struck-through criteria do not count.
    `closed` stops work without claiming completion and requires `resolution.reason`.
    Terminal parents cannot retain open children. Reopen a parent before adding work.
    
    Every work item keeps one generated children region, including leaves. Edit
    outside the markers; `just sync` refreshes views, while `just check` reports
    invalid records or drift without repairing them. Put longer supporting detail
    in linked files rather than growing the 1,500-token entry point.
    # CCFinance
    
    CCFinance is a data engineering project for filtering and enriching public
    Common Crawl News (CC-News) copies for research into language in finance.
    
    ## Start
    
    Exordio supplies the Python and LaTeX toolchains, a pinned Nix environment and CI.
    Copier answers record Exordio `v0.1.1-alpha` (the documented `v0.1.0` tag was not
    available in the local source).
    
    ```bash
    bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh
    devenv shell
    just setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run stages list
    just check
    ```
    
    Shared agent instructions and Codex configuration are maintained in
    [`.agents/`](.agents/README.md). `just setup` applies them; use
    `just agents::preview` to preview link changes and `just agents::check` to
    verify the generated links.
    
    `just check` validates Justfile syntax and formatting alongside the other
    quality gates. Run `just fmt` to format Justfiles and other source files.
    
    For Python alone, with Python 3.13, uv and just installed:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::check
    ```
    
    ## Data and reproducibility
    
    DVC is initialized at the repository root with analytics disabled. Use:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc status
    just dvc dag
    ```
    
    Semflow tracks the executable Python dependencies of DVC stages. When adding a
    stage, run `just semflow-patch` to review its proposed fingerprints, then
    `just semflow-apply` to materialize them. Commit the generated
    `.semflow/hashes/` files with the DVC definition. After semantic source changes,
    run `just semflow-refresh`; `just semflow-check` detects stale fingerprints.
    The frozen [Fine News acquisition stage](data/inputs/fine-news/README.md) documents
    the staging dataset's historical selection. Keep data, configuration and
    environment dependencies explicit
    in DVC: Semflow's static analysis cannot discover string-driven dynamic imports.
    
    See [Python commands](src/python/README.md), [LaTeX commands](src/latex/README.md)
    and [infrastructure](infra/README.md). The scaffold's Apache-2.0 license covers
    code; it does not grant rights to upstream article content.
    # Architecture
    
    CCFinance separates code and research artifacts. Git stores source, configuration,
    locks, provenance definitions and documentation. DVC defines data dependencies
    and will track large data and experiment outputs once they are materialized.
    
    - `src/python/apps/pipeline` owns the CLI and data stage implementations.
    - `src/python/uv.lock` locks runtime, quality, testing, packaging and DVC tools.
    - `src/latex` owns the manuscript source and bibliography.
    - `data` holds ignored data payloads and versioned DVC pointer files.
    - `infra/nix` and `devenv.lock` own the reproducible system environment.
    
    Tach enforces module boundaries; Ruff and strict Pyrefly check Python source.
    pytest-layout-enforcer checks test file placement during collection and CI.
    Semflow fingerprints the Python code used by DVC stages, allowing DVC to
    invalidate tracked results when executable behavior changes.
    CI executes those checks, tests and builds through the same just recipes as local
    work. Setup may download dependencies; ordinary checks use cached dependencies
    and do not repair authored content. LaTeX uses a versioned Tectonic asset bundle.
    
    The Hugging Face dataset is staging, and the bucket is intended for intermediate
    and experiment artifacts. The frozen raw acquisition stage documents the
    historical selection without fetching its output. Coverage criteria, later stages
    and remote transport remain future work.
    
    Copier answers record the source and tag for future template updates. Review
    update conflicts and preserve project-specific code and configuration. The
    upstream template is [Exordio](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/exordio).

    """Prepare probability samples and acquire publisher-matched Parquet row groups."""
    
    import json
    import random
    import re
    from fnmatch import fnmatchcase
    from pathlib import Path
    from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
    from time import perf_counter
    from typing import Annotated
    
    import duckdb
    import httpx
    import typer
    import yaml
    from huggingface_hub import HfApi, hf_hub_url
    from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
    
    from pipeline.stages.raw.fine_news import (
        ENGLISH_DEFINITIONS,
        PROJECTED_COLUMNS,
        extract_group,
    )
    
    
    class DatasetInput(BaseModel):
        """A native Parquet glob at an immutable Hub commit."""
    
        model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
        source: str
    
    
    class ComparisonConfig(BaseModel):
        """Shared comparison parameters without environment-variable overrides."""
    
        model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
        seed: int
        draws: int = Field(gt=0)
        domains: Path
        datasets: dict[str, DatasetInput]
    
    
    class FileRecord(BaseModel):
        """A member of the complete eligible file inventory."""
    
        file: str
        size: int = Field(gt=0)
        identity: str
    
    
    class Draw(BaseModel):
        """One replacement draw, with half-open source row bounds."""
    
        draw: int = Field(ge=0)
        file: str
        row_group: int = Field(ge=0)
        row_start: int = Field(ge=0)
        row_stop: int = Field(gt=0)
        probability: float = Field(gt=0, le=1)
        file_size_bytes: int = Field(gt=0)
        file_row_groups: int = Field(gt=0)
        projected_bytes: int = Field(ge=0)
    
    
    class Manifest(BaseModel):
        """The source frame and every planned draw, including repeated groups."""
    
        dataset: str
        source: str
        revision: str
        seed: int
        file_count: int = Field(gt=0)
        listed_bytes: int = Field(gt=0)
        english_definition: str
        footer_bytes: int = Field(ge=0)
        draws: list[Draw] = Field(min_length=1)
    
    
    def load_config(params: Path) -> ComparisonConfig:
        """Read just the comparison section of the versioned parameters."""
        document = yaml.safe_load(params.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        return ComparisonConfig.model_validate(document["comparison"])
    
    
    def hub_path(source: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
        """Split a pinned dataset URI into repository, commit and relative path."""
        if not source.startswith("hf://datasets/"):
            raise ValueError("Expected an hf://datasets/ URI at a pinned commit")
        owner, repository, path = source.removeprefix("hf://datasets/").split("/", 2)
        name, revision = repository.rsplit("@", 1)
        if re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", revision) is None:
            raise ValueError("Source revisions must be immutable 40-character commits")
        return f"{owner}/{name}", revision, path
    
    
    def source_files(source: str) -> list[FileRecord]:
        """List native files and stored sizes without downloading their contents."""
        repository, revision, pattern = hub_path(source)
        info = HfApi(token=False).dataset_info(
            repository, revision=revision, files_metadata=True
        )
        files = []
        for entry in info.siblings or []:
            if fnmatchcase(entry.rfilename, pattern):
                if entry.size is None or entry.blob_id is None:
                    raise ValueError(f"Incomplete file metadata: {entry.rfilename}")
                files.append(
                    FileRecord(
                        file=f"hf://datasets/{repository}@{revision}/{entry.rfilename}",
                        size=entry.size,
                        identity=entry.lfs.sha256 if entry.lfs else entry.blob_id,
                    )
                )
        if not files:
            raise ValueError(f"No native Parquet files matched {source}")
        return sorted(files, key=lambda entry: entry.file)
    
    
    def check_range(file: FileRecord) -> int:
        """Verify an eight-byte range response and return the Parquet footer size."""
        repository, revision, path = hub_path(file.file)
        url = hf_hub_url(repository, path, repo_type="dataset", revision=revision)
        # Streaming prevents a server ignoring Range from returning the whole file.
        with httpx.stream(
            "GET", url, headers={"Range": "bytes=-8"}, follow_redirects=True, timeout=60
        ) as response:
            if response.status_code != 206:
                raise ValueError(f"Range reads unavailable for {file.file}")
            if response.headers.get("Content-Range") != (
                f"bytes {file.size - 8}-{file.size - 1}/{file.size}"
            ):
                raise ValueError(f"Unexpected range response for {file.file}")
            tail = response.read()
        if len(tail) != 8 or tail[4:] != b"PAR1":
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid Parquet footer for {file.file}")
        footer_bytes = int.from_bytes(tail[:4], "little") + 8
        if footer_bytes > file.size:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid footer length for {file.file}")
        return footer_bytes
    
    
    def prepare_comparison(
        dataset: Annotated[str, typer.Option(help="Dataset key in params.yaml.")],
        params: Annotated[Path, typer.Option()] = Path("params.yaml"),
        output: Annotated[Path | None, typer.Option()] = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Persist a file inventory and sampled group bounds using metadata only."""
        config = load_config(params)
        source = config.datasets[dataset].source
        columns = PROJECTED_COLUMNS[dataset]
        _, revision, _ = hub_path(source)
        output = output or Path("data/raw/source-comparison/manifests") / dataset
        if output.exists():
            raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {output}")
        files = source_files(source)
        # Stable ordering plus a separate source seed makes source additions independent.
        rng = random.Random(f"{config.seed}:{dataset}")  # noqa: S311
        draws: list[Draw] = []
        groups: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, int, int]]] = {}
        footer_bytes = 0
        output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with TemporaryDirectory(dir=output.parent) as temporary, duckdb.connect() as con:
            staging = Path(temporary) / "manifest"
            staging.mkdir()
            con.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs")
            for draw in range(config.draws):
                file = rng.choice(files)
                if file.file not in groups:
                    footer_bytes += check_range(file)
                    con.execute(
                        "CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE group_metadata AS "
                        "SELECT * FROM parquet_metadata($source)",
                        {"source": file.file},
                    )
                    con.execute(
                        "COPY group_metadata TO $target (FORMAT PARQUET)",
                        {"target": str(staging / f"metadata-{len(groups)}.parquet")},
                    )
                    rows = con.execute(
                        "SELECT row_group_id, max(row_group_num_rows), "
                        "coalesce(sum(total_compressed_size) FILTER (WHERE "
                        "trim(split_part(path_in_schema, ',', 1)) IN "
                        "(SELECT unnest($columns))), 0) "
                        "FROM group_metadata GROUP BY row_group_id ORDER BY row_group_id",
                        {"columns": list(columns)},
                    ).fetchall()
                    start = 0
                    groups[file.file] = []
                    for group_id, count, size in rows:
                        stop = start + int(count)
                        groups[file.file].append((int(group_id), start, stop, int(size)))
                        start = stop
                    if not groups[file.file]:
                        raise ValueError(f"No row groups in {file.file}")
                choices = groups[file.file]
                group_id, start, stop, size = rng.choice(choices)
                draws.append(
                    Draw(
                        draw=draw,
                        file=file.file,
                        row_group=group_id,
                        row_start=start,
                        row_stop=stop,
                        probability=1 / (len(files) * len(choices)),
                        file_size_bytes=file.size,
                        file_row_groups=len(choices),
                        projected_bytes=size,
                    )
                )
            manifest = Manifest(
                dataset=dataset,
                source=source,
                revision=revision,
                seed=config.seed,
                file_count=len(files),
                listed_bytes=sum(file.size for file in files),
                english_definition=ENGLISH_DEFINITIONS[dataset],
                footer_bytes=footer_bytes,
                draws=draws,
            )
            (staging / "manifest.json").write_text(
                manifest.model_dump_json(indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
            )
            (staging / "files.json").write_text(
                json.dumps([file.model_dump() for file in files], indent=2) + "\n",
                encoding="utf-8",
            )
            staging.rename(output)
        unique = {(draw.file, draw.row_group): draw for draw in draws}
        typer.echo(
            f"{dataset}: {len(unique)} unique groups, "
            f"{sum(draw.row_stop - draw.row_start for draw in unique.values()):,} rows; "
            f"projected chunks {sum(draw.projected_bytes for draw in unique.values()):,} "
            f"bytes; footers {footer_bytes:,} bytes. Article data not acquired."
        )
    
    
    def sample_comparison(
        dataset: Annotated[str, typer.Option(help="Dataset key in params.yaml.")],
        params: Annotated[Path, typer.Option()] = Path("params.yaml"),
        manifest: Annotated[Path | None, typer.Option()] = None,
        output: Annotated[Path | None, typer.Option()] = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Acquire the prepared groups and retain English publisher-matched records."""
        config = load_config(params)
        manifest = manifest or (
            Path("data/raw/source-comparison/manifests") / dataset / "manifest.json"
        )
        selection = Manifest.model_validate_json(manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if selection.dataset != dataset or selection.source != config.datasets[dataset].source:
            raise ValueError("Manifest does not describe the configured dataset snapshot")
        if selection.seed != config.seed or len(selection.draws) != config.draws:
            raise ValueError("Sampling parameters changed; prepare a new manifest")
        output = output or Path("data/raw/source-comparison/samples") / dataset
        if output.exists():
            raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {output}")
        output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        counts: list[dict[str, int]] = []
        cached: dict[tuple[str, int], dict[str, int]] = {}
        started = perf_counter()
        with TemporaryDirectory(dir=output.parent) as temporary, duckdb.connect() as con:
            staging = Path(temporary) / "sample"
            staging.mkdir()
            con.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs")
            for draw in selection.draws:
                key = (draw.file, draw.row_group)
                if key not in cached:
                    check_range(FileRecord(file=draw.file, size=draw.file_size_bytes, identity=""))
                    cached[key] = extract_group(
                        con,
                        dataset,
                        draw.file,
                        draw.row_start,
                        draw.row_stop,
                        config.domains,
                        staging / f"group-{draw.draw}.parquet",
                    )
                    if cached[key]["input_rows"] != draw.row_stop - draw.row_start:
                        raise ValueError("Acquired row count differs from the prepared group")
                counts.append({"draw": draw.draw, **cached[key]})
            report = {
                "dataset": dataset,
                "draws": counts,
                "elapsed_seconds": perf_counter() - started,
                "output_bytes": sum(path.stat().st_size for path in staging.glob("*.parquet")),
                "network_bytes": None,
            }
            (staging / "counts.json").write_text(
                json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
            )
            staging.rename(output)
        typer.echo(f"Wrote {dataset}: {len(cached)} unique groups -> {output}")

    """Select publisher records from Fine News and comparison source row groups."""
    
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
    from typing import Annotated
    
    import duckdb
    import typer
    from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
    
    
    def _hostname(host: str, url: str) -> str:
        """Build the shared normalization for explicit source projection expressions."""
        return f"""lower(rtrim(trim(coalesce(
            nullif(trim({host}), ''),
            regexp_extract({url}, '(?i)^https?://([^/:?#]+)', 1)
        )), '.'))"""
    
    
    PUBLISHER_MATCH = """
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM read_csv($domains, header=true) AS d
            WHERE hostname = lower(rtrim(trim(d.domain), '.'))
               OR ends_with(hostname, '.' || lower(rtrim(trim(d.domain), '.')))
        )
    """
    
    QUERY = f"""
            WITH articles AS (
                SELECT text, id, metadata,
                    {_hostname("metadata.url_hostname", "metadata.url")} AS hostname
                FROM read_parquet($source)
            )
            SELECT text, id, metadata FROM articles
            WHERE {PUBLISHER_MATCH}
    """  # noqa: S608 - only authored expressions compose this query.
    
    # These roots match the native columns read by the projections below. Preparation
    # uses their compressed column chunks to estimate payload bytes before acquisition.
    PROJECTED_COLUMNS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {
        "fine_news": ("text", "id", "metadata"),
        "infini_news": (
            "text",
            "url",
            "url_hostname",
            "warc_record_id",
            "warc_filename",
            "warc_date",
            "publish_date",
            "title",
            "author",
            "sitename",
            "categories",
            "tags",
            "description",
            "language",
            "language_score",
        ),
        "refinedweb": ("content", "url", "timestamp", "dump", "segment"),
        "fineweb_hq": (
            "text",
            "id",
            "date",
            "dump",
            "file_path",
            "language",
            "language_score",
            "token_count",
            "url",
            "quality_score",
        ),
    }
    
    ENGLISH_DEFINITIONS: dict[str, str] = {
        "fine_news": "Files in the source's eng_Latn directories.",
        "infini_news": "Records whose native language label equals eng_Latn.",
        "refinedweb": "The source release declares its records to be English.",
        "fineweb_hq": "Records whose native language label equals en.",
    }
    
    _PROJECTIONS = {
        "fine_news": f"""text, id, metadata, true AS _english,
            {_hostname("metadata.url_hostname", "metadata.url")} AS hostname""",
        "infini_news": f"""text, warc_record_id AS id,
            struct_pack(url, url_hostname, warc_record_id, warc_filename, warc_date,
                publish_date, title, author, sitename, categories, tags, description,
                language, language_score) AS metadata,
            language = 'eng_Latn' AS _english,
            {_hostname("url_hostname", "url")} AS hostname""",
        "refinedweb": f"""content AS text, NULL::VARCHAR AS id,
            struct_pack(url, timestamp, dump, segment) AS metadata,
            true AS _english, {_hostname("NULL", "url")} AS hostname""",
        "fineweb_hq": f"""text, id,
            struct_pack(date, dump, file_path, language, language_score, token_count,
                url, quality_score) AS metadata,
            language = 'en' AS _english,
            {_hostname("NULL", "url")} AS hostname""",
    }
    
    
    def _write_parquet(
        con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection,
        query: str,
        parameters: dict[str, object],
        target: Path,
    ) -> None:
        """Publish a complete Parquet output without replacing an existing file."""
        if target.exists():
            raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {target}")
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with TemporaryDirectory(dir=target.parent) as staging:
            temporary = Path(staging) / "articles.parquet"
            con.execute(
                f"COPY ({query}) TO $target "
                "(FORMAT PARQUET, COMPRESSION ZSTD, COMPRESSION_LEVEL 9, "
                "ROW_GROUP_SIZE 16384)",
                {**parameters, "target": str(temporary)},
            )
            os.link(temporary, target)
    
    
    def extract_group(
        con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection,
        dataset: str,
        source: str,
        row_start: int,
        row_stop: int,
        domains: Path,
        target: Path,
    ) -> dict[str, int]:
        """Read one row interval once and retain its English publisher records.
    
        Bounds are zero-based and stop-exclusive. Restricting the virtual Parquet
        row number at the scan enables remote row-group pruning. The temporary table
        preserves the selected input for counts and copying without a second read.
        """
        if row_start < 0 or row_stop <= row_start:
            raise ValueError("A nonempty, nonnegative row interval is required.")
        if target.exists():
            raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {target}")
        projection = _PROJECTIONS[dataset]
        con.execute(
            f"""CREATE TEMP TABLE comparison_group AS
            SELECT {projection}, $source AS source_file, file_row_number AS source_row
            FROM read_parquet($source, file_row_number=true, hive_partitioning=false)
            WHERE file_row_number >= $row_start AND file_row_number < $row_stop
            """,  # noqa: S608 - projection comes from the fixed source registry.
            {"source": source, "row_start": row_start, "row_stop": row_stop},
        )
        try:
            counts = con.execute(
                f"""SELECT count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE _english),
                    count(*) FILTER (WHERE _english AND {PUBLISHER_MATCH})
                    FROM comparison_group""",  # noqa: S608 - authored predicate.
                {"domains": str(domains)},
            ).fetchone()
            if counts is None or counts[0] != row_stop - row_start:
                raise ValueError("The selected row interval differs from its manifest.")
            _write_parquet(
                con,
                f"""SELECT * EXCLUDE (_english, hostname) FROM comparison_group
                    WHERE _english AND {PUBLISHER_MATCH}""",  # noqa: S608
                {"domains": str(domains)},
                target,
            )
            return dict(
                zip(("input_rows", "english_rows", "matched_rows"), counts, strict=True)
            )
        finally:
            con.execute("DROP TABLE comparison_group")
    
    
    class FineNewsConfig(BaseModel):
        """Versioned inputs and output for the Fine News selection."""
    
        model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    
        source: str
        domains: Path
        output: Path
    
    
    def filter_fine_news(
        config: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="Historical acquisition configuration.")
        ] = Path("data/inputs/fine-news/acquisition.json"),
    ) -> None:
        """Select English publisher shards from a pinned Fine News revision."""
        settings = FineNewsConfig.model_validate_json(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        target = settings.output / "articles.parquet"
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            if settings.source.startswith("hf://"):
                con.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs")
            _write_parquet(
                con,
                QUERY,
                {"source": settings.source, "domains": str(settings.domains)},
                target,
            )
        typer.echo(f"Wrote: {settings.source} -> {target}")
    """Estimate publisher-filter yield from independently drawn source row groups."""
    
    import csv
    import json
    import math
    import os
    from collections.abc import Sequence
    from pathlib import Path
    from statistics import fmean
    from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
    from typing import Annotated, Self
    
    import typer
    from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, model_validator
    from scipy.stats import t
    
    DATASETS = ("fine_news", "infini_news", "refinedweb", "fineweb_hq")
    type Metric = int | float | None
    
    
    class SelectedGroup(BaseModel):
        """One probability draw, including repeated selections of the same group."""
    
        draw: int = Field(ge=0)
        file: str
        row_group: int = Field(ge=0)
        row_start: int = Field(ge=0)
        row_stop: int = Field(gt=0)
        probability: float = Field(gt=0, le=1, allow_inf_nan=False)
        file_row_groups: int = Field(gt=0)
        projected_bytes: int = Field(ge=0)
    
    
    class ComparisonManifest(BaseModel):
        """The pinned population frame and the selected Parquet row groups."""
    
        dataset: str
        source: str
        revision: str
        seed: int
        file_count: int = Field(gt=0)
        listed_bytes: int = Field(ge=0)
        english_definition: str
        draws: list[SelectedGroup] = Field(min_length=1)
    
    
    class DrawCounts(BaseModel):
        """Nested record counts from one selected group before and after filtering."""
    
        draw: int = Field(ge=0)
        input_rows: int = Field(ge=0)
        english_rows: int = Field(ge=0)
        matched_rows: int = Field(ge=0)
    
        @model_validator(mode="after")
        def validate_counts(self) -> Self:
            """Require retained publisher records to be a subset of English records."""
            if not self.matched_rows <= self.english_rows <= self.input_rows:
                raise ValueError("Counts must satisfy matched <= English <= input rows")
            return self
    
    
    class SampleCounts(BaseModel):
        """Acquisition counts with physical sizes measured once per unique group."""
    
        dataset: str
        draws: list[DrawCounts] = Field(min_length=1)
        elapsed_seconds: float = Field(ge=0, allow_inf_nan=False)
        output_bytes: int = Field(ge=0)
        network_bytes: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)
    
    
    def _estimate(
        values: Sequence[float], critical: float, maximum: float | None = None
    ) -> dict[str, float | None]:
        mean = fmean(values)
        variance = (
            sum((value - mean) ** 2 for value in values) / (len(values) * (len(values) - 1))
            if len(values) > 1
            else 0.0
        )
        standard_error = math.sqrt(variance) if variance > 0 else None
        return {
            "estimate": mean,
            "standard_error": standard_error,
            "ci95_low": max(0.0, mean - critical * standard_error)
            if standard_error is not None
            else None,
            "ci95_high": min(maximum, mean + critical * standard_error)
            if standard_error is not None and maximum is not None
            else mean + critical * standard_error
            if standard_error is not None
            else None,
        }
    
    
    def estimate_population(
        probabilities: Sequence[float],
        english_counts: Sequence[int],
        matched_counts: Sequence[int],
    ) -> dict[str, float | None]:
        """Estimate totals and a yield ratio using all with-replacement draws.
    
        Each group contributes its count divided by its draw probability. Totals
        use Hansen-Hurwitz means; the ratio uses a linearized standard error.
        Missing or zero between-draw variation cannot establish precision.
        """
        if not probabilities or not (
            len(probabilities) == len(english_counts) == len(matched_counts)
        ):
            raise ValueError("Probabilities and counts must have equal nonzero lengths")
        if any(not math.isfinite(q) or not 0 < q <= 1 for q in probabilities):
            raise ValueError("Draw probabilities must be finite and in (0, 1]")
        if any(
            not 0 <= y <= n for n, y in zip(english_counts, matched_counts, strict=True)
        ):
            raise ValueError("Counts must satisfy 0 <= matched <= English")
        english = [n / q for n, q in zip(english_counts, probabilities, strict=True)]
        matched = [y / q for y, q in zip(matched_counts, probabilities, strict=True)]
        critical = (
            float(t.ppf(0.975, len(probabilities) - 1)) if len(probabilities) > 1 else 0.0
        )
        estimates: dict[str, float | None] = {}
        for prefix, values in (
            ("english_records", english),
            ("publisher_records", matched),
        ):
            estimates.update(
                {
                    f"estimated_{prefix}_{key}": value
                    for key, value in _estimate(values, critical).items()
                }
            )
        denominator = fmean(english)
        ratio = fmean(matched) / denominator if denominator else None
        estimates["estimated_publisher_yield"] = ratio
        if ratio is not None:
            residuals = [
                (y - ratio * n) / denominator for n, y in zip(english, matched, strict=True)
            ]
            uncertainty = _estimate(residuals, critical)
            standard_error = uncertainty["standard_error"]
        else:
            standard_error = None
        estimates.update(
            estimated_publisher_yield_standard_error=standard_error,
            estimated_publisher_yield_ci95_low=max(0.0, ratio - critical * standard_error)
            if ratio is not None and standard_error is not None
            else None,
            estimated_publisher_yield_ci95_high=min(1.0, ratio + critical * standard_error)
            if ratio is not None and standard_error is not None
            else None,
        )
        return estimates
    
    
    def _summarize(
        manifest: ComparisonManifest, sample: SampleCounts
    ) -> tuple[dict[str, Metric], dict[str, str | int]]:
        if manifest.dataset != sample.dataset:
            raise ValueError("Manifest and acquisition dataset identifiers differ")
        draw_ids = {draw.draw for draw in manifest.draws}
        count_ids = {draw.draw for draw in sample.draws}
        if (
            len(draw_ids) != len(manifest.draws)
            or len(count_ids) != len(sample.draws)
            or draw_ids != count_ids
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "Manifest and acquisition need matching, unique draw identifiers"
            )
        counts = {draw.draw: draw for draw in sample.draws}
        unique: dict[tuple[str, int], tuple[SelectedGroup, DrawCounts]] = {}
        ordered_counts = []
        for draw in manifest.draws:
            count = counts[draw.draw]
            if count.input_rows != draw.row_stop - draw.row_start:
                raise ValueError("Acquired row count differs from the selected row bounds")
            if draw.row_group >= draw.file_row_groups or not math.isclose(
                draw.probability, 1 / (manifest.file_count * draw.file_row_groups)
            ):
                raise ValueError(
                    "Draw probability differs from the declared sampling design"
                )
            key = (draw.file, draw.row_group)
            if key in unique:
                earlier, earlier_count = unique[key]
                if draw.model_dump(exclude={"draw"}) != earlier.model_dump(
                    exclude={"draw"}
                ):
                    raise ValueError(
                        "Repeated group selections contain inconsistent metadata"
                    )
                if count.model_dump(exclude={"draw"}) != earlier_count.model_dump(
                    exclude={"draw"}
                ):
                    raise ValueError(
                        "Repeated group selections contain inconsistent counts"
                    )
            unique[key] = (draw, count)
            ordered_counts.append(count)
        english_rows = sum(count.english_rows for _, count in unique.values())
        matched_rows = sum(count.matched_rows for _, count in unique.values())
        metrics: dict[str, Metric] = {
            "population_files": manifest.file_count,
            "population_listed_bytes": manifest.listed_bytes,
            "draws": len(manifest.draws),
            "selected_files": len({draw.file for draw in manifest.draws}),
            "selected_groups": len(unique),
            "sampled_input_rows": sum(count.input_rows for _, count in unique.values()),
            "sampled_english_rows": english_rows,
            "sampled_matched_rows": matched_rows,
            "observed_publisher_yield": matched_rows / english_rows
            if english_rows
            else None,
            "projected_column_bytes": sum(
                draw.projected_bytes for draw, _ in unique.values()
            ),
            "elapsed_seconds": sample.elapsed_seconds,
            "output_bytes": sample.output_bytes,
            "network_bytes": sample.network_bytes,
        }
        metrics.update(
            estimate_population(
                [draw.probability for draw in manifest.draws],
                [count.english_rows for count in ordered_counts],
                [count.matched_rows for count in ordered_counts],
            )
        )
        details = {
            "source": manifest.source,
            "revision": manifest.revision,
            "english_definition": manifest.english_definition,
            "seed": manifest.seed,
            "degrees_of_freedom": len(manifest.draws) - 1,
            "uncertainty_status": "exploratory"
            if metrics["estimated_publisher_yield_standard_error"] is not None
            else "insufficient_evidence",
        }
        return metrics, details
    
    
    def compare_sources(
        manifests: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="Prepared manifests for all four comparison sources.")
        ] = Path("data/raw/source-comparison/manifests"),
        samples: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="Acquisition counts for all four comparison sources.")
        ] = Path("data/raw/source-comparison/samples"),
        output: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="New directory for the comparison table and metrics.")
        ] = Path("data/research/source-comparison"),
    ) -> None:
        """Compare observed retention and exploratory population estimates."""
        if output.exists():
            raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {output}")
        metrics = {}
        details = {}
        for dataset in DATASETS:
            manifest = ComparisonManifest.model_validate_json(
                (manifests / dataset / "manifest.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            )
            sample = SampleCounts.model_validate_json(
                (samples / dataset / "counts.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            )
            if manifest.dataset != dataset:
                raise ValueError(f"Manifest dataset differs from its directory: {dataset}")
            metrics[dataset], details[dataset] = _summarize(manifest, sample)
        methods = {
            "estimand": "English source records retained by the publisher filter",
            "design": "Independent uniform file and row-group draws with replacement",
            "totals": "Hansen-Hurwitz mean of count / draw probability",
            "yield": "Estimated publisher-matched records / estimated English records",
            "uncertainty": "Exploratory Student t intervals; linearized yield variance",
            "interval_bounds": "Nonnegative totals; yield intervals bounded to [0, 1]",
            "missing_uncertainty": (
                "Fewer than two draws, zero matches, or zero between-draw variance"
            ),
            "physical_counts": "Observed counts count each unique selected group once",
            "repeated_draws": "Population estimates retain repeated selections",
            "size_scope": (
                "Eligible-file bytes include non-English rows in multilingual files"
            ),
            "transfer_scope": (
                "Projected compressed column bytes exclude HTTP overhead and footers; "
                "network bytes require measurement"
            ),
            "limitations": [
                "Four cluster draws poorly characterize rare or uneven publisher matches",
                "Records do not establish unique articles or incremental source coverage",
                "Publisher retention does not establish research eligibility or coverage",
                "Native English labels and release scopes differ between sources",
            ],
            "sources": details,
        }
        output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with TemporaryDirectory(dir=output.parent) as temporary:
            staging = Path(temporary) / "report"
            staging.mkdir()
            for name, payload in (("metrics.json", metrics), ("methods.json", methods)):
                (staging / name).write_text(
                    json.dumps(payload, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
                )
            rows = [
                {"dataset": dataset, **details[dataset], **metrics[dataset]}
                for dataset in DATASETS
            ]
            with (staging / "comparison.csv").open(
                "w", encoding="utf-8", newline=""
            ) as handle:
                writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
                writer.writeheader()
                writer.writerows(rows)
            os.rename(staging, output)
        typer.echo(f"Wrote comparison for {len(DATASETS)} sources: {output}")
    .github/workflows/ci.yml
    .github/workflows/security.yml
    name: CI
    on:
      pull_request:
        types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, ready_for_review, converted_to_draft]
      push:
        branches: [main]
      workflow_dispatch:
    permissions:
      contents: read
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    jobs:
      check:
        # Draft PRs emit a skipped run; compute-heavy checks only run when ready.
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.draft == false }}
        env:
          TECTONIC_CACHE_DIR: /tmp/exordio-tectonic-cache
        strategy:
          matrix:
            runner: [ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-24.04-arm]
        runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262
            with:
              persist-credentials: false
          - name: Free hosted runner disk space
            run: |
              df -h /
              sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /usr/local/share/powershell /opt/ghc
              df -h /
          # cache-nix-action requires a store writable by the runner user.
          - uses: nixbuild/nix-quick-install-action@9f63be77f412a248c9d9a65a4c82cf066cdf8f0c # v35
            with:
              nix_version: 2.34.7
          - uses: nix-community/cache-nix-action@135667ec418502fa5a3598af6fb9eb733888ce6a
            if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
            with:
              primary-key: nix-single-user-v1-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('devenv.lock', 'devenv.nix', 'infra/nix/**') }}
              restore-prefixes-first-match: nix-single-user-v1-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
          - uses: actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830
            if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
            with:
              path: |
                ~/.cache/uv
                ${{ env.TECTONIC_CACHE_DIR }}
                ~/.cache/mathlib
                ~/.bun/install/cache
              key: tools-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('**/uv.lock', '**/*.py.lock', '**/bun.lock', '**/lake-manifest.json') }}
          - name: Install matching devenv
            run: bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh
          - name: Prepare dependencies
            run: devenv shell -- just setup
          - name: Validate
            run: devenv shell -- just check

    """Verify bounded source projections against native local Parquet layouts."""
    
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import duckdb
    import pytest
    from pipeline.stages.raw.fine_news import extract_group
    
    
    @pytest.mark.integration
    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        ("dataset", "projection", "english_rows", "expected_rows"),
        [
            (
                "fine_news",
                """text, i::VARCHAR AS id,
                    struct_pack(url, url_hostname, title := 'headline') AS metadata,
                    ['excluded media'] AS media""",
                4,
                [1, 3, 4],
            ),
            (
                "infini_news",
                """text, url, url_hostname, i::VARCHAR AS warc_record_id,
                    'crawl.warc.gz' AS warc_filename, '2020-01-01' AS warc_date,
                    '2020-01-01' AS publish_date, 'headline' AS title,
                    'reporter' AS author, 'publisher' AS sitename,
                    ['finance'] AS categories, ['markets'] AS tags,
                    'description' AS description,
                    CASE WHEN i = 4 THEN 'fra_Latn' ELSE 'eng_Latn' END AS language,
                    0.9 AS language_score""",
                3,
                [1, 3],
            ),
            (
                "refinedweb",
                """text AS content, url, '2020-01-01' AS timestamp,
                    'CC-MAIN-2020-05' AS dump, 'segment' AS segment,
                    ['excluded image'] AS image_urls""",
                4,
                [1, 3, 4],
            ),
            (
                "fineweb_hq",
                """text, i::VARCHAR AS id, url, '2020-01-01' AS date,
                    'CC-MAIN-2020-05' AS dump, 'source.warc.gz' AS file_path,
                    CASE WHEN i = 4 THEN 'fr' ELSE 'en' END AS language,
                    0.9 AS language_score, 10 AS token_count, 0.8 AS quality_score,
                    [[0.5, 0.4]] AS embeddings""",
                3,
                [1, 3],
            ),
        ],
        ids=["fine_news", "infini_news", "refinedweb", "fineweb_hq"],
    )
    def test_group_preserves_native_metadata_and_source_rows(
        tmp_path: Path,
        dataset: str,
        projection: str,
        english_rows: int,
        expected_rows: list[int],
    ) -> None:
        # Arrange: each native layout contains excluded rows around the interval.
        source = tmp_path / "source.parquet"
        target = tmp_path / "articles.parquet"
        domains = tmp_path / "domains.csv"
        domains.write_text("domain\nEXAMPLE.COM.\n", encoding="utf-8")
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            con.execute(
                f"""COPY (
                    WITH native AS (
                        SELECT i, 'article-' || i AS text,
                            CASE WHEN i = 2 THEN 'https://notexample.com/a'
                                ELSE 'https://News.Example.COM./a' END AS url,
                            CASE WHEN i = 2 THEN 'notexample.com'
                                WHEN i = 3 THEN ''
                                ELSE 'News.Example.COM.' END AS url_hostname
                        FROM range(6) AS rows(i)
                    ) SELECT {projection} FROM native
                ) TO $target (FORMAT PARQUET)""",  # noqa: S608 - fixed test cases.
                {"target": str(source)},
            )
    
            # Act: materialize and filter exactly rows one through four.
            counts = extract_group(con, dataset, str(source), 1, 5, domains, target)
            result = con.execute(
                "SELECT text, id, metadata.url, source_file, source_row "
                "FROM read_parquet(?) ORDER BY source_row",
                [str(target)],
            ).fetchall()
            columns = con.execute("DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM read_parquet(?)", [str(target)])
            column_names = [row[0] for row in columns.fetchall()]
    
        # Assert: language filtering, counts, payload and provenance agree.
        assert counts == {
            "input_rows": 4,
            "english_rows": english_rows,
            "matched_rows": len(expected_rows),
        }
        assert result == [
            (
                f"article-{i}",
                None if dataset == "refinedweb" else str(i),
                "https://News.Example.COM./a",
                str(source),
                i,
            )
            for i in expected_rows
        ]
        assert column_names == ["text", "id", "metadata", "source_file", "source_row"]
    """Check probability weighting, uncertainty and complete comparison reports."""
    
    import json
    import math
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import pytest
    from hypothesis import given
    from hypothesis import strategies as st
    from hypothesis.strategies import DrawFn
    from pipeline.stages.research.source_comparison import (
        DATASETS,
        compare_sources,
        estimate_population,
    )
    
    
    @st.composite
    def group_counts(draw: DrawFn) -> tuple[int, int]:
        rows = draw(st.integers(min_value=1, max_value=100))
        matches = draw(st.integers(min_value=0, max_value=rows))
        return rows, matches
    
    
    @pytest.mark.unit
    @given(
        st.lists(st.lists(group_counts(), min_size=1, max_size=3), min_size=1, max_size=3)
    )
    def test_probability_weighting_recovers_frame_totals(
        files: list[list[tuple[int, int]]],
    ) -> None:
        # Arrange: a finite population whose files have unequal numbers of groups.
        expected_english = sum(rows for groups in files for rows, _ in groups)
        expected_matches = sum(matches for groups in files for _, matches in groups)
        expected_estimates = {"english_records": 0.0, "publisher_records": 0.0}
    
        # Act: enumerate every possible one-draw outcome and its known probability.
        for groups in files:
            probability = 1 / (len(files) * len(groups))
            for rows, matches in groups:
                estimates = estimate_population([probability], [rows], [matches])
                for name in expected_estimates:
                    value = estimates[f"estimated_{name}_estimate"]
                    assert value is not None
                    expected_estimates[name] += probability * value
    
        # Assert: expected estimated totals equal the independently counted population.
        assert expected_estimates["english_records"] == pytest.approx(expected_english)
        assert expected_estimates["publisher_records"] == pytest.approx(expected_matches)
    
    
    @pytest.mark.unit
    def test_unequal_weights_use_draw_variation_for_uncertainty() -> None:
        # Arrange: four draws with weighted English counts 100, 100, 300 and 200.
        probabilities = [0.1, 0.2, 0.1, 0.2]
        english = [10, 20, 30, 40]
        matched = [1, 4, 3, 8]
    
        # Act: estimate totals, the ratio and uncertainty across the four draws.
        estimates = estimate_population(probabilities, english, matched)
    
        # Assert: independently calculated totals and linearized errors are recovered.
        assert estimates["estimated_english_records_estimate"] == 175
        assert estimates["estimated_publisher_records_estimate"] == 25
        assert estimates["estimated_publisher_records_standard_error"] == pytest.approx(
            math.sqrt(125 / 3)
        )
        assert estimates["estimated_publisher_yield"] == pytest.approx(1 / 7)
        assert estimates["estimated_publisher_yield_standard_error"] == pytest.approx(
            math.sqrt(17000 / (49 * 12 * 175**2))
        )
        standard_error = math.sqrt(125 / 3)
        assert estimates["estimated_publisher_records_ci95_high"] == pytest.approx(
            25 + 3.182446305284263 * standard_error
        )
    
    
    @pytest.mark.unit
    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        ("probabilities", "english", "matched", "expected_yield"),
        [
            ([0.25] * 4, [10] * 4, [0] * 4, 0.0),
            ([0.25] * 4, [10] * 4, [2] * 4, 0.2),
            ([1.0], [0], [0], None),
            ([0.5], [10], [2], 0.2),
        ],
    )
    def test_insufficient_variation_does_not_claim_precision(
        probabilities: list[float],
        english: list[int],
        matched: list[int],
        expected_yield: float | None,
    ) -> None:
        # Arrange: no matches, identical groups, an empty denominator or a single draw.
    
        # Act: retain point estimates while estimating available uncertainty.
        estimates = estimate_population(probabilities, english, matched)
    
        # Assert: missing evidence produces null intervals, never zero-width intervals.
        assert estimates["estimated_publisher_yield"] == expected_yield
        assert estimates["estimated_publisher_records_standard_error"] is None
        assert estimates["estimated_publisher_yield_standard_error"] is None
        assert estimates["estimated_publisher_yield_ci95_low"] is None
        assert estimates["estimated_publisher_yield_ci95_high"] is None
    
    
    def _write_comparison_inputs(root: Path) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
        manifests = root / "manifests"
        samples = root / "samples"
        for dataset in DATASETS:
            draws = []
            counts = []
            for draw, (file, rows, matches) in enumerate(
                [
                    ("a.parquet", 10, 1),
                    ("b.parquet", 20, 6),
                    ("b.parquet", 20, 6),
                    ("b.parquet", 20, 6),
                ]
            ):
                draws.append(
                    {
                        "draw": draw,
                        "file": file,
                        "row_group": 0,
                        "row_start": 0,
                        "row_stop": rows,
                        "probability": 0.5,
                        "file_row_groups": 1,
                        "projected_bytes": 100,
                    }
                )
                counts.append(
                    {
                        "draw": draw,
                        "input_rows": rows,
                        "english_rows": rows,
                        "matched_rows": matches,
                    }
                )
            manifest_dir = manifests / dataset
            manifest_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
            (manifest_dir / "manifest.json").write_text(
                json.dumps(
                    {
                        "dataset": dataset,
                        "source": "hf://datasets/example/source@revision/data/*.parquet",
                        "revision": "revision",
                        "seed": 42,
                        "file_count": 2,
                        "listed_bytes": 400,
                        "english_definition": "English release",
                        "draws": draws,
                    }
                ),
                encoding="utf-8",
            )
            sample_dir = samples / dataset
            sample_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
            (sample_dir / "counts.json").write_text(
                json.dumps(
                    {
                        "dataset": dataset,
                        "draws": counts,
                        "elapsed_seconds": 0.1,
                        "output_bytes": 50,
                        "network_bytes": None,
                    }
                ),
                encoding="utf-8",
            )
        return manifests, samples
    
    
    @pytest.mark.integration
    def test_report_keeps_repeated_draws_but_counts_acquisition_once(
        tmp_path: Path,
    ) -> None:
        # Arrange: each source draws group A once and group B three times.
        manifests, samples = _write_comparison_inputs(tmp_path)
        output = tmp_path / "report"
    
        # Act: publish all source estimates and their methods together.
        compare_sources(manifests, samples, output)
    
        # Assert: physical counts use two groups; weighted estimates keep all four draws.
        metrics = json.loads((output / "metrics.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        assert set(metrics) == set(DATASETS)
        for source in metrics.values():
            assert source["draws"] == 4
            assert source["selected_groups"] == 2
            assert source["sampled_input_rows"] == 30
            assert source["sampled_matched_rows"] == 7
            assert source["projected_column_bytes"] == 200
            assert source["observed_publisher_yield"] == pytest.approx(7 / 30)
            assert source["estimated_english_records_estimate"] == 35
            assert source["estimated_publisher_records_estimate"] == 9.5
            assert source["estimated_publisher_yield"] == pytest.approx(9.5 / 35)
            assert source["network_bytes"] is None
        methods = json.loads((output / "methods.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        assert methods["sources"]["fine_news"]["degrees_of_freedom"] == 3
        assert (
            len((output / "comparison.csv").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()) == 5
        )
    
    
    @pytest.mark.integration
    def test_missing_source_cannot_publish_partial_comparison(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        # Arrange: omit one required source's acquisition results.
        manifests, samples = _write_comparison_inputs(tmp_path)
        (samples / DATASETS[-1] / "counts.json").unlink()
        output = tmp_path / "report"
    
        # Act: attempt to publish a comparison with incomplete evidence.
        with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
            compare_sources(manifests, samples, output)
    
        # Assert: no report directory or partial metrics were published.
        assert not output.exists()

    """Exercise metadata preparation and duplicate-safe acquisition locally."""
    
    import json
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import duckdb
    import pytest
    import yaml
    from pipeline.cli import app
    from pipeline.stages.raw import source_comparison
    from pipeline.stages.raw.source_comparison import FileRecord
    from typer.testing import CliRunner
    
    
    @pytest.mark.integration
    def test_prepared_groups_drive_acquisition_without_duplicate_payloads(
        tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
    ) -> None:
        # Arrange: two groups force repeated draws; mock only the remote inventory.
        source = tmp_path / "source.parquet"
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            con.execute(
                """COPY (SELECT i::VARCHAR AS id, 'article-' || i AS text,
                    struct_pack(url_hostname := 'example.com',
                        url := 'https://example.com/' || i) AS metadata,
                    repeat('excluded media', 100) AS media
                    FROM range(4096) AS rows(i)) TO $target
                    (FORMAT PARQUET, ROW_GROUP_SIZE 2048)""",
                {"target": str(source)},
            )
        domains = tmp_path / "domains.csv"
        domains.write_text("domain\nexample.com\n", encoding="utf-8")
        params = tmp_path / "params.yaml"
        params.write_text(
            yaml.safe_dump(
                {
                    "comparison": {
                        "seed": 42,
                        "draws": 4,
                        "domains": str(domains),
                        "datasets": {
                            "fine_news": {
                                "source": "hf://datasets/example/source@"
                                + "0" * 40
                                + "/data/*.parquet"
                            }
                        },
                    }
                }
            ),
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        monkeypatch.setattr(
            source_comparison,
            "source_files",
            lambda _: [FileRecord(file=str(source), size=source.stat().st_size, identity="x")],
        )
        monkeypatch.setattr(source_comparison, "check_range", lambda _: 8)
        manifests = tmp_path / "manifest"
        samples = tmp_path / "sample"
        runner = CliRunner()
    
        # Act: prepare through the public CLI, then acquire only its planned intervals.
        prepared = runner.invoke(
            app,
            [
                "stages", "raw", "prepare-comparison", "--dataset", "fine_news",
                "--params", str(params), "--output", str(manifests),
            ],
        )
        assert prepared.exit_code == 0, prepared.output
        acquired = runner.invoke(
            app,
            [
                "stages", "raw", "sample-comparison", "--dataset", "fine_news",
                "--params", str(params), "--manifest", str(manifests / "manifest.json"),
                "--output", str(samples),
            ],
        )
    
        # Assert: probabilities and physical payloads preserve the replacement design.
        assert acquired.exit_code == 0, acquired.output
        selection = json.loads((manifests / "manifest.json").read_text())
        counts = json.loads((samples / "counts.json").read_text())
        assert len(selection["draws"]) == len(counts["draws"]) == 4
        assert all(draw["probability"] == 0.5 for draw in selection["draws"])
        unique = {draw["row_group"] for draw in selection["draws"]}
        assert len(list(samples.glob("*.parquet"))) == len(unique)
        assert all(draw["input_rows"] == draw["matched_rows"] == 2048
                   for draw in counts["draws"])
        assert counts["network_bytes"] is None
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            rows, distinct_rows = con.execute(
                "SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT source_row) FROM read_parquet(?)",
                [str(samples / "*.parquet")],
            ).fetchone()
        assert rows == distinct_rows == 2048 * len(unique)

    # Publisher-filter sampling methods
    
    ## Population and outcome
    
    The experiment estimates English source records retained by the historical
    115-domain allowlist, including subdomains. Each configured commit and native
    Parquet glob defines a finite source frame. Fine News uses its English files;
    Infini News uses its inline `eng_Latn` label; FineWeb-HQ uses `en`; RefinedWeb
    declares its release English. These source-specific definitions are recorded,
    not independently validated language labels.
    
    The outcome is publisher retention. Dates, tickers, financial relevance and
    article quality are not requirements in this pilot. Physical rows, rather than
    distinct URLs or stories, are counted. Training weights in Fine News do not
    change this record-count estimand. The original compressed DCLM source is
    deferred, and its partial Parquet conversion cannot represent the full source.
    
    ## Selection
    
    Enumerate every eligible file and its stored size at the pinned commit. Make
    four independent draws with replacement: choose a file uniformly from the
    frame, read its footer, then choose one of its row groups uniformly. Only
    selected files require footers. Sort inventories and use a separate deterministic
    seed per source. Persist every selected path, group, row bounds and probability.
    
    For a frame of M files, with G_i groups in selected file i, the probability
    of that physical group on one draw is q = 1 / (M × G_i). This is a draw
    probability, not the probability of appearing at least once in the sample.
    Repeated draws remain in the estimator. Identical groups are acquired once and
    their counts reused, without duplicating retained sample articles.
    
    Selection is fixed before reading outcomes. Do not replace expensive or failing
    draws, select the smallest files, stop after enough matches or interpret a
    convenience partition as a representative source. A costly preparation can be
    deferred; changing the design requires a separately recorded experiment.
    
    ## Acquisition
    
    Read only the selected group's half-open `file_row_number` interval and the
    explicit source projection. DuckDB 1.5.6 pushes those bounds to its Parquet
    reader. A local HTTP test compares transferred body bytes with a full projected
    scan. Ordinary `SYSTEM` or reservoir sampling is not the I/O boundary.
    
    The source must answer a small range request with HTTP 206 and matching source
    size. There is no whole-file fallback. Group sizes and necessary column chunks
    come from the footer; media and embeddings are excluded. Useful native metadata
    and file/row provenance remain in the retained output. A selected group is
    materialized once to reconcile input, English and retained counts.
    
    Listed file bytes describe stored source objects. Projected compressed chunk
    bytes describe selected columns before HTTP overhead, footer reads, prefetching
    or retries. Retained output bytes are measured locally. Actual network bytes
    are not measured and remain null. A single-group file may offer little saving.
    
    ## Estimation and uncertainty
    
    For draw d, count English records n_d and publisher-matched English records
    y_d. Let X_d = y_d / q_d and Z_d = n_d / q_d. The Hansen–Hurwitz estimates are:
    
    ```text
    Publisher records: Y_hat = mean(X_d)
    English records:   N_hat = mean(Z_d)
    Publisher yield:   p_hat = Y_hat / N_hat
    Var(Y_hat):       sum((X_d - Y_hat)^2) / (m × (m - 1))
    Var(p_hat):       sum((X_d - p_hat × Z_d)^2) / (m × (m - 1) × N_hat^2)
    ```
    
    Totals and their design-variance estimates are unbiased for independent
    replacement draws. Yield is a ratio estimate with approximate linearized
    variance, not an exactly unbiased estimator. Unequal group counts make an
    unweighted pooled sample yield inappropriate for population inference.
    
    Approximate 95% intervals use the Student t critical value with m - 1 degrees
    of freedom, with totals bounded below by zero and yield bounded to [0, 1].
    Four draws provide only three degrees of freedom. Rare or skewed group totals
    can make these intervals unreliable; label them exploratory. Zero matches,
    insufficient draws or degenerate variation leave the relevant uncertainty null,
    with an insufficient-evidence status. Zero English rows also leave yield null.
    
    The implementation tests weights against exact expectations over small finite
    frames, validates repeated draws and count reconciliation, and keeps physical
    sample counts separate from statistical draw totals. Sampling uncertainty does
    not include source omissions, language errors or publisher-registry validity.
    
    ## Further inference
    
    This pilot cannot establish unique research articles, cross-source incremental
    yield or companies meeting article thresholds over consecutive publication
    years. Source time composition differs, and crawl time is not publication time.
    Treat capture partitions as source provenance rather than an annual coverage
    estimate. Plan a larger, potentially stratified probability sample and a desired
    precision before a publication-grade comparison. Do not use outcome-dependent
    stopping without a suitable sequential design.
    
    ## References
    
    - [DuckDB Parquet metadata](https://duckdb.org/docs/1.5/data/parquet/metadata)
      describes group counts and compressed column sizes.
    - [DuckDB sampling](https://duckdb.org/docs/1.5/sql/query_syntax/samples)
      describes execution-vector sampling and reservoir behavior.
    - [Hugging Face Parquet conversion](https://huggingface.co/docs/dataset-viewer/parquet)
      describes partial conversions and their scope.
    - [Knottnerus and van Duin, Appendix A](https://www.scb.se/contentassets/ca21efb41fee47d293bbee5bf7be7fb3/variances-in-repeated-weighting-with-an-application-to-the-dutch-labour-force-survey.pdf#page=17)
      gives the Hansen–Hurwitz total and variance formulas.

    # Source comparison
    
    This pilot measures English source records retained by the same publisher
    allowlist as the historical Fine News acquisition. It compares Fine News,
    Infini News, RefinedWeb and FineWeb-HQ. DCLM is deferred: its original compressed
    JSONL requires whole-file reads, while its converted Parquet is partial.
    
    The shared parameters and pinned native source globs live in
    [`params.yaml`](../../../params.yaml). Dataset keys identify small Python source
    projections; the configuration contains no executable SQL. English follows each
    source's native labels or declared release scope. No language model is run.
    
    ## Prepare
    
    Inside `devenv shell`, after `just python::setup`:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc repro prepare_comparison
    ```
    
    This runs the metadata-only `foreach` stages. Each source produces an inventory,
    selected-file Parquet metadata and `manifest.json` beneath
    `data/raw/source-comparison/manifests/`. The inventory records eligible paths,
    object identities and stored sizes at the configured commit. The manifest
    records four replacement draws, source row bounds, probabilities and compressed
    sizes for the columns needed by the extractor.
    
    Preparation checks that the server answers an eight-byte range request with a
    matching partial response. It then reads selected Parquet footers. It does not
    acquire article text, media or embeddings. A source with large row groups can
    still require substantial transfer later: inspect its projected bytes first.
    Projected column bytes exclude footer reads, HTTP overhead, prefetching and
    retries; they are not a measured network total.
    
    ## Acquire and compare
    
    After reviewing the prepared selection and transfer estimates:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc repro sample_comparison
    just dvc repro compare_sources
    just dvc metrics show
    ```
    
    Sampling acquires article payloads. Reproducing `compare_sources` also runs any
    missing or stale upstream sampling stages. The historical `filter_fine_news`
    stage remains frozen and independent of this experiment.
    
    Each acquisition writes filtered group Parquet files and `counts.json` beneath
    `data/raw/source-comparison/samples/`. Records retain text, native identifiers
    where available, useful native metadata, and source file/row provenance.
    Repeated selections acquire one physical copy but retain every draw in the
    counts used for estimation. Samples preserve records rather than deduplicating
    articles. No ticker, date, relevance or body-length qualification is applied.
    
    The research stage writes `comparison.csv`, `metrics.json` and `methods.json`
    beneath `data/research/source-comparison/`. Reports distinguish observed counts
    from weighted population estimates, and stored source bytes from projected
    selected-column bytes and retained output bytes. Network bytes remain unknown.
    Missing sources or inconsistent counts prevent publication of the comparison.
    
    ## Interpret
    
    Four independently selected groups provide a small acquisition pilot, with weak
    precision for rare or clustered publisher matches. Population totals use the
    recorded draw probabilities; uncertainty is exploratory. Zero matches or
    degenerate variation do not establish a precise zero population yield.
    
    The estimates concern publisher-matched records in the declared snapshots.
    They do not establish unique articles, incremental coverage across overlapping
    sources, research eligibility or consecutive-year company coverage. Fine News's
    training sampling weights are not this experiment's sampling probabilities.
    Infini News's file-size inventory includes non-English records.
    
    See the [sampling methods](../../../.context/plan/dataset-research/tasks/source-comparison/methods.md)
    for the design, estimators and limitations. Later pilots should choose their
    sample size and any temporal strata before observing acquisition outcomes.

    # Compare publisher yield across public corpora
    
    ## Goal
    
    Implement a small probability-sampled comparison of English publisher retention
    across four public corpora. Prepare manifests and transfer estimates before
    acquiring article payloads. See [methods](methods.md) and the
    [pipeline guide](../../../../../data/inputs/source-comparison/README.md).
    
    ## Acceptance
    
    - [ ] Share the publisher filter across the four source projections.
    - [ ] Prepare pinned file inventories, random group selections and transfer estimates.
    - [ ] Verify weighting, row-group pruning and the full repository quality gates.
    - [ ] Document the acquisition commands and limits on population inference.
