    """Preserve the historical Fine News publisher acquisition command."""
    
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
    from typing import Annotated
    
    import duckdb
    import typer
    from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
    
    from pipeline.stages.raw.publishers import PUBLISHER_MATCH, SOURCES, write_parquet
    
    
    class FineNewsConfig(BaseModel):
        """Versioned inputs and output for the Fine News selection."""
    
        model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    
        source: str
        domains: Path
        output: Path
    
    
    def filter_fine_news(
        config: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="Historical acquisition configuration.")
        ] = Path("data/inputs/fine-news/acquisition.json"),
    ) -> None:
        """Select English publisher shards from a pinned Fine News revision."""
        settings = FineNewsConfig.model_validate_json(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        target = settings.output / "articles.parquet"
        if target.exists():
            raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {target}")
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with TemporaryDirectory(dir=target.parent) as staging, duckdb.connect() as con:
            if settings.source.startswith("hf://"):
                con.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs")
            temporary = Path(staging) / "articles.parquet"
            write_parquet(
                con,
                f"""WITH articles AS (
                    SELECT {SOURCES["fine_news"].projection} FROM read_parquet($source)
                ) SELECT text, id, metadata FROM articles WHERE {PUBLISHER_MATCH}""",  # noqa: S608 - authored projection and predicate.
                {"source": settings.source, "domains": str(settings.domains)},
                temporary,
            )
            os.link(temporary, target)
        typer.echo(f"Wrote: {settings.source} -> {target}")
    """Extract publisher records from native pre-training dataset layouts."""
    
    from dataclasses import dataclass
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import duckdb
    
    
    def _hostname(host: str | None, url: str) -> str:
        return f"""lower(rtrim(trim(coalesce(
            nullif(trim({host or "NULL"}), ''),
            regexp_extract({url}, '(?i)^https?://([^/:?#]+)', 1)
        )), '.'))"""
    
    
    PUBLISHER_MATCH = """
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM read_csv($domains, header=true) AS d
            WHERE hostname = lower(rtrim(trim(d.domain), '.'))
               OR ends_with(hostname, '.' || lower(rtrim(trim(d.domain), '.')))
        )
    """
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class SourceSpec:
        """Declare native field mappings and derive the columns actually read.
    
        A metadata column is preserved as-is; a tuple of native fields is packed
        into a metadata struct. The optional language pair names its native column
        and English label. Expressions are authored here, never taken from config.
        """
    
        text: str
        identifier: str | None
        metadata: str | tuple[str, ...]
        url: str
        hostname: str | None
        english: tuple[str, str] | None
        english_definition: str
    
        @property
        def columns(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
            """Return unique native roots needed for payload and footer estimates."""
            metadata = (self.metadata,) if isinstance(self.metadata, str) else self.metadata
            fields = [self.text]
            if self.identifier is not None and self.identifier not in metadata:
                fields.append(self.identifier)
            fields.extend(metadata)
            fields.append(self.url)
            if self.hostname is not None:
                fields.append(self.hostname)
            if self.english is not None:
                fields.append(self.english[0])
            return tuple(dict.fromkeys(field.split(".", 1)[0] for field in fields))
    
        @property
        def projection(self) -> str:
            """Project native fields into the shared article and filter columns."""
            metadata = (
                self.metadata
                if isinstance(self.metadata, str)
                else f"struct_pack({', '.join(self.metadata)})"
            )
            english = (
                "true"
                if self.english is None
                else f"{self.english[0]} = '{self.english[1]}'"
            )
            return (
                f"{self.text} AS text, {self.identifier or 'NULL::VARCHAR'} AS id, "
                f"{metadata} AS metadata, {english} AS _english, "
                f"{_hostname(self.hostname, self.url)} AS hostname"
            )
    
    
    SOURCES: dict[str, SourceSpec] = {
        "fine_news": SourceSpec(

        ),
    }
    
    
    def write_parquet(
        con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection,
        query: str,
        parameters: dict[str, object],
        target: Path,
    ) -> None:
        """Write a fresh Parquet file inside the caller's publication boundary."""
        if target.exists():
            raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {target}")
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        con.execute(
            f"COPY ({query}) TO $target "
            "(FORMAT PARQUET, COMPRESSION ZSTD, COMPRESSION_LEVEL 9, "
            "ROW_GROUP_SIZE 16384)",
            {**parameters, "target": str(target)},
        )
    
    
    def extract_group(
        con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection,
        dataset: str,
        source: str,
        row_start: int,
        row_stop: int,
        domains: Path,
        target: Path,
    ) -> dict[str, int]:
        """Read one row interval once and retain its English publisher records.
    
        Bounds are zero-based and stop-exclusive. Restricting the virtual Parquet
        row number at the scan enables remote row-group pruning. The temporary table
        preserves the selected input for counts and copying without a second read.
        The caller owns the staging directory and publishes the completed stage.
        """
        if row_start < 0 or row_stop <= row_start:
            raise ValueError("A nonempty, nonnegative row interval is required.")
        if target.exists():
            raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {target}")
        con.execute(
            f"""CREATE TEMP TABLE comparison_group AS
            SELECT {SOURCES[dataset].projection},
                $source AS source_file, file_row_number AS source_row
            FROM read_parquet($source, file_row_number=true, hive_partitioning=false)
            WHERE file_row_number >= $row_start AND file_row_number < $row_stop
            """,  # noqa: S608 - projection comes from the fixed source registry.
            {"source": source, "row_start": row_start, "row_stop": row_stop},
        )
        try:
            counts = con.execute(
                f"""SELECT count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE _english),
                    count(*) FILTER (WHERE _english AND {PUBLISHER_MATCH})
                    FROM comparison_group""",  # noqa: S608 - authored predicate.
                {"domains": str(domains)},
            ).fetchone()
            if counts is None or counts[0] != row_stop - row_start:
                raise ValueError("The selected row interval differs from its manifest.")
            write_parquet(
                con,
                f"""SELECT * EXCLUDE (_english, hostname) FROM comparison_group
                    WHERE _english AND {PUBLISHER_MATCH}""",  # noqa: S608
                {"domains": str(domains)},
                target,
            )
            return dict(
                zip(("input_rows", "english_rows", "matched_rows"), counts, strict=True)
            )
        finally:
            con.execute("DROP TABLE comparison_group")
    # Fine News acquisition
    
    `filter_fine_news` documents the historical staging selection from
    [Fine News](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ksolovev/fine-news) at the revision
    in [acquisition.json](acquisition.json). It selects `eng_Latn` capture-month
    shards and the exact 115-hostname [allowlist](domains.csv), including subdomains.
    The hostname comes from `metadata.url_hostname`, falling back to `metadata.url`
    when blank. One query reads the input glob and writes `text`, `id` and `metadata`
    to `data/raw/fine-news/articles.parquet`.
    
    This is the historical source filter, not a reviewed publisher list or a
    research-ready article corpus. Fine News applies its own filters and
    deduplication; capture month is not necessarily publication month. The upstream
    dataset card describes content rights and usage restrictions.
    
    ## Restored snapshot
    
    `data/raw/fine-news/` contains the existing publisher-filtered snapshot from
    `marcusinthesky/fine-news-financial-publishers` at Hub revision
    `3168f32f57107eac95a2c53f024e5e340c91ef2e`. It was copied from the local staging
    repository's `data/01_intermediate/` directory, preserving 168 monthly Parquet
    shards, 14,807,287 records and 20,100,064,588 Parquet bytes. Its domain CSV matches
    this recipe's input. Every shard was checked against the published revision's
    Git LFS SHA256 and size; Parquet metadata confirms row counts and columns.
    
    The output's `provenance.json` records the source revision, upstream source,
    domain checksum and each shard's path, SHA256, size and row count. DVC records
    the complete directory in `dvc.lock` and the local cache. This restoration
    preserves the published month/language layout. The reproduction command above
    writes a consolidated `articles.parquet`; a fresh rebuild has not been compared
    row for row with the restored snapshot.
    
    The stage remains frozen: `dvc repro` verifies its existing output without
    executing the acquisition, even with `--force`. On another checkout, restore
    the output with `just dvc checkout filter_fine_news` from the local cache, or
    `just dvc pull filter_fine_news` once an artifact remote contains it. No remote
    cache upload was performed by this restoration.
    
    Unfreezing or invoking the command directly runs acquisition and requires
    network access and substantial resources. Use a fresh output directory when
    rebuilding. DuckDB may download its `httpfs` extension on first remote access.
    
    For a local trial, provide `--config` with a local source glob, domain CSV and
    fresh output directory. The script refuses to overwrite an existing output.
    Output layout, order and Parquet bytes differ from

    ## Free Foundations top 1,000

    [security-year membership panel](free_foundations_us_top_1000_membership.csv),
    and [provenance](free_foundations_us_top_1000.provenance.json) are a preliminary
    research snapshot. The panel has 1,000 December-ranked securities per effective
    year from 2002 through 2025. The source archive has no December 2000 observation;
    2026 is outside its study window. Issuers are grouped by PERMCO and CIK, with
    unresolved identities kept separate. Candidate links are not verified identity
    evidence. SEC and Wikipedia descriptions are not complete or all reviewed.
    
    The issuer CSV contains multiline source text and JSON-encoded lists. Read CIKs
    as strings to preserve leading zeros. SEC descriptions are source text, not
    generated summaries. Wikipedia text is attributed to the contributors at its
    linked permanent revision and is available under
    [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Latest-access
    descriptions, names and aliases are not point-in-time historical features.
    
    To validate the snapshot and attempt conservative recovery, with the pinned
    Free Foundations archive available at `~/Git/free-foundations/research/crsp-study`:
    
    ```sh
    src/python/.venv/bin/python src/python/scripts/recover_universe.py
    EDGAR_IDENTITY='Your Name your.email@example.com' \
      src/python/.venv/bin/python src/python/scripts/recover_universe.py --network
    ```
    
    Use `--archive` to select another copy of the same archive; its four prepared
    inputs must match the recorded hashes. The script uses the workspace's Polars
    installation. Requests are disabled unless `--network` is supplied, SEC requests
    also require `EDGAR_IDENTITY`, and a failed host is skipped for the rest of that
    run. Successful network responses and a review queue are saved under the ignored
    `.tmp/universe-recovery/` directory; reruns reuse cached successes. Output CSVs
    must match the provenance hashes before updates are made.
    Use `--source sec` or `--source wikipedia` to retry one source independently;
    `--workers` controls concurrency while all requests share the rate limit.
    
    The recovery pass only promotes a candidate when the pinned crosswalk already
    has matching, dated, verified SEC evidence. It extracts unambiguous 10-K Item 1
    boundaries as **unreviewed**, and accepts a Wikipedia match only when its
    Wikidata item supplies the same CIK. It does not yet discover new historical
    identities, extract other SEC forms, or resolve ambiguous boundaries and pages;
    those cases remain in the queue for later research. The latest run's status
    counts and access failures are in `.tmp/universe-recovery/last_run.json`.
    # Full-corpus company candidates
    
    The production CPU runner tags every source row with candidate companies from
    the annual US top-1000 panel and the fixed Gawronsky–Huang roster. It extracts
    mentions and publisher evidence; it does not claim substantive relevance,
    primary-company truth or calibrated probabilities.
    
    Install the [CPU extra](company-cpu.md) before running from the repository root
    inside the development environment:
    
    ```sh
    src/python/.venv/bin/python -m fine_news_cli company tag-corpus
    ```
    
    Defaults are six processes, one native thread per process, 128 input rows per
    batch, and compressed Parquet output chunks of 8,192 rows. The default run first
    processes a 100,000-row pilot distributed proportionally across source files,
    then continues to the full corpus. Both stages enforce an 8 GiB combined process
    memory ceiling. Pilot ranges are deterministic contiguous ranges for bounded
    Parquet reads, not a random sample suitable for prevalence inference. Reported
    throughput includes source reads, matching and durable output; preflight source
    hashing and final reports are separate.
    
    The initial successful 100,000-row pilot covered all 168 local files and took
    13.0 seconds (about 7,700 rows/second), with 3.3 GiB peak combined resident memory.
    The reader uses a 512 MiB DuckDB budget per process; the aggregate ceiling also
    accounts for Python objects and output buffers. All 322 CLI tests passed before
    the production run. The optimized matcher produced identical evidence on all
    2,000 checked raw rows,
    and its cased projection matched the frozen policy on all 1,135 clean supported
    evaluation rows.
    
    ## Completed production run
    
    The 2026-11-04 run completed all **14,807,287 source rows in 168 files** with
    exit code zero. Processing took **1,643 seconds (27 minutes 23 seconds)**,
    averaging **9,012 articles/second**, including source reads, matching and durable
    writes. Preflight hashing and final report generation are outside that timing.
    Peak combined process-tree resident memory was **7,533,608,960 bytes (7.02 GiB)**,
    below the 8 GiB guard. Six CPU workers ran on the Ryzen 5 9600X; the GPU was not
    used. No per-core utilization trace was collected, so these measurements do not
    establish exact CPU saturation.
    
    | Universe | Source rows with candidates | Rows with cased name evidence | Rows with publisher evidence |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | Annual US top-1000 | 12,159,551 | 8,365,194 | 512,169 |
    | Fixed GH roster | 3,764,426 | 1,569,478 | 139,298 |
    
    Evidence categories overlap. Candidates include ambiguous and lowercase aliases;
    these counts are not estimates of substantive coverage, precision or recall.
    The independent [2,000-row prevalence audit](company-prevalence.md) addresses
    substantive coverage with a different procedure and remains provisional.
    
    The committed [findings snapshot](company-tagging-findings.json) retains run
    metrics, contract and artifact fingerprints, the GH minimum, and the Nasdaq
    comparison below. Generated predictions remain in the local output directory.
    
    Use `--phase preflight`, `--phase pilot` or `--phase run` for individual stages.
    Use `--resume` to verify and continue a run. `--limit` restricts the processing
    frame in source-file order for development. Configuration, registry, code,
    dependencies and source fingerprints must match the frozen manifest on resume.
    
    ## Evidence and identities
    
    One Rust Aho–Corasick DFA searches the union of registry names and aliases.
    Extended legal suffixes follow the existing tested policy, with separate alias
    ownership and overlap selection for each universe. Publication year controls
    top-1000 eligibility; the GH roster is fixed across years. Current registry
    names and fixed GH ticker spellings are not certified historical identities.
    
    Rows retain all candidate companies. Single-token lowercase matches, shared
    aliases, ambiguous symbols and incomplete catalogs have explicit flags.
    `cased_name_match_count` distinguishes evidence that survives the tested case
    policy; lowercase evidence remains available rather than becoming a negative.
    Neither a complete catalog nor a no-candidate result proves irrelevance.
    
    Publisher exchange annotations, cashtags and conservative standalone ticker
    tags are extracted separately. Explicit annotations are masked in the name
    matching view. Ordinary prose and complete company names remain intact; the
    evaluation sanitizer that could remove parts of company names is not applied.
    No bare ticker search is added to prose unless that spelling already appears
    as a catalog name or alias. Publisher evidence is unverified and must not be
    used as independent evaluation truth for predictions derived from that evidence.
    
    Top-1000 issuer IDs are `top1000:PERMCO`; GH IDs are `gh:CIK` with padded CIKs.
    Their identities remain separate, including when a company belongs to both.
    The output retains catalog CIK link status without inferring a crosswalk.
    Tickers are labels from the relevant catalog, not additional issuer identities.
    
    ## Output and recovery
    
    The destination defaults to `data/02_primary/company_tags/dfa-v1/`:
    
    - `manifest.json` freezes source SHA-256 fingerprints and the run contract.
    - `shards/NNNNN/part-NNNNN.parquet` stores every source row with native nested
      candidate/evidence structs. Each source directory has a `completed.json`.
    - `pilot/` contains separate pilot predictions and timing.
    - `progress.jsonl` records progress, resource observations and failures.
    - `summary.json` reconciles rows and counts by year, universe and evidence.
    - `company-year-counts.csv` counts candidate and publisher-supported source rows.
    - `gh-company-year-2018-2022.csv` includes zero-count cells for all GH companies;
      `gh-floor-2018-2022.json` identifies the minimum candidate count and ties.
    
    Read production predictions with `shards/*/part-*.parquet`; a recursive glob over
    the entire run directory would also include the separate pilot predictions.
    For the launched background run, `background-job.json` and `worker-process.json`
    identify the processes, `runner.log` captures errors, and `background-exit.json`
    records the eventual exit code. A final `summary.json` with `status=complete`
    confirms successful processing and report generation.
    
    `row_key` hashes the relative source path and zero-based physical row number.
    Original article IDs remain nullable and are not assumed unique. Duplicate or
    syndicated source rows are retained. Article text is not copied into outputs.
    Each candidate has full occurrence counts and at most four representative spans
    per field; offsets describe the NFKC/casefold matching view, not raw text.
    
    Workers commit a source directory atomically after row-count reconciliation and
    durable writes. Incomplete `.partial` source directories are rebuilt on resume.
    Completed chunks are checksum-verified and reused; corruption or changed inputs
    causes an error. Source failures prevent successful completion. An output lock
    prevents concurrent writers. A failed row is never silently dropped.
    
    Company-year counts describe source rows with candidate evidence, not unique
    stories or adjudicated substantive company coverage. In particular, the GH
    candidate floor is not a validated academic coverage floor.
    
    ## GH annual floor and Nasdaq comparison
    
    Across the fixed 100-company GH roster and the five publication years 2018–2022,
    the minimum among all 500 company-year cells is **CDNS in 2018: 16 candidate
    source rows**. Fifteen have cased company-name evidence and two have publisher
    ticker evidence; one row has both. None of the 500 candidate cells is zero.
    These source rows have not been deduplicated or adjudicated for substantive
    company coverage.
    
    The local `pricing-perspective` Nasdaq archive is a separately acquired,
    ticker-directed source. Its `main` revision
    `c8a4bd69cf26c87163d5db3c0a2de7b0d8b14cef` documents collection through
    `api.nasdaq.com/api/news/topic/articlebysymbol` in December 2022–January 2023.
    The immutable raw archive contains 397,041 rows; the current normalized local
    artifact contains 214,480 records across 100 symbols. Its global article-ID
    deduplication keeps one scrape-symbol assignment, potentially losing other
    article–symbol memberships. Nasdaq assignments and our extracted candidates
    therefore measure different things.
    
    | Publication year | Nasdaq normalized CDNS records | Fine News CDNS candidates | Fine News Nasdaq-hosted rows, all companies |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | 2018 | 123 | 16 | 0 |
    | 2019 | 97 | 126 | 74,258 |
    | 2020 | 69 | 275 | 212,834 |
    | 2021 | 57 | 134 | 174,027 |
    | 2022 | 381 | 314 | 241,988 |
    
    There are also 123 distinct CDNS article IDs in the raw Nasdaq archive for 2018,
    so deduplication does not explain that year's 123-versus-16 difference. The
    historical `annual_raw_article_floor: 47` admission rule precedes normalization;
    it is not a guaranteed deduplicated annual floor. The realized normalized
    archive's minimum is SNPS in 2018 with 34 records. Its documented minimum of
    449 per ticker concerns the entire recovered history, rather than one year.
    
    The Fine News host counts use publication year from `metadata.publish_date`,
    and the normalized URL hostname with URL fallback. They include `nasdaq.com`
    and its subdomains across all 168 source files. None of the 123 Nasdaq CDNS
    URLs from 2018 matches a Fine News source URL after stripping the Nasdaq
    scheme/hostname and query/fragment components. This establishes a source URL
    coverage gap; it does not rule out copies hosted by original publishers.
    Title matching alone is insufficient: repeated earnings and market-summary
    headlines also occur in different years. The snapshot retains this diagnostic
    with its dates rather than treating repeated titles as duplicate stories.
    
    ## Confirmed recall gaps and next experiment
    
    The frozen GH catalog supplies `Cadence Design Systems` and the branded
    `cādence`, plus the legal name. Suffix expansion adds `CADENCE DESIGN SYSTEMS`;
    neither normalization nor that expansion produces plain `Cadence` or
    `Cadence Design`. Bare `CDNS` in prose is also outside the current ticker policy.
    
    A case-sensitive whole-word search for `Cadence` or `CDNS` in 2018 titles and
    bodies finds 75 source rows, of which 15 already have CDNS candidates. The
    remaining 60 are not all false negatives: they include Cadence Bank, Aerospace,
    Minerals, personal names, ordinary prose and an unrelated CDNS acronym.
    Three inspected untagged examples do identify the semiconductor/EDA company:
    
    | Source and date | Article | Missing spelling |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Korea Herald, 2018-02-28 | [Samsung's non-memory chips at MWC](http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20180228000675) | Cadence |
    | Business Day, 2018-08-17 | [SA is on wrong side of global shift towards new industries](https://www.businesslive.co.za/bd/opinion/2018-08-17-sa-is-on-wrong-side-of-global-shift-towards-new-industries/) | Cadence Design |
    | Forbes, 2018-11-01 | [Simulation Becomes Increasingly Important For Self-Driving Cars](https://www.forbes.com/sites/davidsilver/2018/11/01/simulation-becomes-increasingly-important-for-self-driving-cars/) | Cadence |
    
    These are confirmed missed name mentions from local extracted text, not new
    human gold labels for substantive relevance. Their source IDs and excerpts are
    retained in the snapshot. Consequently, 16 undercounts available mentions and
    cannot establish the academic coverage floor. Both acquisition coverage and
    matching recall require attention.
    
    The next experiment should combine the Nasdaq archive with Fine News while
    preserving provenance and all article–company memberships through deduplication.
    Test provenance-backed aliases and contextual handling of ambiguous names on
    independent data before changing the production dictionary. Then recompute the
    company-year table and review its low-count cells. The completed run and its
    catalog remain frozen; this comparison does not merge sources or revise tags.
    # Data Provenance
    
    This document records the reproducibility root of the news-corpus pipeline and
    the governed encoder identities used to turn that corpus into paper-specific
    artifacts.
    
    ## Raw source
    
    - **API endpoint:** `api.nasdaq.com/api/news/topic/articlebysymbol`
    - **Raw file:** `data/raw/nasdaq.jsonlines`
    - **md5:** `a30d7fe43928f7d99fee118a5cf66b77`
    - **Size:** 1,815,644,085 bytes
    - **Records:** 397,041 JSON lines (one article per line)
    - **Collected:** 2022-12 to 2023-01
    
    The raw file is **immutable**. It is never rewritten by any stage. Corpus-derived
    artifacts additionally bind the encoder provider or checkpoint declared in
    `params.yaml` and the resolved stage identity recorded in `dvc.lock`; market-data
    artifacts retain their separate source provenance.
    
    ## Corpus normalization (`normalize_corpus`)
    
    The raw JSON lines are deduplicated, date-parsed, and filtered to the 100-ticker
    universe defined in `params.yaml` (`symbols:`). Dedupe statistics recorded in
    `data/shared/corpus/summary.yaml`:
    
    | Metric | Value |
    | --- | --- |
    | rows_in | 397,041 |
    | rows_out | 214,480 |
    | duplicates_dropped | 182,561 |
    | symbols | 100 |
    | date span | 2009-10 to 2023-01 |
    | per_ticker_min | 449 |
    
    ## Declared firm universe
    
    The 100-name news universe is a prespecified, Nasdaq-100-based sampling frame.
    It was formed from the original Nasdaq scrape using the
    `annual_raw_article_floor: 47` threshold in `params.yaml`: each retained firm
    required at least that many articles in every calendar year from 2018 through
    2022.
    The screen was applied to the raw archive before the current identifier-level
    deduplication; it is therefore a universe-selection rule, not a claim that every
    normalized firm-year still contains 47 distinct records.
    
    The current normalization validates that all 100 declared symbols are present;
    after identifier-level deduplication the least-covered ticker retains 449
    articles over the full recovered history. Annual raw-coverage qualification is
    applied before that deduplication, so this aggregate minimum is not a substitute
    for the firm-year admission rule.
    
    The frame is coverage-conditioned and is not presented as an exhaustive sample
    of every Nasdaq firm satisfying the threshold. The source was chosen because
    Nasdaq exposes a public per-symbol news endpoint and the recovered records carry
    full syndicated article bodies, rather than headline strings alone. The endpoint
    is Nasdaq-hosted; the underlying articles come from multiple publishers.
    
    ## Encoder and representation provenance
    
    Article embeddings are a shared substrate, but there is no repository-wide
    Qwen3-Embedding-4B primary pin. `params.yaml` separately governs the external
    model registry (`embedding.models`), raw provider artifacts
    (`typed_analysis.providers`), deterministic representation transforms
    (`typed_analysis.representations`), and paper-specific selectors. `dvc.yaml`
    materializes those identities into path-disjoint artifacts, and `dvc.lock`
    records the values resolved by each stage.
    
    The shared canonical provider is:
    
    | Field | Governed value |
    | --- | --- |
    | Provider ID | `qwen3-embedding-8b` |
    | External model ID | `qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b` |
    | Hugging Face reference | `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B` |
    | Native width | 4096 |
    | Generation access | OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint |
    | Frozen raw shards | `data/shared/embeddings/qwen3-embedding-8b/<TICKER>.parquet` |
    | Canonical representation | `qwen3-embedding-8b-unit` |
    | Representation transform | Row-wise L2 normalization at full width (4096) |
    
    The API endpoint is the configured generation route; the frozen DVC artifacts
    are the reproduction route. A full-width representation has `dimension: null`
    in the typed registry because it retains the provider's native width, not because
    its width is unknown. The canonical typed-distance summary records both the
    native and realized dimensions as 4096.
    
    ### Paper-specific primary bindings
    
    The first three manuscript projects currently share the canonical provider and
    representation. Paper 6 provisionally selects Qwen3-Embedding-4B; every paper binds
    its provider through a separate selector and derived artifact.
    Changing one paper's selector must not be described as changing another paper's
    primary representation unless its own binding changes.
    
    | Paper | Governing selector and DVC stage | Binding output | Provider / representation | Effective width | Shared artifact access |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | Paper 1 | `scientific_selectors.baseline_model`; `p1_dyadic_confound` | `data/papers/paper1/dyadic_confound/results.json` | `qwen3-embedding-8b` / `qwen3-embedding-8b-unit` | 4096 | `data/shared/typed_distances/qwen3-embedding-8b/qwen3-embedding-8b-unit/wasserstein_w2` |
    | Paper 3 | `scientific_selectors.typed_distance_*` and `paper3.primary_distance_id`; `p3_certificate` | `data/papers/paper3/certificate/provenance.manifest.json` | `qwen3-embedding-8b` / `qwen3-embedding-8b-unit` | 4096 | `data/shared/typed_distances/qwen3-embedding-8b/qwen3-embedding-8b-unit/wasserstein_w2` |
    | Paper 5 | `paper5.provider_id`, `representation_id`, `distance_id`, and `barycentre_arm_id`; `p5_post_corpus_qmle` | `data/papers/paper5/post_corpus_qmle/results.json` | `qwen3-embedding-8b` / `qwen3-embedding-8b-unit` | 4096 | The same typed W2 artifact plus `data/shared/barycentres/qwen3-embedding-8b/qwen3-embedding-8b-unit/wasserstein_w2_loo` |
    | Paper 6 | Fixed input cohort; `p6_panel_sample` | `data/papers/paper6/panel_sample/manifest.json` and `qwen3-embedding-4b.npz` | `qwen3-embedding-4b` / unit-row representation | 2560 | Frozen paper-local observations under `data/papers/paper6/inputs/`; independent of the shared canonical provider. |
    
    Paper 5's merged representation artifact,
    `data/papers/paper5/representation_ablation/results.json`, independently marks
    `qwen8b_full` as canonical and records the same provider, representation, and
    4096-dimensional effective and native widths.
    
    ### Representation-sensitivity roster
    
    `representation_ablation_specs` governs the seven cross-paper base cells below.
    The canonical row is carried as the common comparison reference; the other rows
    are sensitivity arms and do not replace a paper's primary selector.
    
    | Cell | Provider ID | Representation ID | Effective / native width | Role |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | `qwen8b_full` | `qwen3-embedding-8b` | `qwen3-embedding-8b-unit` | 4096 / 4096 | Canonical reference |
    | `qwen4b_full` | `qwen3-embedding-4b` | `qwen3-embedding-4b-unit` | 2560 / 2560 | Within-family capacity and native-width arm |
    | `qwen8b_1024` | `qwen3-embedding-8b` | `qwen3-embedding-8b-1024-unit` | 1024 / 4096 | Matryoshka truncation |
    | `qwen4b_1024` | `qwen3-embedding-4b` | `qwen3-embedding-4b-1024-unit` | 1024 / 2560 | Fixed-width capacity arm |
    | `bge_large_full` | `bge-large-en-v1.5` | `bge-large-en-v1.5-unit` | 1024 / 1024 | External architecture/training-provider arm |
    | `qwen8b_256` | `qwen3-embedding-8b` | `qwen3-embedding-8b-256-unit` | 256 / 4096 | Matryoshka truncation |
    | `qwen8b_64` | `qwen3-embedding-8b` | `qwen3-embedding-8b-64-unit` | 64 / 4096 | Matryoshka truncation |
    
    The eight additional `encoder_vintage_ablation_specs` cells are the pinned
    annual ChronoBERT checkpoints for 2017 through 2024. Each uses a distinct
    `chronobert-<year>` provider and matching unit-normalized representation at 768
    dimensions. The `chronobert` block in `params.yaml` records checkpoint revisions
    and training cutoffs. These cumulative-training comparisons are descriptive
    sensitivities; the 2017 checkpoint precedes article construction, while the
    2023 and 2024 checkpoints overlap the held-out return window. They do not
    identify a causal leakage effect or represent historical deployment.
    
    Raw comparison shards live at `data/shared/embeddings/<provider_id>/`. Their
    typed W2 inputs live at
    `data/shared/typed_distances/<provider_id>/<representation_id>/wasserstein_w2`.
    Paper-specific merge stages consume only the roster declared in `params.yaml`;
    the broader exploratory `ablation.grid` does not silently enter publication
    tables.
    
    Provider IDs, external model IDs, representation IDs, widths, normalization
    transforms, and paper selectors are all part of the reproducibility contract.
    Changing one invalidates the DVC stages that declare or consume the affected
    artifact and propagates through their downstream dependencies. Paper-specific
    selectors keep unrelated branches distinct; they do not stop ordinary DVC
    dependency propagation.
    
    ## Price-data universe (100 tickers)
    
    Price-dependent stages (`market_data`, `compute_returns`, `compute_covariance`,
    and everything downstream of the returns/covariance matrix) run on the same
    **100-ticker** universe as the news stages. `market_symbols` is identical to
    `symbols`, and `market_symbol_exclusions` is empty. EA and HOLX are served from
    recorded market-data archives because live retrieval is no longer available;
    both traded throughout the governed evaluation period and remain in the panel.
    
    Both evaluation windows therefore use the same 100 firms, with no
    news-to-price or cross-window firm attrition. The windows are declared once in
    `params.yaml` as `return_panels` and drive the `compute_covariance` matrix
    family: the in-sample matrix is the `@window0` cell under
    `data/shared/`, the out-of-sample matrix the `@window1` cell under
    `data/shared/oos/`. Each entry also carries the complete-case contract
    (`expected_tickers`, `expected_observations`, and the first/last complete date)
    that `compute-covariance` enforces as a hard guard.
    
    To change the governed price universe, update `symbols`, `market_symbols`,
    `data/universe.csv`, and both `return_panels` complete-case contracts together,
    then re-run
    `dvc repro --glob 'compute_returns@*' 'compute_covariance@*'`.

# CPU-first filtering, then Kev scoring

## Objective

Complete the corpus-wide CPU filter first, measure the actual retained population, then size Kev processing against **07:00 SAST on 17 November**. Treat approximately one million survivors as a possibility to measure.

## 1. Finish the CPU pass

- Verify and reuse the existing Rust Aho–Corasick outputs where their contracts match. **All 168 source-shard fingerprints match the restored CCFinance snapshot**, so unchanged matching need not run again.
- Apply deterministic publisher, text-quality and date policies; preserve uncertain cases separately.
- Materialize company candidates and evidence, distinguishing names, aliases, explicit ticker annotations and ambiguous matches.
- Correct known destructive sanitization and alias problems. Re-run matching only where the revised policy requires it.
- Deduplicate normalized-exact documents while preserving every source record and company membership.
- Produce the complete CPU-filtered dataset, exclusion reasons and provenance.

CPU matches remain candidate evidence. They do not establish substantive coverage or a primary company.

## 2. Check the resulting workload

Report actual counts after each operation:

- Source records and distinct document groups.
- Retained documents and candidate-company pairs.
- Ambiguous and no-candidate documents.
- Document lengths and candidates per document.
- Breakdowns by publisher and publication year.

Preserve the broader candidate population when producing a stricter filter. Avoid narrowing the company universe or dropping difficult articles merely to meet the deadline.

## 4. Run and finalize

    # CCFinance
    
    CCFinance is a data engineering project for filtering and enriching public
    Common Crawl News (CC-News) copies for research into language in finance.
    
    ## Start
    
    Exordio supplies the Python and LaTeX toolchains, a pinned Nix environment and CI.
    Copier answers record Exordio `v0.1.1-alpha` (the documented `v0.1.0` tag was not
    available in the local source).
    
    ```bash
    bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh
    devenv shell
    just setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run stages list
    just check
    ```
    
    Shared agent instructions and Codex configuration are maintained in
    [`.agents/`](.agents/README.md). `just setup` applies them; use
    `just agents::preview` to preview link changes and `just agents::check` to
    verify the generated links.
    
    `just check` validates Justfile syntax and formatting alongside the other
    quality gates. Run `just fmt` to format Justfiles and other source files.
    
    For Python alone, with Python 3.13, uv and just installed:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::check
    ```
    
    ## Data and reproducibility
    
    DVC is initialized at the repository root with analytics disabled. Use:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc status
    just dvc dag
    ```
    
    Semflow tracks the executable Python dependencies of DVC stages. When adding a
    stage, run `just semflow-patch` to review its proposed fingerprints, then
    `just semflow-apply` to materialize them. Commit the generated
    `.semflow/hashes/` files with the DVC definition. After semantic source changes,
    run `just semflow-refresh`; `just semflow-check` detects stale fingerprints.
    The frozen [Fine News acquisition stage](data/inputs/fine-news/README.md) retains
    the published staging snapshot and its historical selection recipe. DVC verifies
    the restored output during reproduction. The
    [source comparison](data/inputs/source-comparison/README.md) prepares small
    probability samples using Parquet metadata before acquiring article payloads.
    Keep data, configuration and environment dependencies explicit in DVC: Semflow's
    static analysis cannot discover string-driven dynamic imports.
    
    See [Python commands](src/python/README.md), [LaTeX commands](src/latex/README.md)
    and [infrastructure](infra/README.md). The scaffold's Apache-2.0 license covers
    code; it does not grant rights to upstream article content.
    # Architecture
    
    CCFinance separates code and research artifacts. Git stores source, configuration,
    locks, provenance definitions and documentation. DVC defines data dependencies
    and will track large data and experiment outputs once they are materialized.
    
    - `src/python/apps/pipeline` owns the CLI and data stage implementations.
    - `src/python/uv.lock` locks runtime, quality, testing, packaging and DVC tools.
    - `src/latex` owns the manuscript source and bibliography.
    - `data` holds ignored data payloads and versioned DVC pointer files.
    - `infra/nix` and `devenv.lock` own the reproducible system environment.
    
    Tach enforces module boundaries; Ruff and strict Pyrefly check Python source.
    pytest-layout-enforcer checks test file placement during collection and CI.
    Semflow fingerprints the Python code used by DVC stages, allowing DVC to
    invalidate tracked results when executable behavior changes.
    CI executes those checks, tests and builds through the same just recipes as local
    work. Setup may download dependencies; ordinary checks use cached dependencies
    and do not repair authored content. LaTeX uses a versioned Tectonic asset bundle.
    
    The Hugging Face dataset is staging, and the bucket is intended for intermediate
    and experiment artifacts. The frozen raw acquisition stage documents the
    historical selection without fetching its output. Company-level coverage,
    enrichment and remote artifact transport remain future work. The raw comparison stages prepare
    sampling manifests from Hub listings and Parquet footers, then acquire only the
    selected row groups through the shared publisher filter. Research aggregation
    reads those artifacts without importing raw-stage modules. DVC connects these
    steps; pinned source revisions and recorded draw probabilities define the
    experiment's population and sampling design.
    
    Each data layer groups experimental artifacts beneath `experiments/<name>/`.
    Experimental stage code follows the same grouping under its owning layer.
    `pipeline.experiments.source_comparison` defines shared parameters and artifacts;
    Tach permits raw and research to depend on these contracts without importing one
    another. Raw publisher extraction owns one source-field registry, deriving both
    SQL projections and projected column sizes from it. DVC supplies artifact paths
    explicitly. Research uses statsmodels for survey-estimate summaries and LaTeX
    tables; it preserves the probability-sampling design.
    
    Copier answers record the source and tag for future template updates. Review
    update conflicts and preserve project-specific code and configuration. The
    upstream template is [Exordio](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/exordio).
    # Python workspace
    
    `apps/pipeline` is an installable Typer application in a Python 3.13 uv workspace.
    Run from the repository root:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run version
    just python::run stages list
    just python::run stages raw --help
    just python::layout
    just python::check
    ```
    
    Data processing is organized into three layers, matching `dvc.yaml`:
    
    | Module and CLI group | Purpose | Data location |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `pipeline.stages.raw` / `stages raw` | Preserve source snapshots and provenance | `data/raw/` |
    | `pipeline.stages.processed` / `stages processed` | Build reusable cleaned and enriched tables | `data/processed/` |
    | `pipeline.stages.research` / `stages research` | Curate coverage panels, cohorts and release datasets | `data/research/` |
    
    The raw layer includes the frozen historical Fine News publisher filter described
    in [its acquisition configuration](../../data/inputs/fine-news/README.md), alongside
    `prepare-comparison` and `sample-comparison`. The research layer provides
    `compare-sources` for weighted estimates from the resulting manifests and counts.
    Experimental implementations live under each layer's `experiments` package.
    They share Pydantic artifact contracts through `pipeline.experiments`; the raw
    `publishers` module owns source mappings and extraction. DVC passes artifact
    paths explicitly, while statistical and source parameters live under
    `experiments.source_comparison` in the root parameter file. Reporting follows
    the configured dataset keys and can run a deliberate subset of sources.
    See the [source comparison](../../data/inputs/source-comparison/README.md) before
    running acquisition. Python setup installs DuckDB's `httpfs` extension so the
    local HTTP integration check can run offline. Add other stage commands under their owning layer,
    with explicit inputs and outputs, and declare their dependencies in `dvc.yaml`.
    DVC connects layers through artifacts; Python modules need not import earlier
    layers to read their outputs. Importing a module performs no dataset access.
    
    Setup installs the committed lock. Checks run offline with frozen dependencies.
    Ruff checks formatting, annotations, docstrings and common correctness/security
    issues; strict Pyrefly checks all app code and tests. Tach enforces module
    boundaries, rejects unused dependency declarations and forbids cycles. The CLI
    imports the stage router, which registers the three independent layer modules.
    
    `pytest-layout-enforcer` checks test paths against their owning source modules
    both during pytest collection and with `just python::layout`. Test paths mirror
    `apps/pipeline/src/pipeline` under `apps/pipeline/tests`: for example,
    `cli.py` maps to `test_cli.py`, and `stages/raw/loader.py` maps to
    `stages/raw/test_loader.py`. Feature variants use `__`, as in
    `test_loader__empty.py`; `include-packages` also allows tests for package
    initializers. This checks existing test placement, not test coverage. Tach checks
    imports and does not enforce this layout.
    
    `just python::test` runs all tests. `test-changed` is a local optimization only.
    `build` builds a wheel and source archive. `fmt` explicitly repairs formatting.
    Ruff and Pyrefly run from the same uv lock locally and in CI.

    # Repository workflow
    
    ## Workflow
    
    Read the root README and the relevant local README before changing records.
    Use `just --list` to discover the installed workflow and language commands. Create
    records through their commands, edit canonical metadata, then run `just sync`
    when available and `just check`. Keep task parents terse and store detailed
    evidence in linked records. Verification establishes only what the actual

    ---
    name: architecture-layout
    description: Use when evaluating or designing where CCFinance code, data stages, tests, documents or infrastructure belong, including module boundaries and repository restructures.
    ---
    
    # Architecture layout
    
    ## Workflow
    
    1. Establish the requested scope and outcome: evaluate the current layout,
       design a layout, or implement an authorized change. Read nearby README and
       ARCHITECTURE files. Identify existing owners and consumers before proposing
       a new abstraction; reuse an existing module or library when it satisfies the
       contract. File size alone is not a reason to split or create a package.
    2. Examine the relevant boundaries using evidence:
       - **Ownership and cohesion:** Can a contributor find the owner, and do things
         that change together live together? Keep each unit's responsibility clear.
       - **Dependencies and encapsulation:** Trace relevant imports and public
         interfaces. Keep intended dependency direction clear and cycles forbidden;
         avoid reaching into another module's internals without a reason.
       - **Coupling:** Identify changes that force unrelated owners to change.
         Share a contract only when consumers actually need the same behavior; a
         little local duplication may be preferable to coupling distinct contracts.
       - **Discoverability:** Make CLI commands, transformations, schemas, tests,
         fixtures and documents easy to find from their owning area.
    3. Choose the smallest useful boundary: a function, module, package or separate
       workspace project. A package or project should reflect an actual dependency,
       distribution, build or ownership need. Organize by layer, capability or a
       combination according to the work; do not impose a universal directory tree.
    4. For pipeline work, preserve the established `raw`, `processed` and `research`
       stage ownership. Organize capabilities within those layers as they arise.
       Distinguish Python imports from DVC artifact dependencies: the latter connect
       producers and consumers without requiring cross-layer Python imports. Apply
       Tach rules to durable module boundaries and DVC to artifact dependencies.
    5. For a move or split, trace the affected consumers before changing paths:
       imports and public APIs, CLI registration, package configuration, tests and
       fixtures, Tach, DVC and Semflow dependencies, and documentation links as
       applicable. Preserve behavior and scientific contracts unless the user asks
       for a change; report any intended behavior change separately. Do not treat
       missing static references as proof that dynamic or external consumers do not
       exist.
    6. Use the repository's existing gates rather than adding tests that merely
       assert a directory tree or private call sequence. For tests and fixtures,
       follow [Python testing](../python-testing/SKILL.md). Run focused checks while
       working and `just check` before handoff; report checks that could not run.
    
    ## Results
    
    For an evaluation, report concrete findings with locations, effects and ranked
    recommendations. For a design, show the proposed ownership and dependency
    boundaries, explain meaningful tradeoffs and how they are enforced. For an
    implementation, summarize what moved, whether behavior changed and the evidence
    from verification. Keep the review proportional to the requested change.
    
    For example, if both article cleaning and company linking need the same
    publication-date parser, first inspect its existing owner and date semantics.
    Share it only if both consumers require the same contract; keep separate rules
    when their treatment of missing or ambiguous dates differs.
    ---
    name: python-testing
    description: Use when writing, changing, reviewing or organizing Python tests, pytest fixtures or Hypothesis strategies in CCFinance.
    ---
    
    # Python testing
    
    ## Workflow
    
    1. Inspect the code contract, nearby tests, `conftest.py`, shared fixtures and
       strategies, the package's test README, and pytest configuration. Reuse an
       existing test or generator when it covers the behavior; extend it only for a
       distinct, meaningful risk. Do not add tests for trivial or reversible changes
       just to increase counts, or tests that restate implementation details.
    2. Prefer Hypothesis for input variation when a general property is meaningful.
       Prefer a small explicit example for a single known boundary, regression or
       command smoke check. Decide the expected outcome independently of the code
       under test. Use tiny representative data, bounded generators and the smallest
       appropriate test boundary. Assert public behavior, including error contracts.
    3. Place a test beside its source owner under the mirrored `tests/` layout. Reuse
       existing factories and strategies first. Keep a helper local until several
       tests need it; put cross-module strategies in `tests/_strategies.py` and
       shared pytest fixtures in the nearest common `conftest.py`. Place a fixture
       at broader scope only when its state is safe to share. Measure costly setup
       before broadening scope; avoid creating generic fixture frameworks.
    4. Arrange inputs and prerequisites, act on the behavior, and assert observable
       results (AAA). Cleanup belongs in a fixture finalizer or context manager.
       Label each phase with an `# Arrange`, `# Act` or `# Assert` comment, as in
       the example below. Favor DAMP: clear names and visible expected values can
       justify a little repetition.
    5. Give each new or modified test exactly one scope marker from the table below;
       add `slow` or `external` only when applicable. Mark a class or module only
       when every inherited test has the same scope. Never stack or override scope
       markers, including inherited marks. Before using markers, register the six
       names in the owning pytest configuration; unknown names fail under
       `--strict-markers`. This skill defines the policy; it does not mean the
       current unmarked suite already enforces it. Migrate existing tests deliberately
       if adding a collection-time enforcement hook.
    6. During development, run the smallest relevant test or selection and check
       its output. Before handoff run the repository's required full checks, including
       the complete non-Testmon suite. Run any affected slow or external tests when
       their prerequisites and authorization are available; report what was not run
       and why. A targeted pass is not evidence that the full suite passed.
    
    ## Markers
    
    Use only these six custom markers. Built-in pytest mechanisms such as
    `parametrize`, `skipif` and `xfail` remain available for their intended purposes.
    Scope describes the boundary the assertions exercise, not the number of files,
    the use of Hypothesis, or the choice of a reference oracle.
    
    | Marker | Rule |
    | --- | --- |
    | `unit` | Exactly one scope: an isolated operation or small self-contained behavior. |
    | `component` | Exactly one scope: one coherent subsystem or component through its public behavior. |
    | `integration` | Exactly one scope: interactions across components or a real dependency boundary. |
    | `e2e` | Exactly one scope: a complete user-visible workflow through the public CLI or API. A CLI help check alone is not end-to-end. |
    | `slow` | Optional execution label: the complete test, including setup, teardown and generated examples, consistently exceeds two seconds on the normal local environment. Confirm with repeated pytest duration reports; a single noisy measurement is not enough. |
    | `external` | Optional execution label: the test accesses a live network service or external account. Use even if it is usually fast; require explicit opt-in and appropriate credentials. A local temporary file, subprocess or fake alone does not qualify. |
    
    `slow` and `external` are independent and may accompany any one scope. Do not
    invent custom markers for regression, reference, property, smoke, tools or
    implementation techniques; communicate those in descriptive test names and
    assertions. Run fast local iteration with `-m "not slow and not external"`
    after the markers are registered. Full checks must not silently omit slow tests;
    external tests need a separate explicit lane and must not mutate live services
    without authorization.
    
    ## Hypothesis examples and fixtures
    
    Hypothesis strategies generate values; pytest fixtures manage resources. If
    Hypothesis is absent, add it to the locked workspace development dependencies
    when introducing the first test that uses it. Search
    for reusable strategies or an appropriate first-party Hypothesis extra before
    adding one. Compose built-in strategies, use `@composite` for dependent values,
    and generate valid inputs directly rather than filtering most examples. Keep
    sizes bounded and counterexamples understandable. Preserve an important known
    failure using `@example` or an explicit regression; do not duplicate a property
    with a long list of examples that establish the same behavior.
    
    A function-scoped pytest fixture runs once per test function, not once per
    `@given` example. For per-example mutable resources, create and clean them inside
    the test, for example with `TemporaryDirectory()`. Reuse immutable shared data
    only when safe. Do not suppress health checks or disable deadlines globally to
    make a test pass; investigate the cause and document a narrowly justified
    exception. Choose explicit settings or a shared profile only when warranted by
    measured cost. Preserve failing examples and replay information as appropriate.
    
    This self-contained example illustrates a small property, AAA and the scope
    marker; it uses the standard-library URL parser rather than a CCFinance stage:
    
    ```python
    from string import ascii_lowercase, digits
    from urllib.parse import urlsplit
    
    import pytest
    from hypothesis import example, given, strategies as st
    
    
    @pytest.mark.unit
    @example(host="news")
    @given(host=st.text(alphabet=ascii_lowercase + digits, min_size=1, max_size=20))
    def test_url_hostname_normalizes_ascii_case(host: str) -> None:
        # Arrange: build a URL with an uppercase hostname.
        url = f"https://{host.upper()}.example/article"
    
        # Act: extract the hostname.
        hostname = urlsplit(url).hostname
    
        # Assert: the hostname is lowercase.
        assert hostname == f"{host}.example"
    ```
    
    Use a real local Parquet or filesystem boundary for a small integration test
    when that interaction matters; use a stub or fake for costly or nondeterministic
    remote services. A fake cannot establish that the real service works. Keep
    randomized tests independent of execution order; for numerical or sampling
    claims define tolerances and uncertainty rather than requiring arbitrary
    bit-for-bit agreement across environments.
    
    Consult the Hypothesis [tutorial](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorial/),
    [how-to guides](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how-to/),
    [strategies and API reference](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/)
    and [extras](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/extras.html) when
    choosing or debugging a strategy.

    """Parameters and artifacts shared by source sampling and research reports."""
    
    import math
    from pathlib import Path
    from typing import Self
    
    import yaml
    from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator
    
    
    class DatasetInput(BaseModel):
        """A native Parquet glob at an immutable Hub commit."""
    
        model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
        source: str
    
    
    class ComparisonConfig(BaseModel):
        """Shared comparison parameters without environment-variable overrides."""
    
        model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
        seed: int
        draws: int = Field(gt=0)
        domains: Path
        datasets: dict[str, DatasetInput] = Field(min_length=1)
    
    
    class FileRecord(BaseModel):
        """A member of the complete eligible file inventory."""
    
        file: str
        size: int = Field(gt=0)
        identity: str
    
    
    class Draw(BaseModel):
        """One replacement draw, with half-open source row bounds."""
    
        draw: int = Field(ge=0)
        file: str
        row_group: int = Field(ge=0)
        row_start: int = Field(ge=0)
        row_stop: int = Field(gt=0)
        probability: float = Field(gt=0, le=1, allow_inf_nan=False)
        file_size_bytes: int = Field(gt=0)
        file_row_groups: int = Field(gt=0)
        projected_bytes: int = Field(ge=0)
    
    
    class Manifest(BaseModel):
        """The source frame and every planned draw, including repeated groups."""
    
        dataset: str
        source: str
        revision: str
        seed: int
        file_count: int = Field(gt=0)
        listed_bytes: int = Field(gt=0)
        english_definition: str
        footer_bytes: int = Field(ge=0)
        draws: list[Draw] = Field(min_length=1)
    
        @model_validator(mode="after")
        def validate_draws(self) -> Self:
            """Check the probability design before acquiring any article payload."""
            if len({draw.draw for draw in self.draws}) != len(self.draws):
                raise ValueError("Draw identifiers must be unique")
            groups: dict[tuple[str, int], Draw] = {}
            for draw in self.draws:
                if (
                    draw.row_stop <= draw.row_start
                    or draw.row_group >= draw.file_row_groups
                    or not math.isclose(
                        draw.probability, 1 / (self.file_count * draw.file_row_groups)
                    )
                ):
                    raise ValueError("Draw bounds or probability differ from the design")
                key = (draw.file, draw.row_group)
                if key in groups and draw.model_dump(exclude={"draw"}) != groups[
                    key
                ].model_dump(exclude={"draw"}):
                    raise ValueError("Repeated groups have inconsistent metadata")
                groups[key] = draw
            return self
    
    
    class DrawCounts(BaseModel):
        """Nested record counts from one selected group before and after filtering."""
    
        draw: int = Field(ge=0)
        input_rows: int = Field(ge=0)
        english_rows: int = Field(ge=0)
        matched_rows: int = Field(ge=0)
    
        @model_validator(mode="after")
        def validate_counts(self) -> Self:
            """Require retained publisher records to be a subset of English records."""
            if not self.matched_rows <= self.english_rows <= self.input_rows:
                raise ValueError("Counts must satisfy matched <= English <= input rows")
            return self
    
    
    class SampleCounts(BaseModel):
        """Acquisition counts with physical sizes measured once per unique group."""
    
        dataset: str
        draws: list[DrawCounts] = Field(min_length=1)
        elapsed_seconds: float = Field(ge=0, allow_inf_nan=False)
        output_bytes: int = Field(ge=0)
        network_bytes: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)
    
        def ordered_counts(self, manifest: Manifest) -> list[DrawCounts]:
            """Reconcile the acquisition with every planned draw, preserving order."""
            if manifest.dataset != self.dataset:
                raise ValueError("Manifest and acquisition dataset identifiers differ")
            counts = {count.draw: count for count in self.draws}
            if len(counts) != len(self.draws) or set(counts) != {
                draw.draw for draw in manifest.draws
            }:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Manifest and acquisition need matching, unique draw identifiers"
                )
            groups: dict[tuple[str, int], DrawCounts] = {}
            ordered = []
            for draw in manifest.draws:
                count = counts[draw.draw]
                if count.input_rows != draw.row_stop - draw.row_start:
                    raise ValueError(
                        "Acquired row count differs from the selected row bounds"
                    )
                key = (draw.file, draw.row_group)
                if key in groups and count.model_dump(exclude={"draw"}) != groups[
                    key
                ].model_dump(exclude={"draw"}):
                    raise ValueError(
                        "Repeated group selections contain inconsistent counts"
                    )
                groups[key] = count
                ordered.append(count)
            return ordered
    
    
    def load_config(params: Path) -> ComparisonConfig:
        """Read the source-comparison experiment's versioned parameters."""
        document = yaml.safe_load(params.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        return ComparisonConfig.model_validate(document["experiments"]["source_comparison"])

    # Compare publisher yield across public corpora
    
    ## Goal
    
    Implement a small probability-sampled comparison of English publisher retention
    across four public corpora. Prepare manifests and transfer estimates before
    acquiring article payloads. See [methods](methods.md) and the
    [pipeline guide](../../../../../data/inputs/source-comparison/README.md).
    
    ## Acceptance
    
    - [x] Share the publisher filter across the four source projections.
    - [x] Prepare pinned file inventories, random group selections and transfer estimates.
    - [x] Verify weighting, row-group pruning and the full repository quality gates.
    - [x] Document the acquisition commands and limits on population inference.
    
    The four metadata preparation stages are recorded in `dvc.lock`; article
    acquisition and research estimates have not run. `devenv shell -- just check`
    passed, including 27 Python tests. The pipeline guide records the selected sizes.

    type: changelog
    description: Changes to CCFinance data engineering, research workflows and repository tooling.

    # CHANGELOG
    
    ## Unreleased
    
    ### Added
    
    - Source-comparison DVC stages with metadata preparation, selective Parquet reads
      and exploratory estimates of publisher-filter yield.
    - Statsmodels LaTeX summaries and individual yield and population tables for papers.
    - Frozen Fine News acquisition recipe with the historical publisher filter.
    - Python and LaTeX toolchains generated from Exordio, with locked dependencies.
    - Typer `pipeline` application and a namespace for data processing stages.
    - DVC repository configuration and a workspace for research data.
    - Ruff, strict Pyrefly, Tach, tests and package builds in local checks and CI.
    - Planning and local reference workflows with Schematter validation and Insitu views.
    - A validated changelog with a closed set of change categories.
    - Semflow integration for reviewing and checking semantic DVC fingerprints.
    - pytest-layout-enforcer for source-aligned test paths.
    - Justfile formatting and analysis checks in pre-commit and CI.
    - Agent skill schema and validation for metadata, structure and length.
    - AgentSync-managed shared instructions, skills and Codex configuration.
    
    ### Changed
    
    - Restored the published Fine News shards with verified checksums and provenance
      so the frozen acquisition stage has real outputs for DVC to validate.
    - Grouped experiments within each data layer and consolidated source mappings
      and validated artifact contracts across sampling and research reports.
    - Organized the pipeline into `raw`, `processed` and `research` layers, with
      matching Python modules, CLI groups and proposed data paths.

    Add: /home/marcussky/Git/CCFinance/src/python/apps/pipeline/src/pipeline/experiments/article_labels.py
    """Versioned operating parameters for provisional article-company labels."""
    
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import yaml
    from pydantic import AwareDatetime, BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
    
    
    class ArticleLabelsConfig(BaseModel):
        """Keep decision policy, inference limits and the deadline explicit."""
    
        model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    
        seed: int = 42
        deadline_utc: AwareDatetime
        reserve_seconds: int = Field(default=1800, ge=0)
        server_url: str = "http://127.0.0.1:8008"
        api_model: str = "kev-latest"
        model: str = "jaredpalmer/kev-0.8b"
        model_revision: str = Field(pattern=r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$")
        base_model: str = "Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base"
        base_revision: str = Field(pattern=r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$")
        runtime_manifest: Path = Path("data/inputs/article-labels/runtime.json")
        max_context_tokens: int = Field(default=8192, gt=0)
        max_candidates_per_request: int = Field(default=32, gt=0)
        concurrency: int = Field(default=1, gt=0)
        benchmark_size: int = Field(default=100, gt=0)
        request_timeout_seconds: float = Field(default=60, gt=0, allow_inf_nan=False)
        min_probability: float = Field(default=0.95, ge=0, le=1, allow_inf_nan=False)
        precision_target: float = Field(default=0.95, gt=0, le=1, allow_inf_nan=False)
    
    
    def load_config(params: Path) -> ArticleLabelsConfig:
        """Read the article-labeling experiment without environment overrides."""
        document = yaml.safe_load(params.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        return ArticleLabelsConfig.model_validate(document["experiments"]["article_labels"])

    Add: /home/marcussky/Git/CCFinance/data/inputs/article-labels/README.md
    # Article labels and research filters
    
    This experiment separates fast company-candidate selection from model judgments
    about issuer identity and editorial coverage. Its initial source is the restored
    [Fine News snapshot](../fine-news/README.md). The historical 115-domain allowlist
    is a working acquisition policy, not a reviewed list of trusted publishers.
    
    ## CPU selection
    
    The prior Rust Aho–Corasick run covers the same 168 source shards. Adoption checks
    the source manifest and every prediction chunk before reusing it. Article keys
    use the source's relative path and physical row number; native article IDs are
    preserved but are not assumed unique. Candidate names and publisher ticker
    annotations remain evidence rather than relevance labels.
    
    The processed output stores compact retained and excluded indexes with evidence,
    quality flags and exact-text hashes. Article text remains in the immutable raw
    snapshot and is joined through source coordinates when needed. This representation
    avoids duplicating article bodies. All source rows remain accounted for, including
    no-candidate, missing-date and ambiguous cases. Exact-text groups preserve their
    source memberships; they do not establish complete syndicated-story deduplication.
    
    Current names, aliases and issuer crosswalks are not all certified historical
    identities. Keep these limitations and unknown membership years explicit. Do not
    remove genuine company-name tokens or interpret a no-hit result as proof that
    an article is irrelevant.
    
    ## Decision questions
    
    Native Kev-0.8B runs separately from the pipeline's Python environment. The
    [runtime manifest](runtime.json) pins its source, checkpoint and serving stack.
    The client uses Pydantic's typed System One decision interface. Every article
    provides shared evidence; questions contain structured candidate identities and
    explicit criteria. Question keys alone do not describe a company.
    
    One identity Noul and one editorial-role Choice are requested per candidate.
    Coverage roles are incidental, substantive secondary and central; several issuers
    may be central. Article-kind classification distinguishes editorial reporting,
    analysis/opinion and market roundups from press releases, promotional material,
    non-articles and unresolved content. All questions normally share one request.
    Oversized candidate sets use bounded requests without dropping candidates.
    
    Keep complete probability distributions. Apply identity acceptance before
    interpreting coverage. A central-subject probability is a model judgment under
    the authored rubric, not measured annotation accuracy. Do not multiply independent
    answers into a claimed calibrated joint probability. Changing filtering thresholds
    must reuse saved predictions.
    
    ## Timing and interpretation
    
    Parameters live under `experiments.article_labels` in the root parameter file.
    The initial completion target is 07:00 SAST on 17 November 2026, reserving the
    final 30 minutes for reconciliation and reports. Measure the actual CPU survivors
    and end-to-end native Kev throughput before deciding whether full scoring fits.
    Neither a one-million-document population nor an inference rate is assumed.
    
    All initial model labels are provisional. AI-assisted review and its agreement
    statistics do not establish human-validated precision or recall. The 95% precision
    target is an experimental design goal. Keep failures, unsupported contexts and
    pending records separate from negative classifications. Company-year reports
    distinguish candidate coverage from scored substantive coverage and do not infer

    # Native decision inference
    
    These scripts run the pinned native Kev server using the CUDA libraries of an
    already cached container image. SGLang is not launched. Native Kev shares the
    article prefix across its independent identity and coverage questions.
    
    From the repository root, prepare the small serving dependencies and then supply
    the existing checkpoint and Hugging Face base-model cache:
    
    ```bash
    bash infra/inference/setup.sh
    bash infra/inference/start.sh /path/to/kev-0.8b /path/to/huggingface/hub
    docker logs ccfinance-kev-native
    curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:8008/v1/models
    ```
    
    The versioned runtime manifest records the model, source, image, precision,
    kernels and admission limit. The entrypoint applies that limit to both the
    article and every complete article-question sequence. Oversized inputs fail
    explicitly; text truncation is disabled. Local package and compilation caches
    live under ignored `.runtime/`.
    
    Stop the server with `docker stop ccfinance-kev-native`; remove its stopped
    container with `docker rm ccfinance-kev-native` before starting a replacement.
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    repo_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
    runtime="$repo_root/.runtime"
    source_commit=2074cc44256200bb37540103fa4572901faa10f3
    image=lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:f7876bef696ccf9cf75a2bf7ccb82970f5fac577f082fb8ca95c9a59d2160eb5
    mkdir -p "$runtime/serving-site"
    if [[ ! -d "$runtime/kev/.git" ]]; then
        git init "$runtime/kev"
        git -C "$runtime/kev" remote add origin https://github.com/jaredpalmer/kev.git
        git -C "$runtime/kev" fetch --depth 1 origin "$source_commit"
        git -C "$runtime/kev" checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD
    fi
    test "$(git -C "$runtime/kev" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$source_commit"
    docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null
    docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
        --mount "type=bind,source=$runtime/serving-site,target=/runtime-site" \
        --mount "type=bind,source=$repo_root/infra/inference/requirements.txt,target=/requirements.txt,readonly" \
        --entrypoint python "$image" -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check \
        --no-cache-dir --no-deps --target /runtime-site -r /requirements.txt
