    {"i": 0, "title": "GLOBAL MARKETS-Shares retreat as Fed minutes soften stimulus bias", "date": "2012-04-04", "candidates": [["top1000:52840", "MSCI Inc.", "MSCI"]], "text": "GLOBAL MARKETS-Shares retreat as Fed minutes soften stimulus bias\n* MSCI Asia ex-Japan falls 0.8 pct, Nikkei sheds 1.7 pct\n* Gold, copper pressured as dollar firms\n* European shares likely fall\nBy Chikako Mogi\nTOKYO, April 4 Asian shares fell on Wednesday after the minutes from the U.S. Federal Reserve's March meeting reduced expectations of further stimulus measures to spur growth, leaving investors looking for more clues to the global economic outlook.\nEuropean equity markets will likely follow the weak Asian mood, with financial spreadbetters predicting major European markets to open as much as 0.8 percent lower. U.S. stock futures were down 0.4 percent.\nFed policymakers remained focused on a still elevated jobless rate while noting signs of slightly stronger growth, but the minutes suggested the appetite for further quantitative easing, so-called QE3, has waned significantly in light of an improving U.S. economy.\nAlong with falling stocks, gold extended losses from Tuesday's 2 percent while the dollar held on to gains.\nMSCI's broadest index of Asia Pacific shares outside Japan fell 0.8 percent. Japan's Nikkei average fell more than 2 percent, and below the key 10,000 points level, to a one-month low, raising concerns that Tokyo's strong equities rally so far this year was screeching to a halt.\n\"The minutes do not suggest any change in the Fed's broad policy stance, and the central bank still stands ready to take additional easing measures if economic conditions worsen,\" said Makoto Noji, senior strategist at SMBC Nikko Securities.\n\"While the U.S. economy is firming now, signs of slowdown in Australia, China and the euro zone would eventually put downside risks to the export-reliant U.S. economy,\" he said.\nHong Kong and Shanghai markets were closed for a public holiday.\nGOLD AND DOLLAR\nSpot gold fell 0.1 percent to $1,645 an ounce while U.S. gold futures slipped as much as 1.8 percent to $1,642 an ounce. Copper fell 0.7 percent to $8,510 a tonne on waning hopes for more Fed stimulus.\nMining firms weighed on Australian shares while the Australian dollar tumbled to a fresh 11-week low of $1.0263 after the country's trade balance surprisingly showed a deficit in February.\nDiminished expectations of QE3 - the creation of money by the central bank to buy assets - lifted the dollar index against a basket of key currencies to its highest since March 26. But the dollar struggled to gain further against the yen after recovering from Tuesday's three-week low of 81.55 yen.\nWhether gold closes the week above or below its 55-week moving average, which stands at $1,642, will set the direction for not only bullion prices but also the dollar, analysts say.\n\"Everything is linked through the phenomenon of massive cash supply from central banks,\" said a Singapore-based trader. \"The minutes seem to support a view that the Fed is not going to pump more and more cash into the markets.\"\nMore Fed stimulus would be tantamount to printing money and depreciate the dollar's value, which in turn would enhance the appeal of gold.\nNON-FARM PAYROLLS, DEBT SALES\nThe markets will face key U.S. non-farm payrolls data on Friday, which could offer further evidence for a reduced need of additional monetary measures to spur faster economic growth.\nThe U.S. economy likely notched up a fourth month of solid job growth in March and is expected to have added 203,000 jobs last month, according to a Reuters survey, after non-farm payrolls rose 227,000 in February.\nIn a double test of appetite for lower-rated debts, the Spanish Treasury will sell up to 3.5 billion euros ($4.67 billion) in debt and Portugal will offer 18-month bills for the first time since March 2011, a month before the European Union and International Monetary Fund staged a rescue.\nOil also extended its decline as the Fed dashed hopes of further economic stimulus for the world's largest oil consumer, while top crude exporter Saudi Arabia pledged to keep output high in the event of a strategic stocks release.\nU.S. crude futures eased 0.5 percent to $103.53 a barrel while Brent fell 0.2 percent to $124.62.\nA recent rise in oil prices is one indication for recovery staying on track, and concerns about high oil prices hurting U.S. growth may be overblown, some argue.\n\"U.S. gasoline demand falling to its weakest since 2001 in January suggests the impact from rising oil prices is not as damaging to consumer sentiment and the broad economy as in the past when demand for gasoline was strong,\" said Tetsu Emori, a Tokyo-based commodities fund manager at Astmax Investments."}
    {"i": 1, "title": "Ford recalls 2,900 EV F-150 Lightning pickup trucks", "date": "2022-06-27", "candidates": [["top1000:20750", "FORD MOTOR CO", "F"]], "text": "Ford recalls 2,900 EV F-150 Lightning pickup trucks\nRegister now for FREE unlimited access to Reuters.com\nJune 27 (Reuters) - Ford Motor Co (F.N) said Monday it will recall about 2,900 F-150 Lightning trucks because a software issue may result in a failure to provide adequate warning of low tire pressure.\nThe recall is the first for the Ford electric pickup truck. Ford said the trucks tire pressure monitoring system light may not illuminate when intended and may not be able to provide adequate warning of low tire inflation pressure because the recommended tire cold inflation pressure value was incorrectly set to 35 psi rather than the correct inflation pressure of 42 psi.\nThe recall covers 2,666 U.S. vehicles and 220 in Canada. There are no accidents or injuries connected to the recall.\nFord said low tire inflation pressure may lead to poor vehicle handling and a possible loss of vehicle control, which could increase the risk of a crash. Dealers will update the Body Control Module software for undelivered vehicles and customers who want the remedy immediately, a fix that takes approximately 20 minutes.\nFord will also have the software update available through an over-the-air update in 30 days for all current customers.\nRegister now for FREE unlimited access to Reuters.com\nOur Standards: The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles."}
    {"i": 2, "title": "Novartis says experimental drug helps chronic migraine sufferers", "date": "2016-09-16", "candidates": [["top1000:11901", "Match Group, Inc.", "IACI"], ["top1000:216", "Amgen Inc.", "AMGN"], ["top1000:2664", "Bath & Body Works, Inc.", "LB"], ["gh:0000318154", "Amgen Inc.", "AMGN"]], "text": "ZURICH About 40 percent of chronic migraine sufferers taking an experimental drug developed by Novartis and Amgen saw the number of days they suffered a migraine cut by at least half, beating the placebo in the trial.\nThe latest analysis from the mid-phase study amounted to a \"statistically significant reduction in monthly migraine days\", Novartis said about the experimental AMG 334 compound. \nNovartis has struck pacts with its U.S.-based rival Amgen to develop migraine and Alzheimer's treatments as it seeks to bolster its neuroscience portfolio.\n\"These important data further support the efficacy of AMG 334 in patients who currently have limited therapeutic options,\" said Vasant Narasimhan, global head of drug development and chief medical officer for Novartis.\nThe release follows data from June showing AMG 334, whose generic name is erenumab, had achieved its main goal of reducing the number of monthly attacks, regardless of dosage, compared to a placebo.\nAccording to the latest analysis of the 667-person Phase II study, 40 percent of those taking a 70 milligram (mg) dose and 41 percent of those on a 140 mg dose saw the number of days they suffered a migraine cut by at least half.\nOnly 24 percent of those getting the placebo drug had a similar reduction.\n\"This is part of ongoing research,\" a Novartis spokesman said on Friday. \"We are continuing to analyze the data from the chronic migraine trial and across the entire AMG 334 (erenumab) program in an effort to better understand who will respond.\" \nNovartis is also studying AMG 334 in people suffering from episodic migraines.\nThe safety profile for erenumab was similar to the placebo group.\nUnder the collaboration agreement with Novartis, Amgen holds sales rights for the United States, Canada and Japan, while Novartis would sell the drug in Europe and the rest of the world, if it wins regulatory approval.\n (Reporting by John Miller; editing by David Clarke)\n "}
    {"i": 3, "title": "Fleetwood leads as storm clouds gather at BMW PGA Championship", "date": "2022-09-08", "candidates": [["top1000:21541", "RYDER SYSTEM INC", "R"]], "text": "Fleetwood leads as storm clouds gather at BMW PGA Championship\nLONDON :Stormy weather provided a fitting backdrop for the opening round of the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth on Thursday where players on both sides of golf's bitter power struggle were in action on the soggy fairways.\nThe flagship tournament of the DP World Tour (formerly the European Tour) has been overshadowed by the presence of 17 golfers who have signed up for the divisive LIV Tour - the Saudi-backed series rocking golf's status quo.\nNorthern Ireland's four-time major champion Rory McIlroy, one of the favourites for the title has pulled no punches in criticising some of his former Ryder Cup colleagues who have jumped ship for the LIV Tour riches.\nHe is joined in a strong field by the likes of U.S. Open champion Matt Fitzpatrick, 2021 Wentworth winner Billy Horschel and Spain's former U.S. Open winner John Rahm, all of whom have had nothing to do with the LIV Tour.\nEngland's Tommy Fleetwood, another player who is not part of the LIV breakaway tour, topped the leaderboard midway through Thursday's opening round with a superb eight-under 64, finishing with four successive birdies.\nFellow Englishman Jordan Matthew was second after a 65 with 2019 Open champion Shane Lowry, who described the presence of LIV golfers as 'disruptive', carding a 66.\nOf the LIV Tour contingent, Austria's Bernd Wiesberger was the highest-placed on four-under after 17 holes.\nMcIlroy has said it would be \"hard to stomach\" playing alongside the likes of Ian Poulter, Lee Westwood and Sergio Garcia at Wentworth and re-stated his opposition on Wednesday.\nFormer Europe Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley, a DP World Tour board member, told Sky Sports that those signed up for the LIV Tour should not be playing at Wentworth.\n\"They've decided to leave the collective that is the European Tour which is a little bit like a trade union where everybody's in together and then the value of that collective is used to lever and get commercial opportunities,\" he said.\n\"Should you leave that collective that's fine, you go on a different path, but you then shouldn't be allowed to come back and also play as part of a collective that you left and are actually hurting economically.\"\nThe LIV Tour, which was launched at the first event near London in June, boasts an eye-popping $255 million in prize-money - dwarfing what is available on the DP World Tour.\nUnlike the powerful PGA Tour, which has suspended players such as Phil Mickelson and Dustin Johnson for jumping ship, the DP World Tour has not yet followed suit with a court case next year likely to decide whether they can play in both.\nMcIlroy was at least spared any awkwardness as he was paired for his first round with Fitzpatrick and Horschel in front of large galleries hiding under umbrellas from the heavy showers.\nThere was no disguising the tension in the air as the LIV Tour signees began their rounds, but McIlroy let his golf do the talking as he opened with a four-under 68."}
    {"i": 4, "title": "Gaudium IVF IPO listing date today. GMP, experts suggest muted debut of shares in stock market today | Stock Market News", "date": "2026-02-27", "candidates": [["gh:0000909832", "Costco Wholesale Corporation", "COST"]], "text": " Ankit Gohel\nPublished27 Feb 2026, 06:18 AM IST\nGaudium IVF & Women Health IPO Listing: The equity shares of Gaudium IVF & Women Health Ltd will be listed in the Indian stock market today after its initial public offering received strong demand. Gaudium IVF IPO listing date is today, 27 February 2026, Friday.\nThe public issue of the In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) treatments major was open for public subscription from February 20 to 24, and the IPO allotment date was February 25. Gaudium IVF IPO listing date is today, February 27, and the shares will be listed on both the stock exchanges, BSE and NSE.\n“Trading Members of the Exchange are hereby informed that effective from Friday, February 27, 2026, the equity shares of Gaudium IVF and Women Health Limited shall be listed and admitted to dealings on the Exchange in the list of ‘T’ Group of Securities,” said a notice on the BSE.\nGaudium IVF and Women Health shares will be in the Trade-for-Trade segment for 10 trading days.\nFurther the trading members may please note that the above-mentioned scrip will be a part of Special Pre-open Session (SPOS) on Friday, February 27, 2026, it added, and the stock will be available for trading from 10:00 AM.\nAhead of Gaudium IVF IPO listing today, investors watch out for the trends in the grey market premium (GMP) to gauge the estimated listing price. Gaudium IVF IPO GMP today and analysts signal a muted listing of shares.\nHere’s what Gaudium IVF IPO GMP today signals:\nGaudium IVF & Women Health shares are not commanding any premium or discount in the unlisted market. According to websites tracking the grey market, Gaudium IVF IPO GMP today is ₹0 per share. This indicates that in the grey market, Gaudium IVF shares are trading equal to their issue price, without any premium or discount.\nGaudium IVF IPO GMP today signals that the estimated listing price of the stock would be ₹79 apiece, which is at par to the issue price of ₹79 per share.\nAnalysts also expect Gaudium IVF & Women Health shares to see a muted listing in the Indian stock market today.\nThe bidding for Gaudium IVF IPO began on Friday, February 20, and closed on Tuesday, February 24. The IPO allotment date was February 25, Wednesday, while Gaudium IVF IPO listing date is today, February 27, Friday. Gaudium IVF & Women Health shares will be listed on BSE and NSE.\nGaudium IVF & Women Health IPO price band was set at ₹75 to ₹79 per share. The company raised ₹165 crore from the public issue, which was a combination of fresh issue of 1.14 crore equity shares worth ₹90 crore, and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of 94.93 lakh shares amounting to ₹75 crore.\nGaudium IVF IPO was subscribed 7.27 times in total, NSE data showed. The public issue was booked 7.60 times in the Retail Individual Investors category, and 14.05 times in the Non Institutional Investors (NII) segment. The Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) category received 1.62 times subscription.\nSarthi Capital Advisors Pvt. Ltd. is the book running lead manager and Bigshare Services Pvt. Ltd. is the Gaudium IVF IPO registrar.\nGet Latest real-time updates\nCatch all the Business News , Market News , Breaking News Events and Latest News Updates on Live Mint. Download The Mint News App to get Daily Market Updates.\nBusiness NewsMarketsIPOGaudium IVF IPO listing date today. GMP, experts suggest muted debut of shares in stock market today"}
    {"i": 5, "title": "At Ayodhya Deepotsav, grandeur of 'treta yug' comes alive", "date": "2020-11-13", "candidates": [["top1000:11901", "Match Group, Inc.", "IAC"], ["top1000:54433", "NEWS CORP", "NWS"], ["top1000:54824", "NAVIENT CORP", "NAVI"]], "text": "AYODHYA (UP): The Uttar Pradesh government on Friday went all out in marking the homecoming of Lord Ram to this holy town – the mythical event in 'treta yug' on which the festival of Diwali is based.\nSo, there was the reenactment of the arrival of God Ram and Goddess Sita on their 'pushpak viman', a laser and sound show, cultural programmes and the lighting of a record 5.51 lakh earthen lamps on the banks of the Saryu. The figure has been claimed by the government.\nChief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Governor Anandiben Patel were there at Ayodhya's 'Deepotsav', the first since the groundbreaking ceremony earlier this year of a Ram temple in the holy town.\nSeveral new development projects were launched to mark the occasion.\n\"Our generation is not only fortunate to see the start of the construction of a Ram temple here but we also attended the historic event. In the struggle of 500 years, many saints passed away with a dream to see the start of construction. I thank PM Modi who is the one who implemented the ideology of Ram Rajya,\" Adityanath said while addressing the 'Deepotsav' event here.\nPrime Minister Narendra Modi had performed the 'bhoomi pujan' of a Supreme Court-mandated Ram temple in Ayodhya on August 5 this year, bringing to fruition the BJP's 'mandir' movement that defined its politics for three decades and took it to the heights of power.\n\"It is the dream of PM Modi to develop Ayodhya as Vedic Ramayana City and it should be the most beautiful. We are here to seek support of you all as to how it can be developed that it has glimpse of a Vedic city,\" the chief minister said.\nActors representing Lord Ram, Goddess Sita and Lakshman descended on the Saryu bank in a 'pushpak viman' -- a helicopter that sprinkled rose petals -- and were received by the governor and the chief minister.\nThe BJP government in Uttar Pradesh started Deepotsav celebration in Ayodhya after Yogi Adityanath became the chief minister in March 2017.\nAs a special Diwali gift from the chief minister, Ayodhya will get an international airport project this time.\nThe celebrations began from Friday afternoon itself when a grand coronation procession of Lord Ram started from Saket college in Ayodhya to reach the riverbank after covering a stretch of about five kilometres. The procession has 11 tableaux, built on the Ramayana themes, participating in it.\nThe themes include Gurukul Shiksha, Ram-Sita Vivah, Kewat Prasang, Ram Darbaar, Shabri-Ram Milaap and Lanka Dahan among others. Besides the Saryu bank, the Ram Janmabhoomi, the site of upcoming Ram temple, was lit up by 11,000 earthen lamps in the evening, when a grand Aarti was held at the Saryu river after the sunset.\nOther projects for people of Ayodhya include a modern sewage treatment plant to maintain the flow and cleanliness of the river. The pilgrim town will also have an international Ramlila Centre to be built at a cost of around Rs 3.47 crore, a 'Bhajan' site at Rs 19.02 crore, a Queen Heo Memorial Park for Rs 21.92 crore, a Ram Katha Gallery worth Rs 7.59 crore, the expansion of Ram Katha Park at Rs 2.75 crore and the beautification of Ram ki Paidi at Rs 12.65 crore, officials said.\nAmong development projects, the holy city will also have a modern bus stand (Rs 7.40 crore), a multi-level parking lot (Rs 16.44 crore) and the renovation of road and footpaths (Rs 8.40 crore) besides others, they said.\nHailing the prime minister for India's fight against the coronavirus, Adityanath said, \"We are fighting strongly under his (PM's) leadership and we will defeat the virus.\"\nIn her speech, the Governor said Ram and Ramrajya were \"inseparable parts of the Indian culture\" and spoke at length about the ideals of the Maryada Purushottam.\nShe advised the people not to lower their guards in their fight against the pandemic till it was finished.\nDeputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya, BJP state president Swatantra Dev Singh and a number of saints and ministers were present on the occasion.\nWith a view to ensuring a global recognition and identity to Ayodhya, Adityanath has initiated a number of works in the temple town including Deepotsav being organised on the occasion of Diwali every year.\n\"Since the formation of the Adityanath government in Uttar Pradesh, many events have been organised, from Deepotsav to Ram Leela, which have earned a new identity to Ayodhya globally,\" a government spokesman said on Friday.\nGiving an account of the works in the temple town, he said apart from setting up of Navya Ayodhya as the coordinated model of Vedic and modern city, the grandest and divine temple of Lord Ram, a tall statue of the Hindu deity -- which would be the world's tallest statue -- is set to leave an \"indelible impression\" on the people of the world.\nA four-lane road from Ayodhya to Sultanpur National Highway (NH) 330 to the airport is to be renovated at a cost of Rs 18.75 crore. The National Highways Authority of India is making a proposal for construction of a bypass for Ayodhya Dham from Sohawal to Vikramjot, the spokesman said.\nThe work of widening of the four-lane road from Rae Bareli to Ayodhya is also to be done at a cost of about Rs 1,500 crore, he said.\nRecently, at a review meeting of the tourism department, the chief minister had said that to make Ayodhya a global city for tourism, a consultant has to be zeroed in on accordingly.\nRead More News on\nDownload The Economic Times News App to get Daily Market Updates & Live Business News."}
    {"i": 6, "title": "European shares steady, hope for U.S. payrolls boost", "date": "2012-11-02", "candidates": [["top1000:20235", "AUTOMATIC DATA PROCESSING, INC.", "ADP"], ["top1000:31769", "NOV Inc.", "NOV"], ["top1000:7882", "Costco Wholesale Corporation", "COST"], ["gh:0000008670", "AUTOMATIC DATA PROCESSING, INC.", "ADP"], ["gh:0000909832", "Costco Wholesale Corporation", "COST"]], "text": "BRIEF-Civista Bancshares prices offering at $21.75 per share\n* Civista Bancshares, Inc. announces pricing of offering of common shares\nX\n* FTSEurofirst 300 flat, EuroSTOXX 50 off 0.2 pct\n    * U.S. data boosts expectations of strong jobs number\n    * Alcatel down, Beiersdorf up in mixed earnings season\n    By Toni Vorobyova\n    LONDON, Nov 2 European equities steadied on\nFriday, looking to the U.S. jobs report for reassurance on the\nhealth of the world's biggest economy that might give key\nindexes the momentum to test two-week highs.\n    The pan-European FTSEurofirst 300 was flat at\n1,109.70 points at 0835 GMT, while the EuroSTOXX 50 index of\neuro zone blue chips edged 0.2 percent lower to 2,529.66 points,\noff the previous session's intra-day high of 2,541.87.\n    Expectations for a strong reading from the U.S. non-farm\npayroll report - the last before next week's presidential\nelections - were bolstered by a better than expected ADP private\nsector employment report and ISM manufacturing index in the\nprevious session. \n    \"The ADP figures were quite good ... and there is a rather\nhigh likelihood that U.S. government did not lay off staff this\nmonth as well, and that would be good for non-farm payrolls,\"\nsaid Peter Garnry, equity strategist at Saxo Bank.\n    \"If the non-farm payrolls are better than expected, I think\nit could be a catalyst for the market to continue the momentum\nfrom yesterday going into the weekend.\"\n    A number above the 125,000 consensus could help the\nEuroSTOXX 50 break out of the 165 point range of around 2,440 to\n2,605 it has held to since mid-September.\n    That followed a rally of more than 460 points in the two\nprevious months on a European Central Bank pledge to protect the\neuro.\n    \"If the positive tone continues, we will have a new trading\nsignal if we have new highs compared to yesterday,\" said Petra\nKerssenbrock, technical analyst at Commerzbank, forecasting that\nEuroSTOXX 50 could test 2,600 by year-end.\n    \n    The economic health of the United States has become\nincreasingly key for European companies as the region stutters\ndue to the debt crisis. The third quarter earnings season has\nunderscored the divide, as companies with strong foreign\nrevenues outperform home-focused peers.\n    A 15 percent drop in revenues in Europe pushed telecom\nequipment market Alcatel towards a bigger than\nexpected third quarter loss, shaving 7.2 percent off the share\nprice on Friday.\n    Skincare manufacturer Beiersdorf rallied 6.6\npercent after raising its 2012 outlook thanks to a strong\nperformance in emerging markets. \n    With the third quarter earnings season half way through, 44\npercent of companies in developed Europe have missed forecasts\nand the remainder are expected to undershoot by on average 1.6\npercent, according to Thomson Reuters Starmine data.\n            \n            \n            \n            \n\t"}
    {"i": 7, "title": "Lucy Hale's Secret To Repeating Outfits, The Trend She's Most Excited For & Her New Degree Campaign", "date": "2018-03-19", "candidates": [["top1000:11901", "Match Group, Inc.", "IAC"], ["top1000:54824", "NAVIENT CORP", "NAVI"]], "text": "As the star of the hit TV show Pretty Little Liars and with a major role on the CW’s new series Life Sentence—not to mention her upcoming releases Truth or Dare, Dude and The Unicorn—it’s fair to assume that Lucy Hale can get her hands on pretty much whatever she wants to wear. But just like the rest of us, she actually loves to repeat outfits. And her new campaign with Degree is making that even easier. She accepted the Degree challenge to re-wear a piece from her closet and proved that her chic black top remained streak-free. That’s because the Ultraclear Black + White antiperspirants don’t leave yellow stains on light clothing or white marks on darker hues. She tells us all about it, plus shares her fashion and beauty wisdom.\nWhy was partnering with Degree a good fit for you? The whole purpose of the Ultraclear Black + White Antiperspirants is you’re able to re-wear articles of clothing and re-wear your favorite items. For me that felt super authentic and organic because I do that all the time. Not everyone sees that I do that, but I love having a favorite item and mixing it to create new looks. This deodorant is amazing because you’re usually trying to avoid putting on your black clothes because of all the streaks and the marks and this doesn’t do that at all. It comes in a spray form and a solid, but I love the spray form—it smells so good. Everyone should have it.\nWhat is your beauty routine like? I’m pretty diligent about my skincare routine and there’s a lot of steps to it. I’m letting my skin breathe and keeping it clear so the routine revolves around that. I typically don’t wear a lot of makeup, but if I do it’s just concealer, mascara and a good highlighter. But (for work) I love getting dressed up and trying new things. I have such a fun glam team who is always willing to do new things and making me feel like a human on days when I don’t necessarily feel like a human. I am sort of like the best of both worlds because I love putting on a dress and lipstick and going out, but I also love the complete opposite of that too.\nWhat are your beauty staples? Sunscreen—Skinceuticals has a really good one. Lucas Papaw Ointment, because it’s amazing. Any makeup wipes. Deodorant. And I really love micellar water lately because you wash your skin, you think you have everything off. But if you swipe over your face with that you’re like, oh, unaware that was still there.\nWhat have you learned from working with your glam squad? There’s so many things that people have put me in on a show, or my stylist has pulled for me, or a makeup look that I never in a million years would think would work and so being surrounded by all these people pushes me to try new things. It’s really cool to have access to new designers that I never would have heard of before because if it were up to me I’d probably play it safe. It’s nice to have people to challenge you to try new things.\nWhat spring fashion trend are you most excited for? Yellow is really big right now. I love a good mustard, but bright yellow is back and I love a good monochromatic look. I saw this outfit the other day—it was yellow shoes, yellow pants, and a yellow top and it looked amazing. So I’ll have to try that next.\nIt’s an unexpected color. Yeah, it can be a little obnoxious but they’re making it work. It’s like a walking highlighter.\nWhat’s a fashion rule worth breaking? I used to not mix metals. If I wore silver I couldn’t wear gold. If I wore gold I couldn’t wear silver or if I wore black I couldn’t wear brown. But there are ways to make it cool and ways to make it work. And mixing patterns is fun too, like unexpected patterns."}
    {"i": 8, "title": "Apple 'Confirms' iPhone 8 Has A Nasty Surprise", "date": "2017-09-28", "candidates": [["top1000:45483", "Alphabet Inc.", "GOOG"], ["top1000:54084", "Meta Platforms, Inc.", "FB"], ["top1000:54638", "TWITTER, INC.", "TWTR"], ["top1000:54824", "NAVIENT CORP", "NAVI"], ["top1000:7", "Apple Inc.", "AAPL"]], "text": "This is not one of \n  \n‘Great Secret Features’ and ‘Nasty Surprises’ are my regular columns investigating operating system updates for the best features / biggest problems hidden behind the headlines.\nSpeaking to The Verge, an Apple spokesperson said the company is aware of a ‘crackling’ fault in the iPhone 8’s earpiece which disrupts audio during phone and FaceTime calls. The consequence is there’s currently little ‘phone’ about this new iPhone.\nThe good news is Apple said “Our team is at work on a fix, which will be included in an upcoming software release”, though it declined to provide a more precise timescale.\nInterestingly Apple said it believes only a “small number” of iPhone 8s are affected, but with numerous complaints from affected iPhone 8 owners spread across MacRumors, Apple’s official Communities support forum, Reddit and @applesupport being flooded with complaints on Twitter this seems optimistic. Especially considering the iPhone 8 has been on sale less than a week and far fewer have been sold than normal as fans patiently wait for the more ambitious iPhone X.\nIt is worth pointing out there are also complaints from affected iPhone 8 Plus users, but so far these appear to less frequent. This might be because of a component difference with the iPhone 8 or simply because fewer iPhone 8 Plus phones have been sold (there’s only $50 between a top tier iPhone 8 Plus and the iPhone X).\nPerhaps the best news, however, comes from reading between the lines in Apple’s statement. While affected users might wait a while, the fact Apple states the crackle will be fixed “in an upcoming software release” suggests this isn’t a hardware issue and a mass recall isn’t necessary. Then again this depends on how well the software fix does its job.\nIt’s also important affected iPhone 8 and iPhone 8 Plus owners are vigilant. Apple boosted the external speakers on both new iPhones by 25% compared to the iPhone 7 and iPhone 7 Plus. If this was a factor in the fault and the upcoming iOS fix works by reducing their volume, then that’s not a satisfactory solution.\nBut let’s not get ahead of ourselves. As it stands the iPhone 8 and (possibly to a lesser extent) iPhone 8 Plus officially have a problem, but Apple deserves credit for stepping up and taking this on the chin. Now let’s see that fix ASAP.\n___\nFollow Gordon on Twitter, Facebook and Google+\nMore On Forbes\nApple’s New iPhones Have Nasty Surprises\nApple iOS 11 Has 25 Great Secret Features\niPhone X Vs iPhone 8: What's The Difference?"}
    {"i": 9, "title": "UPDATE 2-EU delays enforcing new Russia sanctions", "date": "2014-09-08", "candidates": [["top1000:11901", "Match Group, Inc.", "IACI"], ["top1000:20561", "TARGET CORP", "TGT"], ["top1000:30474", "RELIANCE, INC.", "RS"], ["top1000:4998", "WEST PHARMACEUTICAL SERVICES INC", "WST"]], "text": "* EU allows time to see if Ukraine ceasefire holds\n* Sanctions now expected to take effect “in next few days”\n* EU doves seize on ceasefire to block new sanctions (Updates with decision)\nBy Jan Strupczewski and Adrian Croft\nBRUSSELS, Sept 8 (Reuters) - The European Union adopted new sanctions against Russia over its involvement in the Ukraine war on Monday, but delayed enforcing them to leave time to assess whether a ceasefire in Ukraine is holding.\nThe sanctions, which target the ability of Russia’s top oil producers to raise capital in Europe, were originally due to take effect on Tuesday.\nBut that was pushed back by a few days after some EU governments suggested that new sanctions be put on hold to give a chance to a shaky ceasefire in eastern Ukraine.\nSome EU countries opposed to further punishment of Moscow see the ceasefire, which was declared on Friday and still largely intact on Monday, as an opportunity to block the new EU sanctions package and avoid retaliation from Russia, diplomats said.\n“The entry into force (of the new sanctions) through the publication in the Official Journal will take place in the next few days. This will leave time for an assessment of the implementation of the ceasefire agreement and the peace plan,” EU Council President Herman Van Rompuy said in a statement.\n“Depending on the situation on the ground, the EU stands ready to review the agreed sanctions in whole or in part,” he said after EU ambassadors held an extraordinary meeting to thrash out the issue.\nAn EU diplomat said there was no clarity on when the new sanctions would take effect. Ambassadors would probably discuss the issue next on Wednesday.\nHinting at disunity in the EU, the diplomat said it would require “political” support for the sanctions to take effect, suggesting that ambassadors would have to escalate the issue to a higher level of their governments.\nA deadline for EU governments to agree to the new sanctions had earlier been pushed back.\nThe EU has always been divided over sanctions on Russia, with countries such as Poland and the Baltics taking a hard line while the prime ministers of Hungary and Slovakia have been publicly hostile to sanctions.\nAt Monday’s ambassadors’ meeting, some EU governments wanted to discuss whether the new sanctions should be frozen before being implemented because of the ceasefire in Ukraine, or alternatively if the new sanctions were implemented, how they could be suspended and when.\nThe EU has always said its sanctions would be reversible if Russia stopped destabilising Ukraine. Moscow annexed Ukraine’s Crimea region in March and NATO says it has sent several thousand troops to help pro-Moscow separatists in the eastern part of the country.\nAustria, Finland, Sweden, Cyprus and Slovakia were among countries wanting to give the ceasefire more time, according to one EU diplomat.\nThe ceasefire in Ukraine is part of a peace plan intended to end a five-month conflict that the United Nations’ human rights envoy said had killed more than 3,000 people.\nThe truce was largely holding on Monday, though each side accused the other of sporadic shelling, including in Mariupol, a city of about half a million people.\nGerman Chancellor Angela Merkel told conservative members of parliament in a closed-door meeting in Berlin on Monday that the sanctions were needed despite the ceasefire agreement, according to several participants.\nMerkel told the deputies Russia had already deceived the West repeatedly with broken promises and she pointed out that Russian troops are still in Ukraine, they said. The EU had to act decisively now, Merkel was quoted as saying.\nThe proposed new EU sanctions put Russia’s top oil producers and pipeline operators Rosneft, Transneft and Gazprom Neft on a list of Russian state-owned firms that will not be allowed to raise capital or borrow on European markets, an EU diplomat said earlier.\nEU sanctions, however, do not include the gas sector and in particular state-owned Gazprom, the world’s biggest gas producer and the biggest gas supplier to Europe.\nIn general, the EU sanctions on Russian companies raising money in the European Union will apply to firms that have turnover of more than 1 trillion roubles ($26.95 billion), half of which is generated from the sale or transport of oil, the diplomat said.\nA further 24 people will be added to a list of those barred from entry to the bloc and whose assets in the EU are frozen.\nDetails of the new sanctions would only be made public when published in the EU’s Official Journal.\nThe list is expected to include new separatist leaders in eastern Ukraine, the government of Ukraine’s Crimea region annexed by Moscow, and Russian decision-makers and oligarchs.\nRussia signalled on Monday it might ban Western airlines from flying over its territory as part of an “asymmetrical” response to new European Union sanctions over the Ukraine crisis.\nBlaming the West for damaging the Russian economy by triggering “stupid” sanctions, Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev said Moscow would press on with measures to reduce reliance on imports, starting with increasing output of domestic aircraft. (Additional reporting by Robin Emmott, Francesco Guarascio, Martin Santa and Julia Fioretti and Andreas Rinke in Berlin; Editing by Tom Heneghan)\nOur Standards:The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles.\n- narrow-browser-and-phone\n- medium-browser-and-portrait-tablet\n- landscape-tablet\n- medium-wide-browser\n- wide-browser-and-larger\n- medium-browser-and-landscape-tablet\n- medium-wide-browser-and-larger\n- above-phone\n- portrait-tablet-and-above\n- above-portrait-tablet\n- landscape-tablet-and-above\n- landscape-tablet-and-medium-wide-browser\n- portrait-tablet-and-below\n- landscape-tablet-and-below"}
    {"i": 10, "title": "Candidate for FIFA presidency Sexwale warns against 'sponsor activism'", "date": "2015-11-03", "candidates": [["top1000:20468", "COCA COLA CO", "KO"], ["top1000:21177", "MCDONALDS CORP", "MCD"], ["top1000:31769", "NOV Inc.", "NOV"], ["top1000:52983", "VISA INC.", "V"], ["top1000:54824", "NAVIENT CORP", "NAVI"]], "text": "UPDATE 2-Unilever promises cash to shareholders after rebuffing Kraft approach\n* Combining foods/refreshment businesses into one organisation\nX\n        \n            | NEW YORK \n\t\t\nNEW YORK Nov 3 Major sponsors of world soccer went too far when they issued calls last month for the resignation of FIFA President Sepp Blatter, South African businessman Tokyo Sexwale and candidate to succeed Blatter, said on Tuesday.\nIn September, Swiss authorities said they were opening a criminal investigation into Blatter, who has led FIFA since 1988. It was the latest blow to FIFA's reputation after U.S. prosecutors announced indictments in May accusing top soccer officials and marketing executives of multi-million dollar bribery schemes over 24 years.\nIn response to the scandals, Coca-Cola Co, McDonald's, Visa, and Budweiser owner Anheuser-Busch InBev, companies that have long linked their brand names to soccer, issued almost simultaneous statements in October demanding Blatter step down immediately in a strong push for change at the organization.\nSexwale is one of the candidates vying to be elected president of FIFA in a vote next February. He criticized the statements made by some of the sponsors.\n\"Coca Cola, Budweiser, these companies, partners of FIFA have got the right to speak. But I think we should be very careful how far we go with sponsors activism,\" Sexwale said at a conference on sport security in New York.\nSexwale praised instead a more muted statement by sportswear company Adidas, which supported FIFA reforms efforts without calling for Blatter's ouster.\n\"One of the things that needs to be done in giving confidence and building back the brand of FIFA is to sit down with the sponsors and say there is a way of doing things without you saying so-and-so should go,\" he said.\nBlatter has denied any wrongdoing. FIFA's ethics committee last month suspended him for 90 days.\nSexwale, who spent 13 years in prison under apartheid until 1990 and then became a provincial premier four years later, also said that within the next two weeks he would issue a \"manifesto\" on his ambitions for FIFA should he be elected president.\nHe said the running of FIFA was \"not going to be a one man show\" but rather he would seek to rely on the \"collected wisdom\" of elected FIFA officials. Sexwale said he would try to ensure that power in the sport is more widely shared around the world. (Reporting by Mica Rosenberg and Mark Hosenball; editing by Grant McCool)"}
    {"i": 11, "title": "How Long Should You Hold A Microcap?", "date": "2017-11-06", "candidates": [["top1000:7882", "Costco Wholesale Corporation", "COST"], ["gh:0000909832", "Costco Wholesale Corporation", "COST"]], "text": "Value investing is probably at least a hundred years old: it was already a long-established practice by the time Benjamin Graham and David Dodd published the first edition of Security Analysis in 1934. And one of its central tenets is patience. One buys a stock that appears cheap and one waits patiently for it to rise in price to a level that approximates its intrinsic value. This could take years, and often does.\nLet’s say you bought all the stocks in the S&P 500 and held them for four years. When would be the optimal time to sell each one? When their price is the highest, of course. The chart below plots the number of bars that it takes S&P 500 stocks to reach their four-year peak. (I obtained this data, and the data in the rest of the article, from Portfolio123 by screening every two years since 1999 for stocks that were in the S&P 500 or microcap universe four years earlier, so it therefore does not include stocks that no longer existed after four years). The bar on the right shows the most recent five months; that’s when 38% of the stocks reached their highest points. And no doubt most of those went (or will go) still higher.\nNow the chart below repeats the same experiment with microcaps. The result is markedly different. 25% of the microcaps reached their peaks within five months of purchase, and another 25% reached their peaks within the last five months. Not only that, but the four-year survivorship rate for microcaps is only 74%--compared to 90% for the S&P 500--due to a higher level of mergers, acquisitions, and bankruptcies; if one were to take that into account, the percentage that reach their peaks four years after purchase would be markedly smaller.\nAnd what kinds of peaks are they? Well, the average peak among that 25% that achieved their high within five months was an increase of 52% over the purchase price. Of course, one would have to be superhuman to sell at exactly the right point, but considering that peak was achieved an average of 43 bars (two months) after purchase, your superhuman stock seller would achieve a CAGR of over 1,000%. By contrast, the average high among the microcaps that lasted close to four years was an increase of 212% over the purchase price, which makes for a CAGR of 34%. There’s a huge survivorship issue here too, which I wasn’t able to take into account—a lot more microcaps are going to survive for 43 bars than for four years.\nAll this suggests that the optimal holding period for microcaps is significantly shorter than that for large caps—in fact, it’s only about two or three months.\nMicrocap investors have a host of advantages over other investors, which I’ve detailed here and Jim O’Shaughnessy has detailed here. But to reap the maximum profit from those advantages, it’s best not to play the buy-and-hold game. Over the last two years I’ve doubled my money by investing in microcaps. I would not have done half as well if I hadn’t sold most of my holdings within a few months. Patience is indeed essential to successful value investing, but with microcaps impatience may be more profitable.\nDisclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.\nI wrote this article myself, and it expresses my own opinions. I am not receiving compensation for it. I have no business relationship with any company whose stock is mentioned in this article."}
    {"i": 12, "title": "Vatican to introduce temperature checks at St. Peter's Basilica", "date": "2020-05-14", "candidates": [["top1000:11901", "Match Group, Inc.", "IAC"], ["top1000:54824", "NAVIENT CORP", "NAVI"]], "text": "May 14, 2020 /  5:53 PM / Updated 23 minutes ago\nVATICAN CITY (Reuters) - People attending Masses in St. Peter’s and other papal basilicas in Rome will have their temperature checked as part of measures to contain the spread of coronavirus, the Vatican said on Thursday.\nIt did not say when the new measures will take effect. Public Masses will resume in churches in Italy on Monday under strict conditions outlined in a protocol signed last week by Italy’s bishops conference and the government.\nSt. Peter’s is on Vatican territory and the other three papal basilicas - St. Paul’s Outside the Walls, St. John’s In Lateran and St. Mary Major - have sovereign, extra-territorial status and so technically are not part of Italy.\nThe new rules for churches in Italy include limiting numbers, distancing and masks but they do not impose thermal scanning, meaning the papal basilicas will have even stricter rules.\nVatican spokesman Matteo Bruni said thermal temperature scanning will be used at least during services on Sundays and religious feast days.\nHe said officials at each basilica will decide the maximum number of people who can safely enter and that Vatican police, Italian police and volunteers will control the flow.\nBruni did not say when the new provisions would take effect and when Pope Francis would next say a Mass from the main altar of St. Peter’s.\nHe is due to say a private Mass on Monday at a side chapel where the St. Pope John Paul is buried, to commemorate the 100th anniversary of John Paul’s birth.\nThousands of people usually attend major papal events in St. Peter’s and the other basilicas but it is unlikely that those numbers will be allowed in again for some time.\nThe pope has been saying Masses in either an empty St. Peter’s or the chapel in his residence and the faithful have been watching on television or the internet.\nTechnically, St. Peter’s has remained open during the Italian lockdown, which began in early March, although only for private prayer and few people have entered because of increased security.\nIt was still not clear when it and the other basilicas will be reopened to tourists.\nItalian museums will reopen on Monday but the reopening of the Vatican Museums, which received 7 million visitors last year, will likely be further delayed while safety measures are put in place, according to a Vatican source.\nReporting by Philip Pullella; Editing by Susan Fenton\nOur Standards:The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles.\n- narrow-browser-and-phone\n- medium-browser-and-portrait-tablet\n- landscape-tablet\n- medium-wide-browser\n- wide-browser-and-larger\n- medium-browser-and-landscape-tablet\n- medium-wide-browser-and-larger\n- above-phone\n- portrait-tablet-and-above\n- above-portrait-tablet\n- landscape-tablet-and-above\n- landscape-tablet-and-medium-wide-browser\n- portrait-tablet-and-below\n- landscape-tablet-and-below"}
    {"i": 13, "title": "BlackRock Analyst Warns Of 'New Geopolitical Regime' That Could Disrupt Markets: 'The Old Playbook No Longer Applies' - MSCI (NYSE:MSCI)", "date": "2024-01-23", "candidates": [["top1000:21880", "Walmart Inc.", "WMT"], ["top1000:36336", "BlackRock Finance, Inc.", "BLK"], ["top1000:52840", "MSCI Inc.", "MSCI"], ["top1000:56668", "DOW INC.", "DOW"], ["top1000:7", "Apple Inc.", "AAPL"]], "text": "BlackRock, the world’s largest asset manager, has issued a warning about the impact of geopolitical volatility on global markets.\nWhat Happened: BlackRock’s analysts, led by Wei Li, have highlighted the increasing geopolitical risks and their potential to disrupt traditional market dynamics, reported Business Insider on Monday.\n“The old playbook no longer applies, in our view,” the analysts said in a note, pointing out that the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average have recently reached record highs despite the geopolitical turmoil.\nLi emphasized that geopolitical fragmentation is contributing to persistent inflation pressures and keeping policy rates above pre-pandemic levels. The recent Red Sea attacks have already begun to impact shipping costs and goods inflation.\nThese developments have led to a drop in the odds of a Fed rate cut in March, from 75% a month ago to 40% currently, as per the CME FedWatch Tool.\nLi also noted that with increasing political tensions, supply chains are becoming longer, with countries like Mexico and Vietnam acting as intermediary trading partners between different power blocs.\nMoreover, the US-China rift, particularly concerning Taiwan, remains a significant flashpoint. Li believes that intense structural competition between the U.S. and China, especially in defense and technology, is the new normal.\nWhy It Matters: BlackRock’s warning comes amid a series of geopolitical and economic developments that could significantly impact global markets. In a recent interview, BlackRock’s Chief Investment Officer of global fixed income, Rick Rieder, dismissed recession fears and predicted a potential 12% surge in stocks for 2024.\nMeanwhile, the global economy is facing other challenges. For instance, economist Campbell Harvey, who has historically used the inverted yield curve as a recession predictor, has forecasted a slowdown for the U.S. economy in 2024.\nBlackRock has also been actively tracking the expansion of AI opportunities beyond the semiconductor and cloud sectors, which could be further impacted by the new geopolitical regime.\nRead Next: Jim Cramer Says Customers Can Buy 60-Inch TV At Walmart For $289 Than Apple Vision Pro\nImage Via Shutterstock\nEngineered by Benzinga Neuro, Edited by Kaustubh Bagalkote\nThe GPT-4-based Benzinga Neuro content generation system exploits the extensive Benzinga Ecosystem, including native data, APIs, and more to create comprehensive and timely stories for you. Learn more."}
    {"i": 14, "title": "Kejriwal 'invited' ED arrest by not responding to its notices: Himanta", "date": "2024-03-24", "candidates": [["top1000:16149", "STRATEGY INC", "MSTR"]], "text": "Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said his Delhi counterpart Arvind Kejriwal effectively invited his own arrest by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) due to his repeated failure to respond to summonses, suggesting that it might have been a tactic to garner political sympathy.\nSarma emphasised that when a person disregards nine summonses from the ED, it indicates a deliberate invitation for arrest.\nHe remarked that if Kejriwal had complied with the initial summonses, his arrest might have been avoided.\n Speaking to reporters at the state BJP headquarters here after a poll-preparedness meeting on Saturday, Sarma said, \"If the ED serves someone nine summonses and that person doesn't show up, it is evident that he is inviting his arrest. The ED didn't arrest Kejriwal, he invited the agency to arrest him.\"\nThe BJP leader cited the examples of politicians such as Rahul Gandhi and Sonia Gandhi, who appeared before the ED when they were issued summonses, implying that Kejriwal's actions deviated from this norm.\nWhen questioned about Kejriwal's refusal to comply with the summonses, Sarma speculated about potential political motivations, suggesting that it could have been a strategy to elicit sympathy from the public.\nThe ED arrested Kejriwal on Friday, hours after the Delhi High Court refused to grant him protection from coercive action by the federal anti-money laundering agency."}
    {"i": 15, "title": "ViacomCBS to launch new streaming platform - CNBC", "date": "2020-02-07", "candidates": [["top1000:11901", "Match Group, Inc.", "IAC"], ["top1000:20587", "TWDC Enterprises 18 Corp.", "DIS"], ["top1000:21866", "Banzai International, Inc.", "VIAC"], ["top1000:54824", "NAVIENT CORP", "NAVI"], ["top1000:7", "Apple Inc.", "AAPL"]], "text": "ViacomCBS to launch new streaming platform - CNBC\nViacomCBS is working on a streaming service that will build on CBS All Access, CNBC reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.\nREUTERS: ViacomCBS is working on a streaming service that will build on CBS All Access, CNBC reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.\nViacomCBS executives have not made a firm decision, but are considering a service with advertisements that will combine CBS All Access with Viacom's channels such as Nickelodeon, MTV, Comedy Central and Paramount Pictures, the report https://cnb.cx/3bh5zUH added.\nThe company did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.\nViacomCBS will become the latest media company to throw its hat in the streaming ring after the launch of streaming services by Apple Inc and Walt Disney Co in November.\nCBS and Viacom completed their merger in December, reuniting media mogul Sumner Redstone's U.S. entertainment empire.\n(Reporting by Neha Malara in Bengaluru; Editing by Shinjini Ganguli)"}
    {"i": 16, "title": "How a hedge funder exposed a $100 million N.J. deli that just got charged with securities fraud: 'The pastrami must be amazing'", "date": "2022-09-27", "candidates": [["top1000:11901", "Match Group, Inc.", "IAC"], ["top1000:7882", "Costco Wholesale Corporation", "COST"], ["gh:0000909832", "Costco Wholesale Corporation", "COST"]], "text": "How a hedge funder exposed a $100 million N.J. deli that just got charged with securities fraud: ‘The pastrami must be amazing’\nThree people involved with a $100 million public company built around a single New Jersey deli were charged with securities fraud and market manipulation.\nFederal prosecutors on Monday accused James T. Patten, Peter L. Coker Sr. and Peter L. Coker Jr. of artificially inflating the price of two companies through manipulative trading. One of them was Hometown International Inc., the sole asset of which was “Your Hometown Deli” in Paulsboro, New Jersey, across the Delaware River from Philadelphia’s airport.\nHometown became infamous when hedge fund legend David Einhorn of Greenlight Capital highlighted the company in a letter to investors in April 2021 as an example of irrational exuberance in the market. Einhorn noted the deli barely had sales of $20,000 in 2019 and even less in 2020 despite reaching a nine-figure valuation.\n“The pastrami must be amazing,” Einhorn observed. “Small investors who get sucked into these situations are likely to be harmed eventually, yet the regulators—who are supposed to be protecting investors—appear to be neither present nor curious.”\nPatten, 63, and Coker Sr., 80, both North Carolina residents, were arrested Monday and are scheduled to appear before a federal magistrate judge in that state. Coker Jr., 53, a Hong Kong resident, remains at large.\nThe criminal charges follow a parallel civil suit filed against the three earlier on Monday by the Securities and Exchange Commission. Lawyers for the three men couldn’t immediately be identified.\nPatten and the two Cokers manipulated the value of Hometown’s over-the-counter shares by trading through accounts they controlled to create the appearance of active trading, the SEC said in its suit filed in federal court in Camden, New Jersey. They drove the value of the company above $13 a share, resulting in a market capitalization of more than $100 million.\nThe suit alleges the three men used the same method to push up the price of E-Waste Corp., a Kent, Washington-based company that merged with EZRaider Global Inc., a private Nevada corporation that distributes electric tactical vehicles, in September 2021.\n$700 Inventory\nAt one point, the manipulative trading pushed E-Waste’s price from 10 cents a share to $10 a share, resulting in a market capitalization of about $120 million for a shell company with no revenue, the SEC said.\nThe three men are charged with conspiracy to commit securities fraud, securities fraud and conspiracy to manipulate securities prices. Patten is also charged with four counts of manipulation of securities, four counts of wire fraud and one count of money laundering. They face as much as 20 years in prison if convicted of the most serious charges.\nAccording to the SEC, Patten started the deli with a childhood friend and his girlfriend in October 2015 but soon began conspiring with the Cokers to create a public company that would serve as a reverse-merger vehicle. After the company began trading in 2019, Patten paid his co-founders $3,000 for a 38% stake in the deli and exercised an option for their remaining stake the following year.\nHometown merged in March with Makamer Holdings, a bioplastics startup, selling the deli’s inventory for $700 and the store itself for $15,000.\nThe criminal case is US v Patten, US District Court, District of New Jersey. The civil case is SEC v Patten, 22-cv-5703, US District Court, District of New Jersey."}
    {"i": 17, "title": "Iraq not equipped to try Islamic State over atrocities in Mosul, against Yazidis: U.N. | The Japan Times", "date": "2017-11-03", "candidates": [["top1000:11901", "Match Group, Inc.", "IAC"], ["top1000:20531", "Crane Co", "CR"], ["top1000:3309", "NORTHWESTERN CORP", "NWE"]], "text": "GENEVA – Iraq is not capable of trying atrocities committed by Islamic State during the battle for Mosul so it must find other routes to justice such as the International Criminal Court (ICC), a U.N. human rights report said on Thursday.\nAt least 2,521 civilians were killed during the nine-month battle, including 741 people who were executed, the report said. Most died as a result of Islamic State (ISIL) attacks.\nIt cited testimonies of mass abductions by Islamic State, as well as killings, the use of human shields, and deliberate targeting of civilians and their homes.\nISIL planted “a huge number” of improvised explosive devices and used drones to drop explosives in Mosul, a city of 1.5 million, as well as setting fire to sulfur fields and oil wells, it said.\nIts forces desecrated religious sites and last June blew up the al-Nuri mosque from which its leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi had declared the caliphate spanning parts of Iraq and Syria in 2014, it said.\n“Iraqi courts and tribunals do not have jurisdiction over international crimes (such as genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes) — and prosecutors, police investigators and judges lack capacity to … (investigate), charge and try persons in relation to such crimes,” the report said, calling for it to amend domestic law.\nIraqi law did not do enough to guarantee due process or fair trials, it said.\nAccepting the jurisdiction of the Hague-based ICC and finding other ways to ensure crimes were tried by a competent court “would reassure the international community that Iraq is serious” about getting justice, which was key to rebuilding trust and reconciliation, it said.\nAt least 74 mass graves have been discovered since June 2014 in areas previously held by ISIL in Iraq, the U.N. report said.\nThese included in Sinjar, the northwestern city where the U.N. has said Islamic State committed genocide against the Kurdish-speaking Yazidi religious minority whom the Sunni militants view as infidels.\nIraq and the international community have a duty to ensure those crimes are prosecuted, Syracuse University professor and former war crimes prosecutor David Crane said on Wednesday in a separate report into the genocide, issued by his law school’s Syrian Accountability Project.\n“Bringing ISIS to justice for genocide against the Yazidi community, at the domestic or the international level, will depend on the strategic preservation of forensic evidence,” Crane’s report said.\nThe U.N. report also called on Iraqi authorities to investigate crimes allegedly committed by Iraqi-backed forces during the operation, including mass abductions and unlawful killings.\nIt called for a separate investigation into air strikes by the international coalition.\nIt said the U.N. had recorded 461 civilian deaths from air strikes during the most intensive phase of the battle for western Mosul, from Feb. 19."}

    {"i": 19, "title": "Bigg Boss 14: Abhinav-Rubina, Kavita-Ronnit's feud leaves Salman Khan angry; see his reaction | Watch", "date": "2020-12-12", "candidates": [["top1000:54824", "NAVIENT CORP", "NAVI"]], "text": "Bigg Boss and fights are synonyms, every day, every week a new drama unfolds inside the house. In tonight's Weekend Ka Vaar episode two more powerful couples Abhinav Shukla- Rubina Dilaik, and Kavita Kaushik- husband Ronnit Biswas will wash their dirty linen on the show. The promo of which is breaking the internet.\nHere's everything you need to about tonight's drama!\nIn the previous night's episode, mastermind Vikas Gupta dropped some truth bombs on Abhinav Shukla regarding Ronnit Biswas' recent tweets on social media.\nVikas informed Abhinav about the allegations against him: \"After Kavita (Kaushik) left from here, bahar yeh nikla tha ki tum bohot zyada sharab peete ho aur tum unko bohot zyada gande-gande messages bhej rahe the (it was claimed that you drink a lot and sent her a number of obscene messages).\"\nA shocked Abhinav shared this information with Rubina, saying that not only Kavita but her husband Ronnit Biswas also made these claims. \"Woh kitna gir sakte hai, yaar (How low can they stoop),\" he remarked. Rubina vowed to 'not leave them' and set things straight as soon as she exited the Bigg Boss house.\nAbhinav and Rubina Vs Kavita-Ronnit: Battle of Bigg Boss 14\nThe Weekend Ka Vaar ousted contestant Kavita Kaushik and her husband Ronnit Biswa will challenge Abhinav about his behaviour towards Kavita in the past. Rubina accuses Kavita of talking about Abhinav after leaving the Bigg Boss house. Kavita accuses Abhinav of drunk-texting her while Abhinav denies the entire episode. Kavita refuses to step back and asks Abhinav to tell out loud just why they ended their friendship.\nRonnit claims that Kavita had told him about Abhinav and Rubina's past and why they broke up with each other. Kavita adds that Abhinav sent her several 'violent' messages and she even threatened to complain about him to the police if he didn't stop. Abhinav replies to her:\nI would love to see those messages, we will deal with it in a legal fashion.\nSalman Khan loses his cool, removes his jacket and slams both the couples saying: 'Ganda hai ye'\nHost Salman Khan seems to have had enough of this banter! Looking at the two couples fighting with each other, Salman removes his blazer and asked all of them to stop for a second. Salman Khan angrily says, \"Ye khilwad bana ke rakha hai, ganda hai ye\" (This is a mockery, this is dirty).\"\nAmidst all this Rubina breaks down and seems inconsolable after the entire argument.\nMeanwhile, Twitteria is trolling Kavita for her behaviour as they trend #ShamelessKavita\nFor the unversed, Ronnit had tweeted earlier this month about Abhinav, \"Well let me put the truth out there.. the not so gentleman we're talking about has a severe alcohol problem and used to get pissed drunk and message KK through the night wanting to talk and meet up at all odd hours. So much so that she had to call the cops on him more than once.\"\nScreenshot of deleted tweet by Ronnit"}
