    {"i": 5, "title": "At Ayodhya Deepotsav, grandeur of 'treta yug' comes alive", "date": "2020-11-13", "candidates": [["top1000:11901", "Match Group, Inc.", "IAC"], ["top1000:54433", "NEWS CORP", "NWS"], ["top1000:54824", "NAVIENT CORP", "NAVI"]], "text": "AYODHYA (UP): The Uttar Pradesh government on Friday went all out in marking the homecoming of Lord Ram to this holy town – the mythical event in 'treta yug' on which the festival of Diwali is based.\nSo, there was the reenactment of the arrival of God Ram and Goddess Sita on their 'pushpak viman', a laser and sound show, cultural programmes and the lighting of a record 5.51 lakh earthen lamps on the banks of the Saryu. The figure has been claimed by the government.\nChief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Governor Anandiben Patel were there at Ayodhya's 'Deepotsav', the first since the groundbreaking ceremony earlier this year of a Ram temple in the holy town.\nSeveral new development projects were launched to mark the occasion.\n\"Our generation is not only fortunate to see the start of the construction of a Ram temple here but we also attended the historic event. In the struggle of 500 years, many saints passed away with a dream to see the start of construction. I thank PM Modi who is the one who implemented the ideology of Ram Rajya,\" Adityanath said while addressing the 'Deepotsav' event here.\nPrime Minister Narendra Modi had performed the 'bhoomi pujan' of a Supreme Court-mandated Ram temple in Ayodhya on August 5 this year, bringing to fruition the BJP's 'mandir' movement that defined its politics for three decades and took it to the heights of power.\n\"It is the dream of PM Modi to develop Ayodhya as Vedic Ramayana City and it should be the most beautiful. We are here to seek support of you all as to how it can be developed that it has glimpse of a Vedic city,\" the chief minister said.\nActors representing Lord Ram, Goddess Sita and Lakshman descended on the Saryu bank in a 'pushpak viman' -- a helicopter that sprinkled rose petals -- and were received by the governor and the chief minister.\nThe BJP government in Uttar Pradesh started Deepotsav celebration in Ayodhya after Yogi Adityanath became the chief minister in March 2017.\nAs a special Diwali gift from the chief minister, Ayodhya will get an international airport project this time.\nThe celebrations began from Friday afternoon itself when a grand coronation procession of Lord Ram started from Saket college in Ayodhya to reach the riverbank after covering a stretch of about five kilometres. The procession has 11 tableaux, built on the Ramayana themes, participating in it.\nThe themes include Gurukul Shiksha, Ram-Sita Vivah, Kewat Prasang, Ram Darbaar, Shabri-Ram Milaap and Lanka Dahan among others. Besides the Saryu bank, the Ram Janmabhoomi, the site of upcoming Ram temple, was lit up by 11,000 earthen lamps in the evening, when a grand Aarti was held at the Saryu river after the sunset.\nOther projects for people of Ayodhya include a modern sewage treatment plant to maintain the flow and cleanliness of the river. The pilgrim town will also have an international Ramlila Centre to be built at a cost of around Rs 3.47 crore, a 'Bhajan' site at Rs 19.02 crore, a Queen Heo Memorial Park for Rs 21.92 crore, a Ram Katha Gallery worth Rs 7.59 crore, the expansion of Ram Katha Park at Rs 2.75 crore and the beautification of Ram ki Paidi at Rs 12.65 crore, officials said.\nAmong development projects, the holy city will also have a modern bus stand (Rs 7.40 crore), a multi-level parking lot (Rs 16.44 crore) and the renovation of road and footpaths (Rs 8.40 crore) besides others, they said.\nHailing the prime minister for India's fight against the coronavirus, Adityanath said, \"We are fighting strongly under his (PM's) leadership and we will defeat the virus.\"\nIn her speech, the Governor said Ram and Ramrajya were \"inseparable parts of the Indian culture\" and spoke at length about the ideals of the Maryada Purushottam.\nShe advised the people not to lower their guards in their fight against the pandemic till it was finished.\nDeputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya, BJP state president Swatantra Dev Singh and a number of saints and ministers were present on the occasion.\nWith a view to ensuring a global recognition and identity to Ayodhya, Adityanath has initiated a number of works in the temple town including Deepotsav being organised on the occasion of Diwali every year.\n\"Since the formation of the Adityanath government in Uttar Pradesh, many events have been organised, from Deepotsav to Ram Leela, which have earned a new identity to Ayodhya globally,\" a government spokesman said on Friday.\nGiving an account of the works in the temple town, he said apart from setting up of Navya Ayodhya as the coordinated model of Vedic and modern city, the grandest and divine temple of Lord Ram, a tall statue of the Hindu deity -- which would be the world's tallest statue -- is set to leave an \"indelible impression\" on the people of the world.\nA four-lane road from Ayodhya to Sultanpur National Highway (NH) 330 to the airport is to be renovated at a cost of Rs 18.75 crore. The National Highways Authority of India is making a proposal for construction of a bypass for Ayodhya Dham from Sohawal to Vikramjot, the spokesman said.\nThe work of widening of the four-lane road from Rae Bareli to Ayodhya is also to be done at a cost of about Rs 1,500 crore, he said.\nRecently, at a review meeting of the tourism department, the chief minister had said that to make Ayodhya a global city for tourism, a consultant has to be zeroed in on accordingly.\nRead More News on\nDownload The Economic Times News App to get Daily Market Updates & Live Business News."}
    {"i": 6, "title": "European shares steady, hope for U.S. payrolls boost", "date": "2012-11-02", "candidates": [["top1000:20235", "AUTOMATIC DATA PROCESSING, INC.", "ADP"], ["top1000:31769", "NOV Inc.", "NOV"], ["top1000:7882", "Costco Wholesale Corporation", "COST"], ["gh:0000008670", "AUTOMATIC DATA PROCESSING, INC.", "ADP"], ["gh:0000909832", "Costco Wholesale Corporation", "COST"]], "text": "BRIEF-Civista Bancshares prices offering at $21.75 per share\n* Civista Bancshares, Inc. announces pricing of offering of common shares\nX\n* FTSEurofirst 300 flat, EuroSTOXX 50 off 0.2 pct\n    * U.S. data boosts expectations of strong jobs number\n    * Alcatel down, Beiersdorf up in mixed earnings season\n    By Toni Vorobyova\n    LONDON, Nov 2 European equities steadied on\nFriday, looking to the U.S. jobs report for reassurance on the\nhealth of the world's biggest economy that might give key\nindexes the momentum to test two-week highs.\n    The pan-European FTSEurofirst 300 was flat at\n1,109.70 points at 0835 GMT, while the EuroSTOXX 50 index of\neuro zone blue chips edged 0.2 percent lower to 2,529.66 points,\noff the previous session's intra-day high of 2,541.87.\n    Expectations for a strong reading from the U.S. non-farm\npayroll report - the last before next week's presidential\nelections - were bolstered by a better than expected ADP private\nsector employment report and ISM manufacturing index in the\nprevious session. \n    \"The ADP figures were quite good ... and there is a rather\nhigh likelihood that U.S. government did not lay off staff this\nmonth as well, and that would be good for non-farm payrolls,\"\nsaid Peter Garnry, equity strategist at Saxo Bank.\n    \"If the non-farm payrolls are better than expected, I think\nit could be a catalyst for the market to continue the momentum\nfrom yesterday going into the weekend.\"\n    A number above the 125,000 consensus could help the\nEuroSTOXX 50 break out of the 165 point range of around 2,440 to\n2,605 it has held to since mid-September.\n    That followed a rally of more than 460 points in the two\nprevious months on a European Central Bank pledge to protect the\neuro.\n    \"If the positive tone continues, we will have a new trading\nsignal if we have new highs compared to yesterday,\" said Petra\nKerssenbrock, technical analyst at Commerzbank, forecasting that\nEuroSTOXX 50 could test 2,600 by year-end.\n    \n    The economic health of the United States has become\nincreasingly key for European companies as the region stutters\ndue to the debt crisis. The third quarter earnings season has\nunderscored the divide, as companies with strong foreign\nrevenues outperform home-focused peers.\n    A 15 percent drop in revenues in Europe pushed telecom\nequipment market Alcatel towards a bigger than\nexpected third quarter loss, shaving 7.2 percent off the share\nprice on Friday.\n    Skincare manufacturer Beiersdorf rallied 6.6\npercent after raising its 2012 outlook thanks to a strong\nperformance in emerging markets. \n    With the third quarter earnings season half way through, 44\npercent of companies in developed Europe have missed forecasts\nand the remainder are expected to undershoot by on average 1.6\npercent, according to Thomson Reuters Starmine data.\n            \n            \n            \n            \n\t"}
    {"i": 7, "title": "Lucy Hale's Secret To Repeating Outfits, The Trend She's Most Excited For & Her New Degree Campaign", "date": "2018-03-19", "candidates": [["top1000:11901", "Match Group, Inc.", "IAC"], ["top1000:54824", "NAVIENT CORP", "NAVI"]], "text": "As the star of the hit TV show Pretty Little Liars and with a major role on the CW’s new series Life Sentence—not to mention her upcoming releases Truth or Dare, Dude and The Unicorn—it’s fair to assume that Lucy Hale can get her hands on pretty much whatever she wants to wear. But just like the rest of us, she actually loves to repeat outfits. And her new campaign with Degree is making that even easier. She accepted the Degree challenge to re-wear a piece from her closet and proved that her chic black top remained streak-free. That’s because the Ultraclear Black + White antiperspirants don’t leave yellow stains on light clothing or white marks on darker hues. She tells us all about it, plus shares her fashion and beauty wisdom.\nWhy was partnering with Degree a good fit for you? The whole purpose of the Ultraclear Black + White Antiperspirants is you’re able to re-wear articles of clothing and re-wear your favorite items. For me that felt super authentic and organic because I do that all the time. Not everyone sees that I do that, but I love having a favorite item and mixing it to create new looks. This deodorant is amazing because you’re usually trying to avoid putting on your black clothes because of all the streaks and the marks and this doesn’t do that at all. It comes in a spray form and a solid, but I love the spray form—it smells so good. Everyone should have it.\nWhat is your beauty routine like? I’m pretty diligent about my skincare routine and there’s a lot of steps to it. I’m letting my skin breathe and keeping it clear so the routine revolves around that. I typically don’t wear a lot of makeup, but if I do it’s just concealer, mascara and a good highlighter. But (for work) I love getting dressed up and trying new things. I have such a fun glam team who is always willing to do new things and making me feel like a human on days when I don’t necessarily feel like a human. I am sort of like the best of both worlds because I love putting on a dress and lipstick and going out, but I also love the complete opposite of that too.\nWhat are your beauty staples? Sunscreen—Skinceuticals has a really good one. Lucas Papaw Ointment, because it’s amazing. Any makeup wipes. Deodorant. And I really love micellar water lately because you wash your skin, you think you have everything off. But if you swipe over your face with that you’re like, oh, unaware that was still there.\nWhat have you learned from working with your glam squad? There’s so many things that people have put me in on a show, or my stylist has pulled for me, or a makeup look that I never in a million years would think would work and so being surrounded by all these people pushes me to try new things. It’s really cool to have access to new designers that I never would have heard of before because if it were up to me I’d probably play it safe. It’s nice to have people to challenge you to try new things.\nWhat spring fashion trend are you most excited for? Yellow is really big right now. I love a good mustard, but bright yellow is back and I love a good monochromatic look. I saw this outfit the other day—it was yellow shoes, yellow pants, and a yellow top and it looked amazing. So I’ll have to try that next.\nIt’s an unexpected color. Yeah, it can be a little obnoxious but they’re making it work. It’s like a walking highlighter.\nWhat’s a fashion rule worth breaking? I used to not mix metals. If I wore silver I couldn’t wear gold. If I wore gold I couldn’t wear silver or if I wore black I couldn’t wear brown. But there are ways to make it cool and ways to make it work. And mixing patterns is fun too, like unexpected patterns."}
    {"i": 8, "title": "Apple 'Confirms' iPhone 8 Has A Nasty Surprise", "date": "2017-09-28", "candidates": [["top1000:45483", "Alphabet Inc.", "GOOG"], ["top1000:54084", "Meta Platforms, Inc.", "FB"], ["top1000:54638", "TWITTER, INC.", "TWTR"], ["top1000:54824", "NAVIENT CORP", "NAVI"], ["top1000:7", "Apple Inc.", "AAPL"]], "text": "This is not one of \n  \n‘Great Secret Features’ and ‘Nasty Surprises’ are my regular columns investigating operating system updates for the best features / biggest problems hidden behind the headlines.\nSpeaking to The Verge, an Apple spokesperson said the company is aware of a ‘crackling’ fault in the iPhone 8’s earpiece which disrupts audio during phone and FaceTime calls. The consequence is there’s currently little ‘phone’ about this new iPhone.\nThe good news is Apple said “Our team is at work on a fix, which will be included in an upcoming software release”, though it declined to provide a more precise timescale.\nInterestingly Apple said it believes only a “small number” of iPhone 8s are affected, but with numerous complaints from affected iPhone 8 owners spread across MacRumors, Apple’s official Communities support forum, Reddit and @applesupport being flooded with complaints on Twitter this seems optimistic. Especially considering the iPhone 8 has been on sale less than a week and far fewer have been sold than normal as fans patiently wait for the more ambitious iPhone X.\nIt is worth pointing out there are also complaints from affected iPhone 8 Plus users, but so far these appear to less frequent. This might be because of a component difference with the iPhone 8 or simply because fewer iPhone 8 Plus phones have been sold (there’s only $50 between a top tier iPhone 8 Plus and the iPhone X).\nPerhaps the best news, however, comes from reading between the lines in Apple’s statement. While affected users might wait a while, the fact Apple states the crackle will be fixed “in an upcoming software release” suggests this isn’t a hardware issue and a mass recall isn’t necessary. Then again this depends on how well the software fix does its job.\nIt’s also important affected iPhone 8 and iPhone 8 Plus owners are vigilant. Apple boosted the external speakers on both new iPhones by 25% compared to the iPhone 7 and iPhone 7 Plus. If this was a factor in the fault and the upcoming iOS fix works by reducing their volume, then that’s not a satisfactory solution.\nBut let’s not get ahead of ourselves. As it stands the iPhone 8 and (possibly to a lesser extent) iPhone 8 Plus officially have a problem, but Apple deserves credit for stepping up and taking this on the chin. Now let’s see that fix ASAP.\n___\nFollow Gordon on Twitter, Facebook and Google+\nMore On Forbes\nApple’s New iPhones Have Nasty Surprises\nApple iOS 11 Has 25 Great Secret Features\niPhone X Vs iPhone 8: What's The Difference?"}
    {"i": 9, "title": "UPDATE 2-EU delays enforcing new Russia sanctions", "date": "2014-09-08", "candidates": [["top1000:11901", "Match Group, Inc.", "IACI"], ["top1000:20561", "TARGET CORP", "TGT"], ["top1000:30474", "RELIANCE, INC.", "RS"], ["top1000:4998", "WEST PHARMACEUTICAL SERVICES INC", "WST"]], "text": "* EU allows time to see if Ukraine ceasefire holds\n* Sanctions now expected to take effect “in next few days”\n* EU doves seize on ceasefire to block new sanctions (Updates with decision)\nBy Jan Strupczewski and Adrian Croft\nBRUSSELS, Sept 8 (Reuters) - The European Union adopted new sanctions against Russia over its involvement in the Ukraine war on Monday, but delayed enforcing them to leave time to assess whether a ceasefire in Ukraine is holding.\nThe sanctions, which target the ability of Russia’s top oil producers to raise capital in Europe, were originally due to take effect on Tuesday.\nBut that was pushed back by a few days after some EU governments suggested that new sanctions be put on hold to give a chance to a shaky ceasefire in eastern Ukraine.\nSome EU countries opposed to further punishment of Moscow see the ceasefire, which was declared on Friday and still largely intact on Monday, as an opportunity to block the new EU sanctions package and avoid retaliation from Russia, diplomats said.\n“The entry into force (of the new sanctions) through the publication in the Official Journal will take place in the next few days. This will leave time for an assessment of the implementation of the ceasefire agreement and the peace plan,” EU Council President Herman Van Rompuy said in a statement.\n“Depending on the situation on the ground, the EU stands ready to review the agreed sanctions in whole or in part,” he said after EU ambassadors held an extraordinary meeting to thrash out the issue.\nAn EU diplomat said there was no clarity on when the new sanctions would take effect. Ambassadors would probably discuss the issue next on Wednesday.\nHinting at disunity in the EU, the diplomat said it would require “political” support for the sanctions to take effect, suggesting that ambassadors would have to escalate the issue to a higher level of their governments.\nA deadline for EU governments to agree to the new sanctions had earlier been pushed back.\nThe EU has always been divided over sanctions on Russia, with countries such as Poland and the Baltics taking a hard line while the prime ministers of Hungary and Slovakia have been publicly hostile to sanctions.\nAt Monday’s ambassadors’ meeting, some EU governments wanted to discuss whether the new sanctions should be frozen before being implemented because of the ceasefire in Ukraine, or alternatively if the new sanctions were implemented, how they could be suspended and when.\nThe EU has always said its sanctions would be reversible if Russia stopped destabilising Ukraine. Moscow annexed Ukraine’s Crimea region in March and NATO says it has sent several thousand troops to help pro-Moscow separatists in the eastern part of the country.\nAustria, Finland, Sweden, Cyprus and Slovakia were among countries wanting to give the ceasefire more time, according to one EU diplomat.\nThe ceasefire in Ukraine is part of a peace plan intended to end a five-month conflict that the United Nations’ human rights envoy said had killed more than 3,000 people.\nThe truce was largely holding on Monday, though each side accused the other of sporadic shelling, including in Mariupol, a city of about half a million people.\nGerman Chancellor Angela Merkel told conservative members of parliament in a closed-door meeting in Berlin on Monday that the sanctions were needed despite the ceasefire agreement, according to several participants.\nMerkel told the deputies Russia had already deceived the West repeatedly with broken promises and she pointed out that Russian troops are still in Ukraine, they said. The EU had to act decisively now, Merkel was quoted as saying.\nThe proposed new EU sanctions put Russia’s top oil producers and pipeline operators Rosneft, Transneft and Gazprom Neft on a list of Russian state-owned firms that will not be allowed to raise capital or borrow on European markets, an EU diplomat said earlier.\nEU sanctions, however, do not include the gas sector and in particular state-owned Gazprom, the world’s biggest gas producer and the biggest gas supplier to Europe.\nIn general, the EU sanctions on Russian companies raising money in the European Union will apply to firms that have turnover of more than 1 trillion roubles ($26.95 billion), half of which is generated from the sale or transport of oil, the diplomat said.\nA further 24 people will be added to a list of those barred from entry to the bloc and whose assets in the EU are frozen.\nDetails of the new sanctions would only be made public when published in the EU’s Official Journal.\nThe list is expected to include new separatist leaders in eastern Ukraine, the government of Ukraine’s Crimea region annexed by Moscow, and Russian decision-makers and oligarchs.\nRussia signalled on Monday it might ban Western airlines from flying over its territory as part of an “asymmetrical” response to new European Union sanctions over the Ukraine crisis.\nBlaming the West for damaging the Russian economy by triggering “stupid” sanctions, Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev said Moscow would press on with measures to reduce reliance on imports, starting with increasing output of domestic aircraft. (Additional reporting by Robin Emmott, Francesco Guarascio, Martin Santa and Julia Fioretti and Andreas Rinke in Berlin; Editing by Tom Heneghan)\nOur Standards:The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles.\n- narrow-browser-and-phone\n- medium-browser-and-portrait-tablet\n- landscape-tablet\n- medium-wide-browser\n- wide-browser-and-larger\n- medium-browser-and-landscape-tablet\n- medium-wide-browser-and-larger\n- above-phone\n- portrait-tablet-and-above\n- above-portrait-tablet\n- landscape-tablet-and-above\n- landscape-tablet-and-medium-wide-browser\n- portrait-tablet-and-below\n- landscape-tablet-and-below"}
    {"i": 10, "title": "Candidate for FIFA presidency Sexwale warns against 'sponsor activism'", "date": "2015-11-03", "candidates": [["top1000:20468", "COCA COLA CO", "KO"], ["top1000:21177", "MCDONALDS CORP", "MCD"], ["top1000:31769", "NOV Inc.", "NOV"], ["top1000:52983", "VISA INC.", "V"], ["top1000:54824", "NAVIENT CORP", "NAVI"]], "text": "UPDATE 2-Unilever promises cash to shareholders after rebuffing Kraft approach\n* Combining foods/refreshment businesses into one organisation\nX\n        \n            | NEW YORK \n\t\t\nNEW YORK Nov 3 Major sponsors of world soccer went too far when they issued calls last month for the resignation of FIFA President Sepp Blatter, South African businessman Tokyo Sexwale and candidate to succeed Blatter, said on Tuesday.\nIn September, Swiss authorities said they were opening a criminal investigation into Blatter, who has led FIFA since 1988. It was the latest blow to FIFA's reputation after U.S. prosecutors announced indictments in May accusing top soccer officials and marketing executives of multi-million dollar bribery schemes over 24 years.\nIn response to the scandals, Coca-Cola Co, McDonald's, Visa, and Budweiser owner Anheuser-Busch InBev, companies that have long linked their brand names to soccer, issued almost simultaneous statements in October demanding Blatter step down immediately in a strong push for change at the organization.\nSexwale is one of the candidates vying to be elected president of FIFA in a vote next February. He criticized the statements made by some of the sponsors.\n\"Coca Cola, Budweiser, these companies, partners of FIFA have got the right to speak. But I think we should be very careful how far we go with sponsors activism,\" Sexwale said at a conference on sport security in New York.\nSexwale praised instead a more muted statement by sportswear company Adidas, which supported FIFA reforms efforts without calling for Blatter's ouster.\n\"One of the things that needs to be done in giving confidence and building back the brand of FIFA is to sit down with the sponsors and say there is a way of doing things without you saying so-and-so should go,\" he said.\nBlatter has denied any wrongdoing. FIFA's ethics committee last month suspended him for 90 days.\nSexwale, who spent 13 years in prison under apartheid until 1990 and then became a provincial premier four years later, also said that within the next two weeks he would issue a \"manifesto\" on his ambitions for FIFA should he be elected president.\nHe said the running of FIFA was \"not going to be a one man show\" but rather he would seek to rely on the \"collected wisdom\" of elected FIFA officials. Sexwale said he would try to ensure that power in the sport is more widely shared around the world. (Reporting by Mica Rosenberg and Mark Hosenball; editing by Grant McCool)"}
    {"i": 11, "title": "How Long Should You Hold A Microcap?", "date": "2017-11-06", "candidates": [["top1000:7882", "Costco Wholesale Corporation", "COST"], ["gh:0000909832", "Costco Wholesale Corporation", "COST"]], "text": "Value investing is probably at least a hundred years old: it was already a long-established practice by the time Benjamin Graham and David Dodd published the first edition of Security Analysis in 1934. And one of its central tenets is patience. One buys a stock that appears cheap and one waits patiently for it to rise in price to a level that approximates its intrinsic value. This could take years, and often does.\nLet’s say you bought all the stocks in the S&P 500 and held them for four years. When would be the optimal time to sell each one? When their price is the highest, of course. The chart below plots the number of bars that it takes S&P 500 stocks to reach their four-year peak. (I obtained this data, and the data in the rest of the article, from Portfolio123 by screening every two years since 1999 for stocks that were in the S&P 500 or microcap universe four years earlier, so it therefore does not include stocks that no longer existed after four years). The bar on the right shows the most recent five months; that’s when 38% of the stocks reached their highest points. And no doubt most of those went (or will go) still higher.\nNow the chart below repeats the same experiment with microcaps. The result is markedly different. 25% of the microcaps reached their peaks within five months of purchase, and another 25% reached their peaks within the last five months. Not only that, but the four-year survivorship rate for microcaps is only 74%--compared to 90% for the S&P 500--due to a higher level of mergers, acquisitions, and bankruptcies; if one were to take that into account, the percentage that reach their peaks four years after purchase would be markedly smaller.\nAnd what kinds of peaks are they? Well, the average peak among that 25% that achieved their high within five months was an increase of 52% over the purchase price. Of course, one would have to be superhuman to sell at exactly the right point, but considering that peak was achieved an average of 43 bars (two months) after purchase, your superhuman stock seller would achieve a CAGR of over 1,000%. By contrast, the average high among the microcaps that lasted close to four years was an increase of 212% over the purchase price, which makes for a CAGR of 34%. There’s a huge survivorship issue here too, which I wasn’t able to take into account—a lot more microcaps are going to survive for 43 bars than for four years.\nAll this suggests that the optimal holding period for microcaps is significantly shorter than that for large caps—in fact, it’s only about two or three months.\nMicrocap investors have a host of advantages over other investors, which I’ve detailed here and Jim O’Shaughnessy has detailed here. But to reap the maximum profit from those advantages, it’s best not to play the buy-and-hold game. Over the last two years I’ve doubled my money by investing in microcaps. I would not have done half as well if I hadn’t sold most of my holdings within a few months. Patience is indeed essential to successful value investing, but with microcaps impatience may be more profitable.\nDisclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.\nI wrote this article myself, and it expresses my own opinions. I am not receiving compensation for it. I have no business relationship with any company whose stock is mentioned in this article."}
    {"i": 12, "title": "Vatican to introduce temperature checks at St. Peter's Basilica", "date": "2020-05-14", "candidates": [["top1000:11901", "Match Group, Inc.", "IAC"], ["top1000:54824", "NAVIENT CORP", "NAVI"]], "text": "May 14, 2020 /  5:53 PM / Updated 23 minutes ago\nVATICAN CITY (Reuters) - People attending Masses in St. Peter’s and other papal basilicas in Rome will have their temperature checked as part of measures to contain the spread of coronavirus, the Vatican said on Thursday.\nIt did not say when the new measures will take effect. Public Masses will resume in churches in Italy on Monday under strict conditions outlined in a protocol signed last week by Italy’s bishops conference and the government.\nSt. Peter’s is on Vatican territory and the other three papal basilicas - St. Paul’s Outside the Walls, St. John’s In Lateran and St. Mary Major - have sovereign, extra-territorial status and so technically are not part of Italy.\nThe new rules for churches in Italy include limiting numbers, distancing and masks but they do not impose thermal scanning, meaning the papal basilicas will have even stricter rules.\nVatican spokesman Matteo Bruni said thermal temperature scanning will be used at least during services on Sundays and religious feast days.\nHe said officials at each basilica will decide the maximum number of people who can safely enter and that Vatican police, Italian police and volunteers will control the flow.\nBruni did not say when the new provisions would take effect and when Pope Francis would next say a Mass from the main altar of St. Peter’s.\nHe is due to say a private Mass on Monday at a side chapel where the St. Pope John Paul is buried, to commemorate the 100th anniversary of John Paul’s birth.\nThousands of people usually attend major papal events in St. Peter’s and the other basilicas but it is unlikely that those numbers will be allowed in again for some time.\nThe pope has been saying Masses in either an empty St. Peter’s or the chapel in his residence and the faithful have been watching on television or the internet.\nTechnically, St. Peter’s has remained open during the Italian lockdown, which began in early March, although only for private prayer and few people have entered because of increased security.\nIt was still not clear when it and the other basilicas will be reopened to tourists.\nItalian museums will reopen on Monday but the reopening of the Vatican Museums, which received 7 million visitors last year, will likely be further delayed while safety measures are put in place, according to a Vatican source.\nReporting by Philip Pullella; Editing by Susan Fenton\nOur Standards:The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles.\n- narrow-browser-and-phone\n-     def _frame(
        input: Path, limit: int | None, seed: int, selection: Path | None = None
    ) -> Iterator[tuple[Iterator[list[Article]], int, int]]:
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            con.execute("SET memory_limit='2GB'")
            con.execute("SET threads=1")
            con.execute("SET preserve_insertion_order=false")
            con.execute("SET max_temp_directory_size='4GB'")
            files = sorted(input.glob("shards/*/retained.parquet"))
            if not files:
                raise ValueError("The CPU index has no completed retained shards")
            if limit is None:
                count = int(
                    con.from_parquet([str(path) for path in files]).count("*").fetchone()[0]
                )
                yield _article_batches(con, files, identities=True), count, count
                return
            frame_metadata = selection.with_suffix(".json") if selection else None
            if (
                selection
                and selection.exists()
                and frame_metadata
                and frame_metadata.exists()
            ):
                saved = json.loads(frame_metadata.read_text())
                if saved["seed"] != seed or saved["requested"] != min(
                    limit, saved["frame_documents"]
                ):
                    raise ValueError("Frozen selection differs from the requested sample")
                if (
                    hashlib.sha256(selection.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
                    != saved["selection_sha256"]
                ):
                    raise ValueError("Frozen selection checksum changed")
                yield (
                    _article_batches(con, [selection], identities=False),
                    int(saved["frame_documents"]),
                    int(saved["requested"]),
                )
                return
            con.read_parquet([str(path) for path in files]).create_view("input_records")
            if limit is not None:
                count_row = con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM input_records").fetchone()
                if count_row is None:
                    raise ValueError("The retained article population is missing")
                count = int(count_row[0])
                con.execute(
                    "CREATE TEMP TABLE sample_keys AS SELECT "
                    "article_id,source_path,source_row "
                    "FROM input_records ORDER BY sha256($seed||':'||article_id),article_id "
                    "LIMIT $limit",
                    {"seed": str(seed), "limit": limit},
                )
                con.execute(
                    "CREATE VIEW chosen AS SELECT i.* FROM input_records i "
                    "JOIN sample_keys s "
                    "USING(article_id,source_path,source_row)"
                )
            else:
                con.execute("CREATE VIEW chosen AS SELECT * FROM input_records")
            con.execute(
                "CREATE VIEW identities AS SELECT *, sha256(to_json(struct_pack("
                "body:=text_sha256,title:=title,date:=publish_date,publisher:=hostname,"
                "candidates:=candidates))) AS inference_id FROM chosen"
            )
            con.execute(
                "CREATE VIEW selected AS SELECT inference_id,article_id FROM identities"
            )
            unit_count = min(count, limit)
            query = (
                "SELECT to_json(i) FROM identities i "
                "JOIN selected s USING(inference_id,article_id) "
                "ORDER BY source_path,source_row"
            )
            requested = unit_count
            if selection:
                con.execute(
                    "COPY (SELECT i.* FROM identities i JOIN selected s "
                    "USING(inference_id,article_id) ORDER BY source_path,source_row) "
                    "TO $output (FORMAT PARQUET)",
                    {"output": str(selection.with_suffix(".parquet.tmp"))},
                )
                selection.with_suffix(".parquet.tmp").replace(selection)
                if frame_metadata:
                    _write_json(
                        frame_metadata,
                        {
                            "frame_documents": count,
                            "requested": requested,
                            "seed": seed,
                            "selection": "SHA256(seed:article_id) retained-row priority",
                            "frame_unit": "retained source article rows",
                            "selection_sha256": hashlib.sha256(
                                selection.read_bytes()
                            ).hexdigest(),
                        },
                    )
                con.execute(
                    "SELECT to_json(s) FROM read_parquet(?) s "
                    "ORDER BY source_path,source_row",
                    [str(selection)],
                )
            else:
                con.execute(query)
            if selection:
                yield _article_batches(con, [selection], identities=False), count, requested
            else:
    
                def batches() -> Iterator[list[Article]]:
                    while rows := con.fetchmany(4096):
                        yield [Article.model_validate_json(row[0]) for row in rows]
    
                yield batches(), count, requested

    def _export(store: _Store, output: Path) -> None:
        jsonl = output / "decisions.jsonl.tmp"
        pairs_path = output / "company-decisions.jsonl.tmp"
        pair_count = 0
        with (
            jsonl.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as documents,
            pairs_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as pairs,
        ):
            for article, decision, _, reused in store.records():
                document = article | decision | {"decision_reused": reused}
                documents.write(_json(document) + "\n")
                candidates = {
                    str(candidate["issuer_id"]): candidate
                    for candidate in article.get("candidates", [])
                    if isinstance(candidate, dict)
                }
                for company in document.get("companies", []):
                    if not isinstance(company, dict):
                        raise ValueError("Company decisions must be mappings")
                    pair = {
                        **company,
                        "article_id": document["article_id"],
                        "document_id": document["document_id"],
                        "inference_id": document["inference_id"],
                        "article": {
                            key: value
                            for key, value in article.items()
                            if key != "candidates"
                        },
                        "candidate": candidates[str(company["issuer_id"])],
                        "request_sha256": decision.get("request_sha256"),
                        "model_name": decision.get("model_name"),
                    }
                    pairs.write(_json(pair) + "\n")
                    pair_count += 1
        jsonl.replace(output / "decisions.jsonl")
        if pair_count:
            with duckdb.connect() as con:
                con.execute(
                    "COPY (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto($json, "
                    "format='newline_delimited')) "
                    "TO $out (FORMAT PARQUET)",
                    {
                        "json": str(pairs_path),
                        "out": str(output / "predictions.parquet.tmp"),
                    },
                )
            (output / "predictions.parquet.tmp").replace(output / "predictions.parquet")
        pairs_path.unlink()
    
    
    def _failure(article: Article, error: Exception) -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
        status = (
            "too_long"
            if getattr(error, "status_code", None) == 422 and "token" in str(error).lower()
            else "server_failed"
        )
        return {
            "status": status,
            "error": str(error),
            "companies": [
                {
                    "issuer_id": candidate["issuer_id"],
                    "status": status if _descriptor(candidate) else "deferred_identity",
                    "identity_score": None,
                    "substantive_score": None,
                    "raw_primary_score": None,
                    "coverage_score": None,
                    "identity_tag": None,
                    "substantive_tag": None,
                    "primary_tag": None,
                    "coverage_tag": None,
                    "relevance_score": None,
                    "primary_score": None,
                    "consistency_flags": []
                    if _descriptor(candidate)
                    else ["unresolved_company_name"],
                    "validation_status": "pending_human",
                }
                for candidate in article.candidates
            ],
        }
    
    
    async def _check_server(config: ArticleLabelsConfig, output: Path) -> None:
    async def _run(
        input: Path, output: Path, params: Path, benchmark: bool, source: Path | None = None
    ) -> None:
        config = load_config(params)
        summary = json.loads((input / "summary.json").read_text())
        if summary.get("status") != "complete":
            raise ValueError("Inference requires a completed CPU index")
        output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        cpu_manifest = TypeAdapter(dict[str, JsonValue]).validate_json(
            (input / "manifest.json").read_bytes()
        )
        source_root = _resolve_source(input, cpu_manifest, source)
        contract = {
            "config": config.model_dump(mode="json"),
            "runtime": json.loads(config.runtime_manifest.read_text()),
            "cpu": cpu_manifest,
            "scorer_sha256": hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
            "benchmark": benchmark,
            "storage": "benchmark-readable"
            if benchmark
            else "compressed-source-record-chunks",
        }
        operational = {
            "deadline_utc",
            "reserve_seconds",
            "concurrency",
            "request_timeout_seconds",
            "server_url",
            "runtime_manifest",
        }
        identity_contract = contract | {
            "config": config.model_dump(mode="json", exclude=operational)
        }
        fingerprint = hashlib.sha256(_json(identity_contract).encode()).hexdigest()
        manifest_path = output / "manifest.json"
        if (
            manifest_path.exists()
            and json.loads(manifest_path.read_text())["contract_sha256"] != fingerprint
        ):
            raise ValueError("Scoring inputs changed; use a new output directory")
        _write_json(manifest_path, {**contract, "contract_sha256": fingerprint})
        _write_json(
            output / "source.json",
            {
                "resolved_source": str(source_root),
                "source_override": str(source) if source is not None else None,
                "body_verification": "SHA256 checked against the immutable CPU index",
            },
        )
        await _check_server(config, output)
        model = SystemOneModel(
            config.api_model, provider=SystemOneProvider(base_url=config.server_url)
        )
        store = _Store(output, production=not benchmark)
        store.source_files_total = len(list(input.glob("shards/*/retained.parquet")))
        saved_clock = store.db.execute("SELECT seconds,preparation FROM clock").fetchone()
        prior_seconds, prior_preparation = float(saved_clock[0]), float(saved_clock[1])
        deadline = config.deadline_utc.timestamp() - config.reserve_seconds
        started = time.monotonic()
        stopped_for_storage = False
        deadline_reached = False

    @pytest.mark.component
    def test_companies_share_one_native_request_with_structured_questions() -> None:
        # Arrange: capture the actual provider transport without starting a model.
        bodies: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    
        def respond(request: httpx2.Request) -> httpx2.Response:
            body = json.loads(request.content)
            bodies.append(body)
            answers: dict[str, object] = {}
            for name, question in body["questions"].items():
                if question["type"] == "noul":
                    answers[name] = {"type": "noul", "noul": 0.99}
                else:
                    options = list(question["criteria"])
                    answers[name] = {
                        "type": "choice",
                        "choice": options[0],
                        "confidence": 1.0,
                        "probabilities": {
                            key: float(index == 0) for index, key in enumerate(options)
                        },
                    }
            return httpx2.Response(
                200,
                json={
                    "model": "kev-latest",
                    "answers": answers,
                    "usage": {"input_tokens": 123, "output_tokens": 0},
                },
            )
    
        client = httpx2.AsyncClient(transport=httpx2.MockTransport(respond))
        model = SystemOneModel(
            "kev-latest",
            provider=SystemOneProvider(
                base_url="http://test.invalid",
                http_client=client,
            ),
        )
        candidates: list[dict[str, JsonValue]] = [
            {"issuer_id": "a", "name": "Alpha Inc."},
            {"issuer_id": "b", "name": "Beta Inc.", "tickers": ["BETA"]},
            {"issuer_id": "c", "name": None, "original_name": "Wrong Company"},
            {"issuer_id": "other-namespace:a", "name": "Alpha Inc."},
        ]
    
        # Act: ask the three binary questions through the real provider adapter.
        response = asyncio.run(
            model.decide(
                DecisionRequest(
                    state={"article": "Alpha acquired Beta."},
                    questions=build_questions(candidates),
                ),
                model_settings={},
            )
        )
    
        # Assert: one request keeps seven typed questions and defers unresolved identity.
        assert len(bodies) == 1
        assert len(response.answers) == 7
        sent = bodies[0]["questions"]
        assert isinstance(sent, dict)
        assert sent["c1.identity"]["instructions"] == (
            "Does this article mention the company Beta Inc. (BETA)?"
        )
        assert sent["c0.substantive"]["type"] == "noul"
        assert sent["c0.primary"]["instructions"] == (
            "Is Alpha Inc. one of the main subjects of this article?"
        )
        assert all(not key.startswith("c2.") for key in sent)
        assert all(not key.startswith("c3.") for key in sent)
        interpreted = interpret_answers(candidates, response.answers, 0.95)
        deferred = interpreted[2]
        assert deferred["status"] == "deferred_identity"
        assert deferred["identity_score"] is None
        assert interpreted[3] == interpreted[0] | {"issuer_id": "other-namespace:a"}
    
    
    @pytest.mark.unit
    @example(identity=0.99, substantive=0.9, primary=0.99)
    @example(identity=0.99, substantive=0.01, primary=0.99)
    @given(
        identity=st.floats(min_value=0, max_value=1),
        substantive=st.floats(min_value=0, max_value=1),
        primary=st.floats(min_value=0, max_value=1),
    )
    def test_binary_scores_preserve_raw_marginals_and_gate_published_primary(
        identity: float,
        substantive: float,
        primary: float,
    ) -> None:
        # Arrange: independent binary heads and a non-editorial article-kind annotation.
        candidate: list[dict[str, JsonValue]] = [{"issuer_id": "a", "name": "Alpha Inc."}]
        answers: dict[str, DecisionAnswer] = {
            "article_kind": ChoiceAnswer(
                choice="press_release",
                confidence=1,
                probabilities={
                    "reporting": 0,
                    "analysis_opinion": 0,
                    "market_roundup": 0,
                    "press_release": 1,
                },
            ),
            "c0.identity": NoulAnswer(noul=identity),
            "c0.substantive": NoulAnswer(noul=substantive),
            "c0.primary": NoulAnswer(noul=primary),
        }
    
        # Act: interpret the native scores under the configured identity threshold.
        row = interpret_answers(candidate, answers, 0.95)[0]
    
        # Assert: raw heads stay intact, inconsistencies stay visible, and identity gates.
        assert row["primary_score"] == (primary if identity >= 0.95 else None)
        assert row["raw_primary_score"] == primary
        assert row["substantive_score"] == row["relevance_score"] == substantive
        assert row["coverage_score"] == max(substantive, primary)
        flags = row["consistency_flags"]
        assert isinstance(flags, list)
        assert ("primary_exceeds_substantive" in flags) == (primary > substantive)
        assert ("substantive_exceeds_identity" in flags) == (substantive > identity)
        assert row["primary_tag"] == (primary >= 0.5)
        assert (row["status"] == "accepted") == (
            identity >= 0.95
            and (primary >= 0.95 or substantive >= 0.95)
            and not (primary >= 0.95 and substantive <= 1 - 0.95)
        )
        assert row["validation_status"] == "pending_human"
    
    
    def _tiny_index(tmp_path: Path) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
        body = "Alpha reported increased sales."
        source = tmp_path / "source"
        source.mkdir()
        index = tmp_path / "index/shards/00000"
        index.mkdir(parents=True)
        records = [
            {
                "article_id": f"row-{row}",
                "source_article_id": f"original-{row}",
                "document_id": "body-id",
                "source_path": "a.parquet",
                "source_row": row,
                "text_sha256": hashlib.sha256(body.encode()).hexdigest(),
                "title": title,
                "hostname": "news.example",
                "publish_date": "2020-01-01",
                "quality_flags": ["partial_company_catalog"],
                "candidates": [
                    {
                        "issuer_id": "a",
                        "name": "Alpha Inc.",
                        "evidence_sources": ["name_alias"],
                        "uncertainty_flags": ["registry_names_not_historically_certified"],
                    }
                ],
            }
            for row, title in enumerate(
                ("Alpha results", "A different headline", "Alpha results")
            )
        ]
        data = tmp_path / "index.jsonl"
        data.write_text("".join(json.dumps(row) + "\n" for row in records))
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            con.execute(
                "COPY (SELECT $text AS text, {'source_id': n, 'byline': 'Reporter'} "
                "AS metadata FROM range(3) rows(n)) TO $file (FORMAT PARQUET)",
                {"text": body, "file": str(source / "a.parquet")},
            )
            con.execute(
                "COPY (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto($json)) TO $file (FORMAT PARQUET)",
                {"json": str(data), "file": str(index / "retained.parquet")},
            )
        (tmp_path / "index/manifest.json").write_text(
            json.dumps({"source_root": "../source"})
        )
        (tmp_path / "index/summary.json").write_text(json.dumps({"status": "complete"}))
        return tmp_path / "index", source
    
    
    @pytest.mark.integration
    def test_stream_preserves_source_copies_and_reuses_original_row_group(
        tmp_path: Path,
    ) -> None:
        # Arrange: equal bodies have two headlines and one exact inference duplicate.
        index, source = _tiny_index(tmp_path)
        body = "Alpha reported increased sales."
    
        # Act: stream source records and recover text and metadata in two batches.
        with _frame(index, None, 42) as (batches, count, requested):
            articles = [article for batch in batches for article in batch]
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            reader = _BodyReader(source, con)
            first = reader.read(articles[:1])
            second = reader.read(articles[1:])
    
        # Assert: three source records keep two request identities and distinct metadata.
        assert count == requested == 3
        assert len({article.inference_id for article in articles}) == 2
        assert {article.title for article in articles} == {
            "Alpha results",
            "A different headline",
        }
        assert [original.text for original in first.values()] == [body]
        assert [original.text for original in second.values()] == [body, body]
        assert [original.metadata for original in first.values()] == [
            {"source_id": 0, "byline": "Reporter"}
        ]
        assert [original.metadata for original in second.values()] == [
            {"source_id": 1, "byline": "Reporter"},
            {"source_id": 2, "byline": "Reporter"},
        ]
        assert reader.groups_read == 1

    async def _score(
        article: Article, text: str, config: ArticleLabelsConfig, model: SystemOneModel
    ) -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
        state: JsonValue = {
            "title": article.title,
            "published_at": article.publish_date,
            "publisher": article.hostname,
            "article": text,
        }
        candidates = {str(item["issuer_id"]): item for item in article.candidates}
        unique = list(candidates.values())
        sources = _question_sources(unique)
        representatives = [
            candidate
            for index, candidate in enumerate(unique)
            if sources.get(index, index) == index
        ]
        rows: dict[str, dict[str, JsonValue]] = {}
        responses: list[JsonValue] = []
        request_hashes: list[JsonValue] = []
        input_tokens = 0
        started = time.monotonic()
        for offset in range(0, len(representatives), config.max_candidates_per_request):
            batch = representatives[offset : offset + config.max_candidates_per_request]
            questions = build_questions(batch)
            request = DecisionRequest(state=state, questions=questions)
            # The request identity includes every native structured question and its rubric.
            request_hashes.append(
                hashlib.sha256(_json(asdict(request)).encode()).hexdigest()
            )
            response = await model.decide(
                request, model_settings={"timeout": config.request_timeout_seconds}
            )
            responses.append(json.loads(_json(asdict(response))))
            typed: dict[str, DecisionAnswer] = {}
            for name, answer in response.answers.items():
                if not isinstance(answer, NoulAnswer | ChoiceAnswer):
                    raise ValueError(f"Unexpected answer kind: {name}")
                typed[name] = answer
            for row in interpret_answers(batch, typed, config.min_probability):
                rows[str(row["issuer_id"])] = row
            input_tokens += response.usage.input_tokens
        return {
            "status": "complete",
            "companies": [
                rows[str(unique[sources.get(index, index)]["issuer_id"])]
                | {"issuer_id": candidate["issuer_id"]}
                for index, candidate in enumerate(unique)
            ],
            "request_sha256": request_hashes,
            "responses": responses,
            "input_tokens": input_tokens,
            "elapsed_seconds": time.monotonic() - started,
            "model_name": config.api_model,
        }
    async def _check_server(config: ArticleLabelsConfig, output: Path) -> None:
        profile = TypeAdapter(dict[str, JsonValue]).validate_json(
            config.runtime_manifest.read_bytes()
        )
        for key, expected in (
            ("api_model", config.api_model),
            ("base_model", config.base_model),
            ("model", config.model),
            ("model_revision", config.model_revision),
            ("base_revision", config.base_revision),
            ("max_context_tokens", config.max_context_tokens),
        ):
            if key in profile and profile[key] != expected:
                raise ValueError(f"Configured {key} differs from the runtime profile")
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=config.request_timeout_seconds) as client:
            response = await client.get(f"{config.server_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/models")
            response.raise_for_status()
            reported = response.json()
        servers = [_ServerInfo.model_validate(row) for row in reported["models"]]
        server = next((row for row in servers if row.name == config.api_model), None)
        if server is None:
            raise ValueError("The server does not advertise the configured model alias")
        expected_fields: dict[str, JsonValue] = {
            "base": config.base_model,
            "max_state_tokens": config.max_context_tokens,
            "truncate_states": profile.get("truncate_states", False),
        }
        for key in ("device", "backend", "dtype", "lora"):
            if key in profile:
                expected_fields[key] = profile[key]
        observed = server.model_dump(mode="json")
        if any(observed[key] != value for key, value in expected_fields.items()):
            raise ValueError("Native server metadata differs from the runtime profile")
        temperature = profile.get("temperature")
        if (
            not isinstance(temperature, int | float)
            or abs(server.temperature - temperature) > 1e-9
        ):
            raise ValueError("Native server calibration differs from the runtime profile")
        _write_json(output / "server.json", reported)
    
    
    def _progress(store: _Store, requested: int, elapsed: float) -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
        counts = store.counts()
        return {
            **counts,
            "requested": requested,
            "succeeded": counts["completed"],
            "unattempted": max(0, requested - counts["attempted"]),
            "remaining": max(
                0, requested - counts["completed"] - counts["context_deferred"]
            ),
            "elapsed_seconds": elapsed,
            "source_record_chunks_committed": int(
                store.db.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM chunks").fetchone()[0]
            ),
            "source_files_total": store.source_files_total,
            "last_source": store.last_source,
        }
    
    
    def _storage_projection(store: _Store, population: int) -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
        counts = store.counts()
        page_size = int(store.db.execute("PRAGMA page_size").fetchone()[0])
        used_pages = int(store.db.execute("PRAGMA page_count").fetchone()[0]) - int(
            store.db.execute("PRAGMA freelist_count").fetchone()[0]
        )
        observed = counts["attempted"]
        measured_bytes = counts["decision_chunk_bytes"] + used_pages * page_size
        bytes_per_record = measured_bytes / observed if observed else None
        remaining = max(0, population - observed)
        return {
            "observed_source_records": observed,
            "compressed_chunk_bytes": counts["decision_chunk_bytes"],
            "active_sqlite_bytes": used_pages * page_size,
            "conditional_bytes_per_source_record": bytes_per_record,
            "conditional_remaining_bytes": remaining * bytes_per_record
            if bytes_per_record is not None
            else None,
            "filesystem_free_bytes": shutil.disk_usage(store.output).free,
            "basis": (

    def _production_metrics(
        connection: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection,
        scores: Path,
        benchmark: dict[str, JsonValue],
        config: ArticleLabelsConfig,
    ) -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
        """Aggregate scalar fields from committed chunks without loading article JSON."""
        files = sorted(scores.glob("chunks/*.parquet"))
        if files:
            connection.from_parquet([str(path) for path in files]).create_view(
                "score_chunks"
            )
            connection.execute(
                "CREATE VIEW scored_records AS SELECT article_id,inference_id,status,"
                "json_extract(decision_json,'$.companies[*]') AS companies,"
                "json_extract_string(decision_json,'$.model_name') AS model_name "
                "FROM score_chunks"
            )
        else:
            connection.execute(
                "CREATE VIEW scored_records AS SELECT NULL::VARCHAR AS article_id,"
                "NULL::VARCHAR AS inference_id,NULL::VARCHAR AS status,"
                "[]::JSON[] AS companies,NULL::VARCHAR AS model_name WHERE false"
            )
        connection.execute(
            "CREATE VIEW company_scores AS SELECT article_id,inference_id,"
            "unnest(companies) AS company FROM scored_records"
        )
        judgments = _query_rows(
            connection,
            "SELECT json_extract_string(company,'$.status') AS status,"
            "count(*) AS candidate_pairs FROM company_scores "
            "GROUP BY status ORDER BY status",
        )
        counts = _query_rows(
            connection,
            "SELECT count(*) AS source_records_in_chunks,"
            "count(*) FILTER(WHERE list_bool_or(list_transform(companies,"
            "c -> try_cast(json_extract(c,'$.identity_score') AS DOUBLE) IS NOT NULL))) "
            "AS source_records_with_scored_companies,"
            "count(*) FILTER(WHERE len(companies)>0 AND list_bool_and("
            "list_transform(companies,c -> json_extract_string(c,'$.status')="
            "'deferred_identity'))) AS source_records_with_only_deferred_identity,"
            "coalesce(sum(len(companies)),0) AS candidate_pairs_in_chunks "
            "FROM scored_records",
        )[0]
        counts["source_status_counts"] = _query_rows(
            connection,
            "SELECT status,count(*) AS source_records FROM scored_records "
            "GROUP BY status ORDER BY status",
        )
        counts["unattempted_source_records"] = benchmark.get("unattempted")
        requested = _number(benchmark, "requested")
        observed = counts["source_records_in_chunks"]
        counts["source_records_without_committed_decisions"] = (
            max(0, int(requested) - observed)
            if requested is not None and isinstance(observed, int)
            else None
        )
        manifest = (
            _read_json(scores / "manifest.json")
            if (scores / "manifest.json").is_file()
            else {}
        )
        settings = manifest.get("config")
        settings = settings if isinstance(settings, dict) else {}
        threshold = _number(settings, "min_probability") or config.min_probability
        distributions = _query_rows(
            connection,
            "WITH values AS (SELECT field,try_cast(json_extract(company,'$.'||field) "
            "AS DOUBLE) AS value FROM company_scores CROSS JOIN "
            "(VALUES('identity_score'),('substantive_score'),('raw_primary_score'),"
            "('primary_score'),('coverage_score')) fields(field)) "
            "SELECT field AS score,count(value) AS observed_candidate_pairs,"
            "min(value) AS minimum,avg(value) AS mean,max(value) AS maximum,"
            "count(*) FILTER(WHERE value >= 0.5) AS at_least_half,"
            "count(*) FILTER(WHERE value >= $threshold) AS at_least_threshold "
            "FROM values GROUP BY field ORDER BY field",
            {"threshold": threshold},
        )
        return {
            "score_source": "committed_production_chunks",
            "observed_judgments": judgments,
            "production_scoring": counts,
            "score_distributions": distributions,
            "scoring_metadata": {
                "scorer_sha256": manifest.get("scorer_sha256"),
                "contract_sha256": manifest.get("contract_sha256"),
                "rubric": manifest.get("rubric"),
                "runtime": manifest.get("runtime"),
                "config": settings,
                "observed_models": _query_rows(
                    connection,
                    "SELECT model_name,count(*) AS source_records FROM scored_records "
                    "GROUP BY model_name ORDER BY model_name",
                ),
                "model_selection_threshold": threshold,
                "validation_status": "pending_human",
                "interpretation": (
                    "Scores and selection thresholds are provisional model outputs; "
                    "no calibrated probabilities or validated precision are inferred. "
                    "The scorer hash identifies the exact rubric when it is not recorded. "
                    "Source-record counts and candidate-pair counts "
                    "have separate denominators."
                ),
            },
        }

        async def decide(

            calls.append(request)
            if (

    $ cat > data/inputs/article-labels/README.md <<'EOF'
        # Article labels and research filters
        
        This experiment separates company retrieval, dated issuer identity and model
        judgments about article coverage. Its source is the restored
        [Fine News snapshot](../fine-news/README.md). The historical 115-domain allowlist
        is an acquisition policy; it has not been reviewed as a trusted-publisher list.
        All model labels remain provisional pending human evaluation.
        
        ## Source and CPU evidence
        
        The adopted Rust Aho–Corasick run covers the same 168 source files. Source and
        prediction checksums are verified before adoption. The compact CPU index retains
        12,241,870 of 14,807,287 source records and accounts separately for every exclusion.
        Article keys use relative source paths and physical row numbers. Native article
        IDs are preserved but are not assumed unique.
        
        Text remains in the raw snapshot. Indexes store coordinates, text hashes,
        candidates and matching evidence. Exact-text groups retain every source membership;
        they do not establish complete syndicated-story deduplication. A literal name or
        publisher keyword match establishes a retrieval candidate, not company relevance.
        
        The independent [CPU audit](../../research/experiments/article-labels/cpu-audit/report.md)
        confirmed correct stored offsets but found generic aliases, footer mentions,
        non-financial publisher tags and a cross-year issuer-name defect. The review is
        qualitative AI evidence, not human gold or measured population precision/recall.
        Its retained and no-hit source samples, observations and checksums are preserved.
        
        ## Dated candidate correction
        
        `correct_article_candidates` preserves every broad candidate and source record.
        It uses a unique verified article-year issuer link to resolve Top1000 names,
        tickers and CIKs together. Ambiguous or unsupported links remain unresolved;
        scoring never substitutes the original, potentially wrong company name.
        
        The corrected index records original values, authority identifiers, supported
        aliases, lexical ambiguity and evidence tiers. The SEC snapshot contains 190
        cached submissions records. Current registry names are not certified historical
        names, and SEC former-name filing dates are not guaranteed validity intervals.
        Undated GH identities retain their limitation. Publisher tags and legacy ticker
        spans remain unverified retrieval evidence.
        
        Title/body evidence tiers are retrieval diagnostics. They do not classify primary
        coverage or remove candidates from the scoring population. Capped stored spans
        remain censored evidence rather than proof that other mentions are absent.
        
        ## Fixed pilot
        
        The pilot selects 1,000 retained source records by the smallest
        `SHA256(seed:article_id)` values before loading bodies or requesting predictions.
        Duplicate source copies remain in this sampling frame. `selection.parquet`
        preserves the sample; it cannot establish missed-company recall from survivors.
        
        The frozen initial pilot lives in
        `data/processed/experiments/article-labels/benchmark-1000/`. It scored 993 records,
        deferred seven beyond 8,192 tokens and had no server failures. Its original rubric
        accepted no pairs at 0.95. Exact scorer, reporter, parameters and runtime assets
        are archived alongside DVC pointers; frozen stages preserve that baseline.
        
        After candidate correction and runtime selection, run the current pilot with:
        
        ```bash
        just dvc repro benchmark_company_labels
        just dvc repro report_company_benchmark
        ```
        
        Outputs use `benchmark-corrected-1000/` beneath the processed and research
        experiment directories. `benchmark.json` records counts and measured throughput;
        `decisions.jsonl` and `predictions.parquet` preserve the small pilot's predictions.
        Fresh source-only audit labels are sealed before model outputs are inspected.
        Neither synthetic examples nor AI agreement establish human-validated accuracy.
        
        ## Native inference and checkpoints
        
        [Native Kev](../../../infra/inference/README.md) runs in a separate pinned GPU
        runtime. Pydantic's System One client shares each article across company questions
        in one request. Exact repeated company descriptors share questions while retaining
        all namespace-specific links. Large candidate sets use bounded requests.
        Article kind is an annotation, rather than an automatic editorial-content gate.
        
        The runtime profile records model revisions, checkpoint hashes, precision,
        kernels and context admission. Oversized documents are explicitly deferred;
        silent text truncation is disabled. Prediction manifests preserve the scorer and
        runtime contract. A changed scientific contract requires a new output directory.
        Operational deadlines, transport timeouts and concurrency can change on resume.
        Pass `--source data/raw/fine-news` to override archived absolute source locations.
        
        ```bash
        just dvc repro score_company_labels
        ```
        
        Production stores compressed source-record Parquet chunks and a small SQLite
        resume ledger in `data/processed/experiments/article-labels/corpus/`. It preserves
        source metadata, candidate provenance and raw model outputs. Successful identical
        requests can be reused; transient server failures are retried on resume. Context
        failures, unresolved identities and pending records stay separate from negatives.
        `progress.json` reports counts and `storage.json` gives a conditional disk estimate.
        
        An incomplete, storage-limited or deadline-limited run exits unsuccessfully after
        saving checkpoints. DVC therefore does not proceed automatically to its report.
        To inspect a partial run, invoke the reporting command directly:
        
        ```bash
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV \
          uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline \
          pipeline stages research report-article-labels \
          --cpu data/processed/experiments/article-labels/cpu \
          --census data/research/experiments/article-labels/cpu \
          --scores data/processed/experiments/article-labels/corpus \
          --output data/research/experiments/article-labels/corpus
        ```
        
        Reports distinguish source records, candidate pairs, scored coverage and pending
        work. They provide CSV and LaTeX tables without projecting accepted model labels
        as validated population coverage. The 0.95 cutoff is a provisional selection rule,
        not an empirical accuracy guarantee. Parameters and the operating deadline live
        under `experiments.article_labels` in `params.yaml`; measured end-to-end capacity
        must support any claim that full scoring will finish before that deadline.
        EOF

    +## Company decisions
    +
    +The selected rubric asks three binary questions per resolved company, using its
    +canonical name and tickers: whether the article mentions it, provides meaningful
    +company-specific information beyond a mention, and treats it as a main subject.
    +Several companies may be primary. The manifest records the exact question
    +templates and article-kind criteria. The current runtime is Kev-4B in BF16.
    +
    +`identity_score`, `substantive_score` and `raw_primary_score` preserve independent
    +model outputs. `coverage_score` is their substantive/primary maximum: a ranking
    +rule rather than a calibrated union probability. Contradictory marginals retain
    +consistency flags. `primary_score` is available only after identity meets the
    +configured cutoff. A provisional accepted pair requires confident identity and
    +coverage without a strong coverage contradiction. Article kind does not gate it.
    +Saved outputs support later threshold comparisons without rerunning inference.
    +
     ## Native inference and checkpoints

    # Native decision inference
    
    These scripts run the pinned native Kev server using the CUDA libraries of an
    already cached container image. SGLang is not launched. Native Kev shares the
    article prefix across its independent identity and coverage questions.
    
    From the repository root, prepare the small serving dependencies and then supply
    the existing checkpoint and Hugging Face base-model cache:
    
    ```bash
    just inference::setup
    just inference::serve /path/to/kev-0.8b /path/to/huggingface/hub
    docker logs ccfinance-kev-native
    just inference::status
    ```
    
    The versioned runtime manifest records the model, source, image, precision,
    kernels and admission limit. The entrypoint applies that limit to both the
    article and every complete article-question sequence. Oversized inputs fail
    explicitly; text truncation is disabled. Local package and compilation caches
    live under ignored `.runtime/`.
    
    The optional third argument selects another versioned runtime profile:
    
    ```bash
    bash infra/inference/start.sh .runtime/models/kev-4b .runtime/hf-cache \
        data/inputs/article-labels/kev-4b.json
    ```
    
    The 4B profile uses BF16 and retains one article prefix. Its adapter and head
    checksums are checked before loading. The serving trial records actual memory
    use separately from the model publisher's memory estimate.
    
    The selected company-labeling pilot uses this 4B profile with three concise
    binary questions per distinct company descriptor. The questions share the full
    article prefix. Its graph buffers are bounded explicitly: four states, 16 rows
    and 16,384 tokens. A fresh restart used 13,628 MiB before inference on the
    16,311 MiB GPU; earlier real-article trials reached 14,716 MiB. One graph capture
    ran out of memory and fell back to eager inference, with every HTTP request
    succeeding. These observations establish the tested workload's behavior, rather
    than a guarantee for every possible input.
    
    `kev-0.8b.json` records a separate experimental 16k admission trial. The smaller
    model was rejected for this pilot after the same fresh source cases produced
    more false positives. The seven-case long-context study was stopped after one
    HTTP success; it does not establish 16k semantic quality. The original
    `runtime.json` remains the historical 8k baseline.
    
    Stop the server with `just inference::stop`; remove its stopped
    container with `docker rm ccfinance-kev-native` before starting a replacement.

    # Candidate identity correction audit
    
    The completed correction preserves all **12,241,870 retained source records and
    38,053,717 company-candidate pairs** across 168 shards. No article or candidate
    was removed by this correction. The original baseline still accounts for all
    14,807,287 source records: 12,241,870 retained and 2,565,417 excluded.
    
    The first complete run took 1,254.24 seconds (20.90 minutes). Its unchanged
    summary is saved in [first-complete-summary.json](first-complete-summary.json).
    
    ## Identity reconciliation
    
    Names and tickers follow the frozen membership's verified article-year CIK,
    rather than aliases pooled across every historical identity sharing a PERMCO.
    Original names, tickers, identity lists and match evidence remain available.
    
    | Identity authority | Candidate pairs |
    | --- | ---: |
    | Verified article-year CIK | 32,062,473 |
    | Fixed GH reference CIK, undated | 4,631,128 |
    | Unverified article-year link; corrected name unresolved | 1,360,116 |
    
    There are 2,202,804 resolved canonical-name changes. This count describes
    reference consistency, not corrected semantic article-company labels.
    
    The title-and-body diagnostic contains 1,934,894 articles and 2,123,555 pairs.
    The other 10,306,976 articles remain retained with their other evidence tiers.
    The summary's `deferred_articles` field means outside that diagnostic; it does
    not mean every such article has an unresolved identity or should be discarded.
    
    Use `identity_status` and the corrected name for identity handling. In
    particular, 15,010 fixed-GH pairs have no stored permitted name evidence and
    receive the fallback `unresolved_identity` evidence tier, while retaining a
    fixed-GH identity and a nonempty corrected name.
    
    ## Frozen sample checks
    
    The original benchmark remains exactly **1,000 distinct source records and
    3,137 candidate pairs**. There are zero missing or added article IDs, source
    coordinate mismatches, or candidate-count changes. Of its pairs, 2,646 have
    verified dated identities, 386 use the fixed undated GH reference, and 105 have
    unverified article-year links.
    
    All five benchmark American Airlines cases now resolve to CIK `0000006201`
    and ticker `AAL`, preserving the original Alpha Metallurgical assignment for
    audit. The separate audited Delta-results article at
    `2021-01/eng_Latn/part-000001.parquet`, row 20489, retains its American Airlines
    secondary-company evidence; lacking a title match does not remove it.
    
    The separate fresh-audit ViacomCBS case at
    `2020-02/eng_Latn/part-000000.parquet`, row 74501, remains unresolved because the
    2020 PERMCO 21866 membership has no verified CIK. Its unrelated original Banzai
    name is preserved for audit and is not supplied as a resolved company name.
    
    The narrow [sample comparison](sample-comparison.parquet) preserves candidate
    order and both original and corrected fields. Exact observed cases are saved
    in [observed-checks.json](observed-checks.json); full census counts and limits
    are in [metrics.json](metrics.json). [Methods](methods.json) record input hashes
    and the census SQL, and [audit.py](audit.py) records the calculations used.
    
    ## Limits
    
    These are structural checks against frozen references, with no semantic gold
    labels, model predictions, precision estimates or confidence intervals. The
    registry names are current or undated; verified article-year CIK links do not
    certify historical alias validity. SEC former-name observations provide
    context flags, not automatic exclusions. A resolved identity still requires
    semantic article-company relevance and subject scoring. Title-and-body tiers
    are diagnostics and do not define the final dataset's scope.
