    class _BodyReader:
        """Read and retain one bounded original row group across consecutive batches."""
    
        def __init__(self, source: Path, con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection) -> None:
            self.source = source
            self.con = con
            self.bounds: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, int]]] = {}
            self.cached_group: tuple[str, int] | None = None
            self.cached_rows: dict[int, tuple[str, JsonValue]] = {}
            self.groups_read = 0
    
        def read(self, articles: list[Article]) -> dict[str, "_Body"]:
            result: dict[str, _Body] = {}
            groups: dict[tuple[str, int], list[Article]] = {}
            for article in articles:
                if article.source_path not in self.bounds:
                    metadata = self.con.execute(
                        "SELECT row_group_id,max(row_group_num_rows),"
                        "sum(total_uncompressed_size) FILTER (WHERE path_in_schema='text') "
                        "FROM parquet_metadata(?) GROUP BY row_group_id "
                        "ORDER BY row_group_id",
                        [str(self.source / article.source_path)],
                    ).fetchall()
                    offset = 0
                    bounds = []
                    for _, rows, size in metadata:
                        bounds.append((offset, offset + int(rows), int(size or 0)))
                        offset += int(rows)
                    self.bounds[article.source_path] = bounds
                bounds = self.bounds[article.source_path]
                index = bisect.bisect_right([b[0] for b in bounds], article.source_row) - 1
                if index < 0 or article.source_row >= bounds[index][1]:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Source row outside original file: {article.article_id}"
                    )
                groups.setdefault((article.source_path, index), []).append(article)
            for (file, index), members in groups.items():
                lower, upper, size = self.bounds[file][index]
                if self.cached_group != (file, index):
                    if size > 128 * 1024 * 1024:
                        rows = self.con.execute(
                            "SELECT file_row_number,text,to_json(metadata) "
                            "FROM read_parquet("
                            "$file,file_row_number=true) WHERE file_row_number "
                            "IN (SELECT unnest($rows))",
                            {
                                "file": str(self.source / file),
                                "rows": [article.source_row for article in members],
                            },
                        ).fetchall()
                        self.cached_group = None
                    else:
                        rows = self.con.execute(
                            "SELECT file_row_number,text,to_json(metadata) "
                            "FROM read_parquet("
                            "$file,file_row_number=true) "
                            "WHERE file_row_number >= $lower "
                            "AND file_row_number < $upper",
                            {
                                "file": str(self.source / file),
                                "lower": lower,
                                "upper": upper,
                            },
                        ).fetchall()
                        self.cached_group = (file, index)
                    self.groups_read += 1
                    self.cached_rows = {
                        int(row): (text, TypeAdapter(JsonValue).validate_json(metadata))
                        for row, text, metadata in rows
                    }
                for article in members:
                    original = self.cached_rows.get(article.source_row)
                    if original is None or not isinstance(original[0], str):
                        raise ValueError(f"Original text missing for {article.article_id}")
                    text, metadata = original
                    if hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest() != article.text_sha256:
                        raise ValueError(f"Text checksum changed for {article.article_id}")
                    result[article.article_id] = _Body(text, metadata)
            return result
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class _Body:
        text: str
        metadata: JsonValue
    
    
    def _resolve_source(
        input: Path, manifest: dict[str, JsonValue], source: Path | None
    ) -> Path:
        if source is not None:
            return source.resolve()
        value = manifest.get("source_root")
        if not isinstance(value, str):
            raise ValueError("Pass --source or provide source_root in the CPU manifest")
        path = Path(value)
        return (path if path.is_absolute() else input / path).resolve()
    
    
    def _article_batches(
        con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, files: list[Path], *, identities: bool
    ) -> Iterator[list[Article]]:
        for file in files:
            query = (
                "SELECT to_json(i) FROM read_parquet(?) i ORDER BY source_path,source_row"
            )
            if identities:
                query = (
                    "SELECT to_json(i) FROM (SELECT *, sha256(to_json(struct_pack("
                    "body:=text_sha256,title:=title,date:=publish_date,publisher:=hostname,"

                    "ORDER BY source_path,source_row"
                )
            con.execute(query, [str(file)])

                            groups.setdefault(article.inference_id, []).append(
                                (position, article)
                            )
                        tasks = []
                        for inference_id, members in groups.items():
                            cached = store.decision(inference_id)
                            if cached is not None:
                                for position, article in members:
                                    store.save_article(
                                        article,
                                        bodies[article.article_id],
                                        key,
                                        position,
                                        reused=True,
                                    )
                            else:
                                article = members[0][1]
                                tasks.append(
                                    score_one(article, bodies[article.article_id].text)
                                )
                        for task in asyncio.as_completed(tasks):
                            representative, decision = await task
                            if decision is None:
                                deadline_reached = True
                                continue
                            store.save_decision(representative.inference_id, decision)
                            for member_number, (position, article) in enumerate(
                                groups[representative.inference_id]
                            ):

        if scores is not None:
            benchmark_path = scores / "benchmark.json"
            if not benchmark_path.is_file():
                benchmark_path = scores / "summary.json"
            benchmark = _read_json(benchmark_path)
        judgments: list[dict[str, JsonValue]] = []
        if scores is not None and (scores / "predictions.parquet").is_file():
            connection.from_parquet(str(scores / "predictions.parquet")).create_view(
                "predictions"
            )
            judgments = _query_rows(
                connection,
                "SELECT status, count(*) AS candidate_pairs, "
                "count(DISTINCT inference_id) AS inference_units "
                "FROM predictions GROUP BY status ORDER BY status",
            )
        candidate_records = population["retained_records"]
        if not isinstance(candidate_records, int):
            raise ValueError("Candidate record count must be an integer")
        measured_frame = _number(benchmark, "frame_documents")
        if measured_frame is not None and not 0 <= measured_frame <= candidate_records:
            raise ValueError("Inference frame differs from retained article records")
        population_unit = benchmark.get("frame_unit")
        if not isinstance(population_unit, str):
            population_unit = (
                "inference_units"
                if measured_frame is not None
                else "retained_source_records"
            )
        result: dict[str, JsonValue] = {
            "observed_judgments": judgments,
            "judgment_counts_scope": (
                "Observed scored subset only; no population or company-year scaling"
            ),
            "capacity": throughput_estimates(
                int(measured_frame) if measured_frame is not None else candidate_records,
                benchmark,
                now=datetime.now(UTC),
                deadline=config.deadline_utc,
                reserve_seconds=config.reserve_seconds,
            ),
            "capacity_workload_unit": population_unit,
            "capacity_workload_basis": (
                "Retained source records; benchmark samples article rows"
                if population_unit == "retained_source_records"

            ),
            "benchmark": benchmark,
        }
        if scores is not None:
            manifest = (

                if (scores / "manifest.json").is_file()

            )
            if any(scores.glob("chunks/*.parquet")) or manifest.get("storage") == (
                "compressed-source-record-chunks"
            ):

        return result

    $ sed -n '1,180p' data/research/experiments/article-labels/accepted-pilot-audit/report.md; git status --short
    # Accepted pilot source review
    
    All 24 accepted namespace pairs in 21 original articles identify the displayed company and contain developed company-specific information. Each company is defensibly one of the article's main subjects, including the two companies in the rail roundup. No accepted pair appears to be a generic-word collision, footer-only mention or attribution-only link in this qualitative review.
    
    This is an AI-assisted **post-selection** check: acceptance was known, model score values were not loaded, and the original text checksums were verified for all 21 articles. These observations are not human gold, a population precision estimate, a 95% precision finding or a recall assessment. The 24 namespace pairs represent 22 distinct article/CIK combinations; Micron and Tractor Supply each appear in both Top1000 and GH namespaces.
    
    Company relevance does not establish suitability for the default editorial dataset:
    
    - **19 articles / 20 pairs** contain identifiable editorial reporting or investment analysis, often syndicated. Twelve of those articles also contain publisher or subscription promotions; the company evidence is developed in the article body.
    - **One article / two pairs** is an explicit Tractor Supply issuer press release syndicated from Business Wire. Its notes offering is primary company coverage, but it belongs in the separate release view under the current intended policy.
    - **One article / two pairs** is a developed Zacks rail roundup with “For Immediate Release,” media-contact and marketing material. The company roles are clear; its editorial-versus-promotional format needs policy review. No exclusion was applied.
    
    The examples expose source-quality limits: Micron is a summary/truncated excerpt; several analyses reference missing figures or tables; Delta contains internally inconsistent revenue/cash-burn wording, and FirstCash appears to omit revenue scale units. The Tesla item's relative weekday wording needs date review. Chipotle and Oracle publication dates precede their crawl partitions, so partition dates must not substitute for publication dates. These are observations about the retained text, not externally verified factual corrections.
    
    Only 15 of the 24 accepted links carry the verified-title-and-body discovery tier. The other nine include developed Nektar, BILL, Delta, Walmart, Chipotle, Micron and United Bankshares coverage, plus the GH Tractor Supply link. This selected subset cannot estimate a stricter filter's population recall, but it shows why stored lexical tiers must not be treated as relevance truth.
    
    The accepted links look sensible for a provisional company-relevance filter. A full run should preserve the separate source-format and quality fields and keep human validation pending. This review did not change any scoring threshold, exclusion rule, source record or sealed audit label.
    
    Evidence: [verified source records](source-records.json), [all pair observations](observations.csv), [rubric and structured observations](observations.json), [counts and limitations](summary.json), and [extraction provenance](manifest.json).

    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    set positional-arguments
    
    default:
        @just --list
    
    # Install exactly the committed workspace and build dependencies.
    setup:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv sync --locked --all-packages
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline python -c 'import duckdb; duckdb.connect().execute("INSTALL httpfs")'
    
    run *args:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline pipeline "$@"
    
    lint:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff check .
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff format --check .
    
    typecheck:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pyrefly check
    
    # Local impacted-test selection, with a bounded number of workers.
    test-changed:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest -q -n 2 --testmon
    
    # The test and CI gates never use affected-test selection.
    test:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest -q -n 2 --no-testmon
    
    # Check that test paths correspond to source modules.
    layout:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest-layout-enforcer check
    
    # Enforce module dependencies, reject unused declarations and forbid cycles.
    tach:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen tach check
    
    build:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv build --python .venv/bin/python --offline --no-build-isolation --all-packages
    
    check: lint typecheck tach layout test build

        def finished(self, chunk: str, expected: int) -> bool:
            row = self.db.execute(
                "SELECT records,server_failed FROM chunks WHERE chunk_key=?", [chunk]
            ).fetchone()
            return row is not None and row[0] == expected and row[1] == 0
    
        def begin(self, chunk: str) -> None:
            saved = self.db.execute(
                "SELECT artifact FROM chunks WHERE chunk_key=?", [chunk]
            ).fetchone()
            if saved is None:
                return
            rows = self.reader.execute(
                "SELECT article_id,inference_id,chunk_position,"
                "article_json,decision_reused "
                "FROM read_parquet(?)",
                [str(self.output / saved[0])],
            ).fetchall()
            self.db.executemany(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO articles VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                [(row[0], row[1], chunk, row[2], row[3], row[4]) for row in rows],
            )
            self.db.execute("DELETE FROM chunks WHERE chunk_key=?", [chunk])
            self.db.commit()
    
        def records(
            self, chunk: str | None = None
        ) -> Iterator[tuple[dict[str, JsonValue], dict[str, JsonValue], int, bool]]:
            query = "SELECT inference_id,article_json,position,reused FROM articles"
            parameters = []
            if chunk is not None:
                query += " WHERE chunk_key=?"
                parameters.append(chunk)
            query += " ORDER BY chunk_key,position"
            for inference_id, provenance, position, reused in self.db.execute(
                query, parameters
            ):
                decision = self.decision(inference_id, terminal=False)
                if decision is None:
                    raise ValueError("An article checkpoint is missing its request result")
                yield (
                    JSON_OBJECT_ADAPTER.validate_json(provenance),
                    decision,
                    position,
                    bool(reused),
                )
    
        def flush(self, chunk: str) -> None:
            if not self.production:
                return
            directory = self.output / "chunks"
            directory.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
            artifact = directory / f"{chunk}.parquet"
            staging = artifact.with_suffix(".jsonl.tmp")
            counts = {
                "records": 0,
                "succeeded": 0,
                "context_deferred": 0,
                "server_failed": 0,
                "reused": 0,
            }
            identities: set[str] = set()
            with staging.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                for article, decision, position, reused in self.records(chunk):
                    identities.add(str(article["inference_id"]))
                    counts["records"] += 1
                    counts[
                        "succeeded"
                        if decision["status"] == "complete"
                        else "context_deferred"
                        if decision["status"] == "too_long"
                        else "server_failed"
                    ] += 1
                    counts["reused"] += int(reused)
                    handle.write(
                        _json(
                            {
                                **{
                                    key: article[key]
                                    for key in (
                                        "article_id",
                                        "document_id",
                                        "inference_id",
                                        "source_path",
                                        "source_row",
                                    )
                                },
                                "chunk_position": position,
                                "status": decision["status"],
                                "decision_reused": reused,
                                "article_json": _json(article),
                                "decision_json": _json(decision),
                            }
                        )
                        + "\n"
                    )
            if not counts["records"]:
                staging.unlink()
                return
            self.reader.execute(
                "COPY (SELECT * REPLACE(cast(article_json AS JSON) AS article_json, "
                "cast(decision_json AS JSON) AS decision_json) "
                "FROM read_json_auto($json)) "
                "TO $output (FORMAT PARQUET, COMPRESSION ZSTD)",
                {"json": str(staging), "output": str(artifact.with_suffix(".parquet.tmp"))},
            )
            artifact.with_suffix(".parquet.tmp").replace(artifact)
            staging.unlink()
            relative = str(artifact.relative_to(self.output))
            for inference_id in identities:
                self.db.execute(
                    "UPDATE requests SET artifact=?,payload=NULL WHERE inference_id=? "
                    "AND (payload IS NOT NULL OR artifact=?)",
                    [relative, inference_id, relative],
                )
            self.db.execute(
                "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO chunks VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                [
                    chunk,
                    relative,
                    counts["records"],
                    counts["succeeded"],
                    counts["context_deferred"],
                    counts["server_failed"],
                    counts["reused"],
                    artifact.stat().st_size,
                ],
            )
            self.db.execute("DELETE FROM articles WHERE chunk_key=?", [chunk])
            self.db.commit()
    
        def counts(self) -> dict[str, int]:
            committed = self.db.execute(
                "SELECT coalesce(sum(records),0),coalesce(sum(succeeded),0),"
                "coalesce(sum(context_deferred),0),coalesce(sum(server_failed),0),"
                "coalesce(sum(reused),0),coalesce(sum(bytes),0) FROM chunks"
            ).fetchone()
            pending = self.db.execute(
                "SELECT count(*),coalesce(sum(r.status='complete'),0),"
                "coalesce(sum(r.status='too_long'),0),coalesce(sum(r.status='server_failed'),0),"
                "coalesce(sum(a.reused),0) FROM articles a "
                "JOIN requests r USING(inference_id)"
            ).fetchone()
            return {
                name: int(committed[index] + pending[index])
                for index, name in enumerate(
                    (
                        "attempted",
                        "completed",
                        "context_deferred",
                        "server_failed",
                        "reused_source_records",
                    )
                )
            } | {"decision_chunk_bytes": int(committed[5])}
    
    
    def _export(store: _Store, output: Path) -> None:
        jsonl = output / "decisions.jsonl.tmp"
        pairs_path = output / "company-decisions.jsonl.tmp"
        pair_count = 0
        with (
            jsonl.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as documents,
            pairs_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as pairs,
        ):
            for article, decision, _, reused in store.records():
                document = article | decision | {"decision_reused": reused}
                documents.write(_json(document) + "\n")
                candidates = {
                    str(candidate["issuer_id"]): candidate
                    for candidate in article.get("candidates", [])
                    if isinstance(candidate, dict)
                }
                for company in document.get("companies", []):
                    if not isinstance(company, dict):
                        raise ValueError("Company decisions must be mappings")
                    pair = {
                        **company,
                        "article_id": document["article_id"],
                        "document_id": document["document_id"],
                        "inference_id": document["inference_id"],
                        "article": {
                            key: value
                            for key, value in article.items()
                            if key != "candidates"
                        },
                        "candidate": candidates[str(company["issuer_id"])],
                        "request_sha256": decision.get("request_sha256"),
                        "model_name": decision.get("model_name"),
                    }
                    pairs.write(_json(pair) + "\n")
                    pair_count += 1
        jsonl.replace(output / "decisions.jsonl")
        if pair_count:
            with duckdb.connect() as con:
                con.execute(
                    "COPY (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto($json, "
                    "format='newline_delimited')) "
                    "TO $out (FORMAT PARQUET)",
                    {
                        "json": str(pairs_path),
                        "out": str(output / "predictions.parquet.tmp"),
                    },
                )
            (output / "predictions.parquet.tmp").replace(output / "predictions.parquet")
        pairs_path.unlink()
    
    
    def _failure(article: Article, error: Exception) -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
        status = (
            "too_long"
            if getattr(error, "status_code", None) == 422 and "token" in str(error).lower()
            else "server_failed"
        )
        return {
            "status": status,
            "error": str(error),
            "companies": [
                {
                    "issuer_id": candidate["issuer_id"],
                    "status": status if _descriptor(candidate) else "deferred_identity",
                    "identity_score": None,
                    "substantive_score": None,
                    "raw_primary_score": None,
                    "coverage_score": None,
                    "identity_tag": None,
                    "substantive_tag": None,
                    "primary_tag": None,
                    "coverage_tag": None,
                    "relevance_score": None,
                    "primary_score": None,
                    "consistency_flags": []
                    if _descriptor(candidate)
                    else ["unresolved_company_name"],
                    "validation_status": "pending_human",
                }
                for candidate in article.candidates
            ],
        }
    
    
    async def _check_server(config: ArticleLabelsConfig, output: Path) -> None:
        profile = JSON_OBJECT_ADAPTER.validate_json(config.runtime_manifest.read_bytes())
        for key, expected in (
            ("api_model", config.api_model),
            ("base_model", config.base_model),
            ("model", config.model),
            ("model_revision", config.model_revision),
            ("base_revision", config.base_revision),
            ("max_context_tokens", config.max_context_tokens),
        ):
            if key in profile and profile[key] != expected:
                raise ValueError(f"Configured {key} differs from the runtime profile")
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=config.request_timeout_seconds) as client:
            response = await client.get(f"{config.server_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/models")
            response.raise_for_status()
            reported = response.json()
        servers = [_ServerInfo.model_validate(row) for row in reported["models"]]
        server = next((row for row in servers if row.name == config.api_model), None)
        if server is None:
            raise ValueError("The server does not advertise the configured model alias")
        expected_fields: dict[str, JsonValue] = {
            "base": config.base_model,
            "max_state_tokens": config.max_context_tokens,
            "truncate_states": profile.get("truncate_states", False),
        }
        for key in ("device", "backend", "dtype", "lora"):
            if key in profile:
                expected_fields[key] = profile[key]
        observed = server.model_dump(mode="json")
        if any(observed[key] != value for key, value in expected_fields.items()):
            raise ValueError("Native server metadata differs from the runtime profile")
        temperature = profile.get("temperature")
        if (
            not isinstance(temperature, int | float)
            or abs(server.temperature - temperature) > 1e-9
        ):
            raise ValueError("Native server calibration differs from the runtime profile")
        _write_json(output / "server.json", reported)
    
    
    def _progress(store: _Store, requested: int, elapsed: float) -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
        counts = store.counts()
        return {
            **counts,
            "requested": requested,
            "succeeded": counts["completed"],
            "unattempted": max(0, requested - counts["attempted"]),
            "remaining": max(
                0, requested - counts["completed"] - counts["context_deferred"]
            ),
            "elapsed_seconds": elapsed,
            "source_record_chunks_committed": int(
                store.db.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM chunks").fetchone()[0]
            ),
            "source_files_total": store.source_files_total,
            "last_source": store.last_source,
        }
    
    
    def _storage_projection(store: _Store, population: int) -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
        counts = store.counts()
        page_size = int(store.db.execute("PRAGMA page_size").fetchone()[0])
        used_pages = int(store.db.execute("PRAGMA page_count").fetchone()[0]) - int(
            store.db.execute("PRAGMA freelist_count").fetchone()[0]
        )
        observed = counts["attempted"]
        measured_bytes = counts["decision_chunk_bytes"] + used_pages * page_size
        bytes_per_record = measured_bytes / observed if observed else None
        remaining = max(0, population - observed)
        return {
            "observed_source_records": observed,
            "compressed_chunk_bytes": counts["decision_chunk_bytes"],
            "active_sqlite_bytes": used_pages * page_size,
            "conditional_bytes_per_source_record": bytes_per_record,
            "conditional_remaining_bytes": remaining * bytes_per_record
            if bytes_per_record is not None
            else None,
            "filesystem_free_bytes": shutil.disk_usage(store.output).free,
            "basis": (
                "Current compressed chunks and active SQLite pages; "
                "conditional on comparable later records"
            ),
        }
    
    
    async def _run(
        input: Path, output: Path, params: Path, benchmark: bool, source: Path | None = None
    ) -> None:
        config = load_config(params)
        summary = json.loads((input / "summary.json").read_text())
        if summary.get("status") != "complete":
            raise ValueError("Inference requires a completed CPU index")
        output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        cpu_manifest = JSON_OBJECT_ADAPTER.validate_json(
            (input / "manifest.json").read_bytes()
        )
        source_root = _resolve_source(input, cpu_manifest, source)
        contract = {
            "config": config.model_dump(mode="json"),
            "runtime": json.loads(config.runtime_manifest.read_text()),
            "rubric": {
                "name": "independent-binary-v1",
                "company_questions": COMPANY_QUESTIONS,
                "article_kind": ARTICLE_CRITERIA,
                "coverage_score": "max(substantive_score, raw_primary_score)",
                "interpretation": (
                    "Independent model marginals, not calibrated joint probabilities. "
                    "Coverage is a ranking rule; "
                    "acceptance remains pending human validation."
                ),
            },
            "cpu": cpu_manifest,
            "scorer_sha256": hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
            "benchmark": benchmark,
            "storage": "benchmark-readable"
            if benchmark
            else "compressed-source-record-chunks",
        }
        operational = {
            "deadline_utc",
            "reserve_seconds",
            "concurrency",
            "request_timeout_seconds",
            "server_url",
            "runtime_manifest",
        }
        identity_contract = contract | {
            "config": config.model_dump(mode="json", exclude=operational)
        }
        fingerprint = hashlib.sha256(_json(identity_contract).encode()).hexdigest()
        manifest_path = output / "manifest.json"
        if (
            manifest_path.exists()
            and json.loads(manifest_path.read_text())["contract_sha256"] != fingerprint
        ):
            raise ValueError("Scoring inputs changed; use a new output directory")
        _write_json(manifest_path, {**contract, "contract_sha256": fingerprint})
        _write_json(
            output / "source.json",
            {
                "resolved_source": str(source_root),
                "source_override": str(source) if source is not None else None,
                "body_verification": "SHA256 checked against the immutable CPU index",
            },
        )
        await _check_server(config, output)
        model = SystemOneModel(
            config.api_model, provider=SystemOneProvider(base_url=config.server_url)

            ):
                scoring_started = time.monotonic()
                preparation_seconds = prior_preparation + scoring_started - started
                store.db.execute("UPDATE clock SET preparation=?", [preparation_seconds])
                store.db.commit()
                reader = _BodyReader(source_root, con)
                semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(config.concurrency)
                if datetime.now(UTC).timestamp() >= deadline:
                    deadline_reached = True
                    chunks = iter(())
    
                async def score_one(
                    article: Article, text: str
                ) -> tuple[Article, dict[str, JsonValue] | None]:
                    async with semaphore:
                        if datetime.now(UTC).timestamp() >= deadline:
                            return article, None
                        try:
                            return article, await _score(article, text, config, model)
                        except Exception as error:
                            return article, _failure(article, error)
    
                for chunk_number, articles in enumerate(chunks):
                    key = f"{chunk_number:08d}"
                    if store.production and store.finished(key, len(articles)):
                        continue
                    if datetime.now(UTC).timestamp() >= deadline:
                        deadline_reached = True
                        break
                    store.begin(key)
                    for offset in range(0, len(articles), 32):
                        pending = []
                        for position, article in enumerate(
                            articles[offset : offset + 32], start=offset
                        ):
                            saved = store.db.execute(
                                "SELECT r.status FROM articles a "
                                "JOIN requests r USING(inference_id) "
                                "WHERE a.article_id=?",
                                [article.article_id],
                            ).fetchone()
                            if saved is None or saved[0] not in ("complete", "too_long"):
                                pending.append((position, article))
                        bodies = reader.read([article for _, article in pending])
                        groups: dict[str, list[tuple[int, Article]]] = {}
                        for position, article in pending:
                            groups.setdefault(article.inference_id, []).append(
                                (position, article)
                            )
                        tasks = []
                        for inference_id, members in groups.items():
                            cached = store.decision(inference_id)
                            if cached is not None:
                                for position, article in members:
                                    store.save_article(
                                        article,
                                        bodies[article.article_id],
                                        key,
                                        position,
                                        reused=True,
                                    )
                            else:
                                article = members[0][1]
                                tasks.append(
                                    score_one(article, bodies[article.article_id].text)
                                )
                        for task in asyncio.as_completed(tasks):
                            representative, decision = await task
                            if decision is None:
                                deadline_reached = True
                                continue
                            store.save_decision(representative.inference_id, decision)
                            for member_number, (position, article) in enumerate(
                                groups[representative.inference_id]
                            ):
                                store.save_article(
                                    article,
                                    bodies[article.article_id],
                                    key,
                                    position,
                                    reused=member_number > 0,
                                )
                        elapsed = prior_seconds + time.monotonic() - scoring_started
                        store.db.execute("UPDATE clock SET seconds=?", [elapsed])
                        store.db.commit()
                        _write_json(
                            output / "progress.json", _progress(store, requested, elapsed)
                        )
                        if deadline_reached:
                            break
                    store.flush(key)
                    if store.production:
                        storage = _storage_projection(store, requested)
                        _write_json(output / "storage.json", storage)
                        required = storage["conditional_remaining_bytes"]
                        available = storage["filesystem_free_bytes"]
                        if (
                            isinstance(required, int | float)
                            and isinstance(available, int)
                            and required > available
                        ):
                            stopped_for_storage = True
                            break
                    if deadline_reached:
                        break
                elapsed = prior_seconds + time.monotonic() - scoring_started
                store.db.execute("UPDATE clock SET seconds=?", [elapsed])
                store.db.commit()
                counts = store.counts()
                completed = counts["completed"]
                attempted = counts["attempted"]
                finished = attempted == requested and counts["server_failed"] == 0
                report = {
                    **_progress(store, requested, elapsed),
                    "status": (
                        "complete"
                        if completed == requested
                        else "complete_with_unscorable"
                        if finished
                        else "storage_limited"
                        if stopped_for_storage
                        else "deadline_reached"
                        if deadline_reached
                        else "incomplete"
                    ),
                    "failed": attempted - completed,
                    "elapsed_seconds": elapsed + preparation_seconds,
                    "frame_preparation_seconds": preparation_seconds,
                    "throughput_completed": completed,
                    "throughput_elapsed_seconds": elapsed,
                    "articles_per_second": completed / elapsed if elapsed else 0,
                    "frame_documents": frame_count,
                    "frame_records": frame_count,
                    "frame_unit": "retained_source_records",
                    "selection": (
                        "deterministic SHA256 priority sample of retained source rows"
                        if benchmark
                        else "all retained source rows in source order"
                    ),
                    "seed": config.seed,
                    "row_groups_read": reader.groups_read,
                    "contract_sha256": fingerprint,
                    "decision_attempts": int(
                        store.db.execute("SELECT attempts FROM clock").fetchone()[0]
                    ),
                    "unique_scored_inference_units": int(
                        store.db.execute(
                            "SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE status='complete'"
                        ).fetchone()[0]
                    ),
                    "estimated_full_seconds": preparation_seconds
                    + frame_count * elapsed / completed
                    if completed
                    else None,
                    "completion_requires_context_policy": counts["context_deferred"] > 0,
                }
                _write_json(
                    output / ("benchmark.json" if benchmark else "summary.json"), report
                )
                _write_json(output / "progress.json", report)
                if benchmark:
                    _export(store, output)
                if not finished:
                    raise RuntimeError(
                        f"Scoring {report['status']}: {completed}/{requested} "
                        "source records "
                        "scored; checkpoints preserved"
                    )
        finally:
            store.close()

    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    set positional-arguments
    
    mod python 'src/python/justfile'
    mod latex 'src/latex/justfile'
    mod agents '.agents/justfile'
    mod inference 'infra/inference/justfile'
    workflow := "env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py"
    
    # Discover this project's commands.
    default:
        @just --list
    
    # Prepare locked dependencies and Git hooks (uses the network).
    setup:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py prepare
        just python::setup
        just latex::setup
        just agents::apply
        prek install
    
    # Check source, views and selected languages without repairing files.
    check:
        bash infra/nix/check.sh
        {{ workflow }} check
        just python::check
        just latex::check
        just data-check
        just semflow-check
        just changelog-check
        just skills-check
        just agents::check
    
    # Run the selected language tests.
    test:
        just python::test
        just latex::test
    
    # Explicitly format sources.
    fmt:
        git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard | while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do case "$file" in justfile|*/justfile|Justfile|*/Justfile|*.just) just --justfile "$file" --fmt --unstable ;; esac; done
        nixfmt devenv.nix infra/nix/devenv.nix infra/nix/pkgs/schematter.nix infra/nix/pkgs/agentsync.nix
        rumdl fmt .
        # DVC's YAML emitter can leave trailing spaces when wrapping scalar values.
        if [[ -f dvc.lock ]]; then sed -i 's/[[:blank:]]*$//' dvc.lock; fi
        just python::fmt
        just latex::fmt
    
    # Check external links online.
    links:
        git ls-files -z '*.md' | xargs -0 -r lychee --config lychee.toml --no-progress
    
    # Run root-level DVC using the locked Python environment.
    dvc *args:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen dvc "$@"
    
    # Validate DVC metadata without fetching data.
    data-check:
        just dvc status
        just dvc dag
    
    # Refresh generated planning and reference views.
    sync:
        {{ workflow }} sync
    
    # Validate document schemas, links and generated views.
    context-check:
        {{ workflow }} check
    
    # Create a plan without overwriting existing content.
    plan-new slug title:
        {{ workflow }} plan-new "$1" --title "$2"
    
    # Create a task inside an existing plan or task.
    task-new parent slug title:
        {{ workflow }} task-new "$1" "$2" --title "$3"
    
    # Create a local reference record with its directory as citation key.
    reference-new key title:
        {{ workflow }} reference-new "$1" --title "$2"
    
    # Validate the repository changelog structure and change categories.
    changelog-check:
        schematter validate --schema infra/schemas/documents/changelog.document-schema.yaml CHANGELOG.md

    # Accepted pilot source review
    
    All 24 accepted namespace pairs in 21 original articles identify the displayed company and contain developed company-specific information. Each company is defensibly one of the article's main subjects, including the two companies in the rail roundup. No accepted pair appears to be a generic-word collision, footer-only mention or attribution-only link in this qualitative review.
    
    This is an AI-assisted **post-selection** check: acceptance was known, model score values were not loaded, and the original text checksums were verified for all 21 articles. These observations are not human gold, a population precision estimate, a 95% precision finding or a recall assessment. The 24 namespace pairs represent 22 distinct article/CIK combinations; Micron and Tractor Supply each appear in both Top1000 and GH namespaces.
    
    Company relevance does not establish suitability for the default editorial dataset:
    
    - **19 articles / 20 pairs** contain identifiable editorial reporting or investment analysis, often syndicated. Twelve of those articles also contain publisher or subscription promotions; the company evidence is developed in the article body.
    - **One article / two pairs** is an explicit Tractor Supply issuer press release syndicated from Business Wire. Its notes offering is primary company coverage, but it belongs in the separate release view under the current intended policy.
    - **One article / two pairs** is a developed Zacks rail roundup with “For Immediate Release,” media-contact and marketing material. The company roles are clear; its editorial-versus-promotional format needs policy review. No exclusion was applied.
    
    The examples expose source-quality limits: Micron is a summary/truncated excerpt; several analyses reference missing figures or tables; Delta contains internally inconsistent revenue/cash-burn wording, and FirstCash appears to omit revenue scale units. The Tesla item's relative weekday wording needs date review. Chipotle and Oracle publication dates precede their crawl partitions, so partition dates must not substitute for publication dates. These are observations about the retained text, not externally verified factual corrections.
    
    Only 15 of the 24 accepted links carry the verified-title-and-body discovery tier. The other nine include developed Nektar, BILL, Delta, Walmart, Chipotle, Micron and United Bankshares coverage, plus the GH Tractor Supply link. This selected subset cannot estimate a stricter filter's population recall, but it shows why stored lexical tiers must not be treated as relevance truth.
    
    The accepted links look sensible for a provisional company-relevance filter. A full run should preserve the separate source-format and quality fields and keep human validation pending. This review did not change any scoring threshold, exclusion rule, source record or sealed audit label.
    
    Evidence: [verified source records](source-records.json), [all pair observations](observations.csv), [rubric and structured observations](observations.json), [counts and limitations](summary.json), and [extraction provenance](manifest.json).

    class _Store:
        """Keep request identities in SQLite and bounded production payloads in Parquet."""
    
        def __init__(self, output: Path, *, production: bool) -> None:
            self.output = output
            self.production = production
            self.source_files_total = 0
            progress = output / "progress.json"
            self.last_source: JsonValue = (
                json.loads(progress.read_text()).get("last_source")
                if progress.exists()
                else None
            )
            self.db = sqlite3.connect(output / "checkpoints.sqlite")
            self.reader = duckdb.connect(config={"memory_limit": "512MB", "threads": 1})
            self.db.executescript(
                "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS requests(inference_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, "
                "status TEXT NOT NULL,artifact TEXT,payload TEXT);"
                "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS articles(article_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, "
                "inference_id TEXT NOT NULL,chunk_key TEXT NOT NULL,position INTEGER, "
                "article_json TEXT NOT NULL,reused INTEGER NOT NULL);"
                "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS chunks(chunk_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, "
                "artifact TEXT NOT NULL,records INTEGER,succeeded INTEGER, "
                "context_deferred INTEGER,server_failed INTEGER,"
                "reused INTEGER,bytes INTEGER);"
                "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clock(seconds REAL,"
                "preparation REAL,attempts INTEGER);"
                "INSERT INTO clock SELECT 0,0,0 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM clock);"
                "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS failures(attempt INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, "
                "inference_id TEXT,status TEXT,error TEXT,recorded_at TEXT);"
            )
    
        def close(self) -> None:
            self.reader.close()
            self.db.close()
    
        def decision(
            self, inference_id: str, *, terminal: bool = True
        ) -> dict[str, JsonValue] | None:
            row = self.db.execute(
                "SELECT status,artifact,payload FROM requests WHERE inference_id=?",
                [inference_id],
            ).fetchone()
            if row is None or (terminal and row[0] not in ("complete", "too_long")):
                return None
            if row[2] is not None:
                return JSON_OBJECT_ADAPTER.validate_json(row[2])
            result = self.reader.execute(
                "SELECT decision_json FROM read_parquet(?) WHERE inference_id=? LIMIT 1",
                [str(self.output / row[1]), inference_id],
            ).fetchone()
            if result is None:
                raise ValueError("A committed request is missing from its decision chunk")
            return JSON_OBJECT_ADAPTER.validate_json(result[0])
    
        def save_decision(self, inference_id: str, decision: dict[str, JsonValue]) -> None:
            self.db.execute(
                "INSERT INTO requests VALUES (?,?,NULL,?) ON CONFLICT(inference_id) "
                "DO UPDATE SET status=excluded.status,artifact=NULL,"
                "payload=excluded.payload",
                [inference_id, decision["status"], _json(decision)],
            )
            self.db.execute("UPDATE clock SET attempts=attempts+1")
            if decision["status"] != "complete":
                self.db.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO failures SELECT attempts,?,?,?,? FROM clock",
                    [
                        inference_id,
                        decision["status"],
                        str(decision.get("error")),
                        datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
                    ],
                )
    
        def save_article(
            self, article: Article, body: _Body, chunk: str, position: int, *, reused: bool
        ) -> None:
            provenance = article.model_dump(mode="json") | {"metadata": body.metadata}
            self.last_source = {
                "path": article.source_path,
                "row": article.source_row,
                "article_id": article.article_id,
            }
            self.db.execute(
                "INSERT INTO articles VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?) ON CONFLICT(article_id) "
                "DO UPDATE SET inference_id=excluded.inference_id,"
                "chunk_key=excluded.chunk_key,"
                "position=excluded.position,article_json=excluded.article_json,reused=excluded.reused",
                [
                    article.article_id,
                    article.inference_id,
                    chunk,
                    position,
                    _json(provenance),
                    reused,
                ],
            )
    
        def finished(self, chunk: str, expected: int) -> bool:
            row = self.db.execute(
                "SELECT records,server_failed FROM chunks WHERE chunk_key=?", [chunk]
            ).fetchone()
            return row is not None and row[0] == expected and row[1] == 0
    
        def begin(self, chunk: str) -> None:
            saved = self.db.execute(
                "SELECT artifact FROM chunks WHERE chunk_key=?", [chunk]
            ).fetchone()
            if saved is None:
                return
            rows = self.reader.execute(
                "SELECT article_id,inference_id,chunk_position,"
                "article_json,decision_reused "
                "FROM read_parquet(?)",
                [str(self.output / saved[0])],
            ).fetchall()
            self.db.executemany(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO articles VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                [(row[0], row[1], chunk, row[2], row[3], row[4]) for row in rows],
            )
            self.db.execute("DELETE FROM chunks WHERE chunk_key=?", [chunk])
            self.db.commit()
    
        def records(
            self, chunk: str | None = None
        ) -> Iterator[tuple[dict[str, JsonValue], dict[str, JsonValue], int, bool]]:
            query = "SELECT inference_id,article_json,position,reused FROM articles"

    from pydantic_ai.providers.system_one import SystemOneProvider
    
    
    @pytest.mark.component
    def test_companies_share_one_native_request_with_structured_questions() -> None:
        # Arrange: capture the actual provider transport without starting a model.
        bodies: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    
        def respond(request: httpx2.Request) -> httpx2.Response:
            body = json.loads(request.content)
            bodies.append(body)
            answers: dict[str, object] = {}
            for name, question in body["questions"].items():
                if question["type"] == "noul":
                    answers[name] = {"type": "noul", "noul": 0.99}
                else:
                    options = list(question["criteria"])
                    answers[name] = {
                        "type": "choice",
                        "choice": options[0],
                        "confidence": 1.0,
                        "probabilities": {
                            key: float(index == 0) for index, key in enumerate(options)
                        },
                    }
            return httpx2.Response(
                200,
                json={
                    "model": "kev-latest",
                    "answers": answers,
                    "usage": {"input_tokens": 123, "output_tokens": 0},
                },
            )
    
        client = httpx2.AsyncClient(transport=httpx2.MockTransport(respond))
        model = SystemOneModel(
            "kev-latest",
            provider=SystemOneProvider(
                base_url="http://test.invalid",
                http_client=client,
            ),
        )
        candidates: list[dict[str, JsonValue]] = [
            {"issuer_id": "a", "name": "Alpha Inc."},
            {"issuer_id": "b", "name": "Beta Inc.", "tickers": ["BETA"]},
            {"issuer_id": "c", "name": None, "original_name": "Wrong Company"},
            {"issuer_id": "other-namespace:a", "name": "Alpha Inc."},
        ]
    
        # Act: ask the three binary questions through the real provider adapter.
        response = asyncio.run(
            model.decide(
                DecisionRequest(
                    state={"article": "Alpha acquired Beta."},
                    questions=build_questions(candidates),
                ),
                model_settings={},
            )
        )
    
        # Assert: one request keeps seven typed questions and defers unresolved identity.
        assert len(bodies) == 1
        assert len(response.answers) == 7
        sent = bodies[0]["questions"]
        assert isinstance(sent, dict)
        assert sent["c1.identity"]["instructions"] == (
            "Does this article mention the company Beta Inc. (BETA)?"
        )
        assert sent["c0.substantive"]["type"] == "noul"
        assert sent["c0.primary"]["instructions"] == (
            "Is Alpha Inc. one of the main subjects of this article?"
        )
        assert all(not key.startswith("c2.") for key in sent)
        assert all(not key.startswith("c3.") for key in sent)
        interpreted = interpret_answers(candidates, response.answers, 0.95)
        deferred = interpreted[2]
        assert deferred["status"] == "deferred_identity"
        assert deferred["identity_score"] is None
        assert interpreted[3] == interpreted[0] | {"issuer_id": "other-namespace:a"}
    
    
    @pytest.mark.unit

    name: architecture-layout
    description: Use when evaluating or designing where CCFinance code, data stages, tests, documents or infrastructure belong, including module boundaries and repository restructures.
    ---
    
    # Architecture layout
    
    ## Workflow
    
    1. Establish the requested scope and outcome: evaluate the current layout,
       design a layout, or implement an authorized change. Read nearby README and
       ARCHITECTURE files. Identify existing owners and consumers before proposing
       a new abstraction; reuse an existing module or library when it satisfies the
       contract. File size alone is not a reason to split or create a package.
    2. Examine the relevant boundaries using evidence:
       - **Ownership and cohesion:** Can a contributor find the owner, and do things
         that change together live together? Keep each unit's responsibility clear.
       - **Dependencies and encapsulation:** Trace relevant imports and public
         interfaces. Keep intended dependency direction clear and cycles forbidden;
         avoid reaching into another module's internals without a reason.
       - **Coupling:** Identify changes that force unrelated owners to change.
         Share a contract only when consumers actually need the same behavior; a
         little local duplication may be preferable to coupling distinct contracts.
       - **Discoverability:** Make CLI commands, transformations, schemas, tests,
         fixtures and documents easy to find from their owning area.
    3. Choose the smallest useful boundary: a function, module, package or separate
       workspace project. A package or project should reflect an actual dependency,
       distribution, build or ownership need. Organize by layer, capability or a
       combination according to the work; do not impose a universal directory tree.
    4. For pipeline work, preserve the established `raw`, `processed` and `research`
       stage ownership. Organize capabilities within those layers as they arise.
       Distinguish Python imports from DVC artifact dependencies: the latter connect
       producers and consumers without requiring cross-layer Python imports. Apply
       Tach rules to durable module boundaries and DVC to artifact dependencies.
    5. For a move or split, trace the affected consumers before changing paths:
       imports and public APIs, CLI registration, package configuration, tests and
       fixtures, Tach, DVC and Semflow dependencies, and documentation links as
       applicable. Preserve behavior and scientific contracts unless the user asks
       for a change; report any intended behavior change separately. Do not treat
       missing static references as proof that dynamic or external consumers do not
       exist.
    6. Use the repository's existing gates rather than adding tests that merely
       assert a directory tree or private call sequence. For tests and fixtures,
       follow [Python testing](../python-testing/SKILL.md). Run focused checks while
       working and `just check` before handoff; report checks that could not run.
    
    ## Results
    
    For an evaluation, report concrete findings with locations, effects and ranked
    recommendations. For a design, show the proposed ownership and dependency
    boundaries, explain meaningful tradeoffs and how they are enforced. For an
    implementation, summarize what moved, whether behavior changed and the evidence
    from verification. Keep the review proportional to the requested change.
    
    For example, if both article cleaning and company linking need the same
    publication-date parser, first inspect its existing owner and date semantics.
    Share it only if both consumers require the same contract; keep separate rules
    when their treatment of missing or ambiguous dates differs.

    name: python-testing
    description: Use when writing, changing, reviewing or organizing Python tests, pytest fixtures or Hypothesis strategies in CCFinance.
    ---
    
    # Python testing
    
    ## Workflow
    
    1. Inspect the code contract, nearby tests, `conftest.py`, shared fixtures and
       strategies, the package's test README, and pytest configuration. Reuse an
       existing test or generator when it covers the behavior; extend it only for a
       distinct, meaningful risk. Do not add tests for trivial or reversible changes
       just to increase counts, or tests that restate implementation details.
    2. Prefer Hypothesis for input variation when a general property is meaningful.
       Prefer a small explicit example for a single known boundary, regression or
       command smoke check. Decide the expected outcome independently of the code
       under test. Use tiny representative data, bounded generators and the smallest
       appropriate test boundary. Assert public behavior, including error contracts.
    3. Place a test beside its source owner under the mirrored `tests/` layout. Reuse
       existing factories and strategies first. Keep a helper local until several
       tests need it; put cross-module strategies in `tests/_strategies.py` and
       shared pytest fixtures in the nearest common `conftest.py`. Place a fixture
       at broader scope only when its state is safe to share. Measure costly setup
       before broadening scope; avoid creating generic fixture frameworks.
    4. Arrange inputs and prerequisites, act on the behavior, and assert observable
       results (AAA). Cleanup belongs in a fixture finalizer or context manager.
       Label each phase with an `# Arrange`, `# Act` or `# Assert` comment, as in
       the example below. Favor DAMP: clear names and visible expected values can
       justify a little repetition.
    5. Give each new or modified test exactly one scope marker from the table below;
       add `slow` or `external` only when applicable. Mark a class or module only
       when every inherited test has the same scope. Never stack or override scope
       markers, including inherited marks. Before using markers, register the six
       names in the owning pytest configuration; unknown names fail under
       `--strict-markers`. This skill defines the policy; it does not mean the
       current unmarked suite already enforces it. Migrate existing tests deliberately
       if adding a collection-time enforcement hook.
    6. During development, run the smallest relevant test or selection and check
       its output. Before handoff run the repository's required full checks, including
       the complete non-Testmon suite. Run any affected slow or external tests when
       their prerequisites and authorization are available; report what was not run
       and why. A targeted pass is not evidence that the full suite passed.
    
    ## Markers
    
    Use only these six custom markers. Built-in pytest mechanisms such as
    `parametrize`, `skipif` and `xfail` remain available for their intended purposes.
    Scope describes the boundary the assertions exercise, not the number of files,
    the use of Hypothesis, or the choice of a reference oracle.
    
    | Marker | Rule |
    | --- | --- |
    | `unit` | Exactly one scope: an isolated operation or small self-contained behavior. |
    | `component` | Exactly one scope: one coherent subsystem or component through its public behavior. |
    | `integration` | Exactly one scope: interactions across components or a real dependency boundary. |
    | `e2e` | Exactly one scope: a complete user-visible workflow through the public CLI or API. A CLI help check alone is not end-to-end. |
    | `slow` | Optional execution label: the complete test, including setup, teardown and generated examples, consistently exceeds two seconds on the normal local environment. Confirm with repeated pytest duration reports; a single noisy measurement is not enough. |
    | `external` | Optional execution label: the test accesses a live network service or external account. Use even if it is usually fast; require explicit opt-in and appropriate credentials. A local temporary file, subprocess or fake alone does not qualify. |
    
    `slow` and `external` are independent and may accompany any one scope. Do not
    invent custom markers for regression, reference, property, smoke, tools or
    implementation techniques; communicate those in descriptive test names and
    assertions. Run fast local iteration with `-m "not slow and not external"`
    after the markers are registered. Full checks must not silently omit slow tests;
    external tests need a separate explicit lane and must not mutate live services
    without authorization.
    
    ## Hypothesis examples and fixtures
    
    Hypothesis strategies generate values; pytest fixtures manage resources. If
    Hypothesis is absent, add it to the locked workspace development dependencies
    when introducing the first test that uses it. Search
    for reusable strategies or an appropriate first-party Hypothesis extra before
    adding one. Compose built-in strategies, use `@composite` for dependent values,
    and generate valid inputs directly rather than filtering most examples. Keep
    sizes bounded and counterexamples understandable. Preserve an important known
    failure using `@example` or an explicit regression; do not duplicate a property
    with a long list of examples that establish the same behavior.
    
    A function-scoped pytest fixture runs once per test function, not once per
    `@given` example. For per-example mutable resources, create and clean them inside
    the test, for example with `TemporaryDirectory()`. Reuse immutable shared data
    only when safe. Do not suppress health checks or disable deadlines globally to
    make a test pass; investigate the cause and document a narrowly justified
    exception. Choose explicit settings or a shared profile only when warranted by
    measured cost. Preserve failing examples and replay information as appropriate.
    
    This self-contained example illustrates a small property, AAA and the scope
    marker; it uses the standard-library URL parser rather than a CCFinance stage:
    
    ```python
    from string import ascii_lowercase, digits
    from urllib.parse import urlsplit
    
    import pytest
    from hypothesis import example, given, strategies as st
    
    
    @pytest.mark.unit
    @example(host="news")
    @given(host=st.text(alphabet=ascii_lowercase + digits, min_size=1, max_size=20))
    def test_url_hostname_normalizes_ascii_case(host: str) -> None:
        # Arrange: build a URL with an uppercase hostname.
        url = f"https://{host.upper()}.example/article"
    
        # Act: extract the hostname.
        hostname = urlsplit(url).hostname
    
        # Assert: the hostname is lowercase.
        assert hostname == f"{host}.example"
    ```
    
    Use a real local Parquet or filesystem boundary for a small integration test
    when that interaction matters; use a stub or fake for costly or nondeterministic
    remote services. A fake cannot establish that the real service works. Keep
    randomized tests independent of execution order; for numerical or sampling
    claims define tolerances and uncertainty rather than requiring arbitrary
    bit-for-bit agreement across environments.
    
    Consult the Hypothesis [tutorial](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorial/),
    [how-to guides](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how-to/),
    [strategies and API reference](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/)
    and [extras](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/extras.html) when
    choosing or debugging a strategy.
