    # CCFinance
    
    CCFinance is a data engineering project for filtering and enriching public
    Common Crawl News (CC-News) copies for research into language in finance.
    
    ## Start
    
    Exordio supplies the Python and LaTeX toolchains, a pinned Nix environment and CI.
    Copier answers record Exordio `v0.1.1-alpha` (the documented `v0.1.0` tag was not
    available in the local source).
    
    ```bash
    bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh
    devenv shell
    just setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run stages list
    just check
    ```
    
    Shared agent instructions and Codex configuration are maintained in
    [`.agents/`](.agents/README.md). `just setup` applies them; use
    `just agents::preview` to preview link changes and `just agents::check` to
    verify the generated links.
    
    `just check` validates Justfile syntax and formatting alongside the other
    quality gates. Run `just fmt` to format Justfiles and other source files.
    
    For Python alone, with Python 3.13, uv and just installed:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::check
    ```
    
    ## Data and reproducibility
    
    DVC is initialized at the repository root with analytics disabled. Use:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc status
    just dvc dag
    ```
    
    Semflow tracks the executable Python dependencies of DVC stages. When adding a
    stage, run `just semflow-patch` to review its proposed fingerprints, then
    `just semflow-apply` to materialize them. Commit the generated
    `.semflow/hashes/` files with the DVC definition. After semantic source changes,
    run `just semflow-refresh`; `just semflow-check` detects stale fingerprints.
    The frozen [Fine News acquisition stage](data/inputs/fine-news/README.md) retains
    the published staging snapshot and its historical selection recipe. DVC verifies
    the restored output during reproduction. The
    [source comparison](data/inputs/source-comparison/README.md) prepares small
    probability samples using Parquet metadata before acquiring article payloads.
    Keep data, configuration and environment dependencies explicit in DVC: Semflow's
    static analysis cannot discover string-driven dynamic imports.
    
    See [Python commands](src/python/README.md), [LaTeX commands](src/latex/README.md)
    and [infrastructure](infra/README.md). The scaffold's Apache-2.0 license covers
    code; it does not grant rights to upstream article content.
    # Article labels and research filters
    
    This experiment separates company retrieval, dated issuer identity and model
    judgments about article coverage. Its source is the restored
    [Fine News snapshot](../fine-news/README.md). The historical 115-domain allowlist
    is an acquisition policy; it has not been reviewed as a trusted-publisher list.
    All model labels remain provisional pending human evaluation.
    
    ## Source and CPU evidence
    
    The adopted Rust Aho–Corasick run covers the same 168 source files. Source and
    prediction checksums are verified before adoption. The compact CPU index retains
    12,241,870 of 14,807,287 source records and accounts separately for every exclusion.
    Article keys use relative source paths and physical row numbers. Native article
    IDs are preserved but are not assumed unique.
    
    Text remains in the raw snapshot. Indexes store coordinates, text hashes,
    candidates and matching evidence. Exact-text groups retain every source membership;
    they do not establish complete syndicated-story deduplication. A literal name or
    publisher keyword match establishes a retrieval candidate, not company relevance.
    
    The independent [CPU audit](../../research/experiments/article-labels/cpu-audit/report.md)
    confirmed correct stored offsets but found generic aliases, footer mentions,
    non-financial publisher tags and a cross-year issuer-name defect. The review is
    qualitative AI evidence, not human gold or measured population precision/recall.
    Its retained and no-hit source samples, observations and checksums are preserved.
    
    ## Dated candidate correction
    
    `correct_article_candidates` preserves every broad candidate and source record.
    It uses a unique verified article-year issuer link to resolve Top1000 names,
    tickers and CIKs together. Ambiguous or unsupported links remain unresolved;
    scoring never substitutes the original, potentially wrong company name.
    
    The corrected index records original values, authority identifiers, supported
    aliases, lexical ambiguity and evidence tiers. The SEC snapshot contains 190
    cached submissions records. Current registry names are not certified historical
    names, and SEC former-name filing dates are not guaranteed validity intervals.
    Undated GH identities retain their limitation. Publisher tags and legacy ticker
    spans remain unverified retrieval evidence.
    
    Title/body evidence tiers are retrieval diagnostics. They do not classify primary
    coverage or remove candidates from the scoring population. Capped stored spans
    remain censored evidence rather than proof that other mentions are absent.
    
    ## Fixed pilot
    
    The pilot selects 1,000 retained source records by the smallest
    `SHA256(seed:article_id)` values before loading bodies or requesting predictions.
    Duplicate source copies remain in this sampling frame. `selection.parquet`
    preserves the sample; it cannot establish missed-company recall from survivors.
    
    The frozen initial pilot lives in
    `data/processed/experiments/article-labels/benchmark-1000/`. It scored 993 records,
    deferred seven beyond 8,192 tokens and had no server failures. Its original rubric
    accepted no pairs at 0.95. Exact scorer, reporter, parameters and runtime assets
    are archived alongside DVC pointers; frozen stages preserve that baseline.
    
    Verify the completed corrected pilot and its report with:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc repro benchmark_company_labels
    just dvc repro report_company_benchmark
    ```
    
    Outputs use `benchmark-corrected-1000/` beneath the processed and research
    experiment directories. `benchmark.json` records counts and measured throughput;
    `decisions.jsonl` and `predictions.parquet` preserve the small pilot's predictions.
    Fresh source-only audit labels are sealed before model outputs are inspected.
    Neither synthetic examples nor AI agreement establish human-validated accuracy.
    Both completed pilots are frozen. A new experiment requires its own output path
    and an unfrozen stage, preserving the existing manifests and implementation hashes.
    
    The corrected pilot scored 993 records and deferred seven by context length.
    One transient timeout succeeded on resume. At the fixed cutoff, 24 candidate
    pairs across 21 records were provisionally accepted; 105 pairs had unresolved
    identities. The cumulative clock includes an unusual stall and sparse source
    reads. Its conditional linear runtime projection is not a reliable dense-corpus
    completion date. `row_groups_read` and `last_source` describe the latest
    invocation; completion counts and elapsed time accumulate across resumes.
    
    ## Company decisions
    
    The selected rubric asks three binary questions per resolved company, using its
    canonical name and tickers: whether the article mentions it, provides meaningful
    company-specific information beyond a mention, and treats it as a main subject.
    Several companies may be primary. The manifest records the exact question
    templates and article-kind criteria. The current runtime is Kev-4B in BF16.
    Production uses the separate `kev-4b-low-memory.json` profile. It retains the
    same model and 8,192-token admission while reducing GPU graph buffers. A fixed
    16-request parity check preserved all tested 0.5 and 0.95 threshold decisions;
    the original corrected pilot retains its original runtime profile.
    
    `identity_score`, `substantive_score` and `raw_primary_score` preserve independent
    model outputs. `coverage_score` is their substantive/primary maximum: a ranking
    rule rather than a calibrated union probability. Contradictory marginals retain
    consistency flags. `primary_score` is available only after identity meets the
    configured cutoff. A provisional accepted pair requires confident identity and
    coverage without a strong coverage contradiction. Article kind does not gate it.
    Saved outputs support later threshold comparisons without rerunning inference.
    
    ## Native inference and checkpoints
    
    [Native Kev](../../../infra/inference/README.md) runs in a separate pinned GPU
    runtime. Pydantic's System One client shares each article across company questions
    in one request. Exact repeated company descriptors share questions while retaining
    all namespace-specific links. Large candidate sets use bounded requests.
    Article kind is an annotation, rather than an automatic editorial-content gate.
    
    The runtime profile records model revisions, checkpoint hashes, precision,
    kernels and context admission. Oversized documents are explicitly deferred;
    silent text truncation is disabled. Prediction manifests preserve the scorer and
    runtime contract. A changed scientific contract requires a new output directory.
    Operational deadlines, transport timeouts and concurrency can change on resume.
    Pass `--source data/raw/fine-news` to override archived absolute source locations.
    
    ```bash
    just dvc repro score_company_labels
    ```
    
    Production stores compressed source-record Parquet chunks and a small SQLite
    resume ledger in `data/processed/experiments/article-labels/corpus/`. It preserves
    source metadata, candidate provenance and raw model outputs. Successful identical
    requests can be reused; transient server failures are retried on resume. Context
    failures, unresolved identities and pending records stay separate from negatives.
    `progress.json` reports counts and `storage.json` gives a conditional disk estimate.
    
    An incomplete, storage-limited or deadline-limited run exits unsuccessfully after
    saving checkpoints. DVC therefore does not proceed automatically to its report.
    To inspect a partial run, invoke the reporting command directly:
    
    ```bash
    env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV \
      uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline \
      pipeline stages research report-article-labels \
      --cpu data/processed/experiments/article-labels/cpu \
      --census data/research/experiments/article-labels/cpu \
      --scores data/processed/experiments/article-labels/corpus \
      --output data/research/experiments/article-labels/corpus
    ```
    
    Reports distinguish source records, candidate pairs, scored coverage and pending
    work. They provide CSV and LaTeX tables without projecting accepted model labels
    as validated population coverage. The 0.95 cutoff is a provisional selection rule,
    not an empirical accuracy guarantee. Parameters and the operating deadline live
    under `experiments.article_labels` in `params.yaml`; measured end-to-end capacity
    must support any claim that full scoring will finish before that deadline.

    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    set positional-arguments
    
    default:
        @just --list
    
    # Install exactly the committed workspace and build dependencies.
    setup:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv sync --locked --all-packages
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline python -c 'import duckdb; duckdb.connect().execute("INSTALL httpfs")'
    
    run *args:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline pipeline "$@"
    
    lint:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff check .
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff format --check .
    
    typecheck:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pyrefly check
    
    # Local impacted-test selection, with a bounded number of workers.
    test-changed:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest -q -n 2 --testmon
    
    # The test and CI gates never use affected-test selection.
    test:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest -q -n 2 --no-testmon
    
    # Check that test paths correspond to source modules.
    layout:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest-layout-enforcer check

    # CPU filter audit
    
    The completed CPU stage reproduces literal candidate extraction and conserves
    source records. Its output is too permissive to use as company relevance labels.
    Generic aliases, unrelated publisher tags, page furniture and a confirmed
    date-aware identity/name defect require separate treatment.
    
    ## Review basis
    
    The fixed benchmark contains 1,000 of 12,241,870 retained source records, ordered
    by `sha256('42:' || article_id), article_id`. The 100-row retained audit is a
    second deterministic hash sample within that cohort. Its first 25 records were
    reviewed in that hash order. The separate 100-row no-hit sample uses the same
    audit seed across all no-company-candidate exclusions; its first 20 were reviewed.
    The seed is `ccfinance-cpu-audit-2026-11-16-v1`.
    
    Original text hashes were verified before review. No model predictions were read.
    These are qualitative AI source observations, not independently adjudicated
    human gold. No population precision, recall or confidence interval is claimed.
    The unit is a source record; identical articles can occur more than once.
    
    The rubric distinguishes a primary issuer in the title/lead and business facts,
    a secondary issuer with a financial role, incidental or footer mentions, and a
    surface match referring to ordinary language or another entity. Among the 25
    retained records, observations were: 2 primary, 2 business-secondary, 3 incidental
    or footer-only, and 18 with no genuine candidate entity identified. All 93 stored
    name spans examined matched the original NFKC/casefold text at their recorded
    offsets. Correct literal offsets do not establish correct entity association.
    
    ## Evidence in the fixed 1,000
    
    There are 3,137 article/issuer-namespace candidate pairs. The following counts
    refer to aliases present in stored spans, counted once per article or pair.
    Spans are capped, so these are observed evidence counts rather than all matches.
    
    | Alias | Articles | Candidate pairs |
    | --- | ---: | ---: |
    | people | 331 | 331 |
    | price | 241 | 476 |
    | new | 216 | 216 |
    | news | 209 | 209 |
    | target | 102 | 102 |
    
    Of 1,000 articles, 226 have every candidate supported exclusively by these five
    surfaces, with all counted name matches stored and no counted signals. Another
    30 show only these surfaces but have capped evidence. The remaining 744 have
    another stored alias or signal, which does not guarantee identity or relevance.
    At the pair level these classes contain 1,189, 143 and 1,805 records respectively.
    This diagnostic set is not exhaustive: `fossil`, `premier`, `popular`, `time`
    and other ambiguous surfaces also occur. Duplicate economic issuers across the
    top1000 and GH namespaces explain, for example, the additional `price` pairs.
    
    Full-corpus diagnostics independently show the leading first stored aliases:
    `people` for PERMCO 11901 in 4,100,590 articles; `price` for Costco in 2,905,743 GH
    and 2,849,044 top1000 articles; `new` for Navient in 2,354,510; and `news` for
    News Corp in 2,267,666. These overlapping counts must not be added as unique
    articles. The frozen registry contains the corresponding aliases, including
    Navient's `New Corp`/`New` and Costco's historical `PRICE`.
    
    ## Confirmed defects and semantic failures
    
    1. **Date-aware identity/name contamination.** The article
       `89567ed1cd7c15ffcf445271425e85d21fa9aabd457db74883938cb7248a868e`,
       dated 2021-01-14, is at `2021-01/eng_Latn/part-000001.parquet`, physical row
       20489. Its American Airlines comparison is matched as `top1000:20010`, with
       ticker `AAL`, verified CIK `0000006201`, and alias `american airlines`, but its
       display name is **Alpha Metallurgical Resources, Inc.** The registry contains
       an older candidate-only AMR/Alpha link for 2002–2006 and the verified American
       Airlines link for 2021. Legacy `company/universe.py` lines 41–71 pool names and
       aliases across all registry years and select the alphabetically first legal
       name. `company/tagging.py` lines 140–142 attach it to year-specific records.
       All five occurrences of this candidate in the 1,000-row cohort have the same
       Alpha-name/AAL-identity inconsistency. A classifier prompted with that name
       can evaluate the wrong company even when lexical matching is correct.
    2. **Generic and capitalized surfaces are not resolved entities.** The petroleum
       reserve article `96e3934d...` is retained solely through `Office of Fossil
       Energy` → Fossil Group. The Petraeus article `370a66e2...` matches the dateline
       `Nov 15` → NOV Inc. `Queensland Premier` and sentence-initial `People` produce
       other capitalized false associations. Legacy `tagging.py` lines 324–326 and
       347–348 count any name match lacking `lowercase_single_token` as cased;
       multiword aliases can receive that count without uppercase characters.
    3. **Publisher keyword collisions.** Article `51c152f9...`, source
       `2023-12/eng_Latn/part-000000.parquet`, physical row 35818, is about the AAP
       politician Sanjay Singh and India's Enforcement Directorate. Its original
       tags include `AAP` and `ED`; these become Advance Auto Parts and Consolidated
       Edison candidates. Legacy `tagging.py` lines 386–403 interpret standalone
       uppercase tags as tickers. The uncertainty flags correctly call these signals
       unverified; a publisher-tag count must not be treated as a precision guarantee.
    4. **Document boundaries matter.** Article `7a6e8366...` concerns Canary Gold;
       Comcast/NASDAQ:CMCSA appears only in a Trending Articles link. Article
       `3d7f10c2...` includes social-platform footer names and `NOW WATCH`, while
       `7bf224cc...` begins with an unrelated story teaser. Nonempty raw text alone
       does not remove these sources of false association.
    
    ## No-hit observations
    
    The 20 reviewed no-hit records did not establish a DFA implementation miss.
    They exposed catalog scope limits that must be reported separately from recall:
    the Philip Morris International story is from 2026, beyond the 2002–2025
    membership roster, and GameStop is not eligible in article year 2021 in that
    roster. Other stories concern foreign/private companies, politics or sport.
    Several Law360 and Seeking Alpha records contain clipped bodies, trial prompts
    or substantial boilerplate. These are quality observations, not validated
    automatic exclusion rules.
    
    ## Recommended next decisions
    
    - Preserve this frozen cohort and broad candidate stage as baseline evidence.
      Do not publish candidate presence as company relevance or as model gold.
    - Resolve display names and permitted aliases against the article-year verified
      CIK/issuer membership. Quarantine candidate-only crosswalks from verified
      identities; retain the original link evidence and version any corrected run.
    - Give aliases explicit provenance, historical validity and ambiguity status.
      Generic legal roots and placeholder-like aliases need contextual adjudication.
      Capitalization and a hand-written list of forbidden words are insufficient.
    - Distinguish financial security tags from general publisher keywords using
      documented field semantics. Treat unverified bare uppercase tags as candidate
      retrieval evidence.
    - Separate article body from recommendations, navigation and subscription text
      before assessing substantive relevance. First validate a small set of such
      rules against preserved source examples.
    - Compare the 1,000 model outputs with this blinded rubric and then independently
      adjudicate disputed cases. Measure accepted precision and excluded recall
      separately, including roster/year coverage and exact-duplicate dependence.
    
    The JSON artifacts hold complete IDs, source coordinates, hashes, observations
    and counts. `manifest.json` records the frozen benchmark and selection hashes;
    `methods.sql` records the aggregate and sample queries. Original reviewed texts
    are retained as audit evidence alongside their SHA256 values.

    # Filter articles and score company coverage
    
    ## Goal
    
    Complete the corpus-wide CPU filter, then size native Kev scoring against
    07:00 SAST on 17 November 2026. Preserve source records, all company candidates,
    exclusion reasons and unresolved outcomes. AI-only review remains exploratory;
    the 95% precision target is not a validated accuracy claim.
    
    The data pipeline agent owns CPU selection, the runtime agent owns native Kev,
    and the research agent owns reconciliation and reports. The coordinating agent
    owns their contracts, DVC integration and the deadline decision. See the
    [labeling guide](../../../../../data/inputs/article-labels/README.md).
    
    ## Acceptance
    
    - [x] Materialize and reconcile the complete CPU selection against the frozen source.
    - [x] Verify native Kev multi-company inference and measure its completion estimate.
    - [x] Preserve resumable scores, uncertainty and an honest completion status.
    - [x] Record data dependencies, methods and the required repository checks.
    
    ## Results
    
    The complete CPU census reconciles. The fixed 1,000-record benchmark scored 993
    records and preserved seven context deferrals without server failures. Its
    6.40 successful records/second implies about 22 days for the current broad
    selection. No full-corpus GPU run was launched. All scores remain provisional,
    and no company pair meets the current 0.95 acceptance policy.
    
    The independent [CPU audit](../../../../../data/research/experiments/article-labels/cpu-audit/report.md)
    found generic aliases, publisher-keyword collisions, article furniture and dated
    company-name contamination. In the fixed sample, 226 records have completely
    observed candidate evidence limited to five generic aliases. See the
    [candidate-quality follow-up](../candidate-quality/README.md) before production
    scoring. The audit's 25 retained and 20 no-hit reviews are AI observations,
    not validated accuracy measurements.
    
    `just check` passed, including 39 tests, Ruff, Pyrefly, Tach, test layout,
    Semflow, DVC metadata, document schemas and the LaTeX build. Existing source
    comparison results retain their original lock provenance; the new dependency
    lock correctly marks those earlier stages stale.

    # Candidate identity correction audit
    
    The completed correction preserves all **12,241,870 retained source records and
    38,053,717 company-candidate pairs** across 168 shards. No article or candidate
    was removed by this correction. The original baseline still accounts for all
    14,807,287 source records: 12,241,870 retained and 2,565,417 excluded.
    
    The first complete run took 1,254.24 seconds (20.90 minutes). Its unchanged
    summary is saved in [first-complete-summary.json](first-complete-summary.json).
    
    ## Identity reconciliation
    
    Names and tickers follow the frozen membership's verified article-year CIK,
    rather than aliases pooled across every historical identity sharing a PERMCO.
    Original names, tickers, identity lists and match evidence remain available.
    
    | Identity authority | Candidate pairs |
    | --- | ---: |
    | Verified article-year CIK | 32,062,473 |
    | Fixed GH reference CIK, undated | 4,631,128 |
    | Unverified article-year link; corrected name unresolved | 1,360,116 |
    
    There are 2,202,804 resolved canonical-name changes. This count describes
    reference consistency, not corrected semantic article-company labels.
    
    The title-and-body diagnostic contains 1,934,894 articles and 2,123,555 pairs.
    The other 10,306,976 articles remain retained with their other evidence tiers.
    The summary's `deferred_articles` field means outside that diagnostic; it does
    not mean every such article has an unresolved identity or should be discarded.
    
    Use `identity_status` and the corrected name for identity handling. In
    particular, 15,010 fixed-GH pairs have no stored permitted name evidence and
    receive the fallback `unresolved_identity` evidence tier, while retaining a
    fixed-GH identity and a nonempty corrected name.
    
    ## Frozen sample checks
    
    The original benchmark remains exactly **1,000 distinct source records and
    3,137 candidate pairs**. There are zero missing or added article IDs, source
    coordinate mismatches, or candidate-count changes. Of its pairs, 2,646 have
    verified dated identities, 386 use the fixed undated GH reference, and 105 have

    All five benchmark American Airlines cases now resolve to CIK `0000006201`

    These are structural checks against frozen references, with no semantic gold
    labels, model predictions, precision estimates or confidence intervals. The
    registry names are current or undated; verified article-year CIK links do not
    certify historical alias validity. SEC former-name observations provide
    context flags, not automatic exclusions. A resolved identity still requires
    semantic article-company relevance and subject scoring. Title-and-body tiers
    are diagnostics and do not define the final dataset's scope.

                "registry_names_not_historically_certified",
            )
            for row in range(3)
        ]
    
        with sqlite3.connect(production / "checkpoints.sqlite") as ledger:
            assert ledger.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM articles").fetchone() == (0,)
            assert ledger.execute(
                "SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE payload IS NOT NULL"
            ).fetchone() == (0,)
    
        # Arrange: realistic large pending decisions must not bloat the durable index.
        with _frame(index, None, 42) as (batches, _, _):
            template = next(batches)[0]
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            original_body = _BodyReader(source, con).read([template])[template.article_id]
        store = _Store(production, production=True)
        try:
            previous_pointer = store.db.execute(
                "SELECT artifact FROM requests WHERE inference_id=?",
                [template.inference_id],
            ).fetchone()
            for number in range(64):
                article = template.model_copy(
                    update={
                        "article_id": f"large-{number}",
                        "inference_id": f"request-{number}",
                    }
                )
                store.save_decision(
                    article.inference_id,
                    {"status": "complete", "companies": [], "responses": ["x" * 3000]},
                )
                store.save_article(article, original_body, "00000002", number, reused=False)
            store.save_article(template, original_body, "00000002", 64, reused=True)
            store.db.commit()
            before_bytes = store.db.execute(
                "SELECT sum(pgsize) FROM dbstat WHERE name='requests'"
            ).fetchone()[0]
    
            # Act: flush only this bounded batch, preserving the earlier cache pointer.
            store.flush("00000002")
    
            # Assert: compact lookup storage drops transient JSON space and retains reuse.
            after_bytes = store.db.execute(
                "SELECT sum(pgsize) FROM dbstat WHERE name='requests'"
            ).fetchone()[0]
            assert after_bytes < before_bytes / 2
            assert store.db.execute(
                "SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE payload IS NOT NULL"
            ).fetchone() == (0,)
            assert (
                store.db.execute(
                    "SELECT artifact FROM requests WHERE inference_id=?",
                    [template.inference_id],
                ).fetchone()
                == previous_pointer
            )
            assert store.decision(template.inference_id)["status"] == "complete"
            assert store.decision("request-63")["responses"] == ["x" * 3000]
        finally:
            store.close()
    
        # Arrange: an expired operating deadline must not manufacture completed work.
        settings = json.loads(params.read_text())
        settings["experiments"]["article_labels"]["deadline_utc"] = "2000-01-01T00:00:00Z"
        params.write_text(json.dumps(settings))
        expired = tmp_path / "expired"
    
        # Act: stop before issuing decisions and preserve an explicit resumable status.
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="deadline_reached"):
            score_articles(index, expired, params, source=source)
    
        # Assert: attempted and succeeded both remain zero, with all source rows pending.
        stopped = json.loads((expired / "summary.json").read_text())
        assert stopped["attempted"] == stopped["completed"] == 0

    # Pipeline layers: raw -> processed -> research.
    # Each layer will contain independently reproducible DVC sub-stages.
    
    ## Raw: source snapshots
    # Ingest versioned article and company-reference snapshots with source manifests.
    # Preserve source content, metadata and provenance for replay and reconciliation.
    # Proposed location: data/raw/.
    
    ## Processed: reusable tables
    # Clean, standardize and deduplicate articles; resolve dated company identities
    # and enrich article-company relationships. Retain evidence and quality flags.
    # Produce reusable article, company and relationship tables.
    # Proposed location: data/processed/.
    
    ## Research: study datasets
    # Build company-year coverage panels, study cohorts and publication-ready datasets
    # from processed tables. Apply explicit publisher, relevance and K/T coverage policies.
    # Include dataset documentation, provenance and measured quality in each release.
    # Proposed location: data/research/.
    
    ## Validation and evaluation
    # Validate contracts and reconcile counts at every layer. Keep method experiments,
    # independent evaluation labels and quality reports as versioned supporting
    # artifacts; they inform promotion between layers rather than forming a data tier.
    
    stages:
      prepare_article_labels:
        desc: Reconcile verified CPU company candidates and retain source-linked article indexes.
        cmd: >-
          env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python
          --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline pipeline stages processed
          prepare-article-labels --source data/raw/fine-news
          --legacy data/raw/experiments/article-labels/legacy
          --domains data/inputs/fine-news/domains.csv
          --output data/processed/experiments/article-labels/cpu

        outs:

      report_cpu_article_labels:

    ---
    type: task
    title: Correct dated company identities and generic aliases
    description: Repair candidate-generation defects identified by the fixed 1,000-record audit.
    links: []
    status: in-progress
    ---
    
    # Correct dated company identities and generic aliases
    
    ## Goal
    
    Correct the dated issuer registry and ambiguous lexical aliases before a full
    scoring run. Preserve the existing audit and broad candidate output as a baseline.
    Evidence lives in `data/research/experiments/article-labels/cpu-audit/`.
    
    The legacy registry pools names across years and chooses an alphabetically first
    display name: a 2021 American Airlines match can identify Alpha Metallurgical
    Resources. Generic aliases such as `PRICE`, `NEW`, `People`, `NEWS` and `TARGET`
    generate millions of overlapping candidates. The legacy cased-name proxy and
    unverified publisher ticker annotations also admit false matches.
    
    ## Acceptance
    
    - [x] Resolve names, identifiers and memberships for the article date; preserve unresolved links.
    - [ ] Define evidence-based restrictions for generic aliases and unverified publisher signals.
    - [ ] Compare corrected retrieval with the frozen retained and no-hit audit samples.
    - [ ] Measure candidate reduction and missed-company risk before scheduling full scoring.
    
    The completed correction preserves all 12,241,870 retained source records and
    38,053,717 candidate links. It aligns resolved names and tickers with verified
    dated CIKs, retains original values and explicitly defers unsupported identities.
    The 1,934,894 records with title/body name evidence form a diagnostic subset;
    they do not replace the broad scoring population or establish retrieval recall.

    # Stopped scoring attempt: storage and conservation
    
    This attempt stopped with status `storage_limited` after its first committed
    source chunk. All **1,598 source records and 4,024 candidate associations** are
    preserved. There are 1,597 completed request records and one `too_long` record;
    these statuses do not establish semantic accuracy or research eligibility.
    
    ## Conservation
    
    The bounded audit compares the committed chunk with corrected shard `00000`
    and the original `2016-08/eng_Latn/part-000000.parquet` source.
    
    - All 1,598 article IDs and inference IDs are distinct; none are missing or added.
    - Every original CPU-index field matches the stored article JSON, including
      corrected identities, original identities and candidate evidence.
    - Original metadata and text checksums have zero mismatches.
    - All 4,024 candidate pairs have corresponding decision-company associations,
      with no issuer-association mismatches.
    - SQLite has 1,598 request identities, zero active article payloads and one
      committed chunk. Every request payload is cleared and points to that chunk.
    
    Exact results are in [conservation-audit.json](conservation-audit.json).
    
    ## Storage diagnosis
    
    | Measured component | Bytes |
    | --- | ---: |
    | Compressed committed Parquet | 1,419,638 |
    | Physical SQLite file | 18,149,376 |
    | Reusable SQLite freelist | 12,996,608 |
    | Allocated SQLite pages, excluding freelist | 5,152,768 |
    | Unused space inside allocated request leaf pages | 4,797,659 |
    | Logical SQLite payload, across tables and indexes | 274,535 |
    
    The compressed chunk uses **888.38 bytes per source record** in this chunk.
    The guard measured 4,112.89 bytes per record including allocated SQLite pages.
    Logical Parquet plus SQLite payload is 1,060.18 bytes per record, excluding
    page overhead and fragmentation; this is not a physical capacity forecast.
    
    The scorer temporarily inserts full JSON into the rowid-based `requests`
    table, then replaces payloads with artifact pointers during flush. The JSON
    is cleared, but request leaf pages remain approximately 96.4% unused. This
    allocated slack is separate from the reusable freelist. Ignoring it in the
    guard alone would not fix the storage lifecycle or establish future disk use.
    This diagnosis concerns fragmentation; the audit found no metadata loss.
    
    The original guard's conditional estimate triggered the stop. That estimate
    is retained as provenance in [storage-audit.json](storage-audit.json), together
    with the read-only SQLite `dbstat` measurements. This source-order prefix is
    not a representative storage sample, and no full-corpus capacity or accuracy
    claim is made here.
    
    ## Reproduction
    
    Run from the repository root into a fresh output directory:
    
    ```sh
    devenv shell -- env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV \
      uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages python \
      data/research/experiments/article-labels/corpus-pre-storage-fix/audit.py \
      --output /tmp/ccfinance-stopped-attempt-audit
    ```
    
    The standalone [audit.py](audit.py) uses SQLite read-only mode and compares only
    this bounded chunk. It neither vacuums nor changes the stopped checkpoint.
    [audit-manifest.json](audit-manifest.json) records input paths and SHA-256
    hashes, including the archived scorer identified by the attempt's manifest.
    Existing reporter-generated metrics, CSV and LaTeX files are unchanged.

    # Native decision inference
    
    These scripts run the pinned native Kev server using the CUDA libraries of an
    already cached container image. SGLang is not launched. Native Kev shares the
    article prefix across its independent identity and coverage questions.
    
    From the repository root, prepare the small serving dependencies and then supply
    the existing checkpoint and Hugging Face base-model cache:
    
    ```bash
    just inference::setup
    just inference::serve /path/to/kev-4b /path/to/huggingface/hub \
        data/inputs/article-labels/kev-4b-low-memory.json
    docker logs ccfinance-kev-native
    just inference::status
    ```
    
    The versioned runtime manifest records the model, source, image, precision,
    kernels and admission limit. The entrypoint applies that limit to both the
    article and every complete article-question sequence. Oversized inputs fail
    explicitly; text truncation is disabled. Local package and compilation caches
    live under ignored `.runtime/`.
    
    The third argument selects the versioned runtime profile. Pass the selected 4B
    profile explicitly; omitting it selects the historical 0.8B baseline.
    
    The 4B profile uses BF16 and retains one article prefix. Its adapter and head
    checksums are checked before loading. The serving trial records actual memory
    use separately from the model publisher's memory estimate.
    
    To restore the pinned public 4B files with the repository's Hugging Face CLI:
    
    ```bash
    uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen hf download jaredpalmer/kev-4b \
        adapter_config.json adapter_model.safetensors head.pt \
        --revision 139fdd94f1b6a6ad80cc15e08fcb99cac885a101 \
        --local-dir .runtime/models/kev-4b
    HF_HUB_CACHE="$PWD/.runtime/hf-cache" \
        uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen hf download Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B-Base \
        --revision 1001bb4d826a52d1f399e183466143f4da7b741b \
        --include '*.json' --include '*.safetensors' \
        --include merges.txt --include vocab.json
    ```
    
    The base weights require approximately 9.3 GB of storage. Model files and caches
    stay under ignored `.runtime/`; their revisions and checkpoint checksums remain
    in the versioned profile. Setup expects the recorded container image to exist
    locally and a working NVIDIA Container Toolkit CDI device.
    
    The completed company-labeling pilot used `kev-4b.json` with three concise
    binary questions per distinct company descriptor, sharing the full article
    prefix. Its graph buffers hold four states, 16 rows and 16,384 tokens. Active
    pilot samples reached 15,654 MiB with 197 MiB free on the 16,311 MiB GPU. An
    earlier diagnostic graph capture ran out of memory and fell back to eager
    inference; the completed pilot's native graph and prefix OOM counters stayed
    zero. One client timeout was retried successfully.
    
    Production uses the separate `kev-4b-low-memory.json` profile: two graph states,
    eight rows and 8,192 graph tokens. The 8,192-token context admission, prefix
    cache, weights, precision, temperature and questions remain the same. Sixteen
    exact pilot requests, including its eight longest admitted bodies, compared 337
    probabilities: maximum difference 0.0073, mean difference 0.0001134, with no
    changes at the 0.5 or 0.95 boundaries. The differences reflect floating-point
    reassociation across smaller passes. Occupancy samples reached 14,580 MiB during
    long-body inference and 15,074 MiB after graph capture, with 777 MiB free. These
    observations describe the tested requests rather than guarantee every future
    workload's peak.
    
    `kev-0.8b.json` records a separate experimental 16k admission trial. The smaller
    model was rejected for this pilot after the same fresh source cases produced
    more false positives. The seven-case long-context study was stopped after one
    HTTP success; it does not establish 16k semantic quality. The original
    `runtime.json` remains the historical 8k baseline.
    
    Stop the server with `just inference::stop`; remove its stopped
    container with `docker rm ccfinance-kev-native` before starting a replacement.
    # Python workspace
    
    `apps/pipeline` is an installable Typer application in a Python 3.13 uv workspace.
    Run from the repository root:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run version
    just python::run stages list
    just python::run stages raw --help
    just python::layout
    just python::check
    ```
    
    Data processing is organized into three layers, matching `dvc.yaml`:
    
    | Module and CLI group | Purpose | Data location |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `pipeline.stages.raw` / `stages raw` | Preserve source snapshots and provenance | `data/raw/` |
    | `pipeline.stages.processed` / `stages processed` | Build reusable cleaned and enriched tables | `data/processed/` |
    | `pipeline.stages.research` / `stages research` | Curate coverage panels, cohorts and release datasets | `data/research/` |
    
    The raw layer includes the frozen historical Fine News publisher filter described
    in [its acquisition configuration](../../data/inputs/fine-news/README.md), alongside
    `prepare-comparison` and `sample-comparison`. The research layer provides
    `compare-sources` for weighted estimates from the resulting manifests and counts.
    Experimental implementations live under each layer's `experiments` package.
    They share Pydantic artifact contracts through `pipeline.experiments`; the raw
    `publishers` module owns source mappings and extraction. DVC passes artifact
    paths explicitly, while statistical and source parameters live under
    `experiments.source_comparison` in the root parameter file. Article labeling uses
    `experiments.article_labels` and the [labeling guide](../../data/inputs/article-labels/README.md).
    Its processed commands adopt verified company candidates and prepare compact
    source-linked selections; research reports reconcile counts and measured runtime.
    Reporting follows
    the configured dataset keys and can run a deliberate subset of sources.
    See the [source comparison](../../data/inputs/source-comparison/README.md) before
    running acquisition. Python setup installs DuckDB's `httpfs` extension so the
    local HTTP integration check can run offline. Add other stage commands under their owning layer,
    with explicit inputs and outputs, and declare their dependencies in `dvc.yaml`.
    DVC connects layers through artifacts; Python modules need not import earlier
    layers to read their outputs. Importing a module performs no dataset access.
    
    Setup installs the committed lock. Checks run offline with frozen dependencies.
    Ruff checks formatting, annotations, docstrings and common correctness/security
    issues; strict Pyrefly checks all app code and tests. Tach enforces module
    boundaries, rejects unused dependency declarations and forbids cycles. The CLI
    imports the stage router, which registers the three independent layer modules.
    
    `pytest-layout-enforcer` checks test paths against their owning source modules
    both during pytest collection and with `just python::layout`. Test paths mirror
    `apps/pipeline/src/pipeline` under `apps/pipeline/tests`: for example,
    `cli.py` maps to `test_cli.py`, and `stages/raw/loader.py` maps to
    `stages/raw/test_loader.py`. Feature variants use `__`, as in
    `test_loader__empty.py`; `include-packages` also allows tests for package
    initializers. This checks existing test placement, not test coverage. Tach checks
    imports and does not enforce this layout.
    
    `just python::test` runs all tests. `test-changed` is a local optimization only.
    `build` builds a wheel and source archive. `fmt` explicitly repairs formatting.
    Ruff and Pyrefly run from the same uv lock locally and in CI.

    # Agent contract
    
    - Read the nearest README.md for commands and ARCHITECTURE.md for design decisions.
    - Use the pinned devenv environment and repository just commands.
    - Run Python commands through the appropriate locked uv project.
    - Authored records own state. Use explicit creation and synchronization commands; never edit generated Insitu regions by hand.
    - Task parents expose immediate children. Put supporting evidence in separate records and preserve stable paths.
    - Checks validate without repair; use just fmt and just sync for explicit changes.
    - Run just check before handoff and report any checks that could not run.
    - Resolve secrets only for commands that need them. Never place credentials in tracked files.

    description: Use when creating or maintaining repository plans, references, tasks or their generated views.

    # Repository workflow
    
    ## Workflow
    
    Read the root README and the relevant local README before changing records.
    Use `just --list` to discover the installed workflow and language commands. Create
    records through their commands, edit canonical metadata, then run `just sync`
    when available and `just check`. Keep task parents terse and store detailed
    evidence in linked records. Verification establishes only what the actual
    command output supports; record incomplete or inconclusive checks honestly.

    """Versioned operating parameters for provisional article-company labels."""
    
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import yaml
    from pydantic import AwareDatetime, BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
    
    
    class ArticleLabelsConfig(BaseModel):
        """Keep decision policy, inference limits and the deadline explicit."""
    
        model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    
        seed: int = 42
        deadline_utc: AwareDatetime
        reserve_seconds: int = Field(default=1800, ge=0)
        server_url: str = "http://127.0.0.1:8008"
        api_model: str = "kev-latest"
        model: str = "jaredpalmer/kev-0.8b"
        model_revision: str = Field(pattern=r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$")
        base_model: str = "Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base"
        base_revision: str = Field(pattern=r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$")
        runtime_manifest: Path = Path("data/inputs/article-labels/runtime.json")
        max_context_tokens: int = Field(default=8192, gt=0)
        max_candidates_per_request: int = Field(default=32, gt=0)
        concurrency: int = Field(default=1, gt=0)
        benchmark_size: int = Field(default=1000, gt=0)
        request_timeout_seconds: float = Field(default=60, gt=0, allow_inf_nan=False)
        min_probability: float = Field(default=0.95, ge=0, le=1, allow_inf_nan=False)
        precision_target: float = Field(default=0.95, gt=0, le=1, allow_inf_nan=False)
    
    
    def load_config(params: Path) -> ArticleLabelsConfig:
        """Read the article-labeling experiment without environment overrides."""
        document = yaml.safe_load(params.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        return ArticleLabelsConfig.model_validate(document["experiments"]["article_labels"])
    """Apply the recorded native serving profile before loading Kev."""
    
    import hashlib
    import json
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    
    profile = json.loads(Path(os.environ["CCFINANCE_RUNTIME_MANIFEST"]).read_text())
    for filename, key in (
        ("adapter_model.safetensors", "model_adapter_sha256"),
        ("head.pt", "model_head_sha256"),
    ):
        if key in profile:
            with (Path("/checkpoint") / filename).open("rb") as source:
                actual = hashlib.file_digest(source, "sha256").hexdigest()
            if actual != profile[key]:
                raise ValueError(f"Checkpoint checksum differs from profile: {filename}")
    os.environ.update(
        {
            "KEV_BACKEND": "torch",
            "KEV_DTYPE": {"bfloat16": "bf16", "float32": "fp32"}[profile["dtype"]],
            "KEV_ATTN": profile["attention"],
            "KEV_FUSED": str(int(profile["fused_linear_attention"])),
            "KEV_CUDA_GRAPHS": str(int(profile["cuda_graphs"])),
            "KEV_MERGE": str(int(profile["merge_adapter"])),
            "KEV_PREFIX_CACHE": str(profile["prefix_cache_states"]),
            "KEV_PREFIX_MIN_TOKENS": str(profile["prefix_cache_min_tokens"]),
            "KEV_PREFIX_MAX_TOKENS": str(profile["prefix_cache_max_tokens"]),
            "KEV_TRUNCATE_STATES": str(int(profile["truncate_states"])),
        }
    )
    
    import kev.model  # noqa: E402
    
    kev.model.SERVE_MAX_STATE = profile["max_context_tokens"]
    kev.model.SERVE_MAX_BRANCH = profile["max_context_tokens"]
    
    if limits := profile.get("cuda_graph_limits"):
        import kev.cuda_graphs
    
        allowed = {"GRAPH_STATES", "GRAPH_ROWS", "GRAPH_TOKENS"}
        if set(limits) != allowed:
            raise ValueError("Specify every supported CUDA graph buffer limit")
        for name, value in limits.items():
            if not isinstance(value, int) or value < 1:
                raise ValueError(f"CUDA graph buffer limit must be positive: {name}")
            setattr(kev.cuda_graphs, name, value)
    
    from kev.serve import main  # noqa: E402
    
    main()

        def read(self, articles: list[Article]) -> dict[str, "_Body"]:
            result: dict[str, _Body] = {}
            groups: dict[tuple[str, int], list[Article]] = {}
            for article in articles:
                if article.source_path not in self.bounds:
                    metadata = self.con.execute(
                        "SELECT row_group_id,max(row_group_num_rows),"
                        "sum(total_uncompressed_size) FILTER (WHERE path_in_schema='text') "
                        "FROM parquet_metadata(?) GROUP BY row_group_id "
                        "ORDER BY row_group_id",
                        [str(self.source / article.source_path)],
                    ).fetchall()
                    offset = 0
                    bounds = []
                    for _, rows, size in metadata:
                        bounds.append((offset, offset + int(rows), int(size or 0)))
                        offset += int(rows)
                    self.bounds[article.source_path] = bounds
                bounds = self.bounds[article.source_path]
                index = bisect.bisect_right([b[0] for b in bounds], article.source_row) - 1
                if index < 0 or article.source_row >= bounds[index][1]:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Source row outside original file: {article.article_id}"
                    )
                groups.setdefault((article.source_path, index), []).append(article)
            for (file, index), members in groups.items():
                lower, upper, size = self.bounds[file][index]
                if self.cached_group != (file, index):
                    if size > 128 * 1024 * 1024:
                        rows = self.con.execute(
                            "SELECT file_row_number,text,to_json(metadata) "
                            "FROM read_parquet("
                            "$file,file_row_number=true) WHERE file_row_number "
                            "IN (SELECT unnest($rows))",
                            {
                                "file": str(self.source / file),
                                "rows": [article.source_row for article in members],
                            },
                        ).fetchall()
                        self.cached_group = None
                    else:
                        rows = self.con.execute(
                            "SELECT file_row_number,text,to_json(metadata) "
                            "FROM read_parquet("
                            "$file,file_row_number=true) "
                            "WHERE file_row_number >= $lower "
                            "AND file_row_number < $upper",
                            {
                                "file": str(self.source / file),
                                "lower": lower,
                                "upper": upper,
                            },
                        ).fetchall()
                        self.cached_group = (file, index)
                    self.groups_read += 1
                    self.cached_rows = {
                        int(row): (text, metadata) for row, text, metadata in rows
                    }
                for article in members:
                    original = self.cached_rows.get(article.source_row)
                    if original is None or not isinstance(original[0], str):
                        raise ValueError(f"Original text missing for {article.article_id}")
                    text, metadata_json = original
                    if hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest() != article.text_sha256:
                        raise ValueError(f"Text checksum changed for {article.article_id}")
                    metadata = (
                        JSON_VALUE_ADAPTER.validate_json(metadata_json)
                        if metadata_json is not None
                        else None
                    )
                    result[article.article_id] = _Body(text, metadata)
            return result
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class _Body:
        text: str
        metadata: JsonValue
    
    
    def _resolve_source(
        input: Path, manifest: dict[str, JsonValue], source: Path | None
    ) -> Path:
        if source is not None:
            return source.resolve()
        value = manifest.get("source_root")
        if not isinstance(value, str):
            raise ValueError("Pass --source or provide source_root in the CPU manifest")
        path = Path(value)
        return (path if path.is_absolute() else input / path).resolve()
    
    
    def _article_batches(
        con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, files: list[Path], *, identities: bool
    ) -> Iterator[list[Article]]:
        for file in files:
            query = (
                "SELECT to_json(i) FROM read_parquet(?) i ORDER BY source_path,source_row"
            )
            if identities:
                query = (
                    "SELECT to_json(i) FROM (SELECT *, sha256(to_json(struct_pack("
                    "body:=text_sha256,title:=title,date:=publish_date,publisher:=hostname,"
                    "candidates:=candidates))) AS inference_id FROM read_parquet(?)) i "
                    "ORDER BY source_path,source_row"
                )
            con.execute(query, [str(file)])
            while rows := con.fetchmany(4096):
                yield [Article.model_validate_json(row[0]) for row in rows]
    
    
    @contextmanager
    def _frame(
        input: Path, limit: int | None, seed: int, selection: Path | None = None
    ) -> Iterator[tuple[Iterator[list[Article]], int, int]]:
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            con.execute("SET memory_limit='2GB'")
            con.execute("SET threads=1")
            con.execute("SET preserve_insertion_order=false")
            con.execute("SET max_temp_directory_size='4GB'")
            files = sorted(input.glob("shards/*/retained.parquet"))
            if not files:
                raise ValueError("The CPU index has no completed retained shards")
            if limit is None:
                count = int(
                    con.from_parquet([str(path) for path in files]).count("*").fetchone()[0]
                )
                yield _article_batches(con, files, identities=True), count, count
                return
            frame_metadata = selection.with_suffix(".json") if selection else None
            if (
                selection
                and selection.exists()
                and frame_metadata
                and frame_metadata.exists()
            ):
                saved = json.loads(frame_metadata.read_text())
                if saved["seed"] != seed or saved["requested"] != min(
                    limit, saved["frame_documents"]
                ):
                    raise ValueError("Frozen selection differs from the requested sample")
                if (
                    hashlib.sha256(selection.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
                    != saved["selection_sha256"]
                ):
                    raise ValueError("Frozen selection checksum changed")
                yield (
                    _article_batches(con, [selection], identities=False),
                    int(saved["frame_documents"]),
                    int(saved["requested"]),
                )
                return
            con.read_parquet([str(path) for path in files]).create_view("input_records")
            if limit is not None:
                count_row = con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM input_records").fetchone()
                if count_row is None:
                    raise ValueError("The retained article population is missing")
                count = int(count_row[0])
                con.execute(
                    "CREATE TEMP TABLE sample_keys AS SELECT "
                    "article_id,source_path,source_row "
                    "FROM input_records ORDER BY sha256($seed||':'||article_id),article_id "
                    "LIMIT $limit",
                    {"seed": str(seed), "limit": limit},
                )
                con.execute(
                    "CREATE VIEW chosen AS SELECT i.* FROM input_records i "
                    "JOIN sample_keys s "
                    "USING(article_id,source_path,source_row)"
                )
            else:
                con.execute("CREATE VIEW chosen AS SELECT * FROM input_records")
            con.execute(
                "CREATE VIEW identities AS SELECT *, sha256(to_json(struct_pack("
                "body:=text_sha256,title:=title,date:=publish_date,publisher:=hostname,"
                "candidates:=candidates))) AS inference_id FROM chosen"
            )
            con.execute(
                "CREATE VIEW selected AS SELECT inference_id,article_id FROM identities"
            )
            unit_count = min(count, limit)
            query = (
                "SELECT to_json(i) FROM identities i "
                "JOIN selected s USING(inference_id,article_id) "
                "ORDER BY source_path,source_row"
            )
            requested = unit_count
            if selection:
                con.execute(
                    "COPY (SELECT i.* FROM identities i JOIN selected s "
                    "USING(inference_id,article_id) ORDER BY source_path,source_row) "
                    "TO $output (FORMAT PARQUET)",
                    {"output": str(selection.with_suffix(".parquet.tmp"))},
                )
                selection.with_suffix(".parquet.tmp").replace(selection)
                if frame_metadata:
                    _write_json(
                        frame_metadata,
                        {
                            "frame_documents": count,
                            "requested": requested,
                            "seed": seed,
                            "selection": "SHA256(seed:article_id) retained-row priority",
                            "frame_unit": "retained source article rows",
                            "selection_sha256": hashlib.sha256(
                                selection.read_bytes()
                            ).hexdigest(),
                        },
                    )
                con.execute(
                    "SELECT to_json(s) FROM read_parquet(?) s "
                    "ORDER BY source_path,source_row",
                    [str(selection)],
                )
            else:
                con.execute(query)
            if selection:
                yield _article_batches(con, [selection], identities=False), count, requested
            else:

    async def _score(
        article: Article, text: str, config: ArticleLabelsConfig, model: SystemOneModel
    ) -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
        state: JsonValue = {
            "title": article.title,
            "published_at": article.publish_date,
            "publisher": article.hostname,
            "article": text,
        }
        candidates = {str(item["issuer_id"]): item for item in article.candidates}
        unique = list(candidates.values())
        sources = _question_sources(unique)
        representatives = [

    def _evidence_tiers(
        connection: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection,
    ) -> list[dict[str, JsonValue]]:
        """Count existing evidence predicates without altering retained eligibility.
    
        Legacy spans contain at most four examples per field. Presence and the
        two-body-span predicate describe those stored examples, not full match counts.
        The legacy cased-name counter tests absence of a lowercase-single-token flag;
        it does not require capitalization of every multiword alias.

        certification and signal uncertainty flags remain in the separate report.
        """
        return _query_rows(
            connection,
            """
            WITH evidence AS (
                SELECT document_id,
                    list_bool_or(list_transform(candidates,
                        c -> c.cased_name_match_count > 0)) AS any_cased_name,
                    list_bool_or(list_transform(candidates,
                        c -> c.tag_match_count > 0)) AS any_publisher_annotation,
                    list_bool_or(list_transform(candidates,
                        c -> len(list_filter(c.spans.title,
                            s -> s.source = 'name_alias')) > 0)) AS any_title_name,
                    list_bool_or(list_transform(candidates,
                        c -> len(list_filter(c.spans.title,
                            s -> s.source = 'name_alias')) > 0
                        AND c.cased_name_match_count > 0)) AS title_and_cased_name,
                    list_bool_or(list_transform(candidates,
                        c -> len(list_filter(c.spans.body,
                            s -> s.source = 'name_alias')) >= 2)) AS repeated_body_name,
                    list_bool_or(list_transform(candidates,
                        c -> NOT list_contains(c.uncertainty_flags, 'shared_alias')
                        AND NOT list_contains(c.uncertainty_flags, 'shared_ticker')))

            ), documents AS (
                SELECT document_id, bool_or(COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE(document_id)))
                FROM evidence GROUP BY document_id
            ), units AS (
                SELECT *, 'record' AS unit FROM evidence
                UNION ALL SELECT *, 'document' AS unit FROM documents
            ), unpivoted AS (
                UNPIVOT units ON COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE(document_id, unit))
                INTO NAME evidence_tier VALUE matches
            ), tiers(evidence_tier) AS (VALUES
                ('any_cased_name'), ('any_publisher_annotation'), ('any_title_name'),
                ('title_and_cased_name'), ('repeated_body_name'),
                ('issuer_without_shared_alias_or_ticker')
            )
            SELECT evidence_tier,
                count(*) FILTER (WHERE matches AND unit = 'record') AS article_records,
                count(*) FILTER (WHERE matches AND unit = 'document')
                    AS exact_text_documents,
                'Existing candidate evidence; unvalidated primary-topic proxy' AS basis
            FROM tiers LEFT JOIN unpivoted USING (evidence_tier)
            GROUP BY evidence_tier ORDER BY evidence_tier
            """,
        )
    
    
    def _cohorts(
        connection: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, membership_available: bool
    ) -> list[dict[str, JsonValue]]:
        rows: list[dict[str, JsonValue]] = []
        for threshold in (42, 47):

                result = _query_rows(
                    connection,
                    "WITH eligible AS (SELECT issuer_id, publish_year, "
                    "publish_year - row_number() OVER "
                    "(PARTITION BY issuer_id ORDER BY publish_year) AS run "
                    "FROM company_year WHERE candidate_documents >= $threshold), "
                    "runs AS (SELECT issuer_id, count(*) AS consecutive_years "
                    "FROM eligible GROUP BY issuer_id, run) "
                    "SELECT count(DISTINCT issuer_id) AS companies FROM runs "
                    "WHERE consecutive_years >= $years",
                    {"threshold": threshold, "years": years},
                )[0]
                rows.append(
                    {
                        "annual_documents": threshold,
                        "consecutive_years": years,
                        "candidate_companies": result["companies"]
                        if membership_available
                        else None,
                        "basis": "Exact-text candidate documents; unvalidated associations",
                    }
                )
        return rows
    
    
    def _latex(metrics: dict[str, JsonValue]) -> dict[str, str]:
        summary = Summary()

        capacity = metrics["capacity"]
        if not isinstance(population, dict) or not isinstance(capacity, dict):
            raise ValueError("Coverage and capacity summaries must be mappings")
        tables = [
            (
                "coverage",
                "Observed CPU article records",
                population,
                (
                    "source_records",
                    "retained_records",
                    "excluded_records",
                    "candidate_documents",
                ),
            ),
            (
                "throughput",
                "Conditional processing capacity",
                capacity,
                (
                    "remaining_inference_units",
                    "available_gpu_seconds",
                    "required_inference_units_per_second",
                    "observed_inference_units_per_second",
                    "conditional_remaining_seconds",
                ),
            ),
        ]
        production = metrics.get("production_scoring")
        if isinstance(production, dict):
            tables.append(
                (
                    "scoring",
                    "Observed provisional production decisions",
                    production,
                    (
                        "source_records_in_chunks",
                        "source_records_with_scored_companies",
                        "source_records_with_only_deferred_identity",
                        "candidate_pairs_in_chunks",
                        "unattempted_source_records",
                    ),
                )
            )
        for _, title, values, fields in tables:
            summary.tables.append(
                SimpleTable(
                    [
                        [f"{value:,.3f}" if isinstance(value, float) else str(value)]
                        if (value := values.get(field)) is not None
                        else ["--"]
                        for field in fields
                    ],
                    headers=["Value"],
                    stubs=[field.replace("_", " ") for field in fields],
                    title=title,

    # Define dataset requirements
    
    ## Goal
    
    Specify a public, reproducible financial news dataset for firm-level text,
    co-mention networks and market research.
    
    ## Requirements
    
    - **Coverage:** Report distinct usable articles per company-year, including zero
      counts for a declared universe, and firms meeting selectable annual thresholds
      over consecutive years. Compare with 47 raw articles per year over 2018–2022

    # Architecture
    
    CCFinance separates code and research artifacts. Git stores source, configuration,
    locks, provenance definitions and documentation. DVC defines data dependencies
    and tracks materialized source snapshots and experiment outputs.
    
    - `src/python/apps/pipeline` owns the CLI and data stage implementations.
    - `src/python/uv.lock` locks runtime, quality, testing, packaging and DVC tools.
    - `src/latex` owns the manuscript source and bibliography.
    - `data` holds ignored data payloads and versioned DVC pointer files.
    - `infra/nix` and `devenv.lock` own the reproducible system environment.
    
    Tach enforces module boundaries; Ruff and strict Pyrefly check Python source.
    pytest-layout-enforcer checks test file placement during collection and CI.
    Semflow fingerprints the Python code used by DVC stages, allowing DVC to
    invalidate tracked results when executable behavior changes.
    CI executes those checks, tests and builds through the same just recipes as local
    work. Setup may download dependencies; ordinary checks use cached dependencies
    and do not repair authored content. LaTeX uses a versioned Tectonic asset bundle.
    
    The Hugging Face dataset is staging, and the bucket is intended for intermediate
    and experiment artifacts. The frozen raw acquisition stage documents the
    historical selection without fetching its output. Company labels and coverage
    are provisional experiments; release validation and remote artifact transport
    remain future work. The raw comparison stages prepare
    sampling manifests from Hub listings and Parquet footers, then acquire only the
    selected row groups through the shared publisher filter. Research aggregation
    reads those artifacts without importing raw-stage modules. DVC connects these
    steps; pinned source revisions and recorded draw probabilities define the
    experiment's population and sampling design.
    
    The article-labeling experiment adopts checksum-verified CPU company candidates
    and materializes compact source-linked selections without copying article bodies.
    Native Kev runs in a separately pinned GPU environment; the pipeline communicates
    through typed System One requests. Article-company probabilities and filtering
    policies remain separate, with resumable checkpoints and explicit unresolved
    outcomes. The research layer reconciles candidate and model-scored coverage and
    reports runtime estimates without treating AI agreement as human validation.
    Completed pilots remain frozen. Full scoring uses compressed source-record
    chunks, a resumable request ledger and explicit pending counts. Separate runtime
    profiles preserve GPU memory experiments without overwriting completed evidence.
    
    Each data layer groups experimental artifacts beneath `experiments/<name>/`.
    Experimental stage code follows the same grouping under its owning layer.
    `pipeline.experiments.source_comparison` defines shared parameters and artifacts;
    Tach permits raw and research to depend on these contracts without importing one
    another. Raw publisher extraction owns one source-field registry, deriving both
    SQL projections and projected column sizes from it. DVC supplies artifact paths
    explicitly. Research uses statsmodels for survey-estimate summaries and LaTeX
    tables; it preserves the probability-sampling design.
    
    Copier answers record the source and tag for future template updates. Review
    update conflicts and preserve project-specific code and configuration. The
    upstream template is [Exordio](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/exordio).

    def _production_metrics(
        connection: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection,
        scores: Path,
        benchmark: dict[str, JsonValue],
        config: ArticleLabelsConfig,
    ) -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
        """Aggregate scalar fields from committed chunks without loading article JSON."""
        files = sorted(scores.glob("chunks/*.parquet"))
        if files:
            connection.from_parquet([str(path) for path in files]).create_view(
                "score_chunks"
            )
            connection.execute(
                "CREATE VIEW scored_records AS SELECT article_id,inference_id,status,"
                "json_extract_string(article_json,'$.document_id') AS document_id,"
                "try_cast(json_extract(article_json,'$.publish_year') AS INTEGER) "
                "AS publish_year,"
                "json_extract(decision_json,'$.companies[*]') AS companies,"
                "json_extract_string(decision_json,'$.model_name') AS model_name "
                "FROM score_chunks"
            )
        else:
            connection.execute(
                "CREATE VIEW scored_records AS SELECT NULL::VARCHAR AS article_id,"
                "NULL::VARCHAR AS inference_id,NULL::VARCHAR AS status,"
                "NULL::VARCHAR AS document_id,NULL::INTEGER AS publish_year,"
                "[]::JSON[] AS companies,NULL::VARCHAR AS model_name WHERE false"
            )
        connection.execute(
            "CREATE VIEW company_scores AS SELECT article_id,inference_id,document_id,"
            "publish_year,"
            "unnest(companies) AS company FROM scored_records"
        )
        judgments = _query_rows(
            connection,
            "SELECT json_extract_string(company,'$.status') AS status,"
            "count(*) AS candidate_pairs FROM company_scores "
            "GROUP BY status ORDER BY status",
        )
        counts = _query_rows(
            connection,
            "SELECT count(*) AS source_records_in_chunks,"
            "count(*) FILTER(WHERE list_bool_or(list_transform(companies,"
            "c -> try_cast(json_extract(c,'$.identity_score') AS DOUBLE) IS NOT NULL))) "
            "AS source_records_with_scored_companies,"
            "count(*) FILTER(WHERE len(companies)>0 AND list_bool_and("
            "list_transform(companies,c -> json_extract_string(c,'$.status')="
            "'deferred_identity'))) AS source_records_with_only_deferred_identity,"
            "coalesce(sum(len(companies)),0) AS candidate_pairs_in_chunks "
            "FROM scored_records",
        )[0]
        counts["source_status_counts"] = _query_rows(
            connection,
            "SELECT status,count(*) AS source_records FROM scored_records "
            "GROUP BY status ORDER BY status",
        )
        counts["reported_attempted_source_records"] = benchmark.get("attempted")
        counts["unattempted_source_records"] = benchmark.get("unattempted")
        requested = _number(benchmark, "requested")
        observed = counts["source_records_in_chunks"]
        counts["source_records_without_committed_decisions"] = (
            max(0, int(requested) - observed)
            if requested is not None and isinstance(observed, int)
            else None
        )
        manifest = (
            _read_json(scores / "manifest.json")
            if (scores / "manifest.json").is_file()
            else {}
        )
        settings = manifest.get("config")
        settings = settings if isinstance(settings, dict) else {}
        threshold = _number(settings, "min_probability") or config.min_probability
        distributions = _query_rows(
            connection,
            "WITH values AS (SELECT field,try_cast(json_extract(company,'$.'||field) "
            "AS DOUBLE) AS value FROM company_scores CROSS JOIN "
            "(VALUES('identity_score'),('substantive_score'),('raw_primary_score'),"
            "('primary_score'),('coverage_score')) fields(field)) "
            "SELECT field AS score,count(value) AS observed_candidate_pairs,"
            "min(value) AS minimum,avg(value) AS mean,max(value) AS maximum,"
            "count(*) FILTER(WHERE value >= 0.5) AS at_least_half,"
            "count(*) FILTER(WHERE value >= $threshold) AS at_least_threshold "
            "FROM values GROUP BY field ORDER BY field",
            {"threshold": threshold},
        )
        return {
            "score_source": "committed_production_chunks",
            "observed_judgments": judgments,
            "production_scoring": counts,
            "score_distributions": distributions,
            "scoring_metadata": {
                "scorer_sha256": manifest.get("scorer_sha256"),
                "contract_sha256": manifest.get("contract_sha256"),
                "rubric": manifest.get("rubric"),
                "runtime": manifest.get("runtime"),
                "config": settings,
                "observed_models": _query_rows(
                    connection,
                    "SELECT model_name,count(*) AS source_records FROM scored_records "
                    "GROUP BY model_name ORDER BY model_name",
                ),
                "model_selection_threshold": threshold,
                "validation_status": "pending_human",
                "interpretation": (
                    "Scores and selection thresholds are provisional model outputs; "
                    "no calibrated probabilities or validated precision are inferred. "
                    "The scorer hash identifies the exact rubric when it is not recorded. "
                    "Source-record counts and candidate-pair counts "
                    "have separate denominators. Attempted and unattempted counters "
                    "come from the selected metadata snapshot; committed chunk counts "
                    "are independently observed."
                ),
            },
        }
