    # Corrected-pilot context deferrals
    
    All seven context-rejected source records in the frozen corrected 1,000-record
    pilot remain deferred. Their 75 candidate associations retain NULL scores and
    tags. This audit changes no selection, model result or runtime profile.
    
    The saved native errors report states of 9,315–13,103 tokens against the configured
    8,192-token limit. Original bodies contain 42,476–62,011 characters. All seven
    titles identify earnings call transcripts; every original body contains speaker
    markers including `Operator`. Six records are from Seeking Alpha and one is from
    Nasdaq. These observations describe the seven exceptions, without estimating
    full-corpus exception rates or labeling accuracy.
    
    [cases.json](cases.json) and [cases.csv](cases.csv) record source paths and physical
    row numbers, titles, dates, issuer IDs, body hashes and verbatim native errors.
    The audit reread the seven original bodies, verified their UTF-8 SHA256 and
    character counts, and checked conservation of all 75 candidate associations.
    Transcript marker counts and source metadata support the document descriptions;
    they are not accuracy gold or adjudicated company labels.
    
    The rejection length measures the serialized article state, including its
    `<state>` token. Native `encode` rejects an oversized state before encoding
    question branches. These error lengths therefore do not measure complete
    question-row lengths or total packed request tokens. A state below 16,384 tokens
    does not establish complete-request admission, GPU memory fit or prediction
    quality at that limit.
    
    The [pinned Kev-4B model card](https://github.com/jaredpalmer/kev/blob/2074cc44256200bb37540103fa4572901faa10f3/docs/model-cards/kev-4b.md#limitations-and-risks)
    validates 8,192 tokens. Its 16k long-document bucket failed the registered
    tolerance: paired CUAD accuracy difference versus 8k was −1.1 percentage points
    with a 95% interval of [−3.4, +1.2]; the lower bound had to reach −3.0. Those
    benchmarks concern a different task and do not validate financial transcript
    labeling. Increasing admission limits alone is not a validated remedy.
    
    The seven records stay in the population with explicit context deferrals. A
    faithful later solution must retain their complete text and company questions
    and undergo a separate quality and resource evaluation. This audit creates no
    16k profile, truncation, window aggregation or exclusion policy, and performs no
    GPU tests.
    
    ## Reproduce
    
    Run from the repository root, choosing a fresh output directory:
    
    ```sh
    devenv shell -- env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV \
      uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages python \
      data/research/experiments/article-labels/context-audit/audit.py \
      --output /tmp/ccfinance-context-audit-rerun
    ```
    
    [methods.json](methods.json) states the cohort and interpretation limits.
    [manifest.json](manifest.json) records input hashes, the pilot/model/native-code
    revisions and source snapshot declarations. Original Parquet file hashes are
    inherited declarations from the frozen CPU manifest; the seven body hashes are
    directly verified here. The script reads SQLite in read-only mode and accesses
    only the seven selected raw records. It uses the locked project's DuckDB and
    Python standard library; it loads no tokenizer or model and makes no network or
    GPU calls.

        )
        connection.execute(

            "try_cast(json_extract(company,'$.identity_score') AS DOUBLE) "

    # Corrected-pilot context deferrals
    
    All seven context-rejected source records in the frozen corrected 1,000-record
    pilot remain deferred. Their 75 candidate associations retain NULL scores and
    tags. This audit changes no selection, model result or runtime profile.
    
    The saved native errors report states of 9,315–13,103 tokens against the configured
    8,192-token limit. Original bodies contain 42,476–62,011 characters. All seven
    titles identify earnings call transcripts; every original body contains speaker
    markers including `Operator`. Six records are from Seeking Alpha and one is from
    Nasdaq. These observations describe the seven exceptions, without estimating
    full-corpus exception rates or labeling accuracy.
    
    [cases.json](cases.json) and [cases.csv](cases.csv) record source paths and physical
    row numbers, titles, dates, issuer IDs, body hashes and verbatim native errors.
    The audit reread the seven original bodies, verified their UTF-8 SHA256 and
    character counts, and checked conservation of all 75 candidate associations.
    Transcript marker counts and source metadata support the document descriptions;
    they are not accuracy gold or adjudicated company labels.
    
    The rejection length measures the serialized article state, including its
    `<state>` token. Native `encode` rejects an oversized state before encoding
    question branches. These error lengths therefore do not measure complete
    question-row lengths or total packed request tokens. A state below 16,384 tokens
    does not establish complete-request admission, GPU memory fit or prediction
    quality at that limit.
    
    The [pinned Kev-4B model card](https://github.com/jaredpalmer/kev/blob/2074cc44256200bb37540103fa4572901faa10f3/docs/model-cards/kev-4b.md#limitations-and-risks)
    validates 8,192 tokens. Its 16k long-document bucket failed the registered
    tolerance: paired CUAD accuracy difference versus 8k was −1.1 percentage points
    with a 95% interval of [−3.4, +1.2]; the lower bound had to reach −3.0. Those
    benchmarks concern a different task and do not validate financial transcript
    labeling. Increasing admission limits alone is not a validated remedy.
    
    The seven records stay in the population with explicit context deferrals. A
    faithful later solution must retain their complete text and company questions
    and undergo a separate quality and resource evaluation. This audit creates no
    16k profile, truncation, window aggregation or exclusion policy, and performs no
    GPU tests.
    
    ## Reproduce
    
    Run from the repository root, choosing a fresh output directory:
    
    ```sh
    devenv shell -- env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV \
      uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages python \
      data/research/experiments/article-labels/context-audit/audit.py \
      --output /tmp/ccfinance-context-audit-rerun
    ```
    
    [methods.json](methods.json) states the cohort and interpretation limits.
    [manifest.json](manifest.json) records input hashes, the pilot/model/native-code
    revisions and source snapshot declarations. Original Parquet file hashes are
    inherited declarations from the frozen CPU manifest; the seven body hashes are
    directly verified here. The script reads SQLite in read-only mode and accesses
    only the seven selected raw records. It uses the locked project's DuckDB and
    Python standard library; it loads no tokenizer or model and makes no network or
    GPU calls.

    # CPU filter audit
    
    The completed CPU stage reproduces literal candidate extraction and conserves
    source records. Its output is too permissive to use as company relevance labels.
    Generic aliases, unrelated publisher tags, page furniture and a confirmed
    date-aware identity/name defect require separate treatment.
    
    ## Review basis
    
    The fixed benchmark contains 1,000 of 12,241,870 retained source records, ordered
    by `sha256('42:' || article_id), article_id`. The 100-row retained audit is a
    second deterministic hash sample within that cohort. Its first 25 records were
    reviewed in that hash order. The separate 100-row no-hit sample uses the same
    audit seed across all no-company-candidate exclusions; its first 20 were reviewed.
    The seed is `ccfinance-cpu-audit-2026-11-16-v1`.
    
    Original text hashes were verified before review. No model predictions were read.
    These are qualitative AI source observations, not independently adjudicated
    human gold. No population precision, recall or confidence interval is claimed.
    The unit is a source record; identical articles can occur more than once.
    
    The rubric distinguishes a primary issuer in the title/lead and business facts,
    a secondary issuer with a financial role, incidental or footer mentions, and a
    surface match referring to ordinary language or another entity. Among the 25
    retained records, observations were: 2 primary, 2 business-secondary, 3 incidental
    or footer-only, and 18 with no genuine candidate entity identified. All 93 stored
    name spans examined matched the original NFKC/casefold text at their recorded
    offsets. Correct literal offsets do not establish correct entity association.
    
    ## Evidence in the fixed 1,000
    
    There are 3,137 article/issuer-namespace candidate pairs. The following counts
    refer to aliases present in stored spans, counted once per article or pair.
    Spans are capped, so these are observed evidence counts rather than all matches.
    
    | Alias | Articles | Candidate pairs |
    | --- | ---: | ---: |
    | people | 331 | 331 |
    | price | 241 | 476 |
    | new | 216 | 216 |
    | news | 209 | 209 |
    | target | 102 | 102 |
    
    Of 1,000 articles, 226 have every candidate supported exclusively by these five
    surfaces, with all counted name matches stored and no counted signals. Another
    30 show only these surfaces but have capped evidence. The remaining 744 have
    another stored alias or signal, which does not guarantee identity or relevance.
    At the pair level these classes contain 1,189, 143 and 1,805 records respectively.
    This diagnostic set is not exhaustive: `fossil`, `premier`, `popular`, `time`
    and other ambiguous surfaces also occur. Duplicate economic issuers across the
    top1000 and GH namespaces explain, for example, the additional `price` pairs.
    
    Full-corpus diagnostics independently show the leading first stored aliases:
    `people` for PERMCO 11901 in 4,100,590 articles; `price` for Costco in 2,905,743 GH
    and 2,849,044 top1000 articles; `new` for Navient in 2,354,510; and `news` for
    News Corp in 2,267,666. These overlapping counts must not be added as unique
    articles. The frozen registry contains the corresponding aliases, including
    Navient's `New Corp`/`New` and Costco's historical `PRICE`.
    
    ## Confirmed defects and semantic failures
    
    1. **Date-aware identity/name contamination.** The article
       `89567ed1cd7c15ffcf445271425e85d21fa9aabd457db74883938cb7248a868e`,
       dated 2021-01-14, is at `2021-01/eng_Latn/part-000001.parquet`, physical row
       20489. Its American Airlines comparison is matched as `top1000:20010`, with
       ticker `AAL`, verified CIK `0000006201`, and alias `american airlines`, but its
       display name is **Alpha Metallurgical Resources, Inc.** The registry contains
       an older candidate-only AMR/Alpha link for 2002–2006 and the verified American
       Airlines link for 2021. Legacy `company/universe.py` lines 41–71 pool names and
       aliases across all registry years and select the alphabetically first legal
       name. `company/tagging.py` lines 140–142 attach it to year-specific records.
       All five occurrences of this candidate in the 1,000-row cohort have the same
       Alpha-name/AAL-identity inconsistency. A classifier prompted with that name
       can evaluate the wrong company even when lexical matching is correct.
    2. **Generic and capitalized surfaces are not resolved entities.** The petroleum
       reserve article `96e3934d...` is retained solely through `Office of Fossil
       Energy` → Fossil Group. The Petraeus article `370a66e2...` matches the dateline
       `Nov 15` → NOV Inc. `Queensland Premier` and sentence-initial `People` produce
       other capitalized false associations. Legacy `tagging.py` lines 324–326 and
       347–348 count any name match lacking `lowercase_single_token` as cased;
       multiword aliases can receive that count without uppercase characters.
    3. **Publisher keyword collisions.** Article `51c152f9...`, source
       `2023-12/eng_Latn/part-000000.parquet`, physical row 35818, is about the AAP
       politician Sanjay Singh and India's Enforcement Directorate. Its original
       tags include `AAP` and `ED`; these become Advance Auto Parts and Consolidated
       Edison candidates. Legacy `tagging.py` lines 386–403 interpret standalone
       uppercase tags as tickers. The uncertainty flags correctly call these signals
       unverified; a publisher-tag count must not be treated as a precision guarantee.
    4. **Document boundaries matter.** Article `7a6e8366...` concerns Canary Gold;
       Comcast/NASDAQ:CMCSA appears only in a Trending Articles link. Article
       `3d7f10c2...` includes social-platform footer names and `NOW WATCH`, while
       `7bf224cc...` begins with an unrelated story teaser. Nonempty raw text alone
       does not remove these sources of false association.
    
    ## No-hit observations
    
    The 20 reviewed no-hit records did not establish a DFA implementation miss.
    They exposed catalog scope limits that must be reported separately from recall:
    the Philip Morris International story is from 2026, beyond the 2002–2025
    membership roster, and GameStop is not eligible in article year 2021 in that
    roster. Other stories concern foreign/private companies, politics or sport.
    Several Law360 and Seeking Alpha records contain clipped bodies, trial prompts
    or substantial boilerplate. These are quality observations, not validated
    automatic exclusion rules.
    
    ## Recommended next decisions
    
    - Preserve this frozen cohort and broad candidate stage as baseline evidence.
      Do not publish candidate presence as company relevance or as model gold.
    - Resolve display names and permitted aliases against the article-year verified
      CIK/issuer membership. Quarantine candidate-only crosswalks from verified
      identities; retain the original link evidence and version any corrected run.
    - Give aliases explicit provenance, historical validity and ambiguity status.
      Generic legal roots and placeholder-like aliases need contextual adjudication.
      Capitalization and a hand-written list of forbidden words are insufficient.
    - Distinguish financial security tags from general publisher keywords using
      documented field semantics. Treat unverified bare uppercase tags as candidate
      retrieval evidence.
    - Separate article body from recommendations, navigation and subscription text
      before assessing substantive relevance. First validate a small set of such
      rules against preserved source examples.
    - Compare the 1,000 model outputs with this blinded rubric and then independently
      adjudicate disputed cases. Measure accepted precision and excluded recall
      separately, including roster/year coverage and exact-duplicate dependence.
    
    The JSON artifacts hold complete IDs, source coordinates, hashes, observations
    and counts. `manifest.json` records the frozen benchmark and selection hashes;
    `methods.sql` records the aggregate and sample queries. Original reviewed texts
    are retained as audit evidence alongside their SHA256 values.
    # Candidate identity correction audit
    
    The completed correction preserves all **12,241,870 retained source records and
    38,053,717 company-candidate pairs** across 168 shards. No article or candidate
    was removed by this correction. The original baseline still accounts for all
    14,807,287 source records: 12,241,870 retained and 2,565,417 excluded.
    
    The first complete run took 1,254.24 seconds (20.90 minutes). Its unchanged
    summary is saved in [first-complete-summary.json](first-complete-summary.json).
    
    ## Identity reconciliation
    
    Names and tickers follow the frozen membership's verified article-year CIK,
    rather than aliases pooled across every historical identity sharing a PERMCO.
    Original names, tickers, identity lists and match evidence remain available.
    
    | Identity authority | Candidate pairs |
    | --- | ---: |
    | Verified article-year CIK | 32,062,473 |
    | Fixed GH reference CIK, undated | 4,631,128 |
    | Unverified article-year link; corrected name unresolved | 1,360,116 |
    
    There are 2,202,804 resolved canonical-name changes. This count describes
    reference consistency, not corrected semantic article-company labels.
    
    The title-and-body diagnostic contains 1,934,894 articles and 2,123,555 pairs.
    The other 10,306,976 articles remain retained with their other evidence tiers.
    The summary's `deferred_articles` field means outside that diagnostic; it does
    not mean every such article has an unresolved identity or should be discarded.
    
    Use `identity_status` and the corrected name for identity handling. In
    particular, 15,010 fixed-GH pairs have no stored permitted name evidence and
    receive the fallback `unresolved_identity` evidence tier, while retaining a
    fixed-GH identity and a nonempty corrected name.
    
    ## Frozen sample checks
    
    The original benchmark remains exactly **1,000 distinct source records and
    3,137 candidate pairs**. There are zero missing or added article IDs, source
    coordinate mismatches, or candidate-count changes. Of its pairs, 2,646 have
    verified dated identities, 386 use the fixed undated GH reference, and 105 have
    unverified article-year links.
    
    All five benchmark American Airlines cases now resolve to CIK `0000006201`
    and ticker `AAL`, preserving the original Alpha Metallurgical assignment for
    audit. The separate audited Delta-results article at
    `2021-01/eng_Latn/part-000001.parquet`, row 20489, retains its American Airlines
    secondary-company evidence; lacking a title match does not remove it.
    
    The separate fresh-audit ViacomCBS case at
    `2020-02/eng_Latn/part-000000.parquet`, row 74501, remains unresolved because the
    2020 PERMCO 21866 membership has no verified CIK. Its unrelated original Banzai
    name is preserved for audit and is not supplied as a resolved company name.
    
    The narrow [sample comparison](sample-comparison.parquet) preserves candidate
    order and both original and corrected fields. Exact observed cases are saved
    in [observed-checks.json](observed-checks.json); full census counts and limits
    are in [metrics.json](metrics.json). [Methods](methods.json) record input hashes
    and the census SQL, and [audit.py](audit.py) records the calculations used.
    
    ## Limits
    
    These are structural checks against frozen references, with no semantic gold
    labels, model predictions, precision estimates or confidence intervals. The
    registry names are current or undated; verified article-year CIK links do not
    certify historical alias validity. SEC former-name observations provide
    context flags, not automatic exclusions. A resolved identity still requires
    semantic article-company relevance and subject scoring. Title-and-body tiers
    are diagnostics and do not define the final dataset's scope.
    # Accepted pilot source review
    
    All 24 accepted namespace pairs in 21 original articles identify the displayed company and contain developed company-specific information. Each company is defensibly one of the article's main subjects, including the two companies in the rail roundup. No accepted pair appears to be a generic-word collision, footer-only mention or attribution-only link in this qualitative review.
    
    This is an AI-assisted **post-selection** check: acceptance was known, model score values were not loaded, and the original text checksums were verified for all 21 articles. These observations are not human gold, a population precision estimate, a 95% precision finding or a recall assessment. The 24 namespace pairs represent 22 distinct article/CIK combinations; Micron and Tractor Supply each appear in both Top1000 and GH namespaces.
    
    Company relevance does not establish suitability for the default editorial dataset:
    
    - **19 articles / 20 pairs** contain identifiable editorial reporting or investment analysis, often syndicated. Twelve of those articles also contain publisher or subscription promotions; the company evidence is developed in the article body.
    - **One article / two pairs** is an explicit Tractor Supply issuer press release syndicated from Business Wire. Its notes offering is primary company coverage, but it belongs in the separate release view under the current intended policy.
    - **One article / two pairs** is a developed Zacks rail roundup with “For Immediate Release,” media-contact and marketing material. The company roles are clear; its editorial-versus-promotional format needs policy review. No exclusion was applied.
    
    The examples expose source-quality limits: Micron is a summary/truncated excerpt; several analyses reference missing figures or tables; Delta contains internally inconsistent revenue/cash-burn wording, and FirstCash appears to omit revenue scale units. The Tesla item's relative weekday wording needs date review. Chipotle and Oracle publication dates precede their crawl partitions, so partition dates must not substitute for publication dates. These are observations about the retained text, not externally verified factual corrections.
    
    Only 15 of the 24 accepted links carry the verified-title-and-body discovery tier. The other nine include developed Nektar, BILL, Delta, Walmart, Chipotle, Micron and United Bankshares coverage, plus the GH Tractor Supply link. This selected subset cannot estimate a stricter filter's population recall, but it shows why stored lexical tiers must not be treated as relevance truth.
    
    The accepted links look sensible for a provisional company-relevance filter. A full run should preserve the separate source-format and quality fields and keep human validation pending. This review did not change any scoring threshold, exclusion rule, source record or sealed audit label.
    
    Evidence: [verified source records](source-records.json), [all pair observations](observations.csv), [rubric and structured observations](observations.json), [counts and limitations](summary.json), and [extraction provenance](manifest.json).

    # Correct dated company identities and generic aliases
    
    ## Goal
    
    Correct the dated issuer registry and ambiguous lexical aliases before a full
    scoring run. Preserve the existing audit and broad candidate output as a baseline.
    Evidence lives in `data/research/experiments/article-labels/cpu-audit/`.
    
    The legacy registry pools names across years and chooses an alphabetically first
    display name: a 2021 American Airlines match can identify Alpha Metallurgical
    Resources. Generic aliases such as `PRICE`, `NEW`, `People`, `NEWS` and `TARGET`
    generate millions of overlapping candidates. The legacy cased-name proxy and
    unverified publisher ticker annotations also admit false matches.
    
    ## Acceptance
    
    - [x] Resolve names, identifiers and memberships for the article date; preserve unresolved links.
    - [ ] Define evidence-based restrictions for generic aliases and unverified publisher signals.
    - [ ] Compare corrected retrieval with the frozen retained and no-hit audit samples.
    - [ ] Measure candidate reduction and missed-company risk before scheduling full scoring.
    
    The completed correction preserves all 12,241,870 retained source records and
    38,053,717 candidate links. It aligns resolved names and tickers with verified
    dated CIKs, retains original values and explicitly defers unsupported identities.
    The 1,934,894 records with title/body name evidence form a diagnostic subset;
    they do not replace the broad scoring population or establish retrieval recall.

    def _score_metrics(
        connection: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection,
        population: dict[str, JsonValue],
        scores: Path | None,
        config: ArticleLabelsConfig,
    ) -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
        benchmark: dict[str, JsonValue] = {}
        benchmark_path: Path | None = None
        if scores is not None:
            benchmark_path = next(
                (
                    scores / name
                    for name in ("benchmark.json", "summary.json", "progress.json")
                    if (scores / name).is_file()
                ),
                None,
            )
            if benchmark_path is None:
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    f"Scoring metadata missing in {scores}: expected benchmark.json, "
                    "summary.json or progress.json"
                )
            benchmark = _read_json(benchmark_path)
            progress_path = scores / "progress.json"
            if benchmark_path.name == "summary.json" and progress_path.is_file():
                progress = _read_json(progress_path)
                # Live progress replaces the prior stop; finalization writes both alike.
                # Keep each snapshot's status and timing fields together, without merging.
                if progress != benchmark:
                    benchmark_path = progress_path
                    benchmark = progress
        judgments: list[dict[str, JsonValue]] = []
        if scores is not None and (scores / "predictions.parquet").is_file():
            connection.from_parquet(str(scores / "predictions.parquet")).create_view(
                "predictions"
            )
            judgments = _query_rows(
                connection,
                "SELECT status, count(*) AS candidate_pairs, "
                "count(DISTINCT inference_id) AS inference_units "
                "FROM predictions GROUP BY status ORDER BY status",
            )
        candidate_records = population["retained_records"]
        if not isinstance(candidate_records, int):
            raise ValueError("Candidate record count must be an integer")
        measured_frame = _number(benchmark, "frame_documents")
        if measured_frame is not None and not 0 <= measured_frame <= candidate_records:
            raise ValueError("Inference frame differs from retained article records")
        population_unit = benchmark.get("frame_unit")
        if not isinstance(population_unit, str):
            population_unit = (
                "inference_units"
                if measured_frame is not None
                else "retained_source_records"
            )
        result: dict[str, JsonValue] = {
            "observed_judgments": judgments,
            "judgment_counts_scope": (
                "Observed scored subset only; no population or company-year scaling"
            ),
            "capacity": throughput_estimates(
                int(measured_frame) if measured_frame is not None else candidate_records,
                benchmark,
                now=datetime.now(UTC),
                deadline=config.deadline_utc,
                reserve_seconds=config.reserve_seconds,
            ),
            "capacity_workload_unit": population_unit,
            "capacity_workload_basis": (
                "Retained source records; benchmark samples article rows"
                if population_unit == "retained_source_records"
                else "Inference units: text, title, date, publisher and candidates"
            ),
            "benchmark": benchmark,
            "benchmark_source": benchmark_path.name if benchmark_path is not None else None,
        }
        if (
    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    set positional-arguments
    
    mod python 'src/python/justfile'
    mod latex 'src/latex/justfile'
    mod agents '.agents/justfile'
    mod inference 'infra/inference/justfile'
    workflow := "env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py"
    
    # Discover this project's commands.
    default:
        @just --list
    
    # Prepare locked dependencies and Git hooks (uses the network).
    setup:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py prepare
        just python::setup
        just latex::setup
        just agents::apply
        prek install
    
    # Check source, views and selected languages without repairing files.
    check:
        bash infra/nix/check.sh
        {{ workflow }} check
        just python::check
        just latex::check
        just data-check
        just semflow-check
        just changelog-check
        just skills-check
        just agents::check
    
    # Run the selected language tests.
    test:
        just python::test
        just latex::test
    
    # Explicitly format sources.
    fmt:
        git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard | while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do case "$file" in justfile|*/justfile|Justfile|*/Justfile|*.just) just --justfile "$file" --fmt --unstable ;; esac; done
        nixfmt devenv.nix infra/nix/devenv.nix infra/nix/pkgs/schematter.nix infra/nix/pkgs/agentsync.nix
        rumdl fmt .
        # DVC's YAML emitter can leave trailing spaces when wrapping scalar values.
        if [[ -f dvc.lock ]]; then sed -i 's/[[:blank:]]*$//' dvc.lock; fi
        just python::fmt
        just latex::fmt
    
    # Check external links online.
    links:
        git ls-files -z '*.md' | xargs -0 -r lychee --config lychee.toml --no-progress
    
    # Run root-level DVC using the locked Python environment.
    dvc *args:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen dvc "$@"
    
    # Validate DVC metadata without fetching data.
    data-check:
        just dvc status
        just dvc dag
    
    # Refresh generated planning and reference views.
    sync:
        {{ workflow }} sync
    
    # Validate document schemas, links and generated views.
    context-check:
        {{ workflow }} check
    
    # Create a plan without overwriting existing content.
    plan-new slug title:
        {{ workflow }} plan-new "$1" --title "$2"
    
    # Create a task inside an existing plan or task.
    task-new parent slug title:
        {{ workflow }} task-new "$1" "$2" --title "$3"
    
    # Create a local reference record with its directory as citation key.
    reference-new key title:
        {{ workflow }} reference-new "$1" --title "$2"
    
    # Validate the repository changelog structure and change categories.
    changelog-check:
        schematter validate --schema infra/schemas/documents/changelog.document-schema.yaml CHANGELOG.md
    
    # Check semantic fingerprints once DVC has executable stages.
    semflow-check:
        if env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen python -c 'import pathlib, sys, yaml; from semflow.config import load_config; load_config(); doc = yaml.safe_load(pathlib.Path("dvc.yaml").read_text()); sys.exit(0 if isinstance(doc, dict) and doc.get("stages") == {} else 1)'; then echo 'Semflow: no DVC stages to instrument.'; else env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow check; fi
    
    # Preview the semantic dependency changes before applying them.
    semflow-patch:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow patch
    
    # Apply reviewed DVC and semantic fingerprint changes.
    semflow-apply:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow patch --apply
    
    # Refresh existing semantic fingerprints without editing the DVC graph.
    semflow-refresh:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow refresh --apply
    
    # Validate repository-owned skill documents and their directory names.
    skills-check:
        git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard -- ':(glob)**/SKILL.md' 'SKILL.md' | while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do [[ -f "$file" ]] || continue; schematter validate --schema infra/schemas/documents/skill.document-schema.yaml "$file"; awk 'END { if (NR > 500) { print FILENAME ": exceeds 500 lines" > "/dev/stderr"; exit 1 } }' "$file"; env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen python -c 'import pathlib, re, sys, yaml; p = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); frontmatter = re.split(r"(?m)^---[ \t]*\r?$", p.read_text(), maxsplit=2)[1]; name = yaml.safe_load(frontmatter)["name"]; sys.exit(0 if name == p.parent.name else f"{p}: name {name!r} must match parent directory {p.parent.name!r}")' "$file"; done

    
    Shared agent instructions and Codex configuration are maintained in
    [`.agents/`](.agents/README.md). `just setup` applies them; use
    `just agents::preview` to preview link changes and `just agents::check` to
    verify the generated links.
    
    `just check` validates Justfile syntax and formatting alongside the other
    quality gates. Run `just fmt` to format Justfiles and other source files.
    
    For Python alone, with Python 3.13, uv and just installed:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::check
    ```
    
    ## Data and reproducibility
    
    DVC is initialized at the repository root with analytics disabled. Use:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc status
    just dvc dag
    ```
    
    Semflow tracks the executable Python dependencies of DVC stages. When adding a
    stage, run `just semflow-patch` to review its proposed fingerprints, then
    `just semflow-apply` to materialize them. Commit the generated
    `.semflow/hashes/` files with the DVC definition. After semantic source changes,
    run `just semflow-refresh`; `just semflow-check` detects stale fingerprints.
    The frozen [Fine News acquisition stage](data/inputs/fine-news/README.md) retains
    the published staging snapshot and its historical selection recipe. DVC verifies
    the restored output during reproduction. The
    [source comparison](data/inputs/source-comparison/README.md) prepares small
    probability samples using Parquet metadata before acquiring article payloads.
    Keep data, configuration and environment dependencies explicit in DVC: Semflow's
    static analysis cannot discover string-driven dynamic imports.
    
    See [Python commands](src/python/README.md), [LaTeX commands](src/latex/README.md)
    and [infrastructure](infra/README.md). The scaffold's Apache-2.0 license covers
    code; it does not grant rights to upstream article content.
    # Article labels and research filters
    
    This experiment separates company retrieval, dated issuer identity and model
    judgments about article coverage. Its source is the restored
    [Fine News snapshot](../fine-news/README.md). The historical 115-domain allowlist
    is an acquisition policy; it has not been reviewed as a trusted-publisher list.
    All model labels remain provisional pending human evaluation.
    
    ## Source and CPU evidence
    
    The adopted Rust Aho–Corasick run covers the same 168 source files. Source and
    prediction checksums are verified before adoption. The compact CPU index retains
    12,241,870 of 14,807,287 source records and accounts separately for every exclusion.
    Article keys use relative source paths and physical row numbers. Native article
    IDs are preserved but are not assumed unique.
    
    Text remains in the raw snapshot. Indexes store coordinates, text hashes,
    candidates and matching evidence. Exact-text groups retain every source membership;
    they do not establish complete syndicated-story deduplication. A literal name or
    publisher keyword match establishes a retrieval candidate, not company relevance.
    
    The independent [CPU audit](../../research/experiments/article-labels/cpu-audit/report.md)
    confirmed correct stored offsets but found generic aliases, footer mentions,
    non-financial publisher tags and a cross-year issuer-name defect. The review is
    qualitative AI evidence, not human gold or measured population precision/recall.
    Its retained and no-hit source samples, observations and checksums are preserved.
    
    ## Dated candidate correction
    
    `correct_article_candidates` preserves every broad candidate and source record.
    It uses a unique verified article-year issuer link to resolve Top1000 names,
    tickers and CIKs together. Ambiguous or unsupported links remain unresolved;
    scoring never substitutes the original, potentially wrong company name.
    
    The corrected index records original values, authority identifiers, supported
    aliases, lexical ambiguity and evidence tiers. The SEC snapshot contains 190
    cached submissions records. Current registry names are not certified historical
    names, and SEC former-name filing dates are not guaranteed validity intervals.
    Undated GH identities retain their limitation. Publisher tags and legacy ticker
    spans remain unverified retrieval evidence.
    
    Title/body evidence tiers are retrieval diagnostics. They do not classify primary
    coverage or remove candidates from the scoring population. Capped stored spans
    remain censored evidence rather than proof that other mentions are absent.
    
    ## Fixed pilot
    
    The pilot selects 1,000 retained source records by the smallest
    `SHA256(seed:article_id)` values before loading bodies or requesting predictions.
    Duplicate source copies remain in this sampling frame. `selection.parquet`
    preserves the sample; it cannot establish missed-company recall from survivors.
    
    The frozen initial pilot lives in
    `data/processed/experiments/article-labels/benchmark-1000/`. It scored 993 records,
    deferred seven beyond 8,192 tokens and had no server failures. Its original rubric
    accepted no pairs at 0.95. Exact scorer, reporter, parameters and runtime assets
    are archived alongside DVC pointers; frozen stages preserve that baseline.
    
    Verify the completed corrected pilot and its report with:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc repro benchmark_company_labels
    just dvc repro report_company_benchmark
    ```
    
    Outputs use `benchmark-corrected-1000/` beneath the processed and research
    experiment directories. `benchmark.json` records counts and measured throughput;
    `decisions.jsonl` and `predictions.parquet` preserve the small pilot's predictions.
    Fresh source-only audit labels are sealed before model outputs are inspected.
    Neither synthetic examples nor AI agreement establish human-validated accuracy.
    Both completed pilots are frozen. A new experiment requires its own output path
    and an unfrozen stage, preserving the existing manifests and implementation hashes.
    
    The corrected pilot scored 993 records and deferred seven by context length.
    One transient timeout succeeded on resume. At the fixed cutoff, 24 candidate
    pairs across 21 records were provisionally accepted; 105 pairs had unresolved
    identities. The cumulative clock includes an unusual stall and sparse source
    reads. Its conditional linear runtime projection is not a reliable dense-corpus
    completion date. `row_groups_read` and `last_source` describe the latest
    invocation; completion counts and elapsed time accumulate across resumes.
    
    The [accepted-pair source review](../../research/experiments/article-labels/accepted-pilot-audit/report.md)
    examines all 24 accepted links against the 21 original articles. It found developed
    company coverage, including a syndicated issuer release and a promotional roundup
    that require separate source-format treatment. This AI-assisted, post-selection
    review does not measure population precision or missed-company recall.
    
    The [context audit](../../research/experiments/article-labels/context-audit/report.md)
    records the seven deferred transcripts and their verified source evidence. Raising
    the admission limit alone would not establish reliable long-document predictions.
    
    ## Company decisions
    
    The selected rubric asks three binary questions per resolved company, using its
    canonical name and tickers: whether the article mentions it, provides meaningful
    company-specific information beyond a mention, and treats it as a main subject.
    Several companies may be primary. The manifest records the exact question
    templates and article-kind criteria. The current runtime is Kev-4B in BF16.
    Production uses the separate `kev-4b-low-memory.json` profile. It retains the
    same model and 8,192-token admission while reducing GPU graph buffers. A fixed
    16-request parity check preserved all tested 0.5 and 0.95 threshold decisions;
    the original corrected pilot retains its original runtime profile.
    
    `identity_score`, `substantive_score` and `raw_primary_score` preserve independent
    model outputs. `coverage_score` is their substantive/primary maximum: a ranking
    rule rather than a calibrated union probability. Contradictory marginals retain
    consistency flags. `primary_score` is available only after identity meets the
    configured cutoff. A provisional accepted pair requires confident identity and
    coverage without a strong coverage contradiction. Article kind does not gate it.
    Saved outputs support later threshold comparisons without rerunning inference.
    
    ## Native inference and checkpoints
    
    [Native Kev](../../../infra/inference/README.md) runs in a separate pinned GPU
    runtime. Pydantic's System One client shares each article across company questions
    in one request. Exact repeated company descriptors share questions while retaining
    all namespace-specific links. Large candidate sets use bounded requests.
    Article kind is an annotation, rather than an automatic editorial-content gate.
    
    The runtime profile records model revisions, checkpoint hashes, precision,
    kernels and context admission. Oversized documents are explicitly deferred;
    silent text truncation is disabled. Prediction manifests preserve the scorer and
    runtime contract. A changed scientific contract requires a new output directory.
    Operational deadlines, transport timeouts and concurrency can change on resume.
    Pass `--source data/raw/fine-news` to override archived absolute source locations.
    
    ```bash
    just dvc repro score_company_labels
    ```
    
    Production stores compressed source-record Parquet chunks and a small SQLite
    resume ledger in `data/processed/experiments/article-labels/corpus/`. It preserves
    source metadata, candidate provenance and raw model outputs. Successful identical
    requests can be reused; transient server failures are retried on resume. Context
    failures, unresolved identities and pending records stay separate from negatives.
    `progress.json` reports counts and `storage.json` gives a conditional disk estimate.
    
    The first production attempt stopped after 1,598 records because temporary JSON
    payloads left sparse SQLite pages after export. That attempt and its implementation
    are preserved under `corpus-pre-storage-fix/` and the scorer archive. Production
    checkpoints now replace exported request payloads with compact lookup records in
    one transaction; the disk estimate still accounts for allocated pages.
    
    An incomplete, storage-limited or deadline-limited run exits unsuccessfully after
    saving checkpoints. DVC therefore does not proceed automatically to its report.
    To inspect a partial run, invoke the reporting command directly:
    
    ```bash
    env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV \
      uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline \
      pipeline stages research report-article-labels \
      --cpu data/processed/experiments/article-labels/cpu \
      --census data/research/experiments/article-labels/cpu \
      --scores data/processed/experiments/article-labels/corpus \
      --output data/research/experiments/article-labels/corpus-progress
    ```
    
    Choose a new output directory for each snapshot; reporting refuses to overwrite
    an existing report. The DVC-owned `corpus/` report is reserved for a completed run.
    
    Reports distinguish source records, candidate pairs, scored coverage and pending
    work. They provide CSV and LaTeX tables without projecting accepted model labels
    as validated population coverage. The 0.95 cutoff is a provisional selection rule,
    not an empirical accuracy guarantee. Parameters and the operating deadline live
    under `experiments.article_labels` in `params.yaml`; measured end-to-end capacity
    must support any claim that full scoring will finish before that deadline.
    
    Production reports add `observed_company_year.csv` and `observed_cohorts.csv`.
    The existing `company_year.csv` and `cohorts.csv` retain CPU candidate counts.
    Observed panels count stored accepted selections; substantive and primary counts
    add the respective score cutoff. Independent scores need not produce nested
    counts. Source copies and exact-text documents remain separate, with explicit
    pending, review and unscorable records. Unrostered namespaces and unknown years
    retain NULL candidate denominators and do not enter membership cohorts. These
    are provisional selections in committed checkpoints, without population scaling
    or validated usable-article claims.

    type: changelog
    description: Changes to CCFinance data engineering, research workflows and repository tooling.
    ---
    
    # CHANGELOG
    
    ## Unreleased
    
    ### Added
    
    - Corpus-wide company candidates with dated issuer corrections, source-only
      audits, provisional native Kev judgments, resumable checkpoints and observed
      company-year coverage reports.
    - Source-comparison DVC stages with metadata preparation, selective Parquet reads
      and exploratory estimates of publisher-filter yield.
    - Statsmodels LaTeX summaries and individual yield and population tables for papers.
    - Frozen Fine News acquisition recipe with the historical publisher filter.
    - Python and LaTeX toolchains generated from Exordio, with locked dependencies.
    - Typer `pipeline` application and a namespace for data processing stages.
    - DVC repository configuration and a workspace for research data.
    - Ruff, strict Pyrefly, Tach, tests and package builds in local checks and CI.
    - Planning and local reference workflows with Schematter validation and Insitu views.
    - A validated changelog with a closed set of change categories.
    - Semflow integration for reviewing and checking semantic DVC fingerprints.
    - pytest-layout-enforcer for source-aligned test paths.
    - Justfile formatting and analysis checks in pre-commit and CI.
    - Agent skill schema and validation for metadata, structure and length.
    - AgentSync-managed shared instructions, skills and Codex configuration.
    
    ### Changed
    
    - Restored the published Fine News shards with verified checksums and provenance
      so the frozen acquisition stage has real outputs for DVC to validate.
    - Grouped experiments within each data layer and consolidated source mappings
      and validated artifact contracts across sampling and research reports.
    - Organized the pipeline into `raw`, `processed` and `research` layers, with
      matching Python modules, CLI groups and proposed data paths.

    @pytest.mark.integration
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("progress_mtime_ns", [1_000_000_000, 0])
    def test_resumed_progress_replaces_stale_summary_until_deadline_finalization(
        tmp_path: Path,
        progress_mtime_ns: int,
    ) -> None:
        # Arrange: a resumed batch advances the clock and counters after an earlier stop.
        cpu, params = _cpu_fixture(tmp_path)
        census = tmp_path / "census"
        report_article_labels(cpu, census, params=params)
        scores = tmp_path / "scores"
        scores.mkdir()
        summary_path = scores / "summary.json"
        progress_path = scores / "progress.json"
        stale_summary = {
            "requested": 215,
            "frame_documents": 215,
            "frame_unit": "retained_source_records",
            "attempted": 2,
            "completed": 2,
            "context_deferred": 0,
            "unattempted": 213,
            "status": "storage_limited",
            "elapsed_seconds": 104,
            "frame_preparation_seconds": 100,
            "throughput_completed": 2,
            "throughput_elapsed_seconds": 4,
        }
        progress = {
            "requested": 215,
            "attempted": 5,
            "completed": 4,
            "context_deferred": 1,
            "unattempted": 210,
            "elapsed_seconds": 6,
        }
        summary_path.write_text(json.dumps(stale_summary))
        progress_path.write_text(json.dumps(progress))
        os.utime(summary_path, ns=(1_000_000_000, 1_000_000_000))
        os.utime(progress_path, ns=(progress_mtime_ns, progress_mtime_ns))
        active = tmp_path / "active"
    
        # Act: report the resumed run while its terminal summary still describes a stop.
        report_article_labels(cpu, active, scores=scores, params=params, census=census)
    
        # Assert: fresh counters and the active clock replace stale status and throughput.
        metrics = json.loads((active / "metrics.json").read_text())
        assert metrics["benchmark_source"] == "progress.json"
        assert metrics["benchmark"] == progress
        assert metrics["capacity"]["completed_inference_units"] == 4
        assert metrics["capacity"]["remaining_inference_units"] == 211
        assert metrics["capacity"]["observed_inference_units_per_second"] == pytest.approx(
            4 / 6
        )
        assert metrics["capacity"]["measured_frame_preparation_seconds"] is None
        assert "active scoring-loop" in metrics["capacity"]["basis"]
    
        # Arrange: the writer finalizes both files with identical rich deadline metadata.
        final_summary = (
            stale_summary
            | progress

                "status": "deadline_reached",

                "throughput_completed": 4,
                "throughput_elapsed_seconds": 6,

        summary_path.write_text(json.dumps(final_summary))

        assert final_metrics["capacity"]["measured_frame_preparation_seconds"] == 100

        # Arrange: only the complete terminal progress snapshot remains available.
        summary_path.unlink()
        progress_only = tmp_path / "progress-only"
    
        # Act: report terminal progress without inventing a live scoring invocation.
        report_article_labels(
            cpu, progress_only, scores=scores, params=params, census=census
        )
    
        # Assert: progress-only fallback preserves terminal metadata and throughput basis.
        progress_metrics = json.loads((progress_only / "metrics.json").read_text())
        assert progress_metrics["benchmark_source"] == "progress.json"
        assert progress_metrics["benchmark"] == final_summary
        assert progress_metrics["capacity"]["basis"] == final_metrics["capacity"]["basis"]

    # Complete corpus article tags and company scores
    
    ## Goal
    
    Complete the full corpus labeling objective following the fixed 1,000-record
    pilot. Preserve all qualifying articles and company links; diagnostic evidence
    tiers and runtime limits must not silently redefine the dataset population.
    The recorded working deadline is 07:00 SAST on 17 November 2026, pending
    clarification of the goal text's October date.
    
    The candidate agent corrects dated identities and lexical evidence. The runtime
    agent evaluates decision questions and bounded GPU batching. The scoring agent
    owns portable, resumable production execution. The coordinator owns DVC,
    reconciliation, quality gates and delivery.
    
    ## Acceptance
    
    - [x] Correct and reconcile candidate identities across the complete source population.
    - [x] Evaluate native decisions against preserved examples and independent audit cases.
    - [ ] Materialize article tags and company scores for the full qualifying population.
    - [ ] Preserve source memberships, unresolved evidence and explicit processing failures.
    - [ ] Verify completion counts, provenance, reproducibility and repository quality gates.
    
    The corrected fixed pilot processed 1,000 records: 993 scored, seven deferred by
    the context limit, and one transient timeout recovered on resume. Its 3,137
    candidate pairs include 24 provisional accepted pairs across 21 articles and
    105 unresolved identities. These outcomes are model suggestions, not validated
    research labels. Local inference remains far below the throughput required for
    the complete 12.24-million-record population by the working deadline.
    
    The [accepted-pair source review](../../../../../data/research/experiments/article-labels/accepted-pilot-audit/report.md)
    found developed company coverage in all 24 links, with separate editorial-format
    questions. It is an AI-assisted, post-selection check without validated precision
    or recall. The initial full-run checkpoint preserved 1,598 source records and
    4,024 candidate links without metadata loss; its sparse-index storage defect and
    original implementation are archived before restarting production.
    
    Observed company-year and consecutive-year panels now distinguish committed
    model selections from CPU candidates, pending records and unscorable links.
    The [context audit](../../../../../data/research/experiments/article-labels/context-audit/report.md)
    preserves the seven deferred transcripts and the model's documented length
    limits. These reports do not complete the unprocessed population or establish
    human-validated research quality.

    def report_article_labels(
        cpu: Annotated[Path, typer.Option(help="Completed CPU index and provenance.")],
        output: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="New directory for coverage and capacity reports.")
        ],
        scores: Annotated[
            Path | None,
            typer.Option(help="Optional Kev benchmark or active scoring checkpoint."),
        ] = None,
        params: Annotated[Path, typer.Option()] = Path("params.yaml"),
        census: Annotated[
            Path | None,
            typer.Option(
                help="Reuse a completed CPU report without rescanning its indices."
            ),
        ] = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Summarize observed candidates and a conditional processing deadline."""
        config = load_config(params)
        if output.exists():
            raise FileExistsError(f"Output exists: {output}")
        output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if census is not None:
            _reuse_census(cpu, census, output, scores, config)
            typer.echo(f"Wrote provisional article-label coverage: {output}")
            return
        manifest = _read_json(cpu / "manifest.json")
        retained = sorted(cpu.glob("shards/*/retained.parquet"))
        excluded = sorted(cpu.glob("shards/*/excluded.parquet"))
        if not retained or not excluded:
            raise ValueError("CPU indices require retained and excluded Parquet artifacts")
        with (
            duckdb.connect(config={"memory_limit": "4GB", "threads": 1}) as connection,
            TemporaryDirectory(dir=output.parent) as temporary,
        ):
            staging = Path(temporary) / "report"
            staging.mkdir()
            connection.execute("SET max_temp_directory_size = '8GB'")
            connection.execute("SET preserve_insertion_order = false")
            connection.from_parquet(
                    "frame_documents": frame_count,
                    "frame_records": frame_count,
                    "frame_unit": "retained_source_records",
                    "selection": (
                        "deterministic SHA256 priority sample of retained source rows"
                        if benchmark
                        else "all retained source rows in source order"
                    ),
                    "seed": config.seed,
                    "row_groups_read": reader.groups_read,
                    "contract_sha256": fingerprint,
                    "decision_attempts": int(
                        store.db.execute("SELECT attempts FROM clock").fetchone()[0]
                    ),
                    "unique_scored_inference_units": int(
                        store.db.execute(
                            "SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE status='complete'"
                        ).fetchone()[0]
                    ),
                    "estimated_full_seconds": preparation_seconds
                    + frame_count * elapsed / completed
                    if completed
                    else None,
                    "completion_requires_context_policy": counts["context_deferred"] > 0,
                }
                _write_json(
                    output / ("benchmark.json" if benchmark else "summary.json"), report
                )
                _write_json(output / "progress.json", report)
                if benchmark:
                    _export(store, output)
                if not finished:
                    raise RuntimeError(
                        f"Scoring {report['status']}: {completed}/{requested} "
                        "source records "
                        "scored; checkpoints preserved"
                    )
        finally:
            store.close()
    
    
    def benchmark_article_labels(
        input: Annotated[Path, typer.Option(help="Completed compact CPU article index.")],
        output: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="Resumable benchmark decisions and measured rate.")
        ],
        params: Annotated[
            Path, typer.Option(help="Versioned experiment parameters.")
        ] = Path("params.yaml"),
        source: Annotated[
            Path | None,
            typer.Option(help="Original article Parquet root; overrides the CPU manifest."),
        ] = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Measure end-to-end scoring on the configured probability sample."""
        asyncio.run(_run(input, output, params, benchmark=True, source=source))

    def _write_json(path: Path, value: object) -> None:
        temporary = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")
        temporary.write_text(_json(value) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        temporary.replace(path)
    
    
    def _descriptor(candidate: dict[str, JsonValue]) -> str | None:
        """Use the resolved canonical name; preserve unsupported aliases as provenance."""
        name = candidate.get("name")
        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip():
            return None
        tickers = candidate.get("tickers")
        if not isinstance(tickers, list) or not tickers:
            tickers = [candidate.get("ticker")]
        symbols = [symbol for symbol in tickers if isinstance(symbol, str) and symbol]
        return name + (" (" + ", ".join(symbols) + ")" if symbols else "")
    
    
    def _question_sources(candidates: list[dict[str, JsonValue]]) -> dict[int, int]:
        """Share exact rendered questions while retaining every candidate namespace."""
        first: dict[str, int] = {}
        return {
            index: first.setdefault(descriptor, index)
            for index, candidate in enumerate(candidates)
            if (descriptor := _descriptor(candidate)) is not None
        }
    
    
    def build_questions(
        candidates: list[dict[str, JsonValue]],
    ) -> dict[str, DecisionQuestion]:
        """Ask three independent binary questions with article kind as annotation."""
        questions: dict[str, DecisionQuestion] = {
            "article_kind": ChoiceQuestion(
                instructions={
                    "question": "What kind of published material is this article?"
                },
                criteria=ARTICLE_CRITERIA,
            )
        }
        for index in sorted(set(_question_sources(candidates).values())):
            company = _descriptor(candidates[index])
            for dimension, instruction in COMPANY_QUESTIONS.items():
                questions[f"c{index}.{dimension}"] = NoulQuestion(
                    instructions=instruction.format(company=company)
                )
        return questions

    async def _score(
        article: Article, text: str, config: ArticleLabelsConfig, model: SystemOneModel
    ) -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
        state: JsonValue = {
            "title": article.title,
            "published_at": article.publish_date,
            "publisher": article.hostname,
            "article": text,
        }
        candidates = {str(item["issuer_id"]): item for item in article.candidates}
        unique = list(candidates.values())
        sources = _question_sources(unique)
        representatives = [
            candidate
            for index, candidate in enumerate(unique)
            if sources.get(index, index) == index
        ]
        rows: dict[str, dict[str, JsonValue]] = {}
        responses: list[JsonValue] = []
        request_hashes: list[JsonValue] = []
        input_tokens = 0
        started = time.monotonic()
        for offset in range(0, len(representatives), config.max_candidates_per_request):
            batch = representatives[offset : offset + config.max_candidates_per_request]
            questions = build_questions(batch)
            request = DecisionRequest(state=state, questions=questions)
            # The request identity includes every native structured question and its rubric.
            request_hashes.append(
                hashlib.sha256(_json(asdict(request)).encode()).hexdigest()
            )
            response = await model.decide(
                request, model_settings={"timeout": config.request_timeout_seconds}
            )
            responses.append(json.loads(_json(asdict(response))))
            typed: dict[str, DecisionAnswer] = {}
            for name, answer in response.answers.items():
                if not isinstance(answer, NoulAnswer | ChoiceAnswer):
                    raise ValueError(f"Unexpected answer kind: {name}")
                typed[name] = answer
            for row in interpret_answers(batch, typed, config.min_probability):
                rows[str(row["issuer_id"])] = row
            input_tokens += response.usage.input_tokens
        return {
            "status": "complete",
            "companies": [
                rows[str(unique[sources.get(index, index)]["issuer_id"])]
                | {"issuer_id": candidate["issuer_id"]}
                for index, candidate in enumerate(unique)
            ],
            "request_sha256": request_hashes,
            "responses": responses,
            "input_tokens": input_tokens,
            "elapsed_seconds": time.monotonic() - started,
            "model_name": config.api_model,
        }
    
    
    class _Store:
        """Keep request identities in SQLite and bounded production payloads in Parquet."""

        question: OPT_NONE for state/instruction, 0..K-1 for option spans, OPT_DECIDE for <decide>).
    
        option_isolation=True: every option span is its own sub-branch (it sees state + instruction + itself only), all
        option spans share the same position ids, and <decide> sits at one fixed position after the longest span. Then the
        per-option representations and <decide>'s attention over them are permutation-invariant by construction.
    
        Not strict, a state over max_state tokens is cut to its first max_state (state_truncated; state_tokens is the whole
        state's count, the <state> token included, as the limit counts it). Strict, it raises ContextOverflow.
        """

        S = [tok.convert_tokens_to_ids(SPECIAL[0])] + state_tokens[: max_state - 1]
        ids, seg, pos, opt = list(S), [0] * len(S), list(range(len(S))), [OPT_NONE] * len(S)
        q_id, o_id, c_id, d_id = (tok.convert_tokens_to_ids(t) for t in SPECIAL[1:])

            instr = [q_id] + user_tokens(tok, q["instr"])
            spans = [[o_id] + user_tokens(tok, o) + [c_id] for o in q["options"]]
            br = instr + [t for sp in spans for t in sp] + [d_id]
            if len(br) > max_branch - len(S):
                raise ContextOverflow(f"branch too long: {len(br)} tokens with a {len(S)}-token state (row limit {max_branch})")
            base = len(ids); p0 = len(S)
            br_opt = [OPT_NONE] * len(instr) + [j for j, sp in enumerate(spans) for _ in sp] + [OPT_DECIDE]
            if option_isolation:
                longest = max(len(sp) for sp in spans)
                br_pos = list(range(p0, p0 + len(instr))) + [p0 + len(instr) + i for sp in spans for i in range(len(sp))] + [p0 + len(instr) + longest]
            else:
                br_pos = list(range(p0, p0 + len(br)))
            ends, cursor = [], len(instr)
            for sp in spans:
                cursor += len(sp); ends.append(cursor - 1)
            ids += br; seg += [k] * len(br); pos += br_pos; opt += br_opt
            decide_idx.append(base + len(br) - 1); opt_idx.append([base + e for e in ends])

    def admit(model, tok, rec, truncate=False):
        def _run(self, encs):
            """One batch through model.probs_batch, with the prefix cache. -> per request (probs, stats). A pass out of device
            memory while states are cached drops the cache and runs once more: the cache only saves time, and kept resident
            it failed every later batch of that size (#75, @vtxyer)."""
            sync(self.device); t = time.time()
            for retry in (False, True):
                keys, cached, keep = self.prefix_cache.plan(encs)
                self.prefix_cache.make_room(keys, cached, keep)
                try: ps, prefixes = self.model.probs_batch(encs, cached, keep); break
                except Exception as e:   # states held: the cache's, and this batch's hits make_room already dropped from it
                    held = self.prefix_cache.entries or any(c is not None for c in cached)
                    if retry or not held or not out_of_memory(e): raise
                cached = None; self.prefix_cache.clear(); self.prefix_cache.oom_retries += 1   # after the except: its traceback holds the failed pass's tensors
                empty_cache(self.device)
            sync(self.device); dt = round((time.time() - t) * 1000, 1)
            self.prefix_cache.store(keys, cached, prefixes)
            self.batches += 1; self.batched_requests += len(encs)
            return [([q.tolist() for q in p], {"tokens": len(enc["ids"]), "state_tokens": enc["state_tokens"], "state_tokens_used": enc["seg"].count(0),
                                               "latency_ms": dt, "prefix_cache_hit": c is not None})   # state_tokens: the request's state; _used: what the model read (less only when truncated)
                    for enc, p, c in zip(encs, ps, cached)]
    
        def wait_idle(self):
            """Block until every submitted request is answered and no CUDA graph waits to be captured (benchmarks, warm-up)."""
            self.queue.join()
    # Article labels and research filters
    
    This experiment separates company retrieval, dated issuer identity and model
    judgments about article coverage. Its source is the restored
    [Fine News snapshot](../fine-news/README.md). The historical 115-domain allowlist
    is an acquisition policy; it has not been reviewed as a trusted-publisher list.
    All model labels remain provisional pending human evaluation.
    
    ## Source and CPU evidence
    
    The adopted Rust Aho–Corasick run covers the same 168 source files. Source and
    prediction checksums are verified before adoption. The compact CPU index retains
    12,241,870 of 14,807,287 source records and accounts separately for every exclusion.
    Article keys use relative source paths and physical row numbers. Native article
    IDs are preserved but are not assumed unique.
    
    Text remains in the raw snapshot. Indexes store coordinates, text hashes,
    candidates and matching evidence. Exact-text groups retain every source membership;
    they do not establish complete syndicated-story deduplication. A literal name or
    publisher keyword match establishes a retrieval candidate, not company relevance.
    
    The independent [CPU audit](../../research/experiments/article-labels/cpu-audit/report.md)
    confirmed correct stored offsets but found generic aliases, footer mentions,
    non-financial publisher tags and a cross-year issuer-name defect. The review is
    qualitative AI evidence, not human gold or measured population precision/recall.
    Its retained and no-hit source samples, observations and checksums are preserved.
    
    ## Dated candidate correction
    
    `correct_article_candidates` preserves every broad candidate and source record.
    It uses a unique verified article-year issuer link to resolve Top1000 names,
    tickers and CIKs together. Ambiguous or unsupported links remain unresolved;
    scoring never substitutes the original, potentially wrong company name.
    
    The corrected index records original values, authority identifiers, supported
    aliases, lexical ambiguity and evidence tiers. The SEC snapshot contains 190
    cached submissions records. Current registry names are not certified historical
    names, and SEC former-name filing dates are not guaranteed validity intervals.
    Undated GH identities retain their limitation. Publisher tags and legacy ticker
    spans remain unverified retrieval evidence.
    
    Title/body evidence tiers are retrieval diagnostics. They do not classify primary
    coverage or remove candidates from the scoring population. Capped stored spans
    remain censored evidence rather than proof that other mentions are absent.
    
    ## Fixed pilot
    
    The pilot selects 1,000 retained source records by the smallest
    `SHA256(seed:article_id)` values before loading bodies or requesting predictions.
    Duplicate source copies remain in this sampling frame. `selection.parquet`

## Assistant

I’d budget **about 15 billion input tokens** to score the 12.24 million articles retained by the CPU filter, assuming we send each article once with all its retrieved companies.

That estimate comes from the saved 1,000-article pilot:

- The 993 articles Kev scored used **1,169,880 input tokens**, including the article text and decision questions.
- The seven deferred transcripts contained another **79,086 state tokens**; their unanswered questions are extra.
- Together, that is approximately **1,249 tokens per article**, or **15.3 billion** across the retained population.

The pilot’s sampling variation suggests roughly **14.5–16.2 billion** tokens, before allowing for differences in the OpenRouter model’s tokenizer, system prompt and output schema. It excludes the 2.57 million articles the CPU filter did not retain. If we reuse the 93,431 completed scores, approximately **15.2 billion** input tokens remain by the same estimate.

The main design choice is to assess **all candidates for an article in one request**. Sending the article again for every company would substantially increase the total. [OpenRouter prompt caching](https://openrouter.ai/blog/tutorials/prompt-caching-sticky-routing/) can reduce charges for repeated prefixes on supported providers, but cached and uncached tokens need to be budgeted separately.

This estimates **input only**. A generative model’s output tokens, and whether its scores are comparable with Kev’s decision scores, would need a separate pilot.

    # Article labels and research filters
    
    This experiment separates company retrieval, dated issuer identity and model
    judgments about article coverage. Its source is the restored
    [Fine News snapshot](../fine-news/README.md). The historical 115-domain allowlist
    is an acquisition policy; it has not been reviewed as a trusted-publisher list.
    All model labels remain provisional pending human evaluation.
    
    ## Source and CPU evidence
    
    The adopted Rust Aho–Corasick run covers the same 168 source files. Source and
    prediction checksums are verified before adoption. The compact CPU index retains
    12,241,870 of 14,807,287 source records and accounts separately for every exclusion.
    Article keys use relative source paths and physical row numbers. Native article
    IDs are preserved but are not assumed unique.
    
    Text remains in the raw snapshot. Indexes store coordinates, text hashes,
    candidates and matching evidence. Exact-text groups retain every source membership;
    they do not establish complete syndicated-story deduplication. A literal name or
    publisher keyword match establishes a retrieval candidate, not company relevance.
    
    The independent [CPU audit](../../research/experiments/article-labels/cpu-audit/report.md)
    confirmed correct stored offsets but found generic aliases, footer mentions,
    non-financial publisher tags and a cross-year issuer-name defect. The review is
    qualitative AI evidence, not human gold or measured population precision/recall.
    Its retained and no-hit source samples, observations and checksums are preserved.
    
    ## Dated candidate correction
    
    `correct_article_candidates` preserves every broad candidate and source record.
    It uses a unique verified article-year issuer link to resolve Top1000 names,
    tickers and CIKs together. Ambiguous or unsupported links remain unresolved;
    scoring never substitutes the original, potentially wrong company name.
    
    The corrected index records original values, authority identifiers, supported
    aliases, lexical ambiguity and evidence tiers. The SEC snapshot contains 190
    cached submissions records. Current registry names are not certified historical
    names, and SEC former-name filing dates are not guaranteed validity intervals.
    Undated GH identities retain their limitation. Publisher tags and legacy ticker
    spans remain unverified retrieval evidence.
    
    Title/body evidence tiers are retrieval diagnostics. They do not classify primary
    coverage or remove candidates from the scoring population. Capped stored spans
    remain censored evidence rather than proof that other mentions are absent.
    
    ## Fixed pilot
    
    The pilot selects 1,000 retained source records by the smallest
    `SHA256(seed:article_id)` values before loading bodies or requesting predictions.
    Duplicate source copies remain in this sampling frame. `selection.parquet`
    preserves the sample; it cannot establish missed-company recall from survivors.
    
    The frozen initial pilot lives in
    `data/processed/experiments/article-labels/benchmark-1000/`. It scored 993 records,
    deferred seven beyond 8,192 tokens and had no server failures. Its original rubric
    accepted no pairs at 0.95. Exact scorer, reporter, parameters and runtime assets
    are archived alongside DVC pointers; frozen stages preserve that baseline.
    
    Verify the completed corrected pilot and its report with:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc repro benchmark_company_labels
    just dvc repro report_company_benchmark
    ```
    
    Outputs use `benchmark-corrected-1000/` beneath the processed and research
    experiment directories. `benchmark.json` records counts and measured throughput;
    `decisions.jsonl` and `predictions.parquet` preserve the small pilot's predictions.
    Fresh source-only audit labels are sealed before model outputs are inspected.
    Neither synthetic examples nor AI agreement establish human-validated accuracy.
    Both completed pilots are frozen. A new experiment requires its own output path
    and an unfrozen stage, preserving the existing manifests and implementation hashes.
    
    The corrected pilot scored 993 records and deferred seven by context length.
    One transient timeout succeeded on resume. At the fixed cutoff, 24 candidate
    pairs across 21 records were provisionally accepted; 105 pairs had unresolved
    identities. The cumulative clock includes an unusual stall and sparse source
    reads. Its conditional linear runtime projection is not a reliable dense-corpus
    completion date. `row_groups_read` and `last_source` describe the latest
