## Plan

# Benchmark local GLiNER2.5 for full-corpus extraction

## Summary

Stop the idle `ccfinance-kev-native` container and benchmark rich extraction on the RTX 5060 Ti. The Kev scoring process has already stopped; its checkpoint must remain intact.

The workload is all **12,241,870 retained source records**, with company spans, mention-level roles and article type extracted from the full text. Meeting 24 hours requires at least **141.7 completed articles/second end to end**, including reading, chunking, decoding and writing.

## Implementation

- Create a small, reproducible benchmark using `gliner2==2.1.0` and pinned Hugging Face revisions for **GLiNER2.5 small (74M)** and **base (194M)**. Keep its GPU dependencies isolated from the existing pipeline runtime.
- Use a single schema per article to extract company spans and mention-level `primary`, `secondary`, `incidental` or `uncertain` roles, plus article type. Preserve character offsets, scores and unmatched company spans; reuse the existing dated candidate evidence for issuer linking.
- Preserve the existing 1,000-record pilot for quality comparison. Create a separate deterministic **10,000-record corpus-wide sample** for throughput, retaining physical source coordinates and reading records in source order after selection. Include the seven known long transcripts in a separate edge-case check.
- Process long documents with overlapping windows, initially using the library’s 384-word chunks and 64-word overlap. Record window counts, coverage and failures; never count truncated or failed articles as completed. Measure larger windows only as separately identified configurations.
- Compare, for both checkpoints:
  - Standard FP32 as the reference.
  - FP16 and BF16 with standard attention and `torch.compile`.
  - FP16 and BF16 with DisentangledFlash, **without** `torch.compile`; the library does not support combining them.
  - A single INT8 weight-only TorchAO experiment on encoder linear layers with standard attention and compilation. Record incompatibility as unsupported rather than silently falling back.
- Tune batch size on the GPU for each viable configuration. Check backend activation and compare spans, labels and scores against the FP32 reference before using its throughput result.

## Verification and reporting

- Measure end-to-end wall time for reading real Parquet, inference, decoding and writing results. Report initialization and compilation separately, then include their amortized cost in the 24-hour projection. Repeat the representative run three times and report variability, peak VRAM, articles/second, chunks/second and failure counts.
- Compare model predictions with the preserved pilot and its existing audit examples. Report mention, identity and role disagreements separately; the existing AI-assisted review is not human ground truth.
- Save the benchmark configuration, software and model hashes, sample membership, results and a concise report as versioned DVC experiment artifacts. Add only targeted tests for sample reproducibility, offset preservation, long-document coverage and failure accounting; run the repository quality gates.
- Identify the **smallest tested configuration** whose observed end-to-end rate reaches 141.7 articles/second with no unreported truncation or failures. Report quality evidence separately. If neither checkpoint reaches the target, state that the tested local configurations did not demonstrate feasibility.

## Assumptions

- The 24-hour target covers the retained 12.24M records, not the 2.57M CPU-excluded records.
- A complete result includes explicit unresolved issuer identities and per-window role evidence; an extracted mention is not automatically a verified primary-company label.
- No cloud inference, paid services, training or production corpus run is included.

## User

Implement the plan.

## Assistant

I’ll stop the idle Kev container, preserve its checkpoint, and build the local benchmark around the existing retained corpus and pilot. I’ll measure the two GLiNER2.5 checkpoints with the supported precision and attention configurations, then report whether either reaches the 24-hour target.

    # Native decision inference
    
    These scripts run the pinned native Kev server using the CUDA libraries of an
    already cached container image. SGLang is not launched. Native Kev shares the
    article prefix across its independent identity and coverage questions.
    
    From the repository root, prepare the small serving dependencies and then supply
    the existing checkpoint and Hugging Face base-model cache:
    
    ```bash
    just inference::setup
    just inference::serve /path/to/kev-4b /path/to/huggingface/hub \
        data/inputs/article-labels/kev-4b-low-memory.json
    docker logs ccfinance-kev-native
    just inference::status
    ```
    
    The versioned runtime manifest records the model, source, image, precision,
    kernels and admission limit. The entrypoint applies that limit to both the
    article and every complete article-question sequence. Oversized inputs fail
    explicitly; text truncation is disabled. Local package and compilation caches
    live under ignored `.runtime/`.
    
    The third argument selects the versioned runtime profile. Pass the selected 4B
    profile explicitly; omitting it selects the historical 0.8B baseline.
    
    The 4B profile uses BF16 and retains one article prefix. Its adapter and head
    checksums are checked before loading. The serving trial records actual memory
    use separately from the model publisher's memory estimate.
    
    To restore the pinned public 4B files with the repository's Hugging Face CLI:
    
    ```bash
    uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen hf download jaredpalmer/kev-4b \
        adapter_config.json adapter_model.safetensors head.pt \
        --revision 139fdd94f1b6a6ad80cc15e08fcb99cac885a101 \
        --local-dir .runtime/models/kev-4b
    HF_HUB_CACHE="$PWD/.runtime/hf-cache" \
        uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen hf download Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B-Base \
        --revision 1001bb4d826a52d1f399e183466143f4da7b741b \
        --include '*.json' --include '*.safetensors' \
        --include merges.txt --include vocab.json
    ```
    
    The base weights require approximately 9.3 GB of storage. Model files and caches
    stay under ignored `.runtime/`; their revisions and checkpoint checksums remain
    in the versioned profile. Setup expects the recorded container image to exist
    locally and a working NVIDIA Container Toolkit CDI device.
    
    The completed company-labeling pilot used `kev-4b.json` with three concise
    binary questions per distinct company descriptor, sharing the full article
    prefix. Its graph buffers hold four states, 16 rows and 16,384 tokens. Active
    pilot samples reached 15,654 MiB with 197 MiB free on the 16,311 MiB GPU. An
    earlier diagnostic graph capture ran out of memory and fell back to eager
    inference; the completed pilot's native graph and prefix OOM counters stayed
    zero. One client timeout was retried successfully.
    
    Production uses the separate `kev-4b-low-memory.json` profile: two graph states,
    eight rows and 8,192 graph tokens. The 8,192-token context admission, prefix
    cache, weights, precision, temperature and questions remain the same. Sixteen
    exact pilot requests, including its eight longest admitted bodies, compared 337
    probabilities: maximum difference 0.0073, mean difference 0.0001134, with no
    changes at the 0.5 or 0.95 boundaries. The differences reflect floating-point
    reassociation across smaller passes. Occupancy samples reached 14,580 MiB during
    long-body inference and 15,074 MiB after graph capture, with 777 MiB free. These
    observations describe the tested requests rather than guarantee every future
    workload's peak.
    
    `kev-0.8b.json` records a separate experimental 16k admission trial. The smaller
    model was rejected for this pilot after the same fresh source cases produced
    more false positives. The seven-case long-context study was stopped after one
    HTTP success; it does not establish 16k semantic quality. The original
    `runtime.json` remains the historical 8k baseline.
    
    Stop the server with `just inference::stop`; remove its stopped
    container with `docker rm ccfinance-kev-native` before starting a replacement.

    ---
    name: repository-workflow
    description: Use when creating or maintaining repository plans, references, tasks or their generated views.

    # Repository workflow
    
    ## Workflow
    
    Read the root README and the relevant local README before changing records.
    Use `just --list` to discover the installed workflow and language commands. Create
    records through their commands, edit canonical metadata, then run `just sync`
    when available and `just check`. Keep task parents terse and store detailed
    evidence in linked records. Verification establishes only what the actual
    command output supports; record incomplete or inconclusive checks honestly.
    # CCFinance
    
    CCFinance is a data engineering project for filtering and enriching public
    Common Crawl News (CC-News) copies for research into language in finance.
    
    ## Start
    
    Exordio supplies the Python and LaTeX toolchains, a pinned Nix environment and CI.
    Copier answers record Exordio `v0.1.1-alpha` (the documented `v0.1.0` tag was not
    available in the local source).
    
    ```bash
    bash infra/nix/install-devenv.sh
    devenv shell
    just setup
    just python::run --help
    just python::run stages list
    just check
    ```
    
    Shared agent instructions and Codex configuration are maintained in
    [`.agents/`](.agents/README.md). `just setup` applies them; use
    `just agents::preview` to preview link changes and `just agents::check` to
    verify the generated links.
    
    `just check` validates Justfile syntax and formatting alongside the other
    quality gates. Run `just fmt` to format Justfiles and other source files.
    
    For Python alone, with Python 3.13, uv and just installed:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::check
    ```
    
    ## Data and reproducibility
    
    DVC is initialized at the repository root with analytics disabled. Use:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc status
    just dvc dag
    ```
    
    Semflow tracks the executable Python dependencies of DVC stages. When adding a
    stage, run `just semflow-patch` to review its proposed fingerprints, then
    `just semflow-apply` to materialize them. Commit the generated
    `.semflow/hashes/` files with the DVC definition. After semantic source changes,
    run `just semflow-refresh`; `just semflow-check` detects stale fingerprints.
    The frozen [Fine News acquisition stage](data/inputs/fine-news/README.md) retains
    the published staging snapshot and its historical selection recipe. DVC verifies
    the restored output during reproduction. The
    [source comparison](data/inputs/source-comparison/README.md) prepares small
    probability samples using Parquet metadata before acquiring article payloads.
    Keep data, configuration and environment dependencies explicit in DVC: Semflow's
    static analysis cannot discover string-driven dynamic imports.
    
    See [Python commands](src/python/README.md), [LaTeX commands](src/latex/README.md)
    and [infrastructure](infra/README.md). The scaffold's Apache-2.0 license covers
    code; it does not grant rights to upstream article content.
    # Architecture
    
    CCFinance separates code and research artifacts. Git stores source, configuration,
    locks, provenance definitions and documentation. DVC defines data dependencies
    and tracks materialized source snapshots and experiment outputs.
    
    - `src/python/apps/pipeline` owns the CLI and data stage implementations.
    - `src/python/uv.lock` locks runtime, quality, testing, packaging and DVC tools.
    - `src/latex` owns the manuscript source and bibliography.
    - `data` holds ignored data payloads and versioned DVC pointer files.
    - `infra/nix` and `devenv.lock` own the reproducible system environment.
    
    Tach enforces module boundaries; Ruff and strict Pyrefly check Python source.
    pytest-layout-enforcer checks test file placement during collection and CI.
    Semflow fingerprints the Python code used by DVC stages, allowing DVC to
    invalidate tracked results when executable behavior changes.
    CI executes those checks, tests and builds through the same just recipes as local
    work. Setup may download dependencies; ordinary checks use cached dependencies
    and do not repair authored content. LaTeX uses a versioned Tectonic asset bundle.
    
    The Hugging Face dataset is staging, and the bucket is intended for intermediate
    and experiment artifacts. The frozen raw acquisition stage documents the
    historical selection without fetching its output. Company labels and coverage
    are provisional experiments; release validation and remote artifact transport
    remain future work. The raw comparison stages prepare
    sampling manifests from Hub listings and Parquet footers, then acquire only the
    selected row groups through the shared publisher filter. Research aggregation
    reads those artifacts without importing raw-stage modules. DVC connects these
    steps; pinned source revisions and recorded draw probabilities define the
    experiment's population and sampling design.
    
    The article-labeling experiment adopts checksum-verified CPU company candidates
    and materializes compact source-linked selections without copying article bodies.
    Native Kev runs in a separately pinned GPU environment; the pipeline communicates
    through typed System One requests. Article-company probabilities and filtering
    policies remain separate, with resumable checkpoints and explicit unresolved
    outcomes. The research layer reconciles candidate and model-scored coverage and
    reports runtime estimates without treating AI agreement as human validation.
    Completed pilots remain frozen. Full scoring uses compressed source-record
    chunks, a resumable request ledger and explicit pending counts. Separate runtime
    profiles preserve GPU memory experiments without overwriting completed evidence.
    
    Each data layer groups experimental artifacts beneath `experiments/<name>/`.
    Experimental stage code follows the same grouping under its owning layer.
    `pipeline.experiments.source_comparison` defines shared parameters and artifacts;
    Tach permits raw and research to depend on these contracts without importing one
    another. Raw publisher extraction owns one source-field registry, deriving both
    SQL projections and projected column sizes from it. DVC supplies artifact paths
    explicitly. Research uses statsmodels for survey-estimate summaries and LaTeX
    tables; it preserves the probability-sampling design.
    
    Copier answers record the source and tag for future template updates. Review
    update conflicts and preserve project-specific code and configuration. The
    upstream template is [Exordio](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/exordio).

    """Apply the recorded native serving profile before loading Kev."""
    
    import hashlib
    import json
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    
    profile = json.loads(Path(os.environ["CCFINANCE_RUNTIME_MANIFEST"]).read_text())
    for filename, key in (
        ("adapter_model.safetensors", "model_adapter_sha256"),
        ("head.pt", "model_head_sha256"),
    ):
        if key in profile:
            with (Path("/checkpoint") / filename).open("rb") as source:
                actual = hashlib.file_digest(source, "sha256").hexdigest()
            if actual != profile[key]:
                raise ValueError(f"Checkpoint checksum differs from profile: {filename}")
    os.environ.update(
        {
            "KEV_BACKEND": "torch",
            "KEV_DTYPE": {"bfloat16": "bf16", "float32": "fp32"}[profile["dtype"]],
            "KEV_ATTN": profile["attention"],
            "KEV_FUSED": str(int(profile["fused_linear_attention"])),
            "KEV_CUDA_GRAPHS": str(int(profile["cuda_graphs"])),
            "KEV_MERGE": str(int(profile["merge_adapter"])),
            "KEV_PREFIX_CACHE": str(profile["prefix_cache_states"]),
            "KEV_PREFIX_MIN_TOKENS": str(profile["prefix_cache_min_tokens"]),
            "KEV_PREFIX_MAX_TOKENS": str(profile["prefix_cache_max_tokens"]),
            "KEV_TRUNCATE_STATES": str(int(profile["truncate_states"])),
        }
    )
    
    import kev.model  # noqa: E402
    
    kev.model.SERVE_MAX_STATE = profile["max_context_tokens"]
    kev.model.SERVE_MAX_BRANCH = profile["max_context_tokens"]

        import kev.cuda_graphs
    
        allowed = {"GRAPH_STATES", "GRAPH_ROWS", "GRAPH_TOKENS"}
        if set(limits) != allowed:

        for name, value in limits.items():

                raise ValueError(f"CUDA graph buffer limit must be positive: {name}")
            setattr(kev.cuda_graphs, name, value)
    
    from kev.serve import main  # noqa: E402
    
    main()

    class _BodyReader:
        """Read and retain one bounded original row group across consecutive batches."""
    
        def __init__(self, source: Path, con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection) -> None:
            self.source = source
            self.con = con
            self.bounds: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, int]]] = {}
            self.cached_group: tuple[str, int] | None = None
            self.cached_rows: dict[int, tuple[str, str | None]] = {}
            self.groups_read = 0
    
        def read(self, articles: list[Article]) -> dict[str, "_Body"]:
            result: dict[str, _Body] = {}
            groups: dict[tuple[str, int], list[Article]] = {}
            for article in articles:
                if article.source_path not in self.bounds:
                    metadata = self.con.execute(
                        "SELECT row_group_id,max(row_group_num_rows),"
                        "sum(total_uncompressed_size) FILTER (WHERE path_in_schema='text') "
                        "FROM parquet_metadata(?) GROUP BY row_group_id "
                        "ORDER BY row_group_id",
                        [str(self.source / article.source_path)],
                    ).fetchall()
                    offset = 0
                    bounds = []
                    for _, rows, size in metadata:
                        bounds.append((offset, offset + int(rows), int(size or 0)))
                        offset += int(rows)
                    self.bounds[article.source_path] = bounds
                bounds = self.bounds[article.source_path]
                index = bisect.bisect_right([b[0] for b in bounds], article.source_row) - 1
                if index < 0 or article.source_row >= bounds[index][1]:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Source row outside original file: {article.article_id}"
                    )
                groups.setdefault((article.source_path, index), []).append(article)
            for (file, index), members in groups.items():
                lower, upper, size = self.bounds[file][index]
                if self.cached_group != (file, index):
                    if size > 128 * 1024 * 1024:
                        rows = self.con.execute(
                            "SELECT file_row_number,text,to_json(metadata) "
                            "FROM read_parquet("
                            "$file,file_row_number=true) WHERE file_row_number "
                            "IN (SELECT unnest($rows))",
                            {
                                "file": str(self.source / file),
                                "rows": [article.source_row for article in members],
                            },
                        ).fetchall()
                        self.cached_group = None
                    else:
                        rows = self.con.execute(
                            "SELECT file_row_number,text,to_json(metadata) "
                            "FROM read_parquet("
                            "$file,file_row_number=true) "
                            "WHERE file_row_number >= $lower "
                            "AND file_row_number < $upper",
                            {
                                "file": str(self.source / file),
                                "lower": lower,
                                "upper": upper,
                            },
                        ).fetchall()
                        self.cached_group = (file, index)
                    self.groups_read += 1
                    self.cached_rows = {
                        int(row): (text, metadata) for row, text, metadata in rows
                    }
                for article in members:
                    original = self.cached_rows.get(article.source_row)
                    if original is None or not isinstance(original[0], str):
                        raise ValueError(f"Original text missing for {article.article_id}")
                    text, metadata_json = original
                    if hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest() != article.text_sha256:
                        raise ValueError(f"Text checksum changed for {article.article_id}")
                    metadata = (
                        JSON_VALUE_ADAPTER.validate_json(metadata_json)
                        if metadata_json is not None
                        else None
                    )
                    result[article.article_id] = _Body(text, metadata)
            return result
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class _Body:
        text: str
        metadata: JsonValue
    
    
    def _resolve_source(
        input: Path, manifest: dict[str, JsonValue], source: Path | None
    ) -> Path:
        if source is not None:
            return source.resolve()
        value = manifest.get("source_root")
        if not isinstance(value, str):
            raise ValueError("Pass --source or provide source_root in the CPU manifest")
        path = Path(value)
        return (path if path.is_absolute() else input / path).resolve()
    
    
    
    def _article_batches(
        con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, files: list[Path], *, identities: bool
    ) -> Iterator[list[Article]]:
        for file in files:
            query = (
                "SELECT to_json(i) FROM read_parquet(?) i ORDER BY source_path,source_row"
            )
            if identities:
                query = (
                    "SELECT to_json(i) FROM (SELECT *, sha256(to_json(struct_pack("
                    "body:=text_sha256,title:=title,date:=publish_date,publisher:=hostname,"
                    "candidates:=candidates))) AS inference_id FROM read_parquet(?)) i "
                    "ORDER BY source_path,source_row"
                )
            con.execute(query, [str(file)])
            while rows := con.fetchmany(4096):
                yield [Article.model_validate_json(row[0]) for row in rows]
    
    
    @contextmanager
    def _frame(
        input: Path, limit: int | None, seed: int, selection: Path | None = None
    ) -> Iterator[tuple[Iterator[list[Article]], int, int]]:
        with duckdb.connect() as con:
            con.execute("SET memory_limit='2GB'")
            con.execute("SET threads=1")
            con.execute("SET preserve_insertion_order=false")
            con.execute("SET max_temp_directory_size='4GB'")
            files = sorted(input.glob("shards/*/retained.parquet"))
            if not files:
                raise ValueError("The CPU index has no completed retained shards")
            if limit is None:
                count = int(
                    con.from_parquet([str(path) for path in files]).count("*").fetchone()[0]
                )
                yield _article_batches(con, files, identities=True), count, count
                return
            frame_metadata = selection.with_suffix(".json") if selection else None
            if (
                selection
                and selection.exists()
                and frame_metadata
                and frame_metadata.exists()
            ):
                saved = json.loads(frame_metadata.read_text())
                if saved["seed"] != seed or saved["requested"] != min(
                    limit, saved["frame_documents"]
                ):
                    raise ValueError("Frozen selection differs from the requested sample")
                if (
                    hashlib.sha256(selection.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
                    != saved["selection_sha256"]
                ):
                    raise ValueError("Frozen selection checksum changed")
                yield (
                    _article_batches(con, [selection], identities=False),
                    int(saved["frame_documents"]),
                    int(saved["requested"]),
                )
                return
            con.read_parquet([str(path) for path in files]).create_view("input_records")
            if limit is not None:
                count_row = con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM input_records").fetchone()
                if count_row is None:
                    raise ValueError("The retained article population is missing")
                count = int(count_row[0])
                con.execute(
                    "CREATE TEMP TABLE sample_keys AS SELECT "
                    "article_id,source_path,source_row "
                    "FROM input_records ORDER BY sha256($seed||':'||article_id),article_id "
                    "LIMIT $limit",
                    {"seed": str(seed), "limit": limit},
                )
                con.execute(
                    "CREATE VIEW chosen AS SELECT i.* FROM input_records i "
                    "JOIN sample_keys s "
                    "USING(article_id,source_path,source_row)"
                )
            else:
                con.execute("CREATE VIEW chosen AS SELECT * FROM input_records")
            con.execute(
                "CREATE VIEW identities AS SELECT *, sha256(to_json(struct_pack("
                "body:=text_sha256,title:=title,date:=publish_date,publisher:=hostname,"
                "candidates:=candidates))) AS inference_id FROM chosen"
            )
            con.execute(
                "CREATE VIEW selected AS SELECT inference_id,article_id FROM identities"
            )
            unit_count = min(count, limit)
            query = (
                "SELECT to_json(i) FROM identities i "
                "JOIN selected s USING(inference_id,article_id) "
                "ORDER BY source_path,source_row"
            )
            requested = unit_count
            if selection:
                con.execute(
                    "COPY (SELECT i.* FROM identities i JOIN selected s "
                    "USING(inference_id,article_id) ORDER BY source_path,source_row) "
                    "TO $output (FORMAT PARQUET)",
                    {"output": str(selection.with_suffix(".parquet.tmp"))},
                )
                selection.with_suffix(".parquet.tmp").replace(selection)
                if frame_metadata:
                    _write_json(
                        frame_metadata,
                        {
                            "frame_documents": count,
                            "requested": requested,
                            "seed": seed,
                            "selection": "SHA256(seed:article_id) retained-row priority",
                            "frame_unit": "retained source article rows",
                            "selection_sha256": hashlib.sha256(
                                selection.read_bytes()
                            ).hexdigest(),
                        },
                    )
                con.execute(
                    "SELECT to_json(s) FROM read_parquet(?) s "
                    "ORDER BY source_path,source_row",
                    [str(selection)],
                )
            else:
                con.execute(query)
            if selection:
                yield _article_batches(con, [selection], identities=False), count, requested

    """Prepare a reproducible, source-verified sample for local extraction benchmarks."""
    
    import argparse
    import hashlib
    import json
    import time
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import duckdb
    
    from pipeline.stages.processed.experiments.article_scoring import _BodyReader, _frame
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Read sampled source bodies and preserve their candidate evidence."""
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
        parser.add_argument("--size", type=int, default=10_000)
        parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        selection = args.output / "selection.parquet"
        sample = args.output / "articles.jsonl"
        if sample.exists():
            raise FileExistsError(sample)
        source = Path("data/raw/fine-news")
        index = Path("data/processed/experiments/article-labels/candidates")
        started = time.monotonic()
        reading = 0.0
        count = 0
        with (
            _frame(index, args.size, args.seed, selection) as (batches, population, requested),
            duckdb.connect() as con,
            sample.open("x", encoding="utf-8") as output,
        ):
            reader = _BodyReader(source, con)
            for batch in batches:
                begin = time.monotonic()
                bodies = reader.read(batch)
                reading += time.monotonic() - begin
                for article in batch:
                    value = article.model_dump(mode="json")
                    value["text"] = bodies[article.article_id].text
                    output.write(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
                    count += 1
        if count != requested:
            raise ValueError(f"Sample has {count} records, expected {requested}")
        manifest = {
            "population": population,
            "sample_size": count,
            "seed": args.seed,
            "selection": "SHA256(seed:article_id) retained-row priority",
            "sample_sha256": hashlib.file_digest(sample.open("rb"), "sha256").hexdigest(),
            "selection_sha256": hashlib.file_digest(selection.open("rb"), "sha256").hexdigest(),
            "source_body_read_seconds": reading,
            "source_row_groups_read": reader.groups_read,
            "total_preparation_seconds": time.monotonic() - started,
        }
        (args.output / "sample.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(json.dumps(manifest))
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

        def extract_long(
            self,
            text: str,
            schema,
            threshold: float = 0.5,

        def batch_extract_long(
            self,
            texts: List[str],
            schemas: Union[Schema, List[Schema], Dict, List[Dict]],
            batch_size: int = 8,
            threshold: float = 0.5,
            num_workers: int = 0,
            format_results: bool = True,
            include_confidence: bool = False,
            include_spans: bool = False,
            chunk_size: int = 384,
            chunk_overlap: int = 64,
            overlap_policy: Optional[str] = None,
        ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
            """Extract from long documents by scanning overlapping word chunks."""
            if not format_results:
                raise ValueError("batch_extract_long currently requires format_results=True")
            if not texts:
                return []
    
            if isinstance(schemas, list):
                if len(schemas) != len(texts):
                    raise ValueError(f"Schema count ({len(schemas)}) != text count ({len(texts)})")
                schema_list = schemas
            else:
                schema_list = [schemas] * len(texts)
    
            all_chunk_texts: List[str] = []
            all_chunk_schemas: List[Any] = []
            doc_chunks = []
            doc_chunk_counts: List[int] = []
    
            for text, schema in zip(texts, schema_list):
                chunks = split_text_into_chunks(
                    text,
                    chunk_size=chunk_size,
                    chunk_overlap=chunk_overlap,
                    word_splitter=word_splitter_from(self),
                )
                doc_chunks.append(chunks)
                doc_chunk_counts.append(len(chunks))
                for chunk in chunks:
                    all_chunk_texts.append(chunk.text)
                    all_chunk_schemas.append(schema)
    
            chunk_results = self.batch_extract(
                all_chunk_texts,
                all_chunk_schemas,
                batch_size=batch_size,
                threshold=threshold,
                num_workers=num_workers,
                format_results=True,
                include_confidence=True,
                include_spans=True,
                max_len=chunk_size,
                overlap_policy=overlap_policy,
            )
    
            merged_results: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
            offset = 0
            for text, schema, chunks, count in zip(texts, schema_list, doc_chunks, doc_chunk_counts):
                results_for_doc = chunk_results[offset : offset + count]
                merged_results.append(
                    merge_chunk_results(
                        text,
                        chunks,
                        results_for_doc,
                        include_confidence=include_confidence,
                        include_spans=include_spans,
                        scalar_entity_labels=self._scalar_entity_labels(schema),
                        overlap_policy=self._resolved_overlap_policy(overlap_policy),
                    )
                )
                offset += count
    
            return merged_results
    
        @staticmethod
        def _scalar_entity_labels(schema) -> set:
            """Names of entity types declared with a non-list dtype."""
            entity_metadata = getattr(schema, "_entity_metadata", None)
            if not isinstance(entity_metadata, dict):
                return set()

        parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=43)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        selection = args.output / "selection.parquet"
        sample = args.output / "articles.jsonl"
        if sample.exists():
            raise FileExistsError(sample)
        source = Path("data/raw/fine-news")
        index = Path("data/processed/experiments/article-labels/candidates")
        started = time.monotonic()
        reading = 0.0
        count = 0
        with (
            _frame(index, args.size, args.seed, selection) as (batches, population, requested),
            duckdb.connect() as con,
            sample.open("x", encoding="utf-8") as output,
        ):
            reader = _BodyReader(source, con)
            for batch in batches:
                begin = time.monotonic()
                bodies = reader.read(batch)
                reading += time.monotonic() - begin
                for article in batch:
                    value = article.model_dump(mode="json")
                    value["text"] = bodies[article.article_id].text
                    output.write(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
                    count += 1
        if count != requested:
            raise ValueError(f"Sample has {count} records, expected {requested}")
        manifest = {
            "population": population,
            "sample_size": count,
            "seed": args.seed,
            "selection": "SHA256(seed:article_id) retained-row priority",
            "sample_sha256": hashlib.file_digest(sample.open("rb"), "sha256").hexdigest(),
            "selection_sha256": hashlib.file_digest(selection.open("rb"), "sha256").hexdigest(),
            "source_body_read_seconds": reading,
            "source_row_groups_read": reader.groups_read,
            "total_preparation_seconds": time.monotonic() - started,
        }
        (args.output / "sample.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(json.dumps(manifest))
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    """Measure full-document GLiNER extraction on a prepared article sample."""
    
    import argparse
    import gzip
    import json
    import time
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import torch
    from gliner2 import AttributeGroup, AutoExtractor
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Run one isolated model configuration and save timings and predictions."""
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("--sample", type=Path, required=True)
        parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)
        parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
        parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=100)
        parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=8)
        parser.add_argument("--precision", choices=["fp32", "fp16", "bf16", "int8"], default="fp32")
        parser.add_argument("--backend", choices=["standard", "compiled", "disentangled_flash"], default="standard")
        args = parser.parse_args()
        args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
        start = time.perf_counter()
        with args.sample.open(encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            articles = [json.loads(line) for _, line in zip(range(args.limit), stream, strict=False)]
        if len(articles) != args.limit:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected {args.limit} articles; got {len(articles)}")
        read_seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        start = time.perf_counter()
        model = AutoExtractor.from_pretrained(
            args.model,
            map_location="cuda",
            quantize=args.precision == "fp16",
            compile=args.backend == "compiled",
            attention_backend="disentangled_flash" if args.backend == "disentangled_flash" else "standard",
        )
        if args.precision == "bf16":
            model.to(dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        if args.precision == "int8":
            from torchao.quantization import Int8WeightOnlyConfig, quantize_
    
            quantize_(model.encoder, Int8WeightOnlyConfig())
        schema = (
            model.create_schema()
            .entities({"company": "Names of companies and businesses"})
            .entity_attributes({
                "article_role": AttributeGroup(
                    ["primary", "secondary", "incidental", "uncertain"],
                    applies_to=["company"],
                    qualify_labels=True,
                )
            })
            .classification(
                "article_type", ["reporting", "opinion", "press release", "promotional", "other"]
            )
        )
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        load_seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        start = time.perf_counter()
        model.batch_extract_long(
            [item["text"] for item in articles[: min(args.batch_size, len(articles))]],
            schema,
            batch_size=args.batch_size,
            include_spans=True,
            include_confidence=True,
        )
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        warmup_seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        start = time.perf_counter()
        output = args.output / "predictions.jsonl.gz"
        with gzip.open(output, "wt", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            for offset in range(0, len(articles), args.batch_size):
                batch = articles[offset : offset + args.batch_size]
                predictions = model.batch_extract_long(
                    [item["text"] for item in batch],
                    schema,
                    batch_size=args.batch_size,
                    include_spans=True,
                    include_confidence=True,
                )
                if len(predictions) != len(batch):
                    raise ValueError("Prediction count does not match the input batch")
                for article, prediction in zip(batch, predictions, strict=True):
                    for entity in prediction.get("entities", {}).get("company", []):
                        if article["text"][entity["start"] : entity["end"]] != entity["text"]:
                            raise ValueError(f"Invalid source span for {article['article_id']}")
                    stream.write(json.dumps({"article_id": article["article_id"], "prediction": prediction}) + "\n")
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        report = {
            "configuration": vars(args) | {"sample": str(args.sample), "output": str(args.output)},
            "articles": len(articles),
            "sample_read_seconds": read_seconds,
            "model_load_seconds": load_seconds,
            "warmup_seconds": warmup_seconds,
            "inference_and_output_seconds": seconds,
            "articles_per_second": len(articles) / seconds,
            "peak_cuda_memory_bytes": torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(),
            "torch_version": torch.__version__,
            "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
            "long_document_handling": "384-word overlapping windows, 64-word overlap; GLiNER2 merge",
        }
        (args.output / "report.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(json.dumps(report), flush=True)
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    class _BodyReader:
        """Read and retain one bounded original row group across consecutive batches."""
    
        def __init__(self, source: Path, con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection) -> None:
            self.source = source
            self.con = con
            self.bounds: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, int]]] = {}
            self.cached_group: tuple[str, int] | None = None
            self.cached_rows: dict[int, tuple[str, str | None]] = {}
            self.groups_read = 0
    
        def read(self, articles: list[Article]) -> dict[str, "_Body"]:
            result: dict[str, _Body] = {}
            groups: dict[tuple[str, int], list[Article]] = {}
            for article in articles:
                if article.source_path not in self.bounds:
                    metadata = self.con.execute(
                        "SELECT row_group_id,max(row_group_num_rows),"
                        "sum(total_uncompressed_size) FILTER (WHERE path_in_schema='text') "
                        "FROM parquet_metadata(?) GROUP BY row_group_id "
                        "ORDER BY row_group_id",
                        [str(self.source / article.source_path)],
                    ).fetchall()
                    offset = 0
                    bounds = []
                    for _, rows, size in metadata:
                        bounds.append((offset, offset + int(rows), int(size or 0)))
                        offset += int(rows)
                    self.bounds[article.source_path] = bounds
                bounds = self.bounds[article.source_path]
                index = bisect.bisect_right([b[0] for b in bounds], article.source_row) - 1
                if index < 0 or article.source_row >= bounds[index][1]:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Source row outside original file: {article.article_id}"
                    )
                groups.setdefault((article.source_path, index), []).append(article)
            for (file, index), members in groups.items():
                lower, upper, size = self.bounds[file][index]
                if self.cached_group != (file, index):
                    if size > 128 * 1024 * 1024:
                        rows = self.con.execute(
                            "SELECT file_row_number,text,to_json(metadata) "
                            "FROM read_parquet("
                            "$file,file_row_number=true) WHERE file_row_number "
                            "IN (SELECT unnest($rows))",
                            {
                                "file": str(self.source / file),
                                "rows": [article.source_row for article in members],
                            },
                        ).fetchall()
                        self.cached_group = None
                    else:
                        rows = self.con.execute(
                            "SELECT file_row_number,text,to_json(metadata) "
                            "FROM read_parquet("
                            "$file,file_row_number=true) "
                            "WHERE file_row_number >= $lower "
                            "AND file_row_number < $upper",
                            {
                                "file": str(self.source / file),
                                "lower": lower,
                                "upper": upper,
                            },
                        ).fetchall()
                        self.cached_group = (file, index)
                    self.groups_read += 1
                    self.cached_rows = {
                        int(row): (text, metadata) for row, text, metadata in rows
                    }
                for article in members:
                    original = self.cached_rows.get(article.source_row)
                    if original is None or not isinstance(original[0], str):
                        raise ValueError(f"Original text missing for {article.article_id}")
                    text, metadata_json = original
                    if hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest() != article.text_sha256:
                        raise ValueError(f"Text checksum changed for {article.article_id}")
                    metadata = (
                        JSON_VALUE_ADAPTER.validate_json(metadata_json)
                        if metadata_json is not None
                        else None
                    )
                    result[article.article_id] = _Body(text, metadata)
            return result

    class _Body:
        text: str
        metadata: JsonValue
    
    
    def _resolve_source(
        input: Path, manifest: dict[str, JsonValue], source: Path | None
    ) -> Path:
        if source is not None:
            return source.resolve()
        value = manifest.get("source_root")
        if not isinstance(value, str):
            raise ValueError("Pass --source or provide source_root in the CPU manifest")
        path = Path(value)
        return (path if path.is_absolute() else input / path).resolve()
    
    
    def _article_batches(
        con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, files: list[Path], *, identities: bool
    ) -> Iterator[list[Article]]:
        for file in files:
            query = (
                "SELECT to_json(i) FROM read_parquet(?) i ORDER BY source_path,source_row"
            )
            if identities:
                query = (
                    "SELECT to_json(i) FROM (SELECT *, sha256(to_json(struct_pack("
                    "body:=text_sha256,title:=title,date:=publish_date,publisher:=hostname,"
                    "candidates:=candidates))) AS inference_id FROM read_parquet(?)) i "
                    "ORDER BY source_path,source_row"
                )
            con.execute(query, [str(file)])
            while rows := con.fetchmany(4096):
                yield [Article.model_validate_json(row[0]) for row in rows]

    description: Use when evaluating or designing where CCFinance code, data stages, tests, documents or infrastructure belong, including module boundaries and repository restructures.
    ---
    
    # Architecture layout
    
    ## Workflow
    
    1. Establish the requested scope and outcome: evaluate the current layout,
       design a layout, or implement an authorized change. Read nearby README and
       ARCHITECTURE files. Identify existing owners and consumers before proposing
       a new abstraction; reuse an existing module or library when it satisfies the
       contract. File size alone is not a reason to split or create a package.
    2. Examine the relevant boundaries using evidence:
       - **Ownership and cohesion:** Can a contributor find the owner, and do things
         that change together live together? Keep each unit's responsibility clear.
       - **Dependencies and encapsulation:** Trace relevant imports and public
         interfaces. Keep intended dependency direction clear and cycles forbidden;
         avoid reaching into another module's internals without a reason.
       - **Coupling:** Identify changes that force unrelated owners to change.
         Share a contract only when consumers actually need the same behavior; a
         little local duplication may be preferable to coupling distinct contracts.
       - **Discoverability:** Make CLI commands, transformations, schemas, tests,
         fixtures and documents easy to find from their owning area.
    3. Choose the smallest useful boundary: a function, module, package or separate
       workspace project. A package or project should reflect an actual dependency,
       distribution, build or ownership need. Organize by layer, capability or a
       combination according to the work; do not impose a universal directory tree.
    4. For pipeline work, preserve the established `raw`, `processed` and `research`
       stage ownership. Organize capabilities within those layers as they arise.
       Distinguish Python imports from DVC artifact dependencies: the latter connect
       producers and consumers without requiring cross-layer Python imports. Apply
       Tach rules to durable module boundaries and DVC to artifact dependencies.
    5. For a move or split, trace the affected consumers before changing paths:
       imports and public APIs, CLI registration, package configuration, tests and
       fixtures, Tach, DVC and Semflow dependencies, and documentation links as
       applicable. Preserve behavior and scientific contracts unless the user asks
       for a change; report any intended behavior change separately. Do not treat
       missing static references as proof that dynamic or external consumers do not
       exist.
    6. Use the repository's existing gates rather than adding tests that merely
       assert a directory tree or private call sequence. For tests and fixtures,
       follow [Python testing](../python-testing/SKILL.md). Run focused checks while
       working and `just check` before handoff; report checks that could not run.
    
    ## Results
    
    For an evaluation, report concrete findings with locations, effects and ranked
    recommendations. For a design, show the proposed ownership and dependency
    boundaries, explain meaningful tradeoffs and how they are enforced. For an
    implementation, summarize what moved, whether behavior changed and the evidence
    from verification. Keep the review proportional to the requested change.
    
    For example, if both article cleaning and company linking need the same
    publication-date parser, first inspect its existing owner and date semantics.
    Share it only if both consumers require the same contract; keep separate rules
    when their treatment of missing or ambiguous dates differs.

    name: python-testing
    description: Use when writing, changing, reviewing or organizing Python tests, pytest fixtures or Hypothesis strategies in CCFinance.
    ---
    
    # Python testing
    
    ## Workflow
    
    1. Inspect the code contract, nearby tests, `conftest.py`, shared fixtures and
       strategies, the package's test README, and pytest configuration. Reuse an
       existing test or generator when it covers the behavior; extend it only for a
       distinct, meaningful risk. Do not add tests for trivial or reversible changes
       just to increase counts, or tests that restate implementation details.
    2. Prefer Hypothesis for input variation when a general property is meaningful.
       Prefer a small explicit example for a single known boundary, regression or
       command smoke check. Decide the expected outcome independently of the code
       under test. Use tiny representative data, bounded generators and the smallest
       appropriate test boundary. Assert public behavior, including error contracts.
    3. Place a test beside its source owner under the mirrored `tests/` layout. Reuse
       existing factories and strategies first. Keep a helper local until several
       tests need it; put cross-module strategies in `tests/_strategies.py` and
       shared pytest fixtures in the nearest common `conftest.py`. Place a fixture
       at broader scope only when its state is safe to share. Measure costly setup
       before broadening scope; avoid creating generic fixture frameworks.
    4. Arrange inputs and prerequisites, act on the behavior, and assert observable
       results (AAA). Cleanup belongs in a fixture finalizer or context manager.
       Label each phase with an `# Arrange`, `# Act` or `# Assert` comment, as in
       the example below. Favor DAMP: clear names and visible expected values can
       justify a little repetition.
    5. Give each new or modified test exactly one scope marker from the table below;
       add `slow` or `external` only when applicable. Mark a class or module only
       when every inherited test has the same scope. Never stack or override scope
       markers, including inherited marks. Before using markers, register the six
       names in the owning pytest configuration; unknown names fail under
       `--strict-markers`. This skill defines the policy; it does not mean the
       current unmarked suite already enforces it. Migrate existing tests deliberately
       if adding a collection-time enforcement hook.
    6. During development, run the smallest relevant test or selection and check
       its output. Before handoff run the repository's required full checks, including
       the complete non-Testmon suite. Run any affected slow or external tests when
       their prerequisites and authorization are available; report what was not run
       and why. A targeted pass is not evidence that the full suite passed.
    
    ## Markers
    
    Use only these six custom markers. Built-in pytest mechanisms such as
    `parametrize`, `skipif` and `xfail` remain available for their intended purposes.
    Scope describes the boundary the assertions exercise, not the number of files,
    the use of Hypothesis, or the choice of a reference oracle.
    
    | Marker | Rule |
    | --- | --- |
    | `unit` | Exactly one scope: an isolated operation or small self-contained behavior. |
    | `component` | Exactly one scope: one coherent subsystem or component through its public behavior. |
    | `integration` | Exactly one scope: interactions across components or a real dependency boundary. |
    | `e2e` | Exactly one scope: a complete user-visible workflow through the public CLI or API. A CLI help check alone is not end-to-end. |
    | `slow` | Optional execution label: the complete test, including setup, teardown and generated examples, consistently exceeds two seconds on the normal local environment. Confirm with repeated pytest duration reports; a single noisy measurement is not enough. |
    | `external` | Optional execution label: the test accesses a live network service or external account. Use even if it is usually fast; require explicit opt-in and appropriate credentials. A local temporary file, subprocess or fake alone does not qualify. |
    
    `slow` and `external` are independent and may accompany any one scope. Do not
    invent custom markers for regression, reference, property, smoke, tools or
    implementation techniques; communicate those in descriptive test names and
    assertions. Run fast local iteration with `-m "not slow and not external"`
    after the markers are registered. Full checks must not silently omit slow tests;
    external tests need a separate explicit lane and must not mutate live services
    without authorization.
    
    ## Hypothesis examples and fixtures
    
    Hypothesis strategies generate values; pytest fixtures manage resources. If
    Hypothesis is absent, add it to the locked workspace development dependencies
    when introducing the first test that uses it. Search
    for reusable strategies or an appropriate first-party Hypothesis extra before
    adding one. Compose built-in strategies, use `@composite` for dependent values,
    and generate valid inputs directly rather than filtering most examples. Keep
    sizes bounded and counterexamples understandable. Preserve an important known
    failure using `@example` or an explicit regression; do not duplicate a property
    with a long list of examples that establish the same behavior.
    
    A function-scoped pytest fixture runs once per test function, not once per
    `@given` example. For per-example mutable resources, create and clean them inside
    the test, for example with `TemporaryDirectory()`. Reuse immutable shared data
    only when safe. Do not suppress health checks or disable deadlines globally to
    make a test pass; investigate the cause and document a narrowly justified
    exception. Choose explicit settings or a shared profile only when warranted by
    measured cost. Preserve failing examples and replay information as appropriate.
    
    This self-contained example illustrates a small property, AAA and the scope
    marker; it uses the standard-library URL parser rather than a CCFinance stage:
    
    ```python
    from string import ascii_lowercase, digits
    from urllib.parse import urlsplit
    
    import pytest
    from hypothesis import example, given, strategies as st
    
    
    @pytest.mark.unit
    @example(host="news")
    @given(host=st.text(alphabet=ascii_lowercase + digits, min_size=1, max_size=20))
    def test_url_hostname_normalizes_ascii_case(host: str) -> None:
        # Arrange: build a URL with an uppercase hostname.
        url = f"https://{host.upper()}.example/article"
    
        # Act: extract the hostname.
        hostname = urlsplit(url).hostname
    
        # Assert: the hostname is lowercase.
        assert hostname == f"{host}.example"
    ```
    
    Use a real local Parquet or filesystem boundary for a small integration test
    when that interaction matters; use a stub or fake for costly or nondeterministic
    remote services. A fake cannot establish that the real service works. Keep
    randomized tests independent of execution order; for numerical or sampling
    claims define tolerances and uncertainty rather than requiring arbitrary
    bit-for-bit agreement across environments.
    
    Consult the Hypothesis [tutorial](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorial/),
    [how-to guides](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how-to/),
    [strategies and API reference](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/)
    and [extras](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/extras.html) when
    choosing or debugging a strategy.

    Shared agent instructions and Codex configuration are maintained in
    [`.agents/`](.agents/README.md). `just setup` applies them; use
    `just agents::preview` to preview link changes and `just agents::check` to
    verify the generated links.
    
    `just check` validates Justfile syntax and formatting alongside the other
    quality gates. Run `just fmt` to format Justfiles and other source files.
    
    For Python alone, with Python 3.13, uv and just installed:
    
    ```bash
    just python::setup
    just python::check
    ```
    
    ## Data and reproducibility
    
    DVC is initialized at the repository root with analytics disabled. Use:
    
    ```bash
    just dvc status
    just dvc dag
    ```
    
    Semflow tracks the executable Python dependencies of DVC stages. When adding a
    stage, run `just semflow-patch` to review its proposed fingerprints, then
    `just semflow-apply` to materialize them. Commit the generated
    `.semflow/hashes/` files with the DVC definition. After semantic source changes,
    run `just semflow-refresh`; `just semflow-check` detects stale fingerprints.
    The frozen [Fine News acquisition stage](data/inputs/fine-news/README.md) retains
    the published staging snapshot and its historical selection recipe. DVC verifies
    the restored output during reproduction. The
    [source comparison](data/inputs/source-comparison/README.md) prepares small
    probability samples using Parquet metadata before acquiring article payloads.
    Keep data, configuration and environment dependencies explicit in DVC: Semflow's
    static analysis cannot discover string-driven dynamic imports.
    
    See [Python commands](src/python/README.md), [LaTeX commands](src/latex/README.md)
    and [infrastructure](infra/README.md). The scaffold's Apache-2.0 license covers
    code; it does not grant rights to upstream article content.
    # Architecture
    
    CCFinance separates code and research artifacts. Git stores source, configuration,
    locks, provenance definitions and documentation. DVC defines data dependencies
    and tracks materialized source snapshots and experiment outputs.
    
    - `src/python/apps/pipeline` owns the CLI and data stage implementations.
    - `src/python/uv.lock` locks runtime, quality, testing, packaging and DVC tools.
    - `src/latex` owns the manuscript source and bibliography.
    - `data` holds ignored data payloads and versioned DVC pointer files.
    - `infra/nix` and `devenv.lock` own the reproducible system environment.
    
    Tach enforces module boundaries; Ruff and strict Pyrefly check Python source.
    pytest-layout-enforcer checks test file placement during collection and CI.
    Semflow fingerprints the Python code used by DVC stages, allowing DVC to
    invalidate tracked results when executable behavior changes.
    CI executes those checks, tests and builds through the same just recipes as local
    work. Setup may download dependencies; ordinary checks use cached dependencies
    and do not repair authored content. LaTeX uses a versioned Tectonic asset bundle.
    
    The Hugging Face dataset is staging, and the bucket is intended for intermediate
    and experiment artifacts. The frozen raw acquisition stage documents the
    historical selection without fetching its output. Company labels and coverage
    are provisional experiments; release validation and remote artifact transport
    remain future work. The raw comparison stages prepare
    sampling manifests from Hub listings and Parquet footers, then acquire only the
    selected row groups through the shared publisher filter. Research aggregation
    reads those artifacts without importing raw-stage modules. DVC connects these
    steps; pinned source revisions and recorded draw probabilities define the
    experiment's population and sampling design.
    
    The article-labeling experiment adopts checksum-verified CPU company candidates
    and materializes compact source-linked selections without copying article bodies.
    Native Kev runs in a separately pinned GPU environment; the pipeline communicates
    through typed System One requests. Article-company probabilities and filtering
    policies remain separate, with resumable checkpoints and explicit unresolved
    outcomes. The research layer reconciles candidate and model-scored coverage and
    reports runtime estimates without treating AI agreement as human validation.
    Completed pilots remain frozen. Full scoring uses compressed source-record
    chunks, a resumable request ledger and explicit pending counts. Separate runtime
    profiles preserve GPU memory experiments without overwriting completed evidence.
    
    Each data layer groups experimental artifacts beneath `experiments/<name>/`.
    Experimental stage code follows the same grouping under its owning layer.
    `pipeline.experiments.source_comparison` defines shared parameters and artifacts;
    Tach permits raw and research to depend on these contracts without importing one
    another. Raw publisher extraction owns one source-field registry, deriving both
    SQL projections and projected column sizes from it. DVC supplies artifact paths
    explicitly. Research uses statsmodels for survey-estimate summaries and LaTeX
    tables; it preserves the probability-sampling design.
    
    Copier answers record the source and tag for future template updates. Review
    update conflicts and preserve project-specific code and configuration. The
    upstream template is [Exordio](https://github.com/marcusinthesky/exordio).

    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    set positional-arguments
    
    mod python 'src/python/justfile'
    mod latex 'src/latex/justfile'
    mod agents '.agents/justfile'
    mod inference 'infra/inference/justfile'
    workflow := "env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py"
    
    # Discover this project's commands.
    default:
        @just --list
    
    # Prepare locked dependencies and Git hooks (uses the network).
    setup:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --frozen --script src/python/scripts/workflow/script.py prepare
        just python::setup
        just latex::setup
        just agents::apply
        prek install
    
    # Check source, views and selected languages without repairing files.
    check:
        bash infra/nix/check.sh
        {{ workflow }} check
        just python::check
        just latex::check
        just data-check
        just semflow-check
        just changelog-check
        just skills-check
        just agents::check
    
    # Run the selected language tests.
    test:
        just python::test
        just latex::test
    
    # Explicitly format sources.
    fmt:
        git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard | while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do case "$file" in justfile|*/justfile|Justfile|*/Justfile|*.just) just --justfile "$file" --fmt --unstable ;; esac; done
        nixfmt devenv.nix infra/nix/devenv.nix infra/nix/pkgs/schematter.nix infra/nix/pkgs/agentsync.nix
        rumdl fmt .
        # DVC's YAML emitter can leave trailing spaces when wrapping scalar values.
        if [[ -f dvc.lock ]]; then sed -i 's/[[:blank:]]*$//' dvc.lock; fi
        just python::fmt
        just latex::fmt
    
    # Check external links online.
    links:
        git ls-files -z '*.md' | xargs -0 -r lychee --config lychee.toml --no-progress
    
    # Run root-level DVC using the locked Python environment.
    dvc *args:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen dvc "$@"
    
    # Validate DVC metadata without fetching data.
    data-check:
        just dvc status
        just dvc dag
    
    # Refresh generated planning and reference views.
    sync:
        {{ workflow }} sync
    
    # Validate document schemas, links and generated views.
    context-check:
        {{ workflow }} check
    
    # Create a plan without overwriting existing content.
    plan-new slug title:
        {{ workflow }} plan-new "$1" --title "$2"
    
    # Create a task inside an existing plan or task.
    task-new parent slug title:
        {{ workflow }} task-new "$1" "$2" --title "$3"
    
    # Create a local reference record with its directory as citation key.
    reference-new key title:
        {{ workflow }} reference-new "$1" --title "$2"
    
    # Validate the repository changelog structure and change categories.
    changelog-check:
        schematter validate --schema infra/schemas/documents/changelog.document-schema.yaml CHANGELOG.md
    
    # Check semantic fingerprints once DVC has executable stages.
    semflow-check:
        if env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen python -c 'import pathlib, sys, yaml; from semflow.config import load_config; load_config(); doc = yaml.safe_load(pathlib.Path("dvc.yaml").read_text()); sys.exit(0 if isinstance(doc, dict) and doc.get("stages") == {} else 1)'; then echo 'Semflow: no DVC stages to instrument.'; else env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow check; fi
    
    # Preview the semantic dependency changes before applying them.
    semflow-patch:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow patch
    
    # Apply reviewed DVC and semantic fingerprint changes.
    semflow-apply:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow patch --apply
    
    # Refresh existing semantic fingerprints without editing the DVC graph.
    semflow-refresh:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages semflow refresh --apply
    
    # Validate repository-owned skill documents and their directory names.
    skills-check:
        git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard -- ':(glob)**/SKILL.md' 'SKILL.md' | while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do [[ -f "$file" ]] || continue; schematter validate --schema infra/schemas/documents/skill.document-schema.yaml "$file"; awk 'END { if (NR > 500) { print FILENAME ": exceeds 500 lines" > "/dev/stderr"; exit 1 } }' "$file"; env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen python -c 'import pathlib, re, sys, yaml; p = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); frontmatter = re.split(r"(?m)^---[ \t]*\r?$", p.read_text(), maxsplit=2)[1]; name = yaml.safe_load(frontmatter)["name"]; sys.exit(0 if name == p.parent.name else f"{p}: name {name!r} must match parent directory {p.parent.name!r}")' "$file"; done

    # Native decision inference
    
    These scripts run the pinned native Kev server using the CUDA libraries of an
    already cached container image. SGLang is not launched. Native Kev shares the
    article prefix across its independent identity and coverage questions.
    
    From the repository root, prepare the small serving dependencies and then supply
    the existing checkpoint and Hugging Face base-model cache:
    
    ```bash
    just inference::setup
    just inference::serve /path/to/kev-4b /path/to/huggingface/hub \
        data/inputs/article-labels/kev-4b-low-memory.json
    docker logs ccfinance-kev-native
    just inference::status
    ```
    
    The versioned runtime manifest records the model, source, image, precision,
    kernels and admission limit. The entrypoint applies that limit to both the
    article and every complete article-question sequence. Oversized inputs fail
    explicitly; text truncation is disabled. Local package and compilation caches
    live under ignored `.runtime/`.
    
    The third argument selects the versioned runtime profile. Pass the selected 4B
    profile explicitly; omitting it selects the historical 0.8B baseline.
    
    The 4B profile uses BF16 and retains one article prefix. Its adapter and head
    checksums are checked before loading. The serving trial records actual memory
    use separately from the model publisher's memory estimate.
    
    To restore the pinned public 4B files with the repository's Hugging Face CLI:
    
    ```bash
    uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen hf download jaredpalmer/kev-4b \
        adapter_config.json adapter_model.safetensors head.pt \
        --revision 139fdd94f1b6a6ad80cc15e08fcb99cac885a101 \
        --local-dir .runtime/models/kev-4b
    HF_HUB_CACHE="$PWD/.runtime/hf-cache" \
        uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen hf download Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B-Base \
        --revision 1001bb4d826a52d1f399e183466143f4da7b741b \
        --include '*.json' --include '*.safetensors' \
        --include merges.txt --include vocab.json
    ```
    
    The base weights require approximately 9.3 GB of storage. Model files and caches
    stay under ignored `.runtime/`; their revisions and checkpoint checksums remain
    in the versioned profile. Setup expects the recorded container image to exist
    locally and a working NVIDIA Container Toolkit CDI device.
    
    The completed company-labeling pilot used `kev-4b.json` with three concise
    binary questions per distinct company descriptor, sharing the full article
    prefix. Its graph buffers hold four states, 16 rows and 16,384 tokens. Active
    pilot samples reached 15,654 MiB with 197 MiB free on the 16,311 MiB GPU. An
    earlier diagnostic graph capture ran out of memory and fell back to eager
    inference; the completed pilot's native graph and prefix OOM counters stayed
    zero. One client timeout was retried successfully.
    
    Production uses the separate `kev-4b-low-memory.json` profile: two graph states,
    eight rows and 8,192 graph tokens. The 8,192-token context admission, prefix
    cache, weights, precision, temperature and questions remain the same. Sixteen
    exact pilot requests, including its eight longest admitted bodies, compared 337
    probabilities: maximum difference 0.0073, mean difference 0.0001134, with no
    changes at the 0.5 or 0.95 boundaries. The differences reflect floating-point
    reassociation across smaller passes. Occupancy samples reached 14,580 MiB during
    long-body inference and 15,074 MiB after graph capture, with 777 MiB free. These
    observations describe the tested requests rather than guarantee every future
    workload's peak.
    
    `kev-0.8b.json` records a separate experimental 16k admission trial. The smaller
    model was rejected for this pilot after the same fresh source cases produced
    more false positives. The seven-case long-context study was stopped after one
    HTTP success; it does not establish 16k semantic quality. The original
    `runtime.json` remains the historical 8k baseline.
    
    Stop the server with `just inference::stop`; remove its stopped
    container with `docker rm ccfinance-kev-native` before starting a replacement.
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    repo_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
    runtime="$repo_root/.runtime"
    source_commit=2074cc44256200bb37540103fa4572901faa10f3
    image=lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:f7876bef696ccf9cf75a2bf7ccb82970f5fac577f082fb8ca95c9a59d2160eb5
    mkdir -p "$runtime/serving-site"
    if [[ ! -d "$runtime/kev/.git" ]]; then
        git init "$runtime/kev"
        git -C "$runtime/kev" remote add origin https://github.com/jaredpalmer/kev.git
        git -C "$runtime/kev" fetch --depth 1 origin "$source_commit"
        git -C "$runtime/kev" checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD
    fi
    test "$(git -C "$runtime/kev" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$source_commit"
    docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null
    docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
        --mount "type=bind,source=$runtime/serving-site,target=/runtime-site" \
        --mount "type=bind,source=$repo_root/infra/inference/requirements.txt,target=/requirements.txt,readonly" \
        --entrypoint python "$image" -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check \
        --no-cache-dir --no-deps --target /runtime-site -r /requirements.txt
    set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]
    set positional-arguments
    
    default:
        @just --list
    
    # Install exactly the committed workspace and build dependencies.
    setup:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv sync --locked --all-packages
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline python -c 'import duckdb; duckdb.connect().execute("INSTALL httpfs")'
    
    run *args:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --package ccfinance-pipeline pipeline "$@"
    
    lint:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff check .
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff format --check .
    
    typecheck:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pyrefly check
    
    # Local impacted-test selection, with a bounded number of workers.
    test-changed:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest -q -n 2 --testmon
    
    # The test and CI gates never use affected-test selection.
    test:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest -q -n 2 --no-testmon
    
    # Check that test paths correspond to source modules.
    layout:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen --all-packages pytest-layout-enforcer check
    
    # Enforce module dependencies, reject unused declarations and forbid cycles.
    tach:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen tach check
    
    build:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv build --python .venv/bin/python --offline --no-build-isolation --all-packages
    
    check: lint typecheck tach layout test build
    
    fmt:
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff check --fix .
        env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --offline --frozen ruff format .

    set -euo pipefail
    repo_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
    runtime="$repo_root/.runtime"
    image=lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:f7876bef696ccf9cf75a2bf7ccb82970f5fac577f082fb8ca95c9a59d2160eb5
    mkdir -p "$runtime/gliner-site"
    docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
        --mount "type=bind,source=$runtime/gliner-site,target=/site" \
        --mount "type=bind,source=$repo_root/infra/inference/gliner-requirements.txt,target=/requirements.txt,readonly" \
        --entrypoint python "$image" -m pip install --upgrade --no-cache-dir --no-deps \
        --target /site -r /requirements.txt
    patch -d "$runtime/gliner-site" -p1 < "$repo_root/infra/inference/gliner2-2.1.0-cuda-attributes.patch"
    env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project "$repo_root/src/python" --offline --frozen \
        hf download fastino/gliner2.5-small-v1 --revision b5d42bf7dc7d01c40304ae4ed43c2f13c325a75b \
        --local-dir "$runtime/models/gliner2.5-small-v1"
    env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run --project "$repo_root/src/python" --offline --frozen \
        hf download fastino/gliner2.5-base-v1 --revision 07d99c0ba5d15cb3b24e0a236fa99bdd4ef87a5c \
        --local-dir "$runtime/models/gliner2.5-base-v1"
