    """Utilities for long-document extraction.
    
    The helpers in this module are intentionally model-agnostic: they split text
    into word-aware windows, remap chunk-local spans back to document offsets, and
    merge duplicate predictions produced by overlapping chunks.
    """
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    from collections import Counter
    from dataclasses import dataclass
    from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Tuple
    
    from gliner2.inference.overlap import normalize_overlap_policy, resolve_overlaps
    from gliner2.processing.word_splitter import resolve_word_splitter
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class TextChunk:
        """A chunk of text with offsets into the original document."""
    
        text: str
        start_char: int
        end_char: int
        start_word: int
        end_word: int
    
    
    def iter_word_offsets(
        text: str,
        word_splitter=None,
    ) -> Iterable[Tuple[str, int, int]]:
        """Yield word tokens and character offsets using the active splitter.
    
        ``word_splitter`` may be a built-in name, a callable, or omitted to use
        the default whitespace splitter. Offsets always index the original text;
        chunking requests original-case token strings (``lower=False``).
        """
        splitter = resolve_word_splitter(word_splitter)
        yield from splitter(text, lower=False)
    
    
    def split_text_into_chunks(
        text: str,
        chunk_size: int = 384,
        chunk_overlap: int = 64,
        word_splitter=None,
    ) -> List[TextChunk]:
        """Split text into overlapping word windows.
    
        Args:
            text: Original document text.
            chunk_size: Maximum number of word tokens per chunk.
            chunk_overlap: Number of word tokens repeated between adjacent chunks.
            word_splitter: Optional splitter name or callable used to count words.
        """
        if chunk_size <= 0:
            raise ValueError("chunk_size must be greater than 0")
        if chunk_overlap < 0:
            raise ValueError("chunk_overlap must be non-negative")
        if chunk_overlap >= chunk_size:
            raise ValueError("chunk_overlap must be smaller than chunk_size")
    
        tokens = list(iter_word_offsets(text, word_splitter=word_splitter))
        if not tokens:
            return [TextChunk(text=text, start_char=0, end_char=len(text), start_word=0, end_word=0)]
    
        chunks: List[TextChunk] = []
        step = chunk_size - chunk_overlap
        start_word = 0
    
        while start_word < len(tokens):
            end_word = min(start_word + chunk_size, len(tokens))
            start_char = tokens[start_word][1]
            end_char = tokens[end_word - 1][2]
            chunks.append(
                TextChunk(
                    text=text[start_char:end_char],
                    start_char=start_char,
                    end_char=end_char,
                    start_word=start_word,
                    end_word=end_word,
                )
            )
            if end_word == len(tokens):
                break
            start_word += step
    
        return chunks
    
    
    def remap_result_spans(result: Any, original_text: str, chunk: TextChunk) -> Any:
        """Recursively remap chunk-local span dicts to document-level offsets."""
        if isinstance(result, list):
            return [remap_result_spans(item, original_text, chunk) for item in result]
    
        if isinstance(result, dict):
            remapped = {key: remap_result_spans(value, original_text, chunk) for key, value in result.items()}
            if _is_span_dict(remapped):
                start = int(remapped["start"]) + chunk.start_char
                end = int(remapped["end"]) + chunk.start_char
                remapped["start"] = start
                remapped["end"] = end
                if 0 <= start <= end <= len(original_text):
                    remapped["text"] = original_text[start:end]
            return remapped
    
        return result
    
    
    def merge_chunk_results(
        original_text: str,
        chunks: List[TextChunk],
        chunk_results: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        include_confidence: bool = False,
        include_spans: bool = False,
        scalar_entity_labels: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None,
        overlap_policy: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Merge formatted extraction results from one document's chunks.
    
        ``scalar_entity_labels`` names entity types declared with a non-list dtype;
        those are collapsed to a single best value (mirroring the base API) instead
        of being returned as a list.
        """
        if len(chunks) != len(chunk_results):
            raise ValueError("chunks and chunk_results must have the same length")
    
        policy = normalize_overlap_policy(overlap_policy, default="disallow")
        scalar_labels = set(scalar_entity_labels or ())
        remapped_results = [
            remap_result_spans(result, original_text, chunk)
            for chunk, result in zip(chunks, chunk_results)
        ]
        merged = _merge_result_dicts(remapped_results, scalar_labels, policy)
        return _strip_span_metadata(merged, include_confidence, include_spans)
    
    
    def _merge_result_dicts(
        results: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        scalar_entity_labels: Optional[set] = None,
        overlap_policy: str = "disallow",
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        merged: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        keys = []
        seen = set()
        for result in results:
            for key in result:
                if key not in seen:
                    seen.add(key)
                    keys.append(key)
    
        for key in keys:
            values = [result.get(key) for result in results if key in result]
            if key == "entities":

                    values, scalar_entity_labels or set(), overlap_policy
                )
            elif key == "relation_extraction":

    def _merge_relation_maps(values: List[Any]) -> Dict[str, List[Any]]:
        merged: Dict[str, List[Any]] = {}

    def _merge_values(values: List[Any], overlap_policy: str = "disallow") -> Any:
        non_empty = [value for value in values if value not in (None, {}, [])]
        if not non_empty:

    $ sed -n '675,755p' .runtime/gliner-site/gliner2/processor.py && cat .runtime/models/gliner2.5-small-v1/config.json | head -60
            max_len: Optional[int] = None,
            *,
            build_targets: Optional[bool] = False,
        ) -> TransformedRecord:
            """Transform a single record (internal).
    
            Args:
                record: Dict with ``text`` and ``schema`` keys.
                max_len: Maximum number of word tokens to keep. Truncation happens
                    after word-splitting but before schema encoding, so span
                    character positions in the output always point into the
                    original text string. ``None`` means no truncation.
            """
            # OPT-4: Caller (_collate_batch) already deepcopies the schema.
            # Only deepcopy here for direct callers (transform_and_format).
            text, schema = record["text"], record["schema"]
    
            # Build classification prefix
            prefix = self._build_classification_prefix(schema)
    
            # Save a copy of the original schema BEFORE wrapping modifies it
            # This preserves choice field info for extraction
            original_schema = copy.deepcopy(schema)
    
            # Handle classification field wrapping
            if prefix:
                self._wrap_classification_fields(schema, prefix)
    
            # Tokenize text
            text_tokens = []
            start_idx_map = []
            end_idx_map = []
            for tkn, start, end in self.word_splitter(text, lower=True):
                text_tokens.append(tkn)
                start_idx_map.append(start)
                end_idx_map.append(end)
    
            char_limit = None
            if max_len is not None and len(text_tokens) > max_len:
                text_tokens = text_tokens[:max_len]
                start_idx_map = start_idx_map[:max_len]
                end_idx_map = end_idx_map[:max_len]
                # gold starting past the last retained token was cut, not misplaced
                char_limit = end_idx_map[-1] if end_idx_map else 0
    
            if prefix:
                text_tokens = prefix + text_tokens
            len_prefix = len(prefix)
    
            # Infer schema
            processed = self._infer_from_json(schema)
    
            ctx = _GoldContext(
                text=text,
                text_tokens=text_tokens,
                start_idx_map=start_idx_map,
                end_idx_map=end_idx_map,
                len_prefix=len_prefix,
                char_limit=char_limit,
            )
            results = self._build_outputs(processed, schema, ctx, build_targets=build_targets)
    
            # Format input
            schema_tokens_list = [r["schema_tokens"] for r in results]
            format_result = self._format_input_with_mapping(schema_tokens_list, text_tokens)
    
            return TransformedRecord(
                input_ids=format_result["input_ids"],
                mapped_indices=format_result["mapped_indices"],
                schema_tokens_list=schema_tokens_list,
                text_tokens=text_tokens,
                structure_labels=[r["output"] for r in results],
                task_types=[r["task_type"] for r in results],
                start_token_idx=start_idx_map,
                end_token_idx=end_idx_map,
                text=text,
                schema=original_schema,  # Use original schema with choice info preserved
                text_word_first_positions=format_result["text_word_first_positions"],
                schema_special_positions=format_result["schema_special_positions"],
            )

    +
    +## GLiNER extraction benchmark
    +
    +The separate GLiNER environment measures company spans, per-span roles and
    +article type on source-verified samples. Its image is pinned above; the package
    +and model revisions are pinned in `gliner-requirements.txt` and
    +`gliner-setup.sh`. Setup downloads public model weights and applies a small
    +GLiNER 2.1.0 patch: attribute logits are on the CPU when indexed, so their
    +index tensor must be on that same device. This patch does not change the model
    +weights.
    +
    +```bash
    +bash infra/inference/gliner-setup.sh
    +uv run --project src/python --offline --frozen --all-packages \
    +    python infra/inference/gliner_sample.py --output .runtime/gliner-benchmark/sample
    +bash infra/inference/gliner-run.sh gliner2.5-small-v1 \
    +    --sample .runtime/gliner-benchmark/sample/articles.jsonl \
    +    --output .runtime/gliner-benchmark/results/small-fp16-flash \
    +    --limit 10000 --batch-size 64 --precision fp16 --backend disentangled_flash
    +```
    +
    +The sample is drawn from retained source rows by a seeded SHA-256 priority; its
    +selection and body checksums are recorded. Samples contain article text and
    +remain in ignored local storage. The output preserves model predictions and
    +identifies invalid offsets explicitly. Timings include extraction, validation
    +and compressed output but exclude model loading, warmup and source reads; those
    +are reported separately. They do not establish model accuracy.
    +
    +Long documents are split into overlapping 384-word windows, with 64 words of
    +overlap. GLiNER merges entity spans across windows and selects the highest
    +confidence window's classification. Roles are per extracted mention and need
    +not describe the entire article. These experimental outputs require validation
    +and a separate company-identity linking step before use as research labels.
    +`quantize=True` in GLiNER means FP16; INT8 is a separate TorchAO trial. GLiNER
    +2.1.0 does not allow DisentangledFlash and `torch.compile` simultaneously.

    """Summarize paired GLiNER benchmark outputs without treating them as truth."""
    
    import argparse
    import gzip
    import json
    from collections import Counter
    from pathlib import Path
    
    
    def read_predictions(path: Path) -> dict[str, dict]:
        """Load one prediction per article, rejecting duplicate identifiers."""
        with gzip.open(path, "rt", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            rows = [json.loads(line) for line in stream]
        result = {row["article_id"]: row for row in rows}
        if len(rows) != len(result):
            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate article IDs in {path}")
        return result
    
    
    def spans(row: dict) -> dict[tuple[int, int], str | None]:
        """Return source spans and their per-mention role labels."""
        entities = row["prediction"].get("entities", {}).get("company", [])
        return {
            (entity["start"], entity["end"]): entity.get("article_role", {}).get("label")
            for entity in entities
        }
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Compare a run with a reference configuration on shared valid records."""
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("reference", type=Path)
        parser.add_argument("candidate", type=Path)
        parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        reference = read_predictions(args.reference)
        candidate = read_predictions(args.candidate)
        shared = sorted(reference.keys() & candidate.keys())
        counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
        for key in shared:
            left, right = reference[key], candidate[key]
            if left.get("status", "ok") != "ok" or right.get("status", "ok") != "ok":
                counts["invalid_articles_excluded"] += 1
                continue
            counts["valid_paired_articles"] += 1
            ref_spans, test_spans = spans(left), spans(right)
            counts["reference_spans"] += len(ref_spans)
            counts["candidate_spans"] += len(test_spans)
            common = ref_spans.keys() & test_spans.keys()
            counts["matching_spans"] += len(common)
            counts["matching_span_roles"] += sum(ref_spans[s] == test_spans[s] for s in common)
            counts["same_span_set_articles"] += ref_spans.keys() == test_spans.keys()
            counts["same_article_type"] += (
                left["prediction"].get("article_type", {}).get("label")
                == right["prediction"].get("article_type", {}).get("label")
            )
        report = {
            "reference": str(args.reference),
            "candidate": str(args.candidate),
            "shared_articles": len(shared),
            "counts": dict(counts),
            "interpretation": "Paired agreement only; neither model is ground truth.",
        }
        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(json.dumps(report))
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # Compare candidate runtimes on the same deterministic screening sample.
    set -uo pipefail
    cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
    sample=.runtime/gliner-benchmark/screen.jsonl
    results=.runtime/gliner-benchmark/screen-results
    logs=.runtime/gliner-benchmark/screen-logs
    mkdir -p "$results" "$logs"
    
    run() {
        local name=$1
        local checkpoint=$2
        shift 2
        if timeout 600 bash infra/inference/gliner-run.sh "$checkpoint" \
            --sample "$sample" --output "$results/$name" --limit 500 \
            --batch-size 64 "$@" > "$logs/$name.log" 2>&1; then
            printf '%s\t%s\n' "$name" 0 | tee -a "$logs/status.tsv"
        else
            local status=$?
            printf '%s\t%s\n' "$name" "$status" | tee -a "$logs/status.tsv"
        fi
    }
    
    run small-fp32 gliner2.5-small-v1 --precision fp32
    run small-fp16 gliner2.5-small-v1 --precision fp16
    run small-fp16-flash gliner2.5-small-v1 --precision fp16 --backend disentangled_flash
    run small-bf16-flash gliner2.5-small-v1 --precision bf16 --backend disentangled_flash
    run small-fp16-compiled gliner2.5-small-v1 --precision fp16 --backend compiled
    run small-bf16-compiled gliner2.5-small-v1 --precision bf16 --backend compiled
    run small-int8 gliner2.5-small-v1 --precision int8
    run base-fp16-flash gliner2.5-base-v1 --precision fp16 --backend disentangled_flash

    """Select a reproducible subset of an existing benchmark sample."""
    
    import argparse
    import hashlib
    import json
    from pathlib import Path
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Order articles by a second hash and retain the requested prefix."""
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("sample", type=Path)
        parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
        parser.add_argument("--size", type=int, default=500)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        with args.sample.open(encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            rows = [json.loads(line) for line in stream]
        if not 0 < args.size <= len(rows):
            raise ValueError("Screen size must be positive and no larger than the sample")
        rows.sort(key=lambda row: hashlib.sha256(("screen:" + row["article_id"]).encode()).digest())
        with args.output.open("x", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            for row in rows[: args.size]:
                stream.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    """Compare GLiNER pilot suggestions with previously saved Kev decisions."""
    
    import argparse
    import gzip
    import json
    import unicodedata
    from collections import Counter
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import duckdb
    
    
    def normalize(value: str) -> str:
        """Normalize case and compatibility characters for exact alias comparison."""
        return unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", value).casefold().strip()
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Count descriptive agreement, keeping unresolved Kev records separate."""
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("sample", type=Path)
        parser.add_argument("gliner", type=Path)
        parser.add_argument("kev", type=Path)
        parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        with args.sample.open(encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            articles = {row["article_id"]: row for line in stream if (row := json.loads(line))}
        with gzip.open(args.gliner, "rt", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            predictions = {row["article_id"]: row for line in stream if (row := json.loads(line))}
        kev = duckdb.sql(
            "SELECT article_id, count(*) AS candidates, "
            "count(*) FILTER (WHERE identity_score IS NULL) AS unresolved, "
            "count(*) FILTER (WHERE identity_score >= 0.5) AS mentioned "
            "FROM read_parquet(?) GROUP BY article_id",
            params=[str(args.kev)],
        ).fetchall()
        counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
        for article_id, _, unresolved, mentioned in kev:
            if article_id not in articles or article_id not in predictions:
                counts["missing_gliner"] += 1
                continue
            prediction = predictions[article_id]
            if prediction.get("status", "ok") != "ok":
                counts["invalid_gliner_spans"] += 1
                continue
            if unresolved:
                counts["unresolved_kev"] += 1
                continue
            article = articles[article_id]
            entities = prediction["prediction"].get("entities", {}).get("company", [])
            extracted = {normalize(entity["text"]) for entity in entities}
            aliases = {
                normalize(alias)
                for candidate in article["candidates"]
                for alias in candidate.get("supported_aliases", [])
                if alias
            }
            kev_yes = mentioned > 0
            exact_alias = bool(extracted & aliases)
            counts["eligible_articles"] += 1
            counts["gliner_any_company_span"] += bool(extracted)
            counts[f"kev_{'yes' if kev_yes else 'no'}_exact_alias_{'yes' if exact_alias else 'no'}"] += 1
        report = {
            "counts": dict(counts),
            "kev_threshold": 0.5,

## Assistant

I found the cause of the offset issue: GLiNER appends a full stop during preprocessing. At a window boundary, that synthetic character can also be mapped onto a real character in the next window, so checking only the final document slice is insufficient. I’m accounting for that before treating the extraction output as usable.

    Add: /home/marcussky/Git/CCFinance/infra/inference/gliner_offset_check.py
    """Check GLiNER's patched chunk-to-document offset handling."""
    
    from gliner2.inference.chunking import TextChunk, remap_result_spans
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Exercise synthetic punctuation, original punctuation and invalid offsets."""
        # Arrange: the processor appends a period to the first unpunctuated window.
        source = "Apple next"
        chunk = TextChunk(text="Apple", start_char=0, end_char=5, start_word=0, end_word=1)
        result = {"text": "Apple.", "start": 0, "end": 6, "confidence": 0.9}
    
        # Act: map the model's window coordinates into the original article.
        mapped = remap_result_spans(result, source, chunk)
    
        # Assert: synthetic punctuation does not consume the source's next character.
        assert mapped["text"] == "Apple"
        assert (mapped["start"], mapped["end"]) == (0, 5)
        assert mapped["synthetic_suffix_removed"] is True
    
        # Arrange: the source itself contains punctuation.
        chunk = TextChunk(text="Apple.", start_char=0, end_char=6, start_word=0, end_word=1)
        result = {"text": "Apple.", "start": 0, "end": 6}
    
        # Act: map an unchanged valid span.
        mapped = remap_result_spans(result, "Apple.", chunk)
    
        # Assert: real punctuation survives and no correction is reported.
        assert mapped["text"] == "Apple."
        assert (mapped["start"], mapped["end"]) == (0, 6)
        assert "synthetic_suffix_removed" not in mapped
    
        # Arrange: an unexpected out-of-window offset cannot be repaired safely.
        chunk = TextChunk(text="Apple", start_char=0, end_char=5, start_word=0, end_word=1)
        result = {"text": "unexpected", "start": 0, "end": 7}
    
        # Act: map the unexpected result.
        mapped = remap_result_spans(result, source, chunk)
    
        # Assert: the caller can reject it even if the document slice exists.
        assert mapped["invalid_window_span"] is True
        print("GLiNER window-offset checks passed")
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    Add: /home/marcussky/Git/CCFinance/infra/inference/gliner_device_check.py
    """Compare CPU and CUDA FP32 predictions after the attribute-index patch."""
    
    import json
    
    import torch
    from gliner2 import AttributeGroup, AutoExtractor
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Run one multi-company example on CPU and GPU with the same weights."""
        # Arrange: request entities, their roles and article type in the same schema.
        torch.set_num_threads(4)
        model = AutoExtractor.from_pretrained("/model", map_location="cpu")
        schema = (
            model.create_schema()
            .entities({"company": "Names of companies and businesses"})
            .entity_attributes(
                {
                    "article_role": AttributeGroup(
                        ["primary", "secondary", "incidental", "uncertain"],
                        applies_to=["company"],
                        qualify_labels=True,
                    )
                }
            )
            .classification(
                "article_type", ["reporting", "opinion", "press release", "promotional", "other"]
            )
        )
        article = "Apple reported earnings. Microsoft was mentioned."
    
        # Act: extract the same schema before and after transferring the model.
        cpu = model.extract(article, schema, include_spans=True, include_confidence=True)
        model.to("cuda")
        gpu = model.extract(article, schema, include_spans=True, include_confidence=True)
    
        # Assert: both devices return the same spans and discrete role labels.
        def labels(result: dict) -> set[tuple]:
            return {
                (entity["start"], entity["end"], entity["text"], entity["article_role"]["label"])
                for entity in result["entities"]["company"]
            }
    
        assert labels(cpu)
        assert labels(cpu) == labels(gpu)
        assert cpu["article_type"]["label"] == gpu["article_type"]["label"]
        print(json.dumps({"cpu": cpu, "cuda": gpu}))
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # Compare batch sizes after the window-offset fix on the same screening sample.
    set -euo pipefail
    cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
    results=.runtime/gliner-benchmark/batch-results
    logs=.runtime/gliner-benchmark/batch-logs
    mkdir -p "$results" "$logs"
    for batch_size in 64 128 256; do
        if timeout 600 bash infra/inference/gliner-run.sh gliner2.5-small-v1 \
            --sample .runtime/gliner-benchmark/screen.jsonl \
            --output "$results/fp16-compiled-b$batch_size" --limit 500 \
            --batch-size "$batch_size" --precision fp16 --backend compiled \
            > "$logs/b$batch_size.log" 2>&1; then
            printf '%s\t%s\n' "$batch_size" 0 | tee -a "$logs/status.tsv"
        else
            status=$?
            printf '%s\t%s\n' "$batch_size" "$status" | tee -a "$logs/status.tsv"
        fi
    done

            attribute_rows: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
            for group in groups.values():

                    prompt = prompt_labels.get(label, label)
                    query_id = query_by_name.get(prompt)
                    if query_id is not None:
                        attribute_rows.append((label, query_id))
            # Labels are unique across groups by Schema.entity_attributes validation.

            indices = pair_tensor.view(1, 1, len(unique_pairs), 2).expand(

            query_states = core["query_states"][

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # Measure the selected compiled configuration on the pilot and full sample.
    set -euo pipefail
    cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
    batch_size=${1:-64}
    results=.runtime/gliner-benchmark/final-results
    logs=.runtime/gliner-benchmark/final-logs
    mkdir -p "$results" "$logs"
    
    run() {
        local name=$1
        local sample=$2
        local limit=$3
        if timeout 900 bash infra/inference/gliner-run.sh gliner2.5-small-v1 \
            --sample "$sample" --output "$results/$name" --limit "$limit" \
            --batch-size "$batch_size" --precision fp16 --backend compiled \
            > "$logs/$name.log" 2>&1; then
            cp infra/inference/gliner_benchmark.py "$results/$name/runner.py"
            printf '%s\t%s\n' "$name" 0 | tee -a "$logs/status.tsv"
        else
            local status=$?
            printf '%s\t%s\n' "$name" "$status" | tee -a "$logs/status.tsv"
            return "$status"
        fi
    }
    
    run pilot .runtime/gliner-benchmark/pilot-1000/articles.jsonl 1000
    for repeat in 1 2 3; do
        run "full-$repeat" .runtime/gliner-benchmark/sample/articles.jsonl 10000
    done

    """Collect local benchmark evidence without copying source article bodies."""
    
    import argparse
    import hashlib
    import json
    import shutil
    from pathlib import Path
    
    
    def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
        """Return the file's SHA-256 digest."""
        with path.open("rb") as stream:
            return hashlib.file_digest(stream, "sha256").hexdigest()
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Copy selections, predictions, reports, logs, and the executing code."""
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        runtime = Path(".runtime/gliner-benchmark")
        args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
        for name in ("sample", "pilot-1000"):
            destination = args.output / name
            destination.mkdir()
            for filename in ("selection.parquet", "selection.json", "sample.json"):
                shutil.copy2(runtime / name / filename, destination / filename)
        with (runtime / "screen.jsonl").open(encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            ids = [json.loads(line)["article_id"] for line in stream]
        (args.output / "screen-article-ids.json").write_text(json.dumps(ids, indent=2) + "\n")
        for name in ("screen-results", "screen-logs", "batch-results", "batch-logs", "final-results", "final-logs"):
            shutil.copytree(runtime / name, args.output / name)
        for name in ("invalid-span-repro", "invalid-span-corrected", "small-fp16-flash-b64-full-2"):
            shutil.copytree(runtime / "results" / name, args.output / "earlier-runs" / name)
        shutil.copy2(runtime / "device-check.log", args.output / "device-check.log")
        code = args.output / "code"
        code.mkdir()
        for file in sorted(Path("infra/inference").glob("gliner*")):
            if file.is_file():
                shutil.copy2(file, code / file.name)
        weights = {
            name: sha256(Path(".runtime/models") / name / "model.safetensors")
            for name in ("gliner2.5-small-v1", "gliner2.5-base-v1")
        }
        manifest = {
            "image": "lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:f7876bef696ccf9cf75a2bf7ccb82970f5fac577f082fb8ca95c9a59d2160eb5",
            "models": {
                "gliner2.5-small-v1": {"revision": "b5d42bf7dc7d01c40304ae4ed43c2f13c325a75b", "weights_sha256": weights["gliner2.5-small-v1"]},
                "gliner2.5-base-v1": {"revision": "07d99c0ba5d15cb3b24e0a236fa99bdd4ef87a5c", "weights_sha256": weights["gliner2.5-base-v1"]},
            },
            "code_sha256": {file.name: sha256(file) for file in sorted(code.iterdir())},
            "article_bodies_included": False,
        }
        (args.output / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n")
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

## User

Our aim should be:
```
>>> 12_000_000/(24*60*60)
138.88888888888889
```
articles per second. Given this GPU supports bfloat16, fp8 and NVFP4, and bfloat alone usually is a 50% increase in throughput with negligible quality loss, and modern optimized kernels around often a 2X performance boost, with batch size optimization and pre-fetching/data loading optimizations offering another 2X in performance, this seems quite feasible.

## Assistant

Yes—**139 articles/sec for 12 million records** is the target. There’s room to optimize further, but the gains need to be measured together: BF16 was slower than FP16 in the current tests, and larger batches also reduced throughput. I’ll check what is limiting the run and which FP8/NVFP4 paths actually support this model on the 5060 Ti.

    class Float8DynamicActivationFloat8WeightConfig(AOBaseConfig):
        """
        Configuration for applying float8 dynamic symmetric quantization to both activations and weights of linear layers.
    
        Args:
            activation_dtype (torch.dtype): The target data type for activation quantization. Default is torch.float8_e4m3fn.
            weight_dtype (torch.dtype): The target data type for weight quantization. Default is torch.float8_e4m3fn.
            granularity (Optional[Union[FP8Granularity, List[FP8Granularity]]]):
                The granularity for quantization. Can be either a single granularity (applied to both
                activations and weights) or a tuple of two granularities (one for activations, one for weights).
                If None, defaults to PerTensor for both. Currently both quantizations need to be the same type. And
                only PerTensor and PerRow are supported.
            mm_config (Float8MMConfig): Configuration for the matrix multiplication. Default uses fast accumulation.
            activation_value_lb (Optional[float]): the lower bound for activation value for calculating scale
            activation_value_ub (Optional[float]): the upper bound for activation value for calculating scale
            kernel_preference (KernelPreference): kernel preference for ops like matmul, grouped matmul etc. by defalut (KernelPreference.AUTO) it will be chosen for user based on hardware or other information, this only needs to be set in weight
            set_inductor_config (bool): if True, adjusts `torchinductor` settings to recommended values.
            version (int): the version of the config, version 1 is deprecated, version 2 is using Float8Tensor (default)
    
        Example:
    
        .. literalinclude:: ../../examples/inference/float8_dynamic_activation_float8_weight.py
           :language: python
        """
    
        activation_dtype: torch.dtype = e4m3_dtype
        weight_dtype: torch.dtype = e4m3_dtype
        granularity: Optional[Union[FP8Granularity, List[FP8Granularity]]] = None
        packing_format: Optional[Float8PackingFormat] = Float8PackingFormat.PLAIN
        mm_config: Optional[Float8MMConfig] = None
        activation_value_lb: Optional[float] = None
        activation_value_ub: Optional[float] = None
        kernel_preference: KernelPreference = KernelPreference.AUTO
        set_inductor_config: bool = True
        version: int = 2
    
        def __post_init__(self):
            torch._C._log_api_usage_once(
                "torchao.quantization.Float8DynamicActivationFloat8WeightConfig"
            )
            activation_granularity, weight_granularity = _normalize_granularity(
                self.granularity
            )
            self.granularity = [activation_granularity, weight_granularity]
    
            default_use_fast_accum = True
            if _granularity_is_a_1_128_w_128_128(self.granularity):
                assert self.kernel_preference in (
                    KernelPreference.AUTO,
                    KernelPreference.TORCH,
                ), "unimplemented"
                assert self.version >= 2, "unimplemented"
                default_use_fast_accum = False
            if torch.xpu.is_available():
                # XPU does not support fast_accum for now
                default_use_fast_accum = False
    
            if self.mm_config is None:
                self.mm_config = Float8MMConfig(use_fast_accum=default_use_fast_accum)
    
    
    def _float8_dynamic_activation_float8_weight_quantize_tensor(weight, config):
        activation_dtype = config.activation_dtype
        weight_dtype = config.weight_dtype
        granularity = config.granularity

    class NVFP4DynamicActivationNVFP4WeightConfig(AOBaseConfig):
        """
        NVIDIA FP4 (NVFP4) Inference Quantization Configuration
    
        This is a specialized configuration for NVIDIA's FP4 format.
        NVFP4 uses "double quantization" with two scale levels:
        - A global per_tensor_scale (float32)
        - Per-block scales (float8_e4m3fn, block_size=16), always dynamically calculated
    
        The activation per_tensor_scale can be determined in two ways:
    
        1. Dynamic per_tensor_scale (default, step=None, use_dynamic_per_tensor_scale=True):
            - Both weight and activation per_tensor_scale are computed at runtime
              from the tensor amax
    
        2. Static per_tensor_scale via observer flow (step="prepare"/"convert"):
            - Weight per_tensor_scale is computed from weight amax at convert time
            - Activation per_tensor_scale is determined statically during calibration:
              step="prepare" inserts observers, then after running calibration data,
              step="convert" extracts the observed amax and bakes the activation
              per_tensor_scale into the quantized weight tensor
            - At inference, the static activation per_tensor_scale is read from the
              weight tensor instead of being computed dynamically
            - Note: activation per-block scales are still computed dynamically at
              inference time
    
        Note: When step is specified, use_dynamic_per_tensor_scale is automatically
        set to False.
    
        Configuration parameters:
        - use_triton_kernel: bool, whether to use fused triton kernel for activation scaling (default: True).
          Requires `MSLK <https://github.com/pytorch/MSLK>`__ to be installed.
        - use_dynamic_per_tensor_scale: bool, whether to dynamically compute per tensor scale (default: True)
        - step: Optional[QuantizationStep], the quantization step for observer-based flow
        - Data: float4_e2m1fn_x2
        - Scales: float8_e4m3fn
        - Block size: 16 along the reduction dim
    
        Note: Triton kernel only works with DYNAMIC mode and has constraints that input dimensions
        must satisfy M % 128 == 0 and K % 64 == 0. Will automatically fallback when constraints aren't met.
    
        Example:
    
        .. literalinclude:: ../../examples/inference/nvfp4_dynamic_activation_nvfp4_weight.py
           :language: python
        """
    
        use_triton_kernel: bool = True
        use_dynamic_per_tensor_scale: bool = True
        step: Optional["QuantizationStep"] = None
    
        def __post_init__(self):
            if isinstance(self.step, str):
                self.step = QuantizationStep(self.step)
            # Validate PyTorch version
            if not torch_version_at_least("2.8.0"):
                raise RuntimeError(
                    "NVFP4DynamicActivationNVFP4WeightConfig requires PyTorch 2.8 or later"
                )
    
            if self.step is not None:
                # Static quantization implies use_dynamic_per_tensor_scale=False
                self.use_dynamic_per_tensor_scale = False

        def forward(self, text_states: torch.Tensor, text_mask: torch.BoolTensor) -> BoundaryEncoding:
            b, l, h = text_states.shape
            text_lengths = text_mask.sum(dim=1).long()  # [B]
    
            left = shift_left_with_bos(text_states, self.bos_state)     # [B, L+1, H]
            right = shift_right_with_eos(text_states, text_lengths, self.eos_state)
    
            left_p = self.left_projection(left)
            right_p = self.right_projection(right)
            states = self.output_projection(torch.cat([left_p, right_p], dim=-1))
            states = self.layer_norm(states)
            states = self.dropout(states)
            mask = build_boundary_mask(text_lengths, l)  # [B, L+1]
            for block in self.attention_blocks:
                states = block(states, mask)
            for block in self.refinement_blocks:
                states = block(states)
    
            # Zero out padding boundary states so they cannot leak into downstream
            # gathers/scores through numerical noise.
            states = states * mask.unsqueeze(-1).to(states.dtype)
            return BoundaryEncoding(states=states, mask=mask)

    """Profile warmed extraction; profiler timings are not throughput measurements."""
    
    import argparse
    import cProfile
    import json
    import pstats
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import torch
    from gliner2 import AutoExtractor
    from gliner_schema import build_schema
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Attribute CPU calls and CUDA operators for a small, warmed real sample."""
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("--sample", type=Path, required=True)
        parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
        parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=64)
        parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=64)
        parser.add_argument("--backend", choices=["compiled", "disentangled_flash"], default="compiled")
        args = parser.parse_args()
        args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
        with args.sample.open(encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            texts = [json.loads(line)["text"] for _, line in zip(range(args.limit), stream, strict=False)]
        model = AutoExtractor.from_pretrained(
            "/model", map_location="cuda", quantize=True,
            compile=args.backend == "compiled",
            attention_backend="disentangled_flash" if args.backend == "disentangled_flash" else "standard",
        )
        schema = build_schema(model)
    
        def extract():
            return model.batch_extract_long(
                texts, schema, batch_size=args.batch_size,
                include_spans=True, include_confidence=True,
            )
    
        extract()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        calls = cProfile.Profile()
        with torch.profiler.profile(activities=[torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CPU, torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CUDA]) as profile:
            calls.enable()
            extract()
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
            calls.disable()
        calls.dump_stats(args.output / "calls.prof")
        with (args.output / "cpu-functions.txt").open("w") as stream:
            pstats.Stats(calls, stream=stream).sort_stats("cumulative").print_stats(50)
        for name, key in (("cpu-operators", "self_cpu_time_total"), ("cuda-operators", "self_device_time_total")):
            (args.output / f"{name}.txt").write_text(profile.key_averages().table(sort_by=key, row_limit=40) + "\n")
        print("Profile saved; use unprofiled benchmark runs for throughput.")
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    """The shared extraction contract used by local GLiNER experiments."""
    
    from gliner2 import AttributeGroup
    
    
    def build_schema(model):
        """Request company spans, per-mention roles, and the article's text type."""
        return (
            model.create_schema()
            .entities({"company": "Names of companies and businesses"})
            .entity_attributes(
                {
                    "article_role": AttributeGroup(
                        ["primary", "secondary", "incidental", "uncertain"],
                        applies_to=["company"],
                        qualify_labels=True,
                    )
                }
            )
            .classification(
                "article_type", ["reporting", "opinion", "press release", "promotional", "other"]
            )
        )

    """Check low-precision CUDA linear kernels independently of model accuracy."""
    
    import argparse
    import copy
    import json
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import torch
    from torchao.quantization import Float8DynamicActivationFloat8WeightConfig, quantize_
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Test the encoder's representative matrix dimensions on this GPU."""
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("--format", choices=["fp8", "nvfp4"], required=True)
        parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        torch.manual_seed(42)
        model = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Linear(384, 1536), torch.nn.GELU(), torch.nn.Linear(1536, 384)
        ).to(device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16).eval()
        reference = copy.deepcopy(model)
        if args.format == "fp8":
            config = Float8DynamicActivationFloat8WeightConfig()
        else:
            from torchao.prototype.mx_formats.inference_workflow import NVFP4DynamicActivationNVFP4WeightConfig
    
            config = NVFP4DynamicActivationNVFP4WeightConfig(use_triton_kernel=False)
        quantize_(model, config)
        inputs = torch.randn(4096, 384, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        with torch.inference_mode():
            expected = reference(inputs)
            observed = model(inputs)
            if not torch.isfinite(observed).all():
                raise ValueError("Low-precision kernel returned non-finite outputs")
            difference = (expected.float() - observed.float()).abs()
            result = {
                "format": args.format,
                "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
                "capability": torch.cuda.get_device_capability(),
                "input_device": str(inputs.device),
                "output_device": str(observed.device),
                "output_dtype": str(observed.dtype),
                "mean_absolute_error": difference.mean().item(),
                "max_absolute_error": difference.max().item(),
                "interpretation": "Kernel compatibility probe, not model accuracy or throughput.",
            }
        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(json.dumps(result))
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    """Load the local extractor with explicit precision and attention choices."""
    
    from collections import Counter
    
    import torch
    from gliner2 import AutoExtractor
    
    
    def load_model(path: str, precision: str, backend: str):
        """Set precision before preparing attention kernels or compiling the model."""
        model = AutoExtractor.from_pretrained(path, map_location="cuda")
        if precision == "fp16":
            model.to(dtype=torch.float16)
        elif precision in {"bf16", "fp8", "nvfp4"}:
            model.to(dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        if precision in {"int8", "fp8", "nvfp4"}:
            from torchao.quantization import quantize_
    
            if backend == "disentangled_flash":
                raise ValueError("Quantized encoder projections need separate backend validation")
            if precision == "int8":
                from torchao.quantization import Int8WeightOnlyConfig
    
                config = Int8WeightOnlyConfig()
            elif precision == "fp8":
                from torchao.quantization import Float8DynamicActivationFloat8WeightConfig
    
                config = Float8DynamicActivationFloat8WeightConfig()
            else:
                from torchao.prototype.mx_formats.inference_workflow import NVFP4DynamicActivationNVFP4WeightConfig
    
                config = NVFP4DynamicActivationNVFP4WeightConfig(use_triton_kernel=False)
            quantize_(model.encoder, config)
        model.eval()
        if backend == "disentangled_flash":
            model.enable_disentangled_flash()
        elif backend == "compiled":
            model.compile(dynamic=True)
        devices = {str(parameter.device) for parameter in model.parameters()}
        if not devices or any(not device.startswith("cuda:") for device in devices):
            raise ValueError(f"Model parameters are not entirely on CUDA: {devices}")
        metadata = {
            "parameter_devices": sorted(devices),
            "parameter_dtypes": dict(Counter(str(p.dtype) for p in model.parameters())),
            "compute_capability": torch.cuda.get_device_capability(),
        }
        return model, metadata

    """Measure full-document GLiNER extraction on a prepared article sample."""
    
    import argparse
    import gzip
    import json
    import time
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import torch
    from gliner2 import AttributeGroup, AutoExtractor
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Run one isolated model configuration and save timings and predictions."""
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("--sample", type=Path, required=True)
        parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)
        parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
        parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=100)
        parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=8)
        parser.add_argument("--gpu-memory-fraction", type=float, default=0.8)
        parser.add_argument(
            "--precision", choices=["fp32", "fp16", "bf16", "int8"], default="fp32"
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--backend",
            choices=["standard", "compiled", "disentangled_flash"],
            default="standard",
        )
        args = parser.parse_args()
        if not 0 < args.gpu_memory_fraction <= 1:
            raise ValueError("GPU memory fraction must be in (0, 1]")
        torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction(args.gpu_memory_fraction)
        args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
        start = time.perf_counter()
        with args.sample.open(encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            articles = [
                json.loads(line) for _, line in zip(range(args.limit), stream, strict=False)
            ]
        if len(articles) != args.limit:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected {args.limit} articles; got {len(articles)}")
        read_seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        start = time.perf_counter()
        model = AutoExtractor.from_pretrained(
            args.model,
            map_location="cuda",
            quantize=args.precision == "fp16",
            compile=args.backend == "compiled",
            attention_backend="disentangled_flash"
            if args.backend == "disentangled_flash"
            else "standard",
        )
        if args.precision == "bf16":
            model.to(dtype=torch.bfloat16)

            from torchao.quantization import Int8WeightOnlyConfig, quantize_

            model.create_schema()

                    "article_role": AttributeGroup(
                        ["primary", "secondary", "incidental", "uncertain"],
                        applies_to=["company"],
                        qualify_labels=True,
                    )
                }
            )
            .classification(
                "article_type",
                ["reporting", "opinion", "press release", "promotional", "other"],
            )
        )
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        load_seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        start = time.perf_counter()
        model.batch_extract_long(
            [item["text"] for item in articles[: min(args.batch_size, len(articles))]],
            schema,
            batch_size=args.batch_size,
            include_spans=True,
            include_confidence=True,
        )
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        warmup_seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        start = time.perf_counter()
        output = args.output / "predictions.jsonl.gz"

        invalid_articles = 0

        corrected_articles = 0

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # Compare buffered preprocessing and low-precision kernels on paired records.
    set -euo pipefail
    cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
    results=.runtime/gliner-benchmark/throughput-results
    logs=.runtime/gliner-benchmark/throughput-logs
    mkdir -p "$results" "$logs"
    
    run() {
        local name=$1
        shift
        if timeout 900 bash infra/inference/gliner-run.sh gliner2.5-small-v1 \
            --sample .runtime/gliner-benchmark/sample/articles.jsonl \
            --output "$results/$name" --limit 2000 --batch-size 64 \
            --buffer-size 2048 "$@" > "$logs/$name.log" 2>&1; then
            cp infra/inference/gliner_benchmark.py "$results/$name/runner.py"
            printf '%s\t%s\n' "$name" 0 | tee -a "$logs/status.tsv"
        else
            local status=$?
            printf '%s\t%s\n' "$name" "$status" | tee -a "$logs/status.tsv"
        fi
    }
    
    run fp16-compiled-w0 --precision fp16 --backend compiled --workers 0
    run fp16-compiled-w4 --precision fp16 --backend compiled --workers 4
    run fp16-flash-w4 --precision fp16 --backend disentangled_flash --workers 4
    run fp16-flash-heads-w4 --precision fp16 --backend disentangled_flash_heads --workers 4
    run bf16-flash-heads-w4 --precision bf16 --backend disentangled_flash_heads --workers 4
    run fp8-compiled-w4 --precision fp8 --backend compiled --workers 4
    run nvfp4-compiled-w4 --precision nvfp4 --backend compiled --workers 4

    +The GPU batch size and article buffer size are separate. A larger article
    +buffer lets GLiNER's DataLoader prepare future window batches while the GPU
    +processes the current batch. Use `--buffer-size 2048 --workers 4` to test this
    +schedule; the container provides 1 GiB of shared memory for worker transfers.
    +The benchmark caps its CUDA allocator at 80% of device memory by default.

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # Check batch scaling with buffered preprocessing and the hybrid attention path.
    set -euo pipefail
    cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
    results=.runtime/gliner-benchmark/buffer-batch-results
    logs=.runtime/gliner-benchmark/buffer-batch-logs
    mkdir -p "$results" "$logs"
    for batch_size in 128 256; do
        if timeout 600 bash infra/inference/gliner-run.sh gliner2.5-small-v1 \
            --sample .runtime/gliner-benchmark/sample/articles.jsonl \
            --output "$results/fp16-b$batch_size" --limit 2000 \
            --batch-size "$batch_size" --buffer-size 2048 --workers 4 \
            --precision fp16 --backend disentangled_flash_heads \
            > "$logs/b$batch_size.log" 2>&1; then
            printf '%s\t%s\n' "$batch_size" 0 | tee -a "$logs/status.tsv"
        else
            status=$?
            printf '%s\t%s\n' "$batch_size" "$status" | tee -a "$logs/status.tsv"
        fi
    done

    """Validate saved extraction structure and finite confidence scores."""
    
    import argparse
    import gzip
    import json
    import math
    from collections import Counter
    from pathlib import Path
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Check saved outputs without treating structural validity as accuracy."""
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("predictions", type=Path)
        parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
        seen: set[str] = set()
        with gzip.open(args.predictions, "rt", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            for line in stream:
                row = json.loads(line)
                article_id = row["article_id"]
                if article_id in seen:
                    raise ValueError(f"Duplicate article: {article_id}")
                seen.add(article_id)
                prediction = row["prediction"]
                article_type = prediction.get("article_type", {})
                entities = prediction.get("entities", {}).get("company", [])
                values = [article_type, *entities, *[entity.get("article_role", {}) for entity in entities]]
                invalid = not all(
                    isinstance(value.get("confidence"), (int, float))
                    and math.isfinite(value["confidence"])
                    and 0 <= value["confidence"] <= 1
                    for value in values
                )
                counts["articles"] += 1
                counts["invalid_confidence_articles"] += invalid
                counts["invalid_span_articles"] += row.get("status", "ok") != "ok"
                counts["articles_with_company_spans"] += bool(entities)
                counts["company_spans"] += len(entities)
        report = {"counts": dict(counts), "interpretation": "Structural checks only; no semantic accuracy claim."}
        args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(json.dumps(report))
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    # CHANGELOG
    
    ## Unreleased
    
    ### Added
    
    - Corpus-wide company candidates with dated issuer corrections, source-only
      audits, provisional native Kev judgments, resumable checkpoints and observed
      company-year coverage reports.
    - Source-comparison DVC stages with metadata preparation, selective Parquet reads
      and exploratory estimates of publisher-filter yield.
    - Statsmodels LaTeX summaries and individual yield and population tables for papers.
    - Frozen Fine News acquisition recipe with the historical publisher filter.
    - Python and LaTeX toolchains generated from Exordio, with locked dependencies.
    - Typer `pipeline` application and a namespace for data processing stages.
    - DVC repository configuration and a workspace for research data.
    - Ruff, strict Pyrefly, Tach, tests and package builds in local checks and CI.
    - Planning and local reference workflows with Schematter validation and Insitu views.
    - A validated changelog with a closed set of change categories.
    - Semflow integration for reviewing and checking semantic DVC fingerprints.
    - pytest-layout-enforcer for source-aligned test paths.
    - Justfile formatting and analysis checks in pre-commit and CI.
    - Agent skill schema and validation for metadata, structure and length.
    - AgentSync-managed shared instructions, skills and Codex configuration.
    
    ### Changed
    
    - Use current progress when reporting a resumed scoring run, keeping counts,
      status and timing from the same snapshot.
    - Restored the published Fine News shards with verified checksums and provenance
      so the frozen acquisition stage has real outputs for DVC to validate.
    - Grouped experiments within each data layer and consolidated source mappings
      and validated artifact contracts across sampling and research reports.
    - Organized the pipeline into `raw`, `processed` and `research` layers, with
      matching Python modules, CLI groups and proposed data paths.

    # Filter articles and score company coverage
    
    ## Goal
    
    Complete the corpus-wide CPU filter, then size native Kev scoring against
    07:00 SAST on 17 November 2026. Preserve source records, all company candidates,
    exclusion reasons and unresolved outcomes. AI-only review remains exploratory;
    the 95% precision target is not a validated accuracy claim.
    
    The data pipeline agent owns CPU selection, the runtime agent owns native Kev,
    and the research agent owns reconciliation and reports. The coordinating agent
    owns their contracts, DVC integration and the deadline decision. See the
    [labeling guide](../../../../../data/inputs/article-labels/README.md).
    
    ## Acceptance
    
    - [x] Materialize and reconcile the complete CPU selection against the frozen source.
    - [x] Verify native Kev multi-company inference and measure its completion estimate.
    - [x] Preserve resumable scores, uncertainty and an honest completion status.
    - [x] Record data dependencies, methods and the required repository checks.
    
    ## Results
    
    The complete CPU census reconciles. The fixed 1,000-record benchmark scored 993
    records and preserved seven context deferrals without server failures. Its
    6.40 successful records/second implies about 22 days for the current broad
    selection. No full-corpus GPU run was launched. All scores remain provisional,
    and no company pair meets the current 0.95 acceptance policy.
    
    The independent [CPU audit](../../../../../data/research/experiments/article-labels/cpu-audit/report.md)
    found generic aliases, publisher-keyword collisions, article furniture and dated
    company-name contamination. In the fixed sample, 226 records have completely
    observed candidate evidence limited to five generic aliases. See the
    [candidate-quality follow-up](../candidate-quality/README.md) before production
    scoring. The audit's 25 retained and 20 no-hit reviews are AI observations,
    not validated accuracy measurements.
    
    `just check` passed, including 39 tests, Ruff, Pyrefly, Tach, test layout,
    Semflow, DVC metadata, document schemas and the LaTeX build. Existing source
    comparison results retain their original lock provenance; the new dependency
    lock correctly marks those earlier stages stale.

    def main() -> int:
        """Dispatch document creation, validation and view updates."""
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
        for name in ("plan-new", "task-new", "reference-new"):
            command = commands.add_parser(name)
            if name == "task-new":
                command.add_argument("parent")
            command.add_argument("slug")
            command.add_argument("--title", required=True)
        for name in ("prepare", "sync", "check"):
            commands.add_parser(name)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        try:
            if args.command == "prepare":
                run(
                    ROOT,
                    "bash",
                    str(ROOT / "infra/nix/prepare-runtime.sh"),
                    str(Path(sys.executable).with_name("insitu")),
                )
            elif args.command.endswith("-new"):
                kind = args.command.removesuffix("-new")
                parent = getattr(args, "parent", None)
                print(create_record(kind, args.slug, args.title, parent=parent))
            else:
                records = read_records()
                schema_check(ROOT, records)
                errors = validate_records(ROOT, records)
                if errors:
                    raise ValueError("\n".join(errors))
                insitu(ROOT, args.command)
        except (
            ValueError,
            OSError,
            yaml.YAMLError,
            subprocess.CalledProcessError,
        ) as error:
            print(f"workflow: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        return 0
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        raise SystemExit(main())

    292:def create_record(
        """Create a new plan, task or local reference without overwriting files."""
        workflow = "reference" if kind == "reference" else "planning"
        if workflow not in config(root)["workflows"]:
            raise ValueError(f"{workflow} is not selected")
        if not SLUG.fullmatch(slug):
            raise ValueError(
                "slug must use lowercase words, digits and single hyphens, "
                "starting with a letter"
            )
        if not title.strip() or "\n" in title or "\r" in title or len(title.strip()) > 160:
            raise ValueError("title must occupy one line with between 1 and 160 characters")
        title = title.strip()
        directory = (
            root / ".context" / ("reference" if kind == "reference" else "plan") / slug
        )
        if kind == "task":
            container = (root / (parent or "")).resolve()
            if container.name == "README.md":
                container = container.parent
            if not container.is_relative_to(root.resolve() / ".context" / "plan"):
                raise ValueError(
                    "parent must be an existing plan or task within .context/plan"
                )
            role = path_kind(container / "README.md", root)
            data, _ = read_document(container / "README.md")
            if (
                role not in {"plan", "task"}
                or data.get("type") != role
                or data.get("status") not in ("backlog", "in-progress", "blocked")
            ):
                raise ValueError("parent must be an open plan or task")
            directory = container / "tasks" / slug
        if not directory.resolve().is_relative_to(root.resolve()):
            raise ValueError("record destination escapes the repository")
        data = {
            "type": "document" if kind == "reference" else kind,
            "title": title,
            "description": title,
            "links": [],
        }
        body = f"# {title}\n\n"
        if kind != "reference":
            data["status"] = "backlog"
            body += f"## Goal\n\n{title}\n\n## Acceptance\n\n"
            body += (
                "- [ ] Define and verify the intended outcome.\n\n"
                + CHILDREN_BLOCK
                + "\n\n"
            )
        else:
            body += "Summarize the source and why it matters here.\n\n"

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # Repeat the selected buffered hybrid configuration on the full article sample.
    set -euo pipefail
    cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
    batch_size=${1:-64}
    precision=${2:-fp16}
    results=.runtime/gliner-benchmark/buffer-final-results
    logs=.runtime/gliner-benchmark/buffer-final-logs
    mkdir -p "$results" "$logs"
    for repeat in 1 2 3; do
        name="$precision-b$batch_size-$repeat"
        if timeout 900 bash infra/inference/gliner-run.sh gliner2.5-small-v1 \
            --sample .runtime/gliner-benchmark/sample/articles.jsonl \
            --output "$results/$name" --limit 10000 --batch-size "$batch_size" \
            --buffer-size 2048 --workers 4 --precision "$precision" \
            --backend disentangled_flash_heads > "$logs/$name.log" 2>&1; then
            cp infra/inference/gliner_benchmark.py "$results/$name/runner.py"
            printf '%s\t%s\n' "$name" 0 | tee -a "$logs/status.tsv"
        else
            status=$?
            printf '%s\t%s\n' "$name" "$status" | tee -a "$logs/status.tsv"
            exit "$status"
        fi
    done

    """Compare CPU and CUDA FP32 predictions after the attribute-index patch."""
    
    import json
    
    import torch
    from gliner2 import AttributeGroup, AutoExtractor
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Run one multi-company example on CPU and GPU with the same weights."""
        # Arrange: request entities, their roles and article type in the same schema.
        torch.set_num_threads(4)
        model = AutoExtractor.from_pretrained("/model", map_location="cpu")
        schema = (
            model.create_schema()
            .entities({"company": "Names of companies and businesses"})
            .entity_attributes(
                {
                    "article_role": AttributeGroup(
                        ["primary", "secondary", "incidental", "uncertain"],
                        applies_to=["company"],
                        qualify_labels=True,
                    )
                }
            )
            .classification(
                "article_type",
                ["reporting", "opinion", "press release", "promotional", "other"],
            )
        )
        article = "Apple reported earnings. Microsoft was mentioned."
    
        # Act: extract the same schema before and after transferring the model.
        cpu = model.extract(article, schema, include_spans=True, include_confidence=True)
        model.to("cuda")
        gpu = model.extract(article, schema, include_spans=True, include_confidence=True)
    
        # Assert: both devices return the same spans and discrete role labels.
        def labels(result: dict) -> set[tuple]:
            return {
                (
                    entity["start"],
                    entity["end"],
                    entity["text"],
                    entity["article_role"]["label"],
                )
                for entity in result["entities"]["company"]
            }
    
        if not labels(cpu) or labels(cpu) != labels(gpu):
            raise AssertionError("CPU and CUDA company spans or roles differ")
        if cpu["article_type"]["label"] != gpu["article_type"]["label"]:
            raise AssertionError("CPU and CUDA article types differ")
        print(json.dumps({"cpu": cpu, "cuda": gpu}))
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

            if indices.dim() != 4 or indices.shape[-1] != 2:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"indices must be [B, Q, C, 2], got {tuple(indices.shape)}"
                )
            b, q, _, _ = indices.shape

    def _group_scored_candidates(
        candidates: CandidateTensorBatch,
        *,
        threshold: Union[float, torch.Tensor] = 0.5,
        probabilities: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        count_log_rates: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        adaptive_threshold: bool = False,
    ) -> List[List[List[Tuple[float, int, int]]]]:
        """Threshold candidates and optionally add top scores up to a predicted count."""
        b, q, c, _ = candidates.indices.shape
        probs = (
            torch.sigmoid(candidates.pair_logits)
            if probabilities is None else probabilities
        )
        eligible = candidates.valid_mask & candidates.query_mask.unsqueeze(-1)
        threshold_value = threshold
        if isinstance(threshold, torch.Tensor):
            if threshold.shape != probs.shape[:2]:
                raise ValueError(
                    "tensor threshold must be [B, Q], got "
                    f"{tuple(threshold.shape)} for probabilities {tuple(probs.shape)}"
                )
            threshold_value = threshold.to(
                device=probs.device, dtype=probs.dtype
            ).unsqueeze(-1)
        keep = eligible & (probs >= threshold_value)
        if adaptive_threshold:
            if count_log_rates is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "adaptive threshold decoding requires count_log_rates"
                )
            predicted_count = torch.exp(count_log_rates).round().long().clamp(
                min=0, max=c
            )
            ranked_scores = probs.masked_fill(~eligible, MASK_LOGIT)
            order = torch.argsort(
                ranked_scores, dim=-1, descending=True, stable=True
            )
            rank = torch.argsort(order, dim=-1)
            # Union with threshold hits: count guidance fills only when fewer than
            # the predicted number survived, and never removes threshold hits.
            keep = keep | (
                eligible & (rank < predicted_count.unsqueeze(-1))
            )
        bi, qi, ci = keep.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
        out: List[List[List[Tuple[float, int, int]]]] = [
            [[] for _ in range(q)] for _ in range(b)
        ]
        if bi.numel() == 0:
            return out
        rows_device = torch.stack(
            (
                bi,
                qi,
                candidates.indices[bi, qi, ci, 0],
                candidates.indices[bi, qi, ci, 1],
            ),
            dim=-1,
        )
        scores_device = probs[bi, qi, ci].float()
        if rows_device.device.type == "cuda":
            rows_cpu = torch.empty_like(rows_device, device="cpu", pin_memory=True)
            scores_cpu = torch.empty_like(scores_device, device="cpu", pin_memory=True)
            rows_cpu.copy_(rows_device, non_blocking=True)
            scores_cpu.copy_(scores_device, non_blocking=True)
            torch.cuda.current_stream(rows_device.device).synchronize()
        else:
            rows_cpu = rows_device.cpu()
            scores_cpu = scores_device.cpu()
        rows = rows_cpu.numpy()
        scores = scores_cpu.numpy()
        segment_ids = rows[:, 0] * q + rows[:, 1]

        ).tolist()

            # pooled spans attend to each other, so score the requested spans inside
            # the pool
            pooled = self.shared_pool_builder(
                encoding.states,
                encoding.mask,
                query_mask,
                marginals.start_logits,

                token_states,
                text_mask,
                inside_prefix_mean=marginals.inside_prefix_mean,
            )
            match = (
                (indices.unsqueeze(3) == pooled.indices[:, None, None]).all(-1)
                & pooled.mask[:, None, None]
            )
            if (legal & ~match.any(-1)).any():
                raise ValueError(
                    "explicit spans exceed the shared candidate pool "
                    f"(pool_size={self.settings.pool_size})"
                )
            position = match.long().argmax(-1)
            scores = logits.transpose(1, 2).gather(2, position)
            return scores.masked_fill(~legal, MASK_LOGIT)

    """Batch span-attribute scoring while retaining GLiNER's own span selection."""
    
    import torch
    
    
    def prepare_attributes(model, batch, core, metadata_list, grouped_candidates, null_probs):
        """Collect exactly the decoded spans, then score all eligible windows together."""
        pending = []
        core["_pending_attribute_inputs"] = pending
        try:
            for index, metadata in enumerate(metadata_list):
                if not metadata.get("entity_attribute_groups"):
                    continue
                model._decode_entities(
                    index, core, core["ext_specs"][index],
                    grouped_candidates[index] if grouped_candidates is not None else [],
                    metadata, null_probs[index] if null_probs is not None else None,
                    model._resolved_overlap_policy(metadata.get("_overlap_policy")),
                    core["word_offsets"][index], batch.start_mappings[index],
                    batch.end_mappings[index], batch.original_texts[index],
                    len(batch.start_mappings[index]), True, True,
                )
        finally:
            del core["_pending_attribute_inputs"]
        cases = []
        for sample_index, specs, metadata, decoded, coordinates in pending:
            pairs = list(dict.fromkeys(coordinates[id(item)] for items in decoded.values() for item in items))
            if not pairs:
                continue
            query_by_name = {
                spec["field_name"]: index for index, spec in enumerate(specs)
                if spec["task_type"] == "entities"
            }
            prompts = metadata.get("entity_attribute_prompt_labels", {})
            rows = list(dict.fromkeys(
                (label, query_by_name[prompt])
                for group in metadata["entity_attribute_groups"].values()
                for label in group.labels
                if (prompt := prompts.get(label, label)) in query_by_name
            ))
            if rows:
                cases.append((sample_index, rows, pairs))
        if not cases:
            return {}
        device = core["query_states"].device
        count = len(cases)
        queries = max(len(rows) for _, rows, _ in cases)
        spans = max(len(pairs) for _, _, pairs in cases)
        query_indices = torch.zeros((count, queries), dtype=torch.long)
        query_valid = torch.zeros((count, queries), dtype=torch.bool)
        indices = torch.zeros((count, queries, spans, 2), dtype=torch.long)
        valid = torch.zeros((count, queries, spans), dtype=torch.bool)
        for index, (_, rows, pairs) in enumerate(cases):
            query_indices[index, :len(rows)] = torch.tensor([query for _, query in rows])
            query_valid[index, :len(rows)] = True
            indices[index, :len(rows), :len(pairs)] = torch.tensor(pairs).unsqueeze(0)
            valid[index, :len(rows), :len(pairs)] = True
        samples = torch.tensor([sample for sample, _, _ in cases], device=device)
        query_indices = query_indices.to(device)
        states = core["query_states"].index_select(0, samples)
        states = states.gather(1, query_indices.unsqueeze(-1).expand(-1, -1, states.shape[-1]))
        mask = core["query_mask"].index_select(0, samples).gather(1, query_indices)
        mask = mask & query_valid.to(device)
        logits = model.boundary_head.score_explicit_spans(
            core["text_states"].index_select(0, samples),
            core["text_mask"].index_select(0, samples),
            states, mask, indices.to(device), valid_mask=valid.to(device),
        )
        logits = (logits / model.boundary_settings.pair_temperature).float().cpu()
        return {
            sample: {
                "labels": [label for label, _ in rows],
                "pairs": {pair: index for index, pair in enumerate(pairs)},
                "logits": logits[index, :len(rows), :len(pairs)],
            }
            for index, (sample, rows, pairs) in enumerate(cases)
        }

        maximum=0.; changed=0

        value={'maximum_top_role_confidence_difference':maximum,'changed_top_role_labels':changed}
        (root/'confidence-agreement.json').write_text(json.dumps(value,indent=2)+'\n')
        print(value)

     compatibility independently of model speed and extraction quality.
    +
    +## Measured configuration
    +
    +On 17 November 2026, the 74M-parameter small checkpoint completed three runs of
    +the same source-verified 10,000-record sample at 163.7, 162.3 and 162.5 articles
    +per second on the RTX 5060 Ti. The aggregate rate was 162.8/second, projecting
    +20.9 hours of extraction for 12,241,870 retained records. This excludes source
    +reconstruction and downstream issuer linking. Peak PyTorch reserved CUDA memory
    +was 7.50 GiB; driver allocations are separate.
    +
    +The configuration uses FP16, DisentangledFlash, compiled extraction heads,
    +batched role scoring, 128-window GPU batches, four preprocessing workers and an
    +8,192-article buffer. Windows contain 384 word tokens with 64-token overlap.
    +All model parameters were verified on CUDA. Every record passed structural
    +checks; the first and third repetitions produced identical predictions.
    +
    +```bash
    +just inference::gliner-run gliner2.5-small-v1 \
    +    --sample .runtime/gliner-benchmark/sample/articles.jsonl \
    +    --output .runtime/gliner-benchmark/custom-run \
    +    --limit 10000 --batch-size 128 --buffer-size 8192 --workers 4 \
    +    --precision fp16 --backend disentangled_flash_heads --batched-attributes
    +```
    +
    +The [benchmark report](../../data/research/experiments/article-labels/gliner-benchmark/report.md)
    +and its DVC artifact retain selections, predictions, timings, comparisons,
    +compatibility probes and historical experiment launchers. These results establish
    +computational feasibility, not label accuracy. Diagnostic examples include
    +people and places labeled as companies; the roles also describe windows rather
    +than calibrated whole-article subject probabilities. Human validation and dated
    +issuer linking remain prerequisites for research use.
