    structured result: {"content":"# GLiNER2.5 Long-Context Extraction Tutorial\n\nLearn how to extract information from documents that are longer than the model's encoded window. Standard `extract(...)` with `max_len` **truncates** to the first N word tokens. Long-context APIs **scan** the full document with overlapping chunks and remap spans to global character offsets.\n\nThis applies to GLiNER2 span checkpoints and GLiNER2.5 boundary checkpoints. Boundary models can extract arbitrarily long spans **inside one encoded window**; they still cannot join a span whose start and end never co-occur in the same chunk.\n\n## Table of Contents\n- [Why Use Long-Context Extraction](#why-use-long-context-extraction)\n- [Setup](#setup)\n- [How Chunking Works](#how-chunking-works)\n- [Entity Extraction](#entity-extraction)\n- [Choosing Chunk Settings](#choosing-chunk-settings)\n- [Overlap Policy](#overlap-policy)\n- [Full Schema Extraction](#full-schema-extraction)\n- [Task-Specific Long APIs](#task-specific-long-apis)\n- [Span Attributes on Long Documents](#span-attributes-on-long-documents)\n- [Classification on Long Documents](#classification-on-long-documents)\n- [Relations and Joint IE](#relations-and-joint-ie)\n- [Batch Long-Document Extraction](#batch-long-document-extraction)\n- [Limits You Should Not Ignore](#limits-you-should-not-ignore)\n- [Best Practices](#best-practices)\n\n## Why Use Long-Context Extraction\n\nUse long-context extraction for reports, contracts, support tickets, transcripts, PDFs converted to text, logs, and other multi-page documents.\n\nIt:\n\n1. Splits the document into overlapping **word** chunks (`chunk_size`, `chunk_overlap`).\n2. Runs normal GLiNER inference on each chunk.\n3. Remaps chunk-local character spans back to the original document.\n4. Merges duplicate detections from overlapping regions.\n\nDo **not** use `extract_entities(..., max_len=512)` for this. `max_len` drops the rest of the file.\n\n## Setup\n\n```python\nfrom gliner2 import AutoExtractor, AttributeGroup\n\n# GLiNER2.5 boundary multi-task checkpoint (see README for small/base/multi sizes)\nmodel = AutoExtractor.from_pretrained(\"fastino/gliner2.5-multi-v1\")\n```\n\nSpan-architecture models work the same way:\n\n```python\nfrom gliner2 import GLiNER2\n\nextractor = GLiNER2.from_pretrained(\"fastino/gliner2-base-v1\")\n```\n\nThe examples below use `model` from `AutoExtractor`.\n\n## How Chunking Works\n\nChunks are counted in **whitespace word tokens**, not characters or subwords.\n\n```\nwords:     0        64              384             448\nchunk 1:   |------------------------|\nchunk 2:            |------------------------------|\n           overlap (64 words)\n```\n\n- `chunk_size=384` — each window has at most 384 words.\n- `chunk_overlap=64` — the next window starts 320 words later.\n- Keep `chunk_overlap < chunk_size`.\n\nOffsets in the result are **global**. If `include_spans=True`:\n\n```python\nassert long_text[entity[\"start\"]:entity[\"end\"]] == entity[\"text\"]\n```\n\nClassification predictions are aggregated across chunks (higher confidence wins when scores exist). Span tasks are merged by position.\n\nBy default, chunks are counted with the `\"whitespace\"` word splitter (the same strategy used to train public checkpoints). Long-document APIs use the splitter attached to the loaded model, so `word_splitter=\"char\"` also changes chunk boundaries. That character-level splitter is suitable for languages without whitespace-delimited words, such as Chinese:\n\n```python\nmodel = AutoExtractor.from_pretrained(\n    \"fastino/gliner2.5-multi-v1\",\n    word_splitter=\"char\",\n)\n# or after loading\nmodel.set_word_splitter(\"char\")\n```\n\nCustom callables must yield `(token, start, end)` with exclusive-end offsets into the original text. Changing a pretrained model's word boundaries can affect quality unless training used the same splitter.\n\n## Entity Extraction\n\n```python\nlong_text = \"\"\"\nAnnual report background and financial commentary...\n\nApple CEO Tim Cook announced Vision Pro updates in Cupertino\nduring September 2025.\n\nMore report text continues for many pages...\n\"\"\"\n\nresult = model.extract_entities_long(\n    long_text,\n    [\"company\", \"person\", \"product\", \"location\", \"date\"],\n    chunk_size=384,\n    chunk_overlap=64,\n    include_spans=True,\n    include_confidence=True,\n)\n\nprint(result)\n# {\n#     \"entities\": {\n#         \"company\": [{\"text\": \"Apple\", \"confidence\": 0.99, \"start\": 52, \"end\": 57}],\n#         \"person\": [{\"text\": \"Tim Cook\", \"confidence\": 0.99, \"start\": 62, \"end\": 70}],\n#         \"product\": [{\"text\": \"Vision Pro\", \"confidence\": 0.99, \"start\": 81, \"end\": 91}],\n#         \"location\": [{\"text\": \"Cupertino\", \"confidence\": 0.99, \"start\": 103, \"end\": 112}],\n#         \"date\": [{\"text\": \"September 2025\", \"confidence\": 0.99, \"start\": 120, \"end\": 134}],\n#     }\n# }\n```\n\nDescriptions still help on noisy long text:\n\n```python\nentity_types = {\n    \"contract_party\": \"Companies or people that are parties to the agreement\",\n    \"effective_date\": \"Dates when the agreement starts or becomes valid\",\n    \"termination_clause\": \"Text describing when or how the agreement can end\",\n}\n\nresult = model.extract_entities_long(\n    contract_text,\n    entity_types,\n    chunk_size=512,\n    chunk_overlap=96,\n    include_spans=True,\n)\n```\n\n## Choosing Chunk Settings\n\n| Goal | Starting point |\n| --- | --- |\n| General prose | `chunk_size=384`, `chunk_overlap=64` |\n| Mentions often sit on boundaries | raise overlap to 96–128 |\n| Faster inference | smaller `chunk_size`, smaller overlap |\n| Long noun phrases / GLiNER2.5 wide spans | keep the whole phrase inside one chunk; overlap still cannot invent a span that never fits |\n\nGLiNER2.5 can extract a span of any length **inside one chunk**. A 200-word clause is fine if `chunk_size` is at least 200. A clause that starts in chunk 1 and ends only in chunk 2 will be missed.\n\n## Overlap Policy\n\nAll local long-document methods accept `overlap_policy`. `None` keeps the architecture default.\n\n| Policy | Behavior |\n| --- | --- |\n| `allow` | Keep distinct overlapping spans |\n| `nested` | Permit containment |\n| `flat` / `disallow` | Remove overlaps deterministically |\n| `longest` | Drop strictly contained shorter spans |\n\n```python\nresult = model.extract_entities_long(\n    long_text,\n    [\"person\", \"organization\"],\n    chunk_size=384,\n    chunk_overlap=64,\n    include_spans=True,\n    overlap_policy=\"nested\",\n)\n```\n\nGLiNER2 deduplicates **overlap artifacts** from adjacent chunks. Distinct mentions at different document positions are kept even if the surface string repeats.\n\n## Full Schema Extraction\n\nUse `extract_long` with any schema the short API accepts.\n\n```python\nschema = (\n    model.create_schema()\n    .entities({\n        \"company\": \"Company names\",\n        \"person\": \"Names of people\",\n        \"product\": \"Product names\",\n    })\n    .classification(\"document_type\", [\"report\", \"contract\", \"email\", \"support_ticket\"])\n)\n\nresult = model.extract_long(\n    long_text,\n    schema,\n    chunk_size=384,\n    chunk_overlap=64,\n    include_spans=True,\n    include_confidence=True,\n)\n```\n\nSpan outputs are merged. Classification is aggregated across chunk predictions.\n\n## Task-Specific Long APIs\n\n```python\nclassification = model.classify_text_long(\n    long_text,\n    {\"document_type\": [\"report\", \"contract\", \"email\"]},\n)\n\nrelations = model.extract_relations_long(\n    long_text,\n    [\"works_for\", \"located_in\"],\n    chunk_size=384,\n    chunk_overlap=64,\n    include_spans=True,\n)\n\nstructured = model.extract_json_long(\n    long_text,\n    {\n        \"invoice\": [\n            \"vendor::str\",\n            \"invoice_number::str\",\n            \"line_item::list\",\n        ]\n    },\n    include_spans=True,\n)\n```\n\nMatching batch methods:\n\n- `batch_extract_entities_long`\n- `batch_extract_long`\n- `batch_classify_text_long`\n- `batch_extract_relations_long`\n- `batch_extract_json_long`\n\n`format_results=True` is required for the long batch APIs.\n\n## Span Attributes on Long Documents\n\nAttribute groups work on `extract_long` because each chunk runs the same schema. Attributes stay attached to globally remapped spans. See [Span Attributes](13-span_attributes.md).\n\n```python\nschema = (\n    model.create_schema()\n    .entities([\"product\", \"company\"])\n    .entity_attributes({\n        \"sentiment\": AttributeGroup(\n            [\"positive\", \"negative\", \"neutral\"],\n            applies_to=[\"product\"],\n            qualify_labels=True,\n        )\n    })\n)\n\nresult = model.extract_long(\n    long_text,\n    schema,\n    chunk_size=384,\n    chunk_overlap=64,\n    include_spans=True,\n    include_confidence=True,\n)\n\nfor item in result[\"entities\"].get(\"product\", []):\n    print(item[\"text\"], item.get(\"sentiment\"))\n    assert long_text[item[\"start\"]:item[\"end\"]] == item[\"text\"]\n```\n\n## Classification on Long Documents\n\n### Independent heads\n\n`classify_text_long` / schema classification in `extract_long` aggregates per-chunk scores (prefers higher confidence when available). Good for document type, language, or overall topic.\n\n### Constrained classification\n\nDo **not** stitch independent chunk labels if tasks constrain each other. Use `Classifier.classify_long`, which aggregates logits then decodes **once**:\n\n```python\nfrom gliner2.classification import Classifier, ClassificationSchema, ClassificationConfig\nfrom gliner2.classification import constraints as C\n\nclf = Classifier.from_pretrained(\"fastino/gliner2.5-multi-v1\")\nschema = (\n    ClassificationSchema()\n    .single(\"intent\", [\"read\", \"write\", \"delete\"])\n    .multi(\"effects\", [\"read_only\", \"create\", \"modify\", \"delete\"], min_labels=1)\n    .constrain(C.implies((\"intent\", \"delete\"), (\"effects\", \"delete\")))\n)\n\nresult = clf.classify_long(\n    long_text,\n    schema,\n    chunk_size=384,\n    chunk_overlap=64,\n    aggregate=\"max\",\n    config=ClassificationConfig(),\n)\n```\n\nSee [Constrained Classification](14-constrained_classification.md).\n\n## Relations and Joint IE\n\n### Unconstrained relations\n\n```python\nrels = model.extract_relations_long(\n    long_text,\n    [\"works_for\", \"located_in\", \"founded\"],\n    chunk_size=384,\n    chunk_overlap=96,  # more overlap helps head/tail near boundaries\n    include_spans=True,\n)\n```\n\nA pair is found only if head and tail appear in the **same chunk**.\n\n### Joint IE\n\n```python\nfrom gliner2.joint_ie import JointIE, JointIEConfig\n\njoint = JointIE.from_pretrained(\"fastino/gliner2.5-multi-v1\")\nschema = (\n    joint.create_schema()\n    .entities([\"person\", \"organization\", \"location\"])\n    .relation(\"works_for\", \"person\", \"organization\", unique_head=True)\n    .relation(\"located_in\", \"organization\", \"location\")\n    .no_self_loops()\n)\n\nresult = joint.extract_long(\n    long_text,\n    schema,\n    chunk_size=384,\n    chunk_overlap=96,\n    config=JointIEConfig(optimizer=\"beam\"),\n)\n\nfor rel in result.relations:\n    head = result.entity(rel.head)\n    tail = result.entity(rel.tail)\n    print(head.text, rel.type, tail.text)\n```\n\n`JointIE.extract_long` never creates cross-chunk edges. Duplicate mentions across overlaps keep the higher-confidence copy. See [Joint Information Extraction](15-joint_ie.md).\n\n## Batch Long-Document Extraction\n\nSame schema, many files:\n\n```python\ndocuments = [\n    open(\"report_2024.txt\").read(),\n    open(\"report_2025.txt\").read(),\n]\n\nresults = model.batch_extract_entities_long(\n    documents,\n    [\"company\", \"person\", \"product\", \"location\", \"date\"],\n    batch_size=8,\n    chunk_size=384,\n    chunk_overlap=64,\n    include_spans=True,\n)\n\nfor doc, result in zip(documents, results):\n    for entities in result[\"entities\"].values():\n        for entity in entities:\n            assert doc[entity[\"start\"]:entity[\"end\"]] == entity[\"text\"]\n```\n\nPer-document schemas:\n\n```python\nschemas = [\n    model.create_schema().entities([\"company\", \"date\"]),\n    model.create_schema().entities([\"person\", \"location\"]),\n]\n\nresults = model.batch_extract_long(\n    documents,\n    schemas,\n    chunk_size=384,\n    chunk_overlap=64,\n    include_spans=True,\n)\n```\n\n## Limits You Should Not Ignore\n\n| Supported | Not supported |\n| --- | --- |\n| Arbitrary span length **inside one chunk** (GLiNER2.5) | A span whose start and end never share a chunk |\n| Relations whose both arguments sit in one chunk | Relations that cross chunk boundaries |\n| Global `[start, end)` offsets into the original string | Treating chunk-local offsets as document offsets |\n| Deduping overlap copies of the same mention | Assuming repeated surface forms are collapsed document-wide |\n\nIf a fact is systematically split (name at the end of a page, employer at the start of the next), increase `chunk_overlap` or pre-segment into sentences/paragraphs that contain both arguments.\n\n## Best Practices\n\n- Prefer `*_long` methods over `max_len` truncation whenever the file can exceed the window.\n- Start with `chunk_size=384`, `chunk_overlap=64`; raise overlap for relations and multi-token names.\n- Request `include_spans=True` until every offset slices back to the expected substring.\n- Use label descriptions on long, repetitive documents to cut generic false positives.\n- For constrained labels, aggregate then decode (`Classifier.classify_long`), do not majority-vote chunk labels.\n- For graphs, use `JointIE.extract_long` and accept that edges are intra-chunk.\n- Keep long-context calls explicit in production so latency (chunks × inference) stays visible.\n- Tune `threshold`, `chunk_size`, and `chunk_overlap` on a small domain sample, not only on short sentences.\n","encoding":"utf-8","sha":"593f012ede8f5302b80e5c0056460a0da8ce41a2","display_url":"https://github.com/fastino-ai/GLiNER2/blob/v2.1.0/tutorial/12-long_context.md","display_title":"12-long_context.md"}

    structured result: {"content":"# GLiNER2 Combining Schemas Tutorial\n\n## Table of Contents\n- [Why Combine Schemas](#why-combine-schemas)\n- [Basic Combinations](#basic-combinations)\n- [Advanced Multi-Task Schemas](#advanced-multi-task-schemas)\n- [Real-World Applications](#real-world-applications)\n\n## Why Combine Schemas\n\nCombining schemas allows you to:\n- Extract multiple types of information in one pass\n- Maintain context between different extraction tasks\n- Improve efficiency by avoiding multiple model calls\n- Build comprehensive information extraction pipelines\n\nFor **per-span labels** (e.g. sentiment on product mentions), combine entities with [`entity_attributes`](13-span_attributes.md). For **typed relation graphs**, see [Joint IE](15-joint_ie.md).\n\n## Basic Combinations\n\n### Entities + Classification\n\n```python\nfrom gliner2 import AutoExtractor\n\nextractor = AutoExtractor.from_pretrained(\"fastino/gliner2.5-base-v1\")\n\n# Sentiment analysis with entity extraction\nschema = (extractor.create_schema()\n    .entities([\"person\", \"product\", \"company\"])\n    .classification(\"sentiment\", [\"positive\", \"negative\", \"neutral\"])\n    .classification(\"category\", [\"review\", \"news\", \"opinion\"])\n)\n\ntext = \"Tim Cook announced that Apple's new iPhone is exceeding sales expectations.\"\nresults = extractor.extract(text, schema)\n# Output: {\n#     'entities': {\n#         'person': ['Tim Cook'],\n#         'product': ['iPhone'],\n#         'company': ['Apple']\n#     },\n#     'sentiment': 'positive',\n#     'category': 'news'\n# }\n```\n\n### Entities + Structures\n\n```python\nschema = (extractor.create_schema()\n    .entities({\n        \"person\": \"Names of people mentioned\",\n        \"date\": \"Dates and time references\"\n    })\n    .structure(\"appointment\")\n        .field(\"patient\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"doctor\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"date\")\n        .field(\"time\")\n        .field(\"type\", dtype=\"str\", choices=[\"checkup\", \"followup\", \"consultation\"])\n)\n\ntext = \"\"\"\nDr. Sarah Johnson confirmed the appointment with John Smith for \nMarch 15th at 2:30 PM. This will be a follow-up consultation \nregarding his previous visit on February 1st.\n\"\"\"\nresults = extractor.extract(text, schema)\n```\n\n### Classification + Structures\n\n```python\nschema = (extractor.create_schema()\n    .classification(\"email_type\", \n        [\"order_confirmation\", \"shipping_update\", \"promotional\", \"support\"])\n    .classification(\"priority\", [\"urgent\", \"normal\", \"low\"])\n    .structure(\"order_info\")\n        .field(\"order_number\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"items\")\n        .field(\"total\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"status\", dtype=\"str\", \n               choices=[\"pending\", \"processing\", \"shipped\", \"delivered\"])\n)\n```\n\n## Advanced Multi-Task Schemas\n\n### Complete Document Analysis\n\n```python\n# Comprehensive invoice extraction\ninvoice_schema = (extractor.create_schema()\n    # Document classification\n    .classification(\"document_type\", \n        [\"invoice\", \"credit_note\", \"purchase_order\", \"receipt\"])\n    .classification(\"payment_status\", \n        [\"paid\", \"unpaid\", \"partial\", \"overdue\"])\n    \n    # Key entities\n    .entities({\n        \"company\": \"Company names (buyer or seller)\",\n        \"person\": \"Contact person names\",\n        \"date\": \"Important dates\",\n        \"amount\": \"Monetary amounts\"\n    })\n    \n    # Structured information\n    .structure(\"invoice_header\")\n        .field(\"invoice_number\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"issue_date\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"due_date\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"vendor_name\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"customer_name\", dtype=\"str\")\n    \n    .structure(\"line_item\")\n        .field(\"description\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"quantity\")\n        .field(\"unit_price\")\n        .field(\"amount\")\n        .field(\"tax_rate\", dtype=\"str\", choices=[\"0%\", \"5%\", \"10%\", \"20%\"])\n    \n    .structure(\"payment_info\")\n        .field(\"method\", dtype=\"str\", \n               choices=[\"bank_transfer\", \"credit_card\", \"check\", \"cash\"])\n        .field(\"terms\", description=\"Payment terms like NET30\")\n        .field(\"bank_details\", dtype=\"list\")\n)\n```\n\n### Customer Feedback Analysis\n\n```python\nfeedback_schema = (extractor.create_schema()\n    # Overall classifications\n    .classification(\"sentiment\", [\"positive\", \"negative\", \"neutral\", \"mixed\"])\n    .classification(\"intent\", {\n        \"complaint\": \"Customer expressing dissatisfaction\",\n        \"compliment\": \"Customer expressing satisfaction\",\n        \"suggestion\": \"Customer providing improvement ideas\",\n        \"question\": \"Customer asking for information\"\n    }, multi_label=True)\n    \n    # Extract mentioned entities\n    .entities({\n        \"product\": \"Products or services mentioned\",\n        \"feature\": \"Specific features discussed\",\n        \"competitor\": \"Competing products mentioned\",\n        \"price_mention\": \"Price points or cost references\"\n    })\n    \n    # Structured feedback components\n    .structure(\"issue\")\n        .field(\"problem\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"severity\", dtype=\"str\", choices=[\"critical\", \"major\", \"minor\"])\n        .field(\"affected_area\", dtype=\"list\")\n    \n    .structure(\"suggestion\")\n        .field(\"improvement\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"benefit\", description=\"Expected benefit of the suggestion\")\n)\n```\n\n### News Article Analysis\n\n```python\nnews_schema = (extractor.create_schema()\n    # Article metadata\n    .classification(\"category\", \n        [\"politics\", \"business\", \"technology\", \"sports\", \"entertainment\"])\n    .classification(\"bias\", [\"left\", \"center\", \"right\", \"neutral\"])\n    .classification(\"factuality\", [\"fact\", \"opinion\", \"analysis\", \"speculation\"])\n    \n    # Key entities\n    .entities({\n        \"person\": \"People mentioned in the article\",\n        \"organization\": \"Companies, agencies, or groups\",\n        \"location\": \"Places, cities, or countries\",\n        \"event\": \"Named events or incidents\"\n    })\n    \n    # Structured content\n    .structure(\"quote\")\n        .field(\"speaker\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"statement\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"context\", description=\"Context of the quote\")\n    \n    .structure(\"claim\")\n        .field(\"statement\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"source\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"evidence\", dtype=\"list\")\n)\n```\n\n## Real-World Applications\n\n### E-commerce Product Listing\n\n```python\nproduct_schema = (extractor.create_schema()\n    # Listing classification\n    .classification(\"condition\", [\"new\", \"used\", \"refurbished\", \"for_parts\"])\n    .classification(\"listing_type\", [\"buy_now\", \"auction\", \"best_offer\"])\n    \n    # Extract key entities\n    .entities({\n        \"brand\": \"Product brand or manufacturer\",\n        \"model\": \"Specific model name or number\",\n        \"color\": \"Product colors mentioned\",\n        \"size\": \"Size specifications\"\n    })\n    \n    # Product details\n    .structure(\"product\")\n        .field(\"title\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"price\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"features\", dtype=\"list\")\n        .field(\"category\", dtype=\"str\")\n    \n    # Shipping information\n    .structure(\"shipping\")\n        .field(\"method\", dtype=\"list\", \n               choices=[\"standard\", \"express\", \"overnight\", \"international\"])\n        .field(\"cost\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"delivery_time\", description=\"Estimated delivery timeframe\")\n    \n    # Seller information\n    .structure(\"seller\")\n        .field(\"name\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"rating\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"location\", dtype=\"str\")\n)\n```\n\n### Healthcare Clinical Note\n\n```python\nclinical_schema = (extractor.create_schema()\n    # Note classification\n    .classification(\"visit_type\", \n        [\"initial_consultation\", \"follow_up\", \"emergency\", \"routine_checkup\"])\n    .classification(\"urgency\", [\"urgent\", \"routine\", \"elective\"])\n    \n    # Medical entities\n    .entities({\n        \"symptom\": \"Patient reported symptoms\",\n        \"diagnosis\": \"Medical diagnoses or conditions\",\n        \"medication\": \"Prescribed or mentioned medications\",\n        \"procedure\": \"Medical procedures or tests\",\n        \"body_part\": \"Anatomical references\"\n    })\n    \n    # Patient information\n    .structure(\"patient_info\")\n        .field(\"name\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"age\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"gender\", dtype=\"str\", choices=[\"male\", \"female\", \"other\"])\n        .field(\"chief_complaint\", dtype=\"str\")\n    \n    # Clinical findings\n    .structure(\"vital_signs\")\n        .field(\"blood_pressure\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"heart_rate\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"temperature\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"respiratory_rate\", dtype=\"str\")\n    \n    # Treatment plan\n    .structure(\"prescription\")\n        .field(\"medication\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"dosage\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"frequency\")\n        .field(\"duration\")\n        .field(\"route\", dtype=\"str\", choices=[\"oral\", \"IV\", \"topical\", \"injection\"])\n)\n```\n\n### Legal Document Analysis\n\n```python\nlegal_schema = (extractor.create_schema()\n    # Document classification\n    .classification(\"document_type\", \n        [\"contract\", \"memorandum\", \"brief\", \"motion\", \"order\"])\n    .classification(\"jurisdiction\", \n        [\"federal\", \"state\", \"local\", \"international\"])\n    \n    # Legal entities\n    .entities({\n        \"party\": \"Parties involved (plaintiff, defendant, etc.)\",\n        \"attorney\": \"Legal representatives\",\n        \"judge\": \"Judicial officers\",\n        \"statute\": \"Laws or regulations cited\",\n        \"case_citation\": \"Referenced legal cases\"\n    })\n    \n    # Contract terms\n    .structure(\"contract_term\")\n        .field(\"clause_type\", dtype=\"str\", \n               choices=[\"payment\", \"delivery\", \"warranty\", \"liability\", \"termination\"])\n        .field(\"obligation\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"party_responsible\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"deadline\")\n    \n    # Legal claims\n    .structure(\"claim\")\n        .field(\"type\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"plaintiff\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"defendant\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"amount\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"basis\", description=\"Legal basis for the claim\")\n)\n```\n\n## Using Confidence Scores and Character Positions with Combined Schemas\n\nWhen using combined schemas, `include_confidence` and `include_spans` parameters apply to all extraction types:\n\n```python\nschema = (extractor.create_schema()\n    .entities([\"person\", \"company\"])\n    .classification(\"sentiment\", [\"positive\", \"negative\", \"neutral\"])\n    .relations([\"works_for\"])\n    .structure(\"product\")\n        .field(\"name\", dtype=\"str\")\n        .field(\"price\", dtype=\"str\")\n)\n\ntext = \"Tim Cook works for Apple. The iPhone 15 costs $999. This is exciting!\"\nresults = extractor.extract(\n    text,\n    schema,\n    include_confidence=True,\n    include_spans=True\n)\n# Output: {\n#     'entities': {\n#         'person': [\n#             {'text': 'Tim Cook', 'confidence': 0.95, 'start': 0, 'end': 8}\n#         ],\n#         'company': [\n#             {'text': 'Apple', 'confidence': 0.92, 'start': 20, 'end': 25}\n#         ]\n#     },\n#     'sentiment': {'label': 'positive', 'confidence': 0.88},\n#     'relation_extraction': {\n#         'works_for': [{\n#             'head': {'text': 'Tim Cook', 'confidence': 0.95, 'start': 0, 'end': 8},\n#             'tail': {'text': 'Apple', 'confidence': 0.92, 'start': 20, 'end': 25}\n#         }]\n#     },\n#     'product': [{\n#         'name': {'text': 'iPhone 15', 'confidence': 0.90, 'start': 30, 'end': 39},\n#         'price': {'text': '$999', 'confidence': 0.88, 'start': 46, 'end': 51}\n#     }]\n# }\n```\n\n**Note**: The `include_confidence` and `include_spans` parameters work consistently across all extraction types (entities, classifications, relations, and structures) when using combined schemas.","encoding":"utf-8","sha":"f720eb85a703c4f8552b5c5d2616eb66a03ec3f2","display_url":"https://github.com/fastino-ai/GLiNER2/blob/v2.1.0/tutorial/4-combined.md","display_title":"4-combined.md"}

If there is no explicit reference to the brand impact, \\type{Product/Service} is tagged.}\n    \\item \\hypertarget{csrbrandvslegal}{\\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Legal}: A scandal or social and environmental violations are often reference a legal framework or proceedings/outcomes. When the event is framed affecting the image or social/environmental responsibility we tag \\type{CSR/Brand}.}\n\t\\item Keywords: ecological efforts, ethical and social efforts, scandal, corruption, social responsibility, environmental responsibility, marketing strategies and efforts, company image, brand image, product image, credibility, award, sponsorship, advertising campaign, affiliation.\n\t\\item \\url{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corporate_social_responsibility}\n\t\\item \\url{https://investopedia.com/terms/c/corp-social-responsibility.asp}\n\t\\item \\url{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brand_management}\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n%-------Deal---------\n\\subsection{Deal}\n\n\\hypertarget{Deal}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| L{2.55cm} L{6cm} L{6.3cm} |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large \\textbf{Deal}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n\t\tDeals and partnerships to cooperate with another company or entity.\n\t\tTwo or more companies, organizations or entities agree to jointly reach a goal.\n\t\tExamples of deals include service and product deals, licensing, contract bid, alliance, partnership, Memorandum of Understanding (MOU), pacts, joint ventures (two companies pool resources to accomplish a task), collaborations, contracts, agreements, development partnerships (usually public private partnerships for development projects), and affiliations. Includes announcements, reports, quotations, and speculation on deal events.\\\\\n\t\\end{minipage}\n\t} & \\annexe{\\exargpart{Ford} surprised the industry when \\exargpart{it} announced a new \\anntrg{joint venture} with \\exargpart{Zotye , a private electric vehicle maker}.~\\footnotesize{[f15 s28]}\n} \\newline\\newline \\annexe{\\exargpart{It} also cut a three-year \\anntrg{deal} with \\exargpart{the Boston Celtics} to \\exargpart{provide data , analytics and equipment} , and \\exargpart{to put its logo on their uniforms}.~\\footnotesize{[ge00 s14]}\n}                                                                         \\\\ \\thline\nPartner & One of the partners in the deal. Taggability: A deal by definition has multiple partners so at least two or more Partner participants need to be tagged (if there is no violation of Event Mention Scope). & \\annexe{\\exargpart{Ford} said \\exargpart{it} will continue to \\anntrg{work with} \\exargpart{China-based internet company Baidu Inc.} to develop driverless cars.~\\footnotesize{[f11 s04]}\n} \\\\\nGoal & Goal and aims of the deal. Taggability: Only annotate non-sentential units as the annotation extent, full sentences are not taggable. & \\annexe{Boeing wins \\anntrg{contract} to \\exargpart{build DARPA XS}.~\\footnotesize{[ba03 s00]}\n} \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\end{tabularx}}\n\n\\begin{itemize}[noitemsep,leftmargin=*]\n\t\\item \\hypertarget{dealvsinvestment}{\\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Investment}: Deal is a more general type than investment: in an \\type{Investment} event one party invest an amount of capital in a second party expecting a return on investment. A deal does not have to involve an expectation of a return nor an amount of capital and is more general.}\n\t\\item \\hypertarget{dealvsmergeracquisition}{\\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Merger/Acquisition}: Mergers and acquisition are large deals in which one company acquires ownership of another company. \\type{Merger/Acquistion} are more specific then the general \\type{Deal}, they require a targeted takeover of the full company or specific departments/assets of a company by an acquiring company.}\n\t\\item \\hypertarget{dealvsemployment}{\\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Employment}: In rare cases, a cooperation or agreement on hiring a company for a task is discussed. When the two parties concerned are companies, organization or governments, we tag a \\type{Deal} event. When on of the parties is uni-vocally described in their function as an employ or job position a \\type{Employment} event is annotated.}\n\t\\item \\hypertarget{dealvsfacility}{\\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Facility}: When two organization, companies or entities close a deal for the use of real-estate (such a lease), we tag \\type{Deal}. When the event as framed as an opening or closing of a specific facility or describes any other issue with a specific facility, we tag \\type{Facility}.}\n    \\item Keywords: service and product deals, licensing, contract bid, alliance, partnership, Memorandum of Understanding (MOU), pacts, joint ventures (two companies pool resources to accomplish a task), collaborations, contracts, agreements, development partnerships (usually public private partnerships for development projects), and affiliations.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n\n%-------Dividend---------- NEW promoted to maintype in v0.9\n\\subsection{Dividend}\n\n\\hypertarget{Dividend}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| L{2.55cm} L{6cm} L{6.3cm} |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large \\textbf{Dividend}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n\t    A dividend is a distribution of a portion of a company's earnings, decided by the board of directors, paid to a class of its shareholders. We also include other types of capital returns in this type such as share buybacks and ROC. Dividends can be issued as cash payments, as shares of stock, or other property. A dividend is a payment made by a corporation to its shareholders, usually as a distribution of profits. When a corporation earns a profit or surplus, the corporation is able to re-invest the profit in the business (called retained earnings) and pay a proportion of the profit as a dividend to shareholders. Distribution to shareholders may be in cash (usually a deposit into a bank account). Investors often view the company’s dividend by its dividend yield which measures the dividend in terms of a percent of the current market price. The dividend rate can also be quoted in terms of the dollar amount each share receives (dividends per share, or DPS). Includes forecasts, reports, announcements, quotations and speculation on dividends and capital returns.\n\t\\end{minipage}\n\t} & \\annexe{example}                                                                         \\\\ \\thline\nCompany & The company giving out dividends.  & \\annexe{Argument 1 example sentence with the argument highlighted} \\\\\nAmount & The total amount of dividends payed-out in monetary amount or as count of dividends.  & \\annexe{Argument 2 example sentence with the argument highlighted}  \\\\\nYieldRatio & The current dividend yield ratio in percentage. &                                    \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\end{tabularx}}\n\n\\begin{itemize}[noitemsep,leftmargin=*]\n    \\item \\hypertarget{dividendvssecurityvalue}{\\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{SecurityValue}: Securities (i.e., stocks, options or bonds) and dividends can be broadly categorized as assets. However, a dividend is only an asset from a shareholder point-of-view. For companies on the other hand, dividends are a temporary liability. Due to this difference it is always clear whether dividends or securities are being discussed. For a more in depth discussion cf. \\url{https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/091115/are-dividends-considered-asset.asp}.}\n    \\item Keywords: dividend yield, yield ratio, pay-out, retained |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large \\textbf{Expense}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n\tAn expense is the cost that a business requires to operate on the short-term and long-term.\n\tAn operating expense (OPEX) is a recurring expense a company incurs through its operations.\n\tOften abbreviated as OPEX, operating expenses include rent, equipment, inventory costs, marketing, payroll, insurance, and funds allocated for research and development.\n\tRevenue and capital expenses (CAPEX) are costs a company makes to maintain or upgrade existing assets made over a period of time.\n    Includes announcements, reports, quotations, and speculation on operating, revenue and capital expenses.\n\t\\end{minipage}\n\t} & \\annexe{example}                                                                         \\\\ \\thline\nCompany & Company making the expense. & \\annexe{Argument 2 example sentence with the argument highlighted}  \\\\\nAmount & The capital cost of the expense expressed as a monetary value. & \\annexe{Argument 2 example sentence with the argument highlighted}  \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\end{tabularx}}\n\n\\begin{itemize}[noitemsep,leftmargin=*]\n    \\item \\hypertarget{expensevsrevenue}{\\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Revenue}}: Revenue is money a company earns from conducting business. Expenses are the costs you incur to generate that revenue. The ingredients you buy to make the ice cream, the wages you pay your employees, the rent and utilities you pay for your stand -- these are all expenses. To remain viable, a company's revenue must exceed its expenses. Revenue is often referred to as the \"top line\" because it sits at the top of the income statement.\n    \\item \\hypertarget{expensevsprofitloss}{\\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Profit/Loss}}: \\type{Profit/Loss} captures total earnings or net income (AKA \"the bottom line\"). It consists of the gross revenue minus all expenses. A reduction in expenses can lead to increased earnings.\n    \\item \\hypertarget{expensevssalesvolume}{\\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{SalesVolume}}: \\type{SalesVolume} events capture changes in the amount of product/service sales or consumers/subscriptions. The volume of sales impacts revenue and expenses. Variable operating expenses (such as delivery costs) closely associated with, and varying in close proportion to, changes in the total sales volume. Although not listed separately in income statement, these expenses are an important item of management accounts.\n    \\item \\hypertarget{expensevsinvestment}{\\textbf{Overlap}} with \\type{Investment}: \\type{Expenses} and \\type{Investments} both incur costs to a business. An investment is an expense for which the primary purpose is to change the future revenue or cost structure of the enterprise. An investment involves an expected future return, while an expense is a cost to cover current operations, production, etc. \n    \\item \\hypertarget{expensevsrevenue}{\\textbf{Overlap}} with \\type{Revenue}:\tA business can incur expenses that relate to acquiring revenue in the short-term, i.e. \"revenue expenses\". Revenue expenses will be tagged under the \\type{Expense} type which is typically associated with capital expenses. The difference between revenue expenses and capital expenses is that revenue expenses are one-time costs instead of gradual over-time capital expense. These involve fixed one-time costs related to real estate, factory equipment, computers, office furniture, and other physical capital asset or intangible assets such as intellectual property, copyrights, patents, trademarks, et. al. Whenever a revenue expense is discussed we tag \\type{Expense}.\n    \\item Keywords: operating expense, capital cost, cost saving, revenue expenditure.\n    \\item OPEX vs. CAPEX: We include both revenue types in \\type{Revenue}. What follows is an explanation of the difference for clarification: Capital expenditure should not be confused with revenue expenditure or operating expenses (OPEX). Revenue expenses are shorter-term expenses required to meet the ongoing operational costs of running a business, and therefore they are essentially identical to operating expenses. Unlike capital expenditures, revenue expenses can be fully tax-deducted in the same year in which the expenses occur. (cf. \\url{https://www.investopedia.com/terms/c/capitalexpenditure.asp}) While these types of expense are different in accounting because of US taxation and legal reasons, we combine them under one event as they capture the cost of operating a company.\n    \\item \"Operating expense\": \\url{https://www.investopedia.com/terms/o/operating_expense.asp}\n    \\item \"Capital expenditure\": \\url{https://www.investopedia.com/terms/c/capitalexpenditure.asp}\n    \\item \"Revenue expenditure\": \\url{https://www.accountingtools.com/articles/the-difference-between-capital-expenditures-and-revenue-expe.html}\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n\\hypertarget{Expense\\_Increase}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| Report}\n\n\\hypertarget{FinancialReport}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| L{2.55cm} L{6cm} L{6.3cm} |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large \\textbf{FinancialReport}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n\t\tFinancial results as discussed in reports published by the company or other instance (such as an rating firm, analyst, or fund).\n\t\tQuarterly and annual reports include key accounting and financial data for a company, including gross revenue, net profit, operational expenses and cash flow.\n\t\tWe include all statements about cash flow that involves the incoming and outgoing transactions of a company (e.g., free cash flow (FCF)) and metrics derived thereof under this type.\n\t\tA quarterly report for a public company typically includes an income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement for the quarter and the year-to-date (YTD), as well as comparative results for the prior year.\n\t\tThis event captures publishing, announcement or discussions of these reports and reported results within them.\\\\\n\t\\end{minipage}\n\t} & \\annexe{example}                                                                         \\\\ \\thline\nReportee & Company that is the topic of the financial report. & \\\\\nResult & The type of result with associated monetary amount that is reported on. & \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\end{tabularx}}\n\n\\begin{itemize}[noitemsep, leftmargin=*]\n    \\item \\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Financing}, \\type{Investment}, \\type{Profit/Loss}, \\type{Revenue}, \\type{SalesVolume}: Business journalism often relies on the financial reporting of a company. Financial statements involve the accounting concepts that are captured by the above types. When a specific result belonging to the above categories is contained in these reports, we tag the more specific event types. We tag \\type{FinancialReport} when i) general financial result trends about the company are assessed or ii) a specific report (10-k, quarterly report, etc.) itself is evaluated.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n\\hypertarget{FinancialReport\\_Beat}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| L{2.55cm} L{6cm} L{6.3cm} |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large \\textbf{Financing}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n\t\tFinancing of a company are ways in which it raises capital through debt and equity.\n\t\tEquity financing involves not just the sale of stocks, but also the sale of other equity or quasi-equity instruments such as preferred stock, convertible preferred stock and equity units that include common shares and warrants.\n\t\tThese events focus on how a company raises equity through issuing shares in IPOs, stock splits, etc.\n\t\tDebt Financing refers to the way in which companies raise funds by taking on debt by issuing bonds or taking on loans. Debt financing occurs when a firm sells fixed income products, such as bonds, bills, or notes, to investors.\n\t\tThe balance between equity and debt of a company is expressed as the weighted average cost of capital (WACC).\n\t\tEvent mentions pertaining to company debt and debt ratios. \n\t\tIncludes debt announcements, debt forecasts, debt increases, debt reductions, and debt and equity restructuring.\n\t\\end{minipage}\n\t} & \\annexe{example}                                                                         \\\\ \\thline\nFinancee & The company selling equity as shares or taking on debt by issuing bonds or taking out loans. & \\\\\nFinancer & The company, institution, or private entity investing in equity or giving out the loan. & \\\\\nAmount & Amount of capital financed as debt or equity. & \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\end{tabularx}}\n\n\\begin{itemize}[noitemsep,leftmargin=*]\n    \\item \\hypertarget{financingvsratingdebt}{\\textbf{Overlap}} with \\type{Ratings\\_Credit/Debt}: The difference with \\type{Ratings\\_Credit/Debt} is not a debt or credit rating by an analyst. Debt Financing focuses on the means of gathering capital through taking on debt while a rating is a judgment made by an analyst an the companies overall debt (or capacity to repay debt).\n\t\\item \\hypertarget{financingvsinvestment}{\\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Investment}}: The difference between \\type{Investment} and \\type{Financing} is that \\type{Financing} events are focused around means of raising capital and not the investor-investee relation and the expectation of a future return. \\type{Financing} events are focused around a company taking on debt to raise capital.\n    \\item \\url{https://www.investopedia.com/terms/d/debtfinancing.asp}\n    \\item \\url{https://www.investopedia.com/terms/e/equityfinancing.asp}\n    \\item \\url{https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/032515/how-does-company-choose-between-debt-and-equity-its-capital-structure.asp}\n    \\item \\url{https://www.investopedia.com/financial-edge/1112/small-business-financing-debt-or-equity.aspx}\n    \\item \\url{https://finance.zacks.com/differences-between-debt-equity-investments-3035.html}\n    \\item \\url{https://corporatefinanceinstitute.com/resources/knowledge/finance/debt-vs-equity/}\n    \\item \\url{https://www.investopedia.com/terms/b/bond.asp}\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n%-------Investment---------\n\\subsection{Investment}\n\n\\hypertarget{Investment}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| L{2.55cm} L{6cm} L{6.3cm} |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large \\textbf{Investment}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n\t    Investment takes place when an organization, company or entity allocates capital or time in expectation for some benefit/return in the future.\n\t\tWe include corporate investment in other companies or subsidiaries as well as investments a company makes in infrastructure or products/services.\n\t\tCorporate capital investment involves one company investing in another company it owns as a subsidiary or does not control or own fully as in affiliate/associate companies.\n\t\tCorporate investments are often Capital Investments as part of a Corporate Finance strategy to strengthen the companies' portfolio.\n\t\\end{minipage}\n\t} & \\annexe{example}                                                                         \\\\ \\thline\nInvestor & Company or organization that makes the investment. & \\\\\nInvestee & Company being in which the Investor invests. Can also be a stock or other security. & \\\\\nReturn  & The expected return or future benefit of the investment. & \\\\\nCapitalInvested & Amount of capital invested as a monetary expression. & \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\end{tabularx}}\n\n\\begin{itemize}[noitemsep,leftmargin=*]\n    \\item \\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Merger/Acquisition}: The difference between \\type{Merger/Acquisition} and \\type{Investment} is that in the \\type{Merger/Acquisition} event one company gains full ownership of another company or parts of that company. This is not the case in Investment where partial ownership through share investment is possible but not the goal.\n    \\item \\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Deal}: \\hyperlink{dealvsinvestment}{See \\type{Deal.}}\n    \\item \\hypertarget{investmentvsproductservice}{\\textbf{Overlap}} with \\type{Product/Service}: We tag \\type{Investment} when a company allocates capital for the development of a future product or service. \\type{Product/Service} types are reserved for an existing, trialed or planned product or service or for any other issue directly related to products or services.\n    \\item \\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Facility}: \\hyperlink{facilityvsinvestment}{See \\type{Facility}.}\n    \\item \\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Financing}: \\hyperlink{financingvsinvestment}{See \\type{Financing}.}\n    \\item \\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Expense}: \\hyperlink{expensevssalesvolume}{See \\type{Expense}.}\n    \\item General term \"Investment\": \\url{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investment}\n\t\\item \"Capital investment\": \\url{https://www.investopedia.com/terms/c/capital-investment.asp}\n\t\\item \"Capital Investment\": \\url{https://www.investopedia.com/terms/c/corporatefinance.asp}\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n%-------Legal---------\n\\subsection{Legal}\n\n\\hypertarget{Legal}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| L{2.55cm} L{6cm} L{6.3cm} |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large \\textbf{Legal}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n\t\tEvents pertaining to governmental justice. Investigations. accusations, litigations, arrest charges, Fraud, Money Laundering, Bribing, Settlement, Judgement, Lawsuit, Legal issues, Regulatory issues, injunctions.\n\t\\end{minipage}\n\t} & \\annexe{example}\n\\\\ \\thline\nDefendant & Entity, company, or person being alleged of a crime, under investigation, convicted, fined, etc. & \\\\\nALLEGATION & Allegation or other formal/legal offence that is alleged against a Defendant. & \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\end{tabularx}}\n\n\\begin{itemize}[noitemsep,leftmargin=*]\n    \\item \\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{CSR/Brand}: \\hyperlink{csrbrandvslegal}{See \\type{CSR/Brand}}.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n\\hypertarget{Legal\\_Proceeding}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| L{2.55cm} L{6cm} L{6.3cm} |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large Legal\\_\\textbf{Proceeding}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n\t\tA court proceeding has been initiated for a defendant accused of an allegation. Legal proceedings include trials, lawsuits, and hearings. Trials are state-initiated proceedings in a court. Hearing are state-initiated proceedings outside the court (e.g. in Senate). Lawsuits are proceedings between private parties. This also includes charges and indictments, i.e. formal accusations, and investigations.\n\t\\end{minipage}\n\t} & \\annexe{example}                                                                         \\\\ \\thline\nDefendant & Entity being convicted, fined, etc. & \\\\\nComplainant & Entity filing suit or initiating the proceeding by accusation of the defendant. Governmental prosecutor, plaintiff, litigator, suer, petitioner. & \\\\\nAdjudicator & Judge or court. In case of investigation, the investigator either private by attorney or public police investigators. & \\\\\nALLEGATION & Allegation or other formal/legal offence that is alleged against a Defendant. & \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\end{tabularx}}\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n\\hypertarget{Legal\\_Conviction/Settlement}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| L{2.55cm} L{6cm} L{6.3cm} |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large Legal\\_\\textbf{Conviction/Settlement}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n\t\tA defendant has been found guilty of an allegation and is at the conclusion of a trial.\n\t\tThe defendant is convicted to a sentence which can be jail-time, a fine, cease-and-desist, etc.\n\t\tAlso applies where allegations are settled out of court.\n\t\\end{minipage}\n\t} & \\annexe{example}                                                                         \\\\ \\thline\nDefendant & Entity being convicted, fined, etc. & \\\\\nAdjudicator & Entity proclaiming the conviction. & \\\\\nSENTENCE & Sentence, fine, incarceration, or other punishment. & \\\\\nALLEGATION & Allegation or other formal/legal offence that is alleged against a Defendant. & \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\end{tabularx}}\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n\\hypertarget{Legal\\_Acquit}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| L{2.55cm} L{6cm} L{6.3cm} |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large Legal\\_\\textbf{Acquit}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n\t\tA defendant has been found not guilty of an allegation at the conclusion of a trial. This is the opposite of conviction.\n\t\\end{minipage}\n\t} & \\annexe{example}                                                                         \\\\ \\thline\nDefendant & Entity being convicted, fined, etc. & \\\\\nAdjudicator & Entity proclaiming the acquittal. & \\\\\nALLEGATION & Allegation or other formal/legal offence that is alleged against a Defendant. & \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em}\n\\end{tabularx}}\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n\\hypertarget{Legal\\_Appeal}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| L{2.55cm} L{6cm} L{6.3cm} |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large Legal\\_\\textbf{Appeal}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n\t\tA court decision is taken to a higher court for review.\n\t\\end{minipage}\n\t} & \\annexe{example}                                                                         \\\\ \\thline\nDefendant & Entity being convicted, fined, etc. & \\\\\nComplainant & Entity filing suit or initiating the proceeding by accusation of the defendant. Governmental prosecutor, plaintiff, litigator, sue-er, petitioner. & \\\\\nAdjudicator & Entity proclaiming the appeal. & \\\\\nALLEGATION & Allegation or other formal/legal offence that is alleged against a Defendant. & \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\end{tabularx}}\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n%-------Macroeconomics---------\n\\subsection{Macroeconomics}\n\n\\hypertarget{Macroeconomics}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| L{2.55cm} L{6cm} L{6.3cm} |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large \\textbf{Macroeconomics}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n\t\tMacro-economic events are aggregated indicators such as sectorial trends, policy, GDP, unemployment rates, national income, price indices, and the interrelations among the different markets and sectors of the economy. Includes events, speculation, expectation, forecasts, announcements, changes on a company's position in the market, the state of the market, sector or country in general, headwinds, tailwinds, business trends, market share, consumer spending, etc.\n\t\tWe include discussions on a company's position in the market (e.g. compared to competitors).\n\t\\end{minipage}\n\t} & \\annexe{example}                                                                         \\\\ \\thline\nAffectedCompany & Company, organization, or entity being affected by the macroeconomic event. & \\\\\nSector & Sector, industry, market, state, geographical location where the event takes effect. & \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\end{tabularx}}\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n\n%-------Merger/Acquisition---------\n\\subsection{Merger/Acquisition}\n\n\\hypertarget{Merger/Acquisition}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| L{2.55cm} L{6cm} L{6.3cm} |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large \\textbf{Merger/Acquisition}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n\t\tConsolidation of companies and assets involving at least two companies. A merger is a legal consolidation of two entities into one entity. An acquisition occurs when one entity takes ownership of another entity's stock, equity interests or assets.\n\t\\end{minipage}\n\t} & \\annexe{example}                                                                         \\\\ \\thline\nAcquirer & Entity receiving the company or assets & \\\\\nTarget & Entity filing suit or initiating the proceeding by accusation of the defendant. Governmental prosecutor, plaintiff, litigator, suer, petitioner. & \\\\\nCost & Cost of the merger or acquisition in monetary amount. & \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\end{tabularx}}\n\n\\begin{itemize}[noitemsep,leftmargin=*]\n\t\\item \\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Deal}: \\hyperlink{dealvsmergeracquisition}{see \\type{Deal}.}\n    \\item \\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Investment}: The difference between \\type{MergerAcquisition} and \\type{Investment} is that in the \\type{MergerAcquisition} event one company gains full ownership of another company or parts of that company. This is not the case in Investment where partial ownership through share investment is possible but not the goal.\n    \\item \"Mergers and Acquisitions\": \\url{https://www.investopedia.com/university/mergers/mergers1.asp}\n    \\item \"Mergers and Acquisitions\": \\url{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mergers_and_acquisitions}\n    % \\item \"Merger\" \\url{https://www.investopedia.com/terms/m/merger.asp}\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n\n%-------Product/Service---------\n\\subsection{Product/Service}\n\n\\hypertarget{Product/Service}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| L{2.55cm} L{6cm} L{6.3cm} |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large \\textbf{Product/Service}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n\t\tEvents pertaining to a specific product or service. Includes announcements, launches, testing, changes, up/downgrades, updates, recalls, trial results, approvals, reviews, and other issues regarding products and services of a company. NOTE: General mentions of a product or service as belonging to a company are not tagged: the product has to be involved in a concrete event or issue.\n\t\\end{minipage}\n\t} & \\annexe{example}                                                                         \\\\ \\thline\nProductService & The Product/Service in question. & \\\\\nProducer & Company, organization, or entity that produces, delivers, or otherwise brings to market the product or service. & \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\end{tabularx}}\n\n\\begin{itemize}[noitemsep,leftmargin=*]\n    \\item \\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Investment}: \\hyperlink{investmentvsproductservice}{See \\type{Investment}.}\n    \\item \\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{CSR/Brand}: \\hyperlink{csrbrandvsproductservice}{See \\type{CSR/Brand}.}\n    \\item Keywords: Launch, recall, cancellation, production pipeline, goods, trial, acceptation.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n\\hypertarget{Product/ServiceLaunch}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| L{2.55cm} L{6cm} L{6.3cm} |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large Product/Service\\_\\textbf{Launch}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n\t\tA company brings a new product/service to market. Inversely, losses happen when the expense exceeds the revenue.\n\t\tNet income is the difference between revenue and the cost of making a product or providing a service, before deducting overheads, payroll, taxation, and interest payments. \n\t\tWe also include operating profit (earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT)) and other metrics for assessing a company's profitability such as \"earnings per share\" (EPS).\n\t\tWe include declarations and forecasts of profit/loss, positive and negative (losses) profit, lower than, higher than, as expected, increased, decreased, and stable profits.\n\t\\end{minipage}\n\t} & \\annexe{example} \\\\ \\thline\nProfiteer & Company, organization, or entity turning a profit or loss. & \\\\\nAmount & The amount of money won/lost. & \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\end{tabularx}}\n\n\\begin{itemize}[noitemsep, leftmargin=*]\n    \\item \\textbf{Overlap} with \\type{Expense}: \\hyperlink{expensevsprofitloss}{See \\type{Expense}.}\n    \\item \\hypertarget{profitvsrevenue}{\\textbf{Overlap}} with \\type{Revenue}: \\type{Profit/Loss} is what remains after expenses are deducted from revenue. Net income is calculated by taking revenues and subtracting the costs of doing business such as depreciation, interest, taxes, and other expenses.\n    \\item Keywords: net income, net earnings, profit, loss, total comprehensive income, net earnings, net profit, bottom line, gross profit, gross margin, sales profit, credit sales, net profit margin percentage.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n\\hypertarget{Profit/Loss\\_Increase}{\\centering\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{| L{2.55cm} L{6cm} L{6.3cm} |}\n\\multicolumn{3}{C{14.85cm}}{\\Large Profit/Loss\\_\\textbf{Increase}}                \\\\\n\\specialrule{.1em}{.05em}{.05em} \n\\multicolumn{2}{|L{8.55cm}}{\n\t\\begin{minipage}{8.55cm}\n        Profit or Loss has increased compared to a historical trend. \\type{SalesVolume}: Sales are the proceeds from the selling of goods or services to its customers. In accounting terms, sales make up one component of a company's revenue. On an income statement, sales are usually referred to as gross sales or \"the top line\" since sales are often used interchangeably with revenue. If your revenues are increasing but your net profits are not, that is a sure sign your expenses are up. For this, we introduce the \\type{CAPITAL} FILLER argument.\n\n\\hypertarget{TIME}{\n\\subsubsection{TIME}}\n\n\\justify\n\\noindent\\textbf{On types and subtypes}: all.\\\\[6pt]\n\\noindent\\textbf{Conceptually}:\nA TIME is a temporal expression that corresponds to a specific duration and point in time.\nThis includes calendar dates (e.g., \"October 29\", \"June 2017\", \"the 24th of April\") but also relative time descriptions (e.g., \"yesterday\". \"last week\", \"next year\") and durations (e.g, \"the coming months\", \"over five years\").\\\\\n\n\\noindent\\textbf{Taggability}:\\\\\nThe full nominal constituent NP of the duration of time point will be tagged.\nThis includes pre- and post-modifiers and excludes the preposition that is the head of the TIME noun phrase.\n\n\\begin{exe}\n    \\ex \\annexe{In [ \\exargfill{2017} ], the company announced their desire for entering the Chinese market.}\n    \\ex \\annexe{The decision to replace the executive will be made [ \\exargfill{next Thursday} ].}\n    \\ex \\annexe{The leaders met [ \\exargfill{last week} ] in Lagos.}\n    \\ex \\annexe{They have been working on the deal for [ \\exargfill{the better part of a year} ]. }\n    \\ex \\annexe{The park will open [ \\exargfill{Monday 23 June} ].}\n    \\ex \\annexe{The Boeing Corp. announced the deal [ \\exargfill{yesterday after Trump's visit to Iran} ].}\n\\end{exe}\n\n\\vspace{0.5cm}\n\n\\hypertarget{PLACE}{\n\\subsubsection{PLACE}}\n\n\\justify\n\\noindent\\textbf{On types and subtypes}: all.\\\\[6pt]\n\\noindent\\textbf{Conceptually}:\\\\\nPLACE encompasses specific mentions of geographic locations.\nIt refers to places (e.g., \"Wall Street\", \"The White House\", \"Downing Street\"), cities (e.g., \"Washington\", \"Detroit\"), countries (\"US\", \"\"), states (e.g., \"Oregon\", \"Kentucky\"), regions (e.g., \"Central-Asia\", \"the Champagne region\", \"the fourth district\", \"CBD\" (Central Business District)), and markets expressed as geographic locations (e.g., \"the Indian market\"). It is usually described in terms of the currency of some country or region (e.g., \"US Dollars\", \"\\$\", \"USD\" or \"Euros\", \"EUR\"), but can also be expressed in an amount of securities, equity or debt (e.g., \"1.5 million dollars in stock\", \"27,000 shares\" or \"3.7 million in Covered Bonds\").\\\\\n\n\\noindent\\textbf{\\type{CAPITAL} vs. similar Participant arguments}:\nMany event types have a Participant argument such as \\type{Cost}, \\type{Amount} or \\type{Capital} that is conceptually similar to this FILLER argument.\nHowever \\type{CAPITAL} has other taggability rules w.r.t.     # Extracting Fine-Grained Economic Events from Business News
    URL: https://aclanthology.org/2020.fnp-1.36.pdf
    Author: Gilles Jacobs ; Veronique Hoste
    
    Proceedings of the 1st Joint Workshop on Financial Narrative Processing and MultiLing Financial Summarisation, pages 235–245 Barcelona, Spain (Online), December 12, 2020.
    
    ## Extracting Fine-Grained Economic Events from Business News
    
    Gilles Jacobs Veronique Hoste ´ Language and Translation Technology Team Ghent University, 9000 Gent, Belgium firstname.lastname@ugent.be
    
    ### Abstract
    
    Based on a recently developed fine-grained event extraction dataset for the economic domain, we present in a pilot study for supervised economic event extraction. We investigate how a state of-the-art model for event extraction performs on the trigger and argument identification and classification. While F1-scores of above 50% are obtained on the task of trigger identification, we observe a large gap in performance compared to results on the benchmark ACE05 dataset. We show that single-token triggers do not provide sufficient discriminative information for a fine grained event detection setup in a closed domain such as economics, since many classes have a large degree of lexico-semantic and contextual overlap.
    
    ### 1 Introduction
    
    We present a pilot study on a novel dataset annotated with economic and financial events in English company-specific news. Event processing automatically obtains the “what, who, where and when” of real-world events described in text. Event extraction consists of identifying event triggers, i.e. the tokens that express an event of a predetermined type, and identifying participant arguments, i.e. the tokens that express prototypical participant roles. Event extraction is typically an upstream step in pipelines for financial applications: it has been used for news summarization of single (Lee et al., 2003; Marujo et al., 2017) or multiple documents (Liu et al., 2007; Glavas and ˇ Snajder, 2014), forecasting and market analysis (Nassirtoussi et al., 2014; Bholat ˇ et al., 2015; Nardo et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2018; Chen et al., 2019), risk analysis (Hogenboom et al., 2015; Wei et al., 2019), policy assessment (Tobback et al., 2018; Karami et al., 2018), and marketing (Rambocas and Pacheco, 2018). This work aims to enable these information extraction tasks in the financial domain by making available a dataset and fine-grained event extraction model for company specific news by classifying economic event triggers and participant arguments in text. Our SENTiVENT dataset of company-specific events was conceived to be compatible with fine grained event representations of the ACE benchmark corpora as to enable direct application of advances in the field. In our pilot study, we investigate the portability of an existing state-of-the-art model for event extraction, named DYGIE++ (Wadden et al., 2019b), to the task of financial event extraction.
    
    ### 2 Related Research
    
    Our work on economic event extraction is accommodated within the rich history of automatic event detection. The ACE (Automatic Content Extraction) annotation scheme and programme was highly in fluential in event processing. Periodically, “Event Detection and Recognition” evaluation competitions were organized where event extraction corpora were released (Consortium, 2005; Walker et al., 2006) to enable automatic inference of entities mentioned in text, the relations among entities, and the events in which these entities participate (Doddington et al., 2004). Some years later, the ERE (Entities, Rela tions, Events) standard was conceived as a continuation of ACE with the goal of improving annotation consistency and quality. Our annotation scheme is inspired by the Rich ERE Event annotation schemes
    
    This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International Licence. Licence details: http:// creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/.
    
    (Linguistic Data Consortium, 2016; Linguistic Data Consortium, 2015a; Linguistic Data Consortium, 
    2015b) as to provide compatibility with on-going research in event extraction, where the ACE and ERE 
    datasets remain dominant benchmarks. 
    Many approaches to the detection of economic events are knowledge-based and pattern-based (Aren 
    darenko and Kakkonen, 2012; Hogenboom et al., 2013; Du et al., 2016; Chen et al., 2019). These use 
    rule-sets or ontology knowledge-bases which are largely or fully created by hand and do not rely fully 
    on manually annotated supervised datasets for machine learning. The Stock Sonar project (Feldman et 
    al., 2011a) notably uses domain experts to formulate event rules for rule-based stock sentiment analysis. 
    Their approach has been successful in formulating trading strategies (Ben Ami and Feldman, 2017) and 
    in assessing the impact of events on the stock market (Boudoukh et al., 2016). Along the same line, 
    Hogenboom et al. (2013) rely on a hand-crafted financial event ontology for pattern-based event de 
    tection in the economic domain and incorporates lexicons, gazetteers, PoS-tagging and morphological 
    analysis. 
    Several semi- or distantly supervision approaches exist in which seed sets are manually labeled or 
    rule-sets are used to generate or enhance training data (Qian et al., 2019; Ronnqvist and Sarlin, 2017; ¨ 
    Ein-Dor et al., 2019). For Chinese, Yang et al. (2018) and Chen et al. (2019) rely on a knowledge-base 
    of rules for extracting ACE-like events in stock market prediction. Han et al. (2018) describe a hybrid 
    approach to ACE-like event extraction by labeling triggers, argument types, and event types for Chinese 
    news articles with 8 economic event types using an automatically expanded trigger dictionary and used 
    a pattern-matching approach for argument extraction. 
    Few strictly supervised approaches exist due to the lack of human-annotated ground-truth data. Malik 
    et al. (2011) annotated Dividend and Profit figure slots and detected these types with high precision by 
    combining supervised learning with rule post-processing. The English and Dutch SentiFM business news 
    corpus (Van De Kauter et al., 2015) contains token-span annotations of 10 event types with only one type 
    of relation. Sentence-level event detection experiments have been conducted (Lefever and Hoste, 2016; 
    Jacobs et al., 2018), but supervised fine-grained extraction of triggers and roles as presented here. We 
    are not aware of any other published fine-grained ACE-like event extraction approaches for the economic 
    domain.

    ### 3 Dataset
    
    We define economic events as ‘textually reported real-world occurrences, actions, relations, and situ ations involving companies and firms’. Fine-grained events in our dataset are operationalized as event triggers, i.e. the minimal span of text (a single word or a phrase) that most succinctly expresses the
    
    occurrence of an event type, and event arguments, i.e., participating entities involved in the event by filling a certain prototypical semantic role. Figure 1 shows examples of annotated event triggers with their TYPE | SUBTYPE label linked to argument with their roles. We annotated 288 documents with structured events containing event types and subtypes, arguments and event attributes (i.e., negation, modality & event co-reference). The news article pertain to 30 S&P500 companies spread over different industries and time between June 2016 to May 2017 to avoid topical specialization. These companies were selected as a starting point for scraping because market data (e.g., key financials, spot prices, dividend, earnings and P/E ratio) for these are readily available, enabling market research. For a full description of the data collection, annotation process, dataset prop erties, and agreement study, we refer to Jacobs and Hoste (2020). The event typology contains 18 event main types with 42 subtypes for which 48 possible argument roles exist. Not every main event type has subtypes and the arguments “Time”, “Place”, and “Capital” can belong to any event. The typology was iteratively developed on a sample corpus in which news events were evaluated by financial domain experts. Starting with the set of event types in previous literature (Feldman et al., 2011b; Boudoukh et al., 2019; Hogenboom et al., 2013; Van De Kauter et al., 2015; Du et al., 2016), types were removed and added based on frequency and cohesion of categories. Relevant argument roles were also added in this process of iterative refinement. For a full description of the types and subtypes, we refer to the annotation guidelines (Jacobs, 2020b). Here is a list of main Types → unique Arguments:
    
    • CSR/BRAND → Company 
    • DEAL → Goal, Partner 
    • DIVIDEND → Amount, Company, Historica lYieldRatio, YieldRatio 
    • EMPLOYMENT → Amount, Employee, Em ployer, Replacer, Replacing, Title 
    • EXPENSE → Amount, Company, Histori calAmount 
    • FACILITY → Company, Facility 
    • FINANCIALREPORT → Reportee, Result 
    • FINANCING → Amount, Financee, Financer 
    • INVESTMENT → CapitalInvested, Investee, In vestor 
    • LEGAL → Allegation, Adjudicator, Com plainant, Defendant, Sentence 
    • MACROECONOMICS → AffectedCompany, Sector 
    • MERGER/ACQUISITION → Acquirer, Cost, Target 
    • PRODUCT/SERVICE → Producer, Prod uct/Service, Trialer 
    • PROFIT/LOSS → Amount, HistoricalAmount, Profiteer 
    • RATING → Analyst, HistoricalRating, Secu rity, TargetPrice 
    • REVENUE → Amount, Company, De creaseAmount, HistoricalAmount, In creaseAmount 
    • SALESVOLUME → Amount, Buyer, GoodsService, HistoricalAmount, Seller 
    • SECURITYVALUE → DecreaseAmount, His toricalPrice, IncreaseAmount, Price, Security 
    The types PROFIT/LOSS, REVENUE, EXPENSE, and SALESVOLUME represent major metrics in fi 
    nancial reporting on the income statement. Of all financial metrics, we found these types to be commonly 
    and generally reported in business news. Other metrics such as debt ratios or cash flow statements as well 
    as highly industry-specific indicators were collected under the FINANCIALREPORT type. Discussion of 
    asset performance are captured by RATING and SECURITYVALUE. MACROECONOMICS is a broad cat 
    egory pertaining to events that do not involve decisions or interactions of specific companies. While 
    this category is not company-specific, it was devised to capture discussions of sector trends, economy 
    wide phenomena, and governmental policy. In the event extraction pilot study, we only experiment with 
    classifying main event types and not the subtypes.

    word triggers (e.g., “upgraded ... to buy”, “cut back ... expenses”, “EPS decline”). In ACE05, triggers 
    are always single-word and any multi-word idiomatic expressions are joined into one token (e.g. “kick
