## Assistant

I would build **one compact joint extraction pass for the corpus, then a richer event pass where it adds value**. The most useful outputs are company identity, substantive relevance, company-specific sentiment, article type, and evidence-backed events.

I screened 85 search results across model documentation, research datasets, practitioner schemas, and public standards. These support the following design; they do not establish that our current model can produce every field accurately.

**The strongest foundations are complementary.**

| Foundation | What I would adopt |
|---|---|
| [IPTC NewsCodes](https://iptc.org/std/NewsCodes/guidelines/) | Separate vocabularies for article subjects and journalistic genres; stable identifiers and versioned definitions. |
| [SEntFiN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.12257) and [SemEval financial sentiment](https://aclanthology.org/S17-2089/) | Sentiment attached to each company. Companies in the same article can have different sentiment. |
| [SENTiVENT](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10579-021-09562-4) | English financial-news events with triggers, participants, argument roles, negation, modality, and coreference. This is our closest annotation reference. |
| [LSEG News Analytics](https://developers.lseg.com/en/product/news/news_analytics) | Useful practitioner dimensions: relevance, sentiment, novelty, news volume, and analyst recommendation flags. |
| [FIBO](https://github.com/edmcouncil/fibo/) | Precise financial concepts and relationships, particularly the distinction between businesses, issuers, securities, and corporate actions. |

These provide foundations for different fields. I would maintain an explicit crosswalk between them and our schema.

**Before model inference, collect the inexpensive metadata.**

We should preserve source identifiers, publisher, URL, title, text, publication and capture timestamps, timestamp precision, language, and content hashes. Deterministic processing can add:

- Exact duplicate groups and cached extraction results for identical inputs.
- Paragraph and sentence boundaries.
- Explicit ticker, exchange, currency, percentage, and date expressions.
- Publisher-provided sections, tags, bylines, and press-release attribution.
- Text-quality and boilerplate indicators.

After extracting company mentions, we can derive mention counts, first-mention position, headline presence, paragraph coverage, and co-mentions. Those are useful, interpretable relevance features without additional GPU inference.

Issuer identifiers, historical names, industry, domicile, and security mappings belong in dated reference-data joins. For example, GLEIF explicitly distinguishes securities’ ISINs from their issuers’ LEIs. [GLEIF mapping documentation](https://www.gleif.org/en/lei-data/lei-mapping/download-isin-to-lei-relationship-files/)

**For the first GLiNER pass, I would prioritize this bundle.**

| Output | Proposed scope | Research value |
|---|---|---|
| **Typed entity mentions** | Companies; test adding people, public bodies, and places | Company linking, co-mention networks, identifying regulators and executives |
| **Local company relevance** | Substantive, incidental, or uncertain within the observed context | Separating meaningful coverage from passing mentions |
| **Company-specific financial sentiment** | Positive, negative, neutral, mixed, or not assessable | Firm-level sentiment panels and differences between companies |
| **Article form** | Reporting, analysis, opinion, interview, roundup, press release, other | Researcher-controlled corpus selection |
| **Coarse event families** | Multiple labels permitted | Finding relevant articles and routing deeper extraction |

This is a proposed schema to benchmark. In particular, adding people and places might help distinguish ambiguous company candidates, but that improvement needs measurement.

GLiNER supports entities, attributes, classifications, relations, and structures in a combined extraction call. Company sentiment should use an `AttributeGroup` restricted with `applies_to=["company"]`; `qualify_labels=True` gives the model less ambiguous attribute queries. That assesses all extracted company spans together. [Combined schemas](https://github.com/fastino-ai/GLiNER2/blob/v2.1.0/tutorial/4-combined.md), [span attributes](https://github.com/fastino-ai/GLiNER2/blob/v2.1.0/tutorial/13-span_attributes.md)

Two definitions need particular care:

- **Sentiment:** Define an investor-facing assessment expressed or supported by the text. Keep “not assessable” distinct from neutral. A positive label does not establish an expected positive stock return.
- **Primary subject:** Preserve local relevance observations, then estimate article–company relevance using the whole article’s evidence. Our current window-level roles do not establish a calibrated primary-subject probability.

For long articles, the standard GLiNER merger can select the highest-confidence window’s classification. We therefore need to preserve window evidence and validate article-level aggregation, particularly for sentiment and relevance. [Long-document documentation](https://github.com/fastino-ai/GLiNER2/blob/v2.1.0/tutorial/12-long_context.md)

**For events, I would start with SENTiVENT’s definitions and use coarse families for routing.**

Its annotation guidelines provide 18 main event types, with more detailed subtypes. A compact initial presentation could group these as follows:

| Family | Examples |
|---|---|
| Financial performance and reporting | Earnings, revenue, expenses, sales volumes, financial reports, guidance |
| Financing and capital distributions | Borrowing, capital raising, dividends, buybacks |
| Ownership and transactions | Acquisitions, disposals, investments, partnerships, contracts |
| People and operations | Executive changes, employment, facilities, products and services |
| Legal, regulatory, and reputation | Proceedings, investigations, approvals, corporate responsibility |
| Markets and macroeconomics | Ratings, security-price changes, economic developments |

These would be **our documented rollups** of existing concepts. Fine-grained labels should retain their reference definitions. The [SENTiVENT guidelines](https://github.com/GillesJ/sentivent-event-annotation-guidelines) are especially useful because they explain boundaries and commonly confused cases.

[EDT](https://aclanthology.org/2021.findings-acl.186/) also motivates explicit distinctions such as dividend increases versus cuts, and stock repurchases versus splits. Its selected event set serves an event-driven trading task, so I would use it as an additional crosswalk.

A coarse article label such as `acquisition` is useful for discovery. An event-study record needs substantially more structure.

**The richer pass should extract linked event records.**

For selected articles or passages, request the following together:

| Component | Fields |
|---|---|
| Event identity | Family, subtype, trigger or supporting passage |
| Participants | Company/person/public body, plus event-specific role |
| Financial arguments | Amount, currency, percentage, metric, reporting period, comparison basis |
| Time | Event date or interval, original expression, precision |
| Assertion | Affirmed, negated, or uncertain according to the text |
| Lifecycle | Proposed, announced, approved, completed, cancelled, where applicable |
| Attribution | Who made the statement or forecast, when explicitly stated |

For example:

> “Acme agreed to acquire Beta for $2 billion, subject to regulatory approval.”

The useful record identifies **Acme as acquirer**, **Beta as target**, **$2 billion as consideration**, and the transaction as **agreed but pending approval**. Both companies being mentioned is a separate observation.

GLiNER2.5’s structured-record mode supports grouping repeated instances using an anchor, such as an event trigger. That is relevant when an article discusses several transactions. Optional arguments should remain absent when unsupported. [Structured extraction documentation](https://github.com/fastino-ai/GLiNER2/blob/v2.1.0/tutorial/3-json_extraction.md)

For relationship extraction, typed endpoints and structural constraints can help keep outputs coherent. They still need semantic evaluation: a structurally valid acquisition edge can be wrong. [Joint extraction documentation](https://github.com/fastino-ai/GLiNER2/blob/v2.1.0/tutorial/15-joint_ie.md)

Two extensions deserve separate evaluation:

- **Financial quantities:** A number becomes useful when connected to a company, metric, unit, period, and actual-versus-forecast status. [FiNER](https://aclanthology.org/2022.acl-long.303/) motivates contextual numeric typing, although its data comes from financial filings.
- **Business relationships:** Supplier/customer, ownership, employment, and transaction relationships can enrich networks. [FinRED](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.03736) motivates this directly from financial news and earnings calls.

**Some valuable fields belong after extraction.**

Novelty, syndication, story updates, and recent news volume require comparisons across articles. I would compute those from duplicate/story groups, timestamps, and company links.

For historical studies, novelty comparisons must use earlier observations only. “First observed in CCFinance” also needs its own definition; our archive cannot establish the first public disclosure everywhere.

Likewise, I would join issuer industry classifications from reference data and classify the article’s subject separately. A company’s industry and a story’s topic answer different questions.

**Getting more value from each pass requires measuring the expanded schema.**

“One forward pass” shares encoder work, but additional schema tokens, attributes, candidate spans, and record decoding still cost time. Changing a schema can also change existing predictions.

Our [measured baseline](/home/marcussky/Git/CCFinance/data/research/experiments/article-labels/gliner-benchmark/report.md) is 162.8 articles/s. Processing all 12,241,870 retained records within 24 hours requires 141.7/s. That leaves approximately **15% additional processing time per article**, before source reads and other downstream work.

I would compare three profiles on the existing 10,000-record sample:

1. **Core:** Typed mentions, local relevance, company sentiment, article form.
2. **Core plus events:** Add coarse event families and a small event-record schema.
3. **Selective enrichment:** Core everywhere, richer event records on selected documents or passages.

The comparison should measure throughput, company-link quality, sentiment quality, event-argument accuracy, and changes to existing outputs. We also need a probability sample outside the selected records to audit missed companies and events.

My first additions would be **company-specific sentiment and better entity typing**. I would then test whether evidence-backed event records fit economically in the joint pass. Every released annotation should retain source offsets, model/schema versions, separate confidence fields, and unresolved outcomes, so researchers can choose their own filtering policy.

    """The shared extraction contract used by local GLiNER experiments."""
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
    
    from gliner2 import AttributeGroup
    
    if TYPE_CHECKING:
        from gliner2.inference.runtime import ExtractorRuntimeMixin
        from gliner2.inference.schema import Schema
    
    
    def build_schema(model: ExtractorRuntimeMixin) -> Schema:
        """Request company spans, per-mention roles, and the article's text type."""
        return (
            model.create_schema()
            .entities({"company": "Names of companies and businesses"})
            .entity_attributes(
                {
                    "article_role": AttributeGroup(
                        ["primary", "secondary", "incidental", "uncertain"],
                        applies_to=["company"],
                        qualify_labels=True,
                    )
                }
            )
            .classification(
                "article_type",
                ["reporting", "opinion", "press release", "promotional", "other"],
            )
        )
    """Measure full-document GLiNER extraction on a prepared article sample."""
    
    import argparse
    import gzip
    import json
    import time
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import torch
    from gliner_runtime import load_model
    from gliner_schema import build_schema
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Run one isolated model configuration and save timings and predictions."""
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("--sample", type=Path, required=True)
        parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)
        parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
        parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=100)
        parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=8)
        parser.add_argument("--buffer-size", type=int)
        parser.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=0)
        parser.add_argument("--torch-threads", type=int)
        parser.add_argument("--chunk-size", type=int, default=384)
        parser.add_argument("--chunk-overlap", type=int, default=64)
        parser.add_argument("--batched-attributes", action="store_true")
        parser.add_argument("--gpu-memory-fraction", type=float, default=0.8)
        parser.add_argument(
            "--precision",
            choices=["fp32", "fp16", "bf16", "int8", "fp8", "nvfp4"],
            default="fp32",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--backend",
            choices=[
                "standard",
                "compiled",
                "disentangled_flash",
                "disentangled_flash_heads",
            ],
            default="standard",
        )
        args = parser.parse_args()
        if not 0 < args.gpu_memory_fraction <= 1:
            raise ValueError("GPU memory fraction must be in (0, 1]")
        if args.batch_size < 1 or args.workers < 0:
            raise ValueError("Batch size must be positive and worker count nonnegative")
        buffer_size = args.batch_size if args.buffer_size is None else args.buffer_size
        if buffer_size < 1:
            raise ValueError("Buffer size must be positive")
        if not 0 <= args.chunk_overlap < args.chunk_size:
            raise ValueError(
                "Chunk overlap must be nonnegative and smaller than chunk size"
            )
        if args.torch_threads is not None:
            torch.set_num_threads(args.torch_threads)
        torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction(args.gpu_memory_fraction)
        args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
        start = time.perf_counter()
        with args.sample.open(encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            articles = [
                json.loads(line) for _, line in zip(range(args.limit), stream, strict=False)
            ]
        if len(articles) != args.limit:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected {args.limit} articles; got {len(articles)}")
        read_seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        start = time.perf_counter()
        model, model_metadata = load_model(
            args.model,
            args.precision,
            args.backend,
            batched_attributes=args.batched_attributes,
        )
        schema = build_schema(model)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        load_seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        start = time.perf_counter()
        model.batch_extract_long(
            [item["text"] for item in articles[: min(args.batch_size, len(articles))]],
            schema,
            batch_size=args.batch_size,
            num_workers=args.workers,
            chunk_size=args.chunk_size,
            chunk_overlap=args.chunk_overlap,
            include_spans=True,
            include_confidence=True,
        )
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        warmup_seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        start = time.perf_counter()
        output = args.output / "predictions.jsonl.gz"
        invalid_spans = 0
        invalid_articles = 0
        corrected_spans = 0
        corrected_articles = 0
        with gzip.open(output, "wt", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            for offset in range(0, len(articles), buffer_size):
                batch = articles[offset : offset + buffer_size]
                predictions = model.batch_extract_long(
                    [item["text"] for item in batch],
                    schema,
                    batch_size=args.batch_size,
                    num_workers=args.workers,
                    chunk_size=args.chunk_size,
                    chunk_overlap=args.chunk_overlap,
                    include_spans=True,
                    include_confidence=True,
                )
                if len(predictions) != len(batch):
                    raise ValueError("Prediction count does not match the input batch")
                for article, prediction in zip(batch, predictions, strict=True):
                    errors = []
                    corrected = 0
                    for entity in prediction.get("entities", {}).get("company", []):
                        span_start, span_end = entity["start"], entity["end"]
                        corrected += bool(entity.get("synthetic_suffix_removed"))
                        if (
                            entity.get("invalid_window_span")
                            or not (0 <= span_start < span_end <= len(article["text"]))
                            or article["text"][span_start:span_end] != entity["text"]
                        ):
                            errors.append(
                                {
                                    "start": span_start,
                                    "end": span_end,
                                    "predicted": entity["text"],
                                    "source": article["text"][span_start:span_end],
                                }
                            )
                    invalid_spans += len(errors)
                    invalid_articles += bool(errors)
                    corrected_spans += corrected
                    corrected_articles += bool(corrected)
                    stream.write(
                        json.dumps(
                            {
                                "article_id": article["article_id"],
                                "status": "invalid_span" if errors else "ok",
                                "span_errors": errors,
                                "prediction": prediction,
                            }
                        )
                        + "\n"
                    )
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        report = {
            "configuration": vars(args)
            | {"sample": str(args.sample), "output": str(args.output)},
            "articles": len(articles),
            "valid_articles": len(articles) - invalid_articles,
            "invalid_span_articles": invalid_articles,
            "invalid_spans": invalid_spans,
            "synthetic_suffix_corrected_articles": corrected_articles,
            "synthetic_suffix_corrected_spans": corrected_spans,
            "sample_read_seconds": read_seconds,
            "model_load_seconds": load_seconds,
            "warmup_seconds": warmup_seconds,
            "inference_and_output_seconds": seconds,
            "articles_per_second": len(articles) / seconds,
            "valid_articles_per_second": (len(articles) - invalid_articles) / seconds,
            "peak_cuda_memory_bytes": torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(),
            "peak_cuda_reserved_bytes": torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved(),
            "torch_version": torch.__version__,
            "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
            "model": model_metadata,
            "torch_threads": torch.get_num_threads(),
            "long_document_handling": "Overlapping word windows with GLiNER2 merge",
        }
        (args.output / "report.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(json.dumps(report), flush=True)
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()
    """Load the local extractor with explicit precision and attention choices."""
    
    from collections import Counter
    from functools import partial
    
    import torch
    from gliner2 import AutoExtractor
    from gliner2.models.boundary.engine import BoundaryExtractor
    
    
    def load_model(
        path: str, precision: str, backend: str, *, batched_attributes: bool = False
    ) -> tuple[BoundaryExtractor, dict]:
        """Set precision before preparing attention kernels or compiling the model."""
        model = AutoExtractor.from_pretrained(path, map_location="cuda")
        if not isinstance(model, BoundaryExtractor):
            raise TypeError("This benchmark requires a GLiNER boundary checkpoint")
        if precision == "fp16":
            model.to(dtype=torch.float16)
        elif precision in {"bf16", "fp8", "nvfp4"}:
            model.to(dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        if precision in {"int8", "fp8", "nvfp4"}:
            from torchao.quantization import quantize_
    
            if backend.startswith("disentangled_flash"):
                raise ValueError(
                    "Quantized encoder projections need separate backend validation"
                )
            if precision == "int8":
                from torchao.quantization import Int8WeightOnlyConfig
    
                config = Int8WeightOnlyConfig()
            elif precision == "fp8":
                from torchao.quantization import Float8DynamicActivationFloat8WeightConfig
    
                config = Float8DynamicActivationFloat8WeightConfig()
            else:
                from torchao.prototype.mx_formats.inference_workflow import (
                    NVFP4DynamicActivationNVFP4WeightConfig,
                )
    
                config = NVFP4DynamicActivationNVFP4WeightConfig(use_triton_kernel=False)
            quantize_(model.encoder, config)
        model.eval()
        if batched_attributes:
            from gliner_attributes import prepare_attributes
    
            model._prepare_batched_attributes = partial(prepare_attributes, model)
        if backend.startswith("disentangled_flash"):
            model.enable_disentangled_flash()
            if backend == "disentangled_flash_heads":
                # Compile the extraction heads only; the prepared attention
                # encoder remains outside torch.compile, as its API requires.
                for name in (
                    "boundary_encoder",
                    "boundary_query_head",
                    "boundary_proposer",
                    "pair_scorer",
                    "shared_pool_builder",
                    "shared_pool_scorer",
                ):
                    module = getattr(model.boundary_head, name, None)
                    if module is not None:
                        setattr(
                            model.boundary_head, name, torch.compile(module, dynamic=True)
                        )
        elif backend == "compiled":
            model.compile(dynamic=True)
        devices = {str(parameter.device) for parameter in model.parameters()}
        if not devices or any(not device.startswith("cuda:") for device in devices):
            raise ValueError(f"Model parameters are not entirely on CUDA: {devices}")
        metadata = {
            "parameter_devices": sorted(devices),
            "parameter_dtypes": dict(Counter(str(p.dtype) for p in model.parameters())),
            "encoder_linear_weight_types": dict(
                Counter(
                    type(module.weight).__name__
                    for module in model.encoder.modules()
                    if isinstance(module, torch.nn.Linear)
                )
            ),
            "compute_capability": torch.cuda.get_device_capability(),
        }
        return model, metadata

    description: Measure full-article GLiNER extraction speed and output stability on the local GPU.

    ---
    
    # Benchmark local company extraction
    
    ## Goal
    
    Assess whether local extraction can process 12 million articles in 24 hours
    (138.9 articles/second), or the current 12,241,870 retained rows at 141.7/second.
    Measure company spans, per-mention roles and article type together, preserving
    long-document coverage. Treat output stability and reviewed accuracy separately.
    
    ## Acceptance
    
    - [x] Stop native Kev serving while preserving completed scores and checkpoints.
    - [x] Prepare a source-verified 10,000-row sample and the existing 1,000-row pilot.
    - [x] Verify CUDA execution and compare precision, attention and batching paths.
    - [x] Repeat the best configuration on the full sample and record runtime limits.
    - [x] Preserve DVC evidence, document quality limits and pass repository checks.
    
    ## Evidence
    
    The [inference tools](../../../../../infra/inference/README.md) pin model and
    library versions, preserve explicit source-offset corrections, and separate
    initialization from steady-state timing. The benchmark remains experimental;
    company identity linking and human validation are required before dataset use.
    
    The selected 74M checkpoint achieved 162.3–163.7 records/second across three
    10,000-record runs, projecting 20.9 hours of extraction for the retained
    population. It uses FP16, DisentangledFlash, compiled extraction heads, buffered
    worker preprocessing and batched role scoring, preserving the original window
    coverage. All records passed structural checks. The
    [DVC benchmark report](../../../../../data/research/experiments/article-labels/gliner-benchmark/report.md)
    records numerical differences and known semantic limitations. The complete
    repository check passed, including 47 tests; GPU parity and reinstall checks
    passed separately.

    ---
    name: architecture-layout
    description: Use when evaluating or designing where CCFinance code, data stages, tests, documents or infrastructure belong, including module boundaries and repository restructures.
    ---
    
    # Architecture layout
    
    ## Workflow
    
    1. Establish the requested scope and outcome: evaluate the current layout,
       design a layout, or implement an authorized change. Read nearby README and
       ARCHITECTURE files. Identify existing owners and consumers before proposing
       a new abstraction; reuse an existing module or library when it satisfies the
       contract. File size alone is not a reason to split or create a package.
    2. Examine the relevant boundaries using evidence:
       - **Ownership and cohesion:** Can a contributor find the owner, and do things
         that change together live together? Keep each unit's responsibility clear.
       - **Dependencies and encapsulation:** Trace relevant imports and public
         interfaces. Keep intended dependency direction clear and cycles forbidden;
         avoid reaching into another module's internals without a reason.
       - **Coupling:** Identify changes that force unrelated owners to change.
         Share a contract only when consumers actually need the same behavior; a
         little local duplication may be preferable to coupling distinct contracts.
       - **Discoverability:** Make CLI commands, transformations, schemas, tests,
         fixtures and documents easy to find from their owning area.
    3. Choose the smallest useful boundary: a function, module, package or separate
       workspace project. A package or project should reflect an actual dependency,
       distribution, build or ownership need. Organize by layer, capability or a
       combination according to the work; do not impose a universal directory tree.
    4. For pipeline work, preserve the established `raw`, `processed` and `research`
       stage ownership. Organize capabilities within those layers as they arise.
       Distinguish Python imports from DVC artifact dependencies: the latter connect
       producers and consumers without requiring cross-layer Python imports. Apply
       Tach rules to durable module boundaries and DVC to artifact dependencies.
    5. For a move or split, trace the affected consumers before changing paths:
       imports and public APIs, CLI registration, package configuration, tests and
       fixtures, Tach, DVC and Semflow dependencies, and documentation links as
       applicable. Preserve behavior and scientific contracts unless the user asks
       for a change; report any intended behavior change separately. Do not treat
       missing static references as proof that dynamic or external consumers do not
       exist.
    6. Use the repository's existing gates rather than adding tests that merely
       assert a directory tree or private call sequence. For tests and fixtures,
       follow [Python testing](../python-testing/SKILL.md). Run focused checks while
       working and `just check` before handoff; report checks that could not run.
    
    ## Results
    
    For an evaluation, report concrete findings with locations, effects and ranked
    recommendations. For a design, show the proposed ownership and dependency
    boundaries, explain meaningful tradeoffs and how they are enforced. For an
    implementation, summarize what moved, whether behavior changed and the evidence
    from verification. Keep the review proportional to the requested change.
    
    For example, if both article cleaning and company linking need the same
    publication-date parser, first inspect its existing owner and date semantics.
    Share it only if both consumers require the same contract; keep separate rules
    when their treatment of missing or ambiguous dates differs.
    ---
    name: python-testing
    description: Use when writing, changing, reviewing or organizing Python tests, pytest fixtures or Hypothesis strategies in CCFinance.
    ---
    
    # Python testing
    
    ## Workflow
    
    1. Inspect the code contract, nearby tests, `conftest.py`, shared fixtures and
       strategies, the package's test README, and pytest configuration. Reuse an
       existing test or generator when it covers the behavior; extend it only for a
       distinct, meaningful risk. Do not add tests for trivial or reversible changes
       just to increase counts, or tests that restate implementation details.
    2. Prefer Hypothesis for input variation when a general property is meaningful.
       Prefer a small explicit example for a single known boundary, regression or
       command smoke check. Decide the expected outcome independently of the code
       under test. Use tiny representative data, bounded generators and the smallest
       appropriate test boundary. Assert public behavior, including error contracts.
    3. Place a test beside its source owner under the mirrored `tests/` layout. Reuse
       existing factories and strategies first. Keep a helper local until several
       tests need it; put cross-module strategies in `tests/_strategies.py` and
       shared pytest fixtures in the nearest common `conftest.py`. Place a fixture
       at broader scope only when its state is safe to share. Measure costly setup
       before broadening scope; avoid creating generic fixture frameworks.
    4. Arrange inputs and prerequisites, act on the behavior, and assert observable
       results (AAA). Cleanup belongs in a fixture finalizer or context manager.
       Label each phase with an `# Arrange`, `# Act` or `# Assert` comment, as in
       the example below. Favor DAMP: clear names and visible expected values can
       justify a little repetition.
    5. Give each new or modified test exactly one scope marker from the table below;
       add `slow` or `external` only when applicable. Mark a class or module only
       when every inherited test has the same scope. Never stack or override scope
       markers, including inherited marks. Before using markers, register the six
       names in the owning pytest configuration; unknown names fail under
       `--strict-markers`. This skill defines the policy; it does not mean the
       current unmarked suite already enforces it. Migrate existing tests deliberately
       if adding a collection-time enforcement hook.
    6. During development, run the smallest relevant test or selection and check
       its output. Before handoff run the repository's required full checks, including
       the complete non-Testmon suite. Run any affected slow or external tests when
       their prerequisites and authorization are available; report what was not run
       and why. A targeted pass is not evidence that the full suite passed.
    
    ## Markers
    
    Use only these six custom markers. Built-in pytest mechanisms such as
    `parametrize`, `skipif` and `xfail` remain available for their intended purposes.
    Scope describes the boundary the assertions exercise, not the number of files,
    the use of Hypothesis, or the choice of a reference oracle.
    
    | Marker | Rule |
    | --- | --- |
    | `unit` | Exactly one scope: an isolated operation or small self-contained behavior. |
    | `component` | Exactly one scope: one coherent subsystem or component through its public behavior. |
    | `integration` | Exactly one scope: interactions across components or a real dependency boundary. |
    | `e2e` | Exactly one scope: a complete user-visible workflow through the public CLI or API. A CLI help check alone is not end-to-end. |
    | `slow` | Optional execution label: the complete test, including setup, teardown and generated examples, consistently exceeds two seconds on the normal local environment. Confirm with repeated pytest duration reports; a single noisy measurement is not enough. |
    | `external` | Optional execution label: the test accesses a live network service or external account. Use even if it is usually fast; require explicit opt-in and appropriate credentials. A local temporary file, subprocess or fake alone does not qualify. |
    
    `slow` and `external` are independent and may accompany any one scope. Do not
    invent custom markers for regression, reference, property, smoke, tools or
    implementation techniques; communicate those in descriptive test names and
    assertions. Run fast local iteration with `-m "not slow and not external"`
    after the markers are registered. Full checks must not silently omit slow tests;
    external tests need a separate explicit lane and must not mutate live services
    without authorization.
    
    ## Hypothesis examples and fixtures
    
    Hypothesis strategies generate values; pytest fixtures manage resources. If
    Hypothesis is absent, add it to the locked workspace development dependencies
    when introducing the first test that uses it. Search
    for reusable strategies or an appropriate first-party Hypothesis extra before
    adding one. Compose built-in strategies, use `@composite` for dependent values,
    and generate valid inputs directly rather than filtering most examples. Keep
    sizes bounded and counterexamples understandable. Preserve an important known
    failure using `@example` or an explicit regression; do not duplicate a property
    with a long list of examples that establish the same behavior.
    
    A function-scoped pytest fixture runs once per test function, not once per
    `@given` example. For per-example mutable resources, create and clean them inside
    the test, for example with `TemporaryDirectory()`. Reuse immutable shared data
    only when safe. Do not suppress health checks or disable deadlines globally to
    make a test pass; investigate the cause and document a narrowly justified
    exception. Choose explicit settings or a shared profile only when warranted by
    measured cost. Preserve failing examples and replay information as appropriate.
    
    This self-contained example illustrates a small property, AAA and the scope
    marker; it uses the standard-library URL parser rather than a CCFinance stage:
    
    ```python
    from string import ascii_lowercase, digits
    from urllib.parse import urlsplit
    
    import pytest
    from hypothesis import example, given, strategies as st
    
    
    @pytest.mark.unit
    @example(host="news")
    @given(host=st.text(alphabet=ascii_lowercase + digits, min_size=1, max_size=20))
    def test_url_hostname_normalizes_ascii_case(host: str) -> None:
        # Arrange: build a URL with an uppercase hostname.
        url = f"https://{host.upper()}.example/article"
    
        # Act: extract the hostname.
        hostname = urlsplit(url).hostname
    
        # Assert: the hostname is lowercase.
        assert hostname == f"{host}.example"
    ```
    
    Use a real local Parquet or filesystem boundary for a small integration test
    when that interaction matters; use a stub or fake for costly or nondeterministic
    remote services. A fake cannot establish that the real service works. Keep
    randomized tests independent of execution order; for numerical or sampling
    claims define tolerances and uncertainty rather than requiring arbitrary

    """Batch span-attribute scoring while retaining GLiNER's own span selection."""
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
    
    import torch
    
    if TYPE_CHECKING:
        from gliner2.models.boundary.engine import BoundaryExtractor
        from gliner2.processor import PreprocessedBatch
    
    
    def prepare_attributes(
        model: BoundaryExtractor,
        batch: PreprocessedBatch,
        core: dict,
        metadata_list: list[dict],
        grouped_candidates: list[list[list[tuple[float, int, int]]]] | None,
        null_probs: torch.Tensor | None,
    ) -> dict[int, dict]:
        """Collect exactly the decoded spans, then score all eligible windows together."""
        pending = []
        core["_pending_attribute_inputs"] = pending
        try:
            for index, metadata in enumerate(metadata_list):
                if not metadata.get("entity_attribute_groups"):
                    continue
                model._decode_entities(
                    index,
                    core,
                    core["ext_specs"][index],
                    grouped_candidates[index] if grouped_candidates is not None else [],
                    metadata,
                    null_probs[index] if null_probs is not None else None,
                    model._resolved_overlap_policy(metadata.get("_overlap_policy")),
                    core["word_offsets"][index],
                    batch.start_mappings[index],
                    batch.end_mappings[index],
                    batch.original_texts[index],
                    len(batch.start_mappings[index]),
                    True,
                    True,
                )
        finally:
            del core["_pending_attribute_inputs"]
        cases = []
        for sample_index, specs, metadata, decoded, coordinates in pending:
            pairs = list(
                dict.fromkeys(
                    coordinates[id(item)] for items in decoded.values() for item in items
                )
            )
            if not pairs:
                continue
            query_by_name = {
                spec["field_name"]: index
                for index, spec in enumerate(specs)
                if spec["task_type"] == "entities"
            }
            prompts = metadata.get("entity_attribute_prompt_labels", {})
            rows = list(
                dict.fromkeys(
                    (label, query_by_name[prompt])
                    for group in metadata["entity_attribute_groups"].values()
                    for label in group.labels
                    if (prompt := prompts.get(label, label)) in query_by_name
                )
            )
            if rows:
                cases.append((sample_index, rows, pairs))
        if not cases:
            return {}
        device = core["query_states"].device
        count = len(cases)
        queries = max(len(rows) for _, rows, _ in cases)
        spans = max(len(pairs) for _, _, pairs in cases)
        query_indices = torch.zeros((count, queries), dtype=torch.long)
        query_valid = torch.zeros((count, queries), dtype=torch.bool)
        indices = torch.zeros((count, queries, spans, 2), dtype=torch.long)
        valid = torch.zeros((count, queries, spans), dtype=torch.bool)
        for index, (_, rows, pairs) in enumerate(cases):
            query_indices[index, : len(rows)] = torch.tensor([query for _, query in rows])
            query_valid[index, : len(rows)] = True
            indices[index, : len(rows), : len(pairs)] = torch.tensor(pairs).unsqueeze(0)
            valid[index, : len(rows), : len(pairs)] = True
        samples = torch.tensor([sample for sample, _, _ in cases], device=device)
        query_indices = query_indices.to(device)
        states = core["query_states"].index_select(0, samples)
        states = states.gather(
            1, query_indices.unsqueeze(-1).expand(-1, -1, states.shape[-1])
        )
        mask = core["query_mask"].index_select(0, samples).gather(1, query_indices)
        mask = mask & query_valid.to(device)
        logits = model.boundary_head.score_explicit_spans(
            core["text_states"].index_select(0, samples),
            core["text_mask"].index_select(0, samples),
            states,
            mask,
            indices.to(device),
            valid_mask=valid.to(device),
        )
        logits = (logits / model.boundary_settings.pair_temperature).float().cpu()
        return {
            sample: {
                "labels": [label for label, _ in rows],
                "pairs": {pair: index for index, pair in enumerate(pairs)},
                "logits": logits[index, : len(rows), : len(pairs)],
            }
            for index, (sample, rows, pairs) in enumerate(cases)
        }

    """Compare CPU and CUDA FP32 predictions after the attribute-index patch."""
    
    import json
    from functools import partial
    
    import torch
    from gliner2 import AutoExtractor
    from gliner_attributes import prepare_attributes
    from gliner_schema import build_schema
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Run one multi-company example on CPU and GPU with the same weights."""
        # Arrange: request entities, their roles and article type in the same schema.
        torch.set_num_threads(4)
        model = AutoExtractor.from_pretrained("/model", map_location="cpu")
        schema = build_schema(model)
        article = "Apple reported earnings. Microsoft was mentioned."
    
        # Act: extract the same schema before and after transferring the model.
        cpu = model.extract(article, schema, include_spans=True, include_confidence=True)
        model.to("cuda")
        gpu = model.extract(article, schema, include_spans=True, include_confidence=True)
    
        # Assert: both devices return the same spans and discrete role labels.
        def labels(result: dict) -> set[tuple]:
            return {
                (
                    entity["start"],
                    entity["end"],
                    entity["text"],
                    entity["article_role"]["label"],
                )
                for entity in result["entities"]["company"]
            }
    
        if not labels(cpu) or labels(cpu) != labels(gpu):
            raise AssertionError("CPU and CUDA company spans or roles differ")
        if cpu["article_type"]["label"] != gpu["article_type"]["label"]:
            raise AssertionError("CPU and CUDA article types differ")
        # Arrange: use different company spans in the same CUDA batch.
        documents = [article, "Microsoft reported higher sales than Apple."]
        expected = model.batch_extract(
            documents, schema, batch_size=2, include_spans=True, include_confidence=True
        )
        model._prepare_batched_attributes = partial(prepare_attributes, model)
    
        # Act: score the same selected spans with batched role scoring.
        observed = model.batch_extract(
            documents, schema, batch_size=2, include_spans=True, include_confidence=True
        )
    
        # Assert: batching preserves FP32 spans, role labels and article types.
        maximum = 0.0
        for reference, candidate in zip(expected, observed, strict=True):
            if labels(reference) != labels(candidate):
                raise AssertionError("Batched role scoring changed FP32 spans or roles")
            if reference["article_type"]["label"] != candidate["article_type"]["label"]:
                raise AssertionError("Batched role scoring changed the article type")
            by_span = {
                (entity["start"], entity["end"]): entity
                for entity in reference["entities"]["company"]
            }
            for entity in candidate["entities"]["company"]:
                original = by_span[(entity["start"], entity["end"])]
                maximum = max(
                    maximum,
                    abs(
                        entity["article_role"]["confidence"]
                        - original["article_role"]["confidence"]
                    ),
                )
        if maximum > 0.0001:
            raise AssertionError(f"FP32 role confidence drift exceeds tolerance: {maximum}")
        print(json.dumps({"cpu": cpu, "cuda": gpu, "batched_fp32_maximum_drift": maximum}))
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()
    """Validate saved extraction structure and finite confidence scores."""
    
    import argparse
    import gzip
    import json
    import math
    from collections import Counter
    from pathlib import Path
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Check saved outputs without treating structural validity as accuracy."""
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("predictions", type=Path)
        parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
        seen: set[str] = set()
        with gzip.open(args.predictions, "rt", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            for line in stream:
                row = json.loads(line)
                article_id = row["article_id"]
                if article_id in seen:
                    raise ValueError(f"Duplicate article: {article_id}")
                seen.add(article_id)
                prediction = row["prediction"]
                article_type = prediction.get("article_type", {})
                entities = prediction.get("entities", {}).get("company", [])
                values = [
                    article_type,
                    *entities,
                    *[entity.get("article_role", {}) for entity in entities],
                ]
                invalid = not all(
                    isinstance(value.get("confidence"), (int, float))
                    and math.isfinite(value["confidence"])
                    and 0 <= value["confidence"] <= 1
                    for value in values
                )
                invalid_labels = article_type.get("label") not in {
                    "reporting",
                    "opinion",
                    "press release",
                    "promotional",
                    "other",
                } or any(
                    entity.get("article_role", {}).get("label")
                    not in {"primary", "secondary", "incidental", "uncertain"}
                    for entity in entities
                )
                counts["articles"] += 1
                counts["invalid_confidence_articles"] += invalid
                counts["invalid_label_articles"] += invalid_labels
                counts["invalid_span_articles"] += row.get("status", "ok") != "ok"
                counts["articles_with_company_spans"] += bool(entities)
                counts["company_spans"] += len(entities)
        report = {
            "counts": dict(counts),
            "interpretation": "Structural checks only; no semantic accuracy claim.",
        }
        args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(json.dumps(report))
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()
    """Collect local benchmark evidence without copying source article bodies."""
    
    import argparse
    import hashlib
    import json
    import shutil
    from pathlib import Path
    
    
    def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
        """Return the file's SHA-256 digest."""
        with path.open("rb") as stream:
            return hashlib.file_digest(stream, "sha256").hexdigest()
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        """Copy selections, predictions, reports, logs, and the executing code."""
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        runtime = Path(".runtime/gliner-benchmark")
        args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
        for name in ("sample", "pilot-1000"):
            destination = args.output / name
            destination.mkdir()
            for filename in ("selection.parquet", "selection.json", "sample.json"):
                shutil.copy2(runtime / name / filename, destination / filename)
        with (runtime / "screen.jsonl").open(encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            ids = [json.loads(line)["article_id"] for line in stream]
        (args.output / "screen-article-ids.json").write_text(
            json.dumps(ids, indent=2) + "\n"
        )
        for name in (
            "screen-results",
            "screen-logs",
            "batch-results",
            "batch-logs",
            "final-results",
            "final-logs",
            "throughput-results",
            "throughput-logs",
            "profile-compiled",
            "precision-probes",
            "throughput-code",
            "buffer-batch-results",
            "buffer-batch-logs",
            "optimized-trials",
            "buffer-final-results",
            "buffer-final-logs",
            "attribute-trials",
            "window-logs",
        ):
            shutil.copytree(runtime / name, args.output / name)
        for name in (
            "invalid-span-repro",
            "invalid-span-corrected",
            "small-fp16-flash-b64-full-2",
        ):
            ignore = (
                shutil.ignore_patterns("report.json")
                if name == "invalid-span-repro"
                else None
            )
            shutil.copytree(
                runtime / "results" / name,
                args.output / "earlier-runs" / name,
                ignore=ignore,
            )
        shutil.copy2(runtime / "device-check.log", args.output / "device-check.log")
        logs = args.output / "logs"
        logs.mkdir()
        for file in runtime.glob("*.log"):
            shutil.copy2(file, logs / file.name)
        for filename in ("metrics.json", "throughput.csv"):
            shutil.copy2(runtime / filename, args.output / filename)
        code = args.output / "code"
        code.mkdir()
        shutil.copytree(runtime / "historical-launchers", code / "historical-launchers")
        for file in sorted(Path("infra/inference").glob("gliner*")):
            if file.is_file():
                shutil.copy2(file, code / file.name)
        shutil.copy2(
            Path(
                "src/python/apps/pipeline/src/pipeline/stages/processed/experiments/article_scoring.py"
            ),
            code / "source_article_scoring.py",
        )
        weights = {
            name: sha256(Path(".runtime/models") / name / "model.safetensors")
            for name in ("gliner2.5-small-v1", "gliner2.5-base-v1")
        }
        manifest = {
            "image": (
                "lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:"
                "f7876bef696ccf9cf75a2bf7ccb82970f5fac577f082fb8ca95c9a59d2160eb5"
            ),
            "models": {
                "gliner2.5-small-v1": {
                    "revision": "b5d42bf7dc7d01c40304ae4ed43c2f13c325a75b",
                    "weights_sha256": weights["gliner2.5-small-v1"],
                },
                "gliner2.5-base-v1": {
                    "revision": "07d99c0ba5d15cb3b24e0a236fa99bdd4ef87a5c",
                    "weights_sha256": weights["gliner2.5-base-v1"],
                },
            },
            "code_sha256": {
                str(file.relative_to(code)): sha256(file)
                for file in sorted(code.rglob("*"))
                if file.is_file()
            },
            "article_bodies_included": False,
        }
        (args.output / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n")

    # CHANGELOG
    
    ## Unreleased
    
    ### Added
    
    - Corpus-wide company candidates with dated issuer corrections, source-only
      audits, provisional native Kev judgments, resumable checkpoints and observed
      company-year coverage reports, plus source-verified GLiNER benchmarks for

    - DVC repository configuration and a workspace for research data.

    - Planning and local reference workflows with Schematter validation and Insitu views.
    - A validated changelog with a closed set of change categories.

      so the frozen acquisition stage has real outputs for DVC to validate.
    - Grouped experiments within each data layer and consolidated source mappings
      and validated artifact contracts across sampling and research reports.
    - Organized the pipeline into `raw`, `processed` and `research` layers, with
      matching Python modules, CLI groups and proposed data paths.

        def _compute_classification_probabilities(
            self,
            schema: Dict,
            embs: torch.Tensor,
            schema_tokens: List[str],
            temperature: float = 1.0,
        ) -> Optional[Tuple[str, Dict, torch.Tensor]]:
            """Compute classification probabilities without reading device values."""
            prompt_str = schema_tokens[2]
            cls_config = self._resolve_classification_config(
                prompt_str, schema.get("classifications", [])
            )
            if cls_config is None:
                return None
            schema_name = cls_config["task"]
    
            cls_embeds = embs[1:]
            if temperature <= 0:
                raise ValueError("classification temperature must be > 0")
            logits = self.classifier(cls_embeds).squeeze(-1) / temperature
    
            activation = cls_config.get("class_act", "auto")
            is_multi = cls_config.get("multi_label", False)
    
            if activation == "sigmoid":
                probs = torch.sigmoid(logits)
            elif activation == "softmax":
                probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
            else:
                probs = torch.sigmoid(logits) if is_multi else torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
    
            return schema_name, cls_config, probs
    
        @staticmethod
        def _decode_classification_probabilities(
            results: Dict,
            schema_name: str,
            cls_config: Dict,
            probs: torch.Tensor,
        ) -> None:
            """Decode precomputed probabilities on either CPU or an accelerator."""
            labels = cls_config["labels"]
            cls_threshold = cls_config.get("cls_threshold", 0.5)
            is_multi = cls_config.get("multi_label", False)
    
            if is_multi:
                chosen = [
                    (labels[j], probs[j].item())
                    for j in range(len(labels))
                    if probs[j].item() >= cls_threshold
                ]
                if not chosen:
                    best = int(torch.argmax(probs).item())
                    chosen = [(labels[best], probs[best].item())]
                top_k = cls_config.get("top_k")
                if top_k is not None:
                    chosen = sorted(chosen, key=lambda pair: pair[1], reverse=True)[:top_k]
                results[schema_name] = chosen
            else:
                best = int(torch.argmax(probs).item())
                results[schema_name] = (labels[best], probs[best].item())

        def _build_schema_dicts_and_metadata(
            self, schema_list: List[Any]
        ) -> Tuple[List[Dict], List[Dict]]:
            """Normalize schemas into ``(schema_dicts, metadata_list)``."""
            schema_dicts: List[Dict] = []
            metadata_list: List[Dict] = []
    
            for schema in schema_list:
                if hasattr(schema, "build"):
                    schema_dict = schema.build()
                    classification_tasks = [c["task"] for c in schema_dict.get("classifications", [])]
                    metadata = {
                        "field_metadata": schema._field_metadata,
                        "entity_metadata": schema._entity_metadata,
                        "relation_metadata": getattr(schema, "_relation_metadata", {}),
                        "relation_descriptions": schema_dict.get("relation_descriptions", {}),
                        "field_orders": schema._field_orders,
                        "entity_order": schema._entity_order,
                        "relation_order": getattr(schema, "_relation_order", []),
                        "classification_tasks": classification_tasks,
                        "entity_attribute_groups": getattr(schema, "_entity_attribute_groups", {}),
                        "entity_attribute_prompt_labels": getattr(
                            schema, "_entity_attribute_prompt_labels", {}
                        ),
                        "entity_attribute_labels": getattr(schema, "_entity_attribute_labels", set()),
                    }
                else:
                    schema_dict = schema
                    entities = schema_dict.get("entities")
                    if isinstance(entities, list):
                        schema_dict = {**schema_dict, "entities": {e: "" for e in entities}}
                    classification_tasks = [c["task"] for c in schema_dict.get("classifications", [])]
                    entity_order = (
                        list(schema_dict["entities"].keys())
                        if isinstance(schema_dict.get("entities"), dict)
                        else []
                    )
                    metadata = {
                        "field_metadata": {},
                        "entity_metadata": {},
                        "relation_metadata": {},
                        "relation_descriptions": schema_dict.get("relation_descriptions", {}),
                        "field_orders": {},
                        "entity_order": entity_order,
                        "relation_order": [],
                        "classification_tasks": classification_tasks,
                        "entity_attribute_groups": {},
                        "entity_attribute_prompt_labels": {},
                        "entity_attribute_labels": set(),
                    }
    
                schema_dicts.append(schema_dict)
                metadata_list.append(metadata)
    
            return schema_dicts, metadata_list
    
        def _resolved_overlap_policy(self, overlap_policy: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[str]:
            """Resolve an explicit policy while preserving architecture defaults."""
            if overlap_policy is not None:
                return normalize_overlap_policy(overlap_policy)
            if getattr(self, "architecture", "span") != "boundary":
                # ``None`` selects the historical confidence-first greedy decoder
                # for span checkpoints. Explicit ``flat``/``disallow`` uses the
                # shared architecture-neutral resolver.
                return None
            settings = getattr(self, "boundary_settings", None)
            default = getattr(settings, "overlap_policy", "disallow")
    if TYPE_CHECKING:
        from gliner2.api_client import GLiNER2API
    
    
    def _is_score(value: object) -> bool:
        """True for a confidence scalar, excluding bools."""
        return isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool)
    
    
    def _format_classification(value: object, include_confidence: bool) -> object:
        """Format a single- or multi-label classification, including JSON lists.
    
        Args:
            value: ``(label, score)``, JSON ``[label, score]``, or a list of pairs.
            include_confidence: When True, keep scores on the public payload.
    
        Returns:
            A label, a ``{label, confidence}`` dict, or a list of those.
        """
        if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)) and value:
            first = value[0]
            if isinstance(first, (list, tuple)):
                if include_confidence:
                    return [{"label": item[0], "confidence": item[1]} for item in value]
                return [item[0] for item in value]
            # A pair is only a (label, score) if the score is numeric; a
            # two-label list stays a list.
            if len(value) == 2 and isinstance(first, str) and _is_score(value[1]):
                label, conf = value
                return {"label": label, "confidence": conf} if include_confidence else label
        return value
    
    
    def format_results(
        results: Dict,
        include_confidence: bool = False,
        requested_relations: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        classification_tasks: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Format extraction results into the public AutoExtractor payload."""
        formatted = {}
        relations = {}
        requested_relations = requested_relations or []
        classification_tasks = classification_tasks or []
    
        for key, value in results.items():
            is_classification = key in classification_tasks
            is_relation = False
    
            if not is_classification:
                if key in requested_relations:
                    is_relation = True
                elif isinstance(value, list) and len(value) > 0:
                    if isinstance(value[0], tuple) and len(value[0]) == 2:
                        is_relation = True
                    elif isinstance(value[0], dict) and "head" in value[0] and "tail" in value[0]:
                        is_relation = True
    
            if is_classification:
                formatted[key] = _format_classification(value, include_confidence)
            elif is_relation:
                relations[key] = value if isinstance(value, list) else []
            elif isinstance(value, list):
                if len(value) == 0:
                    formatted[key] = {} if key == "entities" else value
                elif isinstance(value[0], dict):
                    if key == "entities":

                    else:
                        formatted[key] = [l for l, _ in value]
                else:
                    formatted[key] = value
            elif isinstance(value, tuple):
                label, conf = value
                formatted[key] = {"label": label, "confidence": conf} if include_confidence else label
            elif isinstance(value, dict):
                formatted[key] = format_struct(value, include_confidence)
            else:
                formatted[key] = value
    
        for rel in requested_relations:
            if rel not in relations:
                relations[rel] = []
    
        if relations:
            formatted["relation_extraction"] = relations
    
        return formatted

                spec["field_name"]: query_id
                for query_id, spec in enumerate(specs)
                if spec["task_type"] == "entities"
            }

            for group in groups.values():
                for label in group.labels:
                    prompt = prompt_labels.get(label, label)
                    query_id = query_by_name.get(prompt)
                    if query_id is not None:
                        attribute_rows.append((label, query_id))

            attribute_rows = list(dict.fromkeys(attribute_rows))
            if not attribute_rows:
                return

                token_coordinates[id(item)]
                for items in decoded.values()
                for item in items
            ))
            if not unique_pairs:
                return

                    raise ValueError("Batched attribute query labels differ")

                logits = cached["logits"][:, columns]
            else:
                device = core["query_states"].device
                query_ids = torch.tensor(
                    [query_id for _, query_id in attribute_rows],
                    dtype=torch.long,
                    device=device,
                )
                pair_tensor = torch.tensor(
                    unique_pairs, dtype=torch.long, device=device
                )
                indices = pair_tensor.view(1, 1, len(unique_pairs), 2).expand(
                    1, len(attribute_rows), len(unique_pairs), 2
                )

                    sample_index:sample_index + 1

                    sample_index:sample_index + 1

                    query_mask,
                    indices,
                )[0]

                    logits / self.boundary_settings.pair_temperature

                label: row for row, (label, _) in enumerate(attribute_rows)

                    column = pair_index[token_coordinates[id(item)]]
                    for group_name, group in groups.items():
                        if (
                            group.applies_to is not None
                            and entity_name not in group.applies_to

                            continue
                        present = [
                            (label, row_by_label[label])
                            for label in group.labels
                            if label in row_by_label
                        ]
                        if not present:
                            continue
                        labels, rows = zip(*present)
                        values = logits[
                            torch.tensor(rows, dtype=torch.long, device=logits.device),
                            column,
                        ]
                        if group.multi_label:
                            probabilities = torch.sigmoid(values)
                            item[group_name] = [
                                {
                                    "label": label,
                                    "confidence": float(probabilities[index]),
                                }
                                for index, label in enumerate(labels)
                                if float(probabilities[index]) >= group.threshold
                            ]
                        else:
                            probabilities = torch.softmax(values, dim=-1)
                            best = int(probabilities.argmax())
                            item[group_name] = {
                                "label": labels[best],
                                "confidence": float(probabilities[best]),
                            }

    """Utilities for long-document extraction.
    
    The helpers in this module are intentionally model-agnostic: they split text
    into word-aware windows, remap chunk-local spans back to document offsets, and
    merge duplicate predictions produced by overlapping chunks.
    """
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    from collections import Counter
    from dataclasses import dataclass
    from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Tuple
    
    from gliner2.inference.overlap import normalize_overlap_policy, resolve_overlaps
    from gliner2.processing.word_splitter import resolve_word_splitter
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class TextChunk:
        """A chunk of text with offsets into the original document."""
    
        text: str
        start_char: int
        end_char: int
        start_word: int
        end_word: int
    
    
    def iter_word_offsets(
        text: str,
        word_splitter=None,
    ) -> Iterable[Tuple[str, int, int]]:
        """Yield word tokens and character offsets using the active splitter.
    
        ``word_splitter`` may be a built-in name, a callable, or omitted to use
        the default whitespace splitter. Offsets always index the original text;
        chunking requests original-case token strings (``lower=False``).
        """
        splitter = resolve_word_splitter(word_splitter)
        yield from splitter(text, lower=False)
    
    
    def split_text_into_chunks(
        text: str,
        chunk_size: int = 384,
        chunk_overlap: int = 64,
        word_splitter=None,
    ) -> List[TextChunk]:
        """Split text into overlapping word windows.
    
        Args:
            text: Original document text.
            chunk_size: Maximum number of word tokens per chunk.
            chunk_overlap: Number of word tokens repeated between adjacent chunks.
            word_splitter: Optional splitter name or callable used to count words.
        """
        if chunk_size <= 0:
            raise ValueError("chunk_size must be greater than 0")
        if chunk_overlap < 0:
            raise ValueError("chunk_overlap must be non-negative")
        if chunk_overlap >= chunk_size:
            raise ValueError("chunk_overlap must be smaller than chunk_size")
    
        tokens = list(iter_word_offsets(text, word_splitter=word_splitter))
        if not tokens:
            return [TextChunk(text=text, start_char=0, end_char=len(text), start_word=0, end_word=0)]
    
        chunks: List[TextChunk] = []
        step = chunk_size - chunk_overlap
        start_word = 0
    
        while start_word < len(tokens):
            end_word = min(start_word + chunk_size, len(tokens))
            start_char = tokens[start_word][1]
            end_char = tokens[end_word - 1][2]
            chunks.append(
                TextChunk(
                    text=text[start_char:end_char],
                    start_char=start_char,
                    end_char=end_char,
                    start_word=start_word,
                    end_word=end_word,
                )
            )
            if end_word == len(tokens):
                break
            start_word += step
    
        return chunks
    
    
    def remap_result_spans(result: Any, original_text: str, chunk: TextChunk) -> Any:
        """Recursively remap chunk-local span dicts to document-level offsets."""
        if isinstance(result, list):
            return [remap_result_spans(item, original_text, chunk) for item in result]
    
        if isinstance(result, dict):
            remapped = {key: remap_result_spans(value, original_text, chunk) for key, value in result.items()}
            if _is_span_dict(remapped):
                local_start = int(remapped["start"])
                local_end = int(remapped["end"])
                # The processor appends a full stop to unpunctuated windows.
                # Do not map that synthetic character into the source document.
                if (
                    0 <= local_start < len(chunk.text)
                    and local_end == len(chunk.text) + 1
                    and not chunk.text.endswith((".", "!", "?"))
                    and remapped["text"] == chunk.text[local_start:] + "."
                ):
                    local_end = len(chunk.text)
                    remapped["synthetic_suffix_removed"] = True
                elif not (0 <= local_start < local_end <= len(chunk.text)):
                    remapped["invalid_window_span"] = True
                start = local_start + chunk.start_char
                end = local_end + chunk.start_char
                remapped["start"] = start
                remapped["end"] = end
                if 0 <= start <= end <= len(original_text):
                    remapped["text"] = original_text[start:end]
            return remapped
    
        return result
    
    
    def merge_chunk_results(
        original_text: str,
        chunks: List[TextChunk],
        chunk_results: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        include_confidence: bool = False,
        include_spans: bool = False,
        scalar_entity_labels: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None,
        overlap_policy: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Merge formatted extraction results from one document's chunks.
    
        ``scalar_entity_labels`` names entity types declared with a non-list dtype;
        those are collapsed to a single best value (mirroring the base API) instead
        of being returned as a list.
        """
        if len(chunks) != len(chunk_results):
            raise ValueError("chunks and chunk_results must have the same length")
    
        policy = normalize_overlap_policy(overlap_policy, default="disallow")
        scalar_labels = set(scalar_entity_labels or ())
        remapped_results = [
            remap_result_spans(result, original_text, chunk)
            for chunk, result in zip(chunks, chunk_results)
        ]
        merged = _merge_result_dicts(remapped_results, scalar_labels, policy)
        return _strip_span_metadata(merged, include_confidence, include_spans)
    
    
    def _merge_result_dicts(
        results: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        scalar_entity_labels: Optional[set] = None,
            Relation proposals intentionally score a capped head×tail cross-product.
            Public decoding should nevertheless emit semantic edges, not every
            occurrence combination or contained partial mention.
            """
            if len(edges) < 2:
                return edges
    
            def canonical_mentions(side: str):
                mentions = {
                    (edge[side][1], edge[side][2]): edge[side]
                    for edge in edges
                }
                canonical = {}
                for coordinates, mention in mentions.items():
                    start, end = coordinates
                    containing = [
                        candidate
                        for candidate in mentions.values()
                        if candidate[1] <= start
                        and candidate[2] >= end
                    ]
                    canonical[coordinates] = max(
                        containing,
                        key=lambda candidate: (
                            candidate[2] - candidate[1],
                            -candidate[1],
                        ),
                    )
                return canonical
    
            head_canonical = canonical_mentions("head")
            tail_canonical = canonical_mentions("tail")
            exact: Dict[Tuple[int, int, int, int], Dict[str, Any]] = {}
            for edge in edges:
                head = head_canonical[(edge["head"][1], edge["head"][2])]
                tail = tail_canonical[(edge["tail"][1], edge["tail"][2])]
                normalized = {**edge, "head": head, "tail": tail}
                key = (head[1], head[2], tail[1], tail[2])
                previous = exact.get(key)
                if previous is None or edge["score"] > previous["score"]:
                    exact[key] = normalized
    
            def semantic_text(value: str) -> str:
                return " ".join(value.casefold().split())
    
            semantic: Dict[Tuple[str, str], Dict[str, Any]] = {}
            for edge in exact.values():
                key = (
                    semantic_text(edge["head"][0]),
                    semantic_text(edge["tail"][0]),
                )
                previous = semantic.get(key)
                if previous is None:
                    semantic[key] = edge
                    continue
    
                def rank(candidate):
                    _, hs, he, _ = candidate["head"]
                    _, ts, te, _ = candidate["tail"]
                    distance = max(hs - te, ts - he, 0)
                    return (distance, -candidate["score"], hs, ts)
    
                if rank(edge) < rank(previous):
                    semantic[key] = edge
    
            # If one argument is a strict token-subset of another prediction with
            # the same opposite endpoint, retain the more complete mention.
            kept: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
            values = list(semantic.values())
            for edge in values:
                head_tokens = set(semantic_text(edge["head"][0]).split())
                tail_tokens = set(semantic_text(edge["tail"][0]).split())
                dominated = False
                for other in values:
                    if other is edge:
                        continue
                    other_head = set(semantic_text(other["head"][0]).split())
                    other_tail = set(semantic_text(other["tail"][0]).split())
                    if (
                        head_tokens < other_head
                        and tail_tokens == other_tail
                    ) or (
                        tail_tokens < other_tail
                        and head_tokens == other_head
                    ):
                        dominated = True
                        break
                if not dominated:
                    kept.append(edge)
    
            return sorted(
                kept,
                key=lambda edge: (
                    edge["head"][1],
                    edge["tail"][1],
                    -edge["score"],
                ),
            )
